english: Young cocoa trees act like human babies—they burn easily under direct, intense sunlight. Big shade trees or plantain plants act as natural umbrellas, keeping the sunlight gentle and preserving moisture in the soil so the young cocoa can survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii feɔ amɛnii tamɔ adesai abifabii—amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ye obua ni hulu la ni tsoɔ blɛoo lɛ ahi shi ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ahi shi bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to build healthy leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep for the roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai ni wa aba. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow beside maize, they release this extra food into the soil, acting like free fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi Amɛjieɔ niyenii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them by cutting off oxygen in the soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni ehaa amɛmuɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why is it bad to throw fertilizer onto dry soil when there is no rain in sight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in soil water before roots can drink it in. If applied to dry soil under high heat, the chemical fertilizer sits on top and can scorch or burn the crop roots.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ waa miitsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Chemical ŋmɔshi nibii taraa nɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo eshã tso shishifãi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess moisture and dark, crowded branches create the perfect home for Black Pod disease fungus. Trimming overhead branches lets sunlight and air dry out the crop, stopping the fungal spores from spreading.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ duŋ Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ feɔ shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha black pod hela lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ. Nibii ni afoɔ yɛ yiteŋ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes right inside the main funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ agbɛi titrii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which like to hide inside the central leaves where it is soft and moist. Checking the funnel of the plants early lets you spot them before they destroy the main growing tip.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhi amɛhe yɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli efɔ lɛ ateŋ. Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni ona amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmeii titri ni miida lɛ.

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry spells stress the plant, causing it to drop its flowers to conserve energy instead of spending it on making seeds and fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Ha egbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee dumɔwui kɛ aduawai

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up tightly during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ Harmattan be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds rapidly pull water out of leaves. Plants curl their leaves inward to shrink the surface exposed to the wind, trapping humidity close to the plant.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ lɛ afee bibioo. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam plants make their tubers using energy gathered by their leaves from sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground on wooden stakes gives them more sun exposure and protects them from soil rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo aba amɛnɔ, ni ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why is maize in such high demand in our local markets compared to other grains I could grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa he hiaa waa yɛ wɔ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa krokomɛi ahe lɛ? ni manyɛ madu

english: Maize is a major food staple for Ghanaian households and is also the main ingredient used by commercial poultry and livestock farmers to feed their animals, creating a constant year-round market demand.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii titri kɛha Ghana shiabii. Eji niyenii titri hu ni kooloi kɛ kooloi akwɛlɔi kɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa amɛkooloi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa jarayeli nibii biɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is it better for me to sell all my harvested maize immediately or keep some stored at home?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ mi-abele fɛɛ ni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo makɛto shia?

english: Selling immediately after harvest brings quick cash, but market prices are usually at their lowest then. Storing well-dried maize safely allows you to sell later when scarcity drives prices up, though you must factor in storage protection costs.
ga: Ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ kɛ shika baa oya. Shi bei pii lɛ, jara ni akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni baa shi fe fɛɛ yɛ nakai beaŋ. Abɛi ni egbi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛtoɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli beni nibii ni faaa lɛ haa jara yaa hiɛ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe miihia ni osusu shika ni akɛbuɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ ahe lɛ hu he moŋ.

english: Can I use the maize I harvest on my farm directly to feed my own poultry?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aha mi diɛŋtsɛ mikooloi lɛ niyenii?

english: Yes, maize provides the primary energy source in poultry feed. However, for chickens to digest it properly and grow well, the dried maize kernels need to be crushed or milled and mixed with proteins like soybean meal and key minerals.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ji hewalɛ jɛɛhe titri yɛ kooloi aniyenii amli. Shi, bɔni afee ni kooloi lɛ aná niyenii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara lɛ, esa akɛ atsɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ nɔ loo atsɔ mli ni akɛ protein tamɔ soybean niyenii kɛ minerals ni he hiaa afutu mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get eaten by insects when I store it at home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo ŋmeii yeɔ lɛ kɛ́ mikɛto shia lɛ?

english: Maize spoils when it is stored with too much moisture, which causes mold growth. Insects like weevils also attack stored grain if it is not completely dried below 13% moisture or kept in airtight hermetic bags or treated storage bins.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii hu tutuaa ŋmaa ni ato lɛ kɛji akɛ egbiko kwraa kɛyashɛɛɛ hulutsoo be ni shɛɛɛ 13% loo akɛtoɔ vacuum bags loo ŋmaa ni akɛtoɔ nibii ni atsa mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my young maize plants turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to form green chlorophyll; without enough nutrients or proper fertilizer, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older leaves to support new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee klorofil eŋɔli. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee.

english: What happens to my maize crop if the rains stop right when the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be mli ni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ?

english: Water shortage during flowering (tasseling and silking) prevents successful pollination. Without water at this critical stage, the maize cobs will end up with missing kernels or remain completely empty.
ga: Nu ni faaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli (Tassels kɛ silk) yeɔ omanye ni ekɛtsiɔ fɔfɔii ni baa lɛ anaa. Kɛji nu bɛ yɛ haomɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa loo ebaafee efolo kwraa.

english: Why do some maize plants in my field produce big cobs while others right next to them stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa wuji lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: Uneven cob size happens because plants compete for light, water, and soil nutrients. Planting seeds too close together, uneven fertilizer application, or using saved non-uniform seeds leads to unequal plant growth.
ga: Cob dalɛi ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa ejaakɛ tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ejaaa loo dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni akɛtsuɔ nii Ebaaha tsei lɛ adara yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Can I plant maize together with legumes like cowpeas, or will they compete with each other for food?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaashi akaŋ yɛ niyenii he?

english: Maize and legumes can grow well together. Cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which feeds the maize, while maize provides light shade and structure without suffocating the crop if properly spaced.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kome. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni no haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmãa ni kpɛɔ ni ehaaa tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ to amɛhe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified maize seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from previous harvests lose their vigor and yield potential over time. Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred to resist diseases, handle heat better, and produce much larger, uniform cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii yɛ be ni sa mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ dɔlɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ baa.

english: How can the Ministry of Agriculture help me get quality seeds and fertilizers for my farm?
ga: Te Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni maná dumɔwui ni hi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: The Ministry of Agriculture works through local agricultural extension officers to register farmers, provide advice on best practices, and distribute subsidized farming inputs like improved seeds and fertilizers through government support programs.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi agbɛjianɔtoo he nitsulɔi anɔ koni ekɛ okwaafoi awo wolo nɔ. Ha ŋaawoo yɛ nifeemɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ he ni aja okwaayeli nibii ni akɛyeɔ abuaa tamɔ dumɔwui ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. kɛtsɔ nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi anɔ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun and need shade to survive. Plantain trees grow fast and have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa plants from heat and keeping soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Giving cassava plants enough space lets their tuber roots expand and grow big.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ oha o-cassava tso lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli ni amɛdara.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize after the first rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait for the rain to soak deep into the soil (about hand-depth) before planting. Planting after a light, single shower can cause seeds to sprout and then die if dry weather returns immediately.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. (aaafee o-palm lɛ dalɛ) dani okɛdu. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba trukaa.

english: Why does my farmland produce fewer crops when I plant on it every year without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ beni miduɔ daa afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Crops eat nutrients from the soil every season to grow. If you plant continuously without giving the soil time to recover or adding compost or fertilizer, the soil runs out of food for new crops.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ daa be koni amɛdara. Kɛji odu nii be fɛɛ be ni ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛha tsei heei.

english: Why should I clear weeds before applying fertilizer to my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi dani mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ awo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will steal the fertilizer you put down. Clearing weeds first ensures your maize absorbs all the nutrients so it can grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwo mli lɛ Gbemɔ jwɛi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa oŋmei lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense response to conserve water when the air is dry and hot. However, if leaves stay yellow, it usually means the plant lacks nutrients or is suffering from a sap-sucking insect.
ga: Leaf curling ji hetoo ni akɛbuɔ he koni akɛbu nu he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli loo eyɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why is it important to trim off extra branches and lower leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie niji ni fa fe nine kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛjɛ tomato tsei amli lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary branches allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the plant, preventing fungal diseases and forcing the plant to send its energy into growing bigger fruits instead of leaves.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ awo aduawai wuji amli yɛ baai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my young maize crops get chewed holes in the leaves early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corns lɛ ŋmɔɔ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm attack young maize leaves because they are soft and easy to eat. Checking crops early helps you catch caterpillars before they destroy the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa baai bibii ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ mlɛo. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni omɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does my stored maize get destroyed by tiny black insects after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi diji bibii kpata mi-ŋma ni mikɛto lɛ hiɛ lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Weevils lay eggs inside maize kernels while they are drying. If maize is stored with too much moisture or without proper air-tight sealing, the eggs hatch into insects that eat the grain from the inside.
ga: Weevils woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo akɛtsiii ŋmãa lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ kɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest yield less crop than store-bought certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high yield and disease resistance in their first generation. Saved seeds lose these strong traits in the next generation, producing smaller ears and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni eha yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa toi lɛ feɔ bibii ni ewoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Can my newly planted cocoa seedlings catch diseases right away, or do only older trees get sick?
ga: Kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ baanyɛ aná hela amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Aloo tsei ni edara pɛ hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Diseases caused by viruses can affect cocoa trees at any age, meaning even young seedlings you planted today can be affected.
ga: Virus helai baanyɛ aná kookoo tsei anɔ yɛ afii fɛɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei bibii ni oduɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ po baanyɛ aná he sɛɛ.

english: Are my cocoa trees guaranteed to get sick every single year, or does disease only strike occasionally?
ga: Ani mi cacao tsei lɛ yɛ nɔmimaa akɛ hela baamɔ amɛ daa afi? Aloo ani hela lɛ baa bei komɛi pɛ?

english: Disease does not follow a fixed yearly schedule; any cocoa tree can catch an infection at any time if the virus and its carriers are present.
ga: Hela lɛ nyiɛɛɛɛ afi gbɛjianɔtoo ko sɛɛ. Cacao tsei baanyɛ aná hela be fɛɛ be kɛji akɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yɛ mli.

english: Are there any cocoa trees that are completely safe from catching diseases?
ga: Ani cacao tsei komɛi yɛ ni he yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kwraa kɛjɛ helai ahe?

english: Generally, any cocoa tree can contract viral diseases if exposed, regardless of the variety or location.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko ta cacao tsei ahe lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ baanyɛ aná amɛ. ekɔɔɔ he eko tsɛŋemɔ hela loo he ni eyɔɔ lɛ

english: What actually makes my cocoa trees fall sick on the farm?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miiye hela yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Many serious cocoa diseases are caused by viruses, which are microscopic germs that get inside the tree and disrupt its growth.
ga: Virus kɛ kookoo helai babaoo ni naa wa baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji helatsɛmɛi bibii ni boteɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ edalɛ naa.

english: Is cocoa disease caused by poor soil, or is it something else?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ji nɔ ni kɛ kookoo hela baa loo nɔ kroko?

english: While bad soil can weaken plants, major cocoa diseases are caused by specific viruses, not by the soil itself.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ. Shi kookoo helai ni he hiaa lɛ Virus henɔ ko kɛbaa. Jeee kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mli

english: Does bad weather cause my cocoa leaves and trees to catch viral diseases?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii lɛ haa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ kookoo baai kɛ tsei anɔ?

english: Weather affects plant health, but viral diseases are caused by specific infectious viruses passed into the tree rather than rain or heat alone.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ saa tsei ahewalɛ he. Shi helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi komɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni tsɔɔ tsei amli lɛ amli. Yɛ nugbɔ loo latsaa kɛkɛ najiaŋ

english: How does a disease move from a sick cocoa tree to a healthy one on my farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni hela ajɛ cacao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Diseases move through transmission agencies called vectors, which are usually small insects that carry the virus from sick trees to healthy ones.
ga: Helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nibii ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ vectors lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni hiɛɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Can insects bring cocoa diseases from my neighbor's farm into my farm?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii baanyɛ ajie kookoo hela kɛjɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, insects act as vectors that travel between farms, carrying viruses from infected cocoa trees to healthy ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔnei ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔji ateŋ. Amɛhiɛɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What does it mean when you say an insect is a 'vector' for cocoa disease?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni otsɔɔ kɛ́ okɛɛ akɛ kooloi bibii ji mɛi ni ‘hiɛɔ’ kookoo hela lɛ?

english: A vector is a carrier, like an insect, that picks up a virus when feeding on a sick cocoa tree and transfers it to healthy trees.
ga: Vectors ji vectors, tamɔ kooloi bibii, ni holeɔ hela lɛ kɛji amɛye cacao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛkɛha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees get sick even if I keep the weeds down on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ yeɔ hela eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Even clean farms can get disease because insect vectors can fly or crawl in from elsewhere, carrying viruses directly to your cocoa trees.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli tse po baanyɛ aná hela. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baanyɛ afã loo amɛfo kɛjɛ hei krokomɛi. Amɛwoɔ hela lɛ kɛyaa o-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do commercial buyers know if my mangoes are sweet before they even cut them open?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni jarayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko ale kɛji mi mango lɛ ŋɔɔ dani mafo mli?

english: Buyers use a small optical testing tool that measures light passing through the fruit's juice to calculate its sugar content. This gives them a clear number showing how sweet the mango is without needing to slice it open.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi kɛ tsɔne bibioo ko ni akɛkaa kane ni susuɔ kane ni kpɛɔ kɛtsɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu sugar ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he akɔntaa. Enɛ haa onáa yibɔ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni mango lɛ ŋɔɔ ha ni ehe ehiaaa ni ofo mli bibii bibii.

english: Why do some of my harvested mangoes taste sour while others from the same tree taste very sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi mli edɔ lɛ? be mli ni mangoi krokomɛi Kɛjɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, eŋɔɔɔ waa?

english: Mangoes harvested too early have not had enough time on the tree to convert their natural starches into sugars. Allowing the fruit to mature fully on the tree ensures the sugar levels rise evenly across your crop.
ga: Mango ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ bɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsake amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ amɛwo sugar mli. Kɛ́ oha aduawai lɛ shwere yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha sugar lɛ aya hiɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: What is this 'Brix' measurement that fruit buyers keep talking about when pricing my harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘Brix’ susumɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ aduawai lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii beni amɛwoɔ mi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe jara lɛ?

english: Brix is a scientific scale used to measure the percentage of natural sugar in fruit juice. A higher Brix number means your fruit contains more sugar, which usually makes it higher quality and worth more money to buyers.
ga: Brix ji jeŋ nilee mli sɛkɛl ko ni akɛsusuɔ adebɔɔ mli sugars ni yɔɔ aduawai amli nu mli lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 100 he. Brix jara ni nɔ kwɔ tsɔɔ akɛ o-fruit lɛ yɛ sugar babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ anɔ.

english: Is there a portable tool I can use directly on my farm to check if my fruits are ready for market?
ga: Ani dɛŋdade ko yɛ ni akɛyaa he fɛɛ he ni manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni makwɛ kɛji miyibii lɛ efee klalo akɛ aya jara nɔ?

english: Yes, you can use a small, hand-held device called a refractometer. By squeezing a drop of juice onto its glass surface and looking through the eyepiece, it immediately shows you a reading of the fruit's sweetness level.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsɔne bibioo ko ni akɛyaa he fɛɛ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ refractometer lɛ atsu nii. Kɛtsɔ nu ni mli ewo muji ni akɛwoɔ glase lɛ nɔ ni oootsɔ tsɔne ni akɛkwɛɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ebaatsɔɔ bo bɔ ni aduawai lɛ ŋɔɔ ha amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why can't I just judge the sweetness of my fruit by looking at the skin color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madamɔ ehewolonɔ su nɔ makojo bɔ ni tso yibii ko ŋɔɔ ha lɛ?

english: Skin color can be misleading because some fruits turn yellow or red due to heat or sunlight exposure even when the inside is still immature and low in natural sugars.
ga: Hewolo nɔ su baanyɛ afee nɔ ni lakaa mɔ ejaakɛ aduawai komɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo etsuru yɛ dɔlɛ loo hulu la hewɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ loo lɛ eshɛko lolo ni adebɔɔ mli sugar faaa moŋ.

english: How can I know the right time to pick my pineapples so they are sweet enough for buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ?

english: Pineapples do not get any sweeter after you cut them from the plant. You must wait until the fruit's base starts turning golden yellow and gives off a rich fragrance, showing that maximum natural sugars have developed.
ga: Pineapples lɛ baafee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ fe tsutsu lɛ beni ofo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ he lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi tso yibii lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baabɔi shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ ni ebaaná ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli sugar lɛ etsɔ hiɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my orange trees drop some of their young fruits before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii dani amɛshɛɔ dalɛ he lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop extra fruit when they do not have enough water or nutrients to feed all of them. The tree naturally sheds weak fruits to protect the remaining ones so they can grow properly.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baawo yibii krokomɛi kɛ́ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ lɛ bɛ. Tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my watermelon vines turn yellow while the fruits are still expanding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi watermelon tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã lolo lɛ?

english: When watermelons grow rapidly, the plant redirects most of its food and water straight into the fruit. Yellow leaves mean the plant needs extra fertilizer or water to support both the leaves and the developing melon.
ga: Kɛ́ watermelon lɛ dara oya Tso lɛ tsɔɔ eniyenii kɛ enu lɛ mli babaoo kɛyaa aduawai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu kroko afata he koni eye ebua baai lɛ kɛ melon ni miiya hiɛ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my papayas turn soft after picking but still taste bland inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ papaya lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛji ajie lɛ shi ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo lɛ?

english: If papayas are plucked when completely green, their flesh may soften over time, but they cannot create new sugars once separated from the plant. Waiting until a tinge of yellow appears on the skin before picking ensures a sweet taste.
ga: Kɛji ojie papaya lɛ beni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ, Ehe mfoniri lɛ baanyɛ afee blɛoo yɛ be ni sa mli. Shi amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee sugar hee kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli pɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ko baaje kpo yɛ nɔ dani okɛ ŋmɔlɔ atsu nii koni onine ashɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my harvested cassava spoil so fast within just a few days of uprooting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mikpa lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots are dug out of the soil, their natural defense system breaks down rapidly when exposed to air. This causes internal discoloration and rot within two to three days unless processed quickly.
ga: Kɛji ajie ŋmei shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Amɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa mligbɛ su lɛ tsakeɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. ja atsu he nii oya

english: Why do so many different types of crops grow so easily on land in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Ghana benefits from a warm tropical climate and naturally fertile soils rich in nutrients, which allows many crops to establish strong roots and thrive with standard care.
ga: Ghana náa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ he sɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa kɛ hiɛdɔɔ ni sa.

english: What simple steps can I take to ensure any crop I plant on my land grows well?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Clearing weeds regularly, adding organic compost or manure to enrich the topsoil, and giving plants proper spacing will ensure they get enough nutrients, water, and sunlight to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ aya hiɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ana niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara.

english: Why do fruit crops yield better in some seasons compared to others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni aduɔ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ bei komɛi amli fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Crop yields depend heavily on seasonal weather patterns; sufficient rain during the growing phase encourages strong flower and fruit development, while sunny dry periods help the fruits ripen properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ be mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ waa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ haa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai yaa hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, be ni nu hɔmɔ kɛ hulutsoo be yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes plantains grow so well on our local farmland?
ga: Mɛni haa plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli hei lɛ?

english: Plantains thrive in warm temperatures and moist, well-draining soil, which are naturally present across many farming areas in Ghana.
ga: Plantains yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ okwaayeli hei babaoo yɛ Ghana.

english: Mango trees need full sunlight and deep, loose soil that does not hold stagnant water after heavy rains so that their long roots can grow deep.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ hia hulu ni eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli edɔ ni nu nyɛɛɛ ahi mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ koni shishifãi kakadaji lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: How long does a newly planted mango tree usually take before it produces fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango tso ni adu ehee lɛ woɔ yibii?

english: Grafted mango trees generally start producing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while trees grown directly from seeds can take 5 to 7 years to yield fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahe afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Can I plant plantains and mango trees together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ plantain kɛ mango tsei yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, plantains grow quickly and can provide useful shade and early harvests while young mango trees slowly mature over several years.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ yibiiwoo oya. Yɛ be mli ni mango tsei bibii lɛ baafee fiofio Edaa fiofio yɛ afii babaoo mli.

english: How can starting a small farm boost my family's income alongside my regular day job?
ga: Okwaafoi akuu bibioo ko shishijee Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo miweku lɛ shika kɛfata mibe fɛɛ nitsumɔ lɛ he?

english: Farming even a small piece of land yields extra produce that you can sell in local markets, giving you a steady secondary income to supplement your regular earnings.
ga: Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko po ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli Ewoɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi hu ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa shika ni ji enyɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni okɛfataa shika ni onáa daa lɛ he.

english: Can farming a small patch of fruit crops really help pay for my children's school fees?
ga: Tso yibii abɔɔ bibioo ko ni oooje shishi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni awo obii lɛ askul nyɔmɔ. Ani manyɛ maná minɔ̃ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, high-demand crops like plantains and mangoes sell consistently in local markets, providing reliable cash flow around harvest time to cover major expenses like school fees.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ataoɔ waa tamɔ plantains kɛ mango lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ daa yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei. Enɛ haa shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli koni akɛwo shika wuji tamɔ skul nyɔmɔwoo he nyɔmɔ.

english: Do I need to leave my current job to become a successful farmer?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makpa nitsumɔ ni mitsuɔ amrɔ nɛɛ koni matsɔ okwaafonyo ni yeɔ omanye?

english: No, you can start small on weekends or during off-hours with manageable crops like plantains and fruit trees that require periodic care rather than full-time daily attention.
ga: Dabi, obaanyɛ oje shishi bibioo. yɛ otsii lɛ anaagbee loo yɛ nitsumɔ be lɛ sɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ plantains kɛ aduawai tsei. ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli Yɛ be fɛɛ, daa gbi kwɛmɔ najiaŋ

english: If I see just two small caterpillars on my crops, can I leave them or will they multiply quickly?
ga: Kɛ mina ŋmeii bibii enyɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ Ani mishiɔ amɛ loo amɛbaashwere oya?

english: You should never leave them. Pests like caterpillars lay hundreds of eggs, and leaving just two can lead to hundreds more damaging your entire field within just three days.
ga: Esaaa akɛ oshɛrɛɔ amɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ. Ni kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ ohai abɔ krokomɛi yɛ gbii etɛ pɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops look healthy today, but get completely ruined by pests in just three days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ? Shi ani tsɛŋemɔ helai kpata lɛ hiɛ yɛ gbii etɛ pɛ mli?

english: Pest insects grow very fast and eat much more as they mature. A small group of hidden pests can hatch, multiply, and strip an entire field of leaves in just a few days if you do not catch them early.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyeɔ nii babaoo beni amɛdaraa lɛ. tsɛŋemɔ helai akuu bibioo ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ, amɛshwere, ni amɛshwie ŋmɔji amli baai muu fɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli. Kɛ́ omɔɔɔ amɛ oya lɛ,.

english: Are all green creatures I find on my crop leaves bad for my farm?
ga: Ani bɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni minaa yɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Not all of them are harmful. Some green insects are helpful because they eat bad pests, but green caterpillars and armyworms feed directly on your leaves. Watch if the creature is chewing your plant to know if it is a pest.
ga: Jeee amɛ fɛɛ amɛhe yɛ oshara. Sɛɛnamɔi yɛ kooloi bibii komɛi ahe ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ kooloi ni ehiii. Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛ asraafoi amli ŋmeii yeɔ obaai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛji bɔɔ nii miiye otsei lɛ koni ona kɛji amɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning a very dark green color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Very dark green leaves usually mean your crop has absorbed a lot of nitrogen from the soil or fertilizer. While this shows good growth, overly soft dark green leaves can sometimes attract pests like caterpillars.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ eŋɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ enɛ tsɔɔ dalɛ kpakpa moŋ. Shi bei komɛi lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni darako tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: How can I tell if my crops are healthy just by looking at the color of their leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ahe su pɛ nɔ?

english: Healthy crops typically have a vibrant green color. Pale yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nutrients or water, while very dark or strange spots can signal too much fertilizer or a disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii loo nu. yɛ be mli ni hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ loo nɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii loo hela babaoo he okadi.

english: How can I keep snakes away from my crop farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã onufui akabote mi tsei aŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Snakes hide in bushy weeds and under piles of wood or rubbish where they hunt for mice and frogs. Keep your farm clean, weed regularly, and clear surrounding bushes to remove their hiding places.
ga: Onufui kɛ amɛhe woɔ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli kɛ tsei loo jwɛi ni abua naa lɛ ashishi he ni amɛgbeɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Ha oŋmɔ lɛ mli atse Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli daa. ni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ koni ojie he ni ekɛ ehe ewo mli lɛ

english: Do snakes cause any direct damage to my crops?
ga: Ani onufui fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, snakes do not eat or harm your crops. They enter farms to hunt small animals like rats or frogs. However, you should wear protective boots and keep weeds low to prevent accidentally stepping on one.
ga: Dabi, onufui yeee oŋmɔshi nibii loo amɛyeee amɛ awui. Amɛboteɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛyagbe kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ owo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he ni oha jwɛi lɛ ahi shi koni okɛ onaji akashɛ nɔ yɛ oshara mli.

english: How often should I walk through my field to inspect my plants?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakwɛ tsei lɛ?

english: You should inspect your farm every two to three days. Regular checking helps you spot leaf changes or pest outbreaks early before they become too big to control.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbii enyɔ loo etɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni ooofee daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona baa tsakemɔi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ mra. Dani ebaatsɔ agbo tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ

english: Does clearing weeds around my crops help stop pests from spreading?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ebɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbɛ ashwã?

english: Yes, weeds serve as alternative food and shelter for pests. Clearing weeds prevents pests from jumping onto your main crops and makes it easier for you to see what is happening on your farm.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛ wɔɔhe kroko kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ to he ko lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaho yɛ onibii titrii lɛ anɔ. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ ooona nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What should I look out for when I walk through my crop field every few days?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ minyiɛ ŋmɔji amli daa gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Look for changes in leaf color, small holes chewed in leaves, droppings on plants, or insects hiding under leaves. Catching these signs early saves you money on control treatments.
ga: Taomɔ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe su mli, buji bibii ni jɛ baai ni ashɛre mli, tsei amli ŋmeii, loo kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi. Ni ooomɔ okadii nɛɛ mra Ebaaha okɛ shika akafite yɛ helatsamɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa yibii kpakpai baa.

english: Dry harmattan winds strip water from young cocoa leaves faster than their shallow roots can draw water from the soil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or putting mulch around the tree bases helps lock in moisture.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai bibii amli oya fe shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo mulch ni aduɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' where leaves used to grow on the stem; these buds should always point upward toward the sky so the shoots grow straight up and roots develop properly underground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni be ko ni eho lɛ baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ ni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when weather gets too hot or when plants experience sudden dry spells. Without enough moisture or mild temperatures, pollination fails and the flower dies off instead of forming a tomato.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo be trukaa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa loo hulutsoo be ni esaaa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii ni fɔfɔi lɛ gboi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee tomatoi.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot strips specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on maize to build up in the ground, leading to weaker harvests over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ajieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do I need to make big soil mounds before planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ agbo ko dani adu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft, and deep soil to expand easily. Making high mounds loosens the earth so the tubers can grow long and thick without hitting hard, compacted soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni aaafee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkaná shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkafee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus that thrives in cool, damp shade. Pruning overhead branches to let sunlight and air circulate dries out the pods and keeps the disease away.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ni sumɔɔ nu ni shwereɔ yɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ, ni mli edɔ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ yiteŋ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni helai akabote mli.

english: It is best to water early in the morning because afternoon heat evaporates water before the roots can drink it, and water droplets left on leaves in strong sun can scorch the plant.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei.

english: Why should I cut off the old lower leaves of my oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ?

english: Pruning off old, dead fronds allows the palm tree to send more energy and nutrients directly to growing fruit bunches, while also making it much easier to harvest the oil palm.
ga: Baai ni egbɔ ni egboi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa aduawai akui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmei fɔ ni akpaa lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their vegetable crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that shields soil from harsh sun, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to thoroughly plow and clear my land before planting rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii jogbaŋŋ dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Proper land preparation loosens the soil so roots can grow easily, helps water spread evenly, and destroys existing weeds so your young plants do not have to fight for nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni efiteɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ momo lɛ koni ehe ehiaaa ni otsei bibii lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers ask us to level our rice fields flat before we sow seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ biɔ ni wɔfee ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani wɔdu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Leveling the land prevents water from pooling too deeply in lower spots and drying out in higher spots, ensuring all rice plants get equal water and grow at the same speed.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekafee ekome tsɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ni ekagbi yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa nine shɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ, ni edaa oya.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them by hand across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ minine baagbɛ amɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Row planting gives every crop enough space, air, and sunlight to grow strong, while making it much easier for you to walk through to weed and harvest without stepping on plants.
ga: Row dumɔ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ oootsɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe ni okpa ni onyiɛɛɛ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does this new rice variety produce so many stems from just one seed compared to my old seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ ŋmãa henɔ hee nɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu kome mli kɛ akɛtoɔ midumɔwui momo lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Improved rice seeds are bred to tiller, meaning one plant branches into many stalks. This creates a denser field that chokes out weeds and yields far more rice at harvest.
ga: Aduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ akɛ tillers. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso kome baatse niji babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi lɛ baa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa babaoo kɛji akpa.

english: Why are some improved rice plants shorter than the traditional tall rice we used to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi yɛ kuku fe blema ŋmãa kakadaŋŋ ni wɔduɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Shorter rice plants focus their food and energy into growing thick heads of grain rather than tall leaves, which stops the heavy plants from falling over in strong winds or heavy rain.
ga: Omɔ tsei kukuji lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo nɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni miida ni amɛyitsei lɛ mli wa fe baai ni kɛlɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa tsei akagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli.

english: Why do my rice plants need standing water during their early growth stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi yɛ eshishijee be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Water helps keep the soil moist for the roots and acts as a natural shield that smothers weeds, allowing the young rice to establish itself quickly.
ga: Nu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha shishifãi lɛ, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni haaa jwɛi akabote mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why does harvesting modern rice varieties require much more time and labor than my traditional crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔ hee ni akpaa lɛ heɔ be kɛ nitsumɔ babaoo fe mi blema ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties yield significantly more grain per acre, resulting in a much heavier harvest that often requires extra hands or specialized tools to gather before it spoils.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa babaoo yɛ acre kome mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ ni tsii kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ biɔ ni akɛ niji krɛdɛɛi loo nibii krɛdɛɛi abua naa dani efite.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start harvesting my rice crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa ŋmɔmɔ shishi?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains across the field turn a bright golden-yellow and the lower stalks start to dry out.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 etsɔ shika tsuru ni mli tse. ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ jeɔ shishi egbiɔ

english: Why is my family having a harder time harvesting our rice manually with sickles like we used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa kɛha miweku lɛ akɛ amɛkɛ ŋmãa baakpa ŋmãa tamɔ bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ?

english: Modern high-yielding rice grows much denser and produces heavier panicles than older crop types, making old hand-harvesting tools slow and exhausting for small family groups.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ daa waa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni tsii fe tsei ni etsɛ. Enɛ haa blema nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa wekui bibii lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui.

english: What happens if I delay harvesting my rice after it has matured in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa lɛ kpamɔ be sɛɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature rice in the field too long causes the grains to dry out and break easily during milling, while birds, rain, and insects can destroy a large part of your yield.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ agbi ni ebaakumɔ oya yɛ be mli ni oooŋɔ ŋmãa lɛ, yɛ be mli ni okpoi, nugbɔ, kɛ kooloi baanyɛ afite oŋmãa lɛ mli babaoo.

english: How do I know when my rice is ready to harvest so I do not waste grains?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa koni okafite dumɔwui?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the seed heads turn a golden yellow color. If you wait too long, the grains dry out completely and shatter onto the soil during cutting, causing heavy losses.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Kɛji omɛ be kakadaŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kwraa ni amɛgbalaɔ bibii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni afoɔ lɛ. ni kɛ fitemɔi ni tsii baa

english: Why do extension officers advise threshing harvested rice onto a clean basin or tarpaulin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ashɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ awo tsɛnsi loo tarp ni mli tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Threshing rice onto a basin or tarpaulin keeps soil, stones, and sand out of your grain. Clean grain fetches a much higher market price and prevents you from losing loose seeds in the dirt during harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ wo tsɛnsi loo tarp mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni muji, tɛi, kɛ ŋã akawo ŋmãa lɛ mli muji. Dumɔwui ni he tse lɛ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa baa ni etsĩɔ bo gbɛ koni okafite dumɔwui ni etse amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do my harvested grains turn moldy and spoil after I store them in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ beni mikɛto kotokui amli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains turn moldy in storage bags when they are bagged before drying properly in the sun. Any extra moisture left in the seed gets trapped inside the bag, causing mold to grow and rot the crop.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ amli kɛ́ akɛwo kotoku mli dani agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni eshwɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ baatsɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii daa ni ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rain has washed the plant food away. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea restores the green color and supports healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ejie tsei lɛ amli niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my rice plants fall flat on the ground just when the grains are filling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ be mli ni ŋmãa eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Crop falling (lodging) happens when stalks grow too tall and weak from excess nitrogen fertilizer or when strong winds and rain push down heavy grain heads. Proper planting distance and balanced fertilizer use keep stems strong.
ga: Tso lɛ shigbeemɔ (lodging) baa kɛji tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwere tsɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hewɔ. Aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ tsiɔ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii kɛbaa shi lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do flower buds fall off my pepper plants without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from severe heat, lack of water, or damage from tiny pests. Regular watering during dry spells helps the plant hold onto flowers until they set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii efite amɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together lead to a poor harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmaa ni ehiii baa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce very small yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why does allowing weeds to grow in my field make my crop yield small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than standard crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight intended for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the nutrients it needs to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to plow and loosen the soil before putting seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii dani adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil lets air and water enter easily and makes it simple for young crop roots to spread deep into the ground, leading to faster seed germination and stronger root systems.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu boteɔ mli mlɛo. ni ehaa tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu waa.

english: How can I easily keep track to know if my farm business is making a profit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ bɔ ni miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ he sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ ha?

english: You track profit by writing down every small expense—like seeds, land preparation, fertilizer, and labor—and subtracting that total from the money you receive after selling your harvest. If your sales money is higher than your total expenses, you made a profit.
ga: Okwɛɔ sɛɛnamɔi ni onáa lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ shika bibii fɛɛ ni ofiteɔ tamɔ dumɔwui, shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nitsumɔ nɔ lɛ ni oŋmalaa lɛ nɔ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ojieɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shika ni onáa beni ohɔ̃ɔ onibii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ shika ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ fe shika fɛɛ ni ofite lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ obaanyɛ oná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the middle outward when the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as the main nutrient for leaf growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the rich green color so the plant can grow strong ears.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni eha tsei lɛ aná toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their root nodules. When the plant harvest is complete, that natural plant food remains in the soil to feed nitrogen-heavy crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbe naa lɛ Tse niyenii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha tsei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cover the bare dirt around my pepper crops with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like an umbrella that keeps soil moisture from evaporating in the heat, stops weeds from taking over, and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekafo kɛji edɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaha nɔ. ni oha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once the fruit bunch becomes big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantains have a broad, shallow root system that does not anchor deeply into the soil. As the heavy bunch matures, the top becomes unbalanced, so supporting the stem with a sturdy bamboo pole or wooden prop is necessary to keep it upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni kuu lɛ eda kwraa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ ejaaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni mli wa afi tso lɛ sɛɛ koni ehi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to erect long wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves toward full sunlight to manufacture food, which is then sent down to build the underground tuber. Staking keeps leaves off the hot damp soil where diseases spread, allowing the tuber to grow much larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ lɛ kɛyaa shi koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ he ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo kwraa

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves dry up and drop when the hot harmattan wind starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry spells to protect themselves from losing too much water. Providing shade trees like plantains or forest trees shades the cocoa canopy, maintaining humidity and preventing severe heat stress.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo baa kookoo ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he haomɔ he.

english: Why do my crop seedlings grow tall and skinny without producing good yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, crops compete with one another for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room for root expansion and leaf growth.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots and allowing harmful soil fungi to multiply. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the central leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves (the funnel) to eat young plant tissue. Applying recommended organic control agents like neem leaf extract or targeted pest treatments early protects the growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (cones) koni amɛye tsei bibii lɛ ahe fãji lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni akɛyeɔ wala nɔ tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo mra be mli kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋaa. Ebaabu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers dry up and fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when extreme heat or improper watering stresses the plant, preventing proper pollination. Consistent soil moisture, mulching, and planting during optimal seasons prevent blossom drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni esaaa ha tso lɛ miihao. Enɛ haa anyɛɛɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ, ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baatsi fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa.

english: Can I use natural household ingredients like garlic, ginger, and hot pepper to protect my crops from insects?
ga: Minyɛ mikɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shia tamɔ galiki, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsu nii. Koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe?

english: Yes, strong-smelling spices like garlic, ginger, and chili contain natural compounds that irritate and repel insects. When ground and mixed with water, they create a safe, homemade spray that deters pests from feeding on crop leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni ŋɔɔ waa tamɔ galiki, ginger, kɛ chili yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni woɔ mlifu ni eshwieɔ kooloi. Kɛji akɛ atswa ni akɛ nu futu mli lɛ Amɛfeɔ shĩa tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anaa.

english: Will spraying hot pepper or garlic liquid directly on my crops burn or damage the leaves?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo galiki nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã loo ebaafite baai lɛ?

english: If the mixture is too strong, concentrated pepper or garlic can scorch tender young leaves. It is best to dilute the liquid heavily with water and test it on a few leaves before spraying your entire crop.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper loo galiki ni mli ewo muji lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ nu baawo nu lɛ mli waa. Ni kaa lɛ okwɛ yɛ baai fioo komɛi anɔ dani okɛ tsofa afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: How often do I need to reapply a homemade garlic and pepper spray on my farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni makɛ mi-garlic kɛ pepper spray ni mifee yɛ shia lɛ awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ?

english: Natural mixtures wash off easily when it rains and break down under direct sunlight. You should reapply them every 5 to 7 days, or immediately after a heavy rainfall, to keep insects away.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hoɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ daa gbii 5 kɛyashi 7, loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ nɔŋŋ, koni okɛshwie kooloi bibii.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean the plant is stressed from lack of water or a shortage of nitrogen in the soil. It can also be caused by tiny insects sucking the sap from the undersides of the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu loo nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai ashishi lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛba.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high, when the soil is too dry, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce small, thin tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil makes cassava focus all its energy on growing lush leaves above ground rather than storing food in the roots. Adding potassium helps the plant develop larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Potassium ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa, ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my crops more heavily when the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ́ amɛbɔi fɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers and young buds produce sweet nectar and soft, nutrient-rich tissues that attract insects looking for energy. Pests naturally target these tender parts of the plant first.
ga: Fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nu mli nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni gbalaa kooloi bibii ni taoɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ tutuaa tsei lɛ ahe nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, wet conditions. Pruning dense branches and clearing shade allows sunlight to dry the pods and prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How can I protect my stored dried maize from weevils without buying expensive chemical powders?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni miheee tsofa-kɛ-ŋma powda ni jara wa?

english: Dry your maize grains until they are completely hard, then store them in airtight containers or hermetic bags to suffocate pests. Mixing dry chili powder or clean wood ash with the grains also prevents weevils from laying eggs.
ga: Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli. Kɛ́ akɛ chili powder ni egbi loo tso sũ ni he tse futu dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ awo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my harvested pepper fruits rot so quickly after I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested peppers rot fast if they are picked during wet morning hours, stored in airtight plastic bags without airflow, or bruised during picking, which lets fungal spores enter through the skin.
ga: Pepper ni akpa lɛ baafite oya kɛji akɛ akpa yɛ leebi ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ mli. Okɛto plastic kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ akabote mli lɛ mli. loo ekpɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct heat and strong sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting temporary crops like plantains provides shade and preserves soil moisture so the young cocoa can survive its early stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni aaashi loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni aná hulutsoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni kookoo bibioo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to generate energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground, exposing them to light and preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enaa la ni etsiɔ tso helai anaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore plant health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the exact same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and keeps it rich.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be ni Seasons lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua sũ lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so that roots can suck them up. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the crop roots or waste the fertilizer because the plant cannot absorb it without moisture.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite ejaakɛ tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli.

english: What causes small holes and green waste inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni jwɛi eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a destructive caterpillar that eats maize leaves from the inside out. Inspecting your field early and using recommended neem sprays or insecticides stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra ni okɛ neem spray loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ atsu nii. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting up and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that spread plant viruses. Controlling these pests early with soap-water sprays or insecticides prevents the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining, cutting off oxygen to the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. ni nu lɛ ejeee kpo Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ faaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around a main plantain tree, they steal food and water from the main stem. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong stems, resulting in larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ kɛbɔle Dumɔwui titrii babaoo tsɔ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat is too severe or when the plant experiences sudden drought. Keeping the soil evenly damp and planting at the right time of year helps flowers turn into full tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo ba loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil is low in nitrogen or that excessive rain has washed the nutrients away. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green so the plant can grow big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eha tso lɛ toi agbo.

english: How do I know if the caterpillars eating my maize funnel are Fall Armyworms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii ni yeɔ mi-corn funnel lɛ ji asraafoi a-fall worms?

english: Fall Armyworms hide deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant, leaving ragged holes and light-brown droppings that look like sawdust. If you look closely at their head, you will see a white inverted 'Y' pattern.
ga: Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. Eshiɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ yɛ esɛɛ. Kɛ okwɛ amɛyitsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ Obaana ‘Y’ ni atsake lɛ yɛŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Swapping maize with beans, groundnuts, or cowpeas restores nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ kɛya. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and burn easily under full sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain next to them creates a cool canopy that protects the seedlings while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei ni yɔɔ ekãa ni daa oya yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around them in heavy soil during rainy periods. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets extra water drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ amɛhe. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu kroko ni fa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why do I need to put wooden tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out high off the ground to catch sunlight efficiently. Staking keeps the leaves away from wet soil diseases and allows the plant to produce much larger tubers underneath.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Staking haa baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ bulbs ni da kwraa fe shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant's sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these pests early with soaps or recommended sprays keeps the leaves flat and broad.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ samla loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmli atse.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni amɛtsɔko anɔkwa aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from very high temperatures, irregular watering, or attacks by small insects like thrips. Consistent watering and mulching the soil around the roots helps prevent flower drop.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa mli baa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep root systems that are already adapted to grab water and soil nutrients faster than domestic crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crop a fair chance to take up food and sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe shia tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa onibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kɛ hulu la fioo.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to scatter chemical fertilizer on my farm right before a big rainfall?
