ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo kɛha mi akɛ magbɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash away fertilizer off the soil surface into drainage paths before crop roots can drink it in. Applying fertilizer when the ground is damp, or burying it slightly near the plant base, ensures the crops actually feed on it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nu homɔ gbɛi amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo afu lɛ fioo yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees drop to the ground without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage turn into pods due to limited soil nutrients, lack of tiny insect pollinators, or water stress.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ ŋmeii yɛ niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kplukai bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa loo nu mli haomɔ ni bɛ

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow healthy green leaves and strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting when they are hidden under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni akɛ amɛ tee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, cracks appear in the soil near the stem base, or the crop reaches 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Gbɛjegbɛi jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Aloo nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hiɔ shi nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain trees roll up and droop during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni nu lɛ egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up and droop to reduce their surface area, which helps the plant conserve moisture and protect itself from hot, dry winds.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi he.

english: What causes small holes and sawdust-like dirt in the center of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leaf funnel of the corn plant and feeds on the tender young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai amli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ji bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field help my maize crop grow better the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, naturally fertilizing the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease in the soil that enters the roots and blocks the plant's internal water-carrying tubes, causing it to collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni boteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni etsĩɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. ha efo mli

english: Why is it risky to sow my corn seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a dry hot spell, which can dry out the soil and kill the newly germinated seeds before the main rains fully settle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ asɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni efite dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that stay near the surface, making the heavy plant top-heavy and easy for wind or heavy soil to push over unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii baanyɛ atsɔ mli. Ja nɔ ko ni akɛ tso fee lɛ yɛ.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal essential soil nutrients and fertilizer directly away from your crop's roots, leaving your crop starved.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: Why should I spray weedkiller on my field right when I am starting land preparation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mibɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ pɛ?

english: Spraying at the start clears away aggressive weeds before you plant, stopping them from stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your young seeds when they first sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe jwɛi ni wa lɛ dani odu. ni etsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ odumɔwui bibii lɛ amli lɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ.

english: You should wait until the rains are steady and the soil stays moist for several days in a row, rather than planting after the very first shower, so your seeds do not dry up in hot soil.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ba shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo du lɛ ngɛ kekleekle nu ɔ se. Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray chemical treatments on my crops during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot midday sun causes liquid sprays to evaporate before they work, and the water droplets on the leaves can act like magnifying glasses that scorch and burn your crops.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani etsuɔ ​​nii. Ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo, ni eshãa onibii ni odu lɛ ni eshãa.

english: Why do extension officers advise spraying cocoa trees just as young pods begin to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ jɛmɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afɔse kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ tsofa kɛjɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying early protects tender young cocoa pods from major pests like mirids (capsids) and fungal diseases like black pod before they can infect and destroy your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mra be mli Ebuɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji tamɔ mirids (capsids) kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛbote oŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛfite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen or is too waterlogged; adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving water drainage will help restore green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge stems and leaves above ground, but only yield small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ha shishifãi bibii Pɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the plant uses all its energy to grow leaves and foliage instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ baai amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: What causes my pepper flowers to dry up and fall off before fruits start forming?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ?

english: Flower drop is often caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or tiny insect pests like thrips that attack the flower stalks before pollination occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni ejaaa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa fɔfɔii ahe dani pollination baa.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpea or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetable crops with dried grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Mulching with dry grass keeps the soil cool under hot weather, traps moisture so you water less often, and stops weeds from taking over your garden bed.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaha obɔɔ lɛ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers lose their leaves shortly after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Transplant shock makes young suckers drop old leaves while establishing new roots; trimming the leaves before planting reduces water loss and speeds up recovery.
ga: Transplant shock haa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ baai momoi lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi heei. Kɛ́ afo baai lɛ amli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why should I pour fertilizer on both the left and right sides of my crop instead of putting it all in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɛku kɛ ninejurɔ fɛɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ fɛɛ baawo he kome lɛ?

english: Spreading fertilizer evenly on both sides of the crop allows roots on all sides to gather food equally, encouraging strong, balanced growth and preventing root damage caused by high concentrations of fertilizer in one spot.
ga: Kɛ́ aja ŋmɔshi nibii amli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ tso lɛ afãi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni jɛ afãi fɛɛ lɛ ni amɛbuaa niyenii anaa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ewoɔ dalɛ ni mli wa ni ja lɛ he hewalɛ ni etsiɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ he kome lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Should I pour liquid fertilizer directly onto the main stem of my cassava plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔse nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mawo mi-cassava tso lɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, liquid fertilizer should be poured into the soil around the plant a short distance from the stem. Pouring directly on the stem can scorch tender plant tissue and cause rotting.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ afɔse nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii awo sũ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli, ni ekɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ fãji lɛ ni eha egbo.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to divide my fertilizer into three separate applications instead of applying it all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mija ŋmɔshi nibii amli miwo nibii etɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ fɛɛ baawo mli shikome lɛ

english: Crops absorb nutrients slowly over time. Splitting fertilizer into three doses matches the plant's food needs at key growth stages, preventing rain from washing away unused nutrients.
ga: Tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ blɛoo. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mlijaa etɛ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ yɛ edalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli lɛ kpãa gbee. Etsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekajie niyenii mli nibii ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ.

english: How many times during the growing season do I need to apply nutrients to my maize field for best yield?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mikɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Maize usually performs best when given nutrients three times: once during planting to help root establishment, once when the stalks grow rapidly, and once during flowering to support healthy grain development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ aha lɛ niyenii shii etɛ: klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara; Shikome beni tso lɛ tso lɛ daa oya kɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli koni eye ebua ni ewaje dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cover my fertilizer with soil right after I finish pouring it around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Covering fertilizer with a thin layer of soil prevents the sun from evaporating the nitrogen into the air and keeps rain from washing the plant food away down the slope.
ga: Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ Ebaatsi hulu la naa koni ekajie nitrogen kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekashwie tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ gɔŋji lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my young cocoa trees with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, or mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot afternoons, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from competing with your crops for food.
ga: Mulching loo mulching baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akayeɔ niyenii.

english: Why do my young crop leaves wilt and turn yellow after I pour a strong chemical fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ tsofa ni mli wa ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical fertilizer too close to the plant creates a salt burn on the root system, making it difficult for the crop to drink water and causing leaves to yellow and wilt.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ babaoo wo tso lɛ he tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei ashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaanu nu. ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni egbo.

english: How far away from my plant's stem should I pour the fertilizer into the dirt?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo sũ lɛ mli kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer should be poured roughly 10 to 15 centimeters (about a hand-span) away from the stem, as the active feeding roots expand outward from the plant rather than sitting directly underneath the main trunk.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse ŋmɔshi nibii aaafee sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15 kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi (aaafee nine kome lɛɛmɔ) ejaakɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ baajɛ tso lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaata tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What happens to the fertilizer I apply if heavy pouring rain falls on my farm immediately after?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ no sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Heavy pouring rain can wash unburied fertilizer down the farm slope into streams. Lightly digging and covering the fertilizer with soil keeps it secured in place for root absorption.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni afuuu lɛ ahe kɛya faai amli. Kɛ́ atsa ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni akɛ sũ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to pour water on my vegetable crops early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the crops can absorb moisture before the sun gets strong, preventing high water loss from evaporation and keeping roots cool.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu la lɛ mli awa. Etsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Can I just take seeds from the healthiest cocoa pod on my farm to plant a new field?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ kookoo yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: Even if a pod looks healthy, its seeds may have been pollinated by weaker trees nearby, resulting in low-yielding offspring. Getting certified hybrid seeds from approved nurseries ensures your new trees inherit strong disease resistance and high yields.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ Shi ekolɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmeii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji seshibii ni afɔɔ amɛ fioo. Kɛ́ onine shɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli nɔ kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha otsei heei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my own harvest like I do with maize and vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ tamɔ bɔ ni mifeɔ kɛ ŋmãa kɛ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tree crops like cocoa lose their quality over generations when saved on the farm. Specialty seed gardens produce hybrid seeds under controlled conditions to guarantee fast growth and heavy pod production.
ga: Tsei tamɔ kookoo lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmɔji amli. Dumɔwui abɔɔi krɛdɛɛi woɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome yɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli koni amɛha amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Where is the best place for me to get reliable cocoa seeds for planting my new land?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mana kookoo ŋmeii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ?

english: You should get certified seeds or seedlings directly from the Seed Production Division of COCOBOD or recognized extension centers, as their seeds are tested for high performance and survival.
ga: Esa akɛ onine ashɛ dumɔwui loo dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli nɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ COCOBOD dumɔwui afeemɔ nitsumɔhe loo sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ he ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, aka dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ koni ana bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ amɛhaa kɛ bɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi amɛhaa.

english: If a cocoa tree carries a lot of pods, will seeds from that tree automatically produce high-yielding trees?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo Ani dumɔwui ni jɛ nakai tso lɛ mli lɛ baaha tso ni woɔ yibii babaoo aba lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not necessarily. The pods on a mother tree show how well that tree performed, but the seeds inside carry mixed traits from surrounding trees, meaning many of the new seedlings won't produce as well as the parent tree.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa. Shi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni akɛfutu. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui heei Tsei babaoo wooo yibii tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do some cocoa trees take up to five years to produce pods while others start much earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi heɔ afii enumɔ dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi jeɔ shishi mra kwraa lɛ?

english: Older traditional seed varieties take 4 to 5 years to bear fruit, whereas modern hybrid varieties distributed by extension officers are bred to start producing pods in just 2 to 3 years.
ga: Shishijee dumɔwui ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid henɔi ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ hɔ̃ɔ lɛ koni amɛje pods feemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli.

english: Can I plant seeds from a pod that had black pod disease if I only pick the seeds that look clean?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ dumɔwui kɛjɛ pods ni black pod hela yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛji mihala dumɔwui ni he tse pɛ?

english: No, microscopic fungal spores from the diseased pod skin can easily contaminate the seeds, causing your new seedlings to rot early or carry the disease into your new farm.
ga: Dabi, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni jɛɔ pod hewolo ni hela emɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite dumɔwui lɛ oya. Enɛ haa odumɔwui heei lɛ fiteɔ oya loo ekɛ helai baa oŋmɔ hee lɛ mli.

english: Should I dry my cocoa seeds in the sun before planting them in polybags?
ga: Ani esa akɛ magbi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dani mawo amɛ yɛ poly kotokui amli?

english: No, cocoa seeds are moist seeds that die if they dry out. Unlike corn or beans, cocoa seeds must be planted while wet immediately after opening the pod.
ga: Dabi, kookoo yibii ji dumɔwui ni mli efɔ ni baagboi kɛji amɛgbi. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, esa akɛ adu kookoo ŋmãa lɛ be mli ni edɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji agbele naa.

english: How soon after opening a cocoa pod do I need to plant the seeds?
ga: Beni agbele kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ Te esa akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ oya aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa seeds should be planted within 3 to 4 days after removing them from the pod. Delaying longer causes the seeds to lose viability quickly or spoil.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cocoa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ. Be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akafee nɔ ko oya loo amɛbaafite.

english: How can I tell if a fresh cocoa seed is good enough to sprout into a strong seedling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo yibii lɛ etsɔ ehe bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni etsɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Good seeds feel plump, firm, and fully formed inside their white mucilage coating. Small, flat, or discolored seeds should be discarded because they produce weak seedlings.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ mli tse, amɛhe wa, ni amɛfee amɛhe kwraa yɛ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ futafuta ni tamɔ mucilaginous mli. Esa akɛ ashɛrɛ dumɔwui bibii, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni amɛhe su etsake lɛ ashwie ejaakɛ ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot tolerate direct sunlight. They need temporary shade trees like plantains to protect them from burning sun while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ŋmɛɛɛ amɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: How long will it take for the new cocoa variety I received to start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani kookoo henɔ hee ni minine shɛ nɔ lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: When planted and cared for properly, improved cocoa varieties in Ghana will enter production in about 3 years.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, kokoo henɔi ni atsake amɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ baaje nitsumɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii etɛ mli.

english: Am I allowed to ask agricultural officers questions about new crop seeds before planting them?
ga: Ani aŋmɛ mi gbɛ ni mibi okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ tsei ahe dumɔwui heei ahe saji dani madu amɛ?

english: Yes, farmers are encouraged to ask extension officers about the growth habits, yield times, and care requirements of any new crop variety brought to their community.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ okwaafoi abi extension nitsulɔi lɛ nibii ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe. Nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ be kɛ taomɔ nii ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei akwɛmɔ he. ni akɛbaa amɛ akutso lɛ mli lɛ

english: How do I know if a new cocoa variety being brought to my area is good for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo henɔ hee ni ajie lɛ kpo yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You can ask the officers bringing the planting materials to explain how long the variety takes to yield and how it performs compared to older types.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi mɔ ni kɛ dumɔ nii lɛ baa lɛ ni etsɔɔ be ni nɛkɛ tso nɛɛ heɔ dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa kɛ akɛto tso ni etsɛ fe tsutsu lɛ he.

english: Why do officers advise cutting down and clearing cocoa trees when disease affects them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ, kɛ́ hela ba lɛ, esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei ni afolɔ amɛmli lɛ?

english: Cutting and clearing diseased cocoa trees prevents the infection from spreading to healthy trees across your farm and neighboring farms.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo ni ojie amɛ lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli.

english: Can a cocoa tree grow back after it has been cut down because of disease?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ beni afo amɛ yɛ hela hewɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, once a diseased cocoa tree is cleared, fresh shoots can sprout from the stump or roots and potentially regrow into productive trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ajie kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ shishifãi heei hu baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi loo shishifã lɛ mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni amɛtsɔ tso ni woɔ yibii.

english: Is it safe for me to let a cocoa tree regrow after clearing it due to sickness?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahã cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ beni mijie amɛ yɛ hela hewɔ?

english: Many farmers experiment with letting cleared trees regrow to see if the new shoots remain healthy, but it requires careful observation to make sure the disease does not return.
ga: Okwaafoi babaoo kaa amɛhe amɛkwɛɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ni ajie amɛ lɛ ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ kɛji ŋmeii heei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shi ehe miihia ni akwɛ mɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni hela lɛ akaku esɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What should I do first if a disease attacks part of my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee klɛŋklɛŋ kɛji hela lɛ ba mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The standard practice is to cut down and clear the affected crops to stop the sickness from spreading, then monitor the area for replanting or regrowth.
ga: Nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ ji ni afolɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni ajie amɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. No sɛɛ lɛ, kwɛmɔ he ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ loo aduɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to visit other farmers' fields in my community?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mayasara okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ aŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Visiting other farms helps you observe how different crops respond to diseases, see how neighbors handle crop clearing, and learn from their trial methods.
ga: Okwaafoi krokomɛi saramɔ Ebaaye ebua bo ni okadi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi Te ofeɔ tɛŋŋ otsuɔ hela he nii? Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni akutsoŋbii kɛ tsei ni ajieɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa. ni amɛkase nii kɛjɛ amɛ kaa gbɛi lɛ amli

english: Does proper field management really make a difference in when my cocoa starts yielding?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha srɔtofeemɔ aba beni mi-kookoo lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, doing the field preparation and crop care properly ensures your cocoa trees reach full production right on schedule at the 3-year mark.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ baaha o-cacao tsei lɛ ashɛ yibiiwoo he yɛ be ni ato lɛ mli yɛ afii 3 mli.

english: What happens if I try out new farming methods that my neighbors are testing?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mika okwaayeli gbɛ hee ko ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ miika lɛ mikwɛ hu?

english: Observing and trying out successful methods used by neighboring farmers allows you to find practical solutions, such as managing regrowth after crop clearing.
ga: Gbɛi ni okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ omanyeyeli mli lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ kaa. Ye obua bo ni ona tsabaai ni hi, tamɔ bɔ ni oookwɛ dalɛ hee nɔ yɛ tsei ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow strong and stay green. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the upper leaves to protect new growth, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛtsi shweremɔ hee naa. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Groundnuts and beans are special plants that pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize helps feed the soil naturally, making the maize grow better without needing as much expensive commercial fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni jarayeli ŋmãa ni jara wa waa he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and curl during the hot afternoon even when the ground isn't dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbiko yɛ?

english: Cassava plants curl and droop their leaves during intense sunshine to reduce the amount of surface exposed to the sun, preventing them from losing too much water. Once the heat cools down in the evening, the leaves usually bounce back.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu la lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ amɛhiɛ lɛ shi. Tsi nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ naa. Kɛ́ latsaa lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa sɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme midday heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Providing light shade and consistent watering helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shade ni mli tse kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow lots of big leaves but leave me with small yams at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ baai wuji waa shi kɛ́ akpa amɛ lɛ, amɛshiɔ baai bibii lɛ?

english: When yam plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing heavy green leaves above ground instead of sending stored food down to build large tubers under the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ maa baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni eeekɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ amaje shi koni efee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that spread out wide near the surface instead of digging deep into the ground. Mounding extra soil around the base and supporting heavy fruit bunches with wooden props helps anchor them.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ kroko ni akɛbaabɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛfiɔ amɛhe shi.

english: Why do pests like the fall armyworm attack my young maize instead of the old plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworm lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ moŋ fe tsei momo lɛ?

english: Young maize plants have soft, tender leaves that are easy for caterpillars to chew and digest. Inspecting your farm early allows you to catch the pests before they eat the growing tip of the young plant.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmeii nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii oya. Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ dani amɛyeɔ tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why do my tomato plants get dark spots and rot when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When tomatoes are planted too close, air cannot move freely between them, keeping the leaves wet from dew or rain. Fungi thrive in damp, crowded spots, causing leaves and fruit to rot.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tomatoi ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ aya tomatoi lɛ ateŋ oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli. Fungus lɛ shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ haa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do I need to wait for the first good rains before putting my maize seeds in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds need steady moisture to wake up and start sprouting roots. Planting seeds in dry soil leaves them vulnerable to burning in the hot dirt or getting eaten by birds and ants before the rain comes.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛte shi ni amɛje shishi amɛshishifãi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ oshara mli akɛ amɛbaashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo okpoi kɛ ŋmeii aye bo dani nugbɔ lɛ aba.

english: How does covering my vegetable garden soil with dry grass or leaves help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds so they can't grow. It also traps moisture in the dirt so your crop roots stay cool and wet longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la akashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ hu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to grow food mainly to feed my family or focus on crops to sell at the market?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ niyenii titri koni mikɛha miweku lɛ loo mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: A balanced farm does both: planting staple food crops like cassava or plantains ensures your family is always fed without buying food, while allocating space for cash crops provides income for household needs.
ga: Okwaafoi ni ja lɛ feɔ nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ: Niyenii nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa oweku lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe niyenii. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni akɛhaa kɛha shika helɛtemɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa shiabii náa shika.

english: How can I safely test a new crop variety without risking my family's food supply if it fails?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka tsei srɔtoi heei lɛ makwɛ shweshweeshwe ni mikɛ miweku lɛ niyenii ni amɛnáa lɛ wooo oshara mli kɛji amɛyeee omanye?

english: You can plant the new crop on a small test portion of your land first while keeping your main crops on the rest; this allows you to see how it performs in your soil before making bigger changes.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii heei yɛ kaa he bibioo ko. yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be mli ni okwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ona bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ofee tsakemɔi wuji.

english: Can I use traditional farming methods passed down by our elders alongside new techniques from extension officers?
ga: Abaakɛ kusum mli okwaayeli gbɛi ni jɛ wɔ onukpai lɛ aŋɔɔ lɛ baatsu nii kɛfata ŋaa heei ahe. Ani abaanyɛ ana kɛjɛ hiɛyaa he nitsulɔ lɛ dɛŋ?

english: Yes, blending traditional practices like intercropping with modern techniques like using improved seeds often produces the strongest crops because it combines local experience with updated science.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni akɛ blema nifeemɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai tamɔ dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baafata he. Bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii ni mli wa fe fɛɛ. Ejaakɛ ekɛ maŋ lɛ mli niiashikpamɔ kɛ jeŋ nilee ni atsake lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: Why do cassava plants stay green and alive during the long dry season when my other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli beni miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ gboi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants have deep taproots that search far underground for water, and they shed their leaves during dry spells to conserve moisture until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni taoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen food in the soil or are getting waterlogged; adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, too little water in the soil, or a lack of nutrients needed for fruiting.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo ni bɛ

english: Why do my tomato plants look limp and wilted in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During intense sun, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil, so the plant temporarily wilts to protect itself until it cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛyashi be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if my damaged crop is suffering from a disease or if insects are eating it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ loo kooloi eye amɛ?

english: Insects usually leave visible signs like chewed edges, holes, or insects present on leaves, whereas diseases often cause yellow spots, rotting stems, or wilting without chewed leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shiɔ okadii ni anaa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli, bu, loo kooloi ni jeɔ kpo yɛ baai anɔ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela lɛ haa mɔ he feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. tso ni egbo loo tso ni egbo ni baai ni ashɛreɔ bɛ mli

english: Local traditional seeds can be saved for next season, but store-bought hybrid seeds should not be reused because their offspring will produce much smaller harvests.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ ato koni akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli. Shi esaaa akɛ akɛ hybrid dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ. Ejaakɛ amɛshwiei lɛ baawo bii fioo kwraa.

english: Cassava thrives in loose, well-drained soil where root tubers can expand easily; it will rot if planted in heavy clay or swampy land where water sits for long periods.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ alɛɛ mli mlɛo. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nu ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaafite.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, strong sunlight because their delicate leaves burn easily. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava to block harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ kookoo tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Bɔni afee ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to plant cocoa on my land in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time to plant cocoa is at the start of the major rainy season, usually around April or May. Planting during the rains ensures the soil has plenty of moisture for the young roots to establish before the dry Harmattan season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ April loo May mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi bibii aba dani Harmattan be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baashɛ.

english: How long will it take after I plant my cocoa before the trees start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ sɛɛ beni midu kookoo dani tso lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take 3 to 5 years to start producing pods, whereas improved hybrid varieties can begin fruiting within 2 to 3 years if they are properly weeded, shaded, and cared for.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hybrid cocoa henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ ajie jwɛi jogbaŋŋ, awo amɛ shade ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa plants when setting up a new field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-kookoo tsei lɛ amli beni mikɛ he hee miito he gbɛjianɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees should generally be spaced about 3 meters by 3 meters (10 feet by 10 feet) apart. Proper spacing ensures the trees have enough room to spread their branches and roots without competing for sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee mitai 3 x mitai 3 (naji 10 x naji 10). He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛnáa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛniji kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akaŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off some branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess, dead, or diseased branches so light and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. This simple practice encourages healthy flower production and reduces the buildup of humidity that causes diseases.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baa shi.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds around my young cocoa trees?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Young cocoa farms should be weeded every 2 to 3 months, particularly during the rainy season. Keeping weeds under control prevents them from stealing nutrients, water, and light from your young cocoa trees.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii amli daa nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Kɛ́ oye jwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ la ni yɔɔ o-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: This rots are usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, dark, and damp conditions. You can prevent it by clearing weeds, pruning thick branches to let sunlight in, and applying recommended fungicides.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ gangrene nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ, duŋ, kɛ hei ni edɔ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni hulu la abote mli. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii.

english: What causes small dark patches and dried-up shoots on my cocoa branches?
ga: Mɛni kɛ okadii diji bibii lɛ baa? Ni ŋmeii ni egbi ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo nine lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: This damage is caused by mirids (capsids), which are tiny insects that suck sap from young cocoa stems and pods. Spraying approved insecticides during peak mirid seasons helps protect your trees from this destruction.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji mirids (capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii. No shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu otsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ he.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain and cassava on the same farm with my young cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cocoa bibioo lɛ?

english: Yes, planting food crops like plantain or cocoyam with young cocoa is recommended. The food crops provide necessary shade for the cocoa, generate quick food and income for your family, and reduce weed growth while the cocoa matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ kookoo ni mli jɔ atsu nii ni akɛdu niyenii tamɔ plantain loo kookoo. Niyenii tsei haa kookoo lɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. Bɔɔ shika oya kɛha weku lɛ ni oha jwɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ aba shi be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land has good soil for growing healthy cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark, rich in decayed organic leaves, and drains water well without turning into a swamp. If water sits on top of the soil like a lagoon after heavy rain, it may not be suitable for cocoa.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋ, ni eyɛ baai ni fiteɔ babaoo. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ ŋshɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Ekolɛ esaaa kɛha kookoo

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients from the soil or when roots stay flooded in water for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bote nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and air helps keep the pods dry and reduces the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni helai aba shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that feed on the sap and transmit viruses. Managing these pests early prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛkɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkafee shwilafo.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is insufficient potassium in the soil. Consistent watering and mulching help keep the plant stable enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same soil drains specific nutrients and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the ground. Alternating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: When too many suckers grow together, they fight for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Leaving only one main plant and one strong follower sucker ensures the plant has enough energy to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo tsɔ ekomefeemɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Tso titri kome kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔ sucker ni he wa kome ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does putting chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my plants damage them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ tsei lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that draw moisture out of the plant's stem and roots if placed too close, causing chemical burns. Fertilizer should always be applied in a circle a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baajie nu kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo amɛhe tsɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ tsofa shãa baa Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce food, which is transferred down to expand the underground tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi koni akɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excess standing water starves the roots of oxygen and encourages rot organisms; planting on raised ridges or mounds helps water drain away safely.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ewoɔ fitemɔ he hewalɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to plant my seeds after the early rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Early rains often only wet the top surface. Sowing is safer when moisture penetrates about a hand's depth into the soil so seeds do not dry out and die if the rains pause for a few days.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, leebi nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Dumɔ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ bote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee inchi kome. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, mɛ gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do some cassava plants have dark reddish-brown stems while others have light green stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii henɔi komɛi yɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii komɛi yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Stem color is simply a natural genetic physical trait that differs between cassava varieties. While local varieties often have darker stems and some improved varieties have green ones, stem color alone does not mean one variety will yield more food than another.
ga: Stem su ji adebɔɔ mli su ko kɛkɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ cassava henɔi lɛ ateŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ fɔɔ tsei ni tsuɔ waa moŋ, shi tsei komɛi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji eŋɔli moŋ. Shi tso lɛ yitso lɛ su pɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ henɔ kome baaha niyenii babaoo fe ekroko.

english: Leaves curling and changing color is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant varieties and removing infected plants early stops the sickness from spreading across your field.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ su ni etsake lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and need protection from direct sunlight and harsh heat. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving forest trees provides the shade and moisture young cocoa needs until its roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛtaoɔ hebuu kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni ashi yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ aahu kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to clear space and stake my yam vines on tall poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie he ko ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei awo tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines produce bigger tubers when their leaves catch maximum sunlight up off the ground. Staking keeps leaves dry, prevents fungal diseases from the soil, and allows the vine to focus energy on growing large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ amɛbaai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa ni oha wain tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ ama bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat as a natural defence to save water and keep from drying out. When temperatures cool down in the evening or when rain falls, the leaves unroll to normal shape.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni akɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi gbimɔ naa. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ loo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Baai lɛ baaje kpo ni amɛfee nɔ ni yɔɔ daa.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their blossoms before any peppers grow out of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ dani pepper lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as very dry soil, excessive heat, or a lack of plant nutrients in the soil. Regular watering and adding compost or animal manure helps flowers turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo tso mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ nu daa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas helps make the soil richer for my maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plant roots decompose after harvest, they release natural plant food into the soil for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛjieɔ tso niyenii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato roots stay thin like pencil sticks instead of swelling into fat tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato shishifãi lɛ ji pensil bibii yɛ bulbs ni efuu ni eyɛ fɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes need loose, soft soil in raised ridges or mounds so their roots can expand easily. Hard ground or putting too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant grow lots of green leaves instead of thick tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná baai eŋɔli babaoo yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why does my plantain tree give very small fruit bunches when many young shoots grow around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from the main plant. Pruning away extra shoots so only two or three remain allows the plant to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ebɔle he Kɛjɛ dumɔwu kome mli lɛ, ejuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni tsei 2 loo 3 pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I wait to plant my maize seeds instead of planting right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ ni adu ŋmãa dumɔwui moŋ fe ni ooodu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can dry out and kill newly germinated seeds. Waiting until the rains become steady ensures your seeds have enough moisture to survive and establish strong root systems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ odumɔwui lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because strong, direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa from heat stress and retains soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning pale yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizers like urea helps restore green color and boosts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is mature enough to harvest, and why do the roots rot if I wait too long?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei eda bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa? Ni mɛni hewɔ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, around 9 to 12 months after planting. Leaving roots in the ground too long—especially during heavy rains—causes waterlogging, which starves the roots of air and causes rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei akwɛ̃. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa nu shwieɔ shi Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the soft inner leaf whorls of young corn. Checking plants early and spraying organic extracts like neem oil helps stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ahe baai bibii. Tsei amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli, tamɔ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa tsei nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Too many extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main mother plantain tree. Removing most suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones ensures the mother plant produces large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Ayɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ babaoo tsɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛju nu ni amɛdu niyenii kɛjɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ajie ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso nyɛ lɛ awo plantain ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden stakes to support my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mikɛfi mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight to make food for growing tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground where diseases spread, allowing maximum sunlight reach to boost tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ. Ehaa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ haa yitso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and drop off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience severe heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. Regular watering, mulching to retain soil moisture, and providing light shade during peak afternoon heat prevent flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa daa Mulching koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli. Tsi fɔfɔii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi

english: Why does my land yield less maize when I plant it in the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows corn pests to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like whiteflies or thrips feeding under the leaves and carrying plant viruses. Using insecticidal soaps or neem sprays reduces insect numbers and protects new foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛhiɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem spray tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi ayibɔ aba shi, ni ebaabu tsei heei ahe.

english: Why does lowland rice grow better when there is standing water around its roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Lowland rice thrives in shallow standing water because water suppresses weeds that compete for nutrients while keeping the soil soft for root growth. Managing the water depth ensures the plants stay nourished without drowning.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli ejaakɛ nu lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ lɛ anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Nu lɛ mlibotemɔ nɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni amɛgbooo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a key plant nutrient, or that excessive rain is drowning the roots and preventing them from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ yeɔ niyenii Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water on your farm for too long, the roots drown and rot-causing organisms in the soil attack them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small young pods before they can grow into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra young pods if they do not have enough water or nutrients to support them all, or if pests like capsids damage the stems.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baajie ŋmeii bibii kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi tamɔ capsids fite tso lɛ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high, when there is a lack of water, or when tiny insects attack the delicate flowers before fruits can form.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ, kɛji nu bɛ, loo kɛji kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani aduawai baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees take so long to produce fruit when I leave all the young shoots growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves more energy for the main stem to grow fast and produce fruit quickly.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ada oya ni ewo yibii oya koni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo aha.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die suddenly even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by a soil disease called bacterial wilt, which enters the plant roots and blocks the water tubes inside the stem, causing the leaves to dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ bacterial wilt lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni boteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli ni etsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni egbi

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than the crops I carefully plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are hardy wild plants that are very good at grabbing sunlight, soil water, and nutrients faster than farm crops, which allows them to outgrow your crops rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni ŋmɛɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and bent when I plant them in hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe kɛ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil or mounds so the tuber can expand downwards easily. Hard or stony ground squeezes the growing yam, making it short and misshapen.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo gɔŋji bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ miimiɔ sweet potatoes ni miida lɛ. ha efee kuku ni ehiɛ afee nɔ ni ejaaa

english: Why should I change the type of crop I plant on my land every season instead of planting maize every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa afi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu ŋmãa daa afi lɛ

english: Planting different crops each season keeps the soil rich and breaks the life cycle of pests and diseases that like to feed on one specific crop year after year.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei srɔtoi yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye tso henɔ kome niyenii afi fɛɛ afi lɛ ashihilɛ mli.

english: Why is it best for me to sow my seeds right at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Sowing at the start of the rains gives seeds steady moisture to sprout and helps young roots grow deep before any unexpected dry spell arrives.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃, ni ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ dani hɔmɔ be ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni afee ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni baabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it important to leave proper space between my crops when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough resources to grow big and produce a good yield.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks essential nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or appropriate nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ otso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How can I check if my soil is rich and healthy without using expensive equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii ni ehi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well without becoming swampy, and contains living organisms like earthworms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nubu bɛ mli. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, shady, and overcrowded farms. Pruning excess branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds helps reduce moisture and stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu lɛ abote mli, ni ojie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi, ni ebaatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: How do crop pests travel so fast from my neighbor's farm to mine?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai fãa gbɛ oya kɛjɛɔ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pests can fly, get carried by wind, or hitch a ride on farm tools, boots, and animals. Keeping your farm borders clean and washing tools after work helps prevent pest invasions.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ afã, kɔɔyɔɔ atswa amɛ kɛya, loo amɛtara ŋmɔ mli nibii, atadei, kɛ kooloi anɔ. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe tse ni ofɔ onitsumɔ dadei ahe yɛ nitsumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: Is it safe for me to plant maize and cassava together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works very well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, giving the cassava time and space to spread out and mature later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa dumɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa oya. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ naa be kɛ he ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ni edaa yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my harvested cassava tubers taste sweet while others turn out bitter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi ŋɔɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava contains natural chemical compounds that cause bitterness, which increase when the plant is stressed by severe drought or when growing specific bitter varieties that require processing before eating.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni haa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ cassava mli. Enɛ yaa hiɛ kɛ́ tsei yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa shishi. Aloo kɛ́ ookwɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ pɔtɛɛ ko ni esa akɛ atsu he nii dani aye lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers during severe heat and dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Plants drop their flowers during extreme heat stress to conserve energy and water. Providing shade, watering at the base, and covering the soil keeps the roots cool so flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ dɔlɛ be mli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Shading, nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ, kɛ mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: This practice is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket over the soil, keeping it cool, preventing soil water from evaporating quickly, and suppressing weed growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants burning and curling up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or banana next to them acts like a natural umbrella, keeping the soil cool and moist while protecting the cocoa leaves until the tree is strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ebuɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ mli waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is hungry for nitrogen. As the plant grows, it pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top, signalling that it is time to add manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ, baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: How does planting cassava stems slanting in the ground help them grow better than planting them straight up?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni adu ni atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni adu lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Slanting cassava stems shallowly under the soil encourages the plant to produce roots close to the surface, which spread out and develop into larger, thicker tuberous roots compared to planting straight down.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi wuji ni mli tse kɛ akɛtoɔ tsei ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Will growing cowpeas together in the same field as my maize steal food from the maize?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛaadu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: No, cowpeas actually help feed the maize. Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen from the air and puts it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa ŋmãa niyenii. Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before turning into pepper fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛtsɔɔ pepper aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When pepper plants experience excessive heat and dry conditions, they drop their flowers to save water and protect themselves from dying. Regular watering during hot spells helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo latsaa ni fe nine kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli lɛ, Amɛbaashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: How can I tell if the holes in my cabbage leaves are caused by insects or by a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo tso hela ko ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage baa lɛ mli lɛ ba?

english: Insects physically eat the leaf tissue, leaving clear holes with clean or chewed edges. Diseases usually show up as discolored brown or yellow spots, mold patches, or wilting before the leaf tissue breaks down.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji, ni amɛshiɔ bu ni mli tse kɛ amɛhe ni he tse loo ni amɛyeɔ. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni etsake. Fungal fãji loo egboi dani baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ fiteɔ

english: Why does putting dry leaves around the base of my tomato plants make them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi fata tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tomato lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, keeps the soil moist by stopping water from evaporating in the sun. It also keeps the roots cool, prevents weeds, and feeds the soil as it decays.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni ehaaa efo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Tsi jwɛi lɛ anaa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Removing extra side branches directs the plant's food and energy into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on extra stems and leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeefite hewalɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce thick green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen or receives excessive rain early on, the yam plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of transferring food down into the tubers.
