ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ babaoo mra lɛ, Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baa shi kɛyaa ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when I remove the weeds every few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mishwieɔ jwɛi lɛ daa otsii fioo komɛi moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast roots that drink water and steal soil nutrients long before your main crop can get them. Removing weeds while they are still tiny prevents them from competing with your crops during their critical early growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya, ni shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baanyɛ aná. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkɛ onibii akaye akaŋ yɛ mra be mli dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the ground too soaked for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and twisting into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or thrips hiding under the leaves. They drink the plant's sap and can leave behind viruses that cause the leaves to grow deformed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshi helai ni haa baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get too stressed, especially from high heat, lack of water, or dry winds. The plant lets the flowers fall to save its remaining energy to stay alive until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao tsɔ. Titri lɛ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ, tsei haa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast during the rainy season. It thrives when there is too much shade, damp air, or poor weed control around the trees.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. ni ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, loo jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ yɛ ni esa akɛ akudɔ. Tso lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves make food, which is sent down into the soil to build big, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots fight over the same water and soil food, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. Spacing seeds properly lets every plant get its full share to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛfaŋnɔ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda waa.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are special plants that pull natural nitrogen out of the air and put it back into the ground. Rotating them with maize restores soil fertility naturally without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmã tsu nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Is it safe to plant cassava and maize together on the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly. By the time the cassava expands and needs space, the maize is already harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo No mli lɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni ehe hiaa he ko. Agbɛnɛ abaanyɛ akpa ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Watering in the afternoon sun wastes water because the hot heat evaporates it before the plant roots can drink it. Morning watering lets the plant soak up water and stay cool through the hot afternoon.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli lɛ fiteɔ nu ejaakɛ la ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why should I mix poultry manure or cow dung into my soil weeks before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ kooloi loo tsina ŋmeii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli otsii babaoo dani madu lɛ?

english: Fresh manure is too strong and hot for young seed roots and can burn them. Mixing it into the soil early allows it to decompose, cool down, and release rich nutrients that feed the crop smoothly once planted.
ga: Nuŋtsɔ ŋmɔŋ mli wa ni edɔ tsɔ kɛha dumɔwui bibii ashishifãi ni ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mra Enɛ baaha egbɛ eshwa, edɔ, ni ejie niyenii kpakpai ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji adu lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants bend and fall over whenever a strong wind blows right before it starts raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa dani nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Heavy winds push hard against tall crops with shallow roots, causing them to bend or snap—a condition called lodging. Mounding extra soil around the base of the plant stems as they grow helps anchor them firmly in the ground against wind gusts.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa tsei kakadaji ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ he eko. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi loo efoɔ—shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ. Shikpɔŋ kroko ni okɛtoɔ he lɛ Tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ amɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shiŋŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ he.

english: How can I prevent strong winds from breaking the branches of my cassava and plantain crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekafite mi yucca kɛ plantain tsei lɛ aniji lɛ?

english: You can plant windbreaks, which are lines of sturdy trees or tall grasses along the boundary of your farmland. These natural barriers slow down powerful winds before they hit your fragile crops, preventing stem breakage.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔne, ni ji tsei ni wa loo jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔ he lɛ, yɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbogboi nɛɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa oya dani etswaa onibii ni waaa lɛ. Etsiɔ tso lɛ fãmɔ naa

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off when a strong wind and rainstorm sweeps through my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tswa kɛtsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Strong winds physically shake fragile blossoms off the branches, while heavy rain can wash away the pollen required to turn flowers into fruit. Planting shade trees or wind barriers helps protect delicate flowers during stormy weather.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie fɔfɔi ni he hiaa koni akɛtsake fɔfɔi lɛ aduawai lɛ kɛya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo kɔɔyɔɔ tsiɔ hei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why does the rich brown topsoil on my farm wash away into nearby streams during heavy rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bare soil gets detached and swept away by fast-moving rainwater runoff, leading to soil erosion. Planting cover crops like cowpeas or making ridges across slopes helps slow down runoff and keep fertile topsoil in your field.
ga: Atse shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli ni nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ baa Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni ooodu loo ŋmeii ni ooofee yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ ahi oŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable crops turn yellow and rot after rainwater collects around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ nu ebua ehe naa yɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to survive just like humans do. When rainwater pools around roots without draining, it suffocates them, leading to root rot and yellow leaves. Digging simple drainage ditches allows excess water to flow away safely.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni nu bɛ mli lɛ ebaaha okɛ ohe awo mli Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nifeemɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ji nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Is natural rainwater better for growing my crops than pumping water from a nearby lake or river?
ga: Ani nugbɔ nu ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ fe nu ni mikɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ loo faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater is naturally soft, free of harmful minerals, and picks up nitrogen from the air as it falls, which gives crops a quick boost in leaf growth. While river water is good for irrigation, rain provides free nutrients that river water often lacks.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli. Ebɛ shika ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ekɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi beni egbeeɔ shi lɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya. Eyɛ mli akɛ faa lɛ mli nu lɛ hi kɛha nu shwiemɔ moŋ, shi nugbɔ hu haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bei pii lɛ faa lɛ mli nu lɛ bɛ ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa and vegetable plants curl up tightly when strong winds begin to blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɔi tswaa lɛ?

english: Strong wind pulls moisture out of plant leaves rapidly. Plants curl their leaves to shrink the exposed surface area, which helps them retain internal water and prevent drying out during windy weather.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ afee bibioo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open after a heavy rain following a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When thirsty plants suddenly take in a massive amount of rainwater, the inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to crack. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulch prevents this sudden surge.
ga: Kɛ tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ ná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mligbalamɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ mulch baakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ ŋshɔkei ni baa trukaa nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings flatten to the ground when hit by wind and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have tender stems that cannot hold up against heavy water droplets and strong wind currents. Using protective palm fronds or shade netting over seedling beds protects fragile young plants until their stems toughen up.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ tso ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ahe tsei ni buɔ mɔ he loo shade netting tsu nii yɛ dumɔwui lɛ asaji lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: What should I do to save my crops right after a violent wind and rain storm passes over my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mahere miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswa kɛtsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Inspect your farm immediately to clear blocked water channels, gently prop up leaning plants before the soil hardens, and trim broken branches so diseases do not enter the damaged parts of your crops.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ojie nu gbɛi fɛɛ ni atsĩ naa lɛ. Fi tsei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ blɛoo dani shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ais. ni amɛfolɔ tsei niji ni ekumɔ lɛ koni helai akabote ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before they produce corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛwoɔ abele lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the plant is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer. The plant pulls nutrients from its lower leaves to feed new upper growth, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the same plot of land two seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei enyɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pests and diseases that target tomatoes stay hidden in the soil after harvest. Planting tomatoes in the same spot immediately feeds those pests, whereas changing to a crop like maize breaks their lifecycle.
ga: Akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tomato nɔ lɛ teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛji amɛtsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshihilɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ akpa.

english: How does planting groundnuts make my farm soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants work with helpful tiny organisms in the soil to pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the ground to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanut tso lɛ kɛ bɔɔ nii bibii tsuɔ nii. Ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ejie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tsei gboi lɛ, nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's way of protecting itself from losing water. By shrinking the leaf area exposed to the hot sun, the maize traps moisture inside to survive until the evening.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ he. Abɛi lɛ baato ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli koni ehi shi kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains flood the soil for long periods, the roots choke from lack of air and decay rapidly underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ ni amɛgboɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Giving plants too much rich nitrogen fertilizer encourages them to build big stem and leaf 'bodies' instead of focusing on 'reproduction', which is what creates flowers and pepper fruits.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ baawo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛná ‘gbɔmɔtsei’ wuji, ŋmeii kɛ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ‘Fɔmɔ’, ni ji nɔ ni haa fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yibii baa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds stop my cassava from growing big tubers under the soil?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmei agboi ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anaa aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that act like thieves, stealing water and fertilizer nutrients from the soil before your cassava roots can drink them up.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yeɔ amɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers from my plantain plant base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Every new shoot or sucker drinks water and food from the main plant. Keeping too many suckers forces the mother plant to share food, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Tso bibioo loo tso bibioo fɛɛ tso bibioo nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii lɛ aha. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stem without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Very high temperatures damage tomato pollen so it cannot fertilize the flower. Unfertilized flowers die and fall off the stem without producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ fɔfɔi afɔ bii. Fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growth stage helps restore the green color and boosts development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he mra yɛ amɛdalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha shweremɔ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help make my soil better for next season's crop?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When the plant roots and leaves decompose after harvest, they leave behind natural fertilizer that nourishes crops planted after them.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural defense mechanism to conserve water during dry weather. Once the rains return, the plant shoots out new leaves and continues storing food in its underground roots.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛha ŋmei koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekɛ niyenii ato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus. Watering consistently around the root zone and mulching the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and helps fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ mli, nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua ni aduawai lɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that scorch easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Is it better to water my crop field early in the morning or during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo hulutsoo be mli shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before heat causes fast evaporation. Afternoon watering wastes water through evaporation and can cause heat stress to hot roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa shwane mli lɛ baafite nu yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shishifãi ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes inside the center of my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the central growing funnel of maize plants. Applying organic neem leaf extracts or recommended pesticides directly into the funnel early in the morning controls them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni teɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaakudɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit plant viruses. Spraying the leaves with a mild soapy water solution or neem oil helps destroy the insects and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni hiɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efite kooloi bibii ni ebaatsi baai heei adalɛ naa.

english: How do I know when my watermelon crop is mature and ready to harvest without cutting it open?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni watermelon lɛ eda ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ ni mifolɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: A watermelon is ripe when the spot touching the ground turns from white to a creamy yellow, and the small curly vine tendril closest to the fruit stem dries up and turns brown.
ga: Watermelon lɛ egbɔ kɛji he ni eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eyɛŋ kɛbatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ aduawai lɛ ashishifã lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting stems even when stored inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally come out of dormancy after a rest period, especially in warm and humid air. Keeping the storage barn cool, shaded, and well-ventilated helps delay sprouting and keeps tubers fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ oha oshĩa lɛ mli jɔ, eyɛ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu bote mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ shi ni eye ebua ni bulb lɛ ahi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves turn pale yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant make food and turn healthy green again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I apply fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer away from your farm into nearby streams before your crops' roots can drink it, wasting your money and leaving the plants unfed.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu. Eji oshika ni ofiteɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts on my farm help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and groundnuts take natural food from the air and store it in their roots. When they die, that food stays in the soil and acts as a free fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. kɛ amɛgboi lɛ Nakai niyenii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves that burn easily and lose water quickly in direct heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects them until their roots grow deep enough to survive the hot weather.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baashɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam leaves need to climb high to catch sunlight and make food for the tubers underground. Keeping the leaves off the hot ground also stops them from rotting during heavy rains.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, no hu yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: No, planting too close makes the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This causes thin, weak stalks with small or empty cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack from swelling roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni efuu lɛ amli.

english: Why are holes suddenly appearing in the tender center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu ko eba trukaa yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ a-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Holes in the inner leaves are usually caused by tiny caterpillars called Fall Armyworms that hide inside the funnel of the plant during the day and eat the soft leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ fall armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by sudden dry heat or a lack of water, because the plant does not have enough strength to nourish the fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo ni egbi trukaa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaahã aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I dig my planting ridges across a hill slope instead of straight up and down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo dumɔwui ashishi yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ moŋ fe ni mafo ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Building ridges across the slope creates small mud walls that stop rainwater from running fast down the hill, preventing it from carrying away your fertile topsoil and seeds.
ga: Kɛ́ afee ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ gbogbo bibioo ko baa. No baatsi nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haaa ekɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ afɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or floods the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe loo ekɛ nu ewo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows maize pests, like the Fall Armyworm, to build up. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: How do groundnut plants help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Te ŋmei tso baafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts have special tiny bumps on their roots containing bacteria that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food, leaving the soil richer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Peanuts yɛ button bibii. Muawai krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi kwɔlɔ ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo, shi amɛyitsei bibii nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing branches and leaves above ground instead of storing food underground in large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ wa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ niji kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ zugba a sisi ngɛ ngmɔkɔ nguahi a mi.

english: Why do many of the small flowers fall off my cocoa trees without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers, but heavy dropping usually happens when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks proper soil nutrients, or lacks tiny insects like midges needed for pollination.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni tsii baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miigba tsei anaa. Niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni he hiaa kɛha pollination lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield when I plant the seeds close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant room to build strong roots and produce bigger food.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa shishifãi ni mli wa waa baa ni amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo.

english: Curled leaves are typically caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees easily fall over during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots carrying heavy bunches. Microscopic worms called nematodes often damage the roots underground, making the plant weak and easy for wind to push over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni amɛyi obɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ ewoɔ lɛ oya.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil gets too dry and then too wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni edɔ tsɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and dry out easily. They need temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava to protect them until they mature and grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Koni abu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe awa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves toward the sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light for better food production and preventing fungal leaf diseases, which helps the tubers underground grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛ baai lɛ awo la mli koni niyenii kpakpa aba. ni atsĩ baai hela ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize farm turning light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nutrients they need to grow green and leafy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha otso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ baai.

english: Why does adding dried animal manure to my farm make my vegetables grow better than planting in plain dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi fata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa mi-aduawai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural nutrients, improves the soil's structure, and helps ground hold water longer during dry hot days, making nutrients readily available to your crops.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii aya hiɛ ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa onibii lɛ yeɔ

english: Weeds are fast-growing competitors that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the soil nutrients and space they need to develop properly.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yaa hiɛ oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ ana niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same nutrients and water, resulting in small bunches. Leaving only two or three strong shoots ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ Plantain kome Plantain muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Planting cassava cuttings about one meter apart gives each plant enough space underground to form big roots without competing with neighboring plants for nutrients and moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei niji ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji baa. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when tiny insects attack the blossoms. Regular morning watering and protecting plants from pests help the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa leebi ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or mites that spread plant viruses. Spraying the leaves with neem oil or appropriate farm remedies stops these pests from damaging new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo ŋmɔ mli tsofa ni sa shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai heei ni eda lɛ.

english: It is best to wait until the rains become consistent with two or three heavy downpours that soak the soil deep down, rather than planting right after the very first light rain, so your seeds do not germinate and then dry up.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli woɔ wu. Mohu ɔ, duɔ amlɔ nɔuu ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se konɛ o duwu ɔmɛ nɛ a ko puɛ nɛ lɔ ɔ se ɔ, a ko gbi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which acts as plant food for healthy growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ tso niyenii kɛha hewalɛ dalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating your maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts vital nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ abɛi lɛ mli lɛ baafite. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil for days, the water fills up all the air spaces, causing the roots to drown, soft-rot, and decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Nu lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Plantain roots grow close to the surface and can be weakened by tiny soil pests called nematodes. When the fruit bunch gets heavy and the soil becomes wet and loose, strong winds easily push the tree over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ daa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ shwiili lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ tswaa tsei amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the plant's sap and spread plant viruses. Using safe neem oil sprays or controlling these insects early prevents leaf distortion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ akɛ neem mu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra lɛ tsu nii Ebaatsi baai lɛ ashishijee naa.

english: Why are small insects eating holes in my cowpea pods, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Insects called pod-borers lay eggs on the flowers and young pods because they are soft and nutrient-rich. Spraying organic neem leaf extract or recommended biological sprays during flowering protects the pods before damage occurs.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ pod borers lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ pod bibii anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ neem tso lɛ mli loo tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii lɛ ahe dani nɔ ko abafite.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my crops when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛji bibii kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil food your crops need. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a strong start without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when they lack water. Extreme heat damages the flower's pollen, preventing fruit from forming, so keeping the soil moist with mulch can help.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu bɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baafite pollen lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua.

english: Why do small green cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Koni egbo ni etsɔ ediŋŋ dani eda lɛ?

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt' or fungal infection. Cocoa trees naturally drop pods they cannot feed if they lack nutrients or water, but black pod disease can also attack young pods during wet weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘cherelle wilt’ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye nii kɛji niyenii loo nu bɛ amɛmli. Shi black pod hela lɛ baanyɛ atutua pod bibii lɛ hu yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: How do I know that my yam tubers are fully mature and ready for harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam tubers tell you they are mature when the leaves above ground turn yellow and the vines dry up and die back. This shows the plant has finished sending all its energy down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ amɛdara beni baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wain tso lɛ gĩɔ ni egboɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa eyitso lɛ naa.

english: If I use water from a river near a galamsey site to irrigate my vegetables, why are the leaves turning yellow and dying?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ Galamsey lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii kɛwo aduawai anɔ nu. Mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Water affected by illegal mining often contains dangerous chemicals and heavy metals like mercury. These substances poison the plant's root system, preventing it from absorbing nutrients properly and causing the leaves to yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ dade ni tsii, tamɔ mercury yɛ nu ni shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ saa he lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ji tsofa fɔŋ kɛha tsei shishifãi. Enɛ haa mɔ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do the roots of my cassava plants rot when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for long periods, it drowns the roots and creates a wet environment where harmful fungi thrive and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu baaha shishifãi lɛ afee nu ni eha shihilɛ ni mli efɔ. he ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa saplings dry up and die when I plant them in open sunlight without plantain trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ ni dumɔwui ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and bright sunlight. Fast-growing shade crops like plantains act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity young cocoa trees need to survive their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ shade tsei ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots compete for the same nutrients, water, and underground space. Proper spacing allows roots enough room to expand into large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he kome lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Why does my maize stay short and yellowish while my neighbor's maize is tall and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowish, stunted maize usually lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow leaves and stems. Adding organic manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant grow tall and deep green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa bibioo mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm has become too tired to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ edu ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Tired soil shows signs like slow crop growth, pale leaves, and low harvest yields despite good rain. Planting leguminous crops like cowpeas or allowing the land to rest helps restore lost soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ okadii tamɔ tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, baai ni tsuɔ, kɛ ŋmaa ni baa shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ kpo. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve water. By curling its leaves, the plant exposes less surface area to the sun, reducing water loss through evaporation until the weather cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ hiɛ he ko ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ faaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when plants experience water stress. Consistent watering during dry spells keeps the plant calm enough to retain its blossoms and produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ dioo bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ekwɛ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Upward leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites. As they feed on the fresh leaf juices, they damage the leaf tissues, causing them to curl up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛnuɔ baa mli nu hee Amɛfiteɔ baa mli fãji. ha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Weeds grow much faster than most crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in harsh sunlight. They require fast-growing shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees around them to shield their leaves and keep the soil moist during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Koni abu baai lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up and show light yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems recommended by agricultural officers prevents this problem.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ adumɔ taakɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ wo ŋaa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: How deep should I bury my maize seeds into the soil when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep (roughly two finger-joints deep). Planting too deep stops the seedling from reaching sunlight, while planting too shallow leaves seeds exposed to birds and hot sun.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5 (aaafee inchi 2) mli. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okpoi kɛ hulu lɛ aná dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience high heat, prolonged dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Consistent watering and balanced feeding encourage the flowers to stay on the plant and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has lost its strength and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔi lɛ miihe ajɔ amɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Soil loses strength when crops grow slowly, leaves turn pale green or yellow early, and yields stay small despite good rains. Adding organic compost or balanced fertilizer replaces the nutrients crops take from the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa fiofio lɛ. Baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ oya. ni nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baafee bibioo lolo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye niyenii ni tso lɛ náa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize farm?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ ko yɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ duɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they enrich the soil with natural fertilizer that helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni edara waa lɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Yams rot quickly when stored in hot, poorly ventilated places or if bruised during digging. Storing undamaged yams in a cool, well-shaded, and airy yam barn prevents fungal rot and extends their storage life.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ ekpɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmeii ni efiteee lɛ ato ŋmeii atsu ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii akafite ni ehaa shĩa lɛ wala sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: How do I know if my vegetable garden is getting too much water after heavy rains?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji nu babaoo miihe o-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Too much water causes plant leaves to turn yellow, droop, and soften because roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Creating simple drainage channels lets excess water flow away from the root zone.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afee Enɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Saving seeds from hybrid crop harvests is not recommended because seeds from the second generation lose their vigorous traits, resulting in smaller cobs and weaker plants. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures maximum yield every season.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ ajie dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ akpamɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni jɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba daa be mli.

english: Why is clearing weeds early so important for young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani ehe hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal vital water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil. Removing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crop full access to food and light needed for rapid growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow much faster with rainwater than when I carry water from the well to water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kɛ mikɛ nugbɔ nu tsuɔ nii fe kɛ́ mikɛ nu jɛ nu bu mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater falls evenly over the whole farm and carries natural nitrogen from the air, which gives plants a quick nutrition boost. It also washes away dust from leaves so they can breathe and make food better.
ga: Nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Etsuɔ sũ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ hu he koni amɛmu ni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: If plants need water to survive, why do extension officers tell us to cover nursery beds so rain doesn't fall directly on new seeds?
ga: Kɛji tsei he miihia nu koni amɛhi shi Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔha tsei akwɛmɔhe saatsoi lɛ anɔ koni nugbɔ akanɛɛ dumɔwui heei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Heavy raindrops can wash away tiny seeds, crush soft young shoots, or pack the soil so tight that air cannot reach the roots. Covering nursery beds lets soil stay moist without the force of rain damaging fragile seedlings.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui bibii, ni efolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli. Aloo okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nursery saatso nɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ni efiteee dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass or palm leaves during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, also called mulching, acts like a blanket that blocks the hot sun from drying out the dirt. It traps moisture in the ground longer so your crops do not dry up quickly between waterings.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni ehaaa muji akagbi. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbiɛɛ oya yɛ nu ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ teŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and rot when rain water sits on my farm for many days without flowing away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ta miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni efooo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air just like humans do. When excess water sits on the farm, it fills all the tiny air spaces in the soil, drowning the roots so they rot and can no longer feed the leaves.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi hu he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Nu lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ amɛgboiɔ ni anyɛɛɛ aha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ niyenii dɔŋŋ.

english: Can I fetch water from the sea or salty lagoon to water my vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ nu kɛjɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli loo ŋmei ŋshɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛwo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: No, salty water pulls moisture out of plant roots instead of feeding them, which burns the leaves and ruins the farm soil so future crops cannot grow.
ga: Dabi, nu ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii. Enɛ baashã baai lɛ ni efite sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akakwɛ̃.

english: Is it good to use muddy water from a nearby pond to water my maize crop?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oookɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ nubu ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛha ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, water mixed with ordinary dirt is usually safe and carries extra rich soil nutrients to your crops. However, you must avoid water contaminated with soap, chemicals, or mining waste.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛ sũ ni sa efutu mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ehaa sũ mli niyenii ni fa babaoo babaoo baa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okpa nu ni samla, tsofai, loo shika tsuru ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ewo mli lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava on raised soil mounds instead of flat ground when the rain season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Mounds lift the tuber roots above heavy rain runoff so they do not sit in water and rot, while making the soil soft enough for the cassava roots to expand easily.
ga: Gɔŋ lɛ baawó tuber lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛya nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nɔ koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkafite. kɛfata he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo bɔ ni sa koni eha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli oya.

english: Where does all the heavy rain water that runs off my farm land eventually go?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ baaya yɛ naagbee?

english: Excess rain flows into small gutters, travels into streams and rivers, and eventually empties into the sea. Making small trenches helps direct this water away from your crops without washing your good soil into the river.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa nubui bibii amli. Ehoɔ kɛyaa faai kɛ faai amli. ni naagbee lɛ ehoɔ kɛyaa ŋshɔ lɛ mli Efeɔ ŋshɔkei bibii Ebaaye ebua ni ejie nu nɛɛ kɛjɛ onibii amli. ni ehe ehiaaa ni afɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa awo faa lɛ mli

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead in the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than the roots can drink it from the ground. They drop their leaves slightly to protect themselves from the heat, but usually rise back up when the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo koni ebu he kɛjɛ latsaa he. Shi amɛfɔɔ shitee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers without making fruit when dry weather lasts too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ yibii ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water, they save energy to stay alive by getting rid of flowers and small fruits, because producing fruit requires a lot of water.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha hewalɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai afeemɔ biɔ nu babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to sprout after I plant them in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow at different speeds depending on how deep they are planted and how healthy the root base was when cut. Burying suckers too deep or using suckers with damaged root bases delays their growth because the plant has to rebuild its root system before leaves can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Edamɔ bɔ ni okɛdu lɛ mli kwɔ oha kɛ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ ahe wa ha kɛ́ afo lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo ŋmeii ni shishitoo efite tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ama amɛshishifãi lɛ ekoŋŋ dani baai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key soil nutrient they need to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes away soil food or when water stays around the roots for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii ko ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why does my pepper plant drop all its flowers without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme afternoon heat, poor soil moisture, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. When the plant is stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo niyenii mli nibii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ beni tso lɛ miihao Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up tightly during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up during very hot weather as a natural way to hide from the burning sun and stop moisture from escaping. If the leaves stay curled continuously, it means the soil needs more water or tiny insects are sucking sap from underneath the leaves.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛteɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni atsĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ. aloo kooloi bibii yɛ ni Nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thin stems and give me small tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa lɛ, eyɛ ŋmeii bibii, ni kɛ́ akpa lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When cassava stem cuttings are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight and soil food. The plants spend all their energy growing tall to beat their neighbors for sunlight, leaving no extra energy to produce big underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ amɛmiida koni amɛye amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ anɔ kunim yɛ hulu la he. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ ko kwraa ahi shi ni akɛbaafee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas on the same land where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil during its growth. Cowpeas are special legumes that take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, naturally feeding and restoring the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ. Cowpeas ji ŋmei krɛdɛɛ ko ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa ehe hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young cocoa pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miishwie amɛ cacao ŋmɔji bibii lɛ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods drop off or turn black when small sap-sucking insects like capsids attack them, or when the tree cannot absorb enough water and nutrients during dry spells to feed all the pods at once.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids lɛ tutua amɛ, loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shikome.

english: Why are there small holes eaten into my cabbage leaves and white insects flying around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabe baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ye ni oná kooloi yɛŋ ni foɔ kɛbɔleɔ he?

english: Those small white moths lay tiny eggs on cabbage leaves that hatch into green caterpillars. The caterpillars feed directly on the soft cabbage leaves, leaving holes behind and preventing the cabbage head from forming properly.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ kaabe baa nɔ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii eŋɔlii. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ kaabii bibii tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa buji shwieɔ sɛɛ ni ehaaa kaabe yitso lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, tough root systems that react instantly to rain, quickly taking up water and soil nutrients before crop seedlings can build their roots. Cleared soil leaves weed seeds exposed to sunlight, causing them to germinate rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tso ko ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ hetoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ Eheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani tso dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ afee shishifãi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ naa hulu la. Ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting in the soil before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ po shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when heavy rain makes water stand in the soil for too long, depriving the tubers of air. It also happens when tiny worms called nematodes make small wounds on the skin of the yam, allowing rot-causing fungi to enter.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ebaa hu kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fee pilamɔi bibii. yɛ sweet potato hewolo nɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni kɛ helai ni fiteɔ baa lɛ boteɔ mli.

english: How many main types of cocoa varieties are available for me to plant in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji kookoo henɔi titrii ni miduɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: There are three main historical and modern types of cocoa in Ghana: Amelonado (traditionally called 'mail'), Amazon cocoa, and modern Hybrid cocoa. Each type differs in how fast it grows, how much yield it gives, and how well it handles pests.
ga: Ghana yɛ yinɔsane kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi titrii etɛ: amelonado (ni shishijee lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘mel’), Amazon kookoo, kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee ekome. Esoro henɔi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya amɛhaa lɛ mli. Yibiiwoo enyiɛ? kɛ bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii jogbaŋŋ amɛhaa lɛ

english: What is the difference between Amazon cocoa and modern hybrid cocoa?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ Amazon kookoo kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee ekome lɛ teŋ?

english: Amazon cocoa is an older, sturdy variety that grows large and yields well, while modern hybrid cocoa is produced by crossing Amazon cocoa with other strong varieties to create trees that grow faster, yield much more, and start bearing fruit early.
ga: Amazon kookoo ji kookoo ko ni etsɛ, ni wa waa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni ehaa yibii kpakpai Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa lɛ, akɛ kookoo ni jɛ Amazon lɛ futuɔ kookooi krokomɛi ni wa lɛ amli. koni ekɛfee tsei ni daa oya ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi oya

english: Why do people refer to older traditional cocoa varieties as 'mail' cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi tsɛɔ kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ, ni ji kusum nifeemɔi lɛ akɛ ‘kookoo mail’ lɛ?

english: Mail' is a local name commonly used by farmers in Ghana for Amelonado cocoa, which was the traditional cocoa variety planted in early farming days before faster-growing Amazon and hybrid varieties were introduced.
ga: Mail’ ji maŋ lɛ mli gbɛi ni okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa amelonado kookoo. Enɛ ji shishijee kookoo henɔ ni adu yɛ okwaayeli shishijee gbii lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ ba dani Amazon ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yaa hiɛ oya kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ba.

english: What does it actually mean when an extension officer says a crop is a 'hybrid'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ extension nitsulɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ji ‘hybrid’?

english: A hybrid crop is created when plant scientists deliberately crossbreed two different parent plants with strong traits—like high yield and disease resistance—so the resulting offspring plant inherits the best qualities of both parents.
ga: Afeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ beni tsei ahe nilelɔi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfɔ tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ sui ni mli wa, tamɔ yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ náa fɔlɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I take seeds directly from a hybrid cocoa pod on my farm to plant new trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ hybrid cocoa pods ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛdu tsei heei?

english: It is not recommended because seeds taken directly from harvest pods will lose their strong hybrid properties in the next generation, leading to unequal growth and lower yields. It is best to buy certified hybrid pods directly from official seed gardens.
ga: Akɛ enɛ etsɔɔɔ ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baafite amɛ hybrid nibii ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe hybrid pods ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui abɔɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Which cocoa variety is best suited to withstand long dry seasons and harsh weather?
ga: Mɛɛ kookoo henɔi hi jogbaŋŋ ni baanyɛ adamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ anaa?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties are specifically bred to be resilient, helping them survive dry spells and resist common diseases better than older, unselected varieties.
ga: Atsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa henɔi anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli, ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ anɔ kunim fe kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni ahalaaa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a particular crop variety will survive well in my local area before I buy seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ko baahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ dani mahe dumɔwui?

english: You can know by consulting local extension officers or asking for seed varieties certified by national agricultural bodies like the Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana, which test crops across different regions to ensure they survive local conditions.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona kɛtsɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ ni ooobi lɛ lɛ nɔ. Aloo bi dumɔwui srɔtoi ni maŋ lɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe ko tamɔ Ghana Cocoa Research Institute lɛ ema nɔ mi. ni kaa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi Enɛ ji koni akwɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do cocoa trees on neighboring farms produce different amounts of pods even if they were planted in the same year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ woɔ yibii sɔrɔtoi eyɛ mli akɛ adu amɛ yɛ afi kome mli moŋ?

english: Differences in yield usually come down to the type of variety planted—such as fast-yielding hybrids versus older varieties—as well as differences in soil quality, shade management, and fertilizer use.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ damɔ tso henɔi ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ tso ni atsake mli ni woɔ yibii mra kɛ tso ni etsɛ. nɔ ni fata he ji srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: How long will it take for new hybrid cocoa trees to start giving me pods compared to older varieties?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tsei heei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ akɛto ŋmeii srɔtoi ni etsɛ fe tsutsu lɛ ahe?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa trees can start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties like Amelonado often take 4 to 5 years before producing their first crop.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu amɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei ni etsɛ tamɔ Amelonado lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii.

english: Is it good practice to mix different cocoa varieties together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafutu kookoo henɔi srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: While different varieties can grow together, planting a single certified variety in clear blocks makes farm management easier, as trees will mature, flower, and require harvesting at the exact same time.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli moŋ Shi ŋmeii kome ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ni aaadu yɛ blɔkii ni mli tse mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ afee mlɛo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃, amɛbaawo fɔfɔi, ni abaakpa amɛ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my crops as soon as the rains start in April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ April mli pɛ?

english: In Ghana, the main rainy season typically runs from April to July. Planting early ensures your crops receive enough water throughout their critical growth period before the rain stops.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, nugbɔnɛmɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ April kɛyashiɔ July. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli fɛɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa.

english: Which types of crops are best for me to grow if I only depend on the normal April to July rains?
ga: Mɛni ji tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji akɛ mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛjɛɔ April kɛyashi July lɛ pɛ nɔ?

english: Short-duration crops like maize, cowpeas, and quick-maturing vegetables are best because they can grow, flower, and produce yield within that short 3-to-4-month rainfall window.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa kɛ aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃, amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii yɛ nakai nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop curl up and turn yellow when there is no rain for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: When plants do not get enough water from rain or irrigation, they curl their leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation and protect themselves from scorching heat.
ga: Kɛji tsei nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛlaaje kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he

english: Why are my crops flowering while they are still very small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: When crops experience water shortage, they feel threatened and try to produce flowers and seeds quickly to reproduce before they dry up completely.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ he naagbai kpe lɛ Amɛnuɔ he akɛ awo amɛhe gbeyei ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ oya ni amɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui koni amɛfɔ dani amɛgbi kwraa.

english: Will my maize produce small or empty cobs if it does not get enough water when flowering?
ga: Ani mi-ŋmãa lɛ baawo toi bibii loo nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛji enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Yes, flowering and seed formation require the most water. If rain fails during this stage, the plant cannot feed the grains, leading to small or empty cobs.
