ga: Hɛɛ, fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui afeemɔ biɔ nu fe fɛɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aha edumɔwui lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa dumɔwui akuu bibioo ko baa. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: What will happen to my crop harvest if the rains stop earlier than expected in June?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ yɛ June mli?

english: Without dams or supplementary water, early stoppage of rain causes water stress, which stunts crop growth, lowers grain weight, and reduces your total harvest output.
ga: Kɛji dam loo nu jɛɛhe kroko bɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baaha nu he haomɔ aba. ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsiɔ dumɔwui ni baa shi lɛ anaa ni ehaa nɔ ni ojieɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Since I do not have a dam or pipe system on my farm, how can I keep water in my soil for longer?
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, miŋmɔ lɛ bɛ faa loo paipi gbɛjianɔtoo. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha nu ahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Covering your soil with dry leaves, straw, or crop residue (mulching) prevents the sun from quickly drying out the soil moisture left by the rain.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu la lɛ akaha sũ lɛ mli nu ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ oya.

english: How can I catch and store rainwater on my farm to use when the rain stops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mamɔ nugbɔ nu ni mikɛto miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛtsu nii kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa?

english: You can dig simple earth basins or small water retention pits on your farm to collect runoff water during heavy rains and keep the nearby soil wet longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa muji tsɛnsi ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo nu bu bibioo ko ni akɛtoɔ mli. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni obua nu ni hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland soil become hard like stone after the July rains end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ yɛ July naagbee nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soil lacks organic matter like compost or leaves, exposure to intense sunshine after rains end bakes the ground dry, making it hard and poor at holding water.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai. Hulu la ni naa wa ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa ewaa ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does leaving some trees on my farm help my crops survive dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Trees provide gentle shade, reduce soil temperature, and break hot dry winds, helping crops retain moisture and survive hot dry spells between rainfalls.
ga: Tsei lɛ haa hulutsoo blɛoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa baa shi ni egbɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ eshwaa Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ be mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh direct sunlight and heat. Planting nurse crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that provides essential shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Nurse tsei tamɔ plantains ni akwɛɔ yɛ masɛi lɛ Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Can strong winds destroy my plantain farm, and how do I keep the plants from falling over?
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ afite mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ. Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã mitso lɛ akagbee shi?

english: Yes, plantains have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches, making them vulnerable to strong winds. Planting windbreak trees around the border of your farm helps block harsh winds and protects your crop from tipping over.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ ni ooodu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baabu ohe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he, ni ebaabu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. Applying manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer restores soil fertility so the plants can grow healthy green leaves and produce good ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛwo toi kpakpai.

english: Is it really necessary to add fertilizer to my farm if the soil already looks dark and rich?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii momo?

english: Dark soil can still run low on specific nutrients after repeated planting. Just as crops consume water, they draw up nutrients every season, so feeding the soil with compost or balanced fertilizer ensures continuous high yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni adu shii abɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Taakɛ tsei kɛ nu tsuɔ nii pɛpɛɛpɛ. Amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii daa be mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ha shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha yibii babaoo aba be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they face heat and water stress as a self-defense mechanism. Giving them a steady, consistent water supply keeps the blossoms healthy so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ he akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa, ni afeɔ lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ anáa hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa koni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Is it harmful to water my vegetable garden during the heat of the afternoon sun?
ga: Okɛ nu awo aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ani eyɛ oshara?

english: Yes, watering in full afternoon heat causes much of the water to evaporate before reaching the roots, and water droplets left on leaves can scorch under direct sunlight. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, nu babaoo shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu mli nu ni ashiɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: What causes white powdery patches to appear on my garden vegetable leaves, and how do I treat it?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsa lɛ?

english: White powder on leaves is usually a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which spreads quickly in warm, damp conditions. Applying an approved organic or chemical fungicide early stops the fungus from spreading and destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, powda yɛŋ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Organic loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are tiny insects clustering under my cassava leaves, and will they harm my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miibua amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cassava baai lɛ ashishi lɛ? Ni ani amɛbaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: These insects, such as whiteflies or mealybugs, suck vital sap from the leaves, causing them to curl and stunt plant growth. Treating the plants with appropriate sprays eliminates the pests before they reduce your tuber yield.
ga: Nɔ ni fata kooloi nɛɛ ahe ji ŋmeii yɛŋ loo ŋmeii. Emuɔ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ dani amɛba o-tuber yibiiwoo lɛ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I just let weeds grow between my crops if they are not touching the main plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Kɛji amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ bɛ tsakpaa

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops even if they are not touching them directly. Clearing weeds regularly ensures your crops receive all the nourishment they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ waa. Kɛji akɛ otaaa he tɛ̃ɛ po. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to compete with each other for water, light, and nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants with small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow large and productive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my mangoes are ripe without cutting them open?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-mango lɛ egbɔ ni mifolɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: You can check if a mango is ripe by looking at its shape and smelling near the stem. Ripe mangoes become rounder at the top, give off a sweet fruity scent, and yield slightly to soft pressure when squeezed gently.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona kɛji mango ekwɛ̃ kɛtsɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni enuɔ he yɛ he ni ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Mango ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ji kokroo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Eyɛ aduawai ahe ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ. ni okɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo aha kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ blɛoo

english: How do I prevent sap from spoiling the skin of my mangoes when I harvest them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nu lɛ naa koni ekafite kɛ́ akpa?

english: Harvest mangoes with a small piece of stem still attached using clippers, then turn them upside down on clean paper or grass so the sap drips away from the fruit skin rather than burning it.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ mango ni tso bibioo lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lolo lɛ. Kɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ afata he. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsɔ mango lɛ nɔ owo wolo loo jwɛi ni he tse nɔ. Enɛ ji koni latex lɛ ajɛ aduawai lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeetswa.

english: A cocoa pod is ripe when its outer shell changes color completely, usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to deep orange.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ etsake su kwraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. aloo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my small mango fruits fall off the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Trees shed young fruit when they do not have enough water or nutrients to support all of them. Watering during dry spells and applying organic manure around the tree base helps retain the fruit.
ga: Tsei woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua yibii lɛ fɛɛ bɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the ears form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Curling leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural extension officers.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the roots absorb the calcium the fruit needs.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni ji nɔ ni kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested fruits get soft spots and rot quickly after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii ni mikpa lɛ yɛ bɔjɔmɔi ni amɛgboɔ oya kɛji mikpa lɛ?

english: Fruits rot quickly if they are bruised during harvesting or picked during heavy rain. Rough handling creates tiny cracks in the skin where fungal germs enter and multiply.
ga: Yibii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo ajie amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. rough management Ehaa hewolo lɛ mli fãji bibii baa he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baanyɛ abote mli ni amɛshwere.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Cowpeas spread across the ground to block weeds and trap natural nitrogen from the air into the soil, which feeds your maize and keeps the land moist.
ga: Akɛ cowpeas shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akafee nɔ ko, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ekɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa o-abele lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and soft-shrinking in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ fioo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when exposed to heat and light because they think it is time to grow. Storing them on raised racks in a cool, dark, and well-ventilated barn stops them from sprouting and losing weight.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ amɛwo la kɛ la mli ejaakɛ amɛsusuɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ ato adekai ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ ni amɛkadara, ni ebaaha amɛtsiimɔ aba shi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight and intense heat. They require shade crops like plantain or shade trees to protect their leaves and keep moisture in the soil until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei koni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet, humid conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing tall weeds lets in sunlight and airflow, keeping the farm dry and reducing disease spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ ajiemɔ Ha hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ abɔle he. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aba shi.

english: What is causing the young leaves and shoots on my cocoa trees to look twisted and burnt?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni eshã?

english: This damage is usually caused by capsids (mirids), small insects that suck sap from young branches and leaves. Applying approved treatments at the right time of year prevents them from destroying your trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji capsids (mirids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ tsei niji bibii kɛ baai amli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekafite otso lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil needs fertilizer to help my cocoa yield better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua ni eha kookoo lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: If your mature trees produce few pods, have pale green leaves, or show slow growth despite getting enough rain, your soil lacks essential nutrients. Applying crop-specific cocoa fertilizer during the rainy season restores soil fertility and boosts yield.
ga: Kɛji otso agbo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. aloo edaa blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli pɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: Pruning removes unnecessary stems (chupons) and overcrowding branches that drain the tree's energy. It opens up the tree canopy to sunlight, lowers disease risk, and forces the tree to direct its energy into growing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa (chupons) kɛ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ fe nine ni fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ helai ni baanyɛ aba lɛ shi ni onyɛ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii koni amɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Is it really necessary to clear the weeds under my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ daa?

english: Yes, weeds compete directly with cocoa trees for water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients in the soil. Keeping the farm floor weeded ensures your crops get all the available food and reduces places for pests to hide.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ. ni ajie hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ lɛ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ahe?

english: Cassava roots expand aggressively and consume large amounts of nutrients and groundwater, starving the delicate young cocoa plants. Plantains are a better neighbor because they provide gentle shade without strangling the cocoa roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ miiye kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Plantains feɔ akutsoŋbii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo blɛoo ni amɛtsiii kookoo shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is it important to measure distance when planting cocoa seedlings instead of putting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asusu he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ he beni aduɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ moŋ fe ni akɛaawo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for light and nutrients, resulting in thin, weak trees that bear few pods. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough resources to thrive.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaashwere.

english: If I hire someone to manage my cocoa farm while I work in town, what main practices should I instruct them to follow?
ga: Kɛji mihe mɔ ko koni ekwɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ko nɔ be mli ni mitsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Mɛɛ nifeemɔi titrii esa akɛ mawo amɛ ŋaa koni amɛnyiɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should ensure they regularly weed the farm, prune unwanted branches, control pests early, and harvest pods promptly when ripe. Following proper, regular agronomy steps prevents loss of crop yield and protects your investment.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ koni amɛjie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa. Kpɔ̃ɔ niji ni ataooo lɛ. Kudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra. Ni okpa ŋmeii lɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ. Kɛ́ onyiɛ dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoi ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite, ni ebaabu oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I harvest green cocoa pods at the same time as the yellow ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikpaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ? kɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni ji ŋmɔtɔ

english: Green pods are unripe and contain underdeveloped beans that do not ferment correctly. Mixing them with ripe beans reduces the overall quality and flavor of your cocoa, which can lead to lower prices or rejected beans at buying centers.
ga: Pods ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ eshɛko ni ŋmeii ni edako jogbaŋŋ ni shwieee shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo futu ŋmeii ni ahoo lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa kookoo lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ fɛɛ baa shi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo jara aba shi loo kookoo ŋmeii ahemɔhei lɛ akpoo.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to come out of the ground if I push them too deep into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: A seed only carries a tiny amount of stored energy to send its first green shoot upwards. If buried too deep, it runs out of food energy before reaching the surface and sunlight, causing it to die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato ni amɛkɛbaatsu klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ahe nii. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ Niyenii hewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani eshɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ kɛ hulu la. ha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do my corn plants grow thin and weak when I plant four or five seeds in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ, kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for the same water and nutrients in the soil. Spacing them out gives each plant its own feeding area so it can grow thick stems and healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. He ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ni amɛyeɔ niyenii yɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aná shishifã ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to wait for the first heavy rains before putting my corn seeds in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mamɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Dry soil cannot activate the seed to start growing. If seeds sit in hot, dry dirt, they can spoil or get eaten by birds and ants before the rain comes to give them the continuous moisture they need to sprout.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui hewalɛ koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ Amɛbaanyɛ okpoi kɛ ŋmeii aye amɛ loo amɛgboi dani nugbɔ lɛ aba. Enɛ ji koni eha amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help showing that the plant is hungry for key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that too much water around the roots is suffocating the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu yɛ he fɛɛ he Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up tight like straws during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural shield against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant hides part of its leaf surface from the hot sun to stop water from escaping, helping it survive until the cool evening.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ fã ko teeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni nu akaje mli. Ye obua lɛ ni ehi shi kɛyashi fɛ̃i be lɛ mli.

english: Why do corn plants grown under large shade trees grow very tall but produce tiny or no ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ daraa babaoo shi amɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi bibii loo amɛwooo ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make the energy required for food production. In the shade, the plant wastes all its strength stretching upward to search for light instead of building strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsei lɛ ahewalɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ akɛni ehe bahiaa ni amɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛna la lɛ hewɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tso nguanguahi.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my crop if there is enough space in the field for all of us?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo? Kɛji akɛ he ko yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha wɔ fɛɛ?

english: Weeds act like uninvited guests at a small family meal. They grow faster than your crops and aggressively steal the water, soil nutrients, and sunlight that your corn needs to produce food.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni afɔ̃ɔɔ amɛ nine yɛ weku niyenii ashishi. Amɛdaraa fe oŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa o-abele lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aba waa.

english: How does leaving dry stalks and clear grass on top of my soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse ni mishiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and moist during hot days. As those old leaves rot, they turn into rich natural food that feeds your next crops.
ga: Tsoi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Kɛ nakai baai momo lɛ fite Ebaatsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jara wa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What are those soft hairs coming out of the top of my corn cobs, and why do they matter for my harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai yitsɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ mi-ŋmei ŋmei lɛ yiteŋ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Each hair, called a silk, leads directly to one potential grain of corn on the cob. Wind must drop dust from the top flower onto these silks; if a silk is missed, that spot on the cob stays empty without a kernel.
ga: Atsɛɔ yitsɔi fɛɛ yitsɔi akɛ siliki. Enɛ kɛ mɔ yaa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ajie sũ ni jɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli lɛ awo nɛkɛ silikii nɛɛ anɔ; kɛji akɛ atse siliki lɛ, nakai he ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ baafee efolo ni ŋmei ko bɛ mli.

english: If I plant beans together in the same field with my maize, will the beans steal all the food from the maize?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa fata ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Ani ŋmeii lɛ baaju niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Beans and maize actually work well together. Beans have special roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil, which helps feed the maize and improves the overall farm yield.
ga: Beans kɛ corn tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ ŋmãa ni ehaa ŋmãa fɛɛ ni anáa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to make green leaves and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking juices from the underside of leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Removing heavily infected plants and spraying mild soap water or neem oil can help protect the rest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plants do not get enough steady water. When stressed by heat or drought, the tomato plant sheds its blossoms to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni yaa nɔ daa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ loo hɔmɔ kpe Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains flood the soil and water cannot drain away, oxygen gets cut off, allowing soil fungi to infect and rot the waterlogged roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hoɔ, ni nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ aho kɛya. Afoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni shishifãi ni nu ewo mli lɛ hu fiteɔ.

english: Why does covering the bare ground around my crops with dry grass help them stay healthy in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aha he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? Mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewɔ lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves acts like a blanket. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps root zones cool, and holds moisture in the ground much longer between rainfalls.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I cut down all the large shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mifo tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and heat. Shade trees shield young cocoa from sun damage and keep the air humid until the cocoa roots grow deep enough to survive in full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. ni okwɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily when the bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are soft and do not have deep taproots like hardwood trees. When a heavy fruit bunch develops, the plant becomes top-heavy, so strong winds or wet, soft soil can easily cause the shallow roots to pull out of the ground unless supported with bamboo props.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ahe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei ni wa. Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ aniji lɛ shwere lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ejieɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya Ja akɛ nibii ni akɛ ŋmei fee lɛ tsu nii.

english: Yam vines produce big tubers by converting sunlight into food through their leaves. Staking keeps the leaves high off the ground where they can get full sunshine and air, preventing leaf diseases and helping the tuber grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ nɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ nɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo yɛ lɛ. Etsiɔ baa helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: Maize feeds heavily on the same nutrients year after year, which weakens the soil over time. Planting maize continuously in the same spot also allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in that soil.
ga: Abɛi nine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ babaoo daa afi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ hu haa abɛi pɔtɛɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and beans have natural helpers on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the earth. When the crop finishes, this trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu nii agbe naa Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why isn't the chemical working when I spray it on my cocoa leaves that are already showing disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai lɛ tsuuu nii kɛ́ mikɛshwie kookoo baai ni miitsɔɔ hela momo lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Crop medicines are designed for prevention, not cure. If you wait until a disease has already entered your farm and infected your plants, spraying will not work to fix the damage.
ga: Afee tsofa ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe lɛ koni akɛbu he. Jeee tsabaa ni. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi hela lɛ bote ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni etswa tsei lɛ, Spraying lɛ esaaa nɔ ni efite lɛ.

english: When is the right time for me to start spraying protective medicine on my young cocoa and okra?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ awo mi-kookoo kɛ okra bɔɔlu lɛ nɔ?

english: You should start applying protective medicine right when the rainy season begins, around five months into the season, so your crops are protected before diseases arrive.
ga: Esa akɛ obɔi tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ yeli kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ. loo aaafee nyɔji enumɔ yɛ be lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha abu onibii ahe dani helai aba.

english: Can I wait until I see signs of sickness on my okra before applying crop protection?
ga: Ani manyɛ mamɛ kɛyashi okra lɛ baaye hela dani mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: No, you must apply protection before any sickness appears. If you wait until the disease enters your farm, any medicine you spray will no longer work.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ojie coverage dani hela aba. Kɛ omɛ kɛyashi hela lɛ bashɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Tsofa ni okɛwo mli lɛ tsuuu nii dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to be so strict and regular about my spraying schedule on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee mɔ ni mli wa ni mafee nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ miŋmɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ he lɛ?

english: You must be very diligent because timing is critical in crop protection; applying medicine at the right moment keeps disease from establishing itself when rains begin.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nii waa ejaakɛ be ji nɔ ni he hiaa waa kɛji akɛ eba ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu he. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni helai akaje shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Why does the rainy season cause my crops to get sick if I don't treat them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ hela kɛji akwɛɛɛ amɛ oya lɛ?

english: The start of the rains creates ideal conditions for crop diseases to spread, which is why young cocoa and okra need protective medicine applied right as wet weather begins.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi enɛɔ, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsei ahe helai gbɛfaŋnɔ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni kookoo kɛ okra biɔ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ.

english: What is the difference between preventing a crop disease and trying to cure it?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsei ahe helai ni atsiɔ naa kɛ mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni atsa lɛ teŋ?

english: Preventing disease means applying medicine to healthy plants so sickness cannot start. Trying to cure a disease after it enters your farm does not work because protective medicines cannot heal infected crops.
ga: Helai atsimɔ tsɔɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli koni helai akaba. Mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni atsa hela lɛ beni ebote oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii ejaakɛ tsofai ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ nyɛŋ atsa tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: How can I protect my young cocoa seedlings from catching diseases during their first year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: Protect young cocoa seedlings by being diligent and applying preventive medicine right at the start of the rains so diseases never get a chance to take root.
ga: Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛtsɔ hiɛdɔɔ ni ooofee kɛ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa kɛjɛ nugbɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ helai srɔtoi anaa Hegbɛ yɛ ni akɛbaawo shishifãi.

english: Will spraying my farm save my okra crops if they are already infected with a disease?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni mi okra tsei lɛ ayiwala? Ni kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ amɛ momo hu?

english: No, if your okra crops are already infected by the time you spray, the medicine will not work. Protective treatments must be applied before infection happens.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ o-roselle tsei lɛ etsɔ hela momo beni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ, tsofa lɛ tsuuu nii. Esa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ atsu nii dani hela lɛ aba.

english: Why is timing more important than the type of medicine I spray on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be he hiaa fe tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Timing is everything because medicine only works to prevent disease before it arrives. Once disease enters your farm, no medicine you spray will work.
ga: Be ji nɔ fɛɛ nɔ Ejaakɛ tsofa tsuɔ nii pɛ koni ekɛtsi hela naa dani eba. Kɛ hela bote oŋmɔ lɛ mli Tsofa ni okɛwo mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Should I apply medicine to my young cocoa plants during the dry season or wait for the rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa awo kookoo tsei bibii anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo mamɛ nugbɔ?

english: You should start applying the protective medicine when the rains begin, around five months in, because that is when moisture increases the risk of disease attacking young cocoa.
ga: Esa akɛ oje tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ shishi kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ. Aaafee nyɔji enumɔ hiɛ Enɛ ji akɛ, hulutsoo be haa helai ni baa kookoo tsei bibii anɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an important food nutrient in the soil, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees curling up and turning brown at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaf curling and browning at the edges is usually caused by excessive heat and sunlight without enough shade, or a lack of water during dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ babaoo kɛ hulu la ni hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ. loo nu ni bɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantains on the same land with my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kookoo tsei heei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant the seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin stems and small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from soil or manure, the plant uses all its energy to grow leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei náa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmei mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack, and the plant reaches 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Ni tsei lɛ baahi shi nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress, irregular watering during dry spells, or when the plant does not get enough direct sunlight.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo be mli ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ shɛɛɛ tso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they were buried too deep in the dirt, if the soil was too dry, or if soil insects ate the seeds before they could grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui kwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Aloo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize farm so much faster than other caterpillars?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miifite mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ oya fe ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms target the deep central funnel of young maize plants where leaves grow, eating the core growth point and multiplying rapidly before they are easily seen.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmãa ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔ he ni baai lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ he titri ni edaa yɛ lɛ ni efɔɔ oya dani anaa lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to the local environment, meaning their roots absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Can I plant bamboo intentionally as a farm crop, or does it only grow wild in the bush?
ga: Ani manyɛ majɛ mijwɛŋmɔ mli madu ŋmei akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii? Aloo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli yɛ tsei bibii pɛ amli?

english: Bamboo can be cultivated like any farm crop. You can plant cuttings or rhizomes in organized rows, and it grows very quickly compared to regular trees, providing a steady supply of wood and biomass.
ga: Abaanyɛ adu ŋmei tamɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmei krokomɛi fɛɛ. Obaanyɛ odu ŋmeii loo rhizomes yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɛo mli. Ni edaa oya waa kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ahe. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baa.

english: If I cut down mature bamboo stalks on my land, will the whole plant die or will it grow back?
ga: Kɛji mifo ŋmeii ni eda yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ani tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbo loo ŋmeii heei baakwɛ̃?

english: Bamboo is a fast-growing grass with a strong underground root system called a rhizome network. Cutting the stalks above ground does not kill the plant; it will sprout new shoots rapidly during the next rainy season.
ga: Bamboo ji jwɛi ni daa oya ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli wa ni atsɛɔ lɛ rhizome network. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yiteŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, egbeee tso lɛ. Ebaakwɛ̃ tsei heei oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why does bamboo spread so quickly across my land once it takes root?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji etswa shishifãi pɛ?

english: Bamboo spreads through underground stems that travel horizontal under the soil and send up new shoots nearby. If not managed or contained by trenches, a single bamboo plant will naturally expand into a dense grove.
ga: Bamboo gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛtsuɔ tsei heei ni bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ loo aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ yɛ nubu ko mli lɛ, ŋmei tso kome pɛ baagbɛ eshwa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔ koo ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Can bamboo grow and survive on poor land where crops like maize or cocoa struggle?
ga: Ani ŋmeii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ohia emɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo kookoo bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, bamboo is extremely resilient and can thrive in degraded or nutrient-poor soils. It helps restore tired land by preventing soil erosion and dropping leaves that break down into organic matter.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi waa ni ebaanyɛ eda yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baa ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I harvest my bamboo and leave it lying directly on the wet ground?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa ŋmei ni mishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: When harvested bamboo lies directly on damp soil, moisture and ground insects like termites penetrate the stems, causing them to rot and weaken quickly instead of drying properly.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Fɛ̃i kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii boteɔ tsei lɛ amli, ni no haa amɛgboiɔ oya ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when bamboo stalks are ready to be harvested from my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Young bamboo shoots are soft and green, but mature bamboo stalks (usually 3 to 5 years old) turn a lighter yellowish-green or brown color and make a solid, hard sound when tapped.
ga: Bamboo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ eŋɔli. Shi ŋmeii ni edara (ni bei pii lɛ amɛyeɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5) lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee. ni ehaa gbee ni naa wa ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ́ atswa lɛ

english: Will my bamboo grove produce stems year after year without me replanting seeds every season?
ga: Ani mi-bamboo koo lɛ baawo tsei afi fɛɛ afi ni ehe ehiaaa ni madu dumɔwui heei daa afi?

english: Yes, bamboo is a perennial plant. Once the root system is established, it will continue to produce new harvestable shoots every year for decades without needing to replant seeds.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei ji tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ ebɔi shi pɛ lɛ Ebaawo ŋmeii heei ni abaanyɛ akpa daa afi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu dumɔwui heei.

english: How can harvested bamboo be used to generate electricity or power for a village?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ atsu nii ni akɛfee srawa hewalɛ loo hewalɛ aha akrowa lɛ?

english: When dry bamboo stalks are chopped and burned in specialized machines called biomass gasifiers, they release clean gas that runs a generator to produce electric power for local lighting and equipment.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi lɛ, afolɔ amɛ ni ashãa amɛ yɛ tsɔne krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ biomass gasifier lɛ mli. Bamboo tsei lɛ jieɔ gas ni he tse ni tsirɛɔ tsɔne ko ni haa hulu kpɛɔ koni ekɛfee srawa hewalɛ kɛha maŋ lɛ mli kanei kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to dry freshly cut bamboo before using it for burning or energy generation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbi ŋmeii ni afo ehee lɛ dani ashã loo afee hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly cut bamboo contains a high amount of water. Drying it in the sun removes this moisture, allowing it to burn hotter, cleaner, and produce the gas needed for power generation without heavy smoke.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ ŋmeii ni afo ehee lɛ amli. Kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ejieɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ. Enɛ haa shãa ni mli edɔ ni ehe tseɔ lɛ baa, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa kɛha srawa hewalɛ baa ni lasu ni mli edɔ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Does planting bamboo steal nutrients and water from nearby food crops on my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli?

english: Bamboo has thick, dense roots close to the surface that absorb water and nutrients aggressively. It is best planted along farm borders or dedicated fields rather than mixed directly next to sensitive crops like vegetables.
ga: Bamboo yɛ shishifãi ni mli tse ni mli tse ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛi. ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya Esa akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔi lɛ ahe loo yɛ ŋmɔji pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ aduawai adu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and small roots that cannot handle direct harsh sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside them provides living umbrellas that keep the soil moist and shield the young plants from heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni mli wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantains, kɛfata tsei nɛɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaabu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the small shoots growing around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain stem, they compete with the main plant for soil food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring you get large, heavy bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Akɛ nɔmimaa ha bo akɛ obaaná tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make food and grow green. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients out of the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves out of the soil and allows pests that feed on it to multiply. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans helps rebuild soil health.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ehaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii sumɔɔ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ koni amɛshwere. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer onto my soil when there has been no rain for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying it to dry soil can burn tender plant roots and leave the fertilizer wasted on top of the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eshi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves that look like small insect bites?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai ni tamɔ kooloi ni ŋmɔɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by caterpillars such as fall armyworms hiding inside the central leaf funnel of the plant, chewing on leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ fall armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ baa. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni oooye dani ojieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Too much standing water fills air spaces in the soil, suffocating cassava tubers underground and encouraging fungal diseases that make the roots soft and rotten.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon even after I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose moisture through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant temporary wilts to save water and usually bounces back by evening as temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei gboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Ni amɛfɔɔ sɛɛkuu gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when extreme afternoon heat damages the pollen or when watering is irregular. Without proper pollination or steady moisture, the plant cancels fruit growth.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli la ni naa wa lɛ kpata pollen lɛ hiɛ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa loo hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ baafo yibii lɛ adalɛ mli.

english: How do weeds growing around my cassava field reduce the size of my tubers?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni miyitso lɛ aba shi aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like thieves in the farm by stealing light, water, and fertilizer away from your main crop. Without enough resources, the cassava cannot make enough food to swell its tubers.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ kane, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Kɛji nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Cassava nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How deep should I bury maize seeds in the dirt when I plant them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep. If you plant them too close to the surface, birds will eat them or the hot sun will dry them out, but if you bury them too deep, the young shoots will run out of energy before reaching the light.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5. Kɛji odu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ lɛ, Okpoi baaye amɛ loo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha amɛgbi. Shi kɛji ofu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Young shoots lɛ hewalɛ baaho dani amɛshɛ la lɛ he.

english: How many days after planting maize seeds will I start seeing the green shoots come up?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni odu ŋmãa lɛ obaaje shishi ona ŋmãa ni eŋɔli lɛ?

english: If the soil has enough moisture and warmth, maize seeds usually sprout and break through the surface in about 4 to 7 days.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ aaafee gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow, or the soil is too soaked with water from heavy rain, causing the roots to drown.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa akwɛ̃. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛ waa ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant yams using small seeds like I do with maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui bibii akwɛ sweet potato? Ani ebaanyɛ efee tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: No, yams are not grown from small seeds like maize. You grow yams by cutting a mature, healthy yam tuber into smaller pieces called setts, or using small seed-yams, and burying them inside raised mounds of soil.
ga: Dabi, sweet potatoes jeee dumɔwui bibii tamɔ ŋmãa. Oduɔ sweet potato kɛtsɔ sweet potato tuber ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ooofo mli bibii bibii lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ nakai gbɛi lɛ Sett. Aloo okɛ yam dumɔwui bibii atsu nii. Kɛkɛ ni efu lɛ yɛ sũ ni abua naa mli.

english: How do I know it is the right time of year to prepare my mounds and plant yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni esa akɛ masaa mi-pile lɛ ni madu mi-sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Yams are typically planted late in the dry season or right at the start of the early rains, usually between December and March, so the root setts can settle in the soil before heavy rainfall begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ atomo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee loo nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa December kɛ March teŋ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa.

english: Why do I need to make sure the soil is soft and loose before planting groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani madu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts flower above ground, but after pollinating, the stem pegs bend down and push into the soil to grow the actual nuts underground. Soft soil allows these pegs to sink in easily.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ Stem pin lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛdu ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Do groundnuts need a lot of expensive chemical fertilizer to grow well?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni jara wa he miihia ŋmeii koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, groundnuts belong to the legume family, which means they can pull nitrogen out of the air and feed themselves and the soil, requiring very little extra fertilizer.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Ebiɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ afata he.

english: What is the difference between crops I must replant every year like maize and crops like plantain?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe hiaa ni adu daa afi, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛ tsei tamɔ plantains lɛ ateŋ?

english: Crops like maize are annuals that die after harvest, meaning you must plant fresh seeds every single year. Plantains are perennials that keep living and producing new suckers from the same root system for years without needing new seed planting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa ji jwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji jwɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni odu dumɔwui heei daa afi. Plantains ji tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei kɛjɛɔ shishifã kome mli afii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu dumɔwui heei.

english: Can I plant groundnuts in the same field as my yams during the same season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmei yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, planting groundnuts around yam mounds works well because groundnuts carpet the soil to keep weeds away and leave valuable nitrogen in the soil that helps the yams grow bigger.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akabote mli ni eshiɔ nitrogen ni jara wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do seed crops like maize and groundnuts need me to clear all the weeds before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni woɔ dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi fɛɛ dani adu.

english: Young plants coming from small seeds are very delicate. If weeds are present, they will steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, choking the weak seedlings before they can grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii ni jɛɔ dumɔwui bibii amli lɛ waaa waa ni kɛji ajie jwɛi lɛ amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ anaa dani amɛdaraa waa.

english: How long can I keep my young cocoa seedlings in their bags before planting them in the field?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makɛ cacao tsei bibii awo kotoku mli dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Cocoa seedlings should ideally be planted in the ground within a few weeks of receiving them during the rainy season. Keeping them in nursery bags for too long causes their roots to become twisted and bound, which can stunt their growth permanent once planted.
ga: Esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ kɛjɛ be mli ni enine shɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo grow bag mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baatsi edalɛ naa kwraa kɛ́ adu lɛ.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to plant cocoa seedlings on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ afi mli be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant cocoa seedlings is at the start of the major rainy season, usually between May and June. This gives the young roots enough moisture and time to grow strong before the harsh, dry Harmattan season begins.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ May kɛ June teŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ be ni amɛkɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa dani Harmattan be ni mli wa ni nu egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do my freshly planted cocoa seedlings seem to grow so slowly above ground during the first few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: In the initial months after transplanting, cocoa seedlings focus most of their energy underground developing a strong, deep taproot rather than sprouting new leaves. Once the root system is established, noticeable top growth will follow.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji ni akɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, kookoo dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli kwɔ. Yɛ baai heei najiaŋ Kɛji shishifãi lɛ ato shishi pɛ lɛ, ŋwɛi-line dalɛ ni kadiɔ mɔ baanyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong, direct heat and light, which burns their tender leaves and stops nutrient production. They need temporary shade trees, like plantain or cassava, to shield them until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ he waa. Enɛ haa baai bibii lɛ shãa ni ekpaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ feemɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Koni amɛtsu nii akɛ gãimlibii kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why are the leaves falling off my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-kokoo dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf loss soon after planting is usually caused by transplant shock, root damage during planting, or lack of water. Ensuring gentle handling and planting during wet weather prevents this stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni laajeɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ jɛɔ dumɔ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ kroko mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ hewɔ. Shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ dumɔ be mli loo nu ni faaa yɛ mli Kwɛmɔ blɛoo kɛ dumɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ haomɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa plants when putting them in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ato he ko beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa plants should be spaced 3 meters by 3 meters apart. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough soil nutrients, water, and sunlight without crowding neighboring trees as they grow large.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee mitai 3 kɛ mitai 3. Nɛkɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. ni ekɛ ehe wooo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ

english: How do I correctly remove the plastic seedling bag without damaging the young cocoa plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie plastic dumɔwui kotokui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni mifiteee cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: You should use a clean blade to slice open the bottom and side of the plastic bag carefully, keeping the soil ball intact around the roots before placing it gently into the dug hole.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsɔne ni he tse atsu nii ni okɛfo plastic kotoku lɛ shishi kɛ esɛɛgbɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ muji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. shishifãi dani fiofio Okɛwo bu ni otsa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to dig and prepare planting holes on my land before my cocoa seedlings arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo ni masaa dumɔ bu lɛ mli dani kookoo dumɔwui lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Preparing holes in advance softens the soil, allows rainfall to collect inside the hole, and ensures quick planting so seedlings do not dry out waiting in their bags on top of the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ osaa bu lɛ he kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ bu lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduɔ oya Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui ni miimɛ yɛ kotokui amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akagbi.

english: Why is it dangerous to let tall weeds grow close to my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mahã jwɛi kakadaji akwɛ̃ yɛ mikoo dumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Tall weeds steal water, light, and nutrients from small seedlings, and they can easily cover young plants so you cannot see them, making them vulnerable to accidental cutting during farm clearing.
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui bibii amli. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha tsei bibii anɔ mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, onyɛɛɛ ona amɛ. Enɛ haa amɛhe feɔ mlɛo akɛ abaafolɔ amɛ yɛ oshara mli yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ.

english: What should I do if the rains suddenly stop right after I plant my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa beni midu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If dry weather returns after planting, manually water each seedling at the stem base during early mornings or late evenings and place dry grass mulch around the base to keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Nu awo dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli yɛ shishigbɛ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shishigbɛ lɛ he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to clear my land and prepare it for planting cocoa in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni masaa mihe koni madu kookoo yɛ Ghana?

english: Land clearing and farm preparation for cocoa are usually done during the dry season, starting around January and February. Clearing early allows you to prepare the soil so that your farm is ready for planting as soon as the main rainy season begins in April or May.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔji ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔji ni asaa kɛha kookoo lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ aaafee January kɛyashi February. early clearing Ehaa osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ bɔni afee ni oŋmɔ lɛ afee klalo kɛha dumɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ je shishi yɛ April loo May mli pɛ.

english: How can I manage the heavy physical labor on my cocoa farm so that my family and I do not suffer severe bodily strain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu nitsumɔ ni tsii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli lɛ he nii? Bɔni afee ni mi kɛ miweku lɛ akaná gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa waa.

english: Heavy tasks like initial land clearing, weeding, and harvesting can be scheduled and shared with hired agricultural laborers during peak months rather than doing everything yourself. Spacing out tasks across the farm calendar prevents overexertion and physical breakdown.
ga: Nitsumɔi ni tsii tamɔ shishijee he ni ajieɔ jwɛi kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ Abaanyɛ akɛwo okwaayeli nitsulɔi ni aŋɔ amɛ nitsumɔ yɛ nyɔji ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ amli lɛ adɛŋ ni akɛ amɛ agba he sane. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni bo diɛŋtsɛ obaafee nɔ fɛɛ nɔ Nitsumɔ ni akɛ he kroko baatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli kalanda lɛ naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ nitsumɔ ni fe nine kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ naa.

english: Which farm tasks on my cocoa farm are most critical to complete during the early dry months of January and February?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ magbe naa yɛ January kɛ February nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ shishijee mli?

english: January and February are critical for land clearing, cutting down old unwanted trees, and laying out planting rows. Completing these labor-intensive tasks during the dry months ensures light can reach the ground and land is ready before the rains set in.
ga: January kɛ February he hiaa waa kɛha he ni ajieɔ nibii kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Tsei ni egbɔ ni ataooo lɛ afolɔmɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ Nitsumɔi ni heɔ nitsumɔ babaoo nɛɛ ni agbeɔ naa yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli lɛ haa la shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ klalo dani nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight and intense heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava to protect their tender leaves, maintain soil moisture, and cool the microclimate around them.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. koni ebu baai bibii ahe Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha nu ŋshɔ ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ mli ajɔ

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed their flowers during the dry season in January and February?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ January kɛ February mli lɛ?

english: Dropping flowers is a natural protective reaction when cocoa trees experience water stress during dry months. The tree sheds flowers to preserve water and energy so it can survive until the rainy season comes.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛ́ cacao tsei na nu he haomɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ ni baahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so quickly in my cocoa farm right after the dry season ends, and how does it affect my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ egbe naa lɛ? Ni te enáa mitsei lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The warm soil combined with the first rains after February causes weed seeds to germinate rapidly. If you do not clear these weeds, they will compete with your cocoa trees for water and essential soil nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ February sɛɛ lɛ fata he lɛ ha jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ oya. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi nɛɛ, Amɛkɛ kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu ni he hiaa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to prune and cut away extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead wood and unnecessary shoots (chupons), allowing fresh air and sunlight to pass through the canopy. This reduces humidity that breeds black pod disease and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni egboi kɛ tsei ni he ehiaaa (chupon) lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la abote ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ cocoa pods wuji.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my cocoa farm lacks nutrients and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your mature cocoa trees have pale green or yellowing leaves, slow growth, or produce very few pods despite good rainfall, the soil is likely depleted of nutrients like potassium and nitrogen and requires suitable cocoa fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ, edaa blɛoo loo ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ kpakpa eba moŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu fɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen ni bɛ. ni ehe miihia ni aná kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa

english: When is the right time for me to spray my cocoa farm to prevent black pod disease?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ afɔse tsofa yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli koni akɛtsi black pod hela naa?

english: Fungicide spraying for black pod disease should begin at the start of the main rainy season (around May or June) before humidity rises, as damp conditions promote the spread of fungal spores on the pods.
ga: Esa akɛ aje tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ black pod hela lɛ nɔ lɛ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. (aaafee May loo June mli) dani hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa beans if I harvest pods that are still green instead of waiting for them to turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cocoa yibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mamɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Unripe green pods contain beans with underdeveloped sugars, which will not ferment properly. Unfermented beans produce a bitter, poor-quality cocoa that buying companies will reject or pay less for.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni ekwɛɛɛ mli lɛ amli ji ŋmeii ni sugar yɔɔ mli ni eshɛko ni baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ. Beans ni afɔɔɔ mli lɛ haa kookoo ni mli edɔ ni ehiii kwraa baa. ni nitsumɔhe ni heɔ lɛ baakpoo loo ebaawo nyɔmɔ fioo.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow with small ragged holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and yellow leaves on maize are major signs of Fall Armyworm attack or nutrient stress. The caterpillars hide inside the leaves and eat them from the inside, which weakens the plant and stops it from growing healthy green leaves.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadii ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ he haomɔ. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa baai eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience sudden stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of holding onto its fruit flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna haomɔi trukaa, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ baai moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: How do I know if my soil needs fertilizer before I plant cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu ŋmei?

english: If your previous crops grew very slowly, produced small roots, or had pale yellow leaves instead of deep green ones, your soil lacks essential food and will need fertilizer or compost to support a good cassava harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ da blɛoo waa, eyɛ shishifãi bibii, loo eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaabi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni eye ebua ŋmei kpamɔ kpakpa.

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong, shallow roots that quickly grab water and nutrients faster than farm crops. They naturally react faster to rainfall, which is why early clearing is necessary to keep them from choking your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe wa waa. Egbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei Amɛjɛɔ amɛfɔmɔ mli amɛfeɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ he miihia koni amɛkatsi oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall over and rot on the ground when they start fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiifite beni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Tomato plants have soft stems that cannot support heavy fruit. When left unsupported, the branches bend to the wet ground, exposing the fruits to damp soil, worms, and fungal diseases that cause rot.
ga: Tomato tsei yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ yibii ni tsii nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ashi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ ni fiɔ esɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ aniji lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ yeɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa seedlings need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Can I save seeds from the hybrid maize I harvested this year to plant next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn ni mikpa afi nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is not recommended to plant saved seeds from hybrid crops. Hybrid seeds lose their high yields and disease strength after the first generation, so planting them again will result in poor growth and smaller cobs.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli. Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ yibii babaoo kɛ helai ahewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni dumɔwui lɛ hu baafee bibii.

english: Why do some of my yam tubers grow twisted and cracked underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow twisted or cracked when the soil is packed too hard or full of rocks, making it difficult for the tuber to expand smoothly down into the earth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafite loo amɛbaagbala kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa bulb lɛ akɛ ebaagbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain trees curl up tight during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl inward during the hottest part of the day as a survival mechanism to reduce sunlight exposure and prevent water from evaporating out of the plant.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves dry up and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack open as the expanding tubers push against the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.
