english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their small leaves lose water faster than their roots can drink it. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that shelter the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpee hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ baai bibii lɛ ahewɔ Ebaafite nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or growing beans on that land helps restore the soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo adu ŋmeii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars chewing ragged holes in the very middle of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ko ni etse yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Those holes are caused by Fall Armyworms, which love to hide inside the growing top of young corn. Checking your farm early and spraying targeted treatments right into the center leaf bundle stops them from ruining your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji lɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsofafeemɔ nibii ni akɛshwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni onibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the plant without growing into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ anɔkwa tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when soil moisture swings from very wet to very dry. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the dirt when the wet season comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long and drowns the root system. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain off safely away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my fertilizer on the farm right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater carries loose fertilizer off the top of your soil and washes it into streams before your crop roots have time to absorb it. It is better to bury fertilizer slightly in moist soil after rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛshwieɔ faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ. Esa akɛ afu ŋmɔshi nibii fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop in the hot afternoon even if the ground still feels a bit damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ fioo lolo moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, leaves give off moisture faster than the roots can suck it up from the dirt. Covering the soil around the base with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and prevents excess evaporation.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaaa la ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad practice to plant maize on the exact same patch of ground every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of its favorite nutrients and lets maize-specific pests live in the dirt permanently. Alternating with crops like peanuts or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akaná niyenii ni esumɔɔ. ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa Ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa baatsake lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I chop off some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Too many small shoots steal water and food away from the main mother plant. Cutting back extra shoots and leaving only two or three allows the main stem to produce a much bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii babaoo tsɔ baaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii 2-3 pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii titri lɛ woɔ plantains akui ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller harvests even if I feed my plants properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal soil food, groundwater, and sunlight directly away from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the growing season leaves all the water and plant food for your cash crops to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ mra yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa nu kɛ tsei niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ koni oshika ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know if the compost manure I made at home is ready to put on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishia ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo akɛ mikɛbaafata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Ready compost looks like dark, rich soil, feels crumbly, and smells like fresh earth rather than rotten trash. If it is still hot to the touch or smells bad, it needs more time to decompose, or it can burn your crop roots.
ga: Kompost ni asaa he lɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ, enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ, ni eŋɔɔɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ hee fe jwɛi ni egbo. Kɛji edɔ lolo kɛji akɛ ota he loo ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Eheɔ be babaoo dani efiteɔ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso shishifãi ashã.

english: Can I put fresh animal manure directly onto my young maize plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei awo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh animal dung is too strong and generates heat as it decomposes, which can scorch the roots and leaves of young plants. You should let the manure dry and decompose for a few weeks or mix it into compost before applying it.
ga: Manɔ hee mli wa tsɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii ashishifãi kɛ baai ashã. Esa akɛ oha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni efite otsii fioo komɛi loo okɛfutu ŋmeii lɛ amli dani okɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow even after I apply my homemade liquid plant food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tso niyenii ni ji nu ni afee yɛ shia tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the plant is still short on nitrogen, or that the liquid fertilizer was too strong and scorched the roots. Homemade liquid plant food usually needs to be diluted with water so it doesn't stress the plant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shãa. Bei pii lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ nu awo tso niyenii ni ji nu ni afee yɛ shia lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ekɛ haomɔ akaha tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to spread fertilizer on top of the soil or bury it near the roots?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mafu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: Burying or covering fertilizer with a thin layer of soil near the base of the plant is better because sunlight and rain can easily wash away or evaporate fertilizer left exposed on top of the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ bibioo ni akɛfuɔ loo akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ Ebɛŋkɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ hi fe fɛɛ. Ejaakɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo etsɔ lasu oya.

english: Why do my crops look wilted and burnt after I apply fertilizer to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi ni eshã beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer gives plants nutrients, but putting too much directly against the plant stem burns the plant's tissue. Fertilizer should always be placed a few inches away from the main stem when the soil is moist.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ baashã tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi be fɛɛ be kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: When should I ask an agricultural extension officer before mixing my own crop nutrients at home?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabi mi-agriculture extension agent lɛ dani mikɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi-ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afutu mli yɛ shia?

english: You should speak with an agricultural officer before mixing unfamiliar substances or chemicals at home, as incorrect mixtures can damage your soil, poison your crops, or harm your health.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ agba sane dani okɛ nibii loo tsofai ni oleee afutu mli yɛ shia. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ejaaa lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyɛ poison kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii loo ebaanyɛ eye ohewalɛ awui

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of key soil nutrients like phosphorus and potassium, which help flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing tall and thin, but producing very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo shi ewoɔ dumɔwui bibii waa lɛ?

english: Maize grows tall and weak when plants are overcrowded or receive too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients. Proper spacing gives each stalk enough sunlight and food to build strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Abɛi daa ni egbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell if my crop is wilting because of a disease or just from lack of rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigbo loo nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ kɛkɛ hewɔ?

english: Plants thirsty for water usually droop during the hot afternoon sun and revive in the cool morning, whereas diseased plants often develop permanent spots, yellowing, or rotting patches that stay even after watering.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛbaa wala mli ekoŋŋ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ he ko ni ehiɔ shi daa. Yellowing loo fitemɔ ni eshwɛɔ yɛ nu ni awo lɛ sɛɛ po

english: How do I know if my farm soil is low on food before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had pale or yellowish leaves, or gave a poor harvest, your soil is likely low in nutrients. Watching plant leaf color and growth speed gives clear clues about soil health.
ga: Kɛji onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ loo kpamɔ ni ehiii Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hu faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso ko baa su kɛ bɔ ni edaa oya lɛ, ehaa wɔleɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha.

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves and delicate stems that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need living shade crops like plantains or bananas to cover them like umbrellas and keep the soil moist until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni hiɛ ka ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo banana. koni ekɛha nɔ tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth, or that heavy rains have washed the plant food too deep into the soil for the roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa tsei aniyenii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: When cassava plants are packed too closely, their roots compete under the ground for nutrients and water, while their leaves fight for sunlight above ground, resulting in tall thin plants with very small tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni ebaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe tseee, ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why are small worms suddenly eating holes through the middle of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei bibioo ko ye bu ko ni yɔɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ teŋ trukaa lɛ?

english: Those worms are likely Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs inside the growing heart of the plant; they feed rapidly on the soft inner leaves before the plant has a chance to develop its full stem and leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ tsei atsui ni miida lɛ mli. Eyeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ oya dani tso lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni eyi obɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruit when the weather becomes too hot during the day, when soil moisture changes too drastically, or when the plant does not have enough strength to feed the developing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa loo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaahã aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my vegetable crops with dry grass or dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry foliage acts like a protective blanket that traps water in the soil, keeps root zones cool under the hot sun, and stops weed seeds from getting the light they need to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkaná la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster after the first heavy rains than when I water them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ fe beni mikɛ niji shwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater picks up natural nitrogen directly from the air as it falls, giving your crops a sudden boost of natural fertilizer that wakes up soil organisms and triggers rapid leafy growth.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ beni egbeeɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ trukaa. Enɛ teɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala shi ni ehaa baai lɛ daa oya.

english: Growing the same crop on the same plot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific soil pests and diseases to build up and ruin future harvests.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai komɛi ni jɛɔ sũ mli lɛ koni amɛto wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ ni amɛfite.

english: Extra shoots act like extra hungry mouths that steal food, water, and nutrients from the main parent stem, causing the main plantain tree to grow slowly and yield smaller bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ waa ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantain titri lɛ daa blɛoo ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Yam plants create tubers by capturing sunlight through their leaves; when vines climb tall stakes, the leaves spread out high above the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight to make bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei feɔ bulbs kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛmɔɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ wain tso lɛ kwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ koni amɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller cobs and tubers when I plant many seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for nutrients, sunlight, and water in the soil. Giving each plant proper space allows its roots to spread wide and absorb enough food to produce big crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of a maize plant are usually a sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow fast. The plant moves its remaining food to the new leaves at the top to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa oya. Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi.

english: Why does my cassava produce very bushy top leaves but tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yiteŋ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen or if the soil is too hard and compacted, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Soft, well-tilled soil helps energy move downward into thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ, Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa hewalɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and thin leaves that lose water very quickly in dry, hot winds. They need temporary shade plants, like plantains or cassava, overhead to block harsh sunlight and keep the surrounding air moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Okɛwo oyitso nɔ koni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ atsĩ naa. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why am I finding small ragged holes in my maize leaves overnight when I cannot see any animals on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome Akɛni minaaa kooloo ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hewɔ lɛ.

english: Ragged holes in leaves are often caused by night-feeding caterpillars like Fall Armyworm that hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the hot day and eat the tender leaves while you are away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni taoɔ niyenii gbɛkɛ, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bulɛ baa baai ni ekumɔ lɛ amli. Ni oye baai bibii lɛ be mli ni obɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Covering the soil, which is called mulching, acts like a blanket that stops the hot sun from evaporating water out of the soil. It keeps the ground cool, keeps moisture in, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ mlɛo.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, too little water, or too much water. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. nu fioo tsɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ Kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli lɛ he.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up toward the sun to make food. When yam leaves climb high on stakes, they capture maximum sunlight, which helps the plant build large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he bɔni afee ni efee niyenii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ baai lɛ kwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ Ebaamɔ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ bulbs agboi ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single season without resting the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe lɛ ehiii.

english: Every crop takes specific food nutrients out of the soil. Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients over and over, causing the soil to become tired and weak, which attracts pests and leads to poor harvests.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ shii abɔ. Ehaa etɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛbaa, ni ehaaa akpaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds are stronger and grow faster than most farm crops. Even with good rain, weeds quickly drink up the fertilizers and soil nutrients before your crops have a chance to feed on them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ahe wa ni amɛdaraa oya fe okwaayeli mli nibii babaoo. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Jwɛi hu nuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ amɛyeɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots swell up big under the ground while the top leaves stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shi ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally store extra energy and food inside their underground roots as they grow. This causes the roots to swell into large, starch-rich tubers that are ready to be harvested.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii krokomɛi toɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli beni edaa lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii agboi ni starch eyi mli obɔ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why are my yams cracking open under the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miitswa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yams often crack when heavy rains come suddenly after a long dry spell. The inside of the yam swells with water very fast, expanding faster than the hard outer skin can stretch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes fãa kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ba trukaa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nu baafu oya yɛ sweet potato lɛ mli. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly collapse and die in a day or two even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that enters the roots and blocks the plant's internal tubes. Even if the soil is wet, water cannot move up the stem, causing the plant to wither rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni boteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ anaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ Nu nyɛŋ aya ŋwɛi kɛyashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ oya.

english: Why is the top center or 'heart' of my oil palm tree turning soft and rotting away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã loo ‘tsui’ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as bud rot. Bacteria or fungal infections enter the growing point at the very center of the palm, causing the core tissue to rot and stopping the tree from producing new leaves.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ hiŋmɛi ni egbo. Muawai loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko boteɔ he ko ni dalɛ yɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ haa fãji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ afee baai heei.

english: Why do my young green cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, humid conditions. It quickly rots the pod tissue, causing green pods to turn black and dry out before they can ripen.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ehaa pod lɛ mli fãji lɛ fiteɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: My maize plants are turning yellow and drying up from the bottom leaves—does this mean my farm is infected with a disease?
ga: Mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Not necessarily. As maize plants reach full maturity, they naturally pull water and food from their lower leaves into the cob. When the leaves dry out at the end of the season, it is a normal sign that harvest time has arrived.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli amɛgbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ gĩ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ Eji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my cowpea plant leaves drop off on their own just as the pods turn brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally shut down their leaves at the end of their life cycle. The plant focuses all remaining energy into drying out the seeds inside the pods so they can be harvested and stored safely.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naagbee. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ tsuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ni egbiɔ lɛ he nii. No hewɔ lɛ abaanyɛ akpa amɛ ni akɛto shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain suckers stop producing large bunches after bearing fruit for a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekpaa ŋmɔji wuji ni amɛwoɔ yibii afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: A single plantain stem naturally dies after producing one bunch. While new suckers sprout around it, the old root system gets tired and nutrients in the soil decrease over time, leading to smaller bunches unless the field is replanted.
ga: Plantain tso kome baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo sɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ Shishifãi momo lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa ja adu tsei heei

english: Cocoa trees drop their leaves during dry periods as a natural survival mechanism. Losing leaves reduces water loss through evaporation, allowing the trunk and roots to stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: How can I tell if my pineapple is naturally ready for harvest or if it is spoiling early in the heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-pineapple lɛ efee klalo kɛha adebɔɔ mli ŋmaa loo kɛji egboɔ oya yɛ latsaa be mli?

english: A healthy, ripening pineapple changes color from dark green to golden yellow starting from the base and moving upward, accompanied by a sweet smell. If it turns dark brown and soft all at once without a pleasant smell, it is rotting rather than ripening.
ga: Pineapple ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehiɛ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ. Kɛji etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efee blɛoo shikome ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ egbo fe ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do I need to place wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in the sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and helping the yam tubers grow much larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why do my crops dry up and wilt so fast even when it rained just a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboɔ oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Your soil may lack organic matter like compost or decomposed manure, which acts like a sponge to hold water. Without organic matter, heat quickly evaporates moisture from sandy or poor soil, leaving the crop roots dry.
ga: Ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ŋmɛɔ nu lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋã loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso shishifãi ni egbi

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that your soil is running low on nitrogen, a major food for crops. When nitrogen is scarce, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii Beni nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛkɛye ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the sap. Treating the plants early stops these pests from spreading viruses that stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Tsei ahe nitsumɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akagbɛ helai ni haaa tsei adara lɛ ashwã.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have roots that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts like free fertilizer for your maize while giving you two different crops from the same land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn lɛ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni jɛ he kome lɛ haa.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crop varieties lose their strength in the second generation, leading to uneven growth and smaller yields. Buying certified seeds ensures every plant grows strong and yields well.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni faaa. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha tso fɛɛ tso ada waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or when there are no tiny insects like midges around to pollinate them. Providing light shade and keeping the soil moist helps flowers set into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ hulutsoo ni mli tse ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is mature and ready to harvest under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to swell and crack as the tubers expand beneath the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them all over the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in rows leaves clear paths so you can weed and apply fertilizer easily without trampling your crops. It also ensures every plant gets equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow properly.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ baa. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi awo mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ ni okɛ onaji shwieee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Ekwɛɔ hu koni tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops after I clear and plant my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant in the soil for years waiting for sunlight. Clearing the land exposes those weed seeds to light and rain, allowing them to sprout rapidly before your main crops get established.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni emɛɔ hulu la. Kɛ́ ajie jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaha nakai jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ aná la kɛ nugbɔ. Ha amɛkwɛ̃ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aje shishi etswa shi.

english: How can looking at my crops help me know that the rain is going to stop for a long time?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ baaye abua mi ni male kɛji nugbɔ lɛ baakpa nɛmɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Crops show early signs of water stress, such as curling their leaves, dropping flowers, or changing leaf color. When large varieties start doing this, it indicates that water in the soil is running low and a dry spell is coming.
ga: Tsei jieɔ nu he haomɔ he okadii mra, tamɔ baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ fɔfɔi ni egbɔjɔ. loo baai lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ Beni kooloi wuji bɔi enɛ feemɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ miiba.

english: Why do my crops roll up their leaves like pencils when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tamɔ pensil yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from the sun. By hiding part of the leaf surface, the crop reduces water loss through evaporation and saves moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ekomɛi ni akɛteeɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do tree leaves fall off before the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi dani harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Plants shed leaves to survive dry periods. Leaves lose a lot of water to the dry air, so dropping them helps the crop conserve moisture inside its stems and roots until rain returns.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Baai laajeɔ nu babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛshwie shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow when the plants are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Tso lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plants lack nitrogen, which is the key nutrient needed to grow healthy green leaves. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil beyond the reach of young roots, or the soil simply needs manure or fertilizer to feed the crop.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adara lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ashɛ he. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmei loo ŋmei koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot weather, lack of water in the soil, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend all its energy growing big leaves instead of fruiting.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛkɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kpe, nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛ́ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo ha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: This leaf damage is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the plant. When infected, the plant cannot make enough food, causing deformed leaves and smaller tubers at harvest.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Agbɛnɛ ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Beni hela lɛ emɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa baai bibii ni efite kɛ bulbs baa kɛji akpa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. When rain is frequent and cocoa trees are planted too close together or surrounded by tall weeds, humidity stays trapped in the farm and allows the fungus to grow on the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ shii abɔ ni aduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle amɛhe lɛ. Fɛ̃i baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eha ŋmeii akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in high afternoon heat to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the sun and stop moisture from escaping. If the leaves unfold and recover in the cool evening, the plant is simply protecting itself, but if they remain wilted at night, the soil needs water.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba baa lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi, ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi ni amɛhe wa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛkɛ. Shi kɛji egbo lolo gbɛkɛ lɛ Nu he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ hu.

english: How can I check if my soil has enough water for my crops before the leaves start wilting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani baai lɛ aje shishi amɛgboi?

english: Dig a small hole about hand-depth near your crop's roots, scoop up a handful of soil, and squeeze it in your palm. If the soil forms a ball that holds together, there is enough water; if it crumbles easily like dry dust, your plants need watering.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu bibioo ko ni miihe ashɛ onine mlibotemɔ he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe. Kpɔ̃ɔ sũ ni okɛwo onine mli lɛ ni okɛmimɔ onine mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ fee bɔɔlu ni kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ lolo. Kɛji efoɔ oya tamɔ sũ ni egbi lɛ Ehe miihia ni awo otsei lɛ nu.

english: When several maize seeds are planted in one hole, the growing stalks compete against each other for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This leaves all the plants thin and weak, resulting in small or empty corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy winds while my neighbor's trees stay standing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallow in the ground and struggle to support heavy bunches of fruit during high winds. If soil is eroded or root-damaging pests like nematodes are in the dirt, the roots lose their anchor unless you support the tree with wooden props.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ nɔ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo wu loo kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi, tamɔ nematodes yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baafee nɔ ni amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe. Ja okɛ nɔ ko ni akɛ tso fee miifi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mifolɔ amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they suffer cuts from cutlasses during harvest or are left sitting in the hot sun. Tiny wounds allow fungi and bacteria from the soil to enter the tuber, so keeping harvested yams shaded, dry, and stored in a well-ventilated barn prevents early decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛ dade shwie nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nibii bibii ni afolɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ wo shĩa mli, ni egbi, ni ehi shĩa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite oya.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder and get small holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powder ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Insects called grain weevils burrow into dry corn to feed and lay eggs. If maize is not thoroughly dried until hard and protected in airtight bags or treated with approved storage dust, weevils will multiply rapidly and destroy the grain harvest.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛwo wɔji. Kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa ni abu he yɛ kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo akɛ sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ he lɛ etsu he nii. Kplukai lɛ faa oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmaa ni akpaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing vital food in the soil, especially nitrogen, or that too much standing water is suffocating their roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ, ni no haa eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: No, not all rice needs flooded fields; while lowland rice thrives in standing water which suppresses weeds, upland rice varieties can grow on regular dry farmland powered only by rainfall.
ga: Dabi, jeee ŋmãa ŋmɔji fɛɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shi ŋmãa henɔi ni kɛlɛ fe no lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ okwaayeli hei ni nugbɔ haa hewalɛ lɛ pɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop grow a tall flower at the top before the ears of corn show up on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi fɔfɔi lɛ daa dani toi lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The flower at the top is called a tassel, and it produces pollen that must drop onto the sticky silks below so that the corn kernels can actually form.
ga: Atsɛɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ akɛ tassel. Ni ejieɔ pollen ni esa akɛ egbee siliki ni shwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ afee diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my tall rice plants fall flat on the ground right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over, known as lodging, when heavy winds hit plants that grew too tall and top-heavy, often from using too much nitrogen fertilizer or planting too closely.
ga: Ale ŋmãa tsei ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ hu akɛ shĩai. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa ni etswaa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni etsii tsɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nitrogen ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo loo ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ.

english: Why do my staple crops grow weaker every year if I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every time, whereas rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas restores natural goodness to the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli kpakpafeemɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, resulting in thin stalks and tiny corn ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, ni no haa amɛnáa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Can I safely leave my cassava crop underground if I am not ready to harvest it yet?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe? Ni kɛji akɛ mifeee klalo akɛ makpa nii lolo hu?

english: Yes, cassava roots can safely remain stored naturally in the ground for several months after maturing, though leaving them too long will make the roots tough and woody.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ato adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ oshi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni amɛfee tamɔ tso.

english: How do I know if it is safe to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is risky to plant after just one isolated rain because the dry soil can heat up and kill your seeds; it is safer to wait until the rainfall pattern becomes consistent.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ adɔ ni efite dumɔwui lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the central, folded leaves inside my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye baai ni abɔle amɛhe yɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a destructive pest that burrows deep inside the growing funnel of maize plants to feed on tender new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni eye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crop's growth even when my crop plants are already taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ fioo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo moŋ.

english: Even short weeds have roots that steal moisture, space, and applied fertilizer from under the soil, depriving your main crops of the nutrients they need to yield heavily.
ga: Jwɛi kukuji po yɛ shishifãi ni juɔ nu, ŋwɛi, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa onibii titrii lɛ náaa niyenii kpakpai ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my corn plants turn yellow in a V-shape down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the middle of older leaves is a sign that your corn is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-ŋmei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Amɛji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize grow much better when I plant cowpeas in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which acts as natural fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Muawai bibii yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas mli. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why are the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off instead of turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ani amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from water stress, extreme heat, or a lack of tiny insects called midges that are needed to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nu mli haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ amɛhe lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ gnats ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔii ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot so fast during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess moisture allows a fungus that causes Black Pod disease to spread quickly. Pruning shade branches to let air flow through helps dry out the farm and prevent the rot.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbiɔ ni ehaaa efite.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with leafy stems but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen, the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves and branches on top instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei niji wuji yɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Yam leaves need to catch direct sunlight to make food for the growing tuber underground, and staking lifts the leaves off the wet soil where damp rot diseases live.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. ni owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ he ni helai ni fiteɔ nii yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Too many small shoots suck food and water away from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves enough energy for the main plant to yield big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso bibii babaoo tsɔ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie tsei bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ niji agboi ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from underneath the leaves, or by a plant virus carried by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ji whiteflies ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ amli

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes rotting before they get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔi lɛ miifite dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot draw up enough calcium from the soil, usually because of irregular watering during dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do I get a smaller total harvest when I plant my seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibiiwoo fɛɛ nɔ bibioo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants that yield much smaller crops.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without producing any fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flowers, preventing fertilization. When daytime temperatures get too high, tomato plants drop their flowers to save water and energy until the weather cools down.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and wilting in the strong afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl during intense heat to reduce their surface area, which helps the plant conserve water and prevent drying out under the harsh sun.
ga: Ha yitsɔi abɔle ehe yɛ latsaa bei amli koni eha nɔ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛtsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi.

english: Why do my green vegetable fruits get white, burnt spots on the side facing the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi greens lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ kɛ shãa yɛ afã ni kwɛɔ hulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is called sunscald, which happens when direct, harsh heat cooks the plant tissue. Leaving enough leafy foliage on the plant helps shade and protect the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ shãa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ hoɔ tso lɛ mli fãji. Kɛ́ oshi baai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha hulutsoo aba ni ebu aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to germinate when I sow them in very hot dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: High soil temperatures combined with lack of moisture can dry out seeds or kill the delicate young sprouts before they can break through the surface.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo egbe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly when left under the hot sun at the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Picked produce continues to breathe and generate heat; strong sunlight speeds up rot and softens produce quickly, so keeping harvested crops in the shade immediately prevents early spoilage.
ga: Yibii ni akpɛ lɛ yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa. Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo oya, ni ebaaha amɛgbɔjɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ to hulutsoo be mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekafite mra.

english: How can I keep my harvested leafy vegetables fresh for a few days without a refrigerator?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai ni mikpa lɛ ahi shi gbii fioo komɛi ni mikɛwooo friji mli?

english: You can keep vegetables fresh by placing them in a cool, dark space or constructing a simple zero-energy cool chamber using damp sand and bricks, which cools produce naturally without electricity.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha o-vegetables lɛ afee ehee kɛtsɔ amɛ ni oookɛwo he ko ni mli ejɔ ni duŋ ewo mli lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ ŋã kɛ brikii ni mli efɔ ama tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni hewalɛ ko bɛ mli. Enɛ baaha aduawai kɛ aduawai lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni akɛ srawa hewalɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and turn soft so fast when taking them to the market on hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya kɛ́ mikɛtee jara nɔ yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Heat causes fruit to produce ethylene gas much faster, which triggers quick ripening. Covering produce with wet sacks during transport keeps them cool and slows down ripening.
ga: Dɔlɛ lɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ ethylene gas oya kwraa. ni shwereɔ oya Kɛ́ okɛ kotokui ni mli ewo nu ha o-fruits kɛ vegetables lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni okɛ amɛ yaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛha amɛhe ajɔ ni eha amɛshweremɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why does my harvested cassava turn dark and spoil within just three days of digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni akpa lɛ su mli ewo duŋ ni efiteɔ yɛ gbii etɛ pɛ mli beni atsa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots react quickly to air and heat after harvest, causing rapid chemical decay. Storing tubers in damp sawdust or underground pits keeps them cool and delays rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he nii oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Ehaa tsofai lɛ fiteɔ oya Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo ŋmeii ni mli ewo fɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ bu ko mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha amɛkafite.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dried grass or leaves during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under the strong sun and stops water from evaporating away from crop roots.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe.

english: Can strong sunlight harm my young vegetable seedlings, and how do I protect them?
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aye mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ awui. Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Yes, young seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Building simple shade structures using palm fronds or netting shields them until they grow stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Feemɔ hulutsoo he gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛtsɔ ŋmei loo ŋshɔŋloo nɔ ni okɛha nɔ kɛyashi ebaawa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning light yellow and growing so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo waa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build green leaves and stems. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives your maize the nourishment it needs to grow strong and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my land needs fertilizer before I start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: If your previous harvest was smaller than usual, or if your crops look pale and weak, the soil has likely lost its nutrients. Testing the soil or adding organic manure restores the soil's strength so your next crops can thrive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onikpamɔ ni okpa tsutsu lɛ faaa fe bɔ ni sa Aloo kɛji akɛ onibii ni okpa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ? Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ elaaje. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are small holes suddenly appearing on my crop leaves, and what should I check for every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii miije kpo trukaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ daa leebi?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by hungry pests like caterpillars or armyworms. Walking through your farm every morning to inspect under leaves helps you spot these insects early before they destroy your whole harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmeii loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ onyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa leebi koni oyakwɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kooloi bibii nɛɛ mra. Dani ebaakpãtã onibii fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during cool, wet weather. Clearing weeds, cutting away extra shade branches to let sunlight in, and removing infected pods keeps the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. weeding Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ mli koni hulu la abote mli. kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and drying up even when the ground is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by bacterial wilt or root pests that block water from moving up the stem. Rotating your tomato field with crops like maize or cassava helps clean the soil for future plantings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ jɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekaya tso lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Tomato ŋmɔji ni atsakeɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ dumɔwui.

english: Why are the roots of my cassava rotting underground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits pooled around them for too long, cutting off air to the roots. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I tell if my plantain suckers are getting thirsty during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kumai yeɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: When plantain leaves roll inward, turn brown at the edges, or hang limply, the plant is struggling with drought. Covering the soil around the base with dry grass or leaves keeps moisture trapped in the ground longer.
ga: Beni plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ mli lɛ Baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. loo efo fioo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ miikpe. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need lots of sunlight to make food for the growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp earth toward the sun, which prevents leaf diseases and helps produce bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Enɛ tsiɔ foliar hela naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa ŋmeii wuji.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when temperatures get too hot, when plants lack water, or when there are no beneficial insects to pollinate them. Regular watering and keeping the soil cool helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ tsei amli loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce empty shells with no nuts inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when the soil lacks essential minerals like calcium while the nuts are forming. Adding agricultural lime or wood ash to your soil before planting helps the pods fill up with plump seeds.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miifee. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ aba.

english: If I put strong fertilizer directly inside the planting hole with my seeds, will it make the crops grow faster?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ adara oya?

english: Putting chemical fertilizer directly in the hole with seeds can burn the delicate young roots and prevent the seed from growing. Fertilizer should be placed a short distance away from the seed or stem so the crop can feed safely without root damage.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ dumɔwu loo tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aye lɛ shweshweeshwe ni efiteee shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why did my maize leaves turn brown and scorch after I applied fertilizer right against the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts. When it touches the stem directly, it draws moisture out of the plant tissues, causing fertilizer burn. Always place fertilizer in a circle or line a few inches away from the stem base.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãji amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashãa lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ kokroo nɔ loo inchi fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Is it safe to put raw manure deep into the planting hole right before dropping my seeds?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔŋ baawo dumɔ bu lɛ mli dani adu dumɔwui?

english: Fresh manure generates heat and releases harsh gases as it breaks down, which can kill young roots inside the hole. Manure should be fully rotted and mixed into the soil weeks before planting, or applied around the base of growing plants.
ga: Manɔ hee haa dɔlɛ baa ni ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa beni efiteɔ lɛ. ni baanyɛ afite shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo kwraa ni akɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli otsii babaoo dani adu loo akɛwo tso ni adu lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Why is it bad to give my crops fertilizer when the farm soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani eji nɔ fɔŋ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa?

english: Crops can only drink their food when it is dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil leaves strong chemical salts resting directly on roots, which scorches the plant instead of nourishing it.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ anu niyenii kɛji akɛ atsɔ nu mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ ashã yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell if my soil is hungry and needs extra food for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni niyenii babaoo he miihia mi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Hungry soil produces weak crops with yellowish leaves, thin stalks, and poor harvests. If your crops stay small despite receiving good rain, it means the soil lacks essential nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ, tsei bibii, kɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii baa. Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I use kitchen waste like cassava peels and plantain skins directly to feed my growing crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shĩa mli jwɛi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ŋmei atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ niyenii?

english: Kitchen waste can feed crops, but it should be composted into rich dirt first. Placing raw food scraps directly next to growing roots can attract pests and create rot that harms your crops.
ga: Kpataashi mli jwɛi baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii. Shi esa akɛ afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Niyenii ni ahoo lɛ ni okɛaawo shishifãi ni miida lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ agbala kooloi ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why do my crops yield less food every year even though I clear the land properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni mikɛjie jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Crops absorb nutrients from the ground every growing season. If you continuously plant and harvest without adding manure, compost, or fertilizer back into the soil, the soil gets tired and empty.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa. Kɛji odu ni okpa nii be fɛɛ be ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: If weeds grow right next to my crops, are they taking food away from my plants?
ga: Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe Ani jwɛi baajie niyenii kɛjɛ mi tsei lɛ amli?

english: Yes, weeds act like uninvited guests at a farm meal. They aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from your crops, leaving your plants weak and unfed.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni afɔ̃ko amɛ nine yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ kɛ yiwalɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why do my young cassava plants wither so easily under the heat even after I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo enɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow roots that cannot reach deep moisture, and their tender leaves lose water fast in direct sun. Covering the soil around the plant base with dried grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni amɛbaai bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing thick green leaves but refusing to produce any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse shi ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen-rich food makes them produce heavy green leaves while forgetting to make flowers and fruits. Plants need balanced nutrients, including phosphorus, to produce good yield.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tso lɛ lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ehiɛ kpaa nɔ akɛ ebaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. ni fɔsfɔs fata he bɔni afee ni aná nibii kpakpai

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantains around them keeps the soil moist and protects the leaves from burning until the trees are strong enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa baa lɛ shãaa kɛyashiɔ tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: How many years will it take for my new cocoa tree to start giving me pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-cacao tso hee lɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take 3 to 5 years to start producing pods, while improved hybrid seeds can begin bearing fruit in about 2 to 3 years if cared for well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can flow through. This prevents fungal diseases from spreading in damp shade and helps the tree send energy to growing bigger pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ agbɛ ashwa yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ yaa ŋmɔji wuji amli.

english: Why does letting tall weeds grow around my cocoa trees lower my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kakadaji ni mihaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water and soil nutrients away from cocoa roots. They also create places for harmful insects like capsids to hide and attack your pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli. Amɛhaa gbɛ hu haa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ oshara, tamɔ capsids, koni amɛtee amɛhe ni amɛtutua o-pods lɛ.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trunk drop off before growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if they do not get enough water or plant nutrients, or if tiny beneficial insects called midges are not present to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛnáaa nu loo tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi fioo komɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ yɛ?

english: How do I know exactly when a cocoa pod is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color, usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange. You can also hear a hollow sound when you tap a fully ripe pod.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. loo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ mli kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ Obaanyɛ onu gbee ni mli ewo muji hu kɛji ota ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet and dark weather. Removing infected pods quickly and keeping the farm clear helps stop it from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rains often mean the soil is waterlogged and root growth is blocked, or key nutrients are being washed away from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ, ni shishifãi lɛ hu tsiɔ amɛnaa. loo ajieɔ niyenii mli nibii titrii lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli

english: Why do I need to heap my harvested cocoa beans and cover them with plantain leaves for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ anaa ni mikɛ plantain baai haa nɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Covering wet beans triggers fermentation, an essential process that removes bitterness, turns the purple beans brown, and creates the rich chocolate flavor buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ ha nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ mlifu kɛjɛɔ mli. Akɛ Purple Beans lɛ afee Brown ni afee tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: How does a long dry season affect my cocoa trees and their yield?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa kookoo tsei kɛ amɛmli nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extended dry weather causes cocoa trees to drop leaves to save water, which makes developing pods stay small, dry up early, or fail to mature properly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ feɔ bibii, amɛgbiɔ oya, loo amɛdarako kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because full sunlight dries out their leaves and roots easily. Leaving some mature trees or planting shade crops like plantain creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from harsh sunlight and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni eda loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green foliage. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the crop regain its deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits around the roots for too long, it drowns them and allows rot-causing fungi to multiply, which is why planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Amɛbaagbee nu mli ni amɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why are insects eating small holes in my pepper plant leaves, and how does it hurt my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi yeɔ buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ Ni te eeye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ?
