english: Insects eat leaves to feed themselves, which weakens the plant because leaves act as food factories that use sunlight to produce energy. Damaged leaves mean the pepper plant has less energy to produce big, healthy pepper fruits.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ baai koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛna niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ejaakɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii afeemɔ nitsumɔhei ni kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ hewalɛ. Baai ni efite lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmei agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato plants often drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water. When the plant feels threatened by dry conditions, it sheds its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival rather than producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ miiwo amɛhe gbeyei lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why do my neighbor's yams grow so much bigger than mine when we planted at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo fe mi nɔ lɛ, kɛ́ wɔdu amɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow larger when the soil is loose enough for roots to expand freely and when the vines are supported by tall stakes. Staking keeps the leaves high up in the sunlight, allowing the plant to make more food for the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baagbɛ eshwa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse bɔ ni sa ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ni kɛ́ wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ni fiɔ esɛɛ lɛ, Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Does leaving weeds around my young plantain suckers hurt them, or do weeds protect the soil?
ga: Jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi plantain dumɔwui lɛ miipila amɛ loo jwɛi lɛ miibu shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: While weeds can shade soil, aggressive weeds actively steal water, light, and nutrients away from young plantain suckers. Clearing a small circle around the base of each sucker removes competition so the plantain gets all the resources it needs to grow quickly.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ Shi jwɛi ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ juɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ amli. ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛibɔfoi bibii ni bɔleɔ ŋwɛibɔfoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi lɛ haa akaŋshii baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, feemɔ ekãa ni oná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni onyɛ oda oya.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and dry up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani akpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, humid conditions. Pruning dense branches lets air flow through the farm and sunlight dry out moisture, which stops the fungus from easily spreading between pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni hulu la lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ mlɛo.

english: Why does my land produce less maize every year even though I plant the exact same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni midu yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously consumes the same nutrients from the soil season after season without giving the earth time to recover. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts valuable nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii yɛ be kɛ bei amli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen ni jara wa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer directly against the stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer directly touching the main stem can burn the tender plant skin and shallow feeder roots due to high mineral concentration. Placing fertilizer in a small ring around the plant allows the roots to safely reach out and drink the nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni kɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ hiɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ yɛ mineral ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Ebɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛnuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I help my crops survive when the rains are very small this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your plants with dry grass or leaves, which is called mulching. This acts like a shade blanket that traps moisture in the ground and stops the sun from drying out the soil too quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. tsei ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo tsɔne ni haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaa hulu lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: Which crops are best for me to plant when I know the rainy season will be short?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu beni mile akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baafee kuku lɛ?

english: Crops like cowpeas, cassava, millet, and early-maturing maize varieties are good choices because they either store water well in their roots or grow quickly before the rain stops completely.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina, ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni shwereɔ mra lɛ ji nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli loo amɛdaraa oya dani nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ kwraa.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when I plant them right after a tiny rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need steady moisture in the top layer of soil to sprout. If the rain was too small, the hot sun dries the ground back out very fast, causing the seeds to dry up and die inside the soil before they can come up.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛ fioo tsɔ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya waa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight like straws during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water in the harsh heat. By curling, less leaf area is exposed to the direct sun, helping the plant save water until the cool evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɛɛ baa lɛ he fioo ko pɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtoɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers when the rain stops for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: When a plant does not get enough water, it enters survival mode. It drops its flowers to save water and energy just to keep its stem and leaves alive.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli. Ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite koni eha shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ ahi shi kɛkɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are turning yellow because of poor rain or because the soil is weak?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ hewɔ?

english: If poor rain is the problem, the whole plant will look limp and soft during the heat of the day. If weak soil is the problem, the plant will stay standing tall, but the lower leaves will turn pale yellow while remaining firm.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbonyo ji naagba lɛ Tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ he naagba lɛ Tso lɛ baadamɔ shi shiŋŋ. Shi baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ be mli ni eyɛ shiŋŋ lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay very small and woody when there is a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants need water to produce food in their leaves and store it in their roots. Without enough water, the plant cannot make or send that food downward, so the tubers remain thin and hard.
ga: Cassava tsei hia nu koni amɛfee niyenii yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee loo amɛmaje niyenii kɛya shi. No hewɔ lɛ, yitso lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ mlɛo ni ewaa.

english: Why is it better for me to water my plants or apply fertilizers very early in the morning at 5:30 AM?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ loo mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli leebi maŋkpa nɛkɛ yɛ 5:30 a.m.?

english: In the cool early morning, plants drink up water and food easily without losing it to evaporation. In the hot sun, water evaporates before the roots can take it in, and heavy heat can burn plants mixed with fertilizer.
ga: Yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mlɛo ni amɛmli la ni hoɔ lɛ sɛɛ efooo. Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Nu lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efutu mli lɛ.

english: Why does my land give me fewer crops every year even though I work hard on it every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni mitsuɔ nii waa daa afi?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same piece of land year after year eats up all the specific plant food in the soil. Rotating your crops, like planting beans or groundnuts after maize, gives the soil a chance to recover.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ yeɔ tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: What can I do with the dry plant stalks left on my farm after harvest instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛ tsei ni egbi ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Leaving dry crop stalks on the field to rot or burying them into the soil turns them into natural plant food. It feeds the earth and helps the ground hold onto rainwater better for the next season.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ahe tsei ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛgboi loo afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over time and carry diseases, while certified seeds are specially produced to resist pests, grow uniformly, and give much higher yields to make your farm profitable.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni ekɛ helai baa. Yɛ be mli ni afee dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai. kwɛ̃ɔ daa ni ohaa yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo koni eha oŋmɔ lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do commercial hybrid seeds cost more money than traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ jara wa fe dumɔwui ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are carefully bred to produce bigger harvests, grow faster, and handle tough weather better, meaning the high seed cost is usually recovered through a much larger harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. shwereɔ oya ni enyɛɔ ekpeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai anaa jogbaŋŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ahe nyɔmɔwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmaa ni fa babaoo fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: How do I choose which crop to plant so that I can make a good profit at harvest time?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mahala koni manyɛ maná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa yɛ nikpamɔ be mli?

english: To make a profit, you must look at local market demand, buyer prices, and transport costs before planting, rather than growing a crop just because it grows easily in your area.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni oná sɛɛnamɔ Esa akɛ okwɛ nibii ni jarayelihe lɛ taoɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ajara, kɛ nibii ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo dani odu. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu tso ko akɛni ekwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ hewɔ kɛkɛ lɛ.

english: Is it safer for my income to plant only one cash crop or mix different crops on my field?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mishika lɛ akɛ makwɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii kome loo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutu mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Mixing crops reduces your financial risk because if market prices drop or pests destroy one crop, you still have other crops to sell for income.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni okɛfutuɔ nii lɛ haa shika he oshara ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ baa shi. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ jara nɔ jara ba shi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kpata ŋmɔshi nii ko hiɛ. Oyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ koni oná shika.

english: Why can't I just dig a quick hole and drop my seeds anywhere on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mafo bu oya kɛkɛ ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Crops need proper spacing, correct planting depth, and loose soil to spread roots; planting randomly leads to overcrowding and poor crop growth.
ga: Ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná he ko ni sa kɛjɛ amɛhe. dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni ja kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse koni akɛgbɛ shishifãi lɛ ashwã Dumɔ ni aduɔ trukaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ ayiɔ obɔ kɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ ni ehiii.

english: Why do some crops like tomatoes need to be grown in a nursery bed before planting on the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ tomato yɛ ŋmɔji amli dani adu yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny seeds produce delicate sprouts that easily die in full sunshine or get destroyed by insects, so a nursery protects them until they are strong enough for the field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni waaa ni gboiɔ oya kɛji hulu la ni naa wa loo koolooi fiteɔ amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa kɛha okwaayeli.

english: Planting on the first rain is risky because the rains may stop for weeks, causing young seeds to dry up and die before the real rainy season sets in.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ baahi shi otsii babaoo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shɛɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving no plant with enough energy to grow full cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwu ni eyi obɔ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when there is plenty of rainwater on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ babaoo nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Rain provides water but not plant food; yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, which heavy rains can actually wash away.
ga: Nugbɔ haa nu shi ehaaa tsei niyenii. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛya.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield every year if I keep planting the same crop in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests to build up; rotating crops helps the land recover.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or the right nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛná baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing, usually two weeks after germination and again during peak growth. Applying it during heavy downpours will just wash the expensive nutrients away before the roots can eat.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ be mli ni edara waa lɛ Nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni jara wa lɛ he dani shishifãi lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full direct sunlight. Leaving some large shade trees or planting plantains next to cocoa provides temporary living umbrellas that keep the seedlings cool and moist until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Kookoo lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over whenever strong winds blow across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that stay close to the top soil. Heap soil higher around the base of the stem and support heavy fruiting stems with bamboo poles to keep them standing during windstorms.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ. Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ abɔle tso lɛ shishi kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni okɛ ŋmeii afi tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around them for too long. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Giving your plants a regular supply of water keeps the soil cool and helps the flowers stay attached to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes in the leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni aye bu bibioo ko yɛ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on tender maize leaves. Applying recommended botanical treatments like neem extract or an extension-approved spray into the leaf funnel stops them early.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akpa mra.

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny invisible insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice out of the leaves. Controlling these insects early with soapy water sprays or appropriate insecticides allows new leaves to expand normally.
ga: Kplukai bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ aphids loo thrips shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli Mra be mli ni akudɔɔ kooloi nɛɛ Kɛtsɔ nu ni sa ni akɛ saamɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, baa heei lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to long sticks in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei kɛ tsei aniji kakadaji fĩɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct light to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking holds the leafy vines high into the sunlight and prevents leaves from touching wet soil where diseases easily spread.
ga: La tɛ̃ɛ he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tsei ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ ni atsĩ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ he ni hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ he.

english: Why does allowing weeds to grow around my crops make my yield very poor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee gbeyei?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal food, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nutrients they need to yield heavily.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts can capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground. Planting them alongside maize improves soil fertility naturally, helping the maize grow stronger without requiring as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ekɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: If your crops grow very slowly, turn light yellow instead of dark green, or yield much smaller harvests than previous years, your soil has lost essential nutrients and needs fertilizer or organic manure.
ga: Kɛji onibii lɛ daraa blɛoo waa lɛ Ha efee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa fe afi ni eho lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo humus awo mli.

english: Why does my maize crop turn yellow and stop growing when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: When heavy rain floods the soil, water fills the tiny air pockets around the roots, preventing them from breathing. Without oxygen, the roots cannot absorb nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu lɛ, eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa amɛmuɔ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: When is the best time of day for me to water my vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha aduawai nu?

english: The best time to water vegetables is early in the morning. This gives plants the water they need before the sun gets hot and prevents moisture from staying on leaves all night, which causes fungal diseases.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu ji leebi maŋkpa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa nu ni he hiaa amɛ dani hulu lɛ mli dɔɔ tsɔ. ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ahe gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ ni ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ naa.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Affected plants cannot catch sunlight properly, resulting in smaller roots.
ga: Kasava lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any fruits show up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to high heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When plants get stressed by extreme weather, they shed their flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hewɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa ha tsei hao lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my yam seeds rot in the ground before they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam seeds rot when planted in waterlogged soil or when attacked by soil fungi and pests like nematodes. Planting yams on raised mounds allows excess water to drain away, keeping the seeds healthy.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha dumɔwui lɛ awa

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn completely dry and brown, and the kernels become hard. You can test a kernel by pressing it with your thumbnail—if it leaves no dent, it is ready.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Obaanyɛ oka kernel lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ o-thumbnail lɛ ni ooonyɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii komɛi bɛ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ kernel lɛ efee klalo.

english: Why do my stored grains get eaten by insects so quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii yeɔ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains are attacked quickly in storage if they are put away while still damp. Insects like weevils thrive in moist grain, so drying your harvest thoroughly in the sun before storing it keeps the pests away.
ga: Atutuaa ŋmaa oya yɛ nitoohe kɛji akɛ akɛto he ni efɔ. Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmaa ni mli efɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ogbi onibii yɛ hulu mli dani okɛto lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, your soil is running low on nitrogen. The plant is pulling nitrogen out of its old bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Beni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ miigba nitrogen kɛmiijɛ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during their first dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle full sunlight or harsh dry winds. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains planted beside them to block the direct sun and trap moisture around them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la fɛɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ.

english: How do my groundnut plants produce nuts underground when the flowers grow above the dirt?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-peanut tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni fɔfɔi lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Once groundnut flowers are pollinated, their petals fall off and long stems called 'pegs' grow downwards toward the ground. These pegs push themselves deep into the soil, where the nuts actually develop away from light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ shwie shi lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ lɛ daa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, he ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛjɛɔ la lɛ he lɛ.

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause tomato flowers to dry up and fall off. Without moderate temperatures and humidity, the flower fails to self-pollinate, so the plant drops the flower to conserve its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe pollination. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn dark and spoil so fast just two days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fee ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is separated from its stem, chemical reactions begin naturally inside the root to seal the fresh wound, causing it to rot within 48 to 72 hours. It is best to leave cassava roots unharvested in the ground until the exact day you are ready to sell or process them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie ŋmei lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Tsofa ko baa yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛkpa pilamɔ hee lɛ. Ha ni egbo yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni akpaaa kɛyashi gbi ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ loo obaatsu he nii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Lifting the vines off the ground on wooden stakes helps them capture maximum sunlight while keeping the leaves away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa wain tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crowded plants compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Instead of growing thick stems and large cobs, they waste energy stretching tall to reach for light.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli wa lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, moŋ lɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Mohu ɔ, a puɛ a he wami nɛ a kɛ hlaa mɛ konɛ a ya su la a he ɔ.

english: Curled and wrinkled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the undersides of young leaves. The physical damage and viruses they spread cause the leaves to distort as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Gbɔmɔtsoŋ nibii ni fiteɔ kɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in standing water while my cassava roots rot and die in waterlogged soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have hollow channels in their stems that pump oxygen from the air down into their roots underwater. Cassava roots do not have these air tubes, so they drown and rot when underwater for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ tsũi ni mli ewo muji yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛkɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ amɛhi nu shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms with strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have a deep main root; instead, they have a shallow root network near the topsoil supporting a heavy stem and leaves. When heavy rain softens the soil, strong wind pulls these shallow roots out easily.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi titrii ni mli kwɔ. Shi eyɛ shishifã ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Ebɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni fiɔ tsei kɛ baai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Enɛɛmɛi jeɔ kpo mlɛo.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight. Without shade crops like plantain or shade trees to shelter them, the heat burns their leaves and dries out the soil before their root system can mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of essential nutrients in the soil. The plant sheds its flowers as a defense mechanism to save energy and stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he ko ni dɔɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akɛ hebuu gbɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is hungry for nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-abele lɛ kɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ?

english: When maize lacks nitrogen, the lower leaves start turning yellow at the tips, with the yellowing spreading down the center of the leaf in a V-shape while the edges stay green.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔŋ yɛ baa lɛ naa. Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli, yɛ be mli ni eshishigbɛ lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ eŋɔli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives during wet, rainy seasons when the farm is too shady, damp, and unpruned.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewoɔ hulutsoo tsɔ, ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseee.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss. The plant goes dormant to save moisture in its roots and will quickly grow fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tso lɛ yaa wɔɔhe koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he. ni ebaaha baai heei akwɛ̃ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too closely, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, resulting in thin stalks and very small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, ni no haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ dumɔwui bibii bibii loo ni bɛ mli baa.

english: Will planting cowpeas alongside my cassava harm my cassava crop?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ baaye mi ŋmei tso lɛ awui?

english: No, cowpeas actually help cassava. Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural food supply that benefits the surrounding crops.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmei yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Why do some of my tomato seeds fail to sprout after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep, if the soil is packed too tightly for air to reach them, if the soil is too dry, or if fungus in wet soil rots the seed before it sprouts.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ he, Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines naturally dry up and turn yellow, showing that the plant has finished growing above ground and stored all its energy into the tuber below.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that are naturally adapted to steal water, light, and nutrients faster than farm crops, allowing them to overpower cultivated plants if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ tsei ni ama shi lɛ anɔ kunim kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside them provides living cover and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ tsei nɛɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naa.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cassava stem cuttings at an angle instead of straight down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmei niji yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mawo ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle encourages roots to develop evenly on one side slightly close to the surface, which makes the growing tubers bigger and much easier to harvest without breaking them.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei niji yɛ 45 degree angle mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. yɛ fa kome ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ daraa kwraa ni efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa ni ŋmeii lɛ akumɔɔɔ.

english: Yams are vine plants that produce food through their leaves. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves get maximum sunlight and air circulation, which prevents leaves from rotting and helps produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kɛ amɛbaai lɛ feɔ niyenii. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ babaoo lɛ anyɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ agbo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants are a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer top leaves, indicating that fertilizer or compost is needed.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛyaha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases that prefer that crop to build up in the soil. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tsei ni miida lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and essential soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to grow fast and strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛhe wa.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plantain stem. Removing all but one or two healthy suckers concentrates the plant's energy into producing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ plantain tso lɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee plantains wuji ni tsii.

english: Small holes and ragged edges in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the fall armyworm, which hide inside the plant's central whorl and require early control before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni esa akɛ akudɔ mra dani akpata he ni edara yɛ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps flowers develop into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: How do I apply fertilizer so that heavy rain does not carry it away from my crops?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer to dry topsoil right before a downpour causes it to wash away. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, place it a few inches away from the stem, and cover it lightly with soil so the roots can absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Okɛto he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ

english: Why do extension officers ask us to cut down our cocoa trees when they catch a disease instead of just spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ biɔ ni wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei kɛji hela mɔ amɛ moŋ fe ni wɔɔwo amɛ tsofa kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Some serious cocoa diseases, like Swollen Shoot Virus, live deep inside the tree's sap where chemical sprays cannot reach. Cutting down the infected tree stops the disease from spreading underground or through insects to healthy trees nearby.
ga: Kookoo helai komɛi ni naa wa waa, tamɔ bud swelling virus lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi loo kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii anɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: If my cocoa leaves start changing color or looking sick, should I wait to see if they recover on their own?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ bɔi su tsakemɔ loo amɛfee tamɔ helatsɛ Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni mana kɛji ebaaya lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You should not wait, because plant diseases spread fast through insects, wind, or rain. Reporting and treating the problem early prevents a small issue from spread across your whole farm.
ga: Esaaa akɛ okɛ be shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ nɔ. Bɔɔ amaniɛ ni osaa naagbai lɛ mra. Ebaatsi naagbai bibii anaa. Gbalamɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: If only one cocoa tree in my farm looks diseased, will the healthy trees right next to it also get sick?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso kome pɛ yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ, Tso ni wa ni bɛŋkɛ Ani hela baamɔ mi hu?

english: Yes, neighboring trees are at high risk. Diseases often spread invisibly through insect vectors like mealybugs or through root contacts underground before you can see any symptoms on the outside.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ oshara mli waa. Bei pii lɛ, helai gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ gbɛ ni anaaa nɔ kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii, tamɔ mealybugs, loo kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ. Dani obaana okadii ni jɛ kponɔgbɛ

english: Why do cocoa diseases seem to cause more trouble during the rainy season than during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo hela ji naagba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and humidity during the rainy season create the ideal conditions for fungal diseases like Black Pod to grow fast and spread spores across damp cocoa pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amɛshwã ŋmeii ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: What are the most important maintenance routine activities I need to do to keep my cocoa farm safe from sickness?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafee koni mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hela he?

english: Regular weeding, pruning overgrown branches, and removing bad pods help light and air move freely through the farm. This reduces moisture, which stops pests and fungal diseases from multiplying.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ afolɔmɔ Kɛ ŋmeii gbohii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni no haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why is pruning branches good for my cocoa trees if it means cutting off parts of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni afoɔ lɛ hi kɛha mi-kookoo tso lɛ kɛji ehe miihia ni ajie tso lɛ fãi komɛi kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning cuts away useless or overcrowded branches so the tree can send all its water and nutrients directly to growing big, healthy cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ aya kookoo tsei wuji ni mli wa lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabi ni akɛ baai krokomɛi afata he lɛ

english: How long must I wait before planting new cocoa seedlings on a spot where I cut down a diseased tree?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu kookoo tso hee yɛ he ni afo tso ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ yɛ lɛ?

english: You need to make sure the old stump and roots are completely dead before replanting. Leaving the spot clear for a short period ensures the virus or disease dies out so the new seedling stays healthy.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi momo lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ egbo kwraa dani odu ehee. Ni aaashi lɛ faŋŋ be kukuoo ko Ebaaha hela loo hela lɛ agbo. koni dumɔwui heei lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: Can land that has grown cocoa for many years suddenly stop supporting healthy crop growth?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni edu kookoo afii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ sɛɛfimɔ trukaa?

english: Yes, continuous farming over decades drains essential nutrients from the soil. Adding organic fertilizer and properly managing shade helps restore the soil so old farmland can produce well again.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Organic fertilizer kɛ shade nɔkwɛmɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo lɛ anyɛ awo yibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing fewer pods even though I am doing all the regular weeding on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeding helps, but low yields can also be caused by hidden diseases, old tree age, nutrient-poor soil, or poor pollination. Regular inspection helps identify if the tree needs fertilizer or pest treatment.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Shi helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ aba. tso ni egbɔ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ mli lɛ mlikwɛmɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni ana kɛji tso lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai awo mli.

english: Why do traditional farming methods handed down by elders sometimes fail to stop new crop diseases on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ blema okwaayeli gbɛi ni jɛ mi onukpai lɛ adɛŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai heei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: New plant diseases and changes in climate create conditions that traditional practices were not designed to handle. Modern agricultural advice updates old practices to help fight stronger pests and weather changes.
ga: Tsoi ahe helai heei Ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shihilɛi ni afeee blema nifeemɔi koni amɛtsu he nii lɛ baa. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaawoo haa tsutsu nifeemɔi yaa hiɛ. Koni eye ebua ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni mli wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ awuu

english: Why are the young leaves on my cocoa seedlings turning brown and dying in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or plantain plants grown beside them to block direct sun, the leaves dry out, scorch, and die.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni adu yɛ emasɛi lɛ bɛ lɛ, Koni hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsĩ naa lɛ, baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, amɛshãa, ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are there holes in my young maize leaves and small dirt-like powder inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ nibii bibii ni tamɔ muji lɛ? yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing point of the maize plant and leaves behind waste that looks like sawdust. Early scouting and spraying with recommended remedies are needed to protect the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ amli, ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Ehe miihia ni akwɛ ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up, turning yellowish, and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfite lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects or spread by planting infected stems. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers prevents this issue.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ ni miida lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards into the shape of little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Pepper leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by insects. Controlling these tiny insects stops the leaf curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni jɛɔ kooloi amli kɛbaa lɛ nɔ kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when inserting them into the soil?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni ŋmei ni afolɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ he hiaa?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the buds (nodes) pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes delayed growth and significantly reduces the size and yield of tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha edalɛ asɛɛ afo. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibiiwoo baa shi waa.

english: Those extra shoots (suckers) steal water and plant food from the main tree. Pruning them away leaves just one or two strong stems, ensuring the main plant grows large, heavy bunches of plantains.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi (ŋmeii) lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ, tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ ada ni etsɔ plantain jwɛi agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants once the vines start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi kɛji wain tso lɛ ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to make food for growing big tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, improving sunlight exposure and preventing leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ anaa.

english: Purple leaves on maize usually mean the plant is short on phosphorus, a vital plant food needed for root growth. This often happens in nutrient-deficient soils or when cold, wet soil stops roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa nɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni efɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nii.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants falling off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering. When water is inconsistent, the plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy rather than producing tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ nu lɛ ejaaa lɛ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafee tomato.

english: Why do groundnut flower stems bend downward and push themselves into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants produce flowers above ground, but the actual nuts grow underground. After the flowers are pollinated, the stems naturally push themselves down into the earth so the pods can develop in the soil.
ga: Peanut tsei woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight because their root systems are shallow and delicate. Leaving shade trees shields young cocoa from the scorching sun and helps the soil retain water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantain before planting my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛdu cocoa tsei dani amɛdu lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as temporary umbrellas. They shield young cocoa trees from intense heat and drought during their first two years in the field.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ be kukuoo mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Amɛbuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni amɛyeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow instead of dark green even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Rain gives plants water, but without nitrogen, the leaves cannot produce the green color needed to make plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ haa tsei nu. Shi kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ nyɛŋ aha su ni ji eŋɔli ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii aha tsei lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very bushy with lots of leaves, but producing tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani eyɛ yitso bibioo?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava focus its energy on growing tall stems and thick leaves instead of sending energy underground to build large, heavy tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ yaa zugba a sisi konɛ e kɛ pee bulb nguahi nɛ a he wa.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly during cold, rainy, and damp weather. Clearing weeds and removing infected pods helps keep the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, nugbɔshiimɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents them from damaging young leaves and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite baai bibii ni amɛkagbɛ tsei ahe helai amɛshwã.

english: Hot temperatures, sudden dry spells, or irregular watering stress tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering prevents flower drop.
ga: hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ trukaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi Loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that spread out near the top layer of soil. Wet soil combined with heavy fruit bunches and strong wind easily pulls those shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni aduawai akui ni tsii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fata he lɛ gbalaa nakai shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why does my yield go down when I plant maize on the exact same land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows pests that attack it to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like beans restores soil health.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly in the barn after I bring them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eba lɛ?

english: Yams rot if they get bruised or cut during harvesting, or if stored in hot, unventilated rooms. Keeping yams off the ground in a cool, airy barn prevents fungal decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ loo afo amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes to shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Cocoa trees shed leaves to conserve water during dry spells like the Harmattan. Providing shade trees or plantains helps keep the soil cool and reduces heat stress on young cocoa plants.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu yɛ hɔmɔ be mli tamɔ Harmattan. Shade loo plantain ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo ni baa kookoo tsei bibii anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it better to split my fertilizer application into two stages instead of giving it all to my maize at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ abaaja ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo fãi enyɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ awo mli shikome lɛ?

english: Maize plants need nutrients at different growth stages. Applying fertilizer gradually—first at planting and later before flowering—prevents heavy rains from washing away nutrients and feeds the plant when it grows fastest.
ga: Abɛi tsei biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fiofio—shishijee lɛ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ, ni sɛɛ mli lɛ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ—baatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni eha tsei lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I keep my farm soil moist for a longer time during dry periods without watering every day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu bɛ lɛ, ni mikɛ nu wooo nɔ daa gbi?

english: Covering the soil around your crop stems with dry grass, fallen leaves, or cocoa pod husks (called mulching) traps soil moisture, stops weeds from growing, and cools plant roots.
ga: Mulching around Your trunk with dry grass fallen leaves or cocoa pod shell (This is called mulching.) It traps moisture in the soil. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpeas loo beans kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize works well because leguminous plants take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, naturally feeding the maize while making full use of your farm land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha o-corn lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni okɛ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines off the ground using tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ kɛ tso ni nɔ kwɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food for the underground tubers. Staking lifts the foliage off damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant produce bigger tubers.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tso helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: How do I know if my cassava plants are growing tubers underground instead of just growing leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ miikwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii moŋ fe baai lɛ pɛ?

english: When cassava plants put energy into tubers, you will see gentle cracks forming in the soil around the base of the stem as the tubers expand beneath the ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei tso lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ Obaana ŋmei bibii. Amɛfeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli beni ŋmeii lɛ mli shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Can I harvest cassava root by root instead of uprooting the whole plant at once?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekomekome moŋ fe ni majie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome?

english: Yes, you can carefully dig around the base and harvest only mature tubers while leaving the plant alive in the soil, which keeps the remaining cassava fresh until you need it.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli. Base jogbaŋŋ ni okpa ŋmeii ni edara kwraa lɛ pɛ, ni oha tsei lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni ehe baahia bo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants filled with holes and small green dropping particles inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔni lɛ mli

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts helps protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings look weak and wilt right after I transplant them into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer transplant shock when moved into hot sun without time to adapt. Gradually exposing them to direct sun before planting and moving them to the field in the late evening reduces shock.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa piŋmɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni be bɛ ni amɛkɛbaatsake amɛhe. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo hulu la mli blɛoo dani odu ni okɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ mli gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shoofeemɔ aba shi.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and curling up when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ mihe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize gets too much heat and not enough water, it curls its leaves to stop moisture from evaporating. Yellowing usually means the plant is heat-stressed or lacking important soil nutrients like nitrogen during dry spells.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ mli dɔ tsɔ ni nu bɛ Ekɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ akafo. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli edɔ loo ebɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground even when the stems and leaves look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Underground root rot happens when water stays trapped around the roots in heavy or poorly drained soil, or due to soil fungal diseases. The top leaves stay green for a short time before the plant eventually dies.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu ebɔle ehe. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa Yitso baa lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli be kukuoo ko. dani tso lɛ baagbo yɛ naagbee.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely hot, when soil moisture changes too drastically from dry to wet, or when small insects feed on the delicate flower stems.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii yeɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is tired and needs fertilizer before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani mibɔi dumɔwui?

english: Tired soil often looks pale, turns hard or dusty easily, loses moisture quickly, and produces short, weak plants with yellowish leaves even when there is enough rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni etse lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehe wa loo sũ shwieɔ shi oya Efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya ni tsei lɛ baafee kuku ni amɛhe waaa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po.

english: What simple step can I take to keep water in my soil for longer during dry periods?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo Koni nu ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the bare ground around your plants with dry grass, leaves, or crop leftover stems—a practice called mulching—blocks direct sunlight from drying out the dirt and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi gbohii, baai, loo ŋmeii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ he lɛ aha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsĩ naa, ni ebaaha muji akagbi, ni ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Weeds have stronger and faster-growing roots than most farm crops, so they quickly drink up the fertilizer and water in the soil before your actual crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛnuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil space, and water, which results in tall, weak stalks that produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ dumɔwui bibii bibii. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and put it naturally into the soil, which feeds and fertilizes hungry crops like maize growing nearby.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ náa niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I remove all the big trees from my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like baby plants that burn easily in full sunlight; they need partial shade from larger trees to keep them cool and moist during their first few years of growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii, tamɔ tsei bibii lɛ, shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ tsei ni eda lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of just planting grain saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and tested to resist common diseases and harsh weather, yielding much more food than saved grains which lose their strength over time.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa. Enɛ haa niyenii babaoo baa fe ŋmaa ni ato, ni amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ.

english: How can I estimate how many bags of corn I will harvest before I finish cutting all the crops on my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ni makpa dani magbe ŋmãa fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa?

english: You can estimate your total yield by counting the number of healthy cobs in a small sample area (like a 10-meter row), weighing the shelled grain from those cobs, and multiplying that average across the total size of your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ osusu yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ he bibioo ko mli lɛ ayibɔ ni oookane (tamɔ mitai 10 ŋmãa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ), ni okɛ ŋmãa ni ajie kɛjɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ asusu he. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ nakai mlijaa lɛ ato oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my corn so the grains do not spoil on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmãa lɛ akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Corn is ready to harvest when the leaves and husks turn brown and dry, and a small black spot appears at the base of the grain where it attaches to the cob, showing that the grain has stopped growing.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni akɛkpɛtɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishi. Enɛ ɔ tsɔɔ kaa wu ɔmɛ kpa pumi.

english: Why should I shuck or husk my corn soon after harvesting instead of leaving it in the husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛji akpa ŋmãa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing the husk allows air to circulate around the cob, which speeds up drying and prevents trapped moisture from causing mold, grain rot, or insect infestations in your harvested crop.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ oya, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni emɔ mli lɛ haaa ŋmeii aba. ŋmãa ŋmaa ni egbo loo kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ amli

english: How can I tell if my corn grains are dry enough to store in bags without rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abɛi lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto kotoku mli ni efiteee?

english: You can test dry corn by pressing your thumbnail into a grain; if it leaves no dent, or if the grains make a sharp metallic sound when dropped into a tin container, the crop is dry enough for bag storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmãa bibii ni ooonyɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii komɛi bɛ mli Aloo kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ feɔ dade ni tswaa gbee kɛji akɛ ashwie tin tsinsii ko mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ awo kotoku mli.

english: Why do some corn fields produce up to 40 bags per acre while my nearby farm produces much less?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji komɛi woɔ ŋmãa ni fa fe kotokui 40 yɛ acre kome mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa lɛ.

english: Higher yields come from combining certified high-yielding seeds with proper plant spacing, timely fertilizer application, and keeping the field completely free of weeds during the early growing stages.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli ni akɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa feɔ ekome lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli yɛ be ni sa mli ni aha he ni jwɛi akafee lɛ kwraa yɛ shishijee be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to keep records of how many bags of corn I harvest every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni miŋmala ŋmãa kotokui enyiɛ ni mikpaa daa afi lɛ?

english: Keeping harvest records helps you see if your farming methods are making a profit, track whether new techniques are improving your yields, and show proof of success if you want to apply for farm loans or support.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa lɛ ahe saji ni oooŋmala lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onaa kɛji gbɛi ni otsɔɔ nɔ otsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Kwɛmɔ kɛji ŋaai heei miiha onitsumɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ. ni okɛ omanyeyeli he odaseyeli aha kɛji oosumɔ ni obi ni aha bo ŋmɔ mli nyɔmɔwoo loo yelikɛbuamɔ.

english: Why do my corn leaves turn yellow and produce very small cobs if I do not apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient that corn needs to grow strong green leaves and produce large, full grain cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni ekɛ ŋmãa agboi ni eye emuu aba.

english: Will planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my corn reduce the number of corn bags I get?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa baadu lɛ baaha ŋmãa kotokui ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: No, if spaced correctly, legumes like cowpeas actually help corn because they capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which feeds the corn and improves overall crop yields.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas baanyɛ aye abua ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Why are some of my harvested corn cobs only half full of grains while others are completely filled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi eyi fã pɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu eyi lɛ?

english: Half-empty cobs happen when the plant lacks water or nutrients during the flowering stage, or when insects damage the silks before pollination can fully complete.
ga: Cobs ni fã efolo lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii kpata siliki lɛ hiɛ dani pollination lɛ egbe naa.

english: How can I protect my bagged corn from being eaten by weevils without using dangerous chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-abele ni mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii?

english: You can protect stored corn by drying it properly, storing it in airtight hermetic bags that suffocate pests, or mixing the dry grains with approved bio-insecticides like neem leaf powder.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu ŋmãa ni okɛto lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ni oooha egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ mli. Aloo okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ neem baa powder lɛ afutu dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there are no bigger plants growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries up the soil moisture quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides living umbrellas that shelter the young trees until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa shade ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.
