english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves, indicating that the soil needs nitrogen fertilizer or compost to keep the whole plant healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã shishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa bibii lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point the buds on a cassava stick when pushing it into the soil?
ga: Beni otsiɔ cassava tsei lɛ kɛyaa mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ? Ani esa akɛ asusu gbɛtsɔɔmɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings have small growth nodes or buds that must point upward toward the sky. Planting the stick upside down causes the new shoots to grow sideways or downward before reaching the surface, which weakens the plant and reduces root yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii. ni esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Niji ni adu ni atsɔ hiɛ awo shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ yɛ afã loo shikpɔŋ dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni shishifãi ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by the tomato leaf curl virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. When whiteflies feed on the sap of the leaves, they inject the virus, causing the leaves to stunt and curl, which stops fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ whiteflies ye baai amli latex lɛ Amɛbaawo hela lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe. ni haa aduawai ni anáa lɛ kpaa

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm make the maize I plant afterwards grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ feɔ agbo lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When these plants finish growing, they leave behind rich natural nutrients that serve as food for the next crop like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei nɛɛ dara kwraa Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa babaoo ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: The first rain after a long dry season often softens only the top soil, followed by a dry hot spell that can last days or weeks. Seeds planted too early will sprout but die off from lack of steady moisture before the real rainy season fully establishes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji dɔlɛ be ni naa wa ni baanyɛ ahi shi gbii loo otsii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ daa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baashɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers underground if I do not give them stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mihaaa amɛkwɔ ŋwɛi?

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight to manufacture the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. When the vines crawl on the ground without stakes, leaves shade each other, collect diseases from the dirt, and cannot produce enough food for big tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛmɔɔ hulu la koni amɛkɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ wain tsei shwie shikpɔŋ ni akulashiŋi bɛ amɛhe lɛ Baai lɛ baaha amɛhe. Helai ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii wuji lɛ adalɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience heat stress, extreme dryness, or lack of soil nutrients. To save its own life under tough conditions, the plant drops its flowers because it does not have enough water or energy to grow green fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni fe nine loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Koni mɔ ko ahere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ shwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi ejaakɛ amɛbɛ nu loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why should I apply my NPK fertilizer in two split doses instead of pouring all of it on the crops at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli shii enyɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ baafɔse miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ shikome?

english: Applying all fertilizer at once can burn young roots and leads to nutrients being washed away by heavy rain before the crop can absorb them. Splitting the dose provides nourishment when the crop is young and another boost when it is preparing to flower or yield.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shikome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii lɛ, ni eha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ mlijaa baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ yaa hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ asaa he koni ewo fɔfɔi loo ewo yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and thin even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that grow faster than crops and steal water, sunlight, and root space from your soil. Even with heavy rain, weeds swallow up the nutrients in the ground before your main crop gets a chance to feed on them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa moŋ, shi jwɛi hu yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ náa hegbɛ eyeɔ amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong and green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the plant regain its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa akwɛ̃ waa ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly in the hot sun, and stops weeds from stealing water from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaju nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why am I finding small holes and brownish dirt inside the top leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Ni muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the corn plant to feed on soft leaves. Detecting them early and treating the funnels helps save the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛ ni ayɔseɔ mra Ni cone tsamɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɔ shi.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves, or transmitting a virus. Controlling these small insects keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ŋmeii bibii ni akudɔɔ Enɛɛmɛi yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ mli waa.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crop seeds too close together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This leaves all of the plants thin and weak, resulting in a poor harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ ni ehiii.

english: Yam vines need to grow upward into the sunlight to capture light energy to make big tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground and prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ hulu la mli koni amɛmɔ kane hewalɛ ni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ, ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantain protects young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Too much water fills up the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. When cassava sits in soggy soil for long periods, rot causes the tubers to spoil; planting on raised mounds helps extra water drain away.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Beni ŋmei ta shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbo. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become too high or when soil moisture changes drastically. Extreme heat stress prevents the flowers from successfully forming tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee tomato jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the applied fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops can use them. Removing weeds early ensures your crop receives the food you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food they need from the soil to grow strong. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or planting beans nearby can help bring back their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ aba.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the center leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which love to hide and feed on the tender young leaves inside the center of the maize stalk. Checking your fields early and spraying approved pest treatments inside the center of the leaves can protect your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oooshwie baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ abu okpamɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn watery and rot inside the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because the soil drains poorly. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water flow away, keeping the roots dry enough to stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Etsɛ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden poles next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb and need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which also prevents fungal leaves diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe miihia ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa helai ni ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ hu naa.

english: Why do all the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi kookoo tso lɛ nɔ koni egbee shi ni etsɔko kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree gets stressed by dry weather, intense heat, or a lack of shade. Keeping some shade trees in your farm and ensuring the soil stays moist helps the flowers stay attached and turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ, ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots in the ground and very heavy tops, especially when carrying a heavy bunch. Supporting the tree with a strong wooden pole or bamboo fork under the bunch helps hold its weight against heavy winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu tsii waa. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ otere tsɔne ni tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa loo ŋmeii ni akɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ fi tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the daytime even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by a soil disease called bacterial wilt that blocks water from moving up inside the plant stem. Sick plants cannot be cured, so it is best to pull them out and avoid planting tomatoes in that same spot for a few seasons.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ bacterial wilt lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haaa nu aya ŋwɛi yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Anyɛɛɛ atsa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi kɛjɛ mli ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tomato ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ he be fioo komɛi.

english: Why are the leaves of my garden egg and pepper plants curling up like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant kɛ pepper tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding under the leaves, or by a plant virus carried by those insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ji mɛi ni kɛ nakai kooloi lɛ baa lɛ Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so the rain doesn't wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp after a light rain, but not right before a heavy downpour. Placing the fertilizer in a small circle a few inches away from the stem and covering it lightly with soil stops the rain from washing it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ ofeɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii amli. Inchi fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo. Bɔni afee ni nugbɔ akashwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts together with my main crops helps my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ du ŋmei lɛ, ehaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a plant family that can pull nitrogen food directly out of the air and put it into the soil. Growing them alongside other crops naturally enriches the soil and helps neighboring plants grow better.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei aweku ko ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to heat and direct sunlight. Keeping mature shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates a cool environment that holds soil moisture and shelters the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa, ni ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow even though there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign that the soil is running out of nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and build energy. Adding compost, manure, or the right fertilizer puts those essential nutrients back into the soil so the maize can grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni amɛfee hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ŋmãa lɛ adara waa

english: Cereal crops like maize use up a lot of nutrients from the ground. Crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, naturally restoring its fertility for the next season without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmaa mli tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my crops give me smaller yields when I crowd many seeds close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo fataa he koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo aba lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they steal light, water, and soil nutrients from each other. Spacing them correctly ensures every plant gets enough food and sunlight to produce large, healthy fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei fɛɛ náa niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the certified hybrid seeds from the agro-dealer perform better than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically developed and tested to resist common local diseases, survive dry weather, and produce higher yields. Seeds saved from previous harvests naturally lose strength over time and are more vulnerable to pests.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni aka amɛ akwɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. hiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be ni sa mli. ni amɛyɔɔ oshara babaoo kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce less food even if my main plants still look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo niyenii fioo lɛ? Shi kɛlɛ, mitso titri lɛ hiɛ hewalɛ lolo.

english: Weeds grow fast and consume the water and soil nutrients meant for your main crops before the crops can use them. Even if your crops look fine, they end up with less energy to develop heavy yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛyeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii titri lɛ mli dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii. Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ po Shi yɛ naagbee lɛ, ehe ehiaaa hewalɛ babaoo dani anyɛ afee nibii babaoo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Why should I cut off some of the leafy stems from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Removing excess leaves allows air and sunlight to move freely through the plant, which reduces diseases caused by trapped moisture. It also forces the plant to send its energy directly into growing bigger fruit instead of extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa helai ni ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ baa shi. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ hu koni ekɛ hewalɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛya aduawai wuji ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai babaoo baafata he.

english: Why do pests attack my farm much more heavily right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ waa kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Warm weather combined with early rains creates ideal conditions for insect eggs to hatch. At the same time, young plants produce fresh, soft leaves that attract hungry insects looking for food.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha kooloi bibii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ hu woɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni ekɛgbala kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni miitao niyenii lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dry leaves or palm leaves during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni gboi loo tsei ahe tsei awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry foliage, known as mulching, works like a blanket that stops the sun from baking the soil. It traps moisture beneath the surface so plants stay hydrated longer and keeps weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ko ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekashã sũ lɛ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why does spraying too much chemical insecticide burn my crop leaves instead of helping them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ miishã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua amɛ lɛ?

english: Farm chemicals are like strong medicine—using the correct amount kills pests safely, but applying too high a concentration scorches the delicate plant tissue and damages the leaves the plant uses to make food.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tamɔ tsofa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ yibɔ ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shweshweeshwe. Shi kɛ akɛ tsofa ni fa babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni efite baai ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: I only have a small backyard space behind my house, so what crops can I plant there to feed my family?
ga: Miyɛ sɛɛtsu bibioo ko. Mɛni manyɛ makwɛ koni makwɛ miweku lɛ?

english: Fast-yielding vegetables like peppers, garden eggs, tomatoes, and leafy greens like contomire grow very well in small spaces, household gardens, or even inside recycled sacks and containers.
ga: Aduawai ni woɔ yibii oya tamɔ ŋmeii, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, tomato, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ contours lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ hei bibii, shia abɔɔi amli, kɛ kotokui kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ amli po.

english: Can crops like maize and cassava grow well on land outside forest areas?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ kooi amli hei lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, cassava and maize can grow successfully outside dense forests as long as the soil drains water properly, receives enough sunlight, and is fed with compost or manure to maintain nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ asɛɛ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Na hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aha lɛ koni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ akafite.

english: Is it good for me to plant beans together with my maize on the same small piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛfata ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside maize is very beneficial because beans naturally add nitrogen to the soil to feed the maize, allowing you to harvest two different crops from one small space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he bibioo kome.

english: Why do my young crop leaves droop and curl during the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Hot sunshine causes water to evaporate rapidly from leaves, so plants curl up to protect themselves from losing moisture. Placing dry grass mulch around the crop roots keeps the soil cool and wet for longer.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ he. Ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ Tse shishifãi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or is getting too much or too little water. Adding well-rotted animal manure around the base of the plant helps restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo eyɛ nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. Koolooi amli ŋmeii ni egboi ni akɛaabɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aba tso lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally aggressive at stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing them while your crop plants are still small prevents them from crowding out your food crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa ni amɛfeɔ basabasa ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ, ebaatsi oniyenii tsei lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too much water from the rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛjɛ nugbɔ mli?

english: When crops get too much water, their leaves often turn pale yellow, and the roots turn soft and rot because they cannot breathe. Soil should feel damp like a wrung-out sponge, not stay flooded.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaagboi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ sponji ni ajie lɛ kpo. jeee nu afua

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when planting on a small land?
ga: Te esa akɛ makɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ato he ko shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko bibioo?

english: Spacing maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 25 to 30 centimeters between plants ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, air, and ground nutrients to produce large ears.
ga: Aaafee sɛntimitai 75 ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ kɛ sɛntimitai 25 kɛyashi 30 ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ toi wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and attracts specific pests. Swapping crop types each season allows the soil to recover its balance.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahenɔi ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more during the wet season than the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: The warm, wet air of the rainy season creates ideal conditions for pest eggs to hatch and multiply quickly on fresh, tender crop leaves. Inspecting plants daily helps you spot and remove pests early.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔfɔi ni amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ tsei ahe baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei lɛ daa gbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni oyɔseɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra ni ojieɔ amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the green color and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land sucks out the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests to multiply. Switching to crops like groundnuts or cowpeas for a season puts food back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baajie abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp after a light rain, but not right before a heavy downpour. Covering the fertilizer with a little bit of soil near the plant roots also keeps it safe from washing away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ ofeɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ fioo ko ha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa efo.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by a viral sickness spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Removing badly affected plants early and spraying neem leaf water helps keep the whiteflies away from your healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ muawai amli ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Tsei ni ena hela waa lɛ ajiemɔ mra Ni neem baa mli nu ni oooshwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni whiteflies lɛ akaje o-tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ he.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree is stressed by hot dry weather, sap-sucking bugs, or a lack of soil food. Keeping good shade trees around your farm and protecting cocoa trees from insects helps flowers stay on and form pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Tsei akwɛmɔ koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Oŋmɔ lɛ kɛ cacao tsei lɛ ahe ni ooobu kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long or when tiny soil pests wound the roots. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tutua shishifãi lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy wind and rain come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and get top-heavy when producing big bunches. Support your plantain trees using bamboo or wooden poles, and clear away weeds around the base so roots can hold firmly in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ afee amɛ kui wuji. Kɛ ŋmei loo tsei ahe tsei afi odumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ. ni ojie jwɛi ni bɔle shishi lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally start sprouting when their sleeping period ends, especially if the barn is warm and humid. Keeping your yam barn cool, dark, and well-ventilated delays sprouting so your yams stay good for longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes baabɔi shweremɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ wɔɔhe be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Ha o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i, efee duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu abote mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi sweet potato lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their blossoms before peppers can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pepper lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper blossoms drop when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when insects attack the blooms. Water your pepper plants regularly in the early morning and shade young plants during extreme heat.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ Numɔ pepper tsei lɛ daa leebi ni oha tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops even if they are not touching them directly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ mihe kpaaa gbee tɛ̃ɛ po?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from underground and around your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops all the food and water they need to yield plenty of harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when I clear all the tall trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the topsoil. Leaving a few tall canopy trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides living shade that keeps the soil moist and protects the young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ oshi tsei fioo komɛi ni kɛlɛ loo odu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaabu kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out and capture sunlight to produce plant food. Without stakes, leaves stay shaded on the ground, grow poorly, and produce much smaller yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛmɔ hulu la koni amɛfee tsei niyenii. Kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry spells as a survival trick to reduce water loss. The plant remains alive underground, and as soon as the rains return, it quickly sprouts fresh leaves and continues growing tubers.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ kɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Taakɛ yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaawoo ni baaha nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi. Tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo. Ni kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ pɛ kɛkɛ ni Baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya ni bulb lɛ baaya nɔ ada.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is essential for green growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or adding well-decomposed animal manure fixes this deficiency.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo kooloi ashishifãi ni efite jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni aye niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa nɛɛ nɔ kunim.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When planted with maize, they naturally enrich the soil with nutrients, reducing the amount of chemical fertilizer your maize needs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli ni he hiaa bo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and humid weather. Clearing weeds, pruning excess cocoa branches, and harvesting ripe pods promptly improves airflow and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, nu, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛi amli. Jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ Cocoa Tsei ni Fa Fe Nine lɛ Afolɔ Kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa helai gbɛfaŋnɔi lɛ kpaɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites, or a virus they transmit. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or recommended sprays prevents leaf twisting and keeps fruit growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi baai lɛ ashishi ni eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves look like caterpillars ate ragged holes in them overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii ye bu ni etse yɛ mli lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests such as the Fall Armyworm, which hide deep inside the plant's growing funnel during the hot day and eat leaves at night. Spraying early in the morning or late evening reaches the pests directly before they destroy the crop's center shoot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe teeɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ gbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli, ni eyeɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahe tsei gbɛkɛ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ shɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do the blossom ends of my tomatoes turn dark and rotten before the fruit turns red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani aduawai lɛ feɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: This dark rot, called blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants don't get a steady supply of water or lack calcium in the soil. Irrigating regularly so the soil stays evenly moist prevents the fruit bottom from breaking down.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ duŋ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end ŋmɔtɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa nu daa loo calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ nu awo mli daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni aduawai lɛ ashishi akagbala.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into white powder with tiny holes after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Storage insects like grain weevils lay eggs inside dry maize grains, where the larvae eat the seed from the inside out. Drying maize thoroughly until it crackles and storing it in airtight hermetic bags suffocates these pests and prevents destruction.
ga: Picker kooloi tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmaa ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli. Lala lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ebaagbala ni akɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaatsi hiɛkpatamɔ lɛ naa.

english: This yellowing is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow, and when the soil runs low, the plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ lɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick foliage, but produce very tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems instead of roots. Potassium is the key nutrient that helps the plant store starch in the underground tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Cassava kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ amli yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Potassium ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ starch toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Heavy rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto the pods, while dense leaf canopies trap moisture that helps the fungus grow.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ duŋ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, baa ni mli tse lɛ mɔɔ nu ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni edaa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, mites, or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves and spreading viruses. The damage distorts leaf growth and stops the plant from absorbing sunlight properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do fall armyworms hide deep inside the funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The inner leaf funnel (whorl) of young maize is soft, moist, and sheltered from hot sunlight and predators like birds. This protected environment allows the caterpillars to feed on tender new leaf tissue undisturbed.
ga: Abɛi bibii lɛ amli baai (rings) lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli edɔ ni amɛhaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ tamɔ okpoi lɛ náa he ko amɛhiɔ. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni abuɔ he nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ baa hee ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa.

english: Early browning of yam vines is usually caused by a leaf disease called Anthracnose, a fungus that attacks leaves during wet weather. Once the leaves are damaged, the vine dies back early, leaving you with smaller tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ mra. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni tutuaa baai yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ fite lɛ Wein tso lɛ baagbo oya. Enɛ haa oyitso feɔ bibioo.

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen dries out and becomes sterile. Since the flowers cannot be successfully pollinated, the plant naturally drops them to save energy until cooler weather returns.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nii yɛ omanyeyeli mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and curl downwards during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: On hot, sunny afternoons, plantain leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Curling and drooping reduces the leaf surface directly exposed to strong sunlight, helping the plant hold onto moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Curling kɛ drooping haa baa lɛ nɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do I get a much lower yield when I plant seeds saved from my previous hybrid maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsutsu ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially created by crossing two distinct parent lines for high performance. The seeds harvested from a hybrid crop lose this balanced genetic strength in the next generation, producing uneven and lower-yielding plants.
ga: Afeɔ Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi akui sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni afoɔ mli koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ ni ja lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ekome kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why do weeds hurt my young crops more than my mature, fully grown crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ awui fe miŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, shallow root systems and few leaves, making them weak competitors. Weeds grow rapidly and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before young seedlings can establish strong roots.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai fioo pɛ. ni haa efeɔ akaŋshilɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green and strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore its green color and health.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi beni tso lɛ he hiaa nitrogen, ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ko lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts on my land makes the soil better for my next maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that trap natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When you harvest the groundnuts, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Should I apply chemical fertilizer to my farm right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, because heavy rain will wash the fertilizer away into water gutters or sink it too deep where roots cannot reach. It is better to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp right after the rain has stopped.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayaje kpo kɛya nubu lɛ mli loo ebaabote mli tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the afternoon heat is too harsh or when the soil gets too dry. Giving the plants light shade and watering them regularly at the roots keeps the flowers cool enough to form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni afɔ lɛ nu daa yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling happens when tiny invisible insects suck the juice out of young pepper leaves, or pass a plant sickness to them. Spraying the leaves with clean water mixed with neem leaf extract or mild soap gets rid of the insects.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii ni Anaaa amɛ, lɛ miinu nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa bibii lɛ amli lɛ. loo ekɛ helai ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ aha amɛ Okɛ nu ni mli tse ni akɛ neem tso mli nu loo samla ni mli ejɔ efutu mli lɛ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie kooloi bibii.

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can drink it from the ground, so they droop to save moisture. As long as the soil has water, the plant will wake back up when evening comes.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Be abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ nu lɛ Tso lɛ baate shi ekoŋŋ kɛ gbɛkɛ shɛ.

english: Yam leaves need to catch direct sunlight to build food for the tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and keeps them away from rot and soil diseases on the wet dirt.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ sũ helai ni yɔɔ sũ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they fight each other for soil food and water. Leaving only one strong shoot allows the main tree to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ, One plantain Plantains baatswa akaŋ koni ena niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ ŋmei kome pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmei wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready for harvesting just by looking at the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ esa akɛ akpa kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: When cassava tubers are fully grown underneath, the plant stops making new leaves, and the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off. This shows the plant has finished putting all its strength into expanding the roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ baakpa baai heei feemɔ. ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagbee shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ etsu nii ni ekɛlɛɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow thick and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when I plant them out in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to harsh direct sunlight and heat. Without shade crops like plantains planted nearby to shelter them, the hot sun scorches their leaves and dries out their roots before they can grow strong.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni amɛha wɔɔhe lɛ bɛ. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã amɛbaai lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi dani amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers through their leaves catching sunlight. Staking lifts the vines high into the sun and keeps the leaves dry and off the wet ground where they could easily rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei haa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi oya lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize turning yellow even though we received rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ enɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need for healthy green leaves. The maize plant starves its older bottom leaves to send remaining nutrients to the growing top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje ŋmãa ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with leafy stems, but the tubers underground stay very thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ŋmeii lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive water, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and branches above ground instead of storing starch in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ niji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into tiny balls on their roots. When the roots decompose after harvest, that natural fertilizer stays in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I get tiny ears of corn when I plant three or four maize seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa toi bibii anɔ lɛ? Beni aduɔ ŋmãa yibii etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted together in one hole, their roots fight each other for space, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing seeds out properly gives every single plant enough food and sunlight to form a full ear.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baawu koni amɛná he ko. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ efoji lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does my main plantain tree give a small bunch if I leave all the young shoots growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ hu?

english: The small shoots, called suckers, share the same root system as the main tree and steal its water and food. Cutting back extra suckers leaves all the soil nutrients for the mother plant to produce a large bunch.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo koni eha tso nyɛ lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I pour water over my vegetable leaves during the hot middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ afɔseɔ nu awoɔ aduawai ahe baai anɔ yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under a hot afternoon sun causes most water to evaporate before reaching the roots. Water droplets on leaves can also scorch the foliage under sunlight and create damp, warm conditions that spread fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni oooha yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛshã yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni baanyɛ agbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ashwã lɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling tightly upwards and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or aphids sucking sap from the underside of the leaf, or from a virus transmitted by whiteflies that distorts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni fiteɔ tsei adalɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. When the plant gets too hot or lacks water, it sheds flowers to save energy instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ miigba enaa. Kɛ tsei lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu faaa amɛmli lɛ Ebaafɔlɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my crop seeds so they do not dry up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui koni amɛkagbi?

english: Crops are delicate like young babies and need reliable water from the start. In Ghana, planting should match the onset of the rainy season—or when you have a reliable water source—so seeds can germinate and grow strong without drying out in hot soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ waaa tamɔ gbekɛbii bibii. ni ebiɔ nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛjɛ shishijee. Yɛ Ghana lɛ, esa akɛ dumɔwui kɛ nugbɔ be lɛ shishijee akpã gbee. aloo beni oyɛ nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara waa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbiŋ.

english: Why should I make a budget and calculate expenses before buying my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee shika he gbɛjianɔtoo ni mabu shika he akɔntaa dani mahe dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Calculations help you know the exact cost of seeds, fertilizers, water, and labor required to support the crop from planting to harvest, preventing you from running out of money halfway through the season.
ga: Akɔntaabuu yeɔ ebua bo ni oyɔseɔ shika pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ nitsumɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ dumɔ mli kɛyashi kpamɔ mli. Enɛ baajie oshika lɛ kɛjɛ be lɛ fã mli.

english: Why can't I just plant my seeds and wait to harvest them without doing daily work on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu dumɔwui ni mamɛ nikpamɔ ni mitsuuu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi lɛ?

english: A crop behaves like a growing child that requires continuous care. Leaving crops unattended allows weeds and pests to steal nutrients and light, which starves the plant and prevents it from producing food.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbekɛbii ni miida ni biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ daa. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ la. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni ehaaaa amɛye niyenii.

english: How does lack of water affect young crops during their first few weeks in the soil?
ga: Te nu ni bɛ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Young crops have shallow roots that cannot reach deep underground water. Without regular water early on, the plant stops growing, turns yellow, and wilts because it cannot absorb essential nutrients from the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Kɛji nu ni sa bɛ kɛjɛ shishijee Tso lɛ baakpa dalɛ. amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: People around me view farming as a hard punishment, so how can I turn crop farming into a successful business?
ga: Mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ buɔ okwaayeli akɛ eji toigbalamɔ ni naa wa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ tsei akwɛmɔ nɔ matsɔ jarayeli nitsumɔ ni yeɔ omanye?

english: Farming stops being a struggle when you treat it as a planned business. By budgeting inputs, timing water and planting schedules properly, and taking care of the crops like family, you get high yields that produce high financial returns.
ga: Okwaayeli kpaɔ gbɛtsii nii ni eji kɛji okɛtsu nii akɛ nitsumɔ ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ. Nibii ni haa afeɔ nii lɛ ahe shika he gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa, nu be, kɛ dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ tamɔ weku Obaaná sɛɛnamɔi babaoo kɛ shika babaoo.

english: What happens to my crops if the rain stops earlier in the season than I calculated?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni mibu he akɔntaa lɛ?

english: If the water source dries up while crops are maturing, the plants get stressed and may produce small, poor-quality produce or fail completely. This is why having an emergency watering plan is important.
ga: Kɛji nu jɛɛhe lɛ gĩ be mli ni tsei lɛ miida lɛ Tsei lɛ naa haomɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii fioo, ni ehiii loo amɛfite kwraa. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni aná nu ni akɛhaa oya lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How do I figure out what materials and tools I actually need before starting my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nibii kɛ nitsumɔ dadei ni he hiaa mi dani mije ŋmɔ shishi?

english: You must calculate the size of your land first, which tells you the precise quantity of seeds, fertilizer, land-clearing tools, and water containers needed so you do not buy too little or waste money buying too much.
ga: Esa akɛ obu oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ he akɔntaa klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baatsɔɔ bo dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nibii ni akɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ayibɔ. kɛ nu tsɛnsii pɔtɛɛ Bɔni afee ni okahe nɔ ko fioo tsɔ loo okafite shika babaoo tsɔ.

english: Why do crop leaves droop or fold during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Drooping or curling leaves are a crop's natural way of saving water. The plant closes up to prevent moisture from evaporating too quickly under intense heat when it feels thirsty.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Akɛ tsei lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ koni ŋmɔtɔ akafo oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ shishi kɛ́ kumai miiye amɛ.

english: What kind of daily attention do young crops need after they sprout from the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ daa gbi hiɛdɔɔ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii beni amɛje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Sprouting crops need regular water, shade from scorching sun if they are fragile species, and protection from surrounding weeds that compete with them for space and nutrients.
ga: Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ he miihia nu daa. Shade kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛji eji nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe ni miitao he ko kɛ niyenii kpakpai ahe akaŋ lɛ ahe

english: Is it better to secure a water supply before or after clearing my farm land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahã nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ dani ajie miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo beni majie miŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should secure your water supply before clearing land. Preparing land without a guaranteed water source leaves your soil bare and risks losing your planted crops if dry weather sets in.
ga: Esa akɛ otsu onu jɛɛhe lɛ he nii dani ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ooosaa ni nu jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ oshara baa akɛ obaafite onibii kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ bɛŋkɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip and moving down the center leaf vein usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or planting leguminous crops like cowpeas before maize helps fix this problem.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni amɛyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli loo adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they naturally feed the soil, helping crops like maize grow bigger without relying solely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Look inside the central funnel of young maize leaves. If you see small ragged holes and sawdust-like droppings inside the funnel, caterpillars are actively feeding and need to be treated immediately.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa bibioo ko teŋgbɛ. Kɛji ona buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ miiye nii ni ehe miihia ni atsa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling upward into small tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miibɔle ehe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoo bibioo ko lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of leaves. Spraying early or using insect traps helps leaves stay flat so the plant can produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo okɛ kooloi bibii atsɔnei atsu nii ni eye ebua ni eha baai lɛ afee ekome bɔni afee ni tso lɛ awo yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava grown beside them during their first few years to protect their leaf tissues and preserve soil moisture.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli koni ebu baai lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Yam plants use leaves to capture sunlight and make food that feeds the growing tuber below ground. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground toward light, leading to healthier foliage and significantly larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛ la lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa baai lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛ bulbs ni da waa.

english: Should I keep all the small shoots that sprout around my main plantain tree?
ga: Esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Keep mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ?

english: No, allowing too many shoots to grow forces the mother plant to share water and nutrients. Pruning extra shoots so only the mother, one medium shoot, and one small shoot remain will result in much larger bunches.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aha. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni ashi tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ pɛ, tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso kome, kɛ tso bibioo kome lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akuu ni da kwraa aba.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot inside the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up in heavy soil and smothers the roots. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds lets excess water drain away, keeping the roots healthy during heavy rains.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli

english: Tomato blossoms drop when plants experience severe heat stress or uneven watering. Mulching the soil with dried grass helps keep the roots cool and holds moisture so the flowers can set tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Mulch ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ato tomatoi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why is it better to water my vegetable garden early in the morning instead of late afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning lets plants drink deeply before the afternoon sun heats the soil. Evening watering leaves leaves damp overnight, which creates an ideal environment for plant fungal diseases to grow.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ nuɔ nu ni mli kwɔ dani shwane hulu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli gbɛkɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii adalɛ yɛ tsei amli.

english: When maize plants are crowded too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition weakens the stems and results in thin plants with small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifã lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad shade leaves that act as protective umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge green leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: When there is too much nitrogen in the soil—often from applying too much fertilizer—the plant puts all its energy into growing leafy stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli—bei pii lɛ, yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ hewɔ lɛ—tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves turn yellow and drop off when the soil stays too wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water in the soil drowns the roots by blocking oxygen. Without oxygen, the roots cannot absorb nutrients or breathe, causing the plant leaves to turn yellow, wither, and drop off.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii loo amɛmu. Ehaa tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgboɔ, ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I spray agrochemicals on my crops in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ okwaayeli tsofai shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Spraying during intense heat causes liquid chemicals to evaporate into the air before the plant can absorb them. The combination of strong sun and chemicals can also scorch and burn crop leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ni ji nu lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ tsofai ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni ashã tsei ahe baai.

english: Young crops have delicate roots that easily lose the fight against aggressive weeds. Removing weeds early ensures the young crop gets full access to fertilizer, water, and sunlight needed for early growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni baa amɛŋɔɔ lɛ mlɛo. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara mra lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot on the ground if I do not tie them to wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ fĩii tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Leaving tomato vines to trail on the bare ground exposes leaves and fruits to damp soil and soil fungi. Staking lifts the plant, keeping it dry and allowing sunlight and air to flow freely.
ga: Tomato wain tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ baa kɛ aduawai lɛ. Staking woɔ tso lɛ nɔ, ehaa egbiɔ, ni ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my bean plants falling off without turning into bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pea ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Flower dropping is usually caused by severe water stress, excessive heat, or small pests like thrips feeding on the flower buds before pod formation can happen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. la ni mli edɔ fe nine loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi. Dani pods lɛ baafee

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines turning black and dying early before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: This early leaf death is often caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads quickly during damp weather. It destroys leaf tissue, preventing the plant from feeding the yam tuber below ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ kɛ baa lɛ gboiɔ mra. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Efiteɔ baai lɛ amli fãji, ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cabbage heads have small round holes eaten into their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitso lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by destructive caterpillars, such as the diamondback moth larvae, which feed on the leaf tissues as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ daimondback ŋmei lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kaabii baa lɛ amli lɛ baa. ni yeɔ baai amli fãji beni amɛdaraa lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because intense heat and direct sunlight burn their delicate leaves and dry out the topsoil quickly. Keeping larger shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides a protective canopy during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋwɛitsu lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it necessary to put up tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔkɛ tsei kakadaji atsu nii lɛ? Kɛyashi koni maha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and capture maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to build large tubers underground. Keeping vines off the hot ground also prevents leaves from burning and catching soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji. Wein tsei ni akɛaatsi he ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai ni shãa kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crop turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is its primary nutrient for growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn deep green and produce larger ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ko he miihia tso lɛ koni enyɛ eda. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛdara.

english: Why does my cassava produce tall green stems with lots of leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, cassava puts its energy into growing top foliage rather than storing food in its roots. Planting cassava in loose, well-drained soil without excessive nitrogen encourages bigger root development.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Yɛ niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai anɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni nitrogen babaoo bɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo shishifãi wuji ni amɛdara lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do the blossom flowers on my tomato plants fall off before forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat or irregular watering. When the weather gets too hot, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and moisture rather than trying to support fruit growth.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa titri yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa hewɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Mohu ɔ, bɔɔ mɔde kaa o maa ye bua tso yiblii ɔ wami.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and twist tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?
