english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a virus carried by them. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji amɛ tsɔnei lɛ Kudɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to cut away the smaller suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Extra suckers steal water and soil nutrients from the main plantain tree, resulting in smaller fruit bunches. Pruning away weaker suckers and leaving only one or two strong followers ensures the main stalk gets enough nourishment to produce heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii. Afoɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ amli ni sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa eshwɛɔ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni tsii.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt during hot afternoons even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During peak afternoon heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can drink it from the soil. As long as the soil remains moist underneath, the plants will naturally recover and stand upright again in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lolo yɛ shishi lɛ. Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaadamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's soft outer bark and shallow roots because the concentrated salts draw moisture out of the plant tissue. Applying fertilizer a few inches away in a ring allows root tips to absorb the nutrients safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite kponɔgbɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. ni ji tsei lɛ baanyɛ ashã. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows maize-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant only a small plot of a new crop seed before planting my entire farm with it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ midu dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko pɛ nɔ lɛ? Dani abaadu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ

english: Testing a small amount allows you to observe how the new seed reacts to your specific soil, rainfall, and climate over a season without risking your family's food security or income if the crop fails.
ga: Kaa ni afeɔ yɛ gbɛ bibioo nɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui heei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. ni niyenii ni anáa loo weku lɛ shika ni anáa lɛ wooo oshara mli kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii fite.

english: How many seasons should I try a new seed variety before I decide whether to keep using it?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ maka dumɔwui heei makwɛ dani makpɛ miyiŋ kɛji maya nɔ mikɛtsu nii?

english: It is best to test a new seed variety for at least two years or seasons. Weather patterns like rainfall and temperature change from year to year, so two full seasons give a clearer picture of how reliable the seed really is.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooka dumɔwui srɔtoi heei lɛ okwɛ kɛ hoo lɛ afii enyɔ loo bei enyɔ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ latsaa tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi, no hewɔ lɛ bei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ haa wɔnaa bɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why does my traditional local seed sometimes grow better than the new seeds brought from outside our region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mishishijee maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛba kɛjɛ wɔkpokpaa lɛ kponɔ lɛ?

english: Traditional seeds have spent many decades adapting to your area's local soil conditions, heat, and pests. New seeds may perform well elsewhere, but they often struggle if local conditions do not match where they were developed.
ga: Kusum dumɔwui heɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ dani amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ, dɔlɛ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei krokomɛi. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛkɛ naagbai kpeɔ kɛji akɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ he ni atsɔse amɛ yɛ lɛ kpãaa gbee.

english: Why is my new rice variety giving me more difficulties and requiring more work than my old rice variety?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã henɔ hee lɛ haa mɔ haoɔ ni ekɛ nitsumɔ babaoo tsuɔ nii fe mi-ŋmã henɔ momo lɛ?

english: Some modern seed varieties are designed for high yield but require precise amounts of fertilizer, exact water levels, or special care. Traditional varieties are often hardier and require less maintenance to produce a steady harvest.
ga: Afee ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni falɛ ko atsu nii. nu lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ loo kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ Kusum mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ fɔɔ shifimɔ babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why does our local rice taste and cook better than some of the new higher-yielding varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ ŋɔɔ ni ehoɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Breeding programs often focus mainly on growth speed and total yield rather than grain texture or taste. Traditional varieties have survived because local farming communities specifically selected them for their superior taste and cooking qualities over many generations.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔmɔ he gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa oyaiyeli ni yaa hiɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ nɔ titri. Nɔ ni fe bɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ ha loo bɔ ni eyɔɔ fɛo ha Kusum mli ŋmãa henɔi lɛ ehi shi ejaakɛ akutsei ni tsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ ehala amɛ krɛdɛɛ yɛ amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ amɛhoomɔ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ ahewɔ yɛ yinɔi babaoo ni eho lɛ amli.

english: Should both male and female farmers in a household try out new seed samples on their individual farm plots?
ga: Ani esa akɛ okwaafoi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shia lɛ akwɛ dumɔwui heei yɛ amɛŋmɔ mli shikpɔji lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, because men and women in a household often farm different plots of land with varying soil types or water access. Testing seeds across different plots gives a better overall picture of how well the crop performs in the community.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, hii kɛ yei ni yɔɔ shia ko mli lɛ tsuɔ okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi ni shikpɔŋ srɔtoi yɔɔ nɔ loo nu ni amɛnáa lɛ nɔ. Tse dumɔwui akamɔ yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ Ebaaha ana bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ he mfoniri kpakpa.

english: If I want to try a new crop variety, should I stop planting my traditional seeds completely?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni maka ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko makwɛ Ani esa akɛ makpa blema dumɔwui adumɔ kwraa?

english: No, you should never replace all your traditional seeds at once. Keep planting your reliable traditional crops on most of your farm to secure your food and income, while using a small section to test the new variety safely.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ okɛ shishijee dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ tsakeɔ shikome. Bɔɔmɔdɛŋ ni odu blema nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo koni onyɛ oye niyenii kɛ shika ni onáa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, okɛ fã bibioo ko aka ŋmeii heei lɛ okwɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do some new crop varieties fail in our region even though extension officers said they worked well in another district?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei No hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi komɛi nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ wɔkpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji yɛ be mli ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɛ tsei lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Soil nutrition, rainfall amounts, humidity, and local pest populations differ greatly across regions in Ghana. A seed variety that thrives in one district may struggle in another if the local environment does not suit its needs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, hulutsoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ayibɔ yɛ srɔto kwraa yɛ kpokpaa nɔ kɛyaa kpokpaa nɔ yɛ Ghana. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ yɛ kpokpaa kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ he kroko kɛji akɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ haaa nakai kpokpaa lɛ hiamɔ nii aba mli.

english: Can I save the seeds from my harvest of this new rice variety to plant again next year like I do with my old rice?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa hee nɛɛ mli lɛ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa momo lɛ?

english: Not always. Some new or hybrid varieties lose their vigor and yield potential in the second generation, meaning saved seeds may produce weak crops. Traditional seeds, however, can usually be saved and replanted year after year.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Henɔi heei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ekomɛi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii agbɔjɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, abaanyɛ ato blema dumɔwui lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ ni adu ekoŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: What are the early signs that a new rice variety is not adapting well to my farm's region?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa henɔ hee ko nyɛɛɛ atsake kɛya he ni miŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Common signs include stunted growth, yellowing leaves despite adequate rainfall, high susceptibility to local pests or diseases, delayed flowering, or empty grain heads at harvest time.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe ji dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Kaadi ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Ehiɛ kã shi waa yɛ jɛmɛ kooloi bibii loo helai ahe. fɔfɔii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo dumɔwui ayitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli

english: Young cocoa trees dry out easily under intense sun. Planting shade plants like plantains alongside them provides necessary shade and moisture to protect the delicate seedlings during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ adumɔ baaha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni akɛbu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth and improves grain formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ, ni eha dumɔwui lɛ afeemɔ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and fall off, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Is it really necessary for me to stake my yam vines with tall wooden sticks?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ atswa sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Yes, staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight. This boost in light exposure helps the plant produce food that makes the underground tubers grow much larger.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking baaha ŋmeii lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. La ni yaa hiɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: Can I plant cowpea together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, cowpea and maize grow well together because cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil, which helps feed the maize plants while giving you an extra food harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aha ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ebaaha niyenii krokomɛi hu aba.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu ko yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. Early treatment with recommended organic or chemical sprays directed into the center of the plant is needed to prevent crop loss.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Tsofafeemɔ he miihia mra. Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop without forming fruit when temperatures are too high or when soil moisture fluctuates drastically from very dry to very wet. Consistent watering helps preserve the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaving too many suckers allows them to steal water and nutrients from the main stem, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only one main plant and one strong sucker ensures larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ ni amɛje kpo lɛ, ehaa amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso bibioo ko Tso titri kome pɛ kɛ sucker ni mli wa kome ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaha plantains lɛ afee wuji.

english: Should I start planting my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the major season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni he hiaa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become consistent, as the first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can scorch and destroy newly germinating seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit leaf curl virus. Controlling these insects early prevents the virus from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ leaf curl virus lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer can restore their healthy color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: How does adding dark organic manure help my soil hold water longer during dry spells?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ diŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Organic manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It binds the soil particles together, allowing the earth to trap rainwater and keep the root zone moist even when the sun is very hot.
ga: Organic fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli, ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli fɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa po.

english: I want to start growing Moringa on my land; why does it grow so fast even when there is little rain?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi moringa dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mɛni hewɔ edaa oya nɛkɛ kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Moringa has a deep taproot that grows far beneath the surface to search for underground water, allowing it to survive harsh dry weather and produce leaf harvests rapidly.
ga: Moringa yɛ shishifã ko ni mli kwɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi koni eyatao shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa mli, ni ewoɔ baai oya.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I harvest more food from my small farm?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ makpa niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Ani manyɛ maná mi nɔ babaoo?

english: Planting too closely actually lowers your yield because the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with tiny fruits or ears.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei baatswa akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei komɛi yɛ aduawai bibii loo toi.

english: Why does my farm produce less harvest if I plant maize in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ naa ŋmaa bibioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts gives the soil time to rebuild its strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ edaa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛtswaa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yes, because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly at first. The maize will mature and be removed before the cassava needs the full space to grow its tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ shishijee mli lɛ. Akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ he hiaa he fɛɛ he ni ekɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Drooping is a plant's natural defense against heat. By curling or hanging down, the leaves reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant save precious water until the air cools down.
ga: Drooping ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ nɔ Baai lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu ni jara wa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my main crops to grow weak and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital food, sunlight, and water directly from the root zone of your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get all the food they need to produce a heavy yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ekpa nii babaoo.

english: Why is it very bad if my maize farm doesn't get rain when the tassels and flowers start appearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kwraa kɛji mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli nugbɔ enɛɛɛ beni ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ?

english: Flowering is the exact time when maize forms its grains. If the plant suffers from lack of water during flowering, pollen cannot fertilize the cob properly, leaving you with empty or half-filled cobs.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ ji be pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmãa woɔ dumɔwui. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, Pollen nyɛŋ aha tso lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli loo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: This damage is often caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which prefer hiding in the soft, young inner leaves (the whorl) of maize plants where they can feed safely away from heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmãa tsei amli baai bibii (rings) lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni baanyɛ ana niyenii shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo bɛ he

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting at the tip and moving along the middle of the leaf, it means the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green again so the plant can grow big cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa baa lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ baa lɛ naagbee kɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tsei he miihia nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves in dry weather to save water and protect themselves from dying heat. The plant is not dead; it goes into a sleeping state and will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni miigbo lɛ he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebaawɔ ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants grow bigger tubers when I stake them with tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ daa bulbs wuji beni mikɛ amɛ fɔ̃ɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp soil, protecting them from fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekafite.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly waterlogged. The plant drops flowers to save its energy until conditions become mild enough to support fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛtee nu ni eyi mli obɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee mlɛo bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my land make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. After you harvest the groundnuts, that trapped plant food stays in the dirt and feeds whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpa ŋmei sɛɛ Tse niyenii ni akɛkpɛtɛ he lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Curling leaves on tomato plants are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the juice out of the leaves, or transmitting a virus. Protecting plants from these insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Plantain roots do not grow deep into the ground; they stay shallow near the surface. When the fruit bunch gets heavy, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with a strong wooden prop prevents wind from uprooting it.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Amɛmli ekɔɔɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ tsii lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when there is heavy rainfall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the field for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown and rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha ŋmɔji ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing big leaves but not forming tight round heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baa agbo shi ebɛ yitsei ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbage plants fail to form tight heads when temperatures are too high or when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing outer leaves instead of wrapping into a dense ball.
ga: Kaabaji tsei nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama esɛɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeebua amɛ naa ni efee kui ni mli eyi obɔ.

english: Why do extra small stems sprout at the bottom of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso bibioo lɛ So extra lɛ miida yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: These extra stems, called tillers, grow when the plant has extra water and nutrients or plenty of space around it. You do not always need to cut them off, as healthy tillers can sometimes grow small cobs of their own.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ akɛ daffodils. Ebaakwɛ̃ beni tso lɛ ná nu kɛ niyenii babaoo loo he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Jeee be fɛɛ be ehe hiaa ni ofolɔ mli. Ejaakɛ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmɔtsɛ ni he wa lɛ baanyɛ adu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eŋmɔ bibioo lɛ.

english: How do I know if my yam setts are ready to be planted in the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii akuu ko efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam setts are ready for planting when you start seeing small green buds or eyespots emerging on the skin, which shows that the tuber has naturally broken its dormancy period and is ready to shoot.
ga: Sweet potato set lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ beni obɔi ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ namɔ. loo hiŋmɛii bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ yitso lɛ efo ebɔɔ su be ni ekɛhiɔ shi lɛ mli ni efee klalo akɛ ebaatu tu.

english: Why do extension officers always advise us to put tall wooden stakes for our yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ wɔkɛ tsei kakadaji ama wɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs daylight to make food for growing underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the sunlight and off the wet ground, which boosts leaf growth and protects the plant from soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ahi hulu la mli ni amɛkabote hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ daraa babaoo ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my yams often grow small and twisted instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe yɛ agbo ni etse lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yams need deep, soft, and well-drained soil to expand properly. If the soil is compacted, rocky, or hard, the tuber struggles to push downward, resulting in stunted or misshapen yams.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia sweet potato koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ wa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shi. Enɛ haa sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi loo efiteɔ.

english: Can I plant maize on the same soil mounds where I plant my yams?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize with yams works well, but you must plant the maize on the sides of the mound so its fast growth does not shade out the young yam sprouts or steal all the soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi esa akɛ odu ŋmãa lɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ masɛi. Enɛ ji koni ekakwɛ oya, ni ekɛ sweet potato tsei bibii akakpãtã loo eju niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from rotting quickly after digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite oya beni mifo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when wounded during harvest. To protect them, dig carefully to avoid cuts, heal minor surface wounds by drying tubers in a shady area for a few days, and store them off the ground in a cool, airy yam barn.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji epila yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. koni ebu amɛhe Tsɔɔmɔ jogbaŋŋ koni pilamɔi akafee bo. Tsamɔ pilamɔi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛtsɔ bulb lɛ ni oooha egbi yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni okɛto sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop tubers spoil so fast when we pack and transport them tightly in trucks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tubers lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛ wɔ wo mli jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwo lɔlei amli lɛ?

english: Tight packing causes skin bruises and high heat buildup among the tubers. Air cannot circulate to keep them cool, creating a warm, damp environment where rot-causing fungi thrive.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa hewolo nɔ shwieɔ shi ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa baa yitsei lɛ ateŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abɔle ehe koni ekɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I put fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plant roots can only drink fertilizer dissolved in soil moisture. Applying fertilizer to dry soil traps the nutrients around the roots, which can scorch or burn them and cause the crop to wither.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ mli nu mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ni baanyɛ ashã loo ashã ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed my farm during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop shoots grow slowly at first and cannot compete with aggressive weeds for sunlight, water, and soil food. Clearing weeds early ensures young plants get all the resources they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ abɔ he akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso bibioo lɛ naa nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves can mean waterlogging in the soil, which smothers the roots so they cannot breathe or absorb nutrients, or it can mean a shortage of nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ nu emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Aloo ekolɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my seed yams start sprouting too early in storage before the land is even ready for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ dani shikpɔŋ lɛ po feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu lɛ?

english: Yams break dormancy faster when stored in warm, dark, or humid places. Storing seed yams in a bright, well-ventilated barn slows down early sprout development until you are ready to plant.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ wɔɔhe oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, duŋ, loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potato dumɔwui to tsũ ko ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu amɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight or dry winds. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them and keep the moisture in until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower maize leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and build strong stalks, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore its health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ ŋmãa ni wa aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetables with dried grass help my crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, keeps the root area cool, and prevents weeds from growing and taking nutrients from your crop.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and white powdery dust inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ sũ yɛŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa mli lɛ mli

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot to feed on young leaves. Catching them early allows you to use appropriate pest control methods before they destroy the crop heart.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛ ni ooomɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsui.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a plant virus they spread. Treating the insects early prevents them from damaging the leaves and stopping plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo tso mli helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ Mra ni akɛbaatsa kooloi bibii Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite baai lɛ ni amɛkakpa tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when heavy rains last for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves the ground waterlogged for too long, the roots suffocate and soil fungi quickly cause them to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi oya.

english: Why do I need to put long sticks for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground into full sunlight, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant make bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ. Etsiɔ tso helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the plant suffers from sudden water stress. Maintaining consistent watering helps the flowers stay attached and produce fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba tso lɛ nɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when the fruit bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be weakened by microscopic worms or strong winds. Supporting the heavy fruit bunches with wooden props prevents the stem from snapping under the weight.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso fiɔ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ yɛ muji lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I delay weeding my farm for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil food that your crops need to be strong. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the resources available in the field.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni onibii lɛ aná hewalɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: When is the right time for me to spray chemicals on my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ?

english: You should apply chemicals early in the plant's life, before the maize produces flowers and turns golden. Spraying early protects the crop without contaminating the growing seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai atsu nii mra yɛ tso lɛ wala mli. Dani ŋmãa lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi ni ebaatsɔ shika tsuru Ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee Ebaabu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ni efiteee dumɔwui ni miida lɛ.

english: What happens if I spray pesticides on my corn after it has already started forming seeds?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ beni ebɔi dumɔwui feemɔ sɛɛ?

english: If you spray after seed formation begins, the chemicals can soak directly into the corn kernels. This leaves harmful chemical residues inside the food you harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ afeemɔ je shishi lɛ, Tsofai baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmãa mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui shwɛɔ yɛ niyenii ni okpaa lɛ mli.

english: Why does my corn plant turning golden mean I should stop spraying chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ji shika tsuru lɛ? Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ makpa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: When the corn turns golden and flowers appear, it means the plant is actively bearing seeds. Spraying at this stage causes the plant to absorb chemicals into the edible kernels, making the harvest unsafe.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ tsɔ shika tsuru ni fɔfɔii je kpo No tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiwo dumɔwui. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ tsofai lɛ amli kɛyaa dumɔwui ni ayeɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, nikpamɔ be lɛ bɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it safe for my family to eat corn from a farm that was sprayed late in the season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miweku lɛ baaye ŋmãa ni jɛ ŋmɔ ko ni akɛ tsofa shwie nɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ mli?

english: No, it can be harmful to human health. Late spraying causes the crop to retain chemical poisons inside the seeds, which people then consume when eating the corn.
ga: Dabi, ebaanyɛ eye adesa gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ awui. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai fɔji shwie tsei lɛ anɔ fiofio lɛ, ehaa tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ hiɔ tsei lɛ amli. ni gbɔmɛi yeɔ kɛ amɛyeɔ ŋmãa

english: Can the chemicals I put on my corn leaves actually get inside the grains?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ abote dumɔwui lɛ amli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, when corn is already bearing seeds, the plant transfers liquids and chemicals from its surface directly into the developing grains.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni ŋmãa lɛ jeɔ dumɔwui shishi lɛ. Tsei jieɔ nu kɛ tsofai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I make sure the corn I harvest is safe for people to eat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni gbɔmɛi baanyɛ aye?

english: Always finish spraying your protective chemicals well before the maize flowers and starts producing seeds so no chemicals end up inside the corn kernels.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ashwie nɔ dani ŋmãa fɔfɔi aba. ni amɛje dumɔwui afeemɔ shishi koni tsofai akabote ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli

english: Will spraying my corn close to harvest time help me get a better yield?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni mikɛshwieɔ shi ni bɛŋkɛɔ kpamɔɔ be lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: No, spraying close to harvest time does not improve yield safely; it only traps toxic chemicals inside the mature seeds, making the crop dangerous to eat.
ga: Dabi, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ kpamɔɔ be lɛ haaa yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe. Emɔɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni eda lɛ amli pɛ. Enɛ haa nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Why are some buyers in Ghana choosing to buy imported corn instead of local corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ Ghana lɛ halaa akɛ amɛbaahɔɔ ŋmãa ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ moŋ fe maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Buyers often turn to imported corn when local farmers spray chemicals at the wrong time, leaving chemical residues in the grain that make consumers fear for their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmãa ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi lɛ shwie tsofai yɛ be ni esaaa mli. Enɛ haa tsofai ni eshwɛɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli ni haa mɛi ni yeɔ nii lɛ haoɔ yɛ amɛhewalɛ he.

english: How does my choice of when to spray chemicals affect my ability to sell my harvest?
ga: Te be ni mihalaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai lɛ baashwie nɔ lɛ saa nyɛmɔ ni miyɔɔ akɛ mikɛ nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baahɔ̃ɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: If you spray late while seeds are present, consumers and traders may reject your corn due to health complaints about chemical tastes or safety, driving them to buy foreign crops instead.
ga: Kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ blɛoo be mli ni dumɔwui yɛ lɛ, Nihɔɔlɔi kɛ jarayelɔi baanyɛ akpoo o-ŋmã lɛ yɛ hewalɛnamɔ he wiemɔi ni kɔɔ ŋmãa loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he lɛ hewɔ. Ha amɛhe maŋsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ.

english: Why did people complain about the quality of locally grown maize in recent seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi wieɔ amɛshiɔ bɔ ni ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ hi ha yɛ bei ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Many people complained because farmers applied chemicals while the corn was already bearing seeds, causing the final food product to contain harmful chemical traces.
ga: Mɛi babaoo wieɔ amɛshiɔ akɛ okwaafoi kɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yɛ dumɔwui momo. Enɛ haa tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɔɔ naagbee niyenii ni afee lɛ mli.

english: Why does spraying my cocoa farm make the trees produce much more fruit than if I leave them alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe kɛji mishi amɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees are often attacked by tiny insects like capsids and fungal diseases like black pod disease. Spraying protects the flowers and young pods from being destroyed, allowing the tree to save its energy to grow lots of healthy, abundant cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids kɛ fungal helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ tutuaa cacao tsei. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ buɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How often should I spray my cocoa trees during the rainy season to prevent pod diseases?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ afɔse kookoo tsei anɔ tsofa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni pod hela akamɔ amɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates damp conditions that make fungal diseases like black pod spread very fast. Spraying your cocoa trees every 3 to 4 weeks during the main wet season coats the pods with protective chemical medicine so the fungus cannot infect them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Kɛ́ afɔ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ daa otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Koni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: If I spray my cocoa late after pests have already appeared, will it still give me a good harvest?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ cocoa shwie sɛɛ beni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ eje kpo lɛ sɛɛ Ani ebaawo yibii kpakpai lolo?

english: Spraying works best when done early before pests and diseases destroy the young flowers and small pods. If you wait until damage has already happened, spraying cannot bring back ruined pods and will yield much less benefit.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ afee lɛ mra. Dani tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baafite fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ, Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi be mli ni nɔ ni efite lɛ baaho lɛ, Spray kɛ ŋmeii ni efite lɛ baaa ekoŋŋ. ni ebaaha sɛɛnamɔ fioo ko pɛ aba.

english: My land is very small, so how can I get a big harvest from just a tiny farm?
ga: Mishikpɔŋ lɛ faaa kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli?

english: You can get high yields on small land by giving intensive care to every single tree—pruning regularly, clearing weeds, and spraying for pests on time. When every tree is fully healthy, a small farm can produce as much cocoa as a poorly managed large farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná shika babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ kɛtsɔ tso fɛɛ tso nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa nɔ. Kɛji eji tso ni afoɔ daa, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be naa lɛ. Beni tso fɛɛ tso mli wa ni eye emuu lɛ, ŋmɔji bibii baanyɛ ajie kookoo babaoo tamɔ ŋmɔji wuji ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when they are planted too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are overcrowded, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, and their roots fight for nutrients and moisture in the soil. Spacing trees properly ensures each tree gets enough light and food to produce maximum pods.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ mli eyi tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: What main steps should I take at the beginning of the new year to prepare my cocoa trees for the next season?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii titrii ni esa akɛ afee yɛ afi hee lɛ shishijee mli koni akɛsaa cacao tsei lɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: At the start of the year, clear weeds around the trunks, prune off dead or unwanted branches, and check your shade trees. Preparing early allows your cocoa trees to sprout healthy fresh leaves and flower buds when the main rains return.
ga: Yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni ofolɔ niji ni egboi loo ni ataooo lɛ fɛɛ. ni okwɛ kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yɛ Cocoa tso lɛ he saamɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ beni nugbɔ titri lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ eba lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed their leaves and stop flowering during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛkpaa fɔfɔi yɛ harmattan be ni nu lɛ egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shedding leaves is a cocoa tree's natural way of saving water during dry weather so it does not dry out and die. Once the dry season ends and rains return, the tree will absorb moisture, grow fresh leaves, and start producing flowers again.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ ni egbooo. Kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee ni nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Tso lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ baafee ehee, ni ebaabɔi fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are yellow leaves appearing on my cocoa trees even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or that tiny insects are sucking nutrients out of the leaves. Adding proper fertilizer or organic manure can restore the dark green color and boost the crop's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen, loo kooloi bibii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my cocoa trees before turning into young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off due to dry weather, insect attacks, or poor pollination. Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects called midges to pollinate them, which thrive best when there is light shade and moisture around the trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, kooloi tutuamɔ loo pollination ni ehiii hewɔ. Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli. Amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ kɛji hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ he.

english: How does joining a cocoa farmers group in my district help me improve my crop yield?
ga: Te kookoo okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mikɛ mihe baawo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Joining a district farmers group allows you to access shared spraying equipment, receive subsidized farm inputs, and get regular training from extension officers on the best ways to care for your crops.
ga: Kpokpaa nɔ okwaafoi akuu ko ni okɛ ohe aaawo mli lɛ haa onáa nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ. Na nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni ayeɔ abuaa amɛ lɛ amli Ni ona tsɔsemɔ daa kɛjɛ extension nitsulɔi adɛŋ yɛ bɔ ni ooofee okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: How does cassava grow under the ground, and how do I know if the tubers are developing well?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi? Ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cassava plants store energy in their underground roots, turning them into thick, starchy tubers. As these tubers expand under the soil, you will often notice the earth around the base of the stem slightly cracking and swelling, which is a good sign that food is forming below.
ga: Cassava tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Feemɔ ŋmɔtɔ yitso ni mli edɔ. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ mli gbala yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Bei pii lɛ obaana akɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli egbɛ eshwa ni efu fioo. Enɛ ji okadi kpakpa ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii miibua ehe naa yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why does cassava need proper water in the soil even though the tubers grow hidden under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he hiaa ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ ehe ewo shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ?

english: Water acts like a transport system that carries food and nutrients from the soil into the roots. Even though cassava can survive dry weather, steady soil moisture during its early stages helps the tubers grow soft and big instead of thin, hard, and woody.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo ni kɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli moŋ, shi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ afee blɛoo ni amɛdara. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ nyakpɛ, e wa, nɛ e ngɛ kaa tso.

english: Why does cassava draw so many nutrients from the land compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ akɛtoɔ tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Cassava creates heavy, thick tubers underground, which requires a lot of food and water from the earth. Because it pulls so much energy out of the ground to build those tubers, it is good practice to let the land rest or add nutrients back into the soil after harvesting.
ga: Cassava woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii. ni biɔ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ ji akɛ, ejieɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee nakai ŋmeii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava on the same farm where I have rubber trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni miyɔɔ rɔbɔt tsei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, you can plant cassava between young rubber trees while the trees are still small. The cassava makes good use of the open space, but you must plant them far enough apart so the expanding cassava roots do not fight with the rubber roots for water and space.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmei yɛ rɔbɔt tsei ateŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ. Yucca kɛ he ni agbele lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi ehe miihia ni odu amɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ ji koni ŋmei shishifãi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ kɛ rɔbɔt shishifãi lɛ akatswa akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ he ko he.

english: When I dig up cassava planted near my rubber trees, how can I avoid damaging the rubber tree roots?
ga: Kɛji akɛ aaakumɔ ŋmei ni adu yɛ rɔbɔt tso ko masɛi Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni akafite rɔbɔt tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: Always dig carefully around the base of the cassava plant using a hoe or cutlass, pulling away from the rubber tree's main trunk. Softening the soil first allows you to lift the tubers out cleanly without tearing the nearby rubber roots.
ga: Kɛ shɔvel loo ŋmei atsu nii ni okɛfo he fɛɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Cassava tso shishi Kɛtsɔ ejiemɔ kɛjɛ rɔbɔt tso lɛ shishitoo titri lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ owó bulb lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ogbalaaa shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli.

english: Can a sickness in my cassava plant spread to my rubber trees?
ga: Ani helai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mi-raba tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Most common cassava sicknesses, like leaf mosaic or stem rot, only affect cassava plants and will not infect rubber trees. However, if the soil stays too wet and causes root rot, that bad soil condition can harm the roots of both crops.
ga: Nɔ ni fata ŋmei helai ni afɔɔ naa waa lɛ ahe ji baai mosaic loo stem rot. Ehaa ŋmeii tsei pɛ yeɔ hela, ni ekɛ hela baaa rɔbɔt tsei anɔ. Shi, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aye tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ shishifãi lɛ awui.

english: Can I transfer plant disease from a sick cassava to healthy plants with my hands or farm tools?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ miniji loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ajie tsei ahe helai kɛjɛ ŋmei ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, plant juice from a diseased cassava plant can stick to your hands, cutlass, or hoe. If you touch or cut a healthy plant right after working on a sick one, you can pass the sickness along, so it is best to clean your tools between plants.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tso mli nu ni jɛ yucca tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ oniji, otsɔnei, loo otsɔnei ahe. Kɛji ota tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he loo ofo lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni otsu tso ni hela mɔ lɛ he nii Obaanyɛ okɛ ohela lɛ aha mɔ kroko. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsumɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ ahe.

english: What should I do if I notice a cassava plant on my farm showing signs of disease?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina akɛ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔɔ hela he okadi?

english: When a cassava plant gets sick, it is best to uproot the whole plant completely—roots and all—and remove it from the field. Leaving sick roots in the ground allows the disease to spread through the soil or be carried by insects to healthy crops.
ga: Beni hela mɔ cassava tso lɛ Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni ajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ. shishifãi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shishifãi ni hela mɔ amɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hela agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛ kooloi bibii aya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How do I properly uproot my cassava so that none of the tuber is left in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie ŋmei lɛ jogbaŋŋ? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akashwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Wait until the soil is slightly moist, cut the main stem back to a manageable height, grab the stem firmly near the ground, and pull straight up while loosening the dirt around the roots with a hoe. Completely uprooting the plant ensures no broken tubers rot underground.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ fioo. Kpãa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashɛ he ko ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii. Mɔ tso lɛ mli shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. No sɛɛ lɛ, gbálamɔ kɛya ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ ni okɛ spade atsu nii ni okɛjie muji ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kwraa lɛ, ehaa bulb lɛ fiteee yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does the ground feel loose and disturbed after I uproot my cassava crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse ni ehao beni mijie ŋmei tsei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As cassava tubers grow large, they push the soil outward. When you uproot the entire crop at harvest, it naturally lifts and loosens the soil, making the ground soft for the next crop, though you should protect it from washing away during heavy rains.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ, amɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛji ojie ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baawó ehe nɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ otsi enaa koni ekaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the rainy season is shorter than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need steady water to support flower development and feed growing pods. When rains are short, the tree conserves energy by shedding flowers or producing fewer and smaller pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia nu daa koni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ Tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii fioo ni amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa harvest output change so much from year to year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ni mikpaa lɛ srɔtoɔ waa kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi lɛ?

english: Harvest yields change mainly due to weather patterns. If a year brings strong, timely rains, the trees stay healthy and yield more, but dry years weaken the trees and lower production.
ga: Nikpamɔ yibiiwoo tsakeɔ titri yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Kɛji afi kome lɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eba yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Shi afii ni nu bɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Does a lack of rain affect the size and weight of the cocoa beans inside the pod?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ saa bɔ ni kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ dalɛ kɛ amɛhe tsii ha lɛ he?

english: Yes, without enough water during the period when pods are filling up, the beans inside stay small, flat, and light, which reduces the overall weight of your harvest bags.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ be mli ni pod lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ. Kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ daraaa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ mlɛo, ni no haa okpamɔ kotoku lɛ mli tsiimɔ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into pods during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers are very delicate. When the tree experiences water stress or extreme heat, it automatically drops its flowers to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa. Kɛ tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpe lɛ Ebaajie efɔfɔi lɛ kɛjɛ ehe koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha ehe ahi wala mli.

english: Can I supply water to my cocoa trees myself during the dry season, or must I wait for rainfall?
ga: Ani mi diɛŋtsɛ manyɛ maha mi-kokoo tsei lɛ nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ wɔmɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ?

english: You can supply water yourself through irrigation. Watering your cocoa trees during dry spells helps them stay green, hold onto their pods, and keep producing even when natural rains stop.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ aha bo diɛŋtsɛ onu. Kɛ́ afɔ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ nu yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli, amɛmɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli, ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ lɛ ekpa po lɛ.

english: Is natural rainfall still enough to get good cocoa yields every year?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa lolo ni baaha aná kookoo kpakpa daa afi?

english: While natural rain used to be enough, weather patterns have become unpredictable. Relying only on rain makes your harvest risky, which is why water management techniques are becoming important.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsutsu lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ fa moŋ Shi anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ ha lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ okpamɔ lɛ woɔ oshara mli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni nu he gbɛjianɔtoo he ŋaai he hiaa waa lɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm holds water well enough for cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Good soil for cocoa feels rich and moist when you dig a few inches down. If your soil turns hard, dry, and cracked quickly after rain stops, it loses water fast and needs extra organic matter or shade to trap moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha kookoo lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ shika ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ ofo shi inchi fioo komɛi. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bafee nɔ ni wa, ni egbi, ni egbɛ eshwa oya beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fiteɔ oya ni ehe miihia ni akɛ nibii krokomɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli loo hulutsoo afata he koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: How can I protect my crops from losing strength when severe dry heat hits my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkafite hewalɛ beni hulutsoo be ni naa wa ko ba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: You can protect your crops by leaving suitable shade trees on your farm to block harsh sunlight and covering the soil around the base of your crop with dry leaves or mulch to trap moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsei ni sa ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ni oooshi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What happens to a cocoa tree when it goes through a long period without any rain?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo tsei anɔ kɛ́ amɛtee be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: During prolonged dry spells, a cocoa tree loses leaf strength, turns yellow, sheds leaves, stops growing new pods, and in severe cases, the branches or the whole tree can dry up and die.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ baa lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ŋmeii heei kpaɔ dalɛ ni yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa mli lɛ Niji loo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baanyɛ agbi ni egbo.

english: What is the best time of year to plant young cocoa seedlings so they do not die from dry weather?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui bibii koni amɛkagboi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant seedlings is at the beginning of the major rainy season. This gives the young roots several months of steady rainfall to establish deep in the soil before any dry weather sets in.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa nyɔji babaoo koni amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba.

english: How long after planting cassava should I wait before I can start harvesting the roots?
ga: Kɛ́ midu ŋmei lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa shishifãi lɛ?

english: Most common cassava varieties in Ghana mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. Harvesting too early results in small, watery roots, while leaving them in the ground past 18 months can cause the roots to turn woody and hard.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nyɔji 18 lɛ ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ tso ni amɛhe wa.

english: How do I choose and prepare cassava stems so that they grow strong when I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei lɛ ni masaa amɛ koni amɛwa kɛji adu amɛ?

english: Select healthy, disease-free stems from plants that are 8 to 12 months old. Cut the middle portion of the stem into stakes about 20 to 25 centimeters long, ensuring each cutting has at least 4 to 6 healthy buds before planting.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ amli tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ ni efee ŋwɛitsu ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 25. Kwɛmɔ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, tso ni afo lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 4 kɛyashi 6 dani adu.

english: Why does cassava spoil so quickly within a few days after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once removed from the soil, cassava roots undergo rapid physiological deterioration caused by exposure to air and moisture loss. To prevent rapid spoiling, keep the roots covered in moist soil or process them into gari or flour immediately after harvest.
ga: Kɛji ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni laajeɔ lɛ hewɔ. Bɔni afee ni ekafite oya lɛ Ha shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ loo okɛfee gari loo ashikishaŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji okpa.

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water rapidly under intense sun. During dry periods, the plant intentionally sheds its outer leaves to reduce water loss and protect its main stem until rainfall resumes.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ eshwieɔ esɛɛ baai lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over when they start producing bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji amɛbɔi shweremɔ yɛ kui amli pɛ?

english: Plantains have a shallow root system rather than a deep taproot. When the heavy fruit bunch develops, top-heavy weight combined with wind or soft soil can pull the plant down, so supporting the stem with a wooden prop is necessary.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ Muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo fata he lɛ baanyɛ agbala tso lɛ kɛba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ tso atsu nii ni akɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I get new plantain shoots to expand my farm without buying new seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná ŋmeii heei ni mikɛgbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni miheee dumɔwui heei?

english: Plantains reproduce through underground stems that sprout young shoots called suckers around the base. You can dig up healthy 'sword suckers'—those with narrow, lance-shaped leaves—and replant them in new holes.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ anɔ, ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii ni bɔleɔ amɛshishi lɛ he. Obaanyɛ okɛ ‘klante tsei’ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai bibii ni tamɔ lance lɛ atsu nii ni okɛwo bu hee mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I safely plant cassava and plantain together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ he kome shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, intercropping plantain and cassava works well because plantains grow taller and create shade, while cassava occupies lower space. Proper spacing is essential so their root systems do not compete excessively for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akɛ plantains kɛ cassava duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ plantains lɛ daa ni ehaa hulutsoo baa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei heɔ he ko fioo. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ teŋ lɛ he miihia bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii babaoo ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it safe to feed fresh cassava leaves and peels directly to my goats?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahã mitooi lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmei baai heei ni ajie amɛhewolo nɔ?

english: Raw cassava leaves and peels contain natural cyanogenic compounds that can upset a goat's stomach or prove toxic. Wilting the peels and leaves in the sun for 24 to 48 hours breaks down these compounds, making them safe for livestock feed.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ji cyanogen ni baanyɛ aha too musu mli afee shoo loo ekɛ tsofa awo mli lɛ yɛ cassava baai ni ahoo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Tso lɛ yibii kɛ baai ni egbo yɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 lɛ fiteɔ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ. ni haa efeɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛbaatsu nii akɛ kooloi aniyenii

english: I have grown crops on the same piece of land for three years; why are my crop yields starting to drop?
ga: Mikɛ afii etɛ edu tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi shibaa lɛ?

english: Continuous cropping over three years depletes key soil nutrients like nitrogen, potassium, and phosphorus. To restore yield, apply compost or animal manure, or rotate food crops with nitrogen-fixing legumes like cowpeas.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ daa afii etɛ lɛ baaha sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, potassium kɛ phosphorus lɛ afite. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji atsu nii. Aloo okɛ ŋmãa ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ tsina ŋmãa lɛ atsake niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: How can I prevent goats and farm animals from destroying my young food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tooi kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi anaa koni amɛkafite mi niyenii bibii lɛ?

english: Young cassava shoots and plantain leaves attract free-roaming farm animals. Building a natural boundary using thorny hedge plants or fencing the plot during the crop's early growth stages keeps animals out until the plants are tall enough to survive.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii kɛ plantain baai gbalaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ. Kɛ́ afee adebɔɔ mli husu ko kɛtsɔ ŋmeii loo kpokpaa nɔ gbogbo nɔ yɛ tso lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dalɛ be mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi akabote mli kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green leaves. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the newer top leaves to survive, leaving the older bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛyeɔ baai eŋɔli ni miida lɛ Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ha shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same place drains the same nutrients from the soil season after season. It also allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans helps put natural food back into the soil and starves out pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ hu faa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out so quickly a day or two after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water rapidly to the hot sun and wind through evaporation. Covering the ground around your crops with dried leaves, grass, or straw acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool and retains moisture in the ground much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle onibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Always pick stems from healthy, fully grown cassava plants that have no insect holes or diseased spots. Select thick cuttings from the middle part of the stem with close, raised buds that look fresh rather than thin, soft, or dried-out branches.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, halamɔ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eda ni bɛ ŋmeii bu loo helai ahe ŋmeii. Halamɔ tsei niji ni mli tse kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ ebɛŋkɛ ni etamɔ ehee. Mohu ɔ, niji ɔmɛ ngɛ nyafii, a he jɔ, aloo a gbi.

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, soil food, and sunlight. This competition makes the plants grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in smaller harvests or tiny fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, egbɔjɔɔ, ni egbɔjɔ, ni no haa yibiiwoo loo yibii bibii baa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the vines up off the damp ground where diseases live and spreads the leaves out so they catch as much sunlight as possible.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ wain tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ni egbɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ eshwaa koni ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no bigger trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sunlight and high heat. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains or cassava act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa seedlings the moisture and shade they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Tomato plants often drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or irregular watering. If the weather gets too hot or the soil completely dries out while flowering, the plant drops its flowers to save energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be kpe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Curled or twisted pepper leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking juice from the underside of the leaves. These insects can also pass viruses to the plant, causing the leaves to deform and stunt overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ebɔle loo etsɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo thrips miinu nu kɛjɛ baa lɛ shishi. Kooloi nɛɛ hu baanyɛ amɛkɛ helai aha tsei. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly right after I clear my land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant deep under the dirt for many months. When you clear the land and disturb the soil, those buried seeds get brought up to the surface where warmth and sunlight wake them up to sprout all at once.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ nyɔji babaoo. Kɛ́ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ogbala shikpɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ, akɛ nakai dumɔwui ni afu lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni hulutsoo kɛ hulu la lɛ baate amɛ shi koni amɛdara yɛ be kome mli lɛ

english: What happens if I plant my maize late in July?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ July naagbee gbɛ?

english: Planting maize late in July is risky because the main rainy season is ending. Without enough steady rainfall, young seedlings will suffer from drought, leading to poor yields or complete crop failure.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ July naagbee lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ miiba naagbee. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ faaa lɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ baaná hɔmɔ he amanehulu. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo ni ehiii loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kwraa.

english: How do I know if it is too late in the season to start planting fresh corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ be lɛ eshɛ sɛɛ tsɔ ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa hee dumɔ?

english: If your previous corn crop is still standing in the field in July and you have not prepared the soil yet, the natural rain cycle is closing, making it too late to start a fresh crop successfully.
ga: Kɛji o-abele momo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo yɛ July mli ni osaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ lolo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔnɛmɔ shihilɛ lɛ miiba naagbee. Enɛ haa esɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ ni abaanyɛ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why is proper seasonal timing so important for growing maize in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Maize relies heavily on the main rainfall window to grow strong roots and form healthy ears. Planting outside this window means the plants run out of water before maturity, causing them to dry up.
ga: Abele kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ samflɛ titri ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ waa koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ ni ekɛ toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. Kɛ́ tso lɛ da yɛ samflɛ nɛɛ kponɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nu efo tso lɛ mli dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbi

english: If my mature corn is still standing in the field in July, should I harvest it or start planting new seeds?
ga: Kɛji mi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo yɛ July mli Ani esa akɛ makpa loo mabɔi dumɔwui heei?

english: You should focus entirely on harvesting your mature corn. Trying to plant new seeds while your ready crop is still standing delays both tasks and risks losing the harvest you already produced.
