ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmãa ni egbɔ lɛ kpamɔ nɔ. Mɔdɛŋ ni ooobɔ ni odu dumɔwui heei yɛ be mli ni onibii ni okɛsaa lɛ damɔ shi lolo lɛ. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa nɔ ni ofee momo lɛ baafite.

english: Can I harvest my standing corn and immediately plant a new batch on the same land in July?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmãa ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni madu ŋmãa hee amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ July mli?

english: Attempting to harvest and immediately replant late in July usually fails. There is not enough time or soil moisture left in the late season for the new crop to mature properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni akpa ni adu ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ July naagbee lɛ yeɔ omanye. Be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ koni tsei heei anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I do if I am running out of time to plant a second crop this season?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji be ni mikɛbaadu tso ni ji enyɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ miiho?

english: It is best to stop planting for the season and dedicate all your time and resources to harvesting, drying, and storing the crops you currently have in the ground.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa dumɔwui kɛha be lɛ ni okɛ obei kɛ onibii fɛɛ atsu nibii ni oyɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akpamɔ, amɛgbimɔ, kɛ amɛtoo he nii.

english: What happens to my ready corn if I leave it standing in the field while trying to prepare new land?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa ni mifee klalo akɛ ayeɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni mibɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni masaa shikpɔŋ hee lɛ?

english: Leaving mature corn in the field too long exposes it to pests, birds, damp rot, and mold, destroying the good crop you worked hard to grow.
ga: Abele ni ashiɔ koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, okpoi, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baa, ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. ni otsu nii waa koni onyɛ oda lɛ

english: Why does trying to grow two back-to-back maize crops late in the season usually fail?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni adu ŋmãa tsei enyɔ ni nyiɛɔ amɛsɛɛ yɛ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ehiii be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: A late second crop usually runs out of rain mid-growth. Without enough soil moisture to sustain the plants during tasseling and ear formation, the second crop produces empty or stunted ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ ni baa sɛɛ lɛ bɛ nugbɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ teŋgbɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tso lɛ yɛ be mli ni tassel kɛ toi lɛ feɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Akpamɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baaha toi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbɔjɔ.

english: Is it better to save my money for the next major season rather than buying new maize seeds late in July?
ga: Ani ebafeŋ nɔ ni hi akɛ oookɛ shika ato kɛha be wulu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo he ngma duwu ehe ngɛ July nyagbe.

english: Yes, saving your resources for the next major rainy season is much safer. Spending money on seeds late in July carries a very high risk of crop failure due to dry weather.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, eyɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa akɛ oookɛ nibii ato kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu ni baa lɛ. Shika ni afiteɔ yɛ dumɔwui ahe yɛ July naagbee lɛ kɛ oshara ni mli wa waa baa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite yɛ shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does rushing land preparation and harvesting at the same time cause crop failure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni asaa he oya kɛ nikpamɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Rushing prevents you from properly clearing and feeding the soil for new plants, while simultaneously delaying your current harvest, resulting in poor performance on both fronts.
ga: Oyaiyeli tsɔɔ akɛ onyɛŋ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ niyenii aha tsei heei. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa okpamɔ ni okpaa amrɔ nɛɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ yɛ hei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ehiii kwraa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen nutrients in the soil or isn't getting enough water. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing season helps leaves stay green so the plant can feed its growing cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they face extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil moist with mulching and watering during dry spells helps the flowers stay attached and turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean plants grow so well when I plant them right next to my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ mi-corn lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans naturally pull nitrogen gas out of the air and deposit it into the soil as plant food. This extra food enriches the soil and feeds neighboring crops like maize, which need a lot of nitrogen to thrive.
ga: Beans jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ tsei aniyenii. Nɛkɛ niyenii ni akɛfataa he nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni he hiaa nitrogen babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so it doesn't rot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni ekafite?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn brown and dry, the silks turn dark brown, and the kernels become hard and glossy. Harvesting too early causes the wet grains to rot quickly, while waiting too long leaves them open to insect attacks.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. Siliki lɛ tsɔɔ blɔfo. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee shiŋŋ ni amɛkpɛ Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ baaha dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ agbo oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kooloi bibii atutua dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested grain get eaten by tiny insects so quickly inside my storeroom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mi nitoohe lɛ yeɔ midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ oya lɛ?

english: Grain pests thrive when crops are stored while still wet or kept in humid, dark rooms. Drying your harvested grain thoroughly in the sun until kernels are hard and storing them in sealed, airtight bags starves insects of the moisture and air they need to survive.
ga: Nibii ni gbeɔ ŋmaa lɛ yeɔ omanye jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni amɛmli efɔ lolo loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli efɔ mli. Akɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛgbiɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha koolooi anine shɛɛɛ fɛ̃i kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and rot underground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifoɔ amɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when soil stays waterlogged for too long or gets infected by soil fungi. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds allows excess rain water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do commercial buyers offer me low prices for my maize during the main harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi ni heɔ nii lɛ haa mi ŋmãa jara ni baa shi yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Prices fall during the main harvest because almost every farmer is harvesting and selling at the same time, creating a huge supply in the market. When buyers have plenty of crop to choose from, prices drop; selling later when crops are scarce brings higher prices.
ga: Jara baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ mli ejaakɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ kpaa ŋmaa ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa nibii babaoo baa jara nɔ. Kɛ́ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhala mli lɛ, amɛjara baa shi. Nihɔɔmɔ sɛɛ mli beni ŋmɔshi nibii faaa lɛ haa jara yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do large grain companies reject some of my maize bags even when the grains look good to me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa nitsumɔhe wulu ko kpoo mi-ŋmaa kotokui lɛ ekomɛi eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmaa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi moŋ?

english: Commercial companies test grains for hidden moisture levels, internal insect damage, and invisible molds like aflatoxin. Ensuring your maize is sun-dried until moisture is low and sorting out cracked or discolored grains helps your crop pass their quality tests.
ga: Jarayeli nitsumɔhei kaa ŋmaa amɛkwɛɔ kɛji amɛmli nu lɛ falɛ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Kplukai ni fiteɔ nii yɛ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni anaaa tamɔ aflatoxins. Kɛji okwɛ koni o-ŋmã lɛ agbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ baa shi lɛ, ni ojie ŋmãa ni egbɛ eshwa loo ehiɛ su lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmãa lɛ ni etsɔ kaai ni akɛkwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ hi ha lɛ nɔ.

english: How do fall armyworms manage to destroy my young maize plants so fast?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni fall cutworms lɛ nyɛ amɛfite mi-kooloi bibii lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Armyworm caterpillars crawl deep into the central funnel of young maize plants where new leaves grow and eat the growing tip from the inside out. Checking the central leaves early and applying control measures while caterpillars are small protects the heart of the plant.
ga: Kplukai lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Eyɛ baai heei ni eyeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mra Ni ofee nɔ ko ni okɛbaakwɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ darako lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ tsui lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after I clear the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that react quickly to rain and steal light, water, and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks of planting gives your crops the space and food they need to grow tall and shade out competing weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃, ni ebaaha jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ aná hulutsoo.

english: Why do my maize crops get weak and die when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egboɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Just like too many people in a small space, overcrowded plants get weak, easily catch diseases, and many will die before harvest.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tamɔ mɛi babaoo tsɔ yɛ he bibioo ko. Tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ. helai baanyɛ amɔ amɛ oya ni mɛi babaoo baagboi dani akpa.

english: Will I get more cassava if I plant fewer stems on my farm plot?
ga: Ani maná ŋmei babaoo kɛji midu tsei fioo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, giving each cassava plant enough space allows its roots to spread and feed properly. Proper spacing produces fewer total plants but yields larger, heavier tubers compared to an overcrowded field.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ aha ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha tsei lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ aba shi. Shi enáa yitsei wuji ni etsiiɔ kɛ akɛto hei ni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants turn yellow and dry up even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the plant is sick with a disease caused by fungi or viruses, not that it is thirsty. When a plant gets sick, its internal pipes get blocked, preventing water and food from moving through it.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ hela ko ni ŋmei loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko kɛbaa. Jeee akɛ kumai miiye amɛ. Kɛ́ tso ko hela mɔ lɛ, paipii ni yɔɔ emli lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe. Etsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii naa koni amɛkatsɔ mli.

english: If I see one sick pepper plant on my farm, can it make the healthy ones sick too?
ga: Kɛji mina pepper tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani ebaanyɛ eha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ hu aná hela?

english: Yes, plant diseases spread quickly through insects, wind, rain drops, or even on your farming tools. Removing and destroying a sick plant immediately protects the rest of your healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kɛ okwaayeli nibii po anɔ. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ofite lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean plants look healthy in the morning but wilt and die by the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ leebi lɛ? Shi ebaagbi ni egbo yɛ shwane mli?

english: This sudden collapse is usually caused by root rot or pests in the soil that destroy the roots silently. Once midday heat hits, the damaged roots cannot draw enough water, causing the plant to collapse rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni egbo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ dioo yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ gbee ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni haa tsei shwieɔ shi oya

english: Why do many of my young cocoa seedlings die shortly after I move them into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo gboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moving young seedlings exposes them to harsh direct sunlight and hot winds, causing shock. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a cool environment that keeps young seedlings alive.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baa amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ, ni ehaa amɛhe feɔ shoo. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni haa dumɔwui bibii hiɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Can using too much chemical fertilizer cause my young crops to burn and die?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha mi dumɔwui lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi?

english: Yes, high amounts of fertilizer act like hot salt on tender crop roots, burning them and cutting off their ability to drink water. This makes plants wither and die instead of growing.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ yɛ tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ. Eshãa tsei ashishifãi ni efoɔ nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my crop field regularly instead of just watching from the edge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔ ŋmɔji amli daa moŋ fe ni makwɛ kɛjɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Walking inside your field lets you spot early signs of crop sickness and pest attacks before they spread. Regular monitoring helps you stop plant deaths early when the problem is still small.
ga: Kɛ́ onyiɛ kɛbote oŋmɔji amli lɛ, ehaa onaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe okadii mra dani amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei lɛ amli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni okpa tsei lɛ agbele mra. Beni naagba lɛ yɔɔ lolo fioo lɛ

english: What causes the top tips of my cocoa branches to dry up and die off?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ayitsei lɛ miigbi ni amɛgboi?

english: This dieback is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like mirids (akate) or fungal infections. They damage the branch tissue, cutting off food flow until the top part dries up and dies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (akate) loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ gbele nɛɛ baa. Amɛfiteɔ tsei niji amli fãji. ni ofo niyenii ni hoɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ baagbi ni egbo.

english: Why are insect pests killing crops on my farm while my neighbor's farm remains healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai miigbe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ kã he ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pests naturally target farms with stressed, overcrowded, or unweeded plants because weak plants cannot defend themselves. Keeping your farm clean and well-spaced keeps your crops strong enough to resist pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔji ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni haoɔ mɔ, ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ abu amɛhe. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni okɛ ohe wo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Is water from a borehole or deep well safe to use directly on my vegetable crops?
ga: Ani nu ni jɛɔ nu bu loo nubu ni mli kwɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, water from a borehole or well is very safe and clean for crops like tomatoes, peppers, and garden eggs. It gives the plants a steady supply of fresh moisture during dry periods so they can grow strong leaves and develop healthy fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni jɛɔ nu bu loo nu bu mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe waa ni ehe tse kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ, ni ehaa amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ hee ni yaa nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ baai ni wa ni ewo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can using water pumped from a village dam help my crops grow better than waiting for rain?
ga: Ani nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ akrowa lɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe nugbɔ ni mimɛɔ?

english: Yes, dam water allows you to feed your crops water whenever they need it rather than waiting for unpredictable rainfall. Dam water also often contains rich soil sediment and nutrients washed from surrounding land, which feeds the plants and encourages green, leafy growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni yɔɔ faa mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu haa onibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ehe baahia bo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ nugbɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ Bei pii lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ nu ŋshɔi lɛ amli lɛ mli sũ ni baa nii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni nu lɛ efo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ yɔɔ mli. ni haa tsei hewalɛ ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ daraa

english: Why do seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in dry soil before the water supply is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nu lɛ shɛɔ?

english: Seeds stay dormant, like they are sleeping, until moisture wakes them up. Without consistent moisture from rain, a well, or a dam, the outer shell of the seed cannot soften, meaning roots cannot break through to start growing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baajɔɔ amɛhe tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiiwɔ. Kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baate bo Kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni jɛɔ nugbɔ, nubui, loo nugbɔshiimɔi amli lɛ bɛ lɛ, dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ nyɛŋ afee blɛoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ abote mli koni amɛje dalɛ shishi.

english: How can I tell by looking at my maize leaves if the crop is not getting enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛtsɔ ŋmãa baai ni mikwɛɔ lɛ nɔ akɛ tso lɛ naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: When maize plants do not get enough water, their broad green leaves start curling inward like straws to trap moisture. If the leaves stay curled early in the morning before the sun gets hot, the crop is under water stress and needs immediate irrigation.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Ebaai eŋɔlii ni mli kwɔ lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛmiiya mli tamɔ jwɛi koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieɔ shi leebi dani hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ shɛɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nu he haomɔ shishi ni ehe miihia ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato plants drop their flowers during hot dry months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences heat and lacks sufficient soil moisture, it goes into survival mode. It drops its flowers to save energy and water for its main stem and roots, which prevents fruits from forming unless you supply steady water.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli. Ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato kɛha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ baatsi aduawai anaa, ja okɛ nu haa amɛ daa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when water sits around the roots for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water sits continuously around the roots without draining away, it chokes the roots, stopping them from absorbing nutrients and causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu bɔle shishifãi ahe be fɛɛ be ni efooo Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. etsĩɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does regular watering encourage crop roots to grow strong in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When soil receives deep and regular watering, the crop roots stretch deeper down into the ground searching for moisture. Deep roots anchor the plant firmly against strong winds and allow it to feed on nutrients hidden deep in the earth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo ni afeɔ daa Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao ŋmɔtɔ. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ teɔ shi ewoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, ni ehaa eyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: At what stage in a crop's lifecycle does it need the most water to ensure a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli tso ko wala shihilɛ mli nu he hiaa lɛ fe fɛɛ koni enyɛ ekpa nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Crops require the most water during their flowering and fruiting or pod-filling stages. If plants lack water during this critical window, the fruits will remain small, seeds will fail to fill out, and the overall harvest weight will drop significantly.
ga: Nu he hiaa tsei fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, amɛwoɔ yibii, kɛ amɛwoɔ pod lɛ mli. Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ, Yibii lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo. Dumɔwui lɛ eyimɔɔɔ. ni ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ mli tsiimɔ baa shi waa.

english: If I start watering my farm early in the year, how does that help me harvest successful crops by August?
ga: Kɛji mibɔi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu hamɔ yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ Te ebaaye ebua mi tɛŋŋ koni makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi August?

english: Starting irrigation early in the dry season gives your crops a head start to complete their growing cycle on time. By the time August arrives, the plants have received enough consistent water during their growing phase to produce fully matured, market-ready yields.
ga: Kɛ́ obɔi nu shwiemɔ mra yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ amɛdalɛ shishi yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ ebashɛ August Tso lɛ baaná nu ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ. Koni ana nibii ni adu lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni asaa he kɛha jarayeli.

english: Why do mature cassava and groundnut crops rot if they receive too much water right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei tsei ni edara lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛná nu babaoo dani akpa lɛ?

english: As crops near maturity, their focus shifts from growing leaves to storing starches in the roots and pods. Too much excess water late in the cycle makes the soil soggy, attracting soil fungi that cause the fully formed tubers and pods to decay before you can harvest them.
ga: Beni eshwɛ fioo ni tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, jwɛŋmɔ lɛ shiɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni abua naa yɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Nu babaoo ni fa fe nine yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaagbala shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe kwraa lɛ fiteɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to write down the exact date I planted my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋma gbi pɔtɛɛ ni midu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Recording your planting date creates a baseline to track your crop's growth stages, schedule weed control, and accurately predict when your maize will be ready for harvest.
ga: Gbii ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ ni oooŋmala lɛ feɔ shishitoo nɔ ni obaanyɛ odamɔ nɔ okwɛ bɔ ni otso lɛ daa lɛ. Be ni akɛbaatsu jwɛi ahe nii ni otsɔɔ be ni oŋmãa lɛ baafee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are growing at the normal speed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miida oya bɔ ni sa?

english: You can check progress by looking at monthly stem height and leaf fullness, comparing your plants' current growth against standard benchmarks for that cassava variety.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni eyaa nɔ ehaa lɛ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛ ebaa lɛ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ daa nyɔŋ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ ni akɛtoɔ shishitoo mlai ni akɛtoɔ nakai ŋmei srɔtoi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: How frequently should I walk through my field to check how my crops are performing?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔji amli koni makwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa?

english: Walking through your field at least once or twice a week allows you to notice subtle changes in plant growth, spot early pest infestations, and fix problems before they reduce your yield.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ otsɔ oŋmɔji amli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni baa tsei lɛ adalɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ shishijee mli. ni osaa naagbai dani amɛha onitsumɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: How can my farming experience from past years help me predict this season's harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niiashikpamɔ ni miná yɛ okwaayeli mli yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni matsɔɔ be nɛɛ mli nikpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Comparing current plant growth against what you observed in previous successful years helps you quickly identify whether your crops are behind schedule or growing normally.
ga: Kɛ okɛ tsei ni daraa amrɔ nɛɛ to nɔ ni ona yɛ afii ni eho ni ye omanye lɛ amli lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni oyɔseɔ oya kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efo be ni ato lɛ sɛɛ loo amɛmiida bɔ ni sa.

english: Extreme heat causes heat stress in pepper plants, forcing them to drop blossoms to conserve energy and moisture until cooler conditions return.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ afolɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni akɛ hewalɛ kɛ hulutsoo akafite kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do changing rainfall patterns in Ghana affect when my crops mature?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ ni tsakeɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rainfall controls soil moisture levels, which directly speeds up or slows down plant development, shifting the timeline for when crops flower and ripen.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ kudɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i. ni baaha tsei lɛ aya hiɛ oya loo amɛya hiɛ fioo tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛtsɔ be ni tsei fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ tsakemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellowish during prolonged dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are a response to heat stress and low soil moisture; cocoa trees reduce nutrient flow to older leaves to conserve water for main plant survival.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji hetoo kɛha dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ. Cacao tsei lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni hoɔ kɛyaa baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ baa shi koni akɛto nu he gbɛjianɔ koni tso ni ŋmɛɔ amɛ lɛ ahi shi.

english: How do I know if my tomato plants are spending too much energy growing leaves instead of fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo miitsu nii ni ekɛmiikwɛ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ?

english: If tomato vines grow thick with dense dark green leaves but produce very few flower clusters, the plant has too much nitrogen and is prioritizing leafy growth over fruiting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-tomato wain tso lɛ daa babaoo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi fɔfɔi akui fioo pɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo tsɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ema baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ fe aduawai ni ato lɛ.

english: Why do two neighboring fields planted in the same week show different crop growth speeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hei enyɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe ni adu yɛ otsi kome mli lɛ jieɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi lɛ akpo lɛ?

english: Growth rates vary based on differences in soil fertility, water retention, land preparation, and weed competition, even when seeds are sown on the exact same date.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ ehaa lɛ yɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ naa. Nu ni ahiɛɔ, shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ kɛ jwɛi akaŋshii Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ po.

english: What signs above the ground show that my yam tubers are developing well under the soil?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ okadii komɛi ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Strong, lush green foliage and thick vines mid-season, followed by a gradual natural yellowing late in the season, indicate that yam tubers are swelling healthy underground.
ga: Foji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ wain tsei ni mli eyi obɔ yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa fiofio yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when planted out in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their sensitive leaves and dries out soil moisture. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them protects the young cocoa until it is mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers when I let them grow on the ground instead of using wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii beni mihaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam vines off the ground so the leaves can catch more sunlight to make food. When vines stay on the ground, leaves get crowded, shaded, and prone to diseases, which reduces the energy available to grow large tubers.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo kɛha nihoomɔ. Beni wain tso lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ, eyɛ hulutsoo ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb wuji lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers from my plantain shoot instead of letting all of them grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo plantain tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛ fɛɛ amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain stem creates competition for light, water, and soil nutrients. Keeping only the main stem and one or two strong suckers ensures the plant has enough resources to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Plantain kome pɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tso lɛ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves in a V-shape pattern is a sign that the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow vigorously, so when it is missing, the plant pulls nitrogen from older leaves to feed newer ones.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ Tsei lɛ elaaje lɛ, amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and developing pale green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by using infected stems for planting. It reduces the plant's ability to produce food, leading to poor yield.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Ehaa nyɛmɔ ni tsei yɔɔ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant draw calcium up to the fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛgbalaa calcium kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat, insufficient water, or poor soil nutrients. High temperatures stress the plant, causing it to shed blossoms to conserve water and energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi baa koni akɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do extension officers encourage me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land before planting maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi hewalɛ koni madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop season ends, leaving these root residues enriches the soil naturally with nitrogen for the next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Shishifãi ni eshwɛ nɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my crops only when the soil is moist rather than dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli pɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe ni egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers must dissolve in water for plant roots to absorb them. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil can burn the roots and kill the crop because there is no moisture to dilute the nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ nu bɛ ni baaha niyenii mli nibii lɛ afee mlɛo.

english: Why does my swamp rice grow much better when there is standing water in the field during its early growth stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-swamp ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ be mli ni nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ shishijee be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Standing water controls weed growth by suffocating unwanted plants while providing continuous moisture that lowland rice varieties need to absorb soil nutrients and develop strong stems.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ kudɔɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni ataooo lɛ ni ehaa amɛmuɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛná tsei ni wa.

english: How long after spraying chemical medicine on my farm should I wait before I can see it working on the pests?
ga: Beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mana tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi?

english: Chemical medicines need time to absorb into the plant or pest body. Systemic chemicals take about 1 to 3 weeks to move through the plant stem and roots to completely stop pest damage, so immediate results are not always visible on the first day.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ heɔ be dani amɛboteɔ tso lɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ mli. Eheɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli lɛ aaafee otsi 1 kɛyashi 3 dani etsɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli koni ekpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, jeee be fɛɛ be anaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ.

english: If heavy rain falls right after I apply liquid medicine to my crops, do I need to spray again?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ nu lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ Ani ehe miihia ni mafo ekoŋŋ?

english: If rain falls within 2 to 4 hours of spraying, it washes the medicine off the leaves before the plant can soak it in. You should wait for a dry day so the medicine has enough time to stick to the leaves and work properly.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 2 kɛyashi 4 mli yɛ tsofa lɛ ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ Tsofa lɛ baaho baai lɛ ahe dani tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi gbi lɛ mli agbi koni tsofa lɛ aha be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkpɛtɛ baai lɛ ahe ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young maize plants have purple leaves even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize are usually a sign of phosphorus deficiency. Cold or overly wet soil prevents young roots from taking in this nutrient, but as the roots grow deeper and the soil warms up, the natural green color usually returns.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ loo edɔ tsɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi bibii anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii nɛɛ. Shi beni shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli woɔ la lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very thick green leaves but producing almost no flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa shi eshwɛ fioo ni fɔfɔi ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Your plants are getting too much nitrogen fertilizer. Nitrogen makes plants focus all their energy on growing leaves and stems, while delaying flower and fruit production. Balancing your fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium helps them bloom.
ga: O tsei lɛ miiná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsɔ. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ akɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potassium to ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why does my land need to rest or grow beans after I harvest maize from it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ajɔɔ mihe loo adu ŋmeii beni mikpa mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize draws heavy amounts of nutrients from the soil every season. Resting the land or planting leguminous crops like beans helps restore nitrogen naturally into the ground and breaks pest cycles before your next planting.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ofo tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli dani adu nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant plantains alongside new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension official lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔdu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: This is called cherelle wilt. The cocoa tree naturally sheds young pods it cannot support if it lacks water, nutrients, or sunlight. It is the tree's way of saving energy for the pods it can successfully mature.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, ni kɛ́ nu, niyenii, loo hulu la bɛ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ. Eji tso lɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so the roots do not become tough and woody?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni shishifãi lɛ akafee nɔ ni wa ni efee tso?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. If left in the ground past their maturity period into a dry season, the roots convert their soft starch into hard woody fibers.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ mli kɛyashi be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ ho kɛtee hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amɛfeɔ tso mli ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Yam vines use their leaves to catch sunlight and convert it into food for the growing tuber under the soil. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay free from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛheɔ hulu la ni amɛfeɔ lɛ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni helai bɛ nɔ lɛ aha.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking sap from the tender leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Removing heavily infected plants and controlling small sucking insects early stops it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra lɛ baaha egbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Why do I need to spray chemical medicine on my crop even when I do not see any insects or disease on it yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi loo helai komɛi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lolo moŋ?

english: Spraying early acts like a vaccine for your crop. Some diseases are caused by tiny germs you cannot see with your eyes, so applying protection early prevents the disease from taking root and destroying the plant later.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Ebaafee tamɔ tsofa ni akɛbaagbe oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Muawai bibii kɛ helai komɛi baa. ni onyɛɛɛ okɛ ohiŋmɛii ana No hewɔ lɛ, tsimɔ kɛjɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akatswa shishifãi ni sɛɛ mli lɛ efite tso lɛ.

english: How do I know the right month or stage to stop spraying my crops before I harvest them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔŋ loo be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwiemɔ dani kpamɔ?

english: Every crop medicine has a safe waiting time before harvest. You must stop spraying a few weeks before harvesting so the medicine has time to wash away and wear off, making the food safe for people to eat.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ yɛ be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛkɛmɛɔ dani akpaa. Esa akɛ okpa tsofa lɛ shwiemɔ otsii fioo komɛi dani akpa. Enɛ haa tsofa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ni ekɛfite. Ehaa niyenii feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha gbɔmɛi ni amɛyeɔ.

english: If I use the same chemical medicine on my farm every season, will it keep working the same way?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa be Ani ebaatsu nii yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ?

english: No, if you use the same medicine continuously, the insects or diseases get used to it and become stronger against it. You should switch between different types of medicine so the pests do not build resistance.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii be fɛɛ be. Kpluka loo hela lɛ baatsɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ ni ebaaná hewalɛ. Esa akɛ otsake tsofai srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ ji koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa.

english: Is the medicine that kills insects on my farm the same as the medicine that treats sickness on the leaves?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsaa tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ egbɔ?

english: No, they are different. Insecticide medicine is made only to kill insects, while fungicide medicine treats diseases caused by germs and fungi. Using insect medicine on a plant leaf disease will not cure it.
ga: Dabi, esoro amɛ. Afeɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi koni akɛgbe kooloi pɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsaa helai ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ baa helai anɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsa.

english: How many months after planting my crop should I start spraying it with disease medicine?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu nii lɛ esa akɛ mabɔi tsofa shwiemɔ?

english: It depends on the crop, but many plants need protection once they start developing heavy leaves or flowers—often around two to four months after planting—because that is when pests and diseases like to attack.
ga: Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ Shi tsei babaoo he miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛji amɛbɔi baai loo fɔfɔi ni tsii kpojiemɔ—bei pii lɛ, nyɔji enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ—ejaakɛ nakai beaŋ ji be ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua amɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my crop falling off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop off when the plant is stressed from lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or attacks by tiny insects. Ensuring the plant gets adequate water and pest care helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mɔ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ nu bɔ ni sa ni akɛ tsofai fɔji tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔii lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Is it safe for me to spray chemical medicine on my crop while the flowers are blooming?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: You must be very careful. Spraying harsh chemicals directly on open flowers can burn them or kill friendly insects like bees that help the flowers turn into fruit. It is best to spray early in the morning or use flower-safe products.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ waa. Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo egbe kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi loo okɛ nɔ ko ni fɔfɔii nyɛŋ afee lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do some of my crop plants produce plenty of flowers while others on the same land produce very few?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ he kome lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Soil quality and sunlight are not always equal across a farm. Plants growing in spots with richer soil or more direct sunlight will gather more energy to produce a lot of healthy flowers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ mlihilɛ jeee be fɛɛ be. Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni sũ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baabua hewalɛ babaoo naa koni ekɛ fɔfɔi babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why does my crop look very strong for the first few months but then start catching diseases when it begins to flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli shi no sɛɛ lɛ, kɛ́ ebɔi fɔfɔii lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni hela lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa mi lɛ?

english: As crops grow bigger and produce flowers, they put a lot of energy into making fruit, which makes them weaker against diseases. Also, bushy plants trap moisture around the stems, creating an easy environment for diseases to spread.
ga: Beni tso lɛ da ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ yibii. Enɛ haa helai nyɛɔ mɔɔ amɛ oya. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ni ehaa shihilɛ ko ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if the flowers blooming on my crop will produce a good yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji fɔfɔi ni fɔ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha ŋmaa kpakpa aba?

english: Healthy blooming flowers are bright, fully open, and free from dark spots, webbings, or insects crawling inside them. Healthy flowers mean the plant has enough energy to grow abundant fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kpɛɔ, amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe kwraa, ni ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ yɛ mli lɛ bɛ mli. Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo.

english: Will spraying one type of weed killer kill every single kind of weed on my farm?
ga: Ani tsofa kome ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baagbe jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No chemical kills every weed. Some weed killers target broad-leaf plants while others target grasses, so you must select the right chemical for the specific weeds growing on your farm.
ga: Akɛ tsofa ko tsuuu nii ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi fɛɛ. Tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ jwɛi nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ohala tsofai ni sa kɛha jwɛi pɔtɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put extra chemical into my spray tank to clear the weeds faster?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai krokomɛi fata tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nu mli lɛ he koni egbe jwɛi oya?

english: Adding more chemical than instructed can burn or kill your crops along with the weeds. Over-dosing turns a safe farm chemical into a poison for your crop.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛfataa he fe bɔ ni esa akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo egbe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛfata jwɛi ahe. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ feɔ poison kɛhaa onibii.

english: Will the chemical I spray to kill weeds stay in the soil and harm the next crop I plant?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ shi koni mikɛgbe jwɛi lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eye ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaadu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ awui?

english: Most weed killers break down in the soil after a few weeks, but using too much can leave residues that weaken the crops you plant in the next season.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Shi kɛ okɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ baagbɔjɔ.

english: Why does my maize look weak and yellowish after I spray my field to control weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ nu shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni mikɛkudɔ jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Even crop-safe weed killers can cause temporary stress to maize as the plant works to process the chemical. The maize usually recovers in a few days if the chemical was measured correctly.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po baanyɛ aha ŋmãa lɛ aná haomɔ be kukuoo ko yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ tsuɔ tsofai lɛ ahe nii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaná hewalɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛji akɛ asusu tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does a weed chemical kill the wild grass on my land without destroying my corn crop?
ga: Te tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tɛŋŋ ni egbeee ŋmãa tsei lɛ?

english: Selective weed chemicals target specific plant structures. Corn plants can naturally break down these specific chemicals safely, while the wild grass cannot and dies.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ. Abele tsei fiteɔ tsofai pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa shweshweeshwe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, koo mli jwɛi nyɛŋ afee enɛ ni amɛgboi.

english: Is it safe for me to spray weed killers when my crop seedlings have just sprouted out of the dirt?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ beni mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ miije kpo kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Very young crop seedlings are delicate and easily injured by chemicals. It is best to use pre-emergence chemicals before seeds sprout, or wait until seedlings are older and stronger.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii waa lɛ waaa ni tsofai yeɔ amɛ awui oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baatsu nii dani dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Aloo mɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ adara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are some weeds still standing on my farm days after I sprayed them with weed killer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi komɛi damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie shi lɛ?

english: Some weeds have waxy leaves or deep roots that stop the chemical from soaking in, or the chemical used was not designed for that specific broad-leaf or grass weed.
ga: Jwɛi komɛi yɛ baai ni tamɔ wax loo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni tsofai akabote mli. Aloo afeee tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahaaa jwɛi loo jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ.

english: If heavy rain falls right after I spray chemical on my farm, do I need to spray again?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afɔ tsofai yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani ehe baahia ni afɔ nɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain washes the chemical off plant leaves before it can work. You should wait for dry weather so the chemical has a few hours to soak into the weeds.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ ahe dani amɛtsuɔ nii. Esa akɛ oha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ agbi bɔni afee ni tsofai lɛ aná ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi ni amɛkɛbote jwɛi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops at the edge of the farm look damaged when I only sprayed the weeds in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite beni mikɛ jwɛi pɛ shwieɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Wind can carry fine chemical mist onto crops you did not mean to spray. Spraying on calm mornings close to the ground prevents this drift from hurting your crops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni osusuuu akɛ obaashwie nɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi ni yɔɔ dioo ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ aerosol nɛɛ naa koni ekaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Is it better for my crops if I clear weeds by hand with a cutlass or with chemical spray?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mikɛ minine shwie jwɛi lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmei loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Clearing by hand with a cutlass carries zero risk of chemical damage to your crops, but chemical spraying saves time on larger farms if you measure the dosage carefully.
ga: Nine ni akɛ ŋmei tsuɔ he nii lɛ bɛ oshara ko kwraa akɛ tsofai baafite oŋmɔshi nibii. Shi tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha be akafite yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli kɛji osusu tsofa lɛ falɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need big shade trees like plantains growing right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tso agbo ko tamɔ plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ aha mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he ajɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that scorch easily in strong sunlight. Shade crops like plantains act like living umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and protecting soil moisture while the young tree grows strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ miida lolo ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná la ni fa babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the branches when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: During the hot, dry season, cocoa trees lose water quickly. To survive the heat stress and conserve water, the tree naturally sheds its delicate flowers and young pods so it doesn't dry out completely.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ nu fiteɔ oya. Bɔni afee ni amɛhi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli ni amɛbu nu he lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛbii bibii lɛ kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiko kwraa.

english: Why does cutting off extra leaves and branches from my cocoa tree make it produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi cacao tso lɛ mli baai kɛ niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo baa lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the canopy so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This stops moisture from trapping damp diseases and forces the tree to direct its energy into growing big pods instead of unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekamɔ helai ni mli edɔ. kɛ tso lɛ ni enyɛɔ enɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with many leaves but gives me tiny cassava roots at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ cassava shishifãi bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akpa?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or green fertilizer, the cassava plant puts all its strength into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending food down to grow thick tubers in the soil.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛhaa ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni adu ŋmeii ni mli edɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall wooden sticks instead of letting them trail on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji akpɛtɛ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha enyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows sunlight to reach every leaf, helping the plant make more food for the root underground. It also keeps the leaves off damp dirt where diseases can easily rot them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ baa fɛɛ baa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo amɛhaa amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa muji ni mli ewo fɔ ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã helai srɔtoi amli lɛ akashɛ baai lɛ ahe. ni fiteɔ oya

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize are a clear sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. The maize plant pulls energy from its older, bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Abɛi tsei lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plant blossoms drop off to the ground without ever turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the daytime weather gets too hot or when the soil goes too dry. Extreme heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop blossoms to save water and stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛfɔ fɔfɔi bɔni afee ni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by tiny water-loving fungi that spread fast when rain drops bounce off wet soil onto low pods. Overgrown weeds and high air humidity create the perfect damp environment for this rot to spread.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei bibioo ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ jɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ eshwie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong rainstorms even when the tree looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots like forest trees; their roots spread out shallowly near the topsoil. Heavy rains soften the soil, making it easy for wind to pull the shallow roots out of the ground under the weight of heavy fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ koo mli tsei. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa fioo. ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ Eshiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlɛo yɛ aduawai ni tsii ni tsii lɛ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I heap dry fertilizer right against the stem or trunk of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi toɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi loo eshishi lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem burns the tree's soft bark and surface roots because fertilizer draws moisture out of plant tissues. Fertilizer should be spread in a circle under the leaf canopy where fine roots can safely drink it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashã. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo baai lɛ ashishi yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ kokroo nɔ. Shishifãi kpakpai lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni anuɔ.

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to heat. This helps the plant trap moisture and prevent water loss through evaporation during extreme heat.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni baa baa lɛ hiɛ ni dɔlɛ baa shi. Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsiɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, leaves lose moisture faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. As long as the roots are healthy, the plant will recover its strength in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni shishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ Tso lɛ baaku esɛɛ eba hewalɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Morning watering is best because it prepares the crop for the midday sun and allows water on the leaves to dry quickly, which prevents fungal diseases from developing overnight.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ esaa tso lɛ kɛha hulutsoo be lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ni egbiɔ oya Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my crop roots turn black and start rotting when water stays on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ be mli ni nu ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When excess water covers the soil without draining, it shuts out air, causing the roots to drown, stop taking in nutrients, and decay.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa. shishifãi lɛ ni shwieɔ nu mli Kpaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ fitemɔ

english: Cassava drops its lower leaves to survive stress caused by poor soil nutrients or drought. The plant intentionally sacrificializes older foliage to send remaining food to the growing top leaves and underground tubers.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishigbɛ baai lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ haomɔ ni shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo hɔmɔ kɛbaa lɛ mli. Tso nɛɛ jɛɔ etsuiŋ ekɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when experienced with high temperature spikes or erratic watering. The plant drops flowers to save energy so it doesn't overexert itself under stressful growing conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa loo nu ni ejaaa kpe. Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, esaaa akɛ akɛ hewalɛ ni fe nine tsuɔ nii yɛ shihilɛi ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni haa mɔ daa lɛ amli.

english: What happens to my swamp rice if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi marsh rice lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When rice plants are crowded, they compete aggressively for light and water. This produces tall, thin, weak stalks that fall over easily in high winds and yield smaller, lighter grain heads.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná la kɛ nu. Enɛ haa dumɔwui akui ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ baa, ni ehaa dumɔwui ayitsei bibii ni waaa baa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees suffer and turn yellow when all shade trees are cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ naa amanehulu ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ afo cacao tsei muu fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily under direct equatorial sun. Shade trees act as natural canopy protection, maintaining humidity and cool soil temperatures required for seedling survival.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ equatorial hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛbuɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my land than my food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally hardy native plants adapted to survive in harsh conditions. They absorb water, fertilizer, and sunlight much faster than cultivated crops, effectively stealing resources meant for food plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. ni juɔ nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do improved seed varieties give higher yields than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred in laboratories to produce larger heads, resist common regional pests, and maximize nutrient use, whereas saved seeds lose these strong genetic traits over successive harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ laboratori ko mli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ yitsei wuji aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient or is waterlogged. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the plant build food and regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni efee niyenii ni ená eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, making them fall off before fruiting. Providing shade or ensuring regular watering during hot spells helps flowers stay healthy and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be loo nu ha fɔfɔi lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my cassava grow very bushy with lots of leaves but gives me small tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of roots. Avoiding heavy nitrogen fertilizers encourages the plant to store energy underground in the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ ebaa lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe eshishifãi lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking leaf sap, or by a virus they spread. Spraying with neem oil or appropriate insect treatments protects the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally during dry periods to save water and stay alive. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and resume growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaada ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees around my new young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ he lɛ? Mi kookoo tso hee lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under bright sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo koni ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants produce lots of flowers but very few pods when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete for light, air, and soil nutrients, causing stress that makes flowers drop early. Giving plants proper space allows enough sunlight and airflow for pod formation.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni haa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi oya baa. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfee pod.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain suckers turning brown and drying up during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains shed their lower leaves during dry spells to reduce water loss and protect their main stem. Putting mulch around the base of the plant helps soil hold moisture longer.
ga: Plantains shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my garden egg plant stop bearing fruit after a few months even though the stem is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekpaa yibiiwoo yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ eshishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Garden egg plants slow down fruiting as branches age and soil nutrients drain away. Pruning old branches and applying compost encourages fresh green shoots and new flowers to grow.
ga: Egg tsei ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛwo yibii be mli ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ daraa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ. Niji momoi ni aaafolɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ baawo tsei ŋmɔji heei kɛ fɔfɔi heei hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my yam leaves turn soft and develop black spots after continuous heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates high humidity that allows fungal diseases to attack yam leaves. Planting on raised mounds and weeding regularly improves airflow so leaves dry faster and stay healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni no haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa sweet potato baai lɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ, ni ajie jwɛi lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning under the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitso yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct heat and burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or banana next to them provides essential shade and moisture needed during their first few years of growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ aba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before growing into proper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii ni sa lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree experiences stress from drought, extreme heat, or damage from insect pests like mirids. Ensuring adequate moisture, shade, and timely pest control helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nibii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ pollen lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ akɛ hulutsoo, shade, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee pods.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in light and airflow, along with removing infected pods, helps stop it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ hu. baaye abua ni akpa lɛ.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the fresh central leaves of young maize. Applying recommended control methods or neem extracts early in the morning kills them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni gbeɔ ŋmãa bibii ahe baai heei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ loo neem mli nu lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting inside the ground if I leave them past harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stop growing after reaching full maturity. If left too long in overly wet soil past their harvest window, excess moisture causes the tubers to suffocate and rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ kɛji amɛshɛ shweremɔ he. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ kɛyashi kpamɔɔ be lɛ baaho lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach light, which makes the stems weak and leaves less energy for producing big ears.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehe ehiaaa hewalɛ babaoo dani ekɛ toi wuji aba.

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can spread out in direct sunlight. Leaves generate food energy from sunlight, which the plant transfers downward to build large, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko ni baaha amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Baai feɔ niyenii hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli. Tso lɛ jieɔ enɛ kɛyaa shi koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms dry up and fall off without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni miduuu tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers dry up when the soil gets too dry or when daytime temperatures are extremely high. Regular watering at the root level and mulching the soil keeps the plant cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ mli ajɔ bɔ ni sa ni ewo yibii.

english: Why does covering the ground around my young crops with dry grass help them during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) shades the soil from heat, reduces water evaporation, and keeps the soil cool so plant roots stay hydrated longer during dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ naa. Nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has run out of food for my crops before the plants dry up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho dani tsei lɛ agbi?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, older lower leaves usually turn yellow while the rest of the plant stays small and pale. Slow growth and thin stems are clear warnings that the soil needs organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. be mli ni fãi krokomɛi Tso lɛ baafee bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo. Nibii ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia humus loo humus.

english: Why are my crops not growing healthy even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ?

english: Crops need essential soil nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus to grow strong. Adding a proper fertilizer like 92 707 gives plants the food they need to flourish and produce high yields.
