ga: Tsei hia niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ 92 707 tsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: What does fertilizer actually do to make crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ afee koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for plants, supplying vital minerals that soil lacks so crops can grow faster, develop strong root systems, and produce bigger leaves and fruit.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei aniyenii. kɛtsɔ shika tsuru ni he hiaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ lɛ ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ Koni tsei lɛ adara oya Eha shishifãi ni mli wa aba ni ewo baai kɛ aduawai wuji

english: How do I know if my soil is missing the food my crops need?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: If your crop leaves are turning yellow, stems remain thin, or plants grow very slowly, your soil is likely depleted and needs fertilizer to replenish its nutrients.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo. aloo tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa Ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How does feeding nutrients to my crops help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli?

english: Proper nutrition helps crops develop deeper, stronger root systems that can draw water from deep under the ground, making them more resistant to dry spells.
ga: Niyenii kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ Haa enyɛɔ eshiɔ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Can I use recommended fertilizers on my farm no matter which region of Ghana I am located in?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ he eko Ghana kpokpaa ni miyɔɔ nɔ.

english: Yes, standard crop fertilizers like 92 707 are formulated to work across different regions in Ghana, whether you farm in the forest zones, coastal areas, or northern savannas.
ga: Hɛɛ, afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ 92 707 lɛ koni akɛtsu nii yɛ kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ yɛ Ghana kɛji ootsu okwaayeli yɛ koo lɛ mli jio. ŋshɔnaa kpokpaa loo kooyigbɛ savannah

english: How can a farmer like me contact reliable fertilizer suppliers in Ghana?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ana okwaafonyo ko tamɔ mi ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa mɔ ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ enɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: You can reach certified agricultural input suppliers directly by phone or through official local distribution channels to order genuine products delivered to your area.
ga: Obaanyɛ oya mɛi ni kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ahe woji lɛ atswa tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ tɛlifoŋ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ anɔ koni obi ni akɛ nibii diɛŋtsɛ aba he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Is it safe to buy any fertilizer I find in the local market?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooohe ŋmɔshi nibii ni anaa yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: It is best to buy directly from licensed dealers or verified suppliers to ensure you get authentic, high-quality products that won't damage your soil or crops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe nii kɛjɛ nihɔɔlɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ loo mɔ ko ni akwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ dɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ onine shɛɔ nɔ ni ji anɔkwale ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni eyeee oshikpɔŋ loo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Do I need any official license or permit before I start farming on a larger scale?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni maná gbɛŋmɛɛ wolo ni maŋ lɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛ dani mabɔi okwaayeli nitsumɔ yɛ gbɛ ni da nɔ?

english: While small gardens do not need permits, starting a commercial farm or handling specialized farm inputs requires proper registration with local agricultural authorities to ensure everything is legally in order.
ga: Abɔɔi bibii po biɔ gbɛŋmɛɛ wolo. Shi jarayeli ŋmɔ shishijee loo ŋmɔ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ biɔ ni aŋmala gbɛi awo maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ kɛ mlai akpã gbee.

english: What key requirements should I complete before planting my first crop of the season?
ga: Mɛɛ taomɔ nii ni he hiaa esa akɛ mafee dani madu klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You need to clear your land properly, test or prepare the soil, secure certified seeds, ensure you have your fertilizers ready, and clear any necessary land-use permissions.
ga: Esa akɛ otsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kaa shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ loo saamɔ Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ hamɔ Kwɛmɔ ni oná ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ he klalo. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hegbɛi ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ faŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale and yellow during the early growing stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a clear sign that plants are starving for key nutrients, which can be quickly corrected by applying balanced plant fertilizers.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii titrii. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ oya kɛtsɔ tso mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to stretch tall looking for light instead of building strong stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee tsei akutsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tso bibioo ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge green leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of feeding and expanding the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ebaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeye ni ekɛduɔ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing in a V-shape on older leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is an essential plant food, and without it, the crop cannot maintain healthy green leaves or form big cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ tamɔ V lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Ni kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu nyɛŋ akwɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ loo afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses to the plant. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves healthy and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni kɛ hela lɛ yaa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli waa ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: What causes the white powdery dust to appear on the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni haa sũ yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: This white dust is powdery mildew, a fungal disease that spreads when warm days are followed by humid nights. It blocks sunlight from reaching the leaf, causing the plant to weaken and drop its leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ sũ yɛŋ nɛɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ, ni gbɛkɛ ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my young seedlings fall over and die at the soil level right after coming up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛba lɛ?

english: This is caused by a soil fungal disease called damping-off. It attacks soft stems when nursery soil stays too wet and shaded, so letting the soil surface dry slightly helps protect young plants.
ga: Hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening off lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Etutuaa tsei bibii beni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ mli lɛ edɔ tsɔ lolo ni eyɛ hulutsoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩ fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they get stressed by sudden dry spells, high heat, or insect attacks. Keeping good shade trees and preserving moisture in the soil helps the tree hold onto its flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi tutuamɔ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha tso lɛ ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hi shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Plantains have shallow roots supporting a heavy top. If tiny root pests weaken the roots under the soil, the wet ground can no longer hold the heavy plant up against strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni fiɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Kɛji shishifãi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Haa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ He ni nu yɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni baa tsei ni tsii anɔ lɛ naa dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside the mound during heavy rainfall seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams need well-drained soil to breathe. When excess rain sits inside a low or tightly packed mound, oxygen cannot reach the roots, allowing water rot bacteria to destroy the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia sweet potato koni enyɛ emu. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ gɔŋ ko ni yɔɔ shishi loo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa helai ni fiteɔ nii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and scorching during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants suffer heat stress under direct sunlight because their young roots cannot draw up water fast enough to keep the leaves cool. Planting shade trees or intercropping with plantains creates a humid microclimate and shields the cocoa from scorching sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni baaha baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo ni akɛ plantains woɔ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko baa, ni ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Yellowing along the central leaf vein is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. Applying nitrogen-based fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure replenishes the nutrient so leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ fãji lɛ ahe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni tsuɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in standing water while my maize rots and dies in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ? Beni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems that bring oxygen down to their underwater roots. Maize roots lack these air channels and suffocate when soil stays waterlogged for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ŋtayaai krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Abele shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during extreme dry spells to prevent water loss through evaporation. The plant goes dormant to protect its underground roots and will quickly produce fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baai shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa koni nu ni laajeɔ lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ. Tsei yaa wɔɔ koni amɛbu amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. ni ebaawo baai heei oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato shikpɔŋ mawo gɔŋ nɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers require soft, loose soil to expand downwards easily. Creating high mounds improves drainage to keep tubers from rotting in wet soil and provides the depth needed for yams to grow long and large.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni he hiaa koni ŋmeii lɛ adara kakadaŋŋ ni amɛdara.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their root nodules. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds neighboring crops like corn without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii, ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Covering bare soil with dry organic matter (mulching) acts like an insulating blanket. It prevents soil moisture from evaporating quickly under the sun, lowers soil temperature, and suppresses weed growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ nibii ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni haa hulutsoo baa. Tsi shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu la shishi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa baa shi ni etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely high or when soil moisture fluctuates unevenly. Irregular watering causes stress, leading the plant to shed blossoms to conserve energy instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa. Ha tsei lɛ afee fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Curled and twisted leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or viruses they transmit. Applying organic control sprays like neem oil helps suppress these pests before they damage the harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem fɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ anaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I prune away extra suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too many shoots compete with the parent plantain tree for nutrients and moisture. Keeping only one or two main suckers allows all the soil nutrients to go into producing one large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi babaoo tsɔ kɛ fɔlɔ dumɔwu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso yibii titrii kome loo enyɔ pɛ to he lɛ, ebaahe niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni ekɛ plantains akui wuji ni tsii aba.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs sunlight to make food. Wooden stakes lift the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, which prevents leaf rot and helps the vine build larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛhoo. Tso ko woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa baa lɛ fiteɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni efeɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the middle moving outwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their green color and strength, so adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea can restore health to your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I add heavy nitrogen fertilizer to my cowpea farm when the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nitrogen ni tsii woɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen causes cowpeas to grow lots of leaves and branches instead of flowers and pods. Cowpeas make their own nitrogen from the air, so extra fertilizer reduces the amount of beans you will harvest.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa cowpea lɛ náa baai kɛ niji babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Cowpeas feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni obaakpa lɛ aba shi.

english: Cassava drops leaves during prolonged dry spells as a natural survival trick to conserve water. The plant remains alive underground, and as soon as the rains return, it quickly sprouts fresh leaves.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he teemɔŋ sane ko kɛha nu ni akɛtoɔ he. Tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni Baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without developing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛmiitsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high or when there is sudden water stress. Regular watering and planting during milder periods help the flowers set into healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ dumɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the top leaves of my pepper plants curling up and growing tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the plant juices, or transmitting a virus. Spraying with neem leaf extract or targeted insecticides can clear the pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ tsei amli nu loo amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akɛtaoɔ kooloi amli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding on tender leaves inside the whorl. Spotting them early and applying organic bio-pesticides or recommended sprays inside the leaf funnels saves the yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Ni ooona amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ amli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ atsu nii lɛ baahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Multiple suckers compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients and moisture. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree receives full nourishment to yield a larger bunch.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ̃ tso lɛ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts underground are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Check readiness by pulling out a couple of sample plants and opening the pods. If the inner shell walls have dark brown or black vein patterns and the seeds fully fill the shells, the farm is ready for harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ hesaamɔ kɛtsɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ogbeleɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli gbogbo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ diŋ kɛ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil holds too much water without draining, or when fungi infect the roots during long periods of heavy rain.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni ekɛjieee nu. aloo kɛ́ ŋmei lɛ bote shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Yam vines produce bigger tubers when their leaves receive direct sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch more sunlight and avoid ground pests.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji kɛji amɛbaai lɛ shɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too wet for the roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they lack sufficient water, because the plant gets stressed and tries to save its energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ miihao ni amɛmiitao ni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously exhausts specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the central funnel leaves of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the central leaves (whorl) of young maize to feed on the tender leaf tissue before the cob forms.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai (rings) amli koni amɛye baa bibii lɛ amli fãji dani ŋmãa lɛ afee.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass keep the plants greener during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) blocks heat from the sun, which keeps moisture in the soil from evaporating quickly and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la lɛ mli baa lɛ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to be moist after a rain before applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so roots can absorb it; putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn the roots and kill the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil, causing all of them to stay weak.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen or is waterlogged. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving soil drainage helps the leaves regain their deep green color for strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if they lack shade, suffer from water stress, or lack natural pollinators like tiny midges. Keeping partial shade trees and avoiding over-spraying insecticides preserves these helpful insects and boosts pod production.
ga: Cocoa tsei baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be ko bɛ. Naagbai ni jɛɔ nu mli haomɔ mli loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ lɛ ni anáa Tsei lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ fioo kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ ahe ni eha pod ni afeɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot mainly due to poor drainage during heavy rains or fungal diseases in waterlogged soil. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and keeps the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: What makes my tomato leaves curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or by severe heat and drought. Controlling whiteflies early and keeping the soil evenly moist prevents the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli Early Whitefly Control Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seed yams so they do not rot in dry soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii? Bɔni afee ni ekagbo yɛ sũ ni egbi lɛ mli.

english: Seed yams should be planted just before the first major rains begin or right at the start of the rainy season. Storing them in a cool, shaded yam barn keeps them healthy and prevents them from rotting or sprouting too early.
ga: Esa akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui dani klɛŋklɛŋ maŋtsɛ nugbɔ lɛ aba loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato lɛ to ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaha amɛkafite loo amɛkakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches, making them top-heavy. Pests like root nematodes can also weaken the base, so supporting heavy plants with bamboo poles and keeping soil healthy prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse ni haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ root nematodes baanyɛ aha shishitoo lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei fi tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ hi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why do people tell me that planting cowpea or groundnuts makes the soil better for my maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni midu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen naturally from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, those nitrogen nutrients remain behind, acting as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen niyenii lɛ baahi shi. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers when the sunshine becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, forcing them to drop flowers to conserve water and survive. Covering the base of the plant with dry grass mulch helps retain soil moisture and lowers root temperature.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ pepper tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli latsaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds very early when my young rice is just coming up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani ehe miihia beni mi-ŋmãa bibioo lɛ ekwɛ̃ pɛŋ lɛ?

english: Young rice plants grow slowly at first and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil food. Clearing weeds within the first three weeks gives young rice the space to establish strong roots.
ga: Omɔ tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa bibii lɛ hegbɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why should I not put fertilizer on my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb them safely. Applying fertilizer to completely dry soil can burn plant roots and leaves, or the fertilizer will sit unused until rain washes it away.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛbaai. Aloo ashiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni akɛtsuuu nii kɛyashi nugbɔ baashwie nɔ.

english: What is a cover crop, and how will planting it help my farmland?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te dumɔ baaye abua miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: A cover crop is a plant like cowpea or velvet bean that you grow to protect and nourish the soil rather than for immediate cash harvest. It spreads over the ground like a blanket, stopping weeds from taking over, preventing heavy rains from washing away your topsoil, and adding natural plant food back into the soil.
ga: Cover crops ji tsei tamɔ cowpeas loo velvet beans ni oduɔ koni okɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni okɛha lɛ niyenii moŋ fe ni oookpa shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ osũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast even after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ po lɛ?

english: When soil is left bare under the direct sun, heat causes water to evaporate very quickly. Leaving crop residues or growing low-lying cover crops keeps the soil shaded and cool, helping it act like a sponge that holds water for a much longer time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ he ni hulu la lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi loo adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛ nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can planting cover crops reduce the amount of chemical fertilizer I need to buy?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni esa akɛ ahe lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, certain cover crops like beans and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots. When these plants die or are plowed back into the ground, they release nitrogen into the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for your main crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ekomɛi haa ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii, Ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi amli. Kɛji tsei nɛɛ gboi loo aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Ebaajie nitrogen kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa otsei titrii lɛ.

english: How can I make sure my crops get enough water when the rains become irregular?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: You can keep water in the soil by keeping the ground covered with plant material, building small dirt mounds or bunds to trap rainwater, and organic digging pits that hold water near crop roots so moisture stays in the soil longer during dry spells.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ tsei ahe nibii ni okɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Feemɔ gɔŋ bibioo ko loo muji ni abua naa. koni akɛmɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ buji ni atsa ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fee ni akɛ nu toɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha aduawai nu?

english: The best time to water crops is early in the morning or late in the evening. During the middle of the day, the heat causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu ji leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ. yɛ gbi lɛ mli Dɔlɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: How do I know if my crops are suffering from lack of water before they die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu efo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani amɛgboi?

english: Crops show signs of water stress when their leaves start curling inward, turning dull green, or drooping during the cooler morning hours. If leaves remain limp in the morning, the crop urgently needs water.
ga: Tsei jieɔ nu he haomɔ he okadii kpo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛmiibɔle amɛhe kɛmiiya mli. Atsake kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo egbee shi yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo yɛ leebi lɛ Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii oya.

english: Why does my topsoil wash away down the slope whenever it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ hoɔ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Rainwater collects speed as it flows down unprotected slopes, taking your most fertile topsoil with it. Planting crop rows across the slope (contour farming) or planting grass barriers slows down the water so it sinks into the ground instead of washing the soil away.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ buaa ehe naa oya beni ehoɔ kɛyaa gɔŋji ni abuuu he lɛ anɔ lɛ. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa fe fɛɛ lɛ tee. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ (Contour farming) loo jwɛi gbɛtsii nii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ afee mlɛo ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeefo lɛ.

english: Why does the ground become hard like cement after rain, preventing my seeds from coming up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ simenti beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ani ehaaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Heavy raindrops hit bare soil directly, breaking down the soil structure and creating a hard crust when it dries. Covering the soil with leaves or cover crops breaks the fall of the raindrops, keeping the surface soft so seeds can sprout easily.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ekpãtãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ ahiɛ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa kɛji egbi. Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ akagbee shi. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ oya.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me improve my farm yield in Ghana?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi koni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension officers visit farms to teach modern, practical techniques tailored to your local soil and climate, such as practical soil protection, proper spacing, pest management, and water conservation methods.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baasara ŋmɔji koni amɛtsɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ni kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kpãa gbee, tamɔ shikpɔŋ hebuu ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa Pest nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning yellow even though I planted on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ be naa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crops are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is too packed and waterlogged for roots to breathe. Improving your soil structure with manure or cover crops helps roots absorb nutrients properly again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii tamɔ nitrogen. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ kɛyashɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fee lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I switch to new recommended crop varieties instead of using my old local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake kɛya tsei srɔtoi ni ajie lɛ kpo ehee lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui momoi baatsu nii?

english: New improved varieties are bred to withstand local diseases, handle heat better, and produce much higher yields than older seeds, which tend to weaken and produce less over time.
ga: Afɔ tsei srɔtoi heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛye helai ni baa jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo fe dumɔwui ni etsɛ Amɛfɔɔ gbɔjɔmɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know which crop variety is best suited for my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Different varieties thrive in different soil types and rainfall conditions; choosing a variety recommended for your specific district ensures the plant can grow strong roots and maximize fruit production.
ga: Henɔi srɔtoi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi kɛ nugbɔ shihilɛi amli. Kɛ́ ohala tsofai srɔtoi ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛtsu nii yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for essential soil nutrients like nitrogen; feeding the plant proper fertilizer or organic manure restores its green color and energy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he hia niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ha tso lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hewalɛ aba tso lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow lots of tall green leaves but very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi aduawai fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen makes them focus entirely on leaf growth; crops need balanced feeding containing phosphorus and potassium to encourage flower and fruit development.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ haa amɛjwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia tsei koni eha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai aya hiɛ.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer on my crops when the ground is dry or wet?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi loo edɔ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plant roots can soak it up; applying fertilizer to damp soil prevents the chemical from burning the roots and helps the crop feed properly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaaa tsofai ashã shishifãi lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni eyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Strong sunshine causes water to evaporate rapidly from leaves; watering early in the morning or late evening gives roots enough time to drink before the high heat sets in.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu dani latsaa lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Plants shed their flowers when they experience water stress or extreme heat as a survival mechanism, so keeping soil consistently moist keeps flowers on the plant.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛbote nu mli haomɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the tall shade trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ? Fɛɛ etee?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight, so growing them alongside shade crops like plantains protects them until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔ lɛ yɛ Shade tsei tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Why do crops grow small and thin when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, crops fight each other for limited water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, whereas proper spacing gives each plant room to grow full and heavy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa kɛyashɛɔ elɛɛmɔ kɛ etsitsinɔnii lɛ he lɛ,

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, so clearing weeds early leaves all the food for your main plants to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ adara.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are logged with too much water. Nitrogen is essential for green leaf growth, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps them regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop due to heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or poor pollination. Tiny insects called midges pollinate cocoa blossoms; if the air is too dry or chemicals kill the midges, flowers fail to set fruit and fall off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo hewɔ lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ woɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo tsofai gbe gbɔmɛi Fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking sap from the leaf undersides, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It occurs when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, which usually happens when watering is irregular—such as long dry periods followed by sudden heavy rain.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, tamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ trukaa lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I space my maize seeds apart instead of planting several together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni abua naa yɛ bu kome mli.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to produce strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baatswa nu he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber through sunlight. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes spreads the leaves out to catch maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil diseases, leading to bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. ni atsĩ hela ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ naa lɛ kɛ yitso ni da baa

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves yellow and shed, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ eekwɛ̃ kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli.

english: Why does putting dried grass on the soil around my vegetables help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ jwɛi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-aduawai lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, acts as a protective shield. It prevents the sun from quickly evaporating soil moisture, keeps the roots cool, and gradually rots to add rich organic matter back into the soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya oya. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfiteɔ fiofio koni amɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers produce weak plants while others grow big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ tsei bibii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers are not all the same. 'Maiden suckers' (which have broad leaves and strong bases attached to the main plant) grow into healthy, high-yielding trees, whereas thin 'water suckers' with narrow leaves lack the stored energy to produce big bunches.
ga: Jeee plantain tsei lɛ fɛɛ ji ekome. ‘Tsobii bibii’ (ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ shishitoo ni mli wa ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ tso titri lɛ he) daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo, yɛ be mli ni ‘tsobii bibii’ ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ato koni akɛfee tsei niji wuji.

english: What is this coco peat material that people use for planting, and where does it come from?
ga: Mɛni ji coco peat ni gbɔmɛi kɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ enɛ ni nɛgbɛ ejɛɔ?

english: Coco peat is a natural planting material made from processed coconut husks. Instead of using regular black soil, farmers use it to plant seeds because it is soft, holds moisture well, and gives young roots a good environment to grow.
ga: Coco peat ji adebɔɔ mli dumɔ nii ni akɛ ŋmei ni afee lɛ ŋmei fee. Yɛ shikpɔŋ diŋ folo ni Okwaafoi kɛbaatsu nii lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, Okwaafoi kɛ shikpɔŋ diŋ duɔ dumɔwui ejaakɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ naa shihilɛ kpakpa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara

english: Why should I buy a growing medium like coco peat when I already have free soil on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe nɔ ko ni akɛkwɛɔ nii tamɔ coco peat be mli ni miyɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli momo lɛ?

english: Farm soil often contains hidden pests, fungi, and diseases that attack delicate young sprouts. Coco peat provides a completely clean growing environment that keeps your young plants safe from soil-borne sicknesses before they are strong enough for the open field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni tutuaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɔɔ mli. Coco peat haa shihilɛ ni mli tse ni shwereɔ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ yeɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe dani amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔji ni mli tse.

english: Is coco peat safe for my vegetable crops, or will it leave chemicals in my plants?
ga: Ani coco peat lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mi aduawai tsei lɛ? Aloo ebaashi tsofai yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Coco peat is totally safe and natural because it comes directly from coconut husks. It is organic in nature and does not rely on harmful chemicals, making it a safe choice for nursing healthy food crops.
ga: Coconut peat lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni eji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ejaakɛ ejɛɔ kokoo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Eji nɔ ko ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui anɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ akwɛmɔ.

english: Can coconut husks from roadside coconut sellers actually be useful for my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii shwapoi ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ he lɛ amli lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, coconut husks are processed into coco peat, which makes a clean, organic medium for nursing plants. It transforms coconut waste into a useful material that helps your seeds sprout safely.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsuɔ ŋmei ŋmeii ahe nii ni afeɔ ŋmei ŋmei. ni ji nɔ ko ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa tsei bibii Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmei ni etse lɛ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young seedlings keep dying of rot when I nurse them in ground soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboɔ beni mikwɛɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Ground soil often carries natural diseases and fungal spores that attack tender seedlings. Using a disease-free medium like coco peat prevents this rot because it doesn't carry crop diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai kɛ ŋmeii ni tutuaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ni hela bɛ mli tamɔ coco peat tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi fitemɔ naa ejaakɛ ekɛ tsei ahe helai baaa.

english: What makes a planting material 'clean' for starting crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni haa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ‘he tseɔ’ kɛha dumɔwui ashishijee?

english: A clean planting material is one that contains no crop diseases, weed seeds, or harmful pests. Materials like coco peat are naturally clean because coconut husks do not harbor common soil diseases that destroy young sprouts.
ga: Dumɔ nibii ni he tse ji nɔ ni tsei ahe helai, jwɛi dumɔwui, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui bɛ mli. Nibii tamɔ coco peat lɛ he tse yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ coco peat lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni fɔɔ baa ni gbeɔ tsei bibii lɛ.

english: How can I protect my nursery seeds from catching diseases before they even sprout?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe dani amɛkwɛ̃?

english: You can protect your nursery seeds by planting them in a disease-free medium like coco peat instead of topsoil. Because it is naturally clean, your seeds can germinate safely without being infected by diseases in the ground.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu odumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ he ko ni hela bɛ mli, tamɔ coco peat, ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ, ejaakɛ ehe tse yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No sɛɛ lɛ, odumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe ni ekɛ hela ko baaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does coco peat act like real soil, or do I need to mix it with dirt?
ga: Ani coco peat tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ diɛŋtsɛ loo esa akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ afutu mli?

english: Coco peat acts as a complete substitute for dirt during the nursery stage. It is an organic growing medium derived from coconuts that holds roots firmly and stays disease-free without needing regular soil mixed in.
ga: Coco peat tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni yeɔ muji najiaŋ kwraa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli. Eji nɔ ko ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni helai bɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ sũ afutu mli daa.

english: Why do seeds germinate faster in coconut fiber medium than in heavy garden soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ ŋmei fiber media mli fe abɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Coconut fiber, or coco peat, is a clean and lightweight material. It allows air to reach young roots easily and stays moist without packing tight like dirt, giving sprouts a quick, disease-free start.
ga: Kokoo fiber loo coco peat ji nɔ ko ni he tse, ni ehiɛ waaa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe oya ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli tamɔ muji. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛjeɔ kpo oya ni hela bɛ amɛhe.

english: What naturally good qualities does coconut material bring to crop roots?
ga: Mɛɛ adebɔɔ mli sui kpakpai nibii ni akɛfee ŋmei lɛ kɛbaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ?

english: Coconut material is naturally organic and free from soil diseases. It creates a hygienic, gentle environment for tender root systems to expand quickly without suffering from pest or disease attacks.
ga: Coconut nibii lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni sũ mli helai bɛ mli. Bɔɔ he ko ni he tse ni yɔɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai akapiŋ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from crops like plantains or shade trees because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries up the soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi koni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why is my maize crop turning pale yellow instead of deep green even after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores their dark green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii tso titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmei loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do extension officers tell me not to burn the dry bushes on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikashã jwɛi ni egbi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Burning heat destroys beneficial soil insects and burns off topsoil nutrients. Leaving cleared plants to rot into the ground feeds the soil naturally and retains moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ lɛ gbeɔ sũ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni eshãa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni ajie amɛhe ni miifite lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli.

english: Why should I plant cassava and groundnuts together on the same ridge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmei kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil to feed the cassava, while cassava grows tall and leaves room below for groundnuts, giving you two harvests from one plot.
ga: Peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛdu ŋmei. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa ni eshiɔ gbɛ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛha ŋmei. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds very close together so I can get more stalks on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the corn stalks fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with very tiny or empty cob yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmei fioo ko pɛ loo nɔ ko bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water suffocates the roots and promotes fungal diseases. Planting on raised mounds or ridges lets extra water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why are small worms eating ragged holes into the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the whorl of maize plants. Checking crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides prevents crop destruction.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akpãtãmɔ naa.

english: Why do I need to erect long sticks for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko kɛha mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni makwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my pepper plants keep them healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfataa mi-pepper tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from evaporating soil water, keeps root temperatures cool, and suppresses weeds.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa hulu la lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, extreme dry soil, or nutrient shortages like calcium. Consistent watering and mulching help keep flowers attached.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to plant my cassava stem cuttings in the soil so they sprout properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni esa akɛ madu mi-cassava niji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or eyes along the stem cutting; they must point upward toward the sky. If you plant a cassava stem upside down, the shoots will struggle to turn upward, resulting in weak plants and a low harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu ŋmei tso ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ shi lɛ Yiteŋ lɛ baaná naagba ni ekɛ ehiɛ baakwɛ ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground but leave tall stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie he ko shi mashi tsei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ koni mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to produce large tubers underground. Leaving vines on the ground leaves them vulnerable to leaf rot and pests from wet soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Wein tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ oya kɛha baai ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant sweet potatoes on raised soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ hi fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Raised soil mounds keep the earth loose and soft, allowing sweet potato roots to easily expand into large, well-shaped tubers. Mounding also improves drainage so rain doesn't sit around the roots and cause them to rot.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa efeɔ blɛoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ fɛo. Stacking hu haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ akanɛɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow before the stalks are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient maize needs to build foliage. Feeding the crop with nitrogen fertilizer or rich compost early in the season keeps the leaves green and growing strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo ha tsei lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa he hewalɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather becomes extremely hot or when soil moisture swings quickly from dry to soaked. Consistent watering and light shade during heatwaves help flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and stop growing new fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibii heei ni amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a viral disease spread by insects. Treating the plants with organic neem spray early on helps protect new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Mra be mli ni akɛ organic neem spray tsuɔ nii kɛtsaa tsei ahe lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ebu shweremɔ hee he.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings grow much better when planted right next to plantain plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa, keeping them cool and moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni ekɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe hulutsoo. Ha kookoo yibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I choose the best plantain shoots from an old farm to start my new plot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantains ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for 'maiden suckers' which have sword-shaped leaves and a wide base, rather than 'water suckers' with broad leaves on thin stems. Sword-like shoots carry strong energy reserves in their root bases, leading to healthier plants.
ga: Taomɔ ‘ŋmei tsei’ ni baai lɛ tamɔ klante kɛ shishi ni mli kwɔ, moŋ fe ‘ŋmei tsei’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ yɛ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ. Tsofai ni tamɔ klante lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni mli wa ni ato yɛ amɛshishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ ahewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why does growing cowpeas or beans make my soil better for planting maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in small root nodules. When the crop harvested and roots rot down, that nitrogen remains in the soil, providing free nutrients for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi bibii amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo lɛ Nitrogen baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni akɛ niyenii babaoo haa kooloi, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and give tiny ears when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ toi bibii beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, individual plants compete for the same pool of water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each crop enough room and food to mature into full-sized, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso fɛɛ tso kɛ ehe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ toi ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and have wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the necessary shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hɔɔŋ. Ha cacao tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the plant is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for leaves to produce food. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach, so applying fertilizer or organic manure helps bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ afee niyenii Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or severe dry spells. High daytime temperatures cause the flowers to dry up and drop off to preserve water and keep the rest of the plant alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa. Gbi mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi bɔni afee ni amɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my seeds when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should wait until the soil stays consistently moist for several consecutive days after the initial rains begin. Planting after the very first rain is risky because a short dry period often follows, which can dry out and kill newly germinated seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ eje shishi lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be kuku ko nyiɛɔ sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge stems and leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy foliage above ground instead of storing food in the roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest yield much smaller ears than the fresh seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo toi bibii kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially created by crossing two specific parent plants to get high yields. The seeds harvested from that crop lose this special combination in the next generation, resulting in weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ nibii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa hu baa shi.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow during dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te mi tso shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground by blocking the hot sun. It keeps the roots cool, reduces water loss through evaporation, and eventually rots into rich compost that feeds the soil.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛtsɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ni etsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ha nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi Ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for my land if I plant cowpeas or beans after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, but leguminous crops like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When harvested, they leave this nutrient in the ground, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akpa lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants and stopping them from growing?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni ekpa amɛdalɛ

english: This is typically caused by fall armyworm caterpillars that hide in the growing center of the maize plant. They eat the tender leaf whorls, which damages the plant's ability to develop new leaves and form healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Enɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaafee baai heei ni ekɛfeɔ toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even if I apply fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than most cultivated crops and actively steal the fertilizer, sunlight, and water intended for your crops. If weeds are not cleared early, your crops will starve despite the fertilizer applied.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii po.

english: Why does the new high-yielding maize I planted taste different from the traditional seeds my elders used to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa hee ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni miduɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ shishijee dumɔwui ni minukpai lɛ du lɛ he lɛ?

english: Newer high-yielding hybrid seeds are bred primarily to grow quickly, resist diseases, and produce larger quantities, rather than for deep traditional flavor. Traditional seeds store natural sugars and oils differently, giving them a richer taste, even though they produce smaller harvests.
ga: Afɔ dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ayinɔ titri koni amɛdara oya, amɛte shi amɛwo helai, ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Mohu ɔ, konɛ a ná nɔ́ nɛ mi kuɔ, nɛ ji sisije nɔ́ ɔ. Kusum mli ŋmaa toɔ adebɔɔ mli sugar kɛ fɔ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Ehaa enáa ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ewooo yibii babaoo moŋ.

english: If I harvest good maize from hybrid seeds this season, why can't I save those seeds to plant again next year?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmãa kpakpa Kɛjɛ hybrid dumɔwui amli yɛ be nɛɛ mli No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mahere nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni madu amɛ ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid crops get their strength from crossing two specific parent plant lines. When you plant seeds saved from a hybrid harvest, that special genetic combination breaks down, resulting in weaker plants, uneven growth, and much lower yields in the second generation.
ga: Hybrid tsei lɛ naa amɛhewalɛ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi akui enyɔ ni amɛfoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmaa ni akɛfee nibii sɔrɔtoi amli lɛ Nakai tsɛŋemɔ hela krɛdɛɛ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ baafite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ. shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetables grow very green with chemical fertilizer, but spoil faster after harvest compared to those grown with manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwereɔ tamɔ nɛkɛ kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛ akɛto aduawai ni akɛ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Chemical nitrogen fertilizers cause plants to absorb a lot of water and grow soft tissues quickly. While this makes the plants look lush and green, the high water content inside the harvested crops causes them to rot much faster than crops grown with balanced organic manure.
ga: Tsofa ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo ni ehaa fãji bibii lɛ daraa oya. Eyɛ mli akɛ enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ. Shi nu ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ haa amɛgboiɔ oya fe tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and moisture young cocoa seedlings need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. These insects suck the sap from the leaves and transfer the virus, stopping the plant from making food and developing tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ yucca baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii ni ekɛ bulbs aba.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers but dropping them without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi egbeeɔ shi ni efeee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers need bees or wind to vibrate their pollen so fruit can form. When temperatures become too hot, or if chemical sprays drive away bees, the flowers dry up and fall off before pollination can happen.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia ni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ atswa pollen lɛ koni aduawai aba. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Aloo kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani pollination baa.

english: Why do fall armyworms destroy my maize crops faster during dry spells than when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms fiteɔ mi ŋmãa oya yɛ hɔmɔ be mli fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain physically washes young armyworm caterpillars off maize leaves and drowns them in the soil. During dry spells, caterpillars survive easily and eat continuously without rain disturbing their feeding.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei baai amli lɛ ahe ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi mlɛo ni amɛyeɔ nii be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ egbaaa amɛ niyenii naa.

english: Why are my pepper plants staying short and yellow instead of growing tall and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ji kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ kakadaŋŋ ni ehiɛ baai lɛ?
