english: Stunted yellow pepper plants usually suffer from root damage, packed soil that prevents root expansion, or a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Weeds growing too close to the plants can also steal the nutrients the pepper roots need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii ni ji yellow pepper lɛ shishifãi fiteɔ. Akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ebɔle ehe bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. loo shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen bɛ nɔ Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ tsei tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aju niyenii ni he hiaa pepper shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and watery even when the leaves on top look thick and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Yam leaves grow using nitrogen, but building a heavy tuber requires potassium and loose soil. If the soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the plant spends all its energy growing top leaves instead of expanding the tuber underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ daa. Shi bulb agboi afeemɔ biɔ potassium kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Tso lɛ baafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cabbage heads rot from the inside when rain falls heavily near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabe yitsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Heavy rain gets trapped inside the tightly wrapped leaves of a cabbage head, creating a damp space where soft-rot bacteria grow. The bacteria enter through tiny leaf cracks and quickly turn the inside of the cabbage into mush.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ŋmɛ kaabe yitsei ni akɛwo mli shiŋŋ lɛ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa he ko ni mli efɔ ni helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ daa yɛ. Muawai lɛ boteɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli. ni ekɛ oyaiyeli tsɔɔ kaabii lɛ amli kɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What is pollination, and why do my crops need insects like bees to produce fruits?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination? Ni mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ he hiaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii koni ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pollination happens when insects move pollen from flower to flower so the plant can make seeds and fruit. Without insects carrying this pollen, many crops cannot form fruits or pods properly, leading to low yields.
ga: Pollination baa kɛji kooloi tsiɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo dumɔwui kɛ aduawai. Kɛji kooloi bibii ni hiɛɔ pollen bɛ Tsei babaoo nyɛɛɛ afee aduawai loo ŋmeii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi

english: Why do some of my crop plants produce many flowers but never end up making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Plants drop flowers without producing fruit if there are no insects around to pollinate them, if the weather is too hot and dry, or if the soil lacks phosphorus, which fuels flower-to-fruit growth.
ga: Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ, kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs ni haa fɔfɔi kɛyaa aduawai anɔ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops lack nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and grow leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ ahi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil is rich enough to produce a healthy harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, holds moisture well after rain, breaks apart easily in your hands, and contains earthworms. If soil is very hard, pale, or dry, it needs organic matter like compost to support crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ su ni tsuɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ enine mli ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo egbi lɛ, ehe miihia nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant cowpeas or beans on the same land where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Rotating your crops stops the soil from losing all its nutrients and breaks the lifecycle of pests living in the ground.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni ebaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ashihilɛ shi

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juice from the underside of leaves or spreading a plant virus. Spraying with neem water or insecticidal soap helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni gbeɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before they grow full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods shrivel and turn black due to fungal diseases like black pod or when the tree lacks enough water and nutrients to support all its pods. Pruning tall trees for sunlight and spraying approved fungicides helps save the pods.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ ahewɔ, loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ aye abua. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ, ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my tomatoes get soft, dark spots at the bottom before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots at the bottom of tomatoes are called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering during dry weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout after I plant them directly into dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need water to activate their growth process. If planted in completely dry soil, the seed stays asleep or dries out and dies inside the soil before roots can push out.
ga: Nu he hia dumɔwui koni ekanya amɛ dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi loo amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why should I spend time clearing weeds around my crops even after the crops are already tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be kɛjie jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ momo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete with crops for water, sunlight, and food in the soil no matter how tall your crops get. Keeping the farm clean also destroys hiding places for insects that attack your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ha lɛ he. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, efiteɔ hei ni kooloi bibii ni tutuaa onibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ hu.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I do not clear all the weeds and bush from my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mijieee jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani miduo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing the land thoroughly gives your young plants space to stretch their roots and get full sunlight without competing for survival.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa odumɔwui lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛgbala amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛhi shi.

english: If I clear my land by burning the bush, will it help my crops grow better?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ jwɛi ni mikɛshãa lɛ jie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ Ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but extreme heat destroys the natural leaf litter and good organisms in the soil. Clearing by hand and letting cut bushes rot back into the earth builds richer soil for your crops.
ga: Shãa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli baai lɛ amli jwɛi kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nine ni okɛjieɔ tsei bibii ni afolɔ lɛ ni oooŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni jara wa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do crops planted too close together stay thin and fail to yield good fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight and water. Instead of storing energy to grow big fruits, they waste energy stretching upward to reach light.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ nu. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ toɔ yiblii nguahi. Mohu ɔ, e puɛɔ he wami nɛ e ngɔɔ kɛ yaa hiɔwe konɛ e ná la.

english: Why do some trees on a neighbor's farm produce heavy pods while mine on the same soil produce very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ be mli ni minɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Yield depends on how the farm is cared for. Proper plant spacing, timely pruning to let in light, and keeping the soil covered with mulch allow trees to hold more flowers and fruit.
ga: Nibii ni anáa lɛ damɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ahaa lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Be mli ni afoɔ koni la atsɔ mli Ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ abua fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai babaoo naa.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land will be good for growing cassava or maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ko hi kɛha ŋmei loo ŋmei dumɔ?

english: Look for dark, loose soil that crumbles easily in your hand and drains water well without turning into sticky mud. Darker soil is rich in broken-down leaves and plant nutrients.
ga: Taomɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni etse ehe ni fiteɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ muji. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ nɔ baa ni ekumɔ kɛ tsei amli niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize make the maize grow greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans have special roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. This acts like natural food that feeds the maize growing next to them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves happen when heavy rain washes nitrogen away from the soil or when flooded soil prevents roots from breathing. Planting on raised soil ridges helps drain excess water.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie nitrogen kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ lɛ nu leebi moŋ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, leaves lose water faster than roots can drink it up. Placing dry grass or mulch around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers before any fruit begins to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Plants drop flowers when they suffer from sudden stress, such as long dry spells, excessive heat, or insect attacks. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps plants keep their flowers.
ga: Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ trukaa, tamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu hɔmɔ, latsaa ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot under the ground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water collects in heavy soil without draining, air cannot reach the tuber roots. This suffocates the root system and encourages soil fungi to attack and rot the cassava.
ga: Beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ tso shishifãi ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to block the intense sun and keep the soil cool until the trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet and dark conditions. Clearing extra shade branches and removing infected pods helps air move freely and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ duŋ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ shade lɛ mligbalamɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya he fɛɛ he ni ekpa ŋmɔtɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young maize plants look ragged with small holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etse ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the shoot of the plant. They feed on the tender young leaves before they unfold, which leaves ragged holes when the leaf opens.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbáa bu kɛji baai lɛ gbele.

english: Yellowing down the middle of older leaves means your soil is low on nitrogen. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the fuel it needs to stay green.
ga: Baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ haa amɛnáa tsofa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects. The virus weakens the leaves so they cannot make enough food, leading to smaller tubers harvest time.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ Virus lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa be ni akɛkpaa ŋmeii lɛ faaa.

english: Why do I need to lift up and stake my yam vines on tall poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb tall sticks so their leaves can capture direct sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down into the ground to swell the yam tuber.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over when heavy rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have broad leaves and shallow root systems, making them top-heavy when carrying a bunch. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden props helps hold the weight against wind.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ atsɔse lɛ yɛ kui amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ muji lɛ fiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do groundnut flowers grow above the ground, but the nuts end up under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: After a groundnut flower is pollinated, it grows a long stem called a peg that bends downward and pushes itself into the soil. The nut then grows underground where it is protected from sunlight and surface heat.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ Eyɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely high or when the soil goes from dry to wet too quickly. It can also happen if there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which makes the plant grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli oya tsɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling up tightly like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Tightly curled pepper leaves are caused by sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids. As these tiny insects suck the sap from young shoots, they cause the leaves to twist, deform, and stop growing normally.
ga: Kplukai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni ebɔle ehe waa lɛ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Amɛhaa baai lɛ fiteɔ, amɛfiteɔ, ni amɛkpaa dalɛ ni sa.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to start planting maize on fresh land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ ŋmãa shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Healthy soil for maize feels soft, holds some moisture without becoming muddy, and has a dark color. If natural weeds grow thick and green on the uncleared land, it is usually a good sign that the soil contains enough nutrients to support a healthy crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha ŋmãa lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaa, ni eyɛ su ni tsuɔ kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli jwɛi kwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hei ni he tseee lɛ. Bei pii lɛ eji okadi kpakpa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during long dry spells to conserve water inside their roots and stems. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves again and continue growing.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛ nu ato amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, wet, and overcrowded farms. Pruning thick shade trees to let in sunlight and clearing out infected pods early prevents the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni efɔ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ waa koni hulu la aba mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yam tubers every time I plant on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii bibii be fɛɛ be ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants feed heavily on nutrients in the soil. Planting yam in the exact same spot year after year drains those specific nutrients, so rotating crops or letting the land rest allows the soil to rebuild its strength.
ga: Sweet potato tsei yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ atsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo aŋmɛ gbɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmãa masɛi?

english: Cowpeas and beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil. This extra nitrogen acts as a natural fertilizer that helps neighboring maize plants grow taller and produce better ears.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ toi kpakpai.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop their leaves in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants temporarily wilt during hot afternoons to slow down water loss through their leaves. As long as the soil has moisture and the leaves stand back up by early morning, the crop is behaving normally to defend itself from heat.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagbi yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ aba shi fioo. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni baai lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa leebi lɛ, Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ baafee amɛnii bɔ ni sa koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he.

english: Why should I not save seeds from high-yielding hybrid maize to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from selected parent plants to give a single high-yielding harvest. The seeds harvested from those crops lose their special strength in the second generation, leading to uneven growth and much smaller yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tsei ni ji nyɛmɛi ni ahala koni amɛwo yibii kome ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa baa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi kwraa.

english: What is causing tiny holes in the leaves of my okra plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi okra baa lɛ nɔ

english: Tiny holes in okra leaves are usually caused by flea beetles or caterpillars chewing on the leaves. Spraying an organic extract made from neem leaves and water helps repel these insects without harming the plants or consumers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ okra baai lɛ amli bu bibii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛ neem baai kɛ nu fee lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eshwieɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni eyeee tsei lɛ loo mɛi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ awui.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when water supply is irregular, preventing successful pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch and planting at the right time of year ensures flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Eyeɔ omanye yɛ pollination naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally dry up and fall off, and the ground around the base of the main stem begins to crack slightly as the underground roots expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso wulu lɛ shishi jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa fioo be mli ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow after heavy rains hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away essential nutrients like nitrogen from the topsoil and fills the air spaces in the soil with water, which smothers the roots and prevents them from taking up food, turning the leaves yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ nu afata kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ lɛ ni amɛtsi enaa koni ekaye nii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji kaadi ŋmɔŋ

english: How do I prevent my crop roots from rotting when the rainy season becomes too heavy?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Creating raised beds or digging simple drainage channels across your farm allows excess rainwater to flow away from the plants, keeping oxygen around the roots and stopping rot.
ga: Saa ni awo nɔ lɛ feemɔ loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni oootsɔ Yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ enɛ baaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ tsei lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ekpaa fitemɔ

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out their roots before they can grow deep enough to find groundwater.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi dani amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ akpee.

english: Planting in straight rows ensures every crop gets enough sunlight, water, and soil space to grow big, while also making it much easier for you to weed and care for them.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up during dry hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants curl their leaves to save moisture and prevent water from escaping into the hot air, though severe curling can also be a sign of sap-sucking insects like whiteflies.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu akaje mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ afee kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji lɛ ahe okadi moŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, which is usually caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of key nutrients in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli nibii titrii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why does my plantain stool produce small bunches when I allow many shoot suckers to grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔtɔ lɛ woɔ jwɛi bibii lɛ? Akɛni miha ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ hewɔ.

english: Too many suckers growing from the same root compete with each other for food and water; removing extra suckers directs all the plant's energy into making large plantain bunches.
ga: Tsofɔi babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifã kome mli lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa lɛ, eheɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfeɔ plantains agboi.

english: What happens if I plant tomatoes in the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu tomato yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot year after year drains specific soil nutrients and allows tomato-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, leading to poor harvests.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tomato nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: Why do groundnut crops leave the soil richer for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which means they extract nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, serving as a free, natural fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ehe.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly attack my young maize crops right after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ trukaa beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The warm air and early rains trigger adult moths to lay eggs on tender, fresh maize shoots, causing a sudden swarm of caterpillars that hatch and feed on the leaves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ fɔɔ wɔji yɛ abele tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ehe tse lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii akui shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient the plant needs to build green leaves and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients or when excessive water in the soil starves the roots of air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo kɛ́ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ha kɔɔyɔɔ hɔmɔ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting broad-leaf crops like plantain alongside young cocoa provides living shade and preserves soil moisture, protecting the seedlings until their roots mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ kɛfataa cocoa bibii ahe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains soak the ground for long periods, water displaces the air in the soil, suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing organisms to attack the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔ̃ɔ be kplaŋŋ. Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa bɔɔ nii ni miifite lɛ tutuaa yitso lɛ.

english: Why does my land need fertilizer now when it used to grow heavy harvests without any inputs years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii bianɛ? Nibii enyiɛ adu ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli afii babaoo ni eho nɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they take away essential nutrients from the earth. After many years of continuous farming without resting the land, the soil becomes depleted, requiring added fertilizer to restore the nutrients crops need to yield well.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaaŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ afii babaoo ni akɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ sɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ, ni ehe bahiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans on the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nitrogen, leaving the ground tired. Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shãa. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it bad to plant my cassava cuttings very close together on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their stems and roots compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper space allows the roots room to expand into large, thick tubers rather than many thin, low-value roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ shishifãhi nɛ a he hia wawɛɛ.

english: Why is it so important to clear weeds from my farm while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will quickly steal the light, water, and nutrients your crops need to establish themselves. Clearing weeds early allows your young plants to grow strong enough to shade out future weeds on their own.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii, ni amɛbaaju la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ oya koni amɛnyɛ amɛtswa amɛhe shi. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua odumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ jwɛi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I buy certified seed from the agro-dealer instead of planting seeds saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from high-yielding hybrid crops lose their vigor and disease resistance in the next generation. Certified seeds are tested and produced under controlled conditions to ensure high germination rates, strong disease resistance, and better yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ ni afeɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo. Helai ahewalɛ ni hi ni ekɛ yibii kpakpai baa

english: What is eating small holes into the central leaves of my young maize plants and leaving tiny droppings?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu bibioo ko yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest hides deep inside the growing tip of the maize plant to feed, and it must be controlled early using recommended sprays or neem leaf extracts before it destroys the plant's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye nii. ni esa akɛ akudɔ lɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ. dani ebaafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rainy season no longer starts in the month it used to?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Akɛni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ejeee shishi dɔŋŋ yɛ nyɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ ejeɔ shishi lɛ mli hewɔ lɛ.

english: Instead of planting by the calendar month, wait until the soil receives consecutive days of good rain that moistens the ground deeply. Planting after just one light rainfall can cause seeds to germinate and then wither if a dry spell immediately follows.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ kalanda nyɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ kpakpa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What is the main difference between hybrid maize seeds and open-pollinated maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni agbele naa lɛ ateŋ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two specific parent plants to produce very high yields, but you must buy fresh seeds every season. Open-pollinated seeds allow plants to pollinate naturally, meaning you can save the seeds to replant, but their quality and characteristics can change over time if they mix with other varieties.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni ji fɔlɔi lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo waa. Shi esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei daa be. Dumɔwui ni agbele amɛhe lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato koni okɛdu ekoŋŋ. Shi bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ hi ha kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ baanyɛ atsake yɛ be ni sa mli kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi krokomɛi futu mli.

english: Why do people advise me not to save seeds from my harvested maize to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikakɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize grows in the open field, wind carries pollen from neighboring fields into your crop. If nearby fields have different maize varieties, your plants will cross-pollinate, meaning the seeds you save will produce a mixed, lower-quality crop compared to the original certified seeds you planted.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ baa onibii amli. Kɛji ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi Otsei lɛ baafee cross-pollinated. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni okɛtoɔ lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efutu, ni ebaafee nɔ ni baa shi kɛ akɛto shishijee dumɔwui ni okɛwo odaseyeli mli lɛ ahe.

english: How can my neighbor's maize crop affect the maize growing on my own farm?
ga: Te mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baaná ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Maize relies on the wind to spread its pollen. If your neighbor is growing a different maize variety, pollen from their plants can blow onto your crop's flowers, causing your maize to cross-pollinate and produce grain that has different traits from what you originally planted.
ga: Abele kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ koni egbɛ pollen lɛ eshwa. Kɛji okutsoŋnyo lɛ du ŋmãa srɔtoi lɛ, abaanyɛ atswa Pollen ni jɛ amɛtsei lɛ amli lɛ awo onibii ni oduɔ lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa o-corn lɛ feɔ cross-pollinate ni ehaa dumɔwui ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ nɔ ni odu shishijee lɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Why did the yellow maize I harvested have white kernels mixed on the same cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmãa yɛŋ ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This happens because of cross-pollination. While your yellow maize was flowering, wind carried pollen from a nearby field of white maize onto your crop, resulting in cobs with a mix of both yellow and white kernels.
ga: Enɛ baa mli yɛ krɔs pollination hewɔ. Be mli ni o-yellow corn lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ pollen ni jɛɔ o-corn white ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ kɛyaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji cob ni dumɔwui ŋmɔŋ kɛ eyɛŋ fɛɛ efutu mli.

english: What does cross-pollination mean when extension officers talk about maize?
ga: Mɛni cross-pollination tsɔɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsulɔi wieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Cross-pollination happens when pollen from one maize plant is carried by wind to fertilize another maize plant. If two different varieties of maize are growing near each other, their pollen mixes, creating harvested seeds that are a combination of both types rather than a pure single variety.
ga: Cross-pollination baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ tswa pollen ni jɛ ŋmãa tso kome mli lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmãa tso kroko awo ŋmãa mli. Kɛji ŋmãa henɔi enyɔ kwɛ̃ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Amɛ pollen lɛ efutu. Enɛ haa anáa dumɔwui ni akpaa ni ji enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni akɛfee ekome. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso kake nɛ he tsɔ.

english: Why should I spend money to buy certified seeds instead of just planting grain bought from the local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika kɛhe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, du wuhi nɛ a he ngɛ ma a jua a nɔ ɔ pɛ.

english: Certified seeds are carefully produced in controlled environments to ensure they are pure, uniform, and high-yielding. Market grain often comes from fields where different open-pollinated varieties mixed together, which leads to unpredictable growth, uneven ripening, and lower overall yields.
ga: Akɛ hiɛdɔɔ feɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ he ko ni akudɔ koni akwɛ akɛ amɛhe tse. Yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa ni ewoɔ babaoo Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni ŋmɔji ni ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ efutu mli lɛ amli, ni no haa amɛdaraa waa ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ ba shi

english: Will the maize I harvest sell for the same value as the certified seed variety I originally bought?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ baahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni tamɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe shishijee lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Not necessarily. If your open-pollinated crop mixed with other varieties from surrounding farms during the growing season, the harvested grain is no longer a pure form of the original certified variety, which can affect its appearance, taste, and market value.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛji akɛ o-open pollinated plant lɛ kɛ tsoi krokomɛi ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ tsɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, Harvested seeds lɛ jeee shishijee tso ni awo he odase lɛ henɔ krɔŋŋ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aná bɔ ni eyɔɔ, bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋɔɔ kɛ bɔ ni jara wa ha lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize look different from the picture on the seed bag I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ mfoniri ni yɔɔ dumɔwui kotoku ni mihe lɛ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: If you planted an open-pollinated variety, wind likely carried pollen from other nearby maize varieties into your field during flowering. This natural mixing changes the physical traits of the harvested grain, making it look different from the original seed picture.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmeii ni agbele naa lɛ, ekolɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ baaya oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii nɛɛ tsakeɔ dumɔwui ni akpaa lɛ ahe gbɔmɔtsoŋ su. Ha efee nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ shishijee dumɔwui ahe mfoniri lɛ he.

english: How far away should I plant my maize field from another farmer's field to keep my grain pure?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛjɛ okwaafonyo kroko ŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni ŋmãa lɛ he atse?

english: To prevent pollen from other maize varieties from blowing into your field, you should keep a distance of at least 200 to 400 meters between different varieties, or stagger your planting dates so the crops do not flower at the same time.
ga: Enɛ ji koni akatswa ŋmãa ni jɛ ŋmãa srɔtoi krokomɛi amli lɛ awo oŋmɔji amli. Esa akɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, okɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni ji mitai 200 kɛyashi 400 ahi tsei srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ, loo okɛ gbii ni akɛduɔ lɛ atsake bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akawo fɔfɔi yɛ be kome mli.

english: If I plant an open-pollinated maize variety, how many times can I save and replant those seeds before quality drops?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa ni agbele naa lɛ Shii enyiɛ manyɛ mafolɔ ni madu ekoŋŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ afite?

english: While you can replant open-pollinated seeds for a few seasons, each year they naturally mix with nearby pollen. After two or three seasons, the crop will lose its original purity, uniformity, and strength, making it necessary to buy fresh certified seeds again.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui ni agbele naa lɛ bei fioo komɛi moŋ, shi daa afi lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Yɛ bei enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛ shishijee hetsemɔ, nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni ahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade during their first two years because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out soil moisture quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains next to them creates a cool environment for survival.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa kɛha wala.

english: How can I keep my vegetable farm moist during the dry season without spending too much money on water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ni mifiteee shika babaoo yɛ nu he nyɔmɔwoo he?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight, traps moisture in the ground, and reduces how often you need to water.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa nu ni afɔɔ lɛ shii abɔ lɛ baa shi

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. Excess standing water smothers the roots by blocking oxygen, causing fungal infections that rot the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko baa ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Is it better for me to mix different crops together on the same land or grow only one crop?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafutu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome?

english: Mixing compatible crops, known as integrated or mixed farming, keeps the soil healthy, deters pest outbreaks, and guarantees you still harvest food even if one crop fails due to bad weather.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni yaa he kome Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ okwaayeli ni akɛfee ekome loo okwaayeli ni akɛfee ekome. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ anaa Ni ayɛ nɔmimaa akɛ obaanyɛ okpa niyenii lolo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii hewɔ po.

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack that crop to build up in the field year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield small fruits when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving no single plant with enough energy to grow strong and produce large yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baaha eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves upward to catch maximum sunlight to make food; keeping leaves off the ground leads to healthier plants and larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food that maize plants need in large amounts to build green leaves and form full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni ŋmãa tsei he hiaa yɛ babaoo mli koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛfee ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ.

english: Extreme heat and erratic watering cause stress to tomato plants, leading their blossoms to drop off before they can be pollinated and form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pollination kɛ aduawai baa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids feeding on the leaf sap or transferring a virus, which prevents proper growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo aphids ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. ni tsiɔ dalɛ ni sa naa

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when water stays sitting on the ground for too long after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water floods the soil and stays on top without draining, it smothers the roots, preventing them from taking up food from the soil, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and weaken.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu shwieee shi. baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye niyenii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo.

english: Why is it better for me to water my crops early in the morning rather than in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu leebi lɛ? Ani ehi fe ni ooona hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering under a hot afternoon sun causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can drink it. Morning watering allows the plant roots to absorb moisture coolly and stay hydrated through the heat of the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu ni mli ejɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my plant stems with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or straw acts like an umbrella that shades the dirt. It keeps the ground cool, reduces water evaporation during hot days, and keeps moisture near the roots longer so your crops don't dry out quickly.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ umbrella ni tsiɔ muji naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ baa shi. ni oha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe be babaoo Bɔni afee ni onibii akagbi oya.

english: Crops need room to search for food, water, and sunlight. When plants are crowded close together, their roots fight over the same nutrients in the soil and their leaves shade one another, resulting in thin stems and small tubers.
ga: Dumɔ nii hia he ko koni amɛna niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la be mli ni tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ baafee amɛhe shade. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ yitsei bibii baa.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even when my soil is rich and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds ensures that all the nourishment in the ground goes directly to feeding your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa otsei titrii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do my crops take in the fertilizer that I place on top of the soil?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tsuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops drink their nourishment through their roots. Rainwater or irrigation dissolves the fertilizer on top of the ground and carries it down into the soil, where the roots suck up the nutrient-rich water to feed the whole plant.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nugbɔ nu loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu ni niyenii yɔɔ mli ni haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young crops grow tall, thin, and weak when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ kɛlɛ, eyɛ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Plants rely on sunlight to make their own food. When shaded by tall trees, young plants stretch upwards as fast as they can to find sunlight, making them tall, slender, and weak instead of strong and healthy.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulu la nɔ koni amɛkɛfee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ amɛyɔɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko shishi lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbala amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛna hulu la, ni no baaha amɛkwɔ, amɛhe afee mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger yam tubers when I give them wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji beni mihaa amɛ tso ni amɛkwɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves up on stakes exposes more of their leaves to direct sunlight, allowing the plant to produce more food energy that gets stored underground as large tubers. It also keeps leaves off damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii hewalɛ babaoo ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ ŋmeii wuji. Ebuɔ baai lɛ hu ahe kɛjɛɔ sũ ni mli edɔ he, ni ji he ni helai fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop down in the hot afternoon even when the ground isn't dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni esa akɛ mafee nakai lɛ? He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbiko yɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose moisture into the air faster than roots can draw it up. The plant temporarily curls or droops its leaves to reduce surface area exposed to the sun and save water, recovering as temperatures cool in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Tsei lɛ baafo amɛhe loo amɛbaafite yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu nu he. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why should I trim off extra small branches from my tomato plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Jiemɔ kɛjɛ tomato tsei lɛ amli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Removing unnecessary extra side branches focuses the plant's food and energy into growing large, high-quality fruits rather than wasting energy on extra leaves and stems.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ lɛ yaa yibii wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to produce green leaves. This often happens when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the soil beyond the reach of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without turning into fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants drop their flowers to save energy and water. Extreme heat can also dry up the pollen, preventing the flowers from producing fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha pollen lɛ agbi. Ehaa fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo yibii

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing during the dry season even when I water them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ minine shwieɔ nɔ nu moŋ?

english: Hand watering often only wet the top layer of soil, leaving deep roots thirsty. In high heat, the plant loses water through its leaves faster than the shallow water can supply, causing growth to stop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nine ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ kumai yeɔ amɛ Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu he nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dalɛ kpaa.

english: Why do insect pests attack my cowpea crop right when the flowers start to open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Flowering cowpea plants produce sweet scents and soft tissues that naturally attract insects looking for food. Spraying or protecting the crop right before flowering prevents these pests from destroying young pods.
ga: Cowpea tsei ni fɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma kɛ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni gbalaa kooloi bibii ni taoɔ niyenii lɛ kɛbaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ loo obu he dani amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines curling up and getting tiny black spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii diji lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and dark spots are common signs of fungal diseases or small insects sucking sap from the leaves. Wet, humid weather allows these fungi to spread quickly across the foliage.
ga: Baai lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela loo kooloi bibii ni miinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ he. Shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya yɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess standing water fills all the tiny air pockets, suffocating the roots and allowing waterlogging fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni oha ŋmeii ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds come before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani kpamɔ baa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the soil surface and struggle to anchor heavy stems filled with fruit, especially if the soil is soft or if underground pests have damaged the root base.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ daa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ tsei ni tsii ni aduawai eyi mli obɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ bɔdɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui efite shishitoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after clearing the farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu lɛ beni mijie he ni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie hidden in the soil for long periods. Clearing the bush exposes these dormant seeds to sunlight and rain, causing them to sprout immediately before your crops can shade the ground.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Tso bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ akwɛ̃. Hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know if the plant spacing recommended by extension officers will really increase my harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni mi-extension agent lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ baaha mi yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures plants do not fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving crops enough space allows individual plants to produce larger fruits and higher overall yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akaŋ. Gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tsei aŋkroaŋkroi woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni fa babaoo.

english: Can I successfully plant and harvest cocoa trees here in the Accra area, or does cocoa only grow in the forest regions?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ kookoo tsei anɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli yɛ Accra kpokpaa lɛ nɔ biɛ? Aloo, kookoo baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ kooi amli pɛ.

english: While cocoa thrives best in forest regions with heavy rainfall and rich shade, it can grow in parts of Accra if the soil retains enough moisture, receives sufficient rain, and has adequate shade during dry spells.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ amli moŋ, shi kookoo baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ Accra hei komɛi hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa. nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa ni eyɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: If a crop grows very well in the Ashanti region, does that mean it will automatically grow well on my land here in Accra?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ko kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ Accra biɛ?

english: Not automatically. Crops depend on specific soil types, temperature, and rainfall patterns. Accra is generally hotter and drier than the forest zones, so crops from wetter regions may need irrigation or extra care to survive.
ga: not automatically Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ henɔi pɔtɛɛ, latsaa, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, Accra mli edɔɔ ni edɔɔ fe kooi amli hei. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ abi ni afɔ amɛ nu loo akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do fruit trees seem to grow so easily on some farmlands while struggling on nearby land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmɔji komɛi amli yɛ be mli ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Soil quality changes from place to place. Land with deep, rich soil that holds water without waterlogging supports fruit trees easily, whereas shallow, sandy, or stony soil starves the trees of water and nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome kɛyaa he kroko. Shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nu shwieɔ nɔ ni nu shwieee nɔ lɛ haa tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ŋã, loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: How can I check if my land's soil is deep and good enough for growing cocoa before spending money on seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ni ehi bɔ ni sa kɛha kookoo dumɔ dani mafite shika kɛdu dumɔwui?

english: Good cocoa soil must be deep, dark, well-drained, and free of hard underground rock layers. An agricultural extension officer can help you dig a soil pit to examine the layers and check if the soil can hold moisture for cocoa roots.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni tɛ ni wa ko bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni otsa bu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fãi lɛ yɔɔ ha, ni okwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha kookoo shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. They require shade from fast-growing nurse crops like plantains or leguminous trees to protect them until their root systems mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo legumes lɛ amli. Koni abu tsei nɛɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: Why do some fruit trees take many years to produce fruit while others start bearing fruit within one year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni woɔ yibii lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu jeɔ yibii womɔ shishi yɛ afi kome mli lɛ?

english: Different tree species have different growth rates. Additionally, trees planted from seeds take longer to mature, whereas trees propagated through grafting or budding bear fruit much faster because they come from mature parent plants.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui duɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ lɛ baawo yibii oya kwraa ejaakɛ amɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso ko ni eda mli.

english: What causes the leaves on my fruit trees to turn yellow and fall off during dry months?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Trees shed their leaves during dry months as a survival strategy to reduce water loss. If this happens during rainy periods, however, it is usually a sign of nutrient deficiency, poor drainage, or root diseases.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi kɛji enɛ ba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ eji niyenii ni esaaa ni ayeɔ lɛ he okadi. nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo shishifã hela

english: How do I know if the rainfall pattern in my district is reliable enough to sustain cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua kookoo tsei?

english: Cocoa trees need regular rainfall spread over most of the year. If your area experiences long dry seasons lasting more than three or four months without irrigation, cocoa trees will dry out and yield very few pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei biɔ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ naa hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni fe nyɔji etɛ loo ejwɛ ni nu shwieee nɔ. Cacao tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant food crops like plantain or cassava on the same land where I want to grow young tree crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava? Ani he ni misumɔɔ ni madu tso bibioo lɛ yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping is useful when done correctly. Plantains provide helpful shade for young trees, but heavy-feeding crops like cassava must be spaced far enough so they do not steal water and nutrients from your tree crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aba sɛɛnamɔ kɛji akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Plantains haa tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi ehe miihia ni tsei ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ yucca lɛ ahi amɛhe shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli.

english: Who can I contact in my district to inspect my farmland and advise me on what crops will grow best?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ matswa yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ tsei ni midu lɛ amli ni ewo mi ŋaa yɛ tsei ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he?

english: You can visit your local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) district office to request a visit from an Agricultural Extension Agent, who will inspect your land and guide you on suitable crops free of charge.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara okwaayeli kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) kpokpaa nɔ nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ni obi ni okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ko abasara bo. Ebaakwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaatsɔɔ bo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an important plant food needed for green growth, or the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. loo shishifãi ni ebote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of leafy green branches but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes leguminous crops like beans to focus all their energy on growing tall stems and green leaves instead of producing flowers and fruit pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔli ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ tso yiblii.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures get too high, when the plants do not get consistent water, or if small insects damage the flowers before pollination happens.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kpataa fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo amɛmli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thick stems, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: Cassava tubers stay small if plants are planted too close together or if the soil has too much nitrogen, forcing the plant to build foliage above ground instead of storing food in the roots.
ga: Cassava ŋmeii lɛ baafee bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Enɛ baaha tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves curl up and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees lose moisture rapidly through their leaves when dry Harmattan winds blow, causing them to shed leaves to conserve water unless they receive protection from taller shade trees.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi jɛ Harmattan, ni no haa cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. ja tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ebu he.

english: What is causing my pepper leaves to curl upwards and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips spreading plant viruses, or by extreme heat and water stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ mli.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam rot underground happens when soil retains too much water without draining, or when tiny soil worms and fungi enter damaged tubers after heavy rain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato rot lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni ekɛjieee nu. Aloo kɛ́ sũ mli ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bote bulbs ni efite lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: Young crops grow slowly and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and nutrients, which can permanently stunt crop development.
ga: Tsei bibii daraa blɛoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa kɛya naanɔ.

english: Why should I alternate my maize farm with groundnuts or cowpeas instead of growing maize every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil, whereas rotating with groundnuts or cowpeas returns vital nitrogen to the earth and stops crop-specific pests from multiplying.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my vegetable plants help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Mulching with dry grass protects the soil from direct heat, reduces water loss from evaporation, prevents weeds from growing, and adds natural manure as it rots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need plantain plants grown beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ yɛ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping moisture to help young cocoa survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha hulutsoo ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni eye ebua kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which maize needs in high amounts to grow green and healthy. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-decomposed animal manure fixes this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi he miihia lɛ babaoo koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea, loo kooloi ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: What causes tiny holes and dark droppings in the center leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: This is a classic sign of Fall Armyworm attack, a caterpillar that feeds inside the central leaves of maize. Applying approved pest treatments or putting clean wood ash directly into the plant funnel early can eliminate them.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nɔ loo tso sũ ni he tse ni akɛaawo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ mra. Obaanyɛ ojie amɛ kɛjɛ ohe.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and gentle digging around the base reveals large, plump tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ miikwɛ̃ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ la ni atsaa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ajieɔ yitso agbo ko ni egbɔjɔ kpo.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture food to build big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiho eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: Wilting in wet soil usually happens when fungal or bacterial diseases attack the plant roots and stop them from drawing water upward. Avoid planting tomatoes in the exact same spot every year to prevent soil disease buildup.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ baa kɛji ŋmeii loo helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli baa lɛ tutua tsei shishifãi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbala nu. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tomato ni ooodu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ he koni helai akabu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. Protecting young plants with neem oil spray or organic repellents stops these pests early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei bibii anɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ tsei bibii lɛ buɔ he lɛ, ehaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kpaa mra.

english: Maize drains nutrients from the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and return it to the ground. Planting them restores natural soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and give small harvests when planted very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?
