english: When seeds are sown too close, plants compete against each other for limited water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and nutrition to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni faaa He ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tso fɛɛ tso mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it critical to weed my field within the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mishia lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings grow slowly at first and can easily be overcrowded by aggressive weeds competing for food and water. Weeding early gives your crop a strong head start before weeds take over.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ shishijee mli, ni ekolɛ jwɛi ni baa amɛnɔ ni kɛ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ oya lɛ aha amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ dani jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there is full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that cannot handle intense direct sunlight. They need shade from plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them from heat burn and to keep the soil moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. kɛ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yam plants grow as climbing vines, and their leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for the roots. When you lift the leaves off the ground with stakes, the plant gets more light, breathes better, stays away from ground pests, and produces much bigger tubers.
ga: Atomɔ tso lɛ daa tamɔ wain tso ni kwɔɔ. Ni hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ okɛ tso lɛ wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ baaná la babaoo. Mumɔ jogbaŋŋ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ahe. ni amɛwoɔ yitsei ni dara kwraa.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize are usually a sign of hunger, specifically a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to build strong stems and healthy green leaves for good growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji hɔmɔ he okadi. Titri lɛ, nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait until the soil is wet from rain before applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli?

english: Fertilizer works like dry salt; plants cannot eat dry chemical grains. Water is needed to dissolve the fertilizer so the roots can suck it up, and applying fertilizer on dry soil can burn and kill the plant roots.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei ni egbi. Tsei nyɛŋ aye tsofa dumɔwui ni egbi. Nu he miihia koni akɛjie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ashã ni amɛgboi.

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight intensely for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. The plants spend all their energy growing tall to reach light instead of using that energy to form big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ amɛmiida yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ koni amɛná la. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ jamɛ a he wami ɔ tsuɔ ní kɛ peeɔ tso nguanguahi nɛ a he wa.

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up from the soil. The wilting is a natural defense mechanism to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun, and the plants usually recover when the afternoon cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Withering ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛba baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. Ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ shwane mli fɛ̃i ba.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the farm stays flooded after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nu afua ba yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the field for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil, causing the roots to drown, decay, and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha ŋmɔji anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of pollination by insects. If the temperature is too high or water is irregular, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miipiŋ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: What is causing tiny ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars, such as the Fall Armyworm, feeding on the leaves. These pests hide inside the central funnel of the plant during the day and eat the tender green tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ fãji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Why does planting beans or cowpeas alongside my main crops make the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have tiny bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into natural soil fertilizer. When planted with or before other crops, they naturally feed and enrich the soil.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ adu kɛ tsei krokomɛi loo dani amɛdu lɛ Amɛyeɔ nii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: How often should I water my tomato plants during the dry season so they do not spoil?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkafite?

english: Tomato plants need consistent moisture, especially when flowering and fruiting. Water them deeply 2 to 3 times a week early in the morning or late evening rather than giving them a little bit of water every day, as deep watering helps roots grow strong and prevents flowers from falling off.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ hia ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii. Nu ni mli kwɔ shii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ otsi mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Mohu ɔ, ha lɛ nyu fioo daa ligbi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni mli kwɔ haa shishifãi lɛ ahe waa, ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and curl up when there is no rain for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce water loss during hot, dry conditions, and yellowing usually means the plant is under stress from lack of water or nitrogen in the soil. Providing supplemental water or covering the soil around the plants with dry grass (mulching) helps keep the moisture in.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu ni laajeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Yellow tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli kɛjɛ nu loo nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛfataa he loo ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough for growing cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei dumɔ?

english: Cassava prefers loose, sandy-loam soil that drains water easily so the roots can expand. If your soil is heavy clay that holds water for a long time, the cassava roots are likely to rot instead of growing large.
ga: Yucca sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ oya koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni hiɛɔ nu be kakadaŋŋ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ fɔɔ fitemɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaadara.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my yam mounds after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is about 1 to 2 months after planting, once the yam vine has sprouted leaves and developed roots capable of taking in the nutrients from the soil.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo mli ji aaafee nyɔji 1 kɛyashi 2 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ,.

english: Why do my watermelon vines grow huge leaves but produce very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ watermelon wain tsei lɛ baai dara shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Watermelon vines produce too many leaves when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. To get more fruit, use a fertilizer that has more phosphorus and potassium, which encourages flowering and fruit growth rather than leaf growth.
ga: Watermelon wain tsei lɛ woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. koni onine ashɛ aduawai babaoo nɔ Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai daa fe baai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do small worms eat the leaves of my young corn plants as soon as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack young maize leaves and tender shoots. Inspecting your field early and using recommended organic treatments or targeted pest control early in the morning or evening can save your young crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Ohe ni oyɔɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ehere oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Cocoa pods rot mainly because of Black Pod disease, which thrives in cool, damp, shaded environments. Pruning heavy shade tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds around the cocoa trees helps keep the air dry and protects the pods.
ga: Cocoa pod ni fiteɔ lɛ babaoo jɛɔ black pod hela mli. Amɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa lɛ amli koni hulu la aba mli, ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni bɔle kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my okra plants get covered in white powdery spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ ahe eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ lɛ?

english: White spots on okra leaves are usually powdery mildew, a fungal disease that spreads when plants are too close together and humidity is high. Spacing your plants farther apart helps air flow freely and keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ okra baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo. Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by intense heat, irregular watering, or lack of key nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding excessive chemical fertilizers will help the plant hold onto its flowers and produce peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli nibii titrii ni bɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ajie tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo ŋmeii.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my plantain suckers while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? dumɔwui lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ

english: Weeds compete with young plantain suckers for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping the area clean allows the young plantain to build a strong stem and grow fast enough to produce heavy bunches.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ plantain tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha he lɛ he tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa ni amɛdaraa oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛfeɔ kui wuji.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning brown and drying up in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves are delicate and burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that filters the sunlight and keeps the soil cool until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ehaa hulu la ni tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a shape like an upside-down V?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize leaves yellow from the tip down the center leaf vein, it means the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main plant food needed to build green leaves and grow big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ baa lɛ naa kɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Groundnuts and beans are special plants that pull natural nitrogen food from the air and store it in their roots. When they die, that food stays in the soil, acting as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. kɛ amɛgboi lɛ Nakai niyenii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rain stays on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to stay alive. When water sits on the field without draining, it smothers the roots, allowing water rot and soil fungi to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ ni ejeee kpo lɛ, efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ, ni ehaa nu lɛ fiteɔ, ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kpataaa ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry leaves help them during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates a blanket called mulch. Mulch blocks the hot sun from baking the ground, keeps moisture in the soil longer, and prevents the plant roots from drying out.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ feɔ nɔ ko. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ tsei shishifãi anaa koni amɛkagbi

english: Why are there ragged holes in the middle whorl of my young maize leaves with small dirt-like powder inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse ehe lɛ? yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ Muji bibioo ko ni tamɔ muji yɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the center funnel of the young maize plant to eat the soft inner leaves before they open.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward and turn pale green, stopping the plant from bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ awo yibii?

english: Leaf curl is caused by a plant virus spread by tiny flies called whiteflies. When whiteflies feed on the leaves, they inject the virus, which disrupts the plant's normal growth.
ga: Tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji whiteflies ye baai Ebaawo virus mli. ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing fruits when weeds surround them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni jwɛi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops and weeds eat from the same soil and light. When weeds surround a crop, the crop spends all its energy stretching upward to catch sunlight instead of using energy to grow thick stems and produce fruit.
ga: Tsei kɛ jwɛi yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ la kome nɔ. Beni jwɛi ebɔle ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse ni awo yibii lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to light to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia kane tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛwo la mli ni otsi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over during rainstorms just when the fruit bunch is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli be mli pɛ ni aduawai akui lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them unbalanced. Supporting the trunk with a strong wooden prop prevents the wind from pushing the tree over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. unbalance Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa tso lɛ shi.

english: How do I know the right chemical or medicine to apply when insects start eating my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai loo tsofai ni sa ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛ́ kooloi bɔi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeli?

english: Different insects require specific treatments, and using the wrong chemical can damage your crops or waste money. You should visit your local agricultural extension station to identify the exact pest and receive the correct medicine and dosage.
ga: Kplukai babaoo biɔ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. Ni tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii loo efite shika. Esa akɛ oyasara okwaayeli he nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ koni oyayoo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni sa lɛ ni oná tsofa ni sa kɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by soil-borne fungus or bacteria attacking the roots and lower stem, which blocks water from traveling up into the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tutuaa shishifãi kɛ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa. Enɛ haaa nu abote baai lɛ amli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food plants need to build chlorophyll and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛfee klorofil ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same spot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does covering the soil with dry leaves or grass help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Te baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant matter, known as mulching, shields the ground from direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Young cocoa plants burn and dry out easily under full, direct sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or fast-growing plants like plantains to protect them while their stems and leaves mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin stems and small harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to place wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up toward the sun. Spreading leaves in sunlight helps the plant manufacture food to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Atomɔ tso lɛ miikwɔ wain tso ko ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ agbɛ baai lɛ ashwã hulu la mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting if left in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain makes the soil waterlogged, depriving roots of oxygen and encouraging fungal growth that rots cassava roots before harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa amɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and bigger than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally survive in tough conditions and absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing them early stops them from starving your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ.

english: Why do some farmers hang their harvested maize under the roof eaves of their house instead of leaving it in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ amɛŋmaa ni amɛkpa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ amɛshiai lɛ ashishi moŋ fe ni amɛaashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Hanging crops like maize under house eaves protects them from sudden rainfall and soil moisture while allowing continuous breeze to dry them safely, which prevents mold and spoilage.
ga: Tsei tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya nɔ etswa koni egbi shweshweeshwe. ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fitemɔ naa

english: Is it better to dry seeds I plan to plant next season in direct sunlight or in a shaded area?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui ni mito gbɛjianɔ akɛ madu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Seeds meant for future planting are best dried in a shaded, well-ventilated area because extreme heat from direct sunlight can damage the delicate embryo inside the seed, reducing its ability to germinate.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaagbi dumɔwui ni abaadu wɔsɛɛ lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite fɔmɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shweremɔ nyɛmɔ ni baa shi.

english: How can I check if my harvested grains are dry enough for storage without using expensive equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji miŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akɛto he ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can use a simple salt test by placing a dry handful of grain with dry salt in a sealed glass jar; if salt sticks to the glass sides after shaking, the grain still holds too much water and needs more drying.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmaa ni egbi kɛ ŋmei ni egbi ni okɛwo glase tsinsii ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmei kpɛtɛ glase lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ekpokpo lɛ sɛɛ Nu babaoo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lolo ni ehe miihia ni agbi lɛ babaoo.

english: How do I select the best grains from my harvest to save as seed for the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛto akɛ dumɔwui kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Select seeds from healthy, high-yielding plants, choosing well-formed grains from the middle section of the cob or pod, as these tend to sprout more reliably and grow into stronger plants than tip seeds.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Halamɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛjɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ fɔɔ kwɛ̃mɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa fe dumɔwui ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell the difference between certified improved seeds and my traditional farm-saved seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli kɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Certified improved seeds come in sealed, labeled packets from registered agro-dealers and produce highly uniform plants, whereas saved seeds from previous harvests vary in size and may yield less over time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni asaa he ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ baa yɛ kotokui ni aŋmala nɔ nibii awo mli ni jɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ ni nɔ kwɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ dalɛi srɔtoi ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What happens if I plant two different maize varieties right next to each other in the same field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa srɔtoi enyɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Maize plants cross-pollinate via wind, meaning pollen from one variety will mix with the other, causing the saved seeds from that harvest to lose their original purity and specific crop traits.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, pollen ni jɛ tso kome mli lɛ kɛ ekroko baafutu. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛshishijee hetsemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe sui.

english: Why should I sort my harvested crops into different batches before taking them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majara mikpamɔ lɛ mli awo kui amli lɛ? dani ajie lɛ kpo kɛya jara nɔ

english: Sorting helps you separate high-grade, undamaged produce that commands premium market prices from smaller or damaged pieces that can be used immediately at home or as animal feed.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ ogbalaa nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni efiteee ni biɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli kɛjɛɔ nibii bibii loo nibii ni efite ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ shia loo akɛ kooloi aniyenii amli.

english: What causes my stored maize to go moldy even when it felt dry when I bagged it?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ eyɛ mli akɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, minuɔ he akɛ egbi moŋ?

english: Grains often retain hidden moisture inside the core, and if stored in airtight plastic bags without complete drying or in a warm, unventilated room, sweat builds up and breeds mold.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ mli. Ni kɛji akɛ akɛwo plastic kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli ni egbiko kwraa. aloo yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli mli Latsaa buaa ehe naa ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa.

english: How can I prevent insects and weevils from eating my stored grains without using harmful chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ ni mikɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii?

english: You can keep pests away by ensuring grains are thoroughly dry, storing them in clean hermetic (airtight) bags that suffocate pests, or mixing the grains with clean, dry wood ash.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa kɛtsɔ nɔmimaa ni ooona akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ nɔ. Akɛwoɔ kotoku ko ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (vacuum) mli, ni no baatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo amɛmumɔ. Aloo okɛ tso sũ ni he tse ni egbi afutu ŋmaa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense response where the plant reduces its leaf surface area exposed to the sun to conserve water and protect itself from intense heat and drought stress.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu hetoo ni tsei tsiɔ baa lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ he.

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make the energy required to grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch full sunlight and stay safe from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ajie tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛ hulu ni yeɔ emuu aha ni ebu he kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn cobs are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the plant lacks nitrogen. When maize doesn't get enough food from the soil, it takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves and developing cob, causing the lower leaves to yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ esa akɛ ajie Nitrogen kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni akɛha ŋwɛi baa bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my hot pepper plants curling up and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects that distorts the plant's normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cowpea plants have plenty of green leaves but very few flowers and bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen fertilizer or are grown in overly rich soil, the plant uses all its energy to grow lush leaves instead of switching to produce flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cowpeas nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nii yɔɔ mli tsɔ nɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsake kɛya fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ashishifãi afeemɔ nɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot and turn watery if left in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ nu kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the soil stays waterlogged for too long during heavy rains, the roots cannot breathe, causing them to drown, spoil, and rot underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehiɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Enɛ haa nu mli shwieɔ shi, egboɔ, ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do groundnuts form their nuts inside the ground after flowering above the soil?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii feɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ?

english: After the groundnut flower is pollinated above ground, its stem grows longer and bends down to push a small shoot called a peg into the soil. Once buried underground, the tip of this peg expands into the groundnut pod.
ga: Beni ajie ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Eshishifã lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ebɔleɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni ekɛtsi ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛje kpo. Atsɛɔ nakai akɛ peg ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ mli. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Pin nɛɛ naagbee lɛ baashɛ ŋmei ŋmei lɛ he fɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime heat gets too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly. Extreme heat stresses the plant, forcing it to shed flowers to conserve water and survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do many small shoots grow around the base of my plantain tree, and should I clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ. mi plantain shishitoo Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mli?

english: Those small shoots are suckers growing from the main root. If you leave all of them, they will compete with the mother plant for nutrients and water, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. You should remove most of them and leave only one or two strong ones.
ga: Nakai tsei bibii lɛ ji tsei ni jɛɔ shishifã titri lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ kwraa lɛ, amɛkɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Esa akɛ ojie amɛteŋ babaoo ni oshi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why does rice grow better in standing water while crops like maize will die if flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa baagboi kɛji nu afua.

english: Rice plants have special tubes inside their stems and roots that allow oxygen from the air to travel down to the roots even when submerged, whereas maize roots drown because they cannot get oxygen under water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli, kɛ́ amɛbote nu mli po. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ nu mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ nu shishi.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says my cocoa trees have a viral disease?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ hela ko?

english: A viral disease in crops is caused by microscopic germs inside the tree's sap that corrupt how the plant grows from the inside out. Unlike common fungal spots or leaf damage, plant viruses move through the whole tree and cannot be cured by spraying regular chemicals.
ga: Virus helai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi bibii ni yɔɔ tsei amli nu lɛ mli lɛ amli. ni fiteɔ tso lɛ dalɛ kɛjɛɔ emli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ fungal spots loo baa ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ, tso mli helai baanyɛ aya tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. ni anyɛɛɛ atsa kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ fɛɛ gbɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the branches and shoots of my young cocoa trees swelling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ aniji kɛ amɛyitsei lɛ efuu ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Swelling along the shoots and yellow veins on leaves are classic signs of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease. The virus forces the tree to produce abnormal, swollen tissue, which blocks water and food from flowing, eventually causing the tree to dry up and die.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efuu kɛ fãji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji okadii ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ emɔ hela. Virus lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni efee fãji ni efuu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. ni tsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii naa koni ekaho Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is sick from a virus or just struggling because of the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ emɔ hela ko loo amɛmiikpe naagbai kɛkɛ yɛ hɔmɔ lɛ hewɔ?

english: Thirsty trees usually have limp, brown leaves evenly across the farm. A viral disease causes distinct abnormal symptoms like swollen stems, mottled yellow patterns on the leaf veins, or stunted growth, even when the soil has enough moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Virus helai kɛ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni ejaaa baa, tamɔ tso yibii ni efuu kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ baa lɛ mli. loo shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: How do cocoa viruses like Swollen Shoot spread from one farm to another?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kookoo mli helai tamɔ Swollen Shoot lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli?

english: The virus is carried mainly by tiny sap-sucking insects called mealybugs. When these bugs feed on an infected tree and then crawl or get carried by ants to a healthy tree, they inject the virus directly into the healthy tree's sap.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji mɛi ni hiɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ye tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛkɛyaa tso ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ. Amɛwoɔ hela lɛ amɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Are tiny bugs on my cocoa trees dangerous even if they aren't eating the pods?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ oshara kɛji amɛyeko ŋmeii lɛ po?

english: Yes, insects like mealybugs don't need to chew pods to cause damage. By drinking sap from infected trees, they pick up plant viruses and act like carriers, spreading deadly diseases like Swollen Shoot to healthy trees across your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs lɛ ashɛre ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛfite nii. kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛnuɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli Amɛheɔ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ mɛi ni kɛ hela lɛ baa. Gbalamɔ helai ni naa wa, tamɔ tsei ni efuu lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cocoa cuttings or pods that come from outside my local area?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ kookoo tsei loo ŋmeii ni jɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ kponɔ?

english: Bringing planting materials from outside your area carries a high risk of introducing new plant viruses or diseases into your soil. It is always safer to use certified, disease-resistant cocoa seeds provided by official agricultural nurseries.
ga: Nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni akɛbaajɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kponɔgbɛ kɛba lɛ kɛ oshara kpele ni ji helai heei loo tsei ahe helai baa. kɛya oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyɛ shweshweeshwe be fɛɛ be akɛ okɛ kookoo yibii ni yɔɔ odaseyeli, ni helai nyɛŋ emɔ amɛ ni jɛ okwaayeli hei ni maŋ onukpai lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why am I advised to cut down an entire cocoa tree when only one or two branches look swollen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tso muu lɛ fɛɛ be mli ni nine kome loo enyɔ pɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efuu lɛ?

english: Once a tree contracts a viral disease like Swollen Shoot, the virus spreads through the sap of the entire plant, including the trunk and roots. Even if other branches look fine, they are already infected and will spread the virus to nearby healthy trees if not removed completely.
ga: Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tso mli baa, tamɔ tsei ashishifãi ni efu lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ nu lɛ mli fɛɛ. Nɔ ni fata he ji tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei niji krokomɛi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ po lɛ, hela lɛ emɔ amɛ momo, ni amɛbaagbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli kɛji ajieee amɛ kwraa.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact spot where an old tree died from Swollen Shoot disease?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni tsei momoi egboi yɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ hewɔ?

english: You should not plant immediately. The insects and root contacts that carried the virus may still be in the soil. You need to clear the infected roots, let the land rest or plant a barrier crop like plantain, and ensure the area is clear of pests before replanting cocoa.
ga: Esaaa akɛ oduɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kplukai kɛ shishifãi ni hiɛ hela lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo odu gbɛtsii nibii tamɔ plantains, ni okwɛ koni he ni kooloi bibii bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ dani odu kookoo.

english: How can the Department of Agriculture help me if a strange disease starts attacking my cocoa farm?
ga: Te Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi aha tɛŋŋ kɛji hela bɔi mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli baa?

english: The Department of Agriculture sends technical extension officers to inspect your farm, test for specific cocoa viruses, teach you how to identify symptoms early, and assist with safe disease management plans to protect the rest of your crop.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ tsuɔ ŋaalɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛbakwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kaa kɛha kookoo mli helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi Tsɔɔmɔ bɔ ni afeɔ ayɔseɔ hela lɛ he okadii lɛ mra. ni oye obua kɛ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni baabu onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Is there any medicine or spray I can buy at the store to cure Swollen Shoot disease in my cocoa?
ga: Ani tsofai loo tsofai komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ mahe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli koni mikɛtsa mi-kokoo fã ni efuu lɛ?

english: Currently, there is no chemical spray or medicine that can cure a cocoa tree once it has a viral disease like Swollen Shoot. The only effective control is removing the infected trees early and planting resistant cocoa varieties recommended by agricultural officers.
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ loo tsofai ni baanyɛ atsa amɛ kɛji amɛyɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ bɛ. Nɔ pɛ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ ji tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra. kɛ kookoo henɔi ni tsei nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing key nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are sitting in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right time helps the crop turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf rolling is the corn plant's natural trick to protect itself. By curling its leaves, the plant hides from direct sunlight to trap moisture inside and stop water from drying out.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji ŋmãa tso ko adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni ekɛbuɔ ehe he. Tsei teɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni amɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛtsi enaa koni ekagbi lɛ nɔ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper plant spacing gives every single plant enough room to feed and grow big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsoi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfiɔ ŋmei ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Can I still grow good crops on farmland that was damaged or dug up by heavy machinery?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lolo yɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni efite loo ni akɛ tsɔnei ni tsii efo mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Damaged land loses its fertile topsoil, but you can restore it over time by leveling the ground, planting cover crops like velvet beans to rebuild the soil, and adding plenty of animal manure or compost.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ fiteɔ eshikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni baa nii lɛ. Shi obaanyɛ okɛto ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ velvet ŋmeii ni aduɔ koni akɛtswa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji babaoo afata he.

english: How do I tell if my farmland soil has become too weak to support a large crop like corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ akɛ manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii wuji tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: If your crop grows very slowly, stays pale, or gives poor yields even when there is enough rainfall, it means the soil has lost its nutrients and needs fertilizer, manure, or a resting period.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa blɛoo waa, amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛwooo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo hejɔɔmɔ be awo mli.

english: Why is it so much harder to manage a very large maize farm compared to a small one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa waa akɛ aaakwɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ agbo waa nɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔ bibioo he lɛ?

english: Large farms require carefully timed labor, equipment, and resources. If weeding, fertilizing, or pest control is delayed on a large field, crops compete with weeds and suffer much faster across the entire area.
ga: Okwaafoi wuji biɔ nitsumɔ, nibii, kɛ nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ he ko ni da lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ ni amɛnaa naagbai yɛ he fɛɛ he oya kwraa.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster than my corn after a rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild and tough plants that take up water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated corn. Removing them while they are small prevents them from stealing food from your crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: What is making holes in the middle leaves of my maize and leaving small dirt-like droppings?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-abele baai lɛ amli eyi kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ muji?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the young leaves to eat. Spraying safe, recommended pesticides early in the morning or late evening reaches them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai bibii amli koni amɛye nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ afɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does planting cassava or cowpea alongside my maize help my farm survive bad weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli lɛ?

english: Mixing different crops reduces risk. Crops like cowpeas put natural food back into the soil for maize, and if bad weather hurts one crop, you still have the other to harvest.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ haa oshara baa shi. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ cowpea lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa ŋmãa. Ni kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii kome he lɛ Oyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome kroko ni eshwɛ ni obaakpa.

english: Why does my harvested corn get holes and turn into dust when I store it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli buɔ ni etsɔɔ sũ kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils eat stored corn if the grains are not dried completely before bagging. Thorough sun-drying and storing grains in special airtight hermetic bags keeps insects out without chemicals.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii baaye ŋmãa ni ato kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛwo kotoku mli. Gbimɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛ ŋmaa lɛ awo vacuum kotokui krɛdɛɛi amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe ni ekɛ tsofai tsuuu nii.

english: Why shouldn't I cut my seed yam into smaller pieces with a knife before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ bibii bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmei dani adu

english: Cutting seed yams with a knife can easily spread diseases and rot from one tuber to another. Planting whole, certified seed yams protects them from infections and ensures they grow strong and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ ŋmei lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela eshwã ni efite kɛjɛ ŋmei kome mli kɛya ekroko mli oya. Sweet potatoes muu ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Will planting a small, whole seed yam actually produce big tubers at harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmeii bibii ni eye emuu ni akwɛɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii wuji aba kɛji akpa?

english: Yes! Small whole seed yams around 50 to 70 grams that come from certified sources are disease-free and full of energy, allowing them to grow into large, high-yielding yams.
ga: hɛɛ! Atomɔ bibii ni eye emuu, ni tsiimɔ ji aaafee gram 50 kɛyashi 70, ni anáa kɛjɛɔ hei ni awo he odase lɛ, hela bɛ mli ni eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii agboi ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How does planting whole seed yams save me time and labor on the farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii muu ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mibe kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting whole seed yams removes the extra work of measuring, cutting, and treating cut pieces before planting, allowing you to plant directly and reduce the risk of crop loss.
ga: Sweet potatoes muu ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ jatsu kroko ni ji ŋmeii lɛ asusumɔ, amɛfomɔ, kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ dani aduɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafite lɛ baa shi.

english: What is a 'certified seed' yam, and why is it better than saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘dumɔwui ni awo he odase’ sweet potatoes ni mɛni hewɔ amɛhi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛbaahere kɛjɛ mi tsutsu kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A certified seed is grown under strict scientific supervision to ensure it is completely free from diseases and pests. Seeds saved from regular harvests often carry hidden diseases that lower your yields over time.
ga: Aduɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ jeŋ nilee nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi koni ana akɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui bɛ mli kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hiɔ shi yɛ kpamɔ ni sa mli lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do extension officers produce certified seed yams before they reach us farmers?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ afee sweet potatoes ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ dani amɛshɛ okwaafoi lɛ ahe?

english: They start with clean plants in a laboratory, grow them safely inside protected net houses, and then transfer them to fields to mature into certified, high-quality seeds.
ga: Amɛjeɔ shishi kɛ tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ laboratori lɛ mli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ trellis shĩa ni abuɔ he lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ajieɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli.

english: Why do new yam varieties seem to yield much better than our traditional varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni sweet potato henɔi heei lɛ woɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ fe wɔ blema henɔi lɛ?

english: New varieties are developed through specialized breeding and laboratory processes to resist diseases, adapt better to growing conditions, and produce larger harvests.
ga: Afeɔ srɔtoi heei kɛtsɔɔ fɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoi krɛdɛɛi kɛ laboratorii anɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shihilɛi ni mli wa lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo

english: How can I protect my farm soil from getting infected by diseased crop seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ akabote mli?

english: The best way is to plant certified whole seeds that originated from clean laboratory processes, as they are guaranteed to be disease-free and will not bring rot or viruses into your land.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui muu ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ laboratori nifeemɔ ni he tse mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ayɛ nɔmimaa akɛ helai bɛ amɛhe, ni amɛkɛ ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ baaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is a screen house, and why are young plants grown inside it?
ga: Mɛni ji shĩa ni akwɛɔ nɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ tso bibioo ko miida yɛ mli lɛ?

english: A screen house is a protective netted structure that keeps destructive insects away from young plants. It creates a safe environment for delicate crops to grow healthy before being moved into the main farm field.
ga: Strainer ji tsɔne ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akashɛɔ tsei bibii ahe. Ehaa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe baa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ waa dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: What does 'tissue culture' mean when scientists talk about growing plants in a lab?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘tissue culture’ shishi kɛ́ jeŋ nilelɔi wie tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ laboratori lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Tissue culture is a modern technique where tiny, healthy pieces of a plant are grown in sterile laboratory conditions to multiply thousands of identical, disease-free plants very quickly.
ga: Tissue culture ji ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaa ko ni akɛduɔ tsei bibii. ni mli wa yɛ laboratori shihilɛi ni mli ewo muji mli Koni ekɛ tsei akpei abɔ ni tamɔ amɛhe ni hela bɛ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: How does a plant move from a laboratory to my farm field safely?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ajie tsei kɛjɛ laboratori lɛ mli kɛya miŋmɔ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe?

english: Plants start sterile in a lab, then get hardened and grown in a protected screen house to build strength, and finally get planted in fields to produce mature seeds for farmers.
ga: Tsei jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli yɛ laboratorio mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ahaa ewaa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni abuɔ he mli koni ewa. ni naagbee lɛ, aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli koni ekɛ dumɔwui ni eda aha okwaafoi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient it uses to stay green and grow tall. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the plant's growth helps keep the leaves green so it can produce full maize ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli koni ŋmãa toi babaoo aba.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight and high temperatures. Shade trees protect tender cocoa seedlings from scorching heat and preserve moisture in the soil, creating a cooler environment so the seedlings can establish strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi. Feemɔ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Cassava roots rot when soil stays completely waterlogged for long periods because the roots cannot get air, allowing fungal diseases to multiply. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away from the tuber roots so they stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or mites, or a virus they transmit. Controlling these insects early with appropriate sprays or insecticidal soaps prevents leaf damage and allows the plant to set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo samla ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite baai lɛ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are tiny insects attacking my cowpea flowers as soon as they open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛfɔ̃ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce a sweet scent and soft petals that attract pests like flower thrips, which feed on the delicate blossoms before pods can form. Checking your crop regularly and applying targeted protection at the first sign of budding stops flower damage.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Egbalaa ŋmeii tamɔ thrips, ni yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa ni okɛ hebuu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ koni ekpa fɔfɔi lɛ afitemɔ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso ko ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni wain tsei lɛ akakwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, reducing fungal diseases spread by muddy soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛnɔ babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo muji nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong wind and rain when carrying fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that struggle to support the heavy weight of a maturing fruit bunch during high winds. Propping the stem with a strong bamboo fork or wooden pole supports the weight and keeps the tree upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ tsiimɔ lɛ ni ebaaha tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut off the old dry branches from my oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ niji momo ni egbi lɛ?

english: Removing dead or old lower fronds helps the oil palm tree direct its energy and nutrients toward developing fresh fruit bunches. It also improves air circulation and light exposure around the tree stem while making harvesting easier.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egboi loo ni egbɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mu tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa aduawai heei ni baa lɛ anɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa la ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. tso shishi Ehaa ekpamɔ feɔ mlɛo

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot or when the plant experiences water stress, which disrupts pollination. Consistent watering at the base of the plant and keeping the soil cool with mulch helps the flowers successfully turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. ni tsiɔ pollination naa Nu ni awoɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ daa ni akɛ mulch haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why are my cabbage plants producing wide outer leaves but not forming a hard round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai ni mli kwɔ shi ebɛ yitsei ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form firm heads when temperatures are too high or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing excessive leaf growth. Planting during cooler periods and using a balanced fertilizer encourages the inner leaves to fold tightly into a head.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni wa kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa baai lɛ daraa fe nine. Kɛ́ adu yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaawo mligbɛ baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfolɔ amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ kɛya yitso lɛ he.

english: How do I know if a new crop variety from outside my area will grow well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsei srɔtoi heei ni jɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ kponɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Soil and weather conditions differ across regions in Ghana. Before planting a new seed variety on your whole farm, plant a small test plot first to observe how it handles local rains, heat, and pests.
ga: Esoro shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɛ kpokpaa fɛɛ kpokpaa nɔ yɛ Ghana. Dani obaadu dumɔwui heei yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Dumɔ kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko. klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ koni ekwɛ bɔ ni maŋbii lɛ kɛ nugbɔ, latsaa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ.

english: The early rains in Ghana are often followed by a brief dry spell. If you plant too early, the young seeds will germinate and then dry up and die before the main rainy season fully sets in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra yɛ Ghana lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nutrients, especially nitrogen, or the soil is too dry. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant make food and regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ otso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛnáa su ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How long does it take for planted pepper seeds to start sprouting out of the soil?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui ni adu lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Pepper seeds usually take between 7 to 14 days to germinate. They need moist soil and warm weather to break out of their shell, so keeping the seedbed damp is essential.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui lɛ heɔ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe hia ni aha he ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: What happens to my crops if insects keep eating their early leaves?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji kooloi bibii tee nɔ amɛye eshishifãi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaves act as the plant's kitchen to make food. When insects destroy early leaves, the crop becomes weak, grows slowly, and produces much smaller yields at harvest time.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ kpataashi kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Kɛji kooloi bibii fite tsei ahe baai lɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which naturally nourishes the maize plants while maximizing your field space.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he. Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni ehaa oŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ babaoo.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Spacing them properly allows each plant to grow strong and produce bigger crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up. Harvesting before this means smaller tubers, while leaving them too long can cause rotting.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛje shishi amɛgbi. Kɛ́ akpa mra lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii bibii aba. Shi kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha egbo.

english: How can I keep the ground moist for my crops when the sun is very hot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly, helping your plants survive hot, dry stretches.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Ye obua otsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Can I save seeds from my current harvest to plant again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: While traditional crop seeds can be saved, packaged hybrid seeds will produce weaker crops and lower yields if replanted. For hybrid varieties, buying fresh certified seeds gives the best harvest.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ ato blema tsei ahe dumɔwui ahe moŋ Shi dumɔwui ni akɛwo kotoku mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ. Kɛha hybrid henɔi lɛ Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to stay green and grow well, so when the soil lacks this food, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii nɛɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them with maize acts like a natural fertilizer, making the soil richer and helping your maize grow better without buying extra chemicals.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ abɛi duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily and they lose water too fast. They need shade from larger trees or temporary crops like plantains to survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni nu lɛ hu sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without producing any fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When the weather gets too hot, tomato flowers cannot pollinate properly. The heat stresses the plant, so it drops its blossoms to save energy instead of forming fruit.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ No hewɔ lɛ, efɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce energy. Raising the vines on stakes helps the leaves catch more sun and keeps them off the hot ground, which leads to much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Wein tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If too many suckers grow around one main plantain stem, they will all fight for the same water and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring you get bigger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ, tso titri kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli, ni ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ahi shi. Ayɛ nɔmimaa akɛ obaaná plantains ŋmɔŋ ni da ni tsii fe no.

english: Why are green caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize crop at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the leaves during the hot daytime and come out at night to eat the tender growing heart of the maize plant. They must be managed early to prevent them from destroying the crop yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛye ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ atsui lɛ. Esa akɛ akwɛ amɛ nɔ mra koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain floods the land and water sits in the soil for too long, the roots drown and harmful soil fungi quickly cause them to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hoɔ ni nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaha amɛgboi oya.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my pepper plants with dry grass or dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or straw is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that stops the sun from drying out the dirt, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaaa muji akagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's harvested hybrid maize yield much less than new seed packets bought from the shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed to produce high yields only for the first planting. The seeds saved from that harvest lose their special combination of strength, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields if replanted.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves start rotting when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso baai lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting too close traps moisture and blocks airflow around the leaves, creating a wet environment where fungal diseases spread quickly from plant to plant.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ naa, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: How do I know which direction to plant cassava stems in the dirt so they grow properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni esa akɛ madu mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cassava stems have tiny buds or nodes where leaves used to be. These buds must point upwards toward the sky so the shoots can grow straight up while roots develop underneath.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ yɛ hiŋmɛii bibii loo fãji yɛ he ni baai lɛ yɔɔ tsutsu lɛ. Ehe miihia ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ ada kɛya ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil that helps leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers instead of turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Aloo kooloi ni bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollin lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are small caterpillars suddenly eating the inside leaves of my corn right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii baa trukaa ni amɛbayeɔ mi-abele baai lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hatch rapidly when warm rains start and feed on the soft, tender leaves inside the central whorl of the corn plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni fɔɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce fewer pods when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind strips moisture from leaves and soil, forcing the cocoa tree to drop flowers and small pods to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ehe bahiaa ni cacao tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Koni okɛ nu ato ni oha ohe ahi wala mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big trees in my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct sunlight. They require shade from larger trees or plantain plants to protect their tender leaves from drying out and scorching.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo dumɔwui adɛŋ koni baai bibii lɛ akagbi ni amɛkashã.

english: How do I choose the best plantain shoots from my old plants to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ mitsei momo lɛ amli koni mikɛje dumɔ saatso hee shishi?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—shoots with narrow, needle-like leaves and a thick base. They grow stronger and yield bigger fruit bunches than shoots with broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante tsei’—tsei ni baai lɛ mli tseee ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni amɛshishigbɛ lɛ mli tse. Amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ kui wuji fe ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans in the same field with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, which helps feed the neighboring maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ Nuts Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does putting dry grass on the soil around my plants help them grow better in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ jwɛi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mitsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, shields the ground from the hot sun, keeping the soil cool and holding in moisture longer for root uptake.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Officer, can I successfully grow vegetables like carrots on a small piece of land near my house in Ghana?
ga: Ofisa Mibaanyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ karɔt yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani ebɛŋkɛ mishia yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, you can grow carrots and other vegetables on small plots of land as long as the area receives good sunlight and the soil is loose, sandy, and well-drained so the roots can expand.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu karɔt kɛ aduawai krokomɛi. yɛ he bibioo ko nɔ, kɛji akɛ hulu la kpakpa yɛ he ni jɛmɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ni shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ. ni etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ alɛɛ mli
