english: Is it good practice for me to plant different types of vegetables together on the same small farm?
ga: Aduawai srɔtoi babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli Ani nakai nɔŋŋ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa kɛha mi?

english: Yes, mixing different crops, known as intercropping, helps you maximize small spaces, improves soil nutrients, and reduces the risk of losing your entire harvest if one crop fails.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ Ni ale lɛ hu akɛ intercropping. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ hei bibii lɛ feɔ babaoo. Ha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni oha oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ baafite kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite lɛ aba shi.

english: How long does it usually take after planting for root vegetables like carrots to be ready to harvest?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛji adu shishifãi, tamɔ karɔt, dani efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Most carrot varieties in warm climates take between 70 to 90 days (about 2.5 to 3 months) after planting to reach full maturity and be ready for harvest.
ga: Karɔt henɔi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ gbii 70 kɛyashi 90 (aaafee nyɔji 2.5 kɛyashi 3) yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my root crops like carrots grow crooked and small instead of straight and big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishishifãi, tamɔ karɔt lɛ, kwɛ̃ɔ ni etse ehe ni efee bibii moŋ fe ni eeefee jalɛsaneyeli ni efee agbo lɛ?

english: Root crops bend and stay small when the soil is too hard, clayey, or full of stones. Deeply tilling and loosening the soil before planting allows the roots to push straight down easily.
ga: Tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Sũ ni. loo tɛi ni eyi mli obɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ ni mli kwɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ dani aduɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shi tɛ̃ɛ. mlɛo

english: How can I easily tell if the soil on my land is good enough to grow vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai?

english: Good agricultural soil is dark in color, crumbly to the touch, holds moisture without turning into heavy mud, and allows water to drain freely rather than forming standing pools.
ga: Okwaayeli shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋ. Efoɔ kɛji akɛ ata he Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni efeee muji waa ni ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaama ŋshɔ ni damɔ shi lɛ

english: Why should I avoid planting the exact same crop on the same patch of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ dumɔ he yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, leading to lower yields in future seasons.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant the seeds too close to each other in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close causes the growing crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How deep into the ground should I bury small vegetable seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu aduawai dumɔwui bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Small vegetable seeds should only be buried shallowly, about two to three times their width deep, so they have enough energy to push through the soil once they sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ afu aduawai dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ pɛ, aaafee bɔ ni amɛlɛɛmɔ lɛ ji shii 2-3. Koni ená hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji amɛje kpo.

english: Officer, is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning or during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ofisa, ani ehi akɛ mawo aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the water cools the soil and reaches the roots before the heat of the afternoon sun causes it to evaporate.
ga: Nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa koni sũ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ aha sũ lɛ mli atsɔ la.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, is receiving too much water, or is struggling with a root disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, ni enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. aloo amɛmiiwuu hela yɛ shishijee mli

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or that too much water around the roots is stopping them from breathing. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer when the soil is moist helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen loo nu yɛ amɛhe. Shishifãi babaoo kpaɔ mumɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my land is prepared well enough for planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cassava needs soft, loose soil so its underground roots can expand easily into large tubers. If the ground is too hard or stays flooded with water, the roots will remain small or rot before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ he miihia cassava. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibii loo amɛbaafite dani akpa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny pests like thrips. Keeping the soil consistently damp and protecting plants during intense heat helps the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni abu tsei ahe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃.

english: What happens if I plant my tomato seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When tomatoes are planted too close together, they fight for sunshine, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and tall with very few fruit, and makes it easier for leaf diseases to spread.
ga: Kɛji adu tomatoi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tomatoi kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ shwilafoi ni amɛkwɔ kɛ yibii fioo ko pɛ. ni ehaa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leaves but very few beans during heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baa babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much rain causes cowpeas to put all their energy into growing thick green vines and leaves instead of flowering. Cowpeas need moderate rain and drier weather to trigger heavy flowering and pod production.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ wain tsei kɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Cowpea biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi koni ewo fɔfɔi ni tsii kɛ pod agbo ni ajieɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking so long to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers sprout slowly if planted too deep, if the soil is overly dry, or if pests damaged the underground corm before planting. Using clean suckers and keeping the soil moist speeds up growth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Kɛji adu mli tsɔ Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛji kooloi fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani aduɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni he tse tsu nii ni akwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why does wild grass grow faster than my maize crop right after clearing the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ beni ajie jɛmɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Wild grass seeds and roots are already established in the soil and adapted to quickly grab water and plant food. Clearing weeds early gives your young maize seedlings a fair chance to take up nutrients and light.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo. ni ekɛ ehe woɔ nu kɛ tsei aniyenii amli oya Ejieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha ŋmãa bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ la.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are fully matured and ready to pull out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-peanuts lɛ egbɔ kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can check by pulling up one test plant; if the inside of the shells has dark brown or black spots and the seeds fill the pod tightly, your crop is fully mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ kaa tso kome ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi mli obɔ ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Will planting beans together with my yam crop spoil the yam tubers?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ baadu lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ afite?

english: No, beans actually help yam crops because beans take nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which feeds the yam vines without competing for the deep root space where tubers grow.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ejaakɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. ni haa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná he ko amɛha shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and shrink while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbɔjɔ beni ekã tso ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods turn black either due to Black Pod fungal disease caused by high dampness and shade, or because the tree naturally sheds extra pods it cannot feed due to water stress.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ blackpod fungus hela ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Aloo akɛni tso lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ niyenii yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava directly under my big mango trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mango tso agbo ko shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Cassava needs full sunlight to develop thick, healthy tubers. Planting it directly under the dense shade of a mango tree causes the plant to grow long, thin stems searching for light, leaving you with very small roots underground.
ga: Hulu ni fa babaoo he miihia Yucca koni enyɛ ená ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ mango tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni taoɔ la. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, oyɛ shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What light-loving crops will fail if I plant them under shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ baafite kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo tsei ashishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crops like cassava, maize, tomatoes, and peppers require direct sunlight all day to manufacture food and produce fruits or tubers. Heavy shade slows their growth and drastically lowers your yield.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, tomato, kɛ ŋmãa biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii kɛ aduawai loo ŋmãa. Su ni tsuɔ waa lɛ baaha ekwɛ̃ fioo ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Which crops perform best when planted under the shade of bigger trees?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi?

english: Crops like cocoyam, ginger, turmeric, and young cocoa plants thrive in partial shade because direct, harsh sunlight can burn their leaves and dry out the soil around their roots.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ cocoa, ginger, turmeric kɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ agbi.

english: Will the roots of my big fruit trees steal water and nutrients from small crops planted nearby?
ga: Ani mi tsei wuji ni woɔ yibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, large tree roots spread widely underground and pull water and fertilizer away from smaller crops. You should plant your field crops a few meters away from the tree canopy or add extra organic manure to compensate.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei wuji ashishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi babaoo ni egbalaa nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli. Esa akɛ odu oŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai fioo komɛi loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he koni okɛwo he nyɔmɔ.

english: How can I tell if a wild plant on my land is cassava or a look-alike weed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ koo mli tso ko ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmei loo jwɛi ni tamɔ lɛ?

english: True cassava has clear, segmented stem joints where leaves attach and produces tuberous roots underground. Look-alike plants like castor bean often have spiky seed pods and hollow stems, so always verify stem cuttings with an extension officer before planting.
ga: Anɔkwale cassava yɛ tso lɛ mli tsei ni mli tse, ni mli eja. He ni baai lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Tsei ni tamɔ nakai, tamɔ castor beans, bei pii lɛ, amɛyɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ewo bu. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ mɔ ni kwɛɔ onɔ lɛ akwɛ o-cuttings lɛ be fɛɛ be dani okɛdu.

english: Why does my cassava have tall stems and lots of green leaves, but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive shade or too much nitrogen in the soil forces cassava to put all its energy into growing top leaves and stems instead of storing energy in the roots below ground.
ga: Shade babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛkwɛ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli lɛ

english: How do I know when cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: As cassava reaches maturity, the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, the stem becomes thick and woody, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to crack as the roots expand.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my neighbor's crops growing much faster than mine even though we planted in the same month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tsei lɛ daa oya fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu amɛ yɛ nyɔŋ kome mli moŋ?

english: Differences in crop growth often come from using higher-quality seed cuttings, better soil moisture, or planting in areas with more direct sunlight and fertile soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni afolɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ Aloo dumɔ yɛ hei ni hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Is it better to plant my root crops early before the main rainy season begins?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmeii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi?

english: Planting early gives your crops a head start to establish roots, but if the rains pause unexpectedly, heat can dry out stem cuttings before they take root.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ shishifãi afeemɔ mli. Shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ Dɔlɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbi dani amɛwo shishifãi.

english: How does mixing different crops in one field protect my farm from crop failure?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ buɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Intercropping spreads your risk—if one crop suffers from a dry spell or pest attack, the second crop can survive, ensuring you still harvest food and income from your land.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli lɛ gbɛɔ oshara lɛ eshwaa—kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ nyɛ ehi shi. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii kɛ shika kɛjɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of the plant usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed manure will help restore the green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do some of my groundnut pods turn out completely empty when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean pods lɛ ekomɛi efee efolo kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops', happen when the soil lacks calcium during pod formation. Adding agricultural lime or wood ash to your soil during land preparation provides the calcium needed for healthy nuts to grow inside the shells.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pops’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ pods feemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa calcium ni he hiaa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain shoots alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the vital shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it necessary to put strong sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso ni wa awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sunlight while preventing soil-borne fungal diseases from destroying the plant.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛ baai lɛ awo hulu la mli ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni ekafite tsei lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, which also spread plant viruses. Using recommended organic deterrents, like neem oil sprays, helps control these insects and keep leaves expanding normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, ni amɛ hu amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Akɛ nibii ni tsiɔ mɔ naa tamɔ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni eha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are tiny insects destroying all the flowers on my cowpea farm before pods appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite fɔfɔi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cowpea blossoms attract flower thrips and pod borers that feed on flower nectar and young buds. Spraying approved botanical or chemical pest controls right as the plant begins flowering protects the buds so they can develop into full seed pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ gbalaa fɔfɔi thrips kɛ pod borers ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi loo kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ beni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ kɛ dumɔwui.

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates around them in heavy, poorly drained soil, allowing fungi to grow. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to run off, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ adara. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why does my swamp rice crop grow better when there is shallow water kept on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-swamp ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ to ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shallow standing water in rice fields smothers aggressive weeds that try to steal plant food and keeps the soil wet enough for swamp rice roots to easily soak up soil nutrients.
ga: Nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ oya.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant suffers stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Maintaining steady soil moisture through regular watering and spreading dry grass mulching around the roots helps prevent blossom drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ shishifãi ni egbi ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees keep falling over during rainstorms before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches, making them top-heavy and easy for wind to tip over. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy bamboo prop or wooden pole helps hold the tree upright until the bunch fully ripens.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse. Enɛ haa efeɔ tsiimɔ, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ebaagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni mli wa fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi niji lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow from the middle instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential plant food. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea when the plants are knee-high helps them turn green and form large, healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea wo tsei lɛ amli beni amɛshɛɔ amɛkuɛ he pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfee ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why does my lowland rice field need shallow water standing on it while it grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he hiaa nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ́ midu nii lɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates weeds that try to steal food from your rice and keeps the soil cool. Rice roots thrive in wet soil, making it easier for the plant to absorb essential nutrients.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa jwɛi ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛju niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Omɔ shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the dry season? Are my crops dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ? Ani miŋmɔshi nibii miigbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves to save water and protect itself during harsh, dry weather. The roots underground stay alive, and the plant will quickly grow fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni ehiii kwraa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ baahi shi. Ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my yam mounds and give the vines tall stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni maha wain tsei lɛ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi fioo koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into sunlight to generate energy, which sends food down to build large underground tubers. Clearing weeds prevents wild grass from choking the vines and stealing soil nutrients.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. ni tsuɔ niyenii kɛyaa shi koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baatsi koo mli jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi wain tsei lɛ anaa ni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do many of the tiny blossoms on my cocoa trees fall off before forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mi kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers they cannot support. However, if too many fall off, it usually means the trees lack water, need protective shade trees, or are under attack by insects like mirids.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei yɛ fɔfɔi krɛdɛɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛto. Shi, kɛji akɛ ashwie babaoo tsɔ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni tsei aná hulutsoo loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui kɛ afua atutua bo.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever there is a strong wind or heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain stems hold a lot of water weight and have shallow roots. Propping the stems up with sturdy bamboo stakes when heavy bunches form prevents wind from knocking them over before harvest.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nu babaoo nɔ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni wa to tsei lɛ ahe be mli ni jwɛi lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani akpa.

english: Why are my tomato plants flowering well, but the blossoms dry up without making fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gboɔ ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: High temperatures and dry air can heat up tomato flowers, preventing proper pollination and causing flowers to drop. Giving plants light shade and adequate water helps flowers set healthy fruit.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baanyɛ aha tomato fɔfɔi lɛ adɔ. Tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa haa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cabbage and pepper plants have tiny holes all over them after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage kɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? No fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Small holes are caused by caterpillars and beetles that hatch after rains to eat tender leaves. Spraying early with neem water or recommended pest treatments protects leaf foliage.
ga: Buji bibii lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ amli. Neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I avoid applying granular fertilizer to my farm right before a very heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: Heavy rain washes expensive fertilizer away from crop roots into streams before plants can drink it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist so roots absorb it directly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli kɛyaa faai amli dani tsei lɛ nuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are ready to harvest from underground without pulling up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mifolɔɔɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are mature when leaves begin turning yellow and dry. Test by pulling up one plant; if the inside shell has dark markings and seeds fill the skin tightly, it is ready for harvest.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Kaa kɛtsɔ tso kome ni oootsi kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ yɛ okadii diji ni dumɔwui lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why do agricultural officers call fertilizer 'crop medicine', and what does it actually do for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi tsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akɛ ‘tso tsofa’ ni mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer is often called 'medicine' because it cures soil weakness and feeds sick or hungry plants. Just like food and vitamins make people strong, fertilizer gives soil essential nutrients so crops can grow healthy and yield plenty of harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akɛ ‘tsofa’ ejaakɛ etsaa shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ loo hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ niyenii. Taakɛ niyenii kɛ vitamini haa gbɔmɛi he waa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara ni amɛwo ŋmaa babaoo.

english: When is the best time for me to apply crop medicine to my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is early in the rainy season when the soil is damp. Moist soil helps the plant roots swallow the nutrients easily, but avoid applying it right before heavy downpours so it does not get washed away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni okɛbaatsu nii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ he koni ekɛshwie shi.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning pale and yellow even though I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil has run out of nutrients like nitrogen. Your crops are starving and need fertilizer or manure to regain their rich green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Hɔmɔ miiye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛná amɛhe su kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why must I clear all the bushes and weeds before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi fɛɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds removes competition. Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil food away from your young crops, so clearing the land gives your crops all the space and food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa. Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni oootsi lɛ haa onibii lɛ naa hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Leveling the ground makes sure water spreads evenly across your field instead of pooling in deep holes or running off high spots. This keeps all your plants equally hydrated.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔji lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobua ehe naa yɛ bu ni mli kwɔ mli loo ooojɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ, Enɛ haa otsei lɛ fɛɛ náa nu abɔ ni tamɔ amɛhe.

english: Will leveling my land stop rain from washing away my fertilizer?
ga: Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni mafee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baaha nugbɔ akashwie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, flat land slows down running rainwater. On flat ground, water sinks gently into the soil rather than rushing across the surface and sweeping your expensive fertilizer away.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ baa shi. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli blɛoo moŋ fe ni eeefo oya kɛho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ atsu nii.

english: How do I know when a coconut is ready to be planted in the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei eshɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: A coconut nut is ready for planting when you hear water sloshing inside when shaken, and a firm sprout begins pushing out from the top of the husk.
ga: Kokooi efee klalo akɛ abaadu kɛji onu nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ he kɛji akpokpo. ni tsei bibii ni wa bɔi shwiemɔ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: How long will I wait for my newly planted coconut tree to start producing fruits?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ mamɛ ni mi-ŋmei tso ni midu ehee lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Traditional tall coconut trees take about 6 to 8 years to start producing fruit, while dwarf varieties can begin bearing coconuts in just 3 to 4 years if well cared for.
ga: Kusum tsei ni kɛlɛ ni ji ŋmei lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmeii feemɔ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How should I care for my young coconut shoot right after putting it in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Keep the area around the base clean of weeds, ensure it gets full sunlight, water it during dry spells, and protect the soft green shoot from stray animals.
ga: Kwɛmɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Ha shishitoo lɛ he atse ni jwɛi akafee nɔ ko. Kwɛmɔ ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni abuɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ ahe.

english: How can I protect my farm boundary so roaming animals do not eat my young crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe koni kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ akaye miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ?

english: You can protect your field by building simple fences using local materials like bamboo or palm branches, or by planting dense, thorny live hedges along the borders of your farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔji lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ gbogbo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni oootswa lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ mli nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsei aniji ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants grow strong and green. It can also happen when the soil stays too wet for long periods, preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on maize to build up in the ground. Alternating with beans or groundnuts puts good nutrients back into the soil and starves maize pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsake lɛ, ehaa niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmei mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and stunted after heavy rains wash across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa etswa miŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away the top layer of soil where all the good plant food sits, while also soaking the ground so much that roots drown. Making raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water run off safely without taking your topsoil with it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baanyɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji tsei niyenii jɛɛhe ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho nu. Gɔŋ lɛ loo ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ ni awoɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ shweshweeshwe ni ejieee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are like tender human babies that burn easily under full sunlight and dry winds. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains or shade trees to cover them and keep the soil moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii tamɔ abifabii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same nutrients and water in the ground. Removing the extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the plant to produce larger and heavier bunches.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Tsoi lɛ fɛɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni no baaha tso lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How long does it take for cassava stems to start forming big tubers under the ground after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most cassava varieties in Ghana spend their first three to four months growing leaves and stems above ground. The underground roots only start swelling into big tubers from the fifth month onward, taking about 9 to 12 months for full harvest.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani amɛbaa kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bulbs wuji kɛjɛɔ nyɔŋ ni ji enumɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa. Aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani anyɛɔ akpaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to lift up my yam vines and tie them onto tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso nɔ ni mikɛfi tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high off the ground to catch direct sunlight, which the plant uses to make food. Lifting the vines on stakes ensures the leaves get enough sun to send energy down into building thick, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa eniyenii lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ awó wein tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ baa shi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Weed seeds are already sleeping deep in the soil and are very tough, so they sprout immediately when clearing opens the ground to sunlight and rain. Clearing weeds early prevents them from drinking up water and food meant for your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ momo ni amɛhe wa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni atse lɛ ha hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkanu nu kɛ niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ.

english: What makes the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ tomato?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without producing fruit when the weather becomes extremely hot or when the soil goes completely dry. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the root zone helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and causing the plant to stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni eha tso lɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or mites are hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juice. Inspecting the undersides of leaves and treating them early keeps the plant healthy and producing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shito baai ni ekpɛtɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo mites, kɛ amɛhe etee baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiinu tso lɛ nu. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni otsa amɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there are no big trees or plantains planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides crucial shade and keeps the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it grows strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnáa la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves is a sign that the plant is short on nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant takes whatever nitrogen it has from its older bottom leaves and sends it to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ Abele tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni amɛyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ, baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛmajeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and turning small and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni eyɛ bibii ni ewa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like mites or thrips sucking the juice from the leaves, or by a virus spread by insects. Checking the undersides of leaves early and applying proper pest control stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ mra. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of bright yellow flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from dry to wet too suddenly. Extreme heat or water stress stops the flower from pollinating itself, causing it to drop before fruit can grow.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli trukaa tsɔ lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature and ready under the ground without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare main stem, and the ground around the base of the plant starts to crack from the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kwraa beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ashiɔ tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne titri lɛ efolo. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food. When the vine climbs a stake, the leaves capture more light, which sends energy down into the root to grow large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baaná la babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds the maize growing alongside them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ yeɔ nii.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain, they compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves enough energy for the main stem to yield a big bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome fa tsɔ. Ekɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ plantains babaoo.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first shower of rain in the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell before the main rainy season fully establishes. Planting too early can cause the seeds to germinate and then dry up and die from lack of continuous moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kwraa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ ehiɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak even when I plant good quality seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil water, plant food (nutrients), and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures that your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow tall and produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ nu, tsei aniyenii (nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ), kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves lose water too quickly and burn. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides natural cover and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa grows.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eshã. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient needed for green growth. Adding organic manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps restore the green color and boosts growth.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know which way to put my cassava stem cutting into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole bɔ ni afoɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems have small raised buds (eyes) along the stalk where leaves will sprout. When planting, make sure these buds are pointing upwards toward the sky so the shoots can grow straight out of the ground.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Tso lɛ nɔ ji he ni baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ. Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, kwɛmɔ ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the funnel of the plant to feed on tender young leaves. Applying organic neem leaf spray or recommended pest control early stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei akui amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Organic neem baa spray loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋaawoo. Abaatsi amɛnaa mra. dani ekpãtãa ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turn dark brown and rot before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: This rot on the bottom of tomatoes is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular soil moisture. Keeping the soil evenly watered and adding compost helps the plant absorb calcium and prevents rotten fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (called mulching) acts like an umbrella for the soil. It traps moisture so you water less, keeps the root zone cool in hot weather, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ umbrella kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Emɔɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to produce large tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up toward the sun and keeps them off the wet ground where leaf diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no ji he ni tsei lɛ ahe hela gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does my land yield less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the land time to recover. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the roots of my crops turn soft and rot when heavy rain flooded my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. When heavy rains leave standing water for days, the soil gets waterlogged, suffocating the roots and causing them to decay.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ta shi gbii babaoo lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboɔ.

english: Weeds are native wild plants that are naturally adapted to compete aggressively for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds early in the season prevents them from crowding out your young crops and stealing their food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkɛ hulu la akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Nu Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ baatsi otsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe ni amɛkaju amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the dry season comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and strong sunlight. They require shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young trees until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli baawo wu.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ dani akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and become top-heavy as the fruit bunch grows. Planting the suckers deep enough and trimming off extra side suckers keeps the plant stable and prevents wind from knocking it over.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni amɛkui lɛ daraa lɛ. Aduɔ tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni afoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ afã lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ lɛ shi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and curl up even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants are delicate and easily affected by heat and tiny insects like whiteflies that spread viruses. Overwatering or insect attacks cause the leaves to curl, so you need to inspect them closely and protect them early with proper pest control.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni hulutsoo kɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ashwã lɛ baanyɛ aná amɛnɔ hewalɛ oya. Nu babaoo loo kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni obu amɛhe mra. Kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ ni sa nɔ

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress, lack of nutrients, or attacks by tiny insects. Mulching around the base keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the plant hold its flowers to produce fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ trukaa, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tutua amɛ. Mulching around Shishitoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Ehaa tsei hiɛɔ fɔfɔi amli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are small holes appearing all over the leaves of my garden egg plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ekɛ ehe miitswa yɛ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf-chewing beetles and caterpillars love to feed on garden egg leaves. Since missing leaves prevent the plant from making food, you must check under the leaves regularly and remove pests or apply protective sprays.
ga: Ladybugs kɛ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe baai. Yɛ baai ni elaaje lɛ hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii. Esa akɛ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ hela lɛ atsu nii loo okɛ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ atsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tips mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is its main food. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK around the roots gives the crop the energy it needs to stay green and produce full cobs.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa, ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK fata shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my lowland rice field need standing water around the plants during growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ aná nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle ehe lɛ? Tso yɛ dalɛ be mli?

english: Standing water smothers weeds that try to steal food from the rice and provides the constant moisture rice needs to develop heavy, full grain heads.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ jwɛi ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ naa nu ni he hiaa lɛ be fɛɛ be koni ekɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ aba.

english: Can I just plant cassava sticks in the ground and leave them to grow without clearing weeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mahã eda ni mikɛ jwɛi akajie?

english: While cassava is a tough crop, aggressive weeds will steal soil nutrients and shade the young shoots during the first three months, which severely reduces the size and number of tubers you harvest later.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei ji tso ko ni wa akɛ aaakwɛ moŋ, shi jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha bulb ni obaakpa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ dalɛ kɛ amɛyibɔ ​​aba shi waa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to produce energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to direct its energy into growing large underground tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni oha tsei kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push thin stems down into the dirt after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ etso bibioo lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts bloom above the ground, but after pollination, the plant sends down special stems called 'pegs' into the soil where the actual nuts grow and mature safely underground.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ Tso lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant plantain trees next to our young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Wɔ kookoo tso bibioo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on nitrogen from the soil, leaving it weak. Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ha egbɔjɔ Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen or getting choked by too much standing water. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo amɛyɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants droop in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛji He ni esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can draw it from the ground. Drooping is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from drying out, and leaves usually bounce back when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Foi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he koni ekagbi. Ni baai lɛ fɔɔ sɛɛkuu kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to make big mounds of earth before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa shikpɔŋ wulu ko dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand and grow deep underground. Large mounds loosen the soil so tubers grow big and smooth while keeping the roots safely above waterlogged ground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Gɔji wuji haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops much more than they harm mature crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ awui fe bɔ ni amɛyeɔ tsei ni eda lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and few leaves, so weeds easily steal their sunlight, water, and plant food. Once crops grow tall and wide, their own shadow blocks sunlight and naturally stops weeds from growing.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai fioo. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ tsei aniyenii oya. Beni tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛdaraa lɛ Amɛ shade lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks nutrients. Keeping the ground evenly moist and covered with mulch helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the stem funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the growing tip of the plant. Spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extracts directly into the leaf funnel early on stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem baa mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ awoɔ baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii akpãtãmɔ.

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower stem leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground right around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains get eaten by insects even when kept in bags inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi yeɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ? Akɛwo kotoku mli yɛ mitsu lɛ mli?

english: Weevils hatch from tiny eggs already on the grain or crawl in through loosely woven bags. Drying seeds thoroughly until they are hard and storing them in sealed, airtight hermetic bags suffocates insects and keeps grain safe.
ga: Moths fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ wɔji bibii amli. momo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ Aloo tsɔ kotoku ko ni akpɛ́ ni etse ehe lɛ mli. Agbiɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate roots that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a natural umbrella that shields young cocoa from scorching sun and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ baa. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong winds before the fruit bunches mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani aduawai akui lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems. Without proper earthing up (mounding soil around the base) or planting them close enough to act as windbreaks for each other, strong winds easily uproot them under the weight of growing fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ kpakpa bɛ (Shikpɔŋ ni abua naa kɛbɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he) loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bɔ ni sa koni etsu nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsimɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ oya yɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe muji lɛ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil needed for green growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots or waterlogs the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hole niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli loo nu afua ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots become soft and watery if I dig them up right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji mifo amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots absorb excess water rapidly during heavy rainfall, which lowers their starch content and increases moisture inside the tuber. Harvesting immediately after heavy rain makes the tubers spoil quickly and lose their firm texture.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛ́ akpa nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛhe feɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put up tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce food that gets stored underground as large tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, which boosts tuber growth and prevents leaves from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni akɛto shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii wuji amli. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tuber lɛ daa, ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why can rice plants survive in flooded fields while my maize plants rot and die in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have hollow spaces in their stems that carry oxygen from the air down to their roots under water. Maize plants lack these internal air tubes, so standing water smothers their roots and causes them to drown.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abɛi tsei bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa efoɔ nu lɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or lack of soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to conserve energy and survive the stress instead of trying to feed new fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi yɛ haomɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okɛ aduawai heei aba

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, mites, or thrips, or by a virus spread by these insects. The feeding damages the young leaf tissues as they expand, causing them to twist and wrinkle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo thrips, loo helai ni kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Niyenii fiteɔ baa bibii lɛ amli fãji beni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil richer for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful bacteria in the soil to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, that captured nitrogen remains in the soil as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite Nitrogen ni aŋɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to water my crops early in the morning instead of at noon when it is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ mitsei lɛ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning lets plant roots absorb moisture before the hot sun causes it to evaporate into the air. Watering at noon wastes water to evaporation and can heat up the topsoil, stressing the delicate roots.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa efoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Nu ni oooha yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛkɛ. ni ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli adɔ waa Okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green and strong. It can also happen if heavy rains have washed nutrients out of the root zone or logged the soil with too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifã lɛ mli lɛ loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu tsɔ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests that feed on maize to multiply in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ajieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ayiɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die during the hot Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ Harmattan hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots that dry out quickly under intense sun and dusty Harmattan winds. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to trap moisture and block direct sunlight during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass and leaves around the stems of their vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai shwieɔ amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ? Amɛ aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry organic material, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool under hot heat, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching ni ebɔle tsei ahe Kɛ nibii ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha tsei lɛ ahe. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits around them for too long in heavy, poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push small shoots down into the dirt after their flowers fall off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miitsi ŋmeii bibii lɛ? kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni fɔfɔi lɛ egbee shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnut plants form their seeds underground. After the flowers are pollinated, the plant grows small stems called pegs that naturally push themselves down into the soil where the groundnut pods can safely develop.
ga: Peanut tsei woɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ tso bibioo ko. atsɛɔ lɛ pins Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ adara shweshweeshwe yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there tiny caterpillars eating holes into the inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the growing central leaves of maize plants. Catching them early with recommended safe insecticides or natural treatments prevents them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing green tomatoes turning black and flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli ni miida lɛ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is usually blossom-end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium while the fruit is forming. It is often caused by irregular watering rather than an infectious insect or disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miiwo yibii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be moŋ fe kooloi loo helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain stem forces them to fight for water, sunlight, and food. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ Ni anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu amɛtao nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii, ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce a small harvest even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves in your farm because their roots are fast and aggressive. They steal fertilizers, soil moisture, and light before your main crops have a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa oya ni amɛhe wa. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ la dani onibii titrii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Heavy rain can wash nutrients out of the soil, or the soil simply needs animal manure or fertilizer to help the plants make food and turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo ani kooloi ashishifã he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛfee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally pull air into the soil and turn it into food that plants need. Planting them near maize feeds the soil for free, helping your maize grow taller and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts gbalaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛfeɔ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.
