english: Why does my maize grow tall and skinny and fall over easily when wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ, efoɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the stalks compete for sunlight and grow thin and weak trying to reach the top. Giving plants enough space lets stems grow thick and strong.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛshɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ oha tso lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee shiŋŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to save water inside its stem and roots. The plant is not dead; it is sleeping to stay alive and will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains start.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni egbiɔ koni nu ahi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ewɔɔ koni ehi shi. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Watering your tomatoes regularly and giving them light shade helps keep the flowers on the stem.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Okɛ nu awo tomatoi lɛ amli daa ni oha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do dark, watery spots appear on my tomato leaves right after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii diji ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-tomato baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Rain splashes dirt onto the lower leaves, spreading small fungal germs that love wet weather. Plucking off the lowest leaves near the ground prevents dirt splashing onto the foliage.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ muji nɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni sumɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ baa Kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni muji akabote baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to make food. When you lift the vines onto wooden poles, the leaves get more light, which sends more energy underground to grow larger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ hulu la ashɛ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni akɛhoo nii. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baaná la babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekwɛ yitsei wuji.

english: Why does my plantain farm yield small bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ashiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ

english: Too many young shoots around one plantain stem fight each other for the same water and food in the soil. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only one strong sucker to feed the main tree, resulting in much bigger bunches.
ga: Tsobii bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Plantain tsei komekomei babaoo tsɔ baawuu amɛhe koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tsei kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baaye abua tso titri lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji niji ni dara kwraa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees burn and die when planted in an open field without big trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei wuji bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot survive hot, direct sunlight all day. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a canopy that shields cocoa leaves from scorching heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects sucking juice from the underside of the leaf or by a virus carried by insects. Keeping weeds out of the farm prevents insects from hiding near your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni ŋmeii lɛ hiɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Can I use ordinary sawdust from the timber mill to grow my crops instead of soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ atsu nii ni mikɛdu tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ najiaŋ?

english: Fresh sawdust can be used as a growing medium or mulch, but it needs to decay or be mixed with animal manure first. Raw sawdust absorbs nitrogen from the soil, which can starve young crops if added directly.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ tsei ahe ŋmɔtɔ hee atsu nii akɛ dumɔ nii loo ŋmɔtɔ. Shi esa akɛ egbo loo akɛ kooloi afɔfɔi afutu mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Sawdust ni ŋmɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ kɛji akɛ akɛfata he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do some farmers spread sawdust around the roots of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmeii shwieɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Sawdust is used as mulch to shade the soil from the harsh sun, retain moisture around the crop roots, and suppress weed growth on the farm.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe ni etsiɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Is it possible to grow crops in local waste materials around the house if I do not have enough farm land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ maŋ lɛ mli jwɛi nibii ni yɔɔ mishia lɛ he lɛ atsu nii kɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mibɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Yes, many vegetables and fungi can be grown in bags or containers filled with composted waste like sawdust, cocoa husks, or dry leaves mixed with good topsoil.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu aduawai kɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ kotokui loo tsɛnsii ni akɛ sũ ni akɛwo mli tamɔ ŋmeii, kookoo ŋmeii, loo baai ni egbi ni akɛ ŋwɛi sũ kpakpa efutu mli lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do crops like cassava and plantain not produce seeds for me to collect and plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmei kɛ plantain wooo dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Certain crops reproduce vegetatively rather than through flowers and seeds. They are propagated by taking stem cuttings or root suckers from healthy mother plants and putting them directly into the ground.
ga: Tsei komɛi baanyɛ afɔ́ kɛtsɔ fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui anɔ. Amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ fɔlɔ tso ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shishifãi loo ŋmeii ni amɛfoɔ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: If a crop does not bear seeds, how can I multiply it for the next planting season?
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ dumɔwui Te mafee tɛŋŋ magbɛ eshwa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You multiply seedless plants by harvesting specific vegetative parts such as stem cuttings, tubers, or young suckers that grow around the base of the main plant.
ga: Ogbɛɔ tsei ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ ashwãa kɛtsɔ tso lɛ fãi pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ tsei niji, ŋmeii bibii, loo ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ ni oookpa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do mushrooms grow when they do not have seeds like maize or beans?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii akwɛ̃ be mli ni dumɔwui bɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Mushrooms are fungi rather than typical flowering plants, so they do not produce seeds. They grow from microscopic spores that feed on moist organic materials like rotted sawdust, straw, or animal manure.
ga: Mushroom ji fungi babaoo fe tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi. no hewɔ lɛ ekɛ dumɔwui baaa Amɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ nibii ni mli ewo fɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbo, jwɛi loo ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant my seeds directly into fresh animal dung to make them grow faster?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: No, fresh animal dung produces high heat and strong ammonia that can burn seeds and tender roots. It should be left to rot and compost properly before mixing it with your soil.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii heei haa dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ammonia ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui kɛ shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ baa. Esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbo ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ dani akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afutu.

english: Why do my crops grow stronger green leaves when I add composted animal manure to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ baa lɛ baa eŋɔli ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Composted animal manure is rich in natural nitrogen, which is the primary nutrient crops use to build green leaves, strong stems, and healthy plant bodies.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli tsotso ni wa kɛ tso gbɔmɔtso ni wa.

english: Why is my crop producing plenty of healthy green leaves but no fruits or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi aduawai loo dumɔwui ko bɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil can cause plants to put all their energy into leaves instead of fruits. Plants also need adequate sunlight, balanced nutrients like phosphorus, and insect pollination to set fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ awo baai lɛ amli yɛ aduawai lɛ najiaŋ. Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa hu he miihia tsei. Niyenii ni ja tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ koni ekɛwo aduawai.

english: Why do some crops die completely after producing fruit once, while others keep fruiting every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi gboiɔ kwraa kɛ́ amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii daa afi lɛ?

english: Annual crops put all their stored energy into making seeds once to finish their life cycle, while perennial crops store energy in their roots and stems to survive and produce fruit across multiple seasons.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ dumɔwu kome ni ekɛgbeɔ ewala shihilɛ naa. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ toɔ hewalɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ.

english: Why do vegetables like tomatoes grow faster and yield better inside a greenhouse structure compared to my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai tamɔ tomatoi lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ greenhouse gbɛjianɔtoo mli kɛ akɛto miŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Inside a protective structure, vegetables are shielded from harsh sunlight, heavy rains, and insect pests. This controlled environment reduces stress on the crops, allowing them to focus all their energy on growing bigger and producing fruit faster.
ga: mligbɛ nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ Abuɔ aduawai ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ nɛɛ haa nɔnyɛɛ ni baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa bɔ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ nii oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves turn yellow and drop off during the very hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Excessive heat causes pepper plants to lose water faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. Dropping their leaves is the plant's natural self-defense to conserve moisture and keep from drying out completely.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa chili tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni ekɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Why do whiteflies attack my vegetable crops more during dry and warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛji tutuaa mi-vegetables lɛ babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be baa lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures speed up the life cycle of whiteflies, allowing them to multiply very quickly. They are attracted to fresh green leaves to suck the plant sap, which weakens the crop and spreads viral diseases.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii yɛji lɛ ashihilɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa amɛfɔɔ bii oya waa. Amɛsumɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ eshwaa.

english: How can I tell if my tomato crops are getting too much water or not enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato lɛ miihe nu babaoo loo eshɛɛɛ nu he?

english: When tomato plants don't get enough water, their leaves wilt and roll inward to conserve moisture. When they get too much water, their roots choke from a lack of air, causing lower leaves to turn yellow and roots to rot.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaabɔle amɛhe kɛya mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛ́ onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close together in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition makes the plants grow tall and thin with weak stems, producing fewer and smaller vegetables.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa aduawai ni anáa lɛ faaa ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why are the flowers on my cucumber plants falling off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi kukumba tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Cucumber flowers drop off if they are not pollinated by insects, or if the plant suffers from sudden heat stress or irregular watering. Without pollination or sufficient moisture, the crop cannot afford the energy to form fruit.
ga: Kukumba fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollination loo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Crops nyɛŋ aha hewalɛ ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale green leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build green leaf tissue. Without enough nitrogen, the plant cannot manufacture its food efficiently.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do dark, wet spots appear on my tomato leaves right after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Rain splashing on the ground bounces soil-borne fungal spores onto the leaves. The damp conditions on the wet leaves create the perfect environment for these spores to grow and cause fungal diseases like blight.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ anɔ kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why does picking my sweet peppers regularly make the plant keep producing more peppers for a longer time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ ni akpaa daa lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ peppers babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: A crop's main natural goal is to mature seeds inside its fruit. When you harvest ripe fruits regularly, you signal to the plant that its reproductive work isn't done, prompting it to produce new flowers and more fruit.
ga: Oti titri ni ma ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ ji ni ekwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji okpa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ daa lɛ Otsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ fɔmɔ egbeko naa lolo. Tswaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi heei ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wilt and struggle when I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔi ŋmɔlɔ beni mijieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings experience 'transplant shock' when their roots are disturbed and suddenly exposed to stronger sunlight and winds. Gradually exposing them to direct sun before moving them helps them adjust smoothly.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baaná ‘Transplant shock’ ni baa kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ gbala amɛnaa ni trukaa lɛ, hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fe tsutsu lɛ ba amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ dani oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it good for me to burn my farm land before planting new crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu tsei heei?

english: Burning clears land quickly, but it destroys essential organic nutrients in the topsoil and kills beneficial organisms like earthworms. Clearing without fire and leaving organic material to decay keeps your soil rich and holds moisture better for your crops.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ. ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni la bɛ mli ni oshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbo lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee nii babaoo ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I need to change the type of crop I plant on my plot every season instead of sticking to cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsake tsei srɔtoi ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa afi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe akpɛtɛ ŋmei he?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases tailored to that crop to build up in the dirt. Rotating your crops keeps the soil balanced and reduces pest infestations naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni etsɔ tso lɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying balanced fertilizer like NPK or adding well-rotted animal manure will supply nitrogen and help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen afata he ni eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Wrinkled or curling leaves are often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that feed on the plant and spread viruses. Spraying your pepper plants with neem oil solution or insecticidal soap helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ tsei ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to allow sunlight and airflow into your cocoa farm helps keep the pods dry and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa plants from heat and keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and allowing beneficial insects like bees into your farm will help flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ ooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni oha kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ ni amɛye omanye.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your young crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to plant food so they can grow strong roots and mature faster.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ náa tsei niyenii kwraa. Koni shishifãi lɛ awa ni amɛdara oya

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. Look for lower leaves naturally turning yellow and falling off, along with visible cracking in the soil around the base of the stem caused by enlarging roots underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Taomɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ mligbalamɔ Visible stem base Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Supporting the stems with sturdy wooden or bamboo forks helps prop up the plants and prevents wind from knocking them down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Ha amɛfee nɔ ni tsii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei ni mli wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efi tso lɛ sɛɛ, ni ebaatsi enaa koni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa lɛ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but very few of them actually turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects like midges or human assistance through hand pollination to transfer pollen from flower to flower. If there are no pollinators around or weather conditions stop them, the unpollinated flowers simply dry up and fall off without producing pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi biɔ kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, loo adesa yelikɛbuamɔ kɛtsɔ nine nɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi lɛ ajɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ he fɛɛ he loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them directly under full sunlight without any big trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and burn easily under direct sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates living shade umbrellas that protect young cocoa leaves and help soil retain moisture during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot on the branches during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This rotting is caused by a fungal attack known as Black Pod disease, which thrives in overly damp and humid conditions. Weeding regularly and cutting back overgrown branches lets sunlight and air dry out the farm to prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛ fɔmɔ kotoku ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ mli. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo fe nine yɔɔ mli. Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli daa kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are small insects sucking on my cocoa pods and making the young shoots dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miinu mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni amɛmiigbi ŋmɔji bibii lɛ?

english: These are likely mirids (capsids), which are harmful insects that pierce cocoa pods and branches to suck out sap. Spraying recommended insecticides at the right times during the year keeps these pests from destroying your leaves and crop harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji mirids (capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔji kɛ tsei aniji amli koni amɛnu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ bei ni sa mli yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe tsei kɛ amɛkpamɔ.

english: Why should I cut off good-looking branches from my cocoa tree when it seems healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tso nine ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess branches, water shoots, and diseased wood so the tree does not waste energy on extra leaves. Instead, the tree directs its food and water straight into growing larger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Tsoi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji, tsei ashishifãi, kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, tsei ɔmɛ ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ nyu kɛ yaa kookoo tso nɛ a he wa nɛ a ngɛ he wami ɔ mi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I tell if the soil in my farm is running out of nutrients for my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ?

english: When soil loses its strength, crop leaves often turn yellow, trees grow very slowly, and pod sizes remain tiny. Applying approved cocoa fertilizers returns essential food like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium back into the soil.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he wa lɛ sɛɛ fo lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa. ni pod lɛ dalɛ ji bibioo lolo Kɛji akɛ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus kɛ potassium aba. Kuu osɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Can I plant heavy feeder crops like cassava close to my cocoa trees, or will it harm them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tsei ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ kookoo tsei ahe? Aloo ebaaye kookoo tso lɛ awui loo ebaayeee lɛ awui?

english: Cassava roots grow aggressively and take away large amounts of water and nutrients from the soil, which can starve nearby cocoa trees. It is better to use lighter shade crops like plantains or legumes that do not compete as fiercely for soil food.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha hɔmɔ aye cacao tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tamɔ plantains loo legumes, ni kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akaŋ lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why does letting tall weeds grow on my farm reduce my total crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kakadaji ni mihaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients directly from your cocoa trees. They also create cool, dark hideouts for destructive farm pests and fungal diseases to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ o-cocoa tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛfeɔ hei ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ duŋ hu koni ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Dry Harmattan winds quickly pull moisture out of both leaves and the ground, causing water stress in trees. Leaving dead leaves as mulch around the base of the trees helps trap ground moisture and protects roots during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ oya. Enɛ haa nu he haomɔ baa tsei amli. Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egboi akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Traditional cocoa trees take about 3 to 5 years to start producing fruit, while improved hybrid varieties can begin fruiting in as little as 2 to 3 years if properly cared for.
ga: Kusum mli cacao tsei lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei sɔrɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow better when I water them late at night or early in the morning instead of during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo waa kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa moŋ fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When you water during the hot afternoon, heat causes most of the moisture to evaporate into the air before roots can absorb it, and hot leaves can suffer stress. Watering at night or early morning allows the water to soak deep into the soil so roots can drink freely without losing moisture to the hot sun.
ga: Beni okɛ nu woɔ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ haa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ. Ni baai ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha mɔ aná haomɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu nu ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa amɛhe afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt during the middle of the day even when the soil around them still feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Enuɔ he lolo akɛ edɔ.

english: During peak heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to close its pores and reduce water loss to protect itself, and it normally bounces back as the day cools down.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ ehe ŋmeii lɛ anaa yɛ be kukuoo mli ni ehaa nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu ehe he. Ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji edɔ.

english: Will spraying water directly onto my young crop seedlings with a high-pressure hose harm them?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛ hose ni mli wa waa shwieɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye dumɔwui lɛ awui?

english: Yes, high water pressure can tear delicate leaves, wash away topsoil, and damage or dislodge fragile young roots. It is best to direct water gently around the base of the plant or use a sprinkler attachment to simulate soft rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli wa lɛ baanyɛ agbala baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni efite loo eha shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ agbo Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ nu afɔ tso lɛ shishi fioo loo okɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛfee nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ he mfoniri.

english: Is underground borehole water always safe to pour directly onto my crops during dry spells?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe be fɛɛ be akɛ aaafɔse miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Borehole water is generally good, but some underground sources contain high levels of salts or minerals that can build up in the soil over time. If you notice a white crust on top of your soil or leaves turning yellow, the water may need testing or treatment before heavy use.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ nubu mli lɛ hi. Shi ŋmeii loo nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ni baanyɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛji ona ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ekolɛ ehe baahia ni aka nu lɛ akwɛ loo atsu he nii dani akɛtsu nii waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops starting to turn yellow after I switched to watering them from a newly dug well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni mitsake kɛtee nu ni jɛ nubu ko ni atsa ehee lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Water from new wells can sometimes carry excessive minerals, high acidity, or salty compounds dissolved from deeper soil layers. These minerals can lock up soil nutrients, making it hard for the crop roots to feed properly until the water quality is tested and balanced.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ nubui heei amli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni minerals babaoo yɔɔ mli. Nibii ni yɔɔ acid loo ŋmei babaoo ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli Nɛkɛ tɛi nɛɛ baanyɛ ato niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaaha tsei shishifãi lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi be mli ni aka nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ akwɛ ni akwɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Can using stagnant water left open in storage tanks for weeks cause diseases on my crop leaves?
ga: Ani nu ni damɔ shi ni ashi ni agbele yɛ nutoohe ko mli otsii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha hela aba mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, stagnant water exposed to air can breed harmful fungi and bacteria. Splashing this contaminated water onto plant leaves can lead to leaf spots, blights, and stem rot, so it is safer to keep storage containers covered and apply water directly to the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni damɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Nu ni mli ewo muji ni akɛshwieɔ tso baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmeii kɛ tso lɛ shishi ŋmeii aba. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oooha tsɛnsi lɛ nɔ ni okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do deep-rooted crops like cassava survive long dry spells much better than crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei tamɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cassava grows deep tuber roots that store moisture and reach water buried far below the surface. Maize has shallow roots that rely mostly on topsoil, which dries out quickly under the hot sun when rain stops.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni enáa nu ni afu yɛ shishi lɛ. Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni damɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ babaoo. Amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa pɛ.

english: How can I tell if I am giving my vegetable crops too much water from my irrigation pump?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo miiha mitsei lɛ kɛjɛ mi-irrigation pɔmp lɛ mli?

english: Overwatered crops often show soft, yellowing leaves, stunted growth, and muddy soil that smells sour. When soil stays constantly soaked, roots cannot get oxygen and begin to rot, causing the plant to starve despite the abundance of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu babaoo yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ jieɔ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ji ŋmɔŋ, kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kpo. kɛ muji ni shãa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ po.

english: Why do my fertilizers seem to stop working after I heavily flood my crop beds with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-fertilizer lɛ kpaɔ nitsumɔ beni mikɛ nu ewo miŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy flooding causes a process called leaching, where excessive water washes plant nutrients deep past the root zone where crops cannot reach them. Applying water in controlled, moderate amounts keeps fertilizers right where roots feed.
ga: Nu afua ni naa wa lɛ kɛ nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching baa. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Nu ni akudɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi he ni shishifãi lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: What simple action can I take to keep my farm soil moist longer so I don't have to pump water every day?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni mikɛ nu awo pɔmpi mli daa gbi.

english: Covering the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or fallen leaves—a practice called mulching—acts like a protective blanket. Mulch blocks direct sunlight from hitting the soil, drastically slowing down water evaporation.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ni okɛbaabɔle he lɛ Okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Mulch tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why should I prune my cocoa trees before spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao lɛ mli dani mikɛwo mli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy and removes infected branches so air can flow easily. This allows the medicine to reach all parts of the tree and work much better to control diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsofa lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe, ni etsuɔ ​​nitsumɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ hela lɛ nɔyeli mli.

english: What happens if I ignore a small disease on my cocoa tree and leave it to grow larger?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji miku mihiɛ mishwie hela bibioo ko nɔ? yɛ cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni eha eda?

english: If a disease is allowed to grow larger, it becomes very serious and difficult to control. It will quickly spread to other healthy trees and destroy your farm yield.
ga: Kɛji aŋmɛ hela lɛ gbɛ ni egbɛ eshwa Ebaafee basabasa ni ewa akɛ abaaye nɔ. Ebaagbɛ eshwa tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can I just apply medicine to my crops without clearing out excess branches first?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ ni mikɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ tsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Applying medicine without pruning first is ineffective because thick leaves block the chemical from reaching hidden areas where disease and pests live, wasting your effort and money.
ga: Tsofa lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni akpaaa tsei lɛ ahe klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ tsuuu nii ejaakɛ tso lɛ yibii ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ tsofa lɛ naa koni ekashɛ hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa ofiteɔ hewalɛ kɛ shika.

english: How does cutting off diseased branches help the medicine do its job?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsofa lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii?

english: Cutting off diseased branches stops the sickness from spreading to new shoots and reduces the strength of the disease, allowing the medicine to easily protect the remaining healthy parts of the plant.
ga: Niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafolɔ Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei heei amli. ni ehaa hela lɛ mli walɛ baa shi Enɛ haa tsofa lɛ buɔ tso lɛ fãi ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe mlɛo.

english: What is the best month for me to start pruning my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mabɔi kookoo tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: The main pruning for cocoa is usually done around July and August. This timing helps prepare the trees for the main crop harvest and reduces disease build-up before the pods mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ kookoo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ July kɛ August aaafee. Be nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni esaa tso lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ, ni ehaa helai ni buaa ehe naa lɛ baa shi dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why is pruning considered an essential step in taking care of cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni afoɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni he hiaa waa yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or unnecessary stems so the tree can direct its nutrients into healthy pods. It also allows sunlight to reach the leaves and dries up dampness that causes crop diseases.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli. Ehaa hulu la hu shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe ni egbiɔ nu ni kɛ helai baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know when it is the right time of year to prune my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ mafolɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei lɛ?

english: Pruning timing depends on the rain patterns and crop growth. For cocoa in Ghana, starting your main pruning work around July and August after the early rains helps keep the farm healthy.
ga: Be ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Kɛha kookoo yɛ Ghana Kɛ́ aje ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ shishi yɛ July kɛ August mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When do the main rains usually start for farming in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be nugbɔ titri lɛ fɔɔ shishijee kɛha okwaayeli yɛ Ghana?

english: The major rainy season typically starts around March and April, which signals the beginning of fresh crop growth and increased farm activity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ March kɛ April aaafee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ebɔi shweremɔ kɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔ ni yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do crop diseases spread faster when the rains begin in March and April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ je shishi yɛ March kɛ April mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater creates damp conditions and splatters spores from plant to plant. This high moisture allows fungal and bacterial diseases to grow rapidly if the farm is not well-managed.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni tso lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo be ni fa nɛɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ oya kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What work should I start doing on my cocoa farm once the March rains begin?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔ esa akɛ mabɔi nitsumɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni March nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: When the March rains start, cocoa trees begin putting out new growth. You should start basic farm maintenance, monitor for early signs of disease, and prepare your field for seasonal maintenance.
ga: Beni nugbɔ jeɔ shishi ehaa yɛ March mli lɛ Cocoa tso lɛ hu bɔi shweremɔ hee. Esa akɛ oje shishi kɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ shishijee. Kwɛmɔ hela okadii mra ni osaa oyale kɛha be mli saamɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow thin and weak, resulting in small ears with fewer grains rather than a big harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa toi bibii ni dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa yɛ ŋmaa babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts in the same farm with my maize makes the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen air into the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural food supply for nearby maize, helping it grow greener and stronger without needing as much artificial fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Ye obua ni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo afee.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when heavy rains flood my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When water sits on the field for too long, the soil runs out of air and the roots drown. Without breathing roots, the maize cannot drink nitrogen from the soil, causing the green leaves to turn yellow from starvation.
ga: Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi. Abɛi nyɛŋ anu nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji shishifãi lɛ mumɔ bɛ mli. Ehaa baai eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees scorch and die if I don't leave big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mishiii tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and sensitive like babies; direct tropical sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Shade trees act like living umbrellas that cool the air and protect the young leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛhe yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ gbekɛ tsei. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai, ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni amɛbuɔ baai bibii ahe.

english: Dropping leaves during Harmattan is cassava's natural defense mechanism to save water. Plants lose water through their leaves, so shedding them keeps the plant alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmeii ahe koni ekɛbu nu he. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around my cassava tubers early instead of waiting until harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ amli mra lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e he hia nɛ ma mɛ kɛ ya si ngma kpami be ɔ.

english: Weeds steal the water, manure, and sunlight that your cassava needs during its early growing stage. Clearing them early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes straight into making large cassava tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmei kɛ hulu la ni ŋmei he hiaa yɛ eshishijee dalɛ be mli lɛ. Ni ajieɔ mra Ebaakwɛ koni kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya tɛ̃ɛ kɛya ŋmei shishifãi babaoo afeemɔ mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the plant. Lifting the vines up on tall sticks catches maximum sunlight, which feeds the plant and allows the underground tubers to swell much larger.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nine ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or when tiny insects fail to pollinate them. Consistent watering during hot spells helps flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ba tso lɛ nɔ. Enyɛŋ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do tiny holes appear on my pepper leaves after the main rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Rainfall encourages tender green growth, which attracts hungry leaf-eating insects like beetles and caterpillars. Checking under the leaves early helps you spot these pests before they eat the whole plant.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ baai ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Baai lɛ ashishi kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni ona nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛye tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn black with mold when stored inside bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: If maize is bagged before the grains are fully dry, hidden moisture gets trapped inside the warm bag. That trapped moisture causes mold to grow and rot the grain, so sun-drying until grains are bone-dry is essential.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ wo kotoku mli dani ŋmeii lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ boteɔ kotoku ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he miihia waa.

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young maize foliage. Applying recommended control methods early into the leaf funnels where they hide prevents them from destroying your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Kɛboteɔ baai lɛ amli he ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in heavy rain and high shade. Pruning dense branches to allow sunlight in and removing infected pods helps keep the tree healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tso lɛ he tsei ni afoɔ waa koni hulu la babaoo aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes curling up and getting yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by using stem cuttings from sick plants. Using disease-resistant cassava stems from an extension officer prevents this spread.
ga: Enɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies loo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli fãi ni afolɔ mli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Plantain leaves have large surface areas that lose water fast under bright sun. Placing dry grass or organic mulch around the base of the plant helps retain soil moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ yɛ he ko ni da ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ. Tsei ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Maintaining steady soil moisture helps the plant hold onto its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli beni amɛkpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas put nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility for future seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ kooloi aniyenii nibii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize leaves are turning pale green because of poor soil rather than disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hewɔ moŋ fe hela?

english: If the lower leaves turn light green or yellow starting from the leaf tips while the upper leaves stay green, the soil is low in nitrogen nutrient and needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ baa lɛ naagbee, yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee eŋɔli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and getting soft while stored in the yam barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ akɛto sweet potatoes ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their dormancy and start sprouting when exposed to heat and moisture. Keeping the barn shade-covered, cool, and well-ventilated slows down sprouting and prevents the tubers from drying out.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i he. Kɛ́ oha otsu lɛ mli hulutsoo, ni eyɛ fɛ̃i, ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu bote mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaatsi bulb lɛ naa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Most cassava varieties in Ghana are ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. Harvesting too late makes the tubers woody and hard, while harvesting too early reduces the starch yield.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo efee klalo kɛha dumɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee tsei ni amɛhe wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the fruit, usually triggered by inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist prevents this damage from occurring.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why should I test my soil before I start planting my crops on new land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka mishikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ yɛ he ko hee?

english: Testing your soil shows you what nutrients are already present and what is missing. It helps you choose the right crop for the land and tells you the exact fertilizer you need so you do not waste money.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa lɛ baatsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli kɛ nɔ ni bɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ekɛɔ bo ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa bo koni okafite oshika.

english: If I test my land this year, do I need to re-test it again every single year?
ga: Kɛji mika mishikpɔŋ lɛ mikwɛ afi nɛɛ Ani ehe miihia ni maka shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ daa afi?

english: No, you do not need to test the soil every year. Testing your land once every 2 to 3 years is usually enough to check if your crops are using up the nutrients or if the soil health is changing.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ daa afi. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ daa afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ, no fa bɔ ni sa koni ona kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ etsake.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing maize or if I should plant something else?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔ loo esa akɛ madu nɔ kroko?

english: Different crops need different soil conditions. A soil test checks the food levels and acidity in your dirt to tell you if it can support heavy-feeding crops like maize or if it is better suited for root crops like cassava.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi srɔtoi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa kwɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛ acidity ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛɛ bo kɛji ebaanyɛ eye ebua niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shishifãi ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Will my land lose its strength if I plant crops on it every season without giving it a break?
ga: Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ daa afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli?

english: Yes, planting continuously drains the natural food out of the ground. Resting the land or planting legumes like beans and peanuts helps put natural nutrients back into the soil so it stays strong.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ewo lɛ hewalɛ.

english: This happens when the soil is hard-packed or heavy clay, which prevents water from flowing through. Adding organic manure or ploughing deeply helps break up the hard ground so water can drain properly.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo ebatsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii. ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ mli Akɛ organic fertilizer loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ baafata he Enɛ baaye abua ni akumɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli koni nu lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I just buy any fertilizer from the market and put it on my farm if my crops are not growing well?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ jara nɔ ni mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, using the wrong fertilizer can harm your plants or waste your money. Your soil might only lack one specific nutrient, so you must know what your land needs before buying fertilizer.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye otsei lɛ awui loo ebaanyɛ efite shika. Ekolɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome pɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ole nɔ ni he hiaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ dani ohe ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning yellow even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are starving for essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the ground is flooded with too much water, which smothers the roots and stops them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni amɛkpa niyenii yeli.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same spot on my land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my crops staying short and weak even after I clear all the weeds from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ efee kuku ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Clearing weeds stops competition, but crops still need rich soil food to grow tall. Short crops usually mean the soil is depleted of nutrients or is too sour for roots to take up food.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii lɛ kpaa. Shi shikpɔŋ kpakpa he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii lolo koni amɛkwɛ̃. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye nii.

english: How does animal manure help my soil differently than the chemical fertilizer I buy in bags?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ srɔto yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni miheɔ yɛ kotokui amli lɛ he?

english: Chemical fertilizer gives plants a fast boost of food, but animal manure improves the structure of the soil itself, helping the ground hold water better and stay soft for root growth over a longer time.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii oya. Shi kooloi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eha efee blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ada be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides natural shade and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa trees are mature enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for air, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough food and light to produce large, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground before I harvest them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around them for too long without draining. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to flow away so the roots can breathe and stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Shika ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the moisture in the soil. It keeps the plant roots cool, saves water, and helps stop weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa nu hiɔ shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough moisture for me to start sowing my seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until heavy rains have soaked the soil deeply two or three times. Sowing too early after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then wither when the ground quickly dries up again.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow strong green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ ji tso ko ni niyenii ni he hia kɛha baai ni wa, ni ji eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular watering. Providing steady moisture to the roots and protecting the soil from overheating helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu be fɛɛ be, ni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekadɔ fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small ragged holes appear in the inner leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young corn leaves are typical signs of fall armyworms or caterpillars eating the growing center of the plant. Checking leaves early and using recommended botanical or chemical sprays controls them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bu ni ekumɔ yɛ abɛi bibii amli lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ cutworms, loo larvae, ni eye he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ amli mra ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ atsu nii kɛkudɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Weeds act as competitor plants that steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crop gets all the nourishment it needs to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap beneath the leaves. Spraying the undersides of leaves with soapy water or appropriate insecticides helps stop the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my pumpkin and garden egg plants fall off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ pɔmpi kɛ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Plants produce both male and female flowers, or flowers that need insects like bees to carry pollen from one flower to another. If insects or wind do not move the pollen to the female flower, that flower cannot produce fruit and will simply wither and drop off.
ga: Tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ. Aloo fɔfɔi ni he hiaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ tsiii pollen lɛ kɛyaa fɔfɔi yoo lɛ nɔ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii. ni ebaagbi ni ebaagbee shi.

english: If I harvest seeds from my sweet peppers and plant them near chili peppers, why do the next peppers come out hot?
ga: Kɛji obua bell pepper dumɔwui anaa ni okɛdu yɛ chili ko masɛi lɛ, mɛni hewɔ chili ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo ni edɔɔ lɛ?

english: Wind and insects carry pollen between plants that are close relatives. When chili pollen mixes with sweet pepper flowers, it changes the traits of the seeds inside, causing the new crops grown from those seeds to taste hot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii kɛ pollen yaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ capsicum pollen lɛ kɛ capsicum fɔfɔii lɛ futu lɛ, etsakeɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji lɛ, ni ehaa tsei heei ni jɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: If I plant seeds saved from my harvested high-yield hybrid maize, will I get the exact same heavy yield next season?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni jara waaa kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo ni tsii tamɔ nɛkɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: No, seeds saved from hybrid crops do not produce exact copies of the parent crop. Just as children inherit different mixtures of traits from their parents, second-generation hybrid seeds usually produce weaker plants with smaller yields. It is best to buy fresh certified seeds each season.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haaa tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ he mfoniri ni ja aba. Tamɔ gbekɛbii pɛpɛɛpɛ Gboshinii ji sui srɔtoi kɛjɛ fɔlɔi adɛŋ Bei pii lɛ, yinɔ ni ji enyɔ ni ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni wooo yibii babaoo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpea beans together on the same land with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tsina ŋmãa kɛfata ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, this is a beneficial combination. Cowpea plants use the tall maize stalks for support to climb toward the sun, while their roots add natural nitrogen into the soil, which feeds the maize and improves harvest quality.
ga: Hɛɛ, enɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛfee ekome ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Cowpea tsei kɛ ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ tsuɔ nii koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni haa ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and yellow even when rain falls regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbours in the soil. They aggressively steal the food ingredients, space, and water away from your crop's roots, leaving your plants starving and unable to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii hiɛjoolɔi yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli nibii, he ko, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ yiwalɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara waa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is missing key plant food ingredients like nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes whatever food is left in its lower, older leaves and sends it to the young top leaves to keep the crop alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ, Tso lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛyaa baai bibii lɛ amli koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and bushy with plenty of leaves but refuse to give me fruits or large roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ehaaa mi yibii loo shishifãi wuji lɛ?

english: Giving your crops too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus all its energy on growing leaves and stems. To form big roots like cassava or good fruits like tomatoes, the soil also needs food ingredients high in phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo ha onibii lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi wuji tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tamɔ tomato lɛ akwɛ lɛ, niyenii nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ hu he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall and thin with very small tubers under my big farm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ bibii waa yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct sunlight to create the energy required to build big underground tubers. Under heavy shade, the crop wastes all its food energy stretching upward toward the sun instead of fattening its roots.
ga: Hulu la he miihia cassava tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ aba. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ amɛ niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛshɛɔ hulu lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and sag during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. The leaves temporarily curl up to protect themselves from losing more moisture, and they will bounce back when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ŋmɔtɔ akaje mli. ni ebaaku esɛɛ kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why should I pinch off the small extra shoots growing in the stem joints of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Those extra shoots—called suckers—steal food energy from the main plant. Removing them forces the plant to send all its food ingredients directly into making bigger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ juɔ niyenii hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ebaabi ni nitsumɔhe lɛ kɛ niyenii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ aha tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee tomato yibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and sensitive to high heat. They need shade from taller trees like plantains or forest trees to shield their leaves from direct sunlight and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to use wooden stakes to lift my yam vines off the ground as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso tso he hiaa mi koni mikɛwo mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make the energy required to grow big tubers underground. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight and prevents fungal diseases from spreading on the damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la babaoo naa tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa ŋmeii helai agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and produce small cobs when I put three or four seeds in one planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ

english: When multiple seeds grow in the same spot, their roots fight each other for the limited water and nutrients in that soil space. Spacing seeds out properly gives each plant enough food and room to grow strong stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cut away the small suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Plantain shishitoo lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra suckers steal water and food away from the main plantain tree. By cutting them back and leaving only one or two shoots, the main tree keeps all its energy to yield a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Kɛtsɔ efomɔ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii 1-2 pɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baato ehewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii aba.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my land make the soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as free food for the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei tsei Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmei krokomɛi.

english: Why do weeds make my crop leaves turn light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal essential food like nitrogen directly out of the soil before your crop roots can catch it. Without enough nitrogen, plant leaves cannot maintain their healthy green color and turn yellow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the stem without turning into fruit when the dry season heat begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages the pollen inside the blossoms, preventing seeds from forming. When a blossom cannot produce seeds, the plant naturally sheds it to save its water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui baaa Kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui. Tsei jieɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt and droop during hot afternoons even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. Drooping is a defense mechanism to reduce sunlight exposure and conserve water until the evening cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Drooping ji gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulu la lɛ baa shi ni akɛtoɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the whole root system?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni atsaaa shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a long bare stem with a cluster of leaves at the very top. You can also carefully dig up just one root to check if it has grown thick enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni baai babaoo yɔɔ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa shishifã kome pɛ hu koni ona kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling tightly into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant sap. Their feeding damages the leaf tissue, causing it to twist and curl up as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Ha etsɔ ni ebɔle ehe be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is too tired or poor to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ loo ebɛ ohia tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: If your soil turns hard and pale, drains water too quickly, or crops remain small with yellowish leaves even after good rains, the land lacks vital nutrients and organic matter. Planting cover crops like beans or adding compost can help restore nutrients to tired soil.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Gbalamɔ nu lɛ oya tsɔ Aloo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa lolo ni amɛyɛ baai ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ po. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.
