Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ loo ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my crops turn yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low on essential plant food like nitrogen. When nitrogen is limited, the crop moves what little it has left to new growing shoots at the top, causing the older bottom leaves to fade and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baajie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my young crop plants dry up and die quickly during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ harmatta be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that lose moisture very quickly in dry, hot winds. Without temporary shade crops like plantains or tall shade trees to block direct sunlight and wind, the heat scorches the plant and dries out the soil moisture.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ fiteɔ nu oya. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei kakadaji ni tsiɔ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã tsei lɛ ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my crop leaves drop and look lifeless in the afternoon heat even when it rained recently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ moŋ?

english: On very hot afternoons, leaves lose water through evapotranspiration faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to curl its leaves and protect itself from losing more water, and it usually recovers as temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ latsaa nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni eha ebaai lɛ abɔle ehe ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu kroko ni baafite lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Can I grow cassava and maize together on the same field at the same time?
ga: Dumɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli. Ani wɔbaanyɛ wɔkɛ wɔhe abɔ?

english: Yes, cassava and maize grow well together because maize matures fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the field's space and sunlight after the maize has been harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kome ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eŋɔ he babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji amli kɛ hulu la mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my yield if I plant maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded too close together, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients, and their leaves shade each other from sunshine. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build strong stems and produce full, heavy ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni mli wa ni ekɛ toi ni eyi obɔ ni tsii baa.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees when the leaves look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he kɛjɛ kookoo tso nɔ be mli ni baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes overgrown or crowded branches so sunlight and fresh air can move freely through the canopy. Good airflow reduces humidity that causes fungal diseases and directs the tree's energy into producing flowers and healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds manage to grow much faster than the food crops I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapted to quickly suck up water, light, and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the season stops them from stealing the food and water your young crops need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ogbeɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haaa amɛju niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do small hole marks on crop leaves reduce the final amount of food I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ, ni no haa naagbee niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi

english: Leaves act like food factories that use sunlight to feed the entire crop. When pests chew holes in leaves, the plant loses its ability to capture light and make food, which leads to weak growth and smaller, fewer fruits.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii afeemɔ he, ni amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii koni amɛha ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ niyenii. Beni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ bu yɛ baai amli lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ la ni amɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa.

english: What causes black spots to spread across my cocoa pods when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which multiplies in damp, cool, and rainy conditions. Rain droplets splash fungal spores from pod to pod, so keeping weeds low and clearing infected pods helps control its spread.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ baa. Efɔɔ bii yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ shi ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ bɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient. The plant moves nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top, showing that the soil needs more plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei niyenii babaoo he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress, water shortages, or tiny insects like whiteflies that suck plant juices and spread viruses, making the plant protect itself by curling its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ he haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. nu ni faaa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa. Ha tsei abu amɛhe he kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛaakpã mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and bushy with lots of leaves but fail to produce big fruits or tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi amɛwooo aduawai wuji loo bulbs lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen without enough phosphorus and potassium, they put all their energy into making leaves instead of developing strong roots, big fruits, or heavy cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo shishifãi ni wa, aduawai wuji, loo shishifãi ni tsii.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or a shortage of key nutrients needed during the flowering stage to convert blossoms into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo niyenii titrii ni he hiaa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli koni amɛtsake fɔfɔi lɛ amɛwo yibii lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow fast during the rainy season but dry up immediately when the rain stops for a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔtsei lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli, shi trukaa lɛ amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko lɛ?

english: Rain helps top leaves grow, but if the soil lacks root-building nutrients like phosphorus, plants grow shallow roots that cannot reach deeper moisture stored in the ground during dry spells.
ga: Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa shishifãi maa shi, tamɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ, tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ ashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ ni buaa ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ he.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is completely exhausted and needs help?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli sũ efo kwraa, ni kɛji akɛ yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia mi?

english: If your crops stay small, look pale, mature very slowly, or yield far less harvest than they used to in previous years, it means the soil has lost its natural nutrients and needs nourishment.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii lɛ faaa, etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, edaa blɛoo waa, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miifite niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehe miihia ni aha lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily whenever strong wind or heavy rain hits my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni naa wa ba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize stalks become weak and fall over if the seeds are planted too close together, or if the soil lacks potassium, which is the nutrient responsible for building strong stems and sturdy root support.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa tsei ni wa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my crops look bright and green right after feeding them, but turn weak again after just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji miye niyenii lɛ? Shi ni egbɔjɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ mli?

english: Some soil nutrients wash away quickly with heavy rains or get used up fast. Crops require steady, continuous nourishment throughout their life cycle to remain strong until harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekomɛi hoɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa loo amɛhe ejɔ oya. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa pods turn black when attacked by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, overly damp conditions where air cannot flow freely between trees.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kɛji black pod hela lɛ tutua amɛ. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ oya lɛ

english: Why are my harvested cassava roots rotting quickly inside the soil before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ mafolɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water collects in the soil without draining away properly, or when soil pests and diseases attack weak plants that lack natural resistance.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ tutua tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni bɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni teɔ shi woɔ helai lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the ground is too dry for the roots to absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the bigger trees on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight; they require shade from larger trees or plantain crops to protect their delicate leaves and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo dumɔwui adɛŋ koni ebu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater accumulates without proper drainage, the roots suffocate and begin to decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu babaoo buaa ehe naa ni nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbɔi fitemɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or insect pests stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop flowers to conserve energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Aloo ani tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ? Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Staking yam vines exposes the leaves to maximum sunlight, which helps the plant make food for the subterranean tuber while keeping foliage off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tso lɛ yibii lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small suckers to grow around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many suckers compete with the main mother plant for water and soil nutrients, leading to small bunches; pruning down to one or two strong suckers yields better harvest.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ nyɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni haa tso bibioo ko baa Kɛ́ atse tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves or transmitting a plant virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni gbeɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli.

english: Why do my cowpea crops make the soil richer for my maize during the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi-ŋmei lɛ shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants trap nitrogen from the air through their roots and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide deep inside the central whorl of the maize plant during the day and feed on the tender green leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do groundnut flower stems bend down and push themselves into the dirt after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants flower above ground, but once pollinated, the stem naturally burrows into the soil so the groundnut pods can safely develop underground.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ pollin wo mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: I noticed a strange black substance spreading on my crop leaves; how do I know if it is a disease and what medicine should I use?
ga: Miyɔse nɔ ko diŋ ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ. Egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miyɛ hela ko ni mɛɛ tsofa esa akɛ maŋɔ?

english: Black patches on leaves usually mean your crop has a fungal disease like leaf spot or sooty mold. You can treat it by spraying an approved fungicide and pruning crowded branches to allow sunlight and fresh air to dry out the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko, tamɔ baa lɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo sooty fungus. Obaanyɛ otsa lɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ kɛ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni oookpa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aha baai lɛ agbi lɛ nɔ.

english: My cocoa pods are turning dark black and rotting on the tree; what is causing this and how do I fix it?
ga: Mikookoo ŋmɔji lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Mɛni kɛ enɛ baa ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet, shaded conditions. You should immediately pick off and destroy the infected pods, then spray your cocoa trees with a copper-based fungicide to protect the healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ tsofa ko ni akɛ akɔɔble fee ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ afɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ koni ebu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my tree look like sticky black powder was sprinkled over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni akɛ powda diŋ ni shwieɔ shi eshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: This is called Sooty Mold, which is a fungus that grows on the sweet, sticky waste produced by tiny insects feeding on your tree. To clear it, you need to spray an insecticide to kill the insects first, and the black powder will disappear.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ Sooty Mold, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ muji ni ŋɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ otsei lɛ feɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oosumɔ ni ofɔ he lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ koni egbe kooloi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, powda diŋ lɛ baaho aya.

english: The bark on my fruit tree looks wet and watery even when it has not rained; why is it acting like this?
ga: Mi aduawai tsei lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efɔ kɛ nu eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko moŋ. Mɛni hewɔ efeɔ enii tamɔ nɛkɛ?

english: When a tree trunk looks wet or leaks fluid, it is usually a sign that stem-boring insects have drilled into the tree or a bacterial disease is growing inside. The tree leaks sap as a defense mechanism to flush out the pest or infection.
ga: Beni tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efɔ loo nu ejɛ mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ efo tso lɛ mli loo akɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ miida yɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ nu akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛtsi kooloi loo helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do I see hundreds of tiny creatures arranged tightly together on the underside of my plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bɔɔ nii bibii lɛ? Amɛteŋ ohai abɔ ebɔle mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Those tiny insects—like mealybugs or aphids—gather under leaves to hide from direct sunlight, rain, and predators while they suck out the nutritious juices from your crop.
ga: Nakai kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo aphids. Bua ohe naa yɛ baai ashishi koni okɛ ohe awo hulu la, nugbɔ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. Beni amɛnuɔ nu ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why does it look like water is dripping from under my crop leaves where small insects are sitting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni nu miiho kɛmiijɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi he ni kooloi bibii tara jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: The liquid dripping from under the leaves is not water; it is a sticky waste called 'honeydew' excreted by sap-sucking insects like scale insects or aphids after they drink your plant's juices.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ jeee nu. Eji jwɛi ni shwieɔ shi ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘honeydew’ ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo aphids lɛ jieɔ lɛ. Beni amɛnu nu ni jɛ otsei lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: I see tiny bugs clustered together moving in strange ways on my plant stems; are they going to destroy my crop?
ga: Mina kooloo bibioo ko Bua ehe naa ni enyiɛɔ yɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ yɛ mitso lɛ nɔ Ani amɛbaafite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, when insects cluster and feed together in large numbers, they drain the energy from your plant, cause the leaves to curl, and can weaken the crop so much that it stops producing fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ kooloi bibii bua amɛhe naa ni amɛye nii babaoo. Ebaajie hewalɛ kɛjɛ otsei lɛ amli. ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ amɛkpaa yibiiwoo.

english: Can I use the same spray medicine I use for insects to treat a black spot disease on my trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛtsa ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: No, insect sprays (insecticides) only kill bugs, while black spot diseases are caused by fungi and require disease medicines (fungicides). Using the wrong chemical wastes your money and won't save the plant.
ga: Dabi, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ (tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi) lɛ gbeɔ kooloi pɛ. Yɛ be mli ni black spot hela lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmei ko kɛbaa ni ebiɔ tsofai ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ. (Fungicide) Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji shika fitemɔ, ni eyeee ebuaaa tso lɛ.

english: What is the best way to stop black rot from attacking my tree fruits during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ anaa koni ekatutua mitsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa beaŋ?

english: During the rainy season, keep the weeds around your trees low, clear out dead branches to let air flow through, and spray preventative copper fungicides before the heavy rains start.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ha jwɛi lɛ ahi shi yɛ tsei lɛ ahe ni ojie tsei lɛ aniji ni egboi lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ni okɛ akɔɔble tsofa ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ awo mli dani nugbɔ ni naa wa lɛ aje shishi.

english: How do I safely get rid of small insects hiding underneath my tree leaves without damaging the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai ashishi lɛ shweshweeshwe ni mifiteee baai lɛ?

english: You can spray an approved systemic or contact insecticide directly under the leaves where the bugs hide, or use a mixture of mild soapy water if the infestation is still small.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ shi akɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo loo akɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baa lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ni kooloi lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ. Aloo okɛ samla ni mli ejɔ kɛ nu ni afutu mli lɛ atsu nii. Kɛji akɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ fioo ko yɛ lolo

english: Why are my cocoa trees taking more than four years without producing any yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ eho afii ejwɛ kɛ sɛɛ ni amɛwooo nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Delayed fruiting often happens when the soil lacks essential nutrients, when young trees suffer from lack of shade, or if old seed varieties were planted. Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually produce pods within two to three years if given adequate fertilizer, shade, and weed control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ lɛ. Beni tso bibioo ko bɛ hulutsoo Aloo kɛji odu dumɔwui momoi Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli kɛji akɛ awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa, hulutsoo kɛ jwɛi ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do crops grow well in some parts of Ghana but produce nothing in soil near mining areas like Tarkwa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana hei komɛi shi amɛwooo nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ hei ni atsaa shika tsuru tamɔ Tarkwa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil quality varies heavily by region. Lands affected by heavy rain washing away topsoil or soil compaction from mining activity lack the nutrients and porous structure roots need to absorb water and food properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ yɛ srɔto kwraa yɛ kpokpaa fɛɛ kpokpaa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hoɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ loo sũ ni mli edɔ kɛjɛɔ shika tsuru nitsumɔi amli lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my cocoa tree leaves to dry up and drop off until the tree becomes completely bare?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo baai lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi, ni amɛmiishi tso lɛ efolo?

english: Complete leaf loss, or defoliation, is usually triggered by intense drought, fungal diseases like black pod, or attacks from sap-sucking pests like mirids (capsids) that damage the stems supplying water to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni naa wa, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni fiteɔ tsei ni kɛ nu haa baa lɛ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ kwraa loo egbɔjɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if a bare cocoa tree on my farm is still alive or completely dead?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli loo amɛgboi?

english: You can scrape a small piece of the outer bark on a main stem with your thumbnail or a knife; if the layer underneath is moist and green, the tree is alive, but if it is dry, brown, and brittle, that section of the tree is dead.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ onine loo ŋmei ajie kponɔgbɛ tso lɛ fã bibioo ko ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji shishigbɛ fã lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo, shi kɛji akɛ egbi, eyɛ ŋmɔŋ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no lɛ nakai tso lɛ fã lɛ egbo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their flowers before any cocoa pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ?

english: Trees drop flowers when they are under stress from prolonged dry weather, nutrient deficiency in the soil, or attacks by small insect pests that feed on delicate blossoms.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛyɛ haomɔ mli kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ mli. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ atuatsemɔ.

english: What causes young cocoa pods on my farm to turn black and dry up while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly during damp, rainy periods when there is poor air circulation between closely packed or unpruned trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ loo tsei ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ ateŋ.

english: How do mirid insects cause my tree branches to look scorched and dried out?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mirid kooloi lɛ aha mitso lɛ niji lɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni shã ni amɛgbi?

english: Mirids suck the sap from young shoots and branches, injecting a toxin that kills the stem tissue, causing leaves to wither and turning stems dark and dry.
ga: Mirids nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei aniji amli lɛ. Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ ni fiteɔ fãji ni jɛ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How do I know if my land has healthy soil for cocoa before I spend money planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛbaadu kookoo dani mafite shika kɛdu lɛ?

english: Healthy cocoa soil is dark, crumbly, deep enough for long roots, and drains water easily without staying waterlogged after heavy rainfall.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi kakadaŋŋ abaanyɛ akwɛ̃. ni ekɛ nu hoɔ oya ni ekɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ efooo.

english: What steps can I take to revive an old cocoa farm that has become bare and stopped fruiting?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛwo kookoo ŋmɔ momo ko ni efee efolo ni ekpa yibiiwoo lɛ mli ekoŋŋ?

english: You can revive an old farm by pruning away dead branches, applying recommended fertilizers, planting plantains or shade trees to cover open canopy spots, and spraying for active pests.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha ŋmɔ momo ko aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ni ooofo lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo mli. Dumɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ koni ekɛha ŋwɛitsu ni agbele lɛ nɔ. kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ koni akɛjie kooloi ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees die when I clear all the tall forest trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei lɛ gboi beni mijie koo mli tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees, especially young ones, need moderate shade to survive; full direct sunlight burns their leaves, dries out the surrounding soil, and weakens the tree's natural defense against pests.
ga: Cocoa tsei, titri lɛ tsei bibii lɛ, he hiaa hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ agbi ni eha tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni ekɛbuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a open field with no big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots, making them extremely sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantain plants to filter the sun and keep the soil moist, the intense heat dries them out before they can establish deep roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni baaha hulu la lɛ atsɔ mli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha amɛgbi dani amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant plantains alongside my new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɔ akɛ adu plantains yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that create a natural canopy. This temporary canopy shields young cocoa plants from harsh direct sunlight and severe weather while preserving moisture in the topsoil.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Nɛkɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni akɛwoɔ ŋtayaai amli yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mlihiɛmɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my green maize plants turning pale yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the soil lacks nitrogen, an vital nutrient plants need to stay healthy and make green leaves. When soil runs low on nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has left to its newer, top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa ni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli. Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei amli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same seeds at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Growing crops continuously on the same soil without giving the land a rest or adding organic manure drains the soil of its natural nutrients, leaving less food for future crop generations.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be ni aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fold up and fall off during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural defense mechanism against drought. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces the amount of water it loses to the hot air, going dormant until rains return to revive leaf growth.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni ŋmei tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baaha nu ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba koni ebaaha baai lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: In intense midday heat, water evaporates from leaves faster than roots can absorb it from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to expose less leaf surface to the sun, then recovers once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni hulu la fioo pɛ ashɛ baa lɛ nɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce tiny young pods that turn shriveled and black before growing full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa kɛyashɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees naturally drop extra young pods when the tree senses it lacks enough water, soil nutrients, or energy to support all the pods to maturity.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu efo mli. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛyashi ebaashɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stem instead of turning into green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Extremely high daytime temperatures or sudden dry spells stress the tomato plant, causing it to shed its flowers before insects or wind can pollinate them into fruits.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa loo trukaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ amɛ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards and look crinkled and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on leaf sap and spreading plant viruses, which interrupt normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baa mli nu kɛ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing crops fight each other for limited sunlight, air, root space, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny corn ears.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, kɔɔyɔɔ, shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii toi bibii baa.

english: Why do many farmers in my area plant plantains in the same field as young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ duɔ plantain yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛduɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Fast-growing plantain trees have large leaves that create living shade to keep the young cocoa cool and moist while also giving the farmer food and income while waiting for cocoa to mature.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo koni eha kookoo bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa okwaafoi lɛ niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: If I don't have enough farm workers, which crop takes less daily work between cassava and cocoa?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ nitsulɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hu? Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heɔ be fioo ni ekɛtsuɔ nii fe ŋmei loo kookoo?

english: Cassava requires much less labor after initial planting and weeding because it tolerates poor soils and dry spells well, whereas cocoa requires continuous work like spraying, pruning shade trees, weeding, and frequent harvesting.
ga: Cassava biɔ nitsumɔ fioo ko kwraa yɛ shishijee dumɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ahe gbɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo biɔ nitsumɔ ni yaa nɔ tamɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ. jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni afeɔ shii abɔ lɛ

english: How long does a new cocoa tree take before it starts producing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take 3 to 5 years to bear fruit, but modern hybrid cocoa varieties planted in Ghana can begin flowering and producing pods in just 2 to 3 years with proper care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi enumɔ dani ewoɔ yibii, shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ aje fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra stems growing out from the trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ

english: Those extra shoots, often called water sprouts or chupons, consume water and nutrients that the main tree needs to grow big pods. Removing them directs all energy into pod production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ nu ŋmeii loo chupon ŋmeii. Nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ he miihia koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, etsɔɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa pod feemɔ mli.

english: How do cocoa trees react if I cut down all the large shade trees on my land?
ga: Te kookoo tsei lɛ baafee amɛnii amɛha tɛŋŋ kɛji mifo tso agbo ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Without shade, young cocoa trees get heat-stressed, their leaves turn yellow or burn, and they become far more vulnerable to insect pests and early death during the dry season.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ, dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa kokoo tsei bibii anɔ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛshãa. ni oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ gbele ni baa oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ yɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and drop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants hold a lot of water in their soft trunks and have shallow roots. When water is scarce, the plant naturally sheds lower leaves to reduce water loss and protect its main growing point.
ga: Dumɔwui toɔ nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ amli. Beni nu faaa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu he titri ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ he.

english: Does a plantain tree keep bearing fruit every year, or does it die after one harvest?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii daa afi loo amɛbaagboi yɛ nikpamɔ kome sɛɛ?

english: A single plantain stem dies after bearing fruit once. However, the underground root system remains alive and shoots up new stems (suckers) to continue producing future plantain bunches.
ga: Plantain kome gboɔ beni ewo yibii shikome sɛɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei (suckers) koni amɛkɛwo plantain tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does a single plantain tree grow so many small shoots around its base, and should I leave them all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwu kome pɛ yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni ebɔle eshishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ni esa akɛ mashi amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Plantain plants naturally multiply by sprouting suckers from their roots. You should cut back most extra suckers so they do not steal water and food from the main fruit-bearing stem.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ aduawai tso titri lɛ mli.

english: If my neighbor's cocoa farm gets black pod disease, will it spread to my trees even if my land is clean?
ga: Kɛji okutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ black pod hela Ani ebaagbɛ eshwa mi tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse po?

english: Yes, black pod disease is caused by a fungus whose tiny spores travel easily on wind, rain splashes, infected farm tools, or farm shoes from neighboring farms.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ko ni feɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa. Gbɛfaa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, ŋmɔ mli nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ. loo ŋmɔ mli tokotai ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli mlɛo

english: What happens to the soil if I keep growing the same crop on the same farm year after year without adding anything?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ nɔ ko fataaa he?

english: Continuous single-crop farming drains specific nutrients from the soil over time, making future harvests smaller and leaving crops weaker against pests unless compost or fertilizer is added.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komekomei amli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaa lɛ feɔ bibioo. ni ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai Ja akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with direct sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting tall crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade and holds soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ebuɔ cacao tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Adding organic manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the green color so the maize can produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ afee toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will planting cowpeas together with my maize harm my crops or help them grow?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Planting cowpeas with maize actually helps both crops. Cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which enriches the earth for the maize while giving you two different harvests from the same plot.
ga: Cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ kɛha ŋmãa Yɛ be kome too mli lɛ, anáa ŋmãa sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems from my farm to plant for the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni madu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Always pick stems from mature, healthy cassava plants that show no signs of leaf spots or disease. Cut smooth stems from the middle portion of the plant with at least four or five clear buds, and plant them facing upward into moist soil.
ga: Esa akɛ ahala tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei tso ni eda, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ejieee baa lɛ he okadi loo hela kpo lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmeii ejwɛ loo enumɔ ni mli tse yɔɔ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, du lɛ hiɛ kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the leaves of my young maize plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are typically Fall Armyworms, which attack maize during early growth. Checking the central shoots of your plants regularly and applying recommended organic treatments or safe sprays early will stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ. Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli daa. ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ he nii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ atsu nii mra. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden poles for my yam plants to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to produce energy for growing tubers underground. Raising the vines on stakes lifts the leaves toward the sun and keeps them off the damp ground where rots and fungal diseases easily attack.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooodu yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ewo tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he, ni ebaaha ekashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ helai tutuaa mɔ oya lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plant flowers dropping off before any peppers form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when plants suffer from excessive heat, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil moist through regular watering and applying organic mulch keeps the root area cool so flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ organic mulch ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Fɔfɔi lɛ batsɔ aduawai.

english: How does covering the ground around my vegetables with dry leaves or grass help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi shwieɔ aduawai ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves (called mulching) blocks the harsh sun, prevents soil water from drying up too fast, stops weeds from growing, and decays over time into rich organic matter for the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Tsi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛtsɔ nibii ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops right on the day I plant the seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ gbi ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Seeds already contain enough natural food to sprout, and applying fertilizer too early can burn young roots. It is best to wait two to three weeks after planting when the crops have established roots to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ tso lɛ dumɔ sɛɛ beni tso lɛ ená shishifãi koni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and showing dark spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves and dark spots on tomatoes are common signs of viral or fungal diseases spread by insects like whiteflies or by excess humidity. Spacing your plants properly for air flow and removing infected leaves early helps keep the disease from spreading.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli loo ŋmɔtɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli. Okɛ tsei lɛ awo tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ojie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela akagbɛ eshwa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when I remove all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight. Shade trees act as a natural shelter, protecting young cocoa leaves from scorching heat and keeping the soil moist enough for the roots to establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shweshweeshwe shihilɛhe. Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Planting cassava too close together causes the plants to fight over nutrients, water, and sunlight. This competition results in tall plants with small, thin roots rather than the thick, healthy tubers you want.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei kakadaji ni shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa. Yɛ yitso ni mli wa ni mli wa ni osumɔɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why must I build high soil mounds to plant yams instead of just putting them flat in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni akɛbaadu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand deep underground. High mounds provide soft earth that lets tubers swell easily without pushing against hard ground, while also protecting the tubers from rotting in waterlogged soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ni no haa bulbs lɛ daa oya ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa etswaaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a signal that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil that helps plants build green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni wa.

english: Why do people say that planting beans or groundnuts together with maize makes the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are naturally able to take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When grown alongside maize, they share this natural fertilizer, helping the maize feed and grow stronger.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii nyɛɔ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaajara adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa nɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni enáa niyenii ni edaa waa.

english: How does leaving dry grass on top of the ground help my crop survive hot, dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks the hot sun from drying out the earth. It keeps the root zone cool and retains soil moisture far longer after it rains.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: How do weeds actually reduce my harvest if there is already enough rain for all plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi? Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ momo ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei fɛɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal vital soil nutrients, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crop's roots, leaving your plants weak and underfed even if water is plentiful.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii, kɛji amɛyɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Why do caterpillars always target and eat the inner leaves right in the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni amɛyeɔ lɛ?

english: The center whorl of a young maize plant contains the youngest, softest, and most tender leaf tissue, making it the easiest and most nutritious spot for pests like the Fall Armyworm to feed.
ga: Abɛi tso bibioo teŋgbɛ ji baa fãji bibii fe fɛɛ, bɔdɔɔ fe fɛɛ, kɛ bɔdɔɔ fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ he ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni niyenii yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ.

english: If I cut off some small branches from my tomato plant, won't that mean I get fewer tomatoes?
ga: Kɛji mifo tomato tso lɛ nine bibioo ko Ani no etsɔɔɔ akɛ maná tomato fioo?

english: Pruning non-essential branches forces the tomato plant to direct its energy and nutrients straight into producing larger, healthier fruit rather than feeding unnecessary leaves.
ga: Tso ni afolɔ ni he ehiaaa lɛ nyɛɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ foliar niyenii ni he ehiaaa baaha lɛ najiaŋ

english: Should I start planting my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait for consistent rainfall. The very first rain is often followed by a dry spell that bakes the ground, drying out and killing newly germinated seeds before the main rains arrive.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ sɛɛ. ni egbeɔ dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baa.

english: Why does the chemical spray I bought seem less effective on my farm weeds today than before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi ni mihe lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Agrochemicals lose their potency over time if stored in hot direct sunlight, kept past their expiration date, or mixed with contaminated water, making them far less effective at killing farm weeds.
ga: Agrochemicals lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛji akɛ akɛto hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ha eho be ni esa akɛ ekɛtsu nii lɛ he. loo akɛ nu ni mli ewo muji efutu mli Enɛ haaa etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ agbemɔ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away fertilizer from the topsoil before your crop roots have a chance to absorb it, wasting your money and starving your plants.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ. Efiteɔ shika ni ehaa tsei yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are a warning sign that your crops lack essential nitrogen in the soil or that waterlogged roots are suffocating and unable to feed the plant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ otso lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ etsɔ nu, ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing lots of green leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Adding too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer makes plants spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids feeding on the plant sap and spreading viral infections that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. kɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni haa mɔ dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Excess water sitting in heavy clay soil breeds fungal diseases that attack and rot cassava roots underground before they mature.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii mli lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ dani amɛdaraa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together compete fiercely for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, causing every individual plant to stay weak and produce low yields.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds require sufficient soil moisture to trigger germination; without water, the seed remains asleep in the soil or dries up and dies.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, dumɔwui baakã he amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are my cocoa trees shedding their flowers before forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, prolonged drought, or sudden insect attacks stress cocoa trees, forcing them to drop flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo kooloi ni baa trukaa Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ cacao tsei lɛ ashi amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year reduce my harvest yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests build up in the field.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. kɛ gbɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli

english: Why are the young leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which acts as the main food for leaf growth, or that excessive water is choking the roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will give the plant the nutrients it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the land a break. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas naturally returns nitrogen to the soil and restores its strength.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under the leaves, drink the sap, and spread plant diseases. Spraying the leaves with organic neem oil or a recommended protective spray gets rid of these insects and allows new leaves to sprout smoothly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi, ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ, ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahelai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaye ebua baai heei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small caterpillars attack and eat the middle section of my maize shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii tutuaa ni amɛyeɔ mi-abɛi ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are fall armyworms that hatch from eggs laid by moths in the central funnel of the plant. Applying recommended treatments directly into the center of the funnel early in the morning or late evening destroys the worms before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaafite ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my seed yams rot under the ground before they even begin to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ po lɛ?

english: Seed yams rot in the soil when planted in waterlogged ground or when infected by fungi and tiny worms present in the earth. Treating your seed yams with wood ash or protective fungicides before burying them shields them from decay until sprouts form.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ye amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso mli sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii tsu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahe nii dani adu lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe koni amɛkafite kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or irregular watering. Providing consistent soil moisture and protecting young plants from excessive heat keeps the flowers healthy so they can turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ekome ni akɛhaa kɛ tsei bibii ahebuu kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I plant them in an open field without trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch under direct sunlight. They need partial shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or taller shade trees to keep them cool and moist until their roots are deep enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei kakadaji amli. Ha tso lɛ mli ajɔ ni edɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli bɔ ni sa koni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ aba nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when many young shoots grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miidara bibii waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ amɛhe lɛ? Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ

english: When too many young shoots grow around a single plantain tree, they steal water and food from the parent plant. Cutting away the excess shoots and leaving only one or two strong ones directs all the soil nutrients back into producing one large bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛbafee ŋmeii agbo kome.

english: How do I tell if my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava lets you know it is ready when its lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack due to the expanding tubers beneath the surface.
ga: Yucca haa oleɔ akɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why does the soil in my vegetable beds harden and dry out so quickly after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli waa ni egbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water rapidly through evaporation when exposed directly to hot sunlight. Covering the soil surface around your plants with dry grass or straw keeps the ground cool, retains moisture longer, and keeps the soil soft.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be babaoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick leaves but give me small tubers when I plant them on freshly cleared bush land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse shi ewoɔ bulb bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ tsei bibii ni agbele ehee lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Freshly cleared bush land is packed with rich organic matter containing lots of nitrogen. Nitrogen makes crops put all their energy into growing tall stalks and lush leaves above ground, leaving very little energy to swell the tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ eyi tsei ahe hei ni agbele ehee lɛ amli obɔ. Nitrogen haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the surrounding trees to give them full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas nearby to create a cool microclimate and trap soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo banana ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛfee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni mli ejɔ ni amɛhiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and produce tiny cobs when I put four or five seeds together in a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni egbɛɔ etsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ko lɛ, mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ to dumɔ bu kome mli.

english: When seeds are crowded into one hole, the plants must fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room for its roots to gather food, resulting in thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo bu kome mli lɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ abua niyenii naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ amli tsei kɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land help the next season's maize crop grow better without adding extra fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni afi ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi fataaa he lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have friendly bacteria living in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that nitrogen stays behind as free fertilizer for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ naanyobɔɔ helai ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã he ahi shi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do I need to make big soil mounds to plant my yams instead of planting them in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ama gɔji wuji ni akɛduɔ sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-drained soil so the root tubers can expand downward easily without meeting resistance. Mounds loosen hard soil and allow extra water to drain away so the yam tubers don't rot.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shi oya ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii enaa. Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nu kroko hoɔ kɛyaa. Bɔni afee ni sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava turning yellow and twisted with ugly patterns during the warm season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. The insects spread a virus that damages the leaves, preventing the plant from capturing sunlight to feed its growing tubers.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni jɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ Kplukai gbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ amɛshwãa. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la ni amɛkɛha bulbs ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plants yellow and drop their leaves after water collects and stays on my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaai miiho beni mibua nu naa ni mihi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just as much as they need water. When water sits on the farm for too long, air gets trapped out of the soil, causing the roots to drown and rot, which starves the plant of nutrients.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni tso shishifãi hu he hiaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ nu he hiamɔ Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ. ni haa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their blossoms without forming any fruits when the heat becomes very intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries up the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing pollination from occurring. When flowers aren't pollinated, the plant aborts them to save energy rather than producing empty or damaged fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ pollen naa koni ekafee. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollen lɛ Tsei lɛ baafo mli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii ni efite loo ni efite.

english: How can I tell when my maize is completely ripe and ready to harvest as dry grain for long-term storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Maize is mature for dry grain when the leaves and outer husks turn dry and brown, and a tiny black mark forms at the base of each kernel where it connects to the cob, showing that the plant has finished feeding the grain.
ga: Abɛi eda kɛha ŋmeii ni egbi beni baai lɛ kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni egbi. Ni okadii diji bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu shishi he ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ kpaa gbee yɛ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe edumɔwui lɛ niyenii egbe naa.

english: Why can cassava survive a long dry spell while my maize crop dries up and dies in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep taproots that dig far down into the ground to find hidden water, and it drops its leaves to save moisture during droughts. Maize has shallow roots and large leaves that lose water rapidly, making it far more sensitive to dry weather.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ena nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. ni ebaashwie baai koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai wuji ni nu fiteɔ oya. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ he waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and fall off when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: During the dry season, the air and sun dry out the soil quickly. Cocoa trees drop their leaves on purpose to reduce water loss through their foliage, which keeps the main trunk and roots alive until the rains return.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why should I plant plantain suckers alongside my young cocoa seedlings on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii ewo mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture to protect cocoa plants in their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tso bibioo ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ahi shi koni ebu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes in them with small green waste inside the center roll?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Yɛ wolokpo lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the growing tip of the plant. Catching this early allows you to use neem leaf extracts or recommended treatments before the caterpillar destroys the plant's main growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni naa niyenii yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii dani ŋmeii lɛ afite hei titri ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I harvest smaller maize ears when I plant my seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa ŋmãa bibii beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to develop thick stalks and big, full ears.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why did my cassava produce tall bushy stems with lots of leaves, but very thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ tso lɛ kɛlɛ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of storing starch in the roots. Balancing soil nutrients helps the plant send food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsuɔ niyenii kɛyaa shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs.

english: Why do my yam tubers start sprouting green shoots in the storage barn before the planting season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shweremɔ yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli dani amɛdalɛ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from dormancy after a resting period, especially if kept in warm, humid air. Storing yams in a well-ventilated, cool, shaded barn slows down early sprouting so they stay fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baate shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe mli yɛ wɔɔhe be ko sɛɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potato to ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ fiofio bɔni afee ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by hot, dry soil, irregular watering, or a lack of flower-promoting nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering and healthy soil help the plant hold flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa fɔfɔi yaa hiɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the roots of my tomato plants have swollen lumps on them that make the whole plant stay small and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni efuu ni haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?
