english: Those lumps are caused by tiny soil worms called root-knot nematodes that block the roots from taking up food and water. Rotating tomatoes with crops like cassava or planting marigolds cleans the soil of these worms.
ga: Sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ root-knot nematodes ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ baa. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo marigolds tsakeɔ. Ye obua ni okɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsuu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaf tips on my cowpea plants turning yellow while the leaf veins remain dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ ahe fãji lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This pattern shows a lack of essential soil minerals like magnesium. Adding well-rotted manure or organic compost restores these nutrients, allowing leaves to become fully green and photosynthesize properly.
ga: Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ magnesium lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli kwraa ni enyɛɔ efeɔ fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every year even though I plant the exact same crop and seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs while allowing crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating different crops or letting the land rest restores natural soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ Aloo ashiɔ he ni eshwɛ lɛ koni eye ebua ni aku sɛɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen nutrient or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil, which stops them from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen loo shishifãi lɛ eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. ni haa amɛnyɛŋ amɛye niyenii

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight, so fast-growing plantains act as natural shade umbrellas and keep the soil moist while the cocoa grows strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, yɛ be mli ni kookoo yɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Does it matter which way I stick my cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ mi-cassava lɛ duɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ miduɔ lɛ he hiaa mi?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the growth buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down makes it very hard for the shoots to sprout and reduces yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃, ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when afternoon temperatures get too high, when the soil lacks moisture, or when there are no insects like bees around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ shwane mli. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baawo fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ.

english: Empty groundnut pods (called 'pops') happen when the soil lacks calcium or is too hard and dry during the period when the plant forms its underground nuts.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko (ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pops’) baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni egbi yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ pea yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: What is causing small green worms to eat holes in the middle of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa teŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the funnel leaf of maize plants during the day and eat through the foliage at night.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli, ni amɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli amɛyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during high afternoon heat to reduce water loss, but if they stay limp in the cool morning, the plant urgently needs water.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei hu he miihia nu oya.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after light rains so the roots can absorb it easily, but avoid applying right before heavy downpours that wash it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ oya. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni ooowo lɛ he dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba, ni no baaho lɛ.

english: Why did the cowpea seeds I saved from last harvest fail to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their ability to sprout if they were stored in damp places, damaged internally by tiny weevils, or kept in high heat over the dry season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋmeii bibii efite amɛ yɛ mli, loo akɛto he ko ni latsaa waa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow faster than my crop plants after the rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally equipped with deep roots to steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight faster than domestic crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli oya fe shia tsei.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if the tree is stressed by drought, lacks proper soil nutrients, or isn't being pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Maintaining moderate shade and keeping the ground covered with mulch helps maintain soil moisture and supports these beneficial pollinators.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. Niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ŋmeii bibii eshɛko nɔ Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Kɛ́ ahiɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eye ebua nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ.

english: How many years will it take for my new cocoa seedlings to start bearing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ aje shishi amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting in the field, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years. Proper weeding, shade, and watering during the first two years shorten the waiting time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, hulutsoo kɛ nu ni akɛhaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mɛmɔ be lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during the dry season mean the young plant is getting too much direct sunlight and losing water faster than its roots can take it up. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava protects the leaves from heat stress and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ. ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aná Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ lɛ baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Is it true that cocoa trees grow better under tall trees, or should I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi? Aloo esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cocoa grows best under moderate shade, especially when young. Leaving select tall forest trees protects young cocoa from harsh sunlight and drying winds, but leaving too many dense trees creates too much shade and promotes fungal diseases.
ga: Cocoa daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Titri lɛ, beni miji oblanyo fioo lɛ. Tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ amɛ awoɔ kooi ni ahala mli lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Shi tsei ni ashiɔ amɛ tsɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo baa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela baa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, overly shady, and crowded farm conditions. Pruning excess branches, weeding regularly, and harvesting mature pods quickly helps reduce humidity and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ afolɔmɔ Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa. Ni ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi oya, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are insects eating holes in the soft, reddish new leaves of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu yɛ mi kookoo baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tsuɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: New reddish leaves are soft and full of moisture, making them an easy meal for pests like capsids (mirids) and leaf-eating beetles. Regular field monitoring and applying approved organic or chemical protections during leaf flush seasons help safeguard young leaves.
ga: Baai tsuji heei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha kooloi tamɔ capsids (myrids) kɛ ladybugs ni yeɔ baai lɛ. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ kwɛmɔ ni afeɔ daa kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei bibii ahe.

english: Why are some of my plantain stems bending and falling over before the fruit is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi efo ni amɛgbee shi dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Plantain stems often fall over because banana weevils or root nematodes have damaged the underground root base, weakening the plant's anchor. Strong winds can easily push over weakened plants, so propping heavy fruiting plants with wooden stakes helps keep them upright.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ banana ŋmeii loo shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishitoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ akumɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ wo tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi jaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to plant cocoa on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ kookoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa thrives in deep, dark, well-drained soil rich in organic matter that holds moisture without standing in pools after heavy rain. If you dig a hole and the topsoil is dark, loose, and drains water smoothly, it is generally suitable for cocoa.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehe ehiaaa ni edamɔ ŋshɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Kɛji otsa bu ko ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How often should I clear weeds around my cocoa trees when they are young?
ga: Esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Shii enyiɛ oduɔ cacao beni cacao tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings should be weeded every 4 to 6 weeks, particularly during the rainy season. Weeds compete directly with young roots for water and light, so keeping a clear ring around each tree trunk speeds up early growth.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daa otsii 4 kɛyashi 6, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Jwɛi kɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu kɛ la. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni mli tse ni akɛbɔleɔ he lɛ. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko haa tso lɛ daa mra.

english: What makes cocoa pods change color from green or red to yellow or orange?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa etsuru nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu mli?

english: Color change is the natural signal that the beans inside the pod are fully developed and mature. Green pods turn yellow and red pods turn bright orange, letting you know it is time to harvest for quality fermentation.
ga: Su tsakemɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ pod lɛ mli lɛ edara ni amɛdara. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni pods tsuru lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ole akɛ be eshɛ kɛha nikpamɔ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight dries out their leaves and roots quickly. Leaving older shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain creates a cool canopy that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni yɔɔ ekãa ni daa oya lɛ adumɔ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does putting dry grass and leaves around the base of my pepper plants keep them from wilting in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai abɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, abuɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishi koni ekagbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with organic material, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight from evaporating water out of the ground. It keeps the soil cool and moist for longer periods so root systems can continually feed the plant during dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ebaatsi nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aha tso lɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why are small worms eating the green leaves inside the funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ a-funnel lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks maize leaves and growing shoots. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant, so applying recommended controls directly into the funnel early in the morning or late evening helps stop them before they ruin your yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ wo tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa amɛ dani amɛfite onibii lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my fresh tomatoes turn soft and black while they are still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato heei lɛ ashishi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, usually caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding compost or lime helps the plant transport calcium to the fruits, preventing the rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa aduawai lɛ amli. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and the whole tree falls over in strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: This collapse is often caused by tiny soil pests called nematodes or stem borers destroying the underground roots, which weakens the plant's anchor in the soil. Using healthy, treated planting suckers and mulching around the base keeps root systems strong and secure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛtsɔ tso sucker ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Shishitoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ ahe wa ni ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: If I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field after harvesting maize, how does it help my soil?
ga: Kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ Te ebaaye ebua mishikpɔŋ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food stored in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the land so that heavy-feeding crops like maize grow much better in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow in a V-shape down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves down the central vein of older leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure replenishes the essential nutrients the crop needs to stay green and healthy.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa lɛ naagbee ni etsɔɔ baa ni edara lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: When crops are planted too close to one another, their leaves and roots fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures that every crop gets enough light and food to build strong stems and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai kɛ shishifãi kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei fɛɛ náa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for maximum yield in their first generation only. Planting seeds saved from that harvest will result in weaker offspring that grow unevenly and produce significantly smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni yeɔ wala yɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha seshibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni daraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ aba ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni sa kadimɔ waa.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so the tubers don't become hard and woody?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafee nɔ ni wa ni efee tsei?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can test one plant by carefully digging around its base; if the tuber is full and cooks soft easily, the farm is ready, whereas leaving tubers too long in the ground makes them tough and fibrous.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ oka tso kome okwɛ kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ ni ehoɔ oya lɛ, amɛfeɔ blɛoo. Okwaafoi lɛ efee klalo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce pods during most months of the year instead of all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli moŋ fe ni amɛwoɔ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees in Ghana fruit in two main cycles—the main crop season (October to February) and the mid-crop season (May to June). The tree continuously flowers and sets pods based on rainfall and temperature patterns, allowing harvests to stretch across about ten months of the year.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ bei titrii enyɔ mli: be titri ni amɛdaraa (October kɛyashi February) kɛ be ni amɛdaraa yɛ teŋgbɛ. (May kɛyashi June) Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii be fɛɛ be yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛ bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa nii aaafee nyɔji nyɔŋma daa afi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but only a few actually turn into mature pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi tsei fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda kwraa?

english: A cocoa tree naturally drops many of its flowers because of limited plant nutrients, poor insect pollination, or natural pod wilt. The tree naturally selects only the amount of pods it can adequately feed and support to maturity.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ tso mli niyenii ni faaa lɛ hewɔ. Pollinators ni ehiii loo pods lɛ gboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe Tsei lɛ halaa pods ayibɔ pɛ ni baanyɛ aha niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ kɛha dalɛ.

english: How can I tell if the cocoa beans I harvested are good enough for trade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha jarayeli?

english: Good cocoa beans are properly fermented, dried to a low moisture level (around 7-8%), uniform in size, and free from mold, insect damage, or bad smells. When you cut a good bean open, it has a rich brown color inside rather than a slaty or purple color.
ga: Esa akɛ afee kookoo ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ha ni egbi kɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi (aaafee 7-8%), ni dalɛ tamɔ ekome. Ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ, kooloi fitemɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ gbonyo. Kɛ́ ogbala ŋmei kpakpa ko mli lɛ, ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ emli. Yɛ slate loo purple najiaŋ.

english: Why do I need to ferment my cocoa beans under plantain leaves for days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ plantain baai ashishi gbii babaoo dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation kills the seed inside the pod to stop it from sprouting and develops the rich chocolate flavor and brown color buyers look for. Skipping fermentation leaves the beans bitter, purple, and of poor commercial quality.
ga: Fɛ̃i gbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ni ehaaa amɛkwɛ̃. ni amɛná tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ awo mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛbaafee nɔ ni jara waaa.

english: Why is it wrong to dry my harvested cocoa beans directly on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ aaagbi kookoo yibii ni akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Drying cocoa on bare soil exposes the beans to dampness, dirt, and mold, which destroys their quality. Drying them on raised bamboo mats allows air to flow freely above and below the beans, keeping them clean and properly dried.
ga: Kookoo ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ, muji, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kɔfe yibii lɛ anɔ, ni no fiteɔ bɔ ni ehi ha lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ nɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ yɛ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛ amɛshishi jogbaŋŋ. Ha kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ ahe atse ni amɛgbi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest a cocoa pod from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: A pod is ready for harvest when its color changes completely from green or deep red to yellow or orange. Harvesting too early results in unripe, flat beans, while leaving pods too long causes seeds to sprout or rot inside.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhe su tsake kwraa kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ akakwɛ̃. Yɛ be mli ni ashiɔ ŋmeii lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, amɛbaahã dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi yɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees naturally prefer forest shade. Direct, intense sunlight burns their young leaves and dries out soil moisture, which is why planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects them until they grow stronger.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔ koo lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ amɛhe waa lɛ.

english: Will cutting off extra branches from my cocoa tree hurt the crop or reduce my yield?
ga: Ani niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui loo ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi?

english: No, pruning dead or unwanted branches actually improves yield. It allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the main trunk, reduces diseases, and directs the tree's energy into growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Dabi, niji ni egboi loo ni ataooo lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi, ehaa helai baa shi, ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and shade during heavy rainy periods. Clearing weeds and trimming shade trees helps air flow through the farm and keeps pods dry.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees giving me fewer pods now than they used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older than 20 to 25 years, their roots become less efficient at absorbing nutrients from the soil, and they become more prone to diseases. Pruning, feeding the soil, or replanting helps maintain continuous high yields.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso eye fe afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni helai srɔtoi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe waa, amɛfoɔ tsei, amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii, loo amɛduɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Giving each plant enough space allows the roots room to expand fully and absorb all the food they need to form thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifã tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kwraa ni ekɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to soak my rice seeds in water before sowing them in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui awo nu mli dani madu yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soaking rice seeds softens their hard outer shells and activates the life inside the seed. This helps the seeds sprout faster and grow more evenly, ensuring you get strong, healthy seedlings for transplanting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmaa lɛ wo nu mli lɛ, ehaa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ni ehaa wala ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛdaraa pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehaa onine shɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni he wa ni okɛduɔ he kroko lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a natural survival trick maize uses to protect itself from extreme heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, stopping water from escaping through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni etsĩ nu naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I cut down all the big trees around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily in direct sunlight. Leaving tall trees or planting shade crops like plantains creates a cool umbrella that keeps the soil moist and protects young cocoa leaves from scorching heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains lɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I apply all my chemical fertilizer to my crops at once to make them grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ fɛɛ woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli shikome koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya lɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer at once can burn delicate roots and waste money, as excess fertilizer gets washed away by rain. Feeding crops in recommended steps ensures they get nutrients as they grow without damaging the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni efite shika. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei niyenii ha yɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ naa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ ni efiteee tso lɛ.

english: Why does animal manure take longer to show results on my vegetables than store-bought chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi a-ŋmei hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ aduawai anɔ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure must first be broken down by beneficial insects and microbes in the soil before plants can feed on it. Although it works slower, manure builds long-term soil health and holds water much better than chemical fertilizer.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii dani aye. Eyɛ mli akɛ etsuɔ ​​nii blɛoo moŋ Shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu hi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do tomato flowers fall off my plants without ever turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii ni esaaa Kɛ́ haomɔ ba Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei lɛ baawo yibii lɛ, amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛwala.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my pepper seedlings right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are hardy wild plants with seeds already hiding in the soil, ready to sprout instantly when water hits them. Cultivated pepper plants need extra care and early weeding so they aren't choked out before their roots establish.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa. Dumɔwui yɛ ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo. ni efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo nu mli Pepper tsei ni adu lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra. koni akafolɔ dani shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Why shouldn't I dry my freshly harvested cocoa beans directly in the hot sun without letting them ferment first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ migbiɔ mi-kookoo ni mikpa ehee lɛ? Gbimɔ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ohaaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Fermentation is a necessary resting stage where natural heat develops the chocolate flavor and rich brown color inside the cocoa bean. Drying beans immediately skips this process, leaving them bitter, purple, and low in market value.
ga: Fermentation ji hejɔɔmɔ gbɛ ni he hiaa. Adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ haa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo yibii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Beans lɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ tsɔɔ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ, su ni ji purple kɛ jara ni baa shi baa.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are ready to harvest since the pods develop hidden under the dirt?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ akpa ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ehiɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You can tell groundnuts are ready when the leaves on the plant begin to turn yellow and drop off. Pulling up a sample plant and cracking open the pods will reveal dark, textured inner skins on mature nuts rather than pale, wet linings.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Kɛ́ ogbala tso ko ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ nɔ ni ogbala ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaajie mligbɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ anɔ lɛ kpo. Mohu ɔ, e ji ngmɔ mi nɛ e mi mi fu.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. Leaving larger shade trees or planting plantains nearby creates a cool environment and protects young cocoa roots from drying out while they establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei wuji kɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni odu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaha shihilɛ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i. ni ebuɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi beni amɛdaraa lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize crops turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to make food. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure restores green leaf color and helps form large maize cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni afee ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: How do I know the right time to put my cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava should be planted immediately after the first steady rainy season begins so the soil stays consistently moist. Planting in wet soil encourages fast root development before hot, dry spells arrive.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa daa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa oya dani be ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: What causes small green insects to gather under my vegetable leaves and make them curl up?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ ashishi ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Those insects are aphids, which suck sap from stems and leaf undersides, weakening the crop. Spraying a natural extract made from boiled neem leaves mixed with soap destroys aphids without damaging your crops or soil.
ga: Kooloi nɛɛ ji aphids, ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ baai lɛ ashishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni akɛ neem baai ni ahoo ni akɛ samla futu mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ ni eyeee oŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ awui.

english: Why should I trim off extra side branches and bottom leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Removing excess side shoots and lower leaves improves airflow to prevent leaf diseases. It also directs the tomato plant's nutrients into growing large, juicy fruits instead of wasting energy on extra leaf growth.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛtsi tso lɛ mli hela naa. Eheɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ tomato tsei amli hu koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni mli ewo nu. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains all its nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ baajɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Ehaa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrition. Spreading dry grass around the roots as mulch keeps soil cooler and retains moisture so flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha he lɛ. shishifãi lɛ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and taller than my crops right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild species adapted to swallow up sunlight, water, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the growth stage prevents them from starving your crops of food and light.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhe hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ amɛdalɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye la kɛ la hɔmɔ.

english: How can I stop small beetles from eating into my harvested beans while they are in storage bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ladybugs lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye mi-beans ni akpa lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beetles thrive in moist grains. Sun-drying your harvested beans thoroughly until they are hard, and storing them in airtight bags or mixing them with dry wood ash, prevents insects from destroying your grain reserve.
ga: Beetles yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ mli. Nibii ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni okɛto vacuum kotoku mli loo okɛ tso sũ ni egbi afutu mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi akafite dumɔwui ni okɛto lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from fresh tomatoes I bought at the market and plant them on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tomato hee ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Market tomatoes often come from specialized hybrid plants whose second-generation seeds produce weak plants with low yields. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures uniform plants with high yields and disease resistance.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ jɛɔ tsei krɛdɛɛi ni akɛfee ekome ni dumɔwui ni ji yinɔ ni ji enyɔ yɔɔ mli ni woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ baaha tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ahi shi daa.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive their early years because direct, intense sunlight burns their leaves and dries out their soil before their roots are strong enough to drink deep ground water.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛnu shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning light yellow from the bottom of the plant upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build healthy green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with huge leaves but gives me very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ.

english: If too many young suckers grow around one plantain stem, they compete for water and nutrients, which leaves the main stem weak and results in smaller bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when there are no small insects around to shake and pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii komɛi bɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe ni baakpokpo ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaves, which damages the leaf cells and spreads crop diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni fiteɔ baa mli wala yibii lɛ ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the sunlight so they can make food faster, while also keeping the leaves off the wet soil to prevent fungal diseases from rotting the plant.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli koni amɛhoo oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote tso lɛ mli, ni eha tso lɛ akafite.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my land make the soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny root swellings that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi bibii ni efuu. No baamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the old, dry leaves at the bottom of my oil palm tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egbɔ ni egbi yɛ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Pruning old, dry palm fronds stops pests from hiding in the tree and allows the palm to direct its food and water straight into developing big fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni egbi ni egbɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akatee tsei lɛ amli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu gbɛ koni etsɔ aduawai wuji.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds while my crops are still very small instead of waiting until they get bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni jwɛi lɛ adara lɛ,.

english: Young crops are weak and can easily lose the fight against fast-growing weeds for sunlight, rain, and soil food; clearing weeds early gives your crops a strong start.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛha hulu la, nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii lɛ anɔ kunim oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is the liquid coming out of my rubber tree so watery instead of thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni jɛɔ mi-gum tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nu moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: When rubber trees are tapped too frequently without enough rest, the tree runs out of nutrients needed to make concentrated latex. This causes the liquid to become thin and watery, which drastically reduces the total weight and quality of rubber you collect.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otswa rɔbɔt lɛ shii abɔ tsɔ ni onáaa hejɔɔmɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee latɛs. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ afee mlɛo ni efee nu. Enɛ baaha otai ni obua naa lɛ mli tsiimɔ kɛ ekpakpafeemɔ fɛɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Why am I getting much less rubber weight from my harvest this month compared to before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛ taii ni tsiimɔ waaa kwraa nɔ kɛjɛ nyɔŋ nɛɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Over-harvesting or tapping trees when they are stressed exhausts the tree. Instead of producing a full yield like one ton, the tree's production can drop by more than half because it does not have the strength to produce extra liquid.
ga: Tsei ni akpaa fe nine loo ni atswaa kɛji akɛ haomɔ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa, kɛ wɔkɛɛ lɛ, tɔn 1 lɛ, abaanyɛ afo tso ko mli nibii ni ejieɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nɔ ni fe fã ejaakɛ ebɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛbaafee nu kroko ni fata he.

english: Why do rubber buyers say my rubber lacks strength and offer me a lower price?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ tai lɛ kɛɔ akɛ mitai lɛ mli waaa ni amɛhaa mi jara ni baa shi lɛ?

english: Rubber loses its strength when it is harvested from weak or over-tapped trees. Latex from tired trees contains mostly water and fewer rubber solids, which makes the dried rubber weak and light on the scale.
ga: Sap lɛ he waaa kɛji akpa kɛjɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ loo ni afolɔ amɛ fe nine lɛ amli. Latex ni jɛɔ rɔbɔt tsei amli lɛ mli babaoo ji nu ni rɔbɔt fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa rɔbɔt ni egbi lɛ mli wa ni ehiɛ waaa kɛshiɔ slag.

english: What will happen if I cut my rubber trees every single day to get more liquid?
ga: Mɛni baaba kɛji mifo mi rɔba tso lɛ daa gbi koni maná nu babaoo?

english: Cutting rubber trees every day wears them out quickly. The tree will stop producing thick latex and start producing watery liquid, and within a short time, the total amount of rubber you collect will drop heavily.
ga: Kɛ́ ooofo rɔbɔt tso lɛ daa gbi lɛ, ebaaha rɔbɔt tso lɛ agbɔjɔ oya. Tso lɛ kpaɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ feemɔ ni ebɔi nu ni tamɔ nu feemɔ. ni yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ Rɔba fɛɛ ni obua naa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Is it okay to tap my rubber trees right after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ atswa rɔba tsei yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait after heavy rain because water mixing with fresh cuts dilutes the latex, making it watery and weak. Rain can also carry diseases into the cut bark and spoil your rubber liquid.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ ejaakɛ nu ni akɛ loo hee efutu mli lɛ baaha latɛs lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni kɛ nu kɛ bɔjɔmɔ baa Nugbɔ hu baanyɛ aŋɔ hela awo tso lɛ yibii ni afo lɛ mli ni efite o-sap lɛ.

english: What is the best time of the day to cut my rubber tree bark for latex?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni akɛfoɔ rɔbɔt ŋmei koni akɛfee latɛs?

english: Early morning is the best time to tap because the air is cool, which keeps the pressure inside the tree high so thick latex flows easily. Tapping in the hot afternoon makes the latex dry up too fast or flow poorly.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ atswa ejaakɛ hulu lɛ miitso. Enɛ haa nɔnyɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Latex lɛ mli edɔ hewɔ lɛ etsɔɔ mlɛo. Kɛ́ otswa yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha latex lɛ agbi oya tsɔ loo efoŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my rubber tree is too exhausted and needs a break from harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi rɔbɔt tso lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni mafo mli kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli?

english: If the liquid flowing out turns very thin like water, or if your weekly harvest weight drops significantly, your tree is tired and needs a resting period without any cuts so it can rebuild its strength.
ga: Kɛji nu ni jeɔ kpo lɛ mli tse waa tamɔ nu Aloo kɛji otsi mli ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ eba shi waa. Otsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ehe baahia ni amɛná be ni amɛkɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfoŋ nɔ ko nɔ ko. Koni tso lɛ awa ekoŋŋ

english: Will cutting deeper into the rubber tree bark give me more latex milk?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akumɔ rɔbɔt lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha latɛs babaoo aba?

english: No, cutting too deep wounds the inner wood of the tree instead of just opening the latex channels. This damages the tree permanently, leading to sick trees, watery liquid, and lower yields in the long run.
ga: Dabi, tso lɛ mli ni afoɔ lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbele rɔbɔt gbɛ lɛ kɛkɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ daa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ Nu ko ni tamɔ nu yɛ. ni nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli

english: Why does my rubber tree still look green and healthy if the liquid it produces is poor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi rɔbɔt tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lolo ni eyɛ hewalɛ kɛji nu ni ejieɔ lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: A tree can keep its green leaves while still being too depleted to manufacture strong latex. Leaf growth and latex production use different energy reserves, so a green tree can still yield poor, watery rubber if it is over-tapped.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ ahi amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛhe ejɔ tsɔ lolo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie nu ni mli wa kpo. Baai adalɛ kɛ latɛs feemɔ kɛ hewalɛ srɔtoi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie nu ni ehiii ni nu yɔɔ mli kɛji akɛ akɛ tapping babaoo tsu nii.

english: How can I protect my rubber trees so they keep giving me good yields for many years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-rɔba tso lɛ he koni ewo yibii afii babaoo?

english: You can protect your trees by giving them rest days between tappings, avoiding deep cuts into the bark, and giving the trees a total break during dry seasons so they can save their strength and recover.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu otsei lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ hejɔɔmɔ ni oooha amɛ yɛ gbee ni amɛtswaa lɛ teŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Ni ha tsei lɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi amɛhewalɛ mli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their tender leaves lose moisture faster than their small roots can absorb it. Providing shade with crops like plantain creates a cooler environment that protects young cocoa from heat stress until it is strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ aŋɔ awo mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantains ni akɛwoɔ shade mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the crop is lacking essential soil nutrients, particularly nitrogen. When plants cannot get enough nitrogen from the soil, they cannot produce green chlorophyll, which lowers their growth and final yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ tso lɛ mli bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil ni ji eŋɔli lɛ. Enɛ baaha dalɛ kɛ naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together maximizes land use because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three to four months, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the space after the maize is cleared.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ yaa hiɛ babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to wait for the major rainy season before planting my food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni amɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ dani adu niyenii lɛ?

english: Crops need consistent soil moisture to germinate seeds and build healthy root systems. Planting at the start of the main rainy season ensures young plants receive steady water so they do not dry out during early growth.
ga: Tsei hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛto shishifãi ni mli wa. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa nu daa. No hewɔ lɛ egbiɛɛ yɛ be mli ni edaa oya lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to cover the soil around our crops with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle wɔŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry organic matter, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the soil, keeps moisture near plant roots longer, and prevents weeds from easily growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ tso shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: How does burning cleared bush on my farm before planting affect my soil in the long run?
ga: Te jwɛi ni mli tse ni ashãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani aduɔ lɛ baaná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: While burning clears the land quickly and temporarily adds ash, it kills beneficial soil organisms and burns away rich organic matter that crops need for long-term health and water retention.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ oya ni ekɛ sũ fataa he yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ, ni eshãa nibii babaoo ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa kɛ nu ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my maize foliage mostly at night instead of during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-abɛi lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide in the soil or deep inside crop leaves during the day to avoid heat and predators, coming out to feed at night when cooler temperatures are safer for them.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsei ahe baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛyatao niyenii gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and dense leafy parts from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning overcrowded branches allows sunlight and fresh air to pass through the tree canopy, which reduces dampness that causes fungal diseases like black pod disease.
ga: Niji ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni aaafolɔ mli lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekabote tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Cassava is ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Cassava efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Harvested seeds from hybrid maize lose their high-yield strength in the second generation, leading to smaller cobs and uneven growth; purchasing fresh certified hybrid seed each season gives better yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ laajeɔ ehewalɛ ni haa yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa. Dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eda waa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground where leaves can get full sun and avoid fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni baa lɛ baanyɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni ekwa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ.

english: Extra suckers act like extra mouths to feed—they steal food and water from the main mother tree. Removing them leaves only one or two strong suckers and ensures the main tree grows large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krɛdɛɛi kɛha niyenii. Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni ji nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ eshwɛɔ. ni ehaa tso titri lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ plantain jwɛi agbo ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to make food and stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extremely hot weather, improper watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. nu ni esaaa loo niyenii ni esaaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when heavy rain floods my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to stay alive and healthy. When soil stays flooded with water for too long, oxygen cannot reach the tubers, causing them to drown, suffocate, and rot underground.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ yitso lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛshwieɔ nu mli, amɛmuɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in harsh heat. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantain or cassava to protect them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo yucca lɛ adɛŋ. Koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ

english: Why does my land produce a smaller harvest when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas replenishes the soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does spreading dry grass on the soil around my pepper plants help them grow?
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ Te mi-pepper tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass creates a blanket called mulch. It keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ feɔ nɔ ko. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and yield smaller fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow tall and produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems from my old farm to plant for a good yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni madu koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Choose stems from healthy, high-yielding parent plants that are 8 to 18 months old. Select the thick middle section of the stem with clean, undamaged buds rather than the soft green top or hard bottom.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni jɛ nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 lɛ mli. Halamɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni mli tse ni ŋmeii ni he tse ni efiteee lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Mohu ɔ, hlami hɛ mi nɛ ngɛ ŋmɔŋ loo sisi nɛ wa.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the stalks to grow thin and weak, resulting in very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmei bibioo loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: How do I identify the right plantain suckers to dig up and plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mayɔse plantain tsei ni sa ni esa akɛ mafo ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which have broad bases tapering up to narrow, spear-like leaves. These grow into strong, fast-yielding plants compared to 'water suckers' that have broad leaves early on and produce weak stems.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni yɔɔ shishi ni mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛɛmɛi daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa, ni woɔ yibii oya kɛ akɛto ‘suckers’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ mra ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil, or that waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing long leaves but failing to form a hard round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitsei ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when temperatures are too high, when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer late in growth, or when watering is irregular during the heading stage.
ga: Kaabage nyɛŋ atswa yitso kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ onine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ loo be mli ni nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need temporary shade from larger trees or nurse crops like plantain to protect their delicate leaves from harsh sun heat and strong winds until their root systems fully establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ biɔ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ, tamɔ plantains, koni akɛbu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baagbe naa.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines with wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mikɛ tsei atswa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam vines off the hot ground so the leaves can catch enough sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers, while also reducing fungal disease infections from damp soil.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ koni baai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become excessively hot, when the soil experiences extreme drought, or when there is a lack of essential nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viral infections spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why do my watermelons crack open while they are still growing on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miitswa be mli ni amɛmiida lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watermelons split open when there is a sudden heavy rain or heavy watering after a prolonged dry period, causing the inside of the fruit to absorb water rapidly and expand faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Watermelon mli gbalaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa loo nu babaoo ba beni egbi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need extra fertilizer when they are already planted in soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ he hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi awo mli kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Cocoa trees pull nutrients out of the ground every time they produce pods. Over time, the soil becomes weak and empty, so fertilizer feeds the soil so the tree can keep growing strong leaves and heavy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ bafeɔ shoo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ baai ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds make my young crop plants grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water and food from the soil before your young crop can reach them, essentially starving your crop of what it needs to grow.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baashɛ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa plants wither and die if they don't have taller trees growing above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji tsei kakadaji bɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, delicate leaves that burn easily in direct harsh sunlight. Taller trees act as a shield, keeping the air cool and moist so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gãimlibii. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and drop off during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Plants drop their leaves when water is scarce to conserve moisture in their stem and roots, protecting themselves from drying out completely until the rains return.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ nu faaa bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Buu ohe he koni okagbi kwraa kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough energy to make big fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why do I need to cut off healthy-looking branches from my growing cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni miida lɛ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Trimming extra branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the main trunk, which stops wet-weather diseases from building up and forces the tree to put its energy into growing pods.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ mli helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kpaa, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal sickness called Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet, shaded conditions and spreads quickly from pod to pod through rain droplets.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli.

english: Why does spraying agrochemicals on my crop's leaves protect the fruits from insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ buɔ miyibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ?

english: Agrochemical sprays create a protective cover on the leaves and stems that repels harmful bugs or destroys tiny pests before they can suck the sap out of the plant.
ga: Agrochemical sprays lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ koni ekɛshwie kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo efite kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Dani ebaaŋɔ nu lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the trunk without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers if they lack water, proper nutrients, or if beneficial insects are not around to pollinate them, saving energy until conditions improve.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji nu bɛ amɛmli. Niyenii ni sa loo kɛji kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ ni baanyɛ afee pollination koni akɛto hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does an old cocoa tree stop producing as many pods as it did years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni egbɔ lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii babaoo tamɔ bɔ ni amɛfee afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As a cocoa tree grows very old, its trunk and roots become tired and struggle to carry water and nutrients up to the branches, leading to fewer flowers and pods.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ egbɔ lɛ Etsitsi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔi nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ.

english: Why do older farmers always advise me to plant plantains on the same land with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko woɔ mi ŋaa be fɛɛ be akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa seedlings need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam plants need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil into the air, which maximizes light exposure and prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni la lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when planting on my field?
ga: Te esa akɛ makɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ abɔ he kɛyashi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting maize too close together forces the plants to fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small cobs. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce big, full ears of corn.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni ŋmeii lɛ hu yɛ bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-based fertilizer like NPK or urea around the base of the plants will help them regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛbaafata he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aku esɛɛ kɛba eŋɔli su lɛ mli ni eda waa.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the plant's sap, or a virus spread by these insects. Spraying your crops early with soapy water or natural neem tree oil can help clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ mra Soap nu loo adebɔɔ mli neem tso mli fɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots during hot periods helps the plant retain its blossoms and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni amɛhaaa amɛ daa. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in waterlogged soil that cannot drain properly. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the root tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: The first rain often moistens only the top layer of soil, and a long dry spell usually follows. Waiting for two or three steady rains ensures deep soil moisture so your germinated seeds won't dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli fũuɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ egbiŋ ni amɛgboiŋ.

english: Can I put strong chemical fertilizer directly into the hole with my crop seeds when planting?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni mli edɔ awo bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ midumɔwui lɛ kɛ́ midu?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against fresh seeds can chemically burn and ruin them before they sprout. It is better to apply fertilizer a few inches away from the plant once the seedling has emerged and grown green leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui heei amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa ashã ni egbe dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ he inchii fioo komɛi amli kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai eŋɔli.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my maize field after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, leaving the soil tired. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts absorb nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ he ajɔ Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to loosen the soil and make mounds before planting yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ajie sũ lɛ ni afee gɔji dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?
