english: Loosening the soil creates soft, aerated earth that makes it easier for roots to spread and grow big tubers. Mounds also prevent rainwater from collecting around the roots, protecting the tubers from rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa ŋmeii lɛ afite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with no shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains creates a cool environment and retains soil moisture, giving young cocoa seedlings the protection they need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa hebuu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food for growing heavy tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground where leaves can get full sunlight and prevents soil-borne diseases from spoiling the foliage.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ baanyɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ akafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth and green color. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa kɛ eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha eŋɔli lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plants decay, this natural nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as a free fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa tsei fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground during heavy rainfall seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long and cuts off oxygen to the roots. Planting cassava on raised ridges or sloping fields allows excess water to drain away naturally, keeping roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when I let many suckers grow around the main plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa beni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Having too many suckers causes them to compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning excess suckers so that only one or two remain leaves enough energy for the main stem to produce a big, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo haa amɛ kɛ tso ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ koni eko loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa plantains tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when the plant goes too long without water. Watering regularly at the base and spreading dry grass or mulch around the stems keeps the roots cool and reduces flower drop.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛtee be kakadaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli. Okɛ nu afɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle he. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What causes small green caterpillars to eat holes through the fresh center leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ baai heei lɛ amli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hatch from moth eggs and feed on the tender, growing leaves inside the maize whorl. Spotting them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or organic soaps stops them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo samla ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites that suck sap from young leaves and spread viruses. Keeping weeds down and spraying neem leaf extracts or recommended treatments controls these insects before they stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni shwieɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Neem tso mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ dani amɛha tsei lɛ afee shoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and curl up in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out their roots. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects them from heat and holds moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close together to try to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ koni mikɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves them weak, thin, and prone to diseases, resulting in smaller yields overall.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe waaa, amɛhe waaa, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fɛɛ fioo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. Heavy rains can wash away soil nutrients, so adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore green foliage and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the ground. Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which naturally restores land fertility for your next harvest.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha okpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do seeds bought from the certified agro-dealer grow better than the seeds I save from my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and dry conditions while producing uniform, large crops. Saved seeds often lose their vigor and yield potential over successive generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yaa nɔ daa. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ yinɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava leaves getting sticky and covered in a white powdery substance?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ mli wa ni nɔ ko ni tamɔ powda yɛŋ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: The white coating comes from tiny sap-sucking insects called mealybugs. They feed on the plant juices, weakening the cassava and causing the leaves to stunt and drop off early.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ jɛɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ amli. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Amɛnuɔ tsei amli nu. Ehaa ŋmei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why should I cut off some healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes overcrowded branches so air and sunlight can pass freely through the cocoa canopy. This keeps humidity down, which prevents fungal problems like black pod disease from spreading.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni egbɔjɔ fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ kookoo ŋtayaa lɛ mli oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants fall off before forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when plants suffer stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or sap-sucking insects. Regular watering and protecting the plants from pests helps flowers set fruits successfully.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ nu daa ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants stay green through the dry Harmattan season while my vegetables die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ Harmattan be ni nu egbi lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni mi-aduawai lɛ gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep root systems and thick leaves that store food and water, allowing it to survive harsh weather. Vegetables have shallow roots that dry out very quickly when rain stops.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni akɛtoɔ niyenii kɛ nu he. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli. Aduawai lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, egbiɔ oya waa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crops as soon as the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to local conditions, so they absorb water and soil food rapidly. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing light and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbalaa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: How often should I apply fertilizer to my crops to get a good harvest?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Applying fertilizer at regular intervals, such as every two weeks during the active growing phase, gives your crops a steady supply of nutrients to grow strong without overloading the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli, tamɔ daa otsii enyɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni haa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni amɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee shoo.

english: Should I pour fertilizer directly on top of my crop leaves or around the base?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔse ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he?

english: Fertilizer should be applied to the soil around the plant's root zone rather than poured directly on top of the leaves, as direct contact can burn the foliage.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. tso lɛ shishifã he lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshwie baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ ehe wo mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Why are my crops growing poorly even though I gave them fertilizer once at planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli shikome pɛ yɛ dumɔ mli moŋ?

english: Crops consume nutrients continuously throughout their life cycle. A single application at planting is usually not enough, so splitting your fertilizer application into regular intervals throughout the season works much better.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli shikome pɛ yɛ dumɔ fɛɛ dumɔ mli lɛ faaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ajaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli awoɔ fãi amli. No hewɔ lɛ be muu lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to spread fertilizer by hand or use a spreading machine?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ minine baagbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwã loo mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwãa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Using a mechanical fertilizer spreader saves you from physical exhaustion, speeds up the job, and ensures that fertilizer is distributed evenly across your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha oná tɔlɛ, ehaa nitsumɔ lɛ yaa oya, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How can I cover a large farm with fertilizer without getting extremely tired?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha ŋmɔ agbo ko nɔ ni mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo bɛ mli?

english: Using a mechanical spreader or simple machine helper reduces the physical effort required to carry and scatter fertilizer, allowing you to complete heavy farm work faster with less fatigue.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛgbɛɔ nii ashwãa loo tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛgbɛɔ ashwãa ni yɔɔ mlɛo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛjie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni akɛgbɛ ashwã lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ogbeɔ onitsumɔ ni wa ni otsuɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa oya ni nijiaŋ ejeee wui.

english: Will using equipment to spread fertilizer damage my crops?
ga: Ani nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwãa lɛ baafite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When operated carefully along your field rows, mechanical spreaders apply fertilizer safely without disturbing the plants, while saving you time and labor.
ga: Beni otsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ. Mɛi ni kɛ tsɔnei shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei lɛ amli shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbaaa tsei lɛ anaa. kɛfata obei kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ he

english: Should I cut down all the existing trees on my land before planting my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You do not need to clear all trees. Keeping select trees on your farm provides valuable shade, shields young crops from scorching sun, and helps keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ojie tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli. Tsei ni ahala yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ baaha oná hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: Will having big trees on my farm steal food and water from my crops?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni miyɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: While trees do draw nutrients, properly managed trees actually improve the farm environment by lowering heat stress, wind damage, and soil erosion for your main crops.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ moŋ Tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli shihilɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo he haomɔ ni baa shi lɛ nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ fitemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi kɛha onibii titrii lɛ.

english: How do shade trees help protect my young crops in hot weather?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Trees act like living umbrellas that block harsh sunlight, lower air temperature around the crop canopy, and slow down water evaporation from the ground.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Tsɔɔmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ ni oha nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: How do I know if the trees on my farm are giving too much shade to my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha mitsei lɛ hulutsoo babaoo tsɔ?

english: If your crops look yellow, thin, or stretch upwards without producing much fruit, they are likely receiving too much shade and the surrounding tree branches need to be trimmed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ, eyɛ mlɛo, loo egbɛ eshwa ni ewooo yibii babaoo. Etamɔ nɔ ni amɛbaaná hulutsoo babaoo tsɔ. Ni ehe miihia ni atse tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a flower on my watermelon plant is female or male?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-watermelon tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji yei loo hii?

english: A female watermelon flower has a small, tiny swollen fruit right at the base of its petals, while a male flower grows on a simple thin stem without any swollen mini-fruit behind it.
ga: Watermelon fɔfɔi yei yɛ aduawai bibii ni efuu yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishi, yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi hii daa yɛ tsei bibii anɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo ni nɔ ko bibioo ko bɛ ni jɛɔ mli baa ni fũuɔ yɛ sɛɛ

english: Do all crop plants have separate male and female plants?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yɛ tsei hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi?

english: No, many crops like cocoa and tomatoes have complete flowers containing both male and female parts inside the same flower, whereas crops like pawpaw often have completely separate male and female trees.
ga: Dabi, tsei babaoo, tamɔ kookoo kɛ tomato, yɛ fɔfɔi ni eye emuu ni hiɛ nuu kɛ yoo fãi fɛɛ yɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ paw paw fɔɔ tsei hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi kwraa.

english: Why do extension officers recommend hand-pollinating crops early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ niji woɔ mli lɛ leebi lɛ?

english: In the early morning, flowers open wide, the air is cool, and pollen is fresh and sticky, which makes it much easier for fertilization to succeed before the hot afternoon sun dries out the flowers.
ga: Leebi lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Ni pollen lɛ yɛ ehee ni ekpɛtɛɔ he. Enɛ haa fɔmɔ nii ni anáa lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ agbiɔ.

english: What actually happens when a crop flower gets fertilized?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ tso ko fɔfɔi wo mli?

english: Fertilization happens when pollen dust from the male flower reaches the female part of the flower, giving the plant the signal to stop growing petals and start expanding that flower into a full fruit or seed.
ga: Fɔmɔ baa kɛji akɛ sũ ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi nuu lɛ mli lɛ shɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni ji yoo lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa okadi akɛ ekpa fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ. Ni obɔi nakai fɔfɔi lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ ni etsɔ aduawai loo dumɔwu ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do some flowers fall off my tomato plants without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off unfertilized if temperatures get too high, if insects are not visiting to move pollen around, or if the soil gets too dry while the plant is blooming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji kooloi bibii baaa koni amɛbajie pollen lɛ, Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ be mli ni tso lɛ miifɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop downward during the middle of the day even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Cassava leaves naturally turn away or droop during intense afternoon sunlight to protect themselves from losing too much water, and they will perk back up once the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. ni ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow before the ears even show up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ po jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which it needs early on to build green leaves and strong stalks before producing corn ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii kɛjɛ shishijee Koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei ni wa dani ajie ŋmãa toi.

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, cowpeas focus all their energy on growing tall leafy stems instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, Cowpeas kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ baai ni daraa lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: How do I know when my papaya tree is ready to start bearing fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mipapaya tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaawo yibii?

english: A papaya tree shows it is mature enough to produce fruit when small flower buds begin appearing at the joints where the leaf stems meet the main trunk, usually around 4 to 6 months after planting.
ga: Papaya tso lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ewo yibii kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii lɛ je kpo. Amɛjeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ he ni baa lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 4 kɛyashi 6 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if a plantain sucker is ready to be removed and planted somewhere else?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain suckers lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaawo amɛ yɛ he kroko?

english: A plantain sucker is ready to transplant when it reaches about 2 to 3 feet tall, has thin spear-like leaves, and has formed a solid bulb base that can survive being cut away from the mother plant.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu kɛji amɛshɛ aaafee ninetalɔi 2 kɛyashi 3 ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ. ni efeɔ bulb shishitoo ni wa ni baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji akɛ afo lɛ kɛjɛ tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and easily scorched by hot sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains provides living umbrellas that shield the young cocoa leaves from heat and help keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akafite.

english: How do I know when my cassava is mature enough to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is time when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the earth around the base of the stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Why do we need to make large soil mounds before planting yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔma sũ agbo ko dani wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose earth to grow long, thick tubers without hitting hard ground. Mounds also keep water from gathering around the tuber, which prevents rots during heavy rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii kakadaji ni mli tse ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ hewalɛ. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa fite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for growth, often caused by poor soil or heavy rains washing nutrients away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛyaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that burrows into the center whorl of maize plants to feed on new growth.
ga: Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ ŋtayaa mli koni eye ŋmãa tsei heei ni eda lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are not enough insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or thrips that spread plant viruses, or by intense heat stress during dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli

english: The first rain is often followed by a heatwave or dry spell that dries out the topsoil, scorching delicate young shoots before the main rainy season settles.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be loo nugbɔshiimɔ be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shãa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my land better for next season's crop?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants break down after harvest, they leave natural fertilizer in the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei gbee shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Tsei shĩɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my farm while my crops are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and will quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil food from young plants that are not yet strong enough to compete.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe awo akaŋshii mli lɛ amli oya.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong direct sunlight. Tall shade trees act like umbrellas that protect the delicate young leaves from sun damage and keep the soil moist during hot days.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei kakadaji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni buɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the maize plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and food. They stretch upwards to reach light instead of putting energy into growing big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Abele tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes turning yellow and twisting up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow, twisted leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems stops this from happening.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ baatsi enɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and crooked when planted in hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand easily under the ground. Hard or stony soil squeezes the growing tubers, making them crooked and preventing them from reaching full size.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi miimɔ bulbs ni miida lɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa eda kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow many green leaves but drop their flowers without making peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miikwɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni afeee chili?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus only on growing leaves. Without balanced food and proper watering, the plant gets stressed and drops its flowers before fruit can form.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ pɛ. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni ja kɛ nu ni sa bɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baaná haomɔ ni ebaaha efɔfɔi ashwie shi dani ewo yibii.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over right when the fruit bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai akutsei lɛ je shishi amɛdara pɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and do not hold deep in the ground. When the fruit bunch becomes heavy, it pulls the plant down, so supporting the trunk with a strong wooden pole is necessary.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ batsɔ tsii Ebaagbala tso lɛ kɛba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tsei ni wa afi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra little branches growing at the bottom of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ shweremɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: These extra branches, called suckers, steal water and food from the main trunk. Removing them keeps the tree strong and allows all the energy to go into making cocoa pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei niji krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsɔne wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ewajeɔ tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize yield less food than new store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ haaa niyenii babaoo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give high yields only in their first planting. Seeds saved from the harvest lose that special strength, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off during the hottest weeks of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from turning into fruit. When the air is too hot, the plant sheds the flowers to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Tsi enaa koni ekatsu nii jogbaŋŋ Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Wild weeds are naturally suited to the local soil and climate, so they drink water and take nutrients faster than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to grow.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ sa shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shia tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight and lose moisture quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living shelter and keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and produce food. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo niyenii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or beans on my plot before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this left-behind nitrogen, growing stronger without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ. Edaraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and getting light yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant stem cuttings is the most effective way to protect your farm from this disease.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nibii ni afolɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hela nɛɛ he.

english: What causes small holes in my cabbage leaves, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii baa kaaba mli ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ otsi naa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by caterpillars, such as the diamondback moth larvae, eating the leaf tissue. You can control them by checking leaves regularly, handpicking caterpillars early, or applying safe biological or chemical sprays recommended for leafy vegetables.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei, tamɔ diamondback moth larvae, ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni baa kabaaji baa lɛ mli baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ daa. Halamɔ ŋmeii mra. Aloo okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii kɛha aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without producing any tomatoes when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ tomato ko baaa beni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil stress tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to conserve energy and water. Watering consistently in the morning and placing dry grass mulch around the base of the plant helps keep the root zone cool and moist.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni akɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Nu daa leebi ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi abɔle he. Shishitoo lɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why should I avoid planting my pepper seeds during heavy rains instead of the early rain period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui adumɔ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli moŋ fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours can wash away delicate pepper seeds, drown young roots, and cause fungal root rot in soggy soil. Planting during early light rains gives the roots time to develop deep into the soil before heavy rains begin.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. shishifãi bibii ni shwieɔ nu mli ni ekɛ fungal shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: What will happen to my crop if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in weak, thin stalks and small, underdeveloped cobs rather than full, heavy ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ mli baa ji ŋmãa ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa bibii ni edako. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona ŋmãa toi ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ

english: Groundnuts develop their pods underground. After the yellow flower is pollinated above ground, the plant sends down a specialized stem called a peg that burrows into the soil, allowing the nut to grow safely under the dirt away from sun and pests.
ga: Peanuts feɔ pods yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni hulu la kɛ kooloi bibii bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Yam tubers rot easily if they get cut or bruised during harvest, left in direct sunlight on the field, or stored in hot, dark rooms without proper airflow where moisture builds up and allows fungi to grow.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afo amɛ loo atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Shi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ. aloo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni mli ewo duŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. He ni ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ abua naa ni eha ŋmɔtɔ akwɛ̃ yɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to apply fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away applied fertilizer from the soil surface before the roots can absorb it. This wastes your money and deprives the crops of the nutrients they need.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ heɔ shika ni ehaa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same place drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and stops pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba ŋmãa mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, harsh sunlight dries out their leaves and burns them. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides necessary shade and soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni eshã baai lɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ baaha shade ni he hiaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ aba klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ amli.

english: Yam is a climbing vine, and lifting its leaves off the ground with stakes allows the plant to get maximum sunlight and air. This helps the plant produce larger tubers and prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Atomɔ ji wain tso ni kwɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ bulbs wuji ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and rolling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are signs that the maize is stressed, usually from a lack of nitrogen in the soil, prolonged dry spells, or attacks by pests like the Fall Armyworm.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa miihao. Nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is inconsistent, making it difficult for the roots to absorb calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: You should leave only 2 to 3 suckers per plantain tree (the mother, a medium follower, and a small shoot). Allowing too many suckers causes them to fight for nutrients, resulting in small plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi ŋmeii bibii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ yɛ dumɔwu kome mli (tso nyɛ, ŋmeii ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, kɛ ŋmeii bibii). Shikpɔŋhosomɔi babaoo baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the essential food they need to grow strong and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack due to expanding roots underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ hewɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, heavy rain, or a lack of water and key nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii titrii ni he hiaa waa lɛ ahe. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient out of the soil, or weeds might be stealing it away from your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo jwɛi baanyɛ aju niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have a special ability to take nitrogen food from the air and drop it into the soil. Planting them with maize feeds your soil naturally and helps your maize grow better without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛjieɔ nitrogen nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa abɛi lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves to save water during dry spells, similar to how people sweat less when water is scarce. The plant is not dead; it is resting and keeping its energy in the underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Etamɔ bɔ ni gbɔmɛi shwieɔ latsaa fioo kɛji nu efo amɛmli lɛ. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ejɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my groundnut flowers bend down and dig into the soil after they open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants bloom above the ground, but the nuts actually grow underground. After the flower is pollinated, the stem grows downwards into the dirt so the groundnut pod can develop safely beneath the soil.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmei ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make food for big tubers. Stakes lift the leaves off the ground where they can get maximum sun and stay away from damp diseases on the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni hulu la babaoo he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshɛ amɛtso lɛ he koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ bulbs wuji lɛ. Tso lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like aphids or mites hiding under the leaf. They suck the juice out of the leaves and spread plant sicknesses that stunt the growth of your pepper crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi. Amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ dalɛ naa lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy and humid weather. High humidity and poor airflow around the trees make it worse, so clearing weeds and harvesting ripe pods quickly helps prevent it.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni bɔleɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hela lɛ he okadii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni abua naa oya lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the heat gets too high, when water supply jumps from very dry to very wet, or when tiny insects attack the blossoms. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant keep its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ nu lɛ tsake kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant gets enough nourishment to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Tsoi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Why does swamp rice survive in standing water while my maize crop rots if flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ swamp rice hiɔ shi yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ be mli ni mi-corn lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shi lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special tubes inside their stems that act like snort tubes, allowing oxygen to travel from the air down to their roots underwater. Maize roots do not have these tubes, so they drown and rot if covered in water for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔnei ni akɛmuɔ nii. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, egboɔ ni egboɔ kɛji akɛ awo lɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why can't I just scatter oil palm seeds across my farm instead of digging proper holes for each one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ magbɛ mu tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafo bu kɛha ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ?

english: Scattering seeds causes plants to grow too close together, forcing them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every tree enough room to grow strong roots and bear large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui amli gbalamɔ haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ ni ewo aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa trees too close to each other so I can fit more trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ bɔni afee ni anyɛ adu tsei krokomɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Overcrowded cocoa trees grow tall and weak as they reach for sunlight, and their roots tangle instead of spreading. Proper spacing allows air to flow, reduces disease spread, and results in more pods per tree.
ga: Kakao tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli. Ha helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aba shi ni ekɛ pods babaoo baa tso fɛɛ tso nɔ

english: Why did my cocoa yield drop drastically after I tried a new spraying mix recommended by a neighbor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibiiwoo lɛ ba shi kwraa beni mika spray mix hee ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ mikwɛ lɛ?

english: Different farms have different pest problems and tree ages. Using unapproved chemical mixtures or applying them at the wrong time can burn cocoa flowers and young pods, ruining a harvest that would have otherwise been bountiful.
ga: Okwaafoi fɛɛ ŋmɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai kɛ tsei afii sɔrɔtoi. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli loo akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Efiteɔ nibii ni baanyɛ afee babaoo lɛ.

english: What makes my cocoa trees suddenly stop producing pods even though the trees look green?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi cacao tsei lɛ miikpa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ?

english: Trees can lose their fruit if they suffer from nutrient shortages, pest attacks like capsids, or if key management steps like pruning and shade control are missed during the flowering season.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ afite yibii kɛji akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids, loo kɛji akɛ amɛkwɛɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Will planting shade trees on my cocoa farm take away nutrients from my cocoa crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli?

english: Selected shade trees actually help cocoa by protecting leaves from harsh direct sun, preserving moisture in the soil, and dropping leaves that decompose into natural fertilizer for your cocoa roots.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua kookoo diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ni oshɛrɛ baai ni egboi lɛ oshwie akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-cocoa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Can I plant palm nuts collected from any farm, or do I need specific seedlings from a nursery?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei tsei ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli loo dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ he miihia mi?

english: Nuts collected from random farms often grow into wild-type trees that take many years to produce fruit and yield very little oil. High-yield nursery seedlings are specially bred to produce large fruit bunches much faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni afee amɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ amli lɛ daa kɛfeɔ koo mli tsei ni heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii ni amɛwoɔ mu fioo ko pɛ. Akwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii wuji oya kwraa.

english: Why do the cocoa pods on my farm turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excess wetness and damp air. Keeping weeds low and pruning overgrown branches helps sunlight and wind dry out the farm, stopping the disease.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ fe nine mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ ba shi ni afo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akagbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekpa hela lɛ

english: Why are the fruit bunches on my oil palm trees drying up before they get big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai akui ni yɔɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Oil palms require consistent water and balanced soil nutrients, especially potassium. Dry bunches occur when trees experience water stress during dry spells or suffer from overcrowded planting.
ga: Mu tsei biɔ nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja. titri lɛ potassium Dry bunches baa kɛji tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo ena amanehulu yɛ nu ni eyi obɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are the small flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when trees are stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or attacks by tiny insects. Ensuring gentle shade and spraying against insects before flowering protects the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tutua tsei lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be blɛoo kɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ nɔ dani fɔfɔi lɛ baawo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it important to cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or unnecessary branches so the tree can send all its energy and nutrients directly into growing healthy flowers and pods, rather than supporting extra leaf growth.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ baa kpahi nɛ a daa ɔ he wami.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost gives the crop the energy it needs to grow healthy green leaves and produce full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why should I cut cassava stems into short slant pieces before planting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ amli kukuji dani okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting cassava stems into short pieces with several growth buds forces the plant to concentrate its energy on pushing out strong roots and shoots quickly from those specific nodes, leading to higher tuber yields.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afoɔ lɛ kukuji ni ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛjɛɔ nakai fãi pɔtɛɛi lɛ amli lɛ ajiemɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tuber yibii babaoo.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade flowers nearby to attract pollinators helps the blossoms turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. aloo pollination ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ shĩa mli fɔfɔii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ koni ekɛgbala pollinatorbii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɔfɔii.

english: Why do the leaves on my cowpea plants curl up and fold together during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ekome yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves fold during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing water. By exposing less leaf surface to the sun, the plant conserves moisture so it can survive hot, dry weather.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Tsei baanyɛ ahiɛ fɛ̃i mli kɛtsɔ baa lɛ nɔ hulu la ni baa shi lɛ nɔ. Koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the soil. Rotating with legumes like peanuts replenishes soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to produce energy for subterranean tuber growth. Keeping the leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaf spot diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ hela naa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that create living umbrellas, providing necessary shade and preserving soil moisture for cocoa trees during their early development.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ amɛshweremɔ shishijee mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt completely during the heat of the day but stand up again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Shi te shi ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: Plants lose water faster through their leaves than their roots can absorb from the soil in strong sun, causing temporary wilting. overnight, root pressure refills the stems with water, restoring the plant's upright structure.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli Gbi gbɛkɛ ko mli lɛ, shishifãi ni nyɛɔ enɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yiɔ nu ekoŋŋ, ni ehaa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my crops right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants with shallow, aggressive root systems adapted specifically to jumpstart growth at the slightest drop of water. They steal nutrients and water from crops unless cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni afee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni eda oya kɛ nu fioo pɛ. Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ja ajie amɛ mra.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots coming out from the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and light. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which ensures larger, heavier bunches of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi, loo tsei lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ la. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni efata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baawo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow fast. Adding manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer gives the maize the food it needs to build strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help the maize grow better without extra fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cowpea kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa kroko fataaa he lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that pull nitrogen directly out of the air and fix it into the soil. When planted together, the cowpea naturally feeds the soil, sharing fertilizer with your maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ adu Cowpeas yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ o-corn lɛ baaja lɛ nɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They spend all their energy growing tall to reach light, leaving no energy to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛshɛ la he. Hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni baaha aná ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I plant my cassava cuttings at an angle instead of standing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni madamɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stem cuttings at a slant helps the plant form roots spread out near the surface of the soil. This spread gives the tubers more room to grow bigger and makes them much easier to harvest later.
ga: Kasava ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwãa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Nɛkɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ naa hegbɛ babaoo ni amɛdaraa, ni ehaa sɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers during the hot dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry harmattan winds suck moisture out of plants very quickly. Dropping flowers is the cocoa tree's natural defense mechanism to save water and energy so the main tree survives until the rains return.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli oya. Fɔfɔi ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves inward to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the scorching sun, which prevents water from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akabaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster after rain than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants with deep, tough root systems already adapted to your local soil. They wake up instantly with rainfall, while farm crop seeds take more time to germinate and settle their roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛte shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ nugbɔ lɛ miinɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui biɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtswa shishifãi.

english: Why do tiny white insects under my pepper leaves cause the leaves to wrinkle and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yɛŋ Mi-pepper baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Those tiny insects, called whiteflies, suck the vital sap out of the leaves and spread plant diseases. As the plant loses its food supply to the insects, the leaves wrinkle up and growth stalls.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai kooloi bibii lɛ akɛ whiteflies. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa. Kɛ tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii nɔ kɛha kooloi lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaakpa dalɛ.

english: Why is cassava able to survive and yield food even if I do not have enough help to weed my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛjieɔ jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ.

english: Cassava is a very hardy crop with deep roots that store energy. Once it grows a thick canopy of leaves after a few months, it blocks sunlight from reaching the ground, naturally slowing down weed growth on its own.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni wa waa. Eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni kɛ hewalɛ toɔ. Beni efee ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, Ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I wait until the leaves of my yam vines turn completely brown before digging up the tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa dani mafolɔ tsei lɛ amli?

english: When yam leaves turn brown and dry, it shows the plant has finished sending all its energy down into the underground tuber. Harvesting too early leaves you with smaller yams that spoil quickly in storage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛmaje shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa. Kɛ́ okpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋmeii bibii ni baafite oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive. Without shade trees or plantains nearby, the intense sun dries out the soil and burns the delicate leaves of young cocoa trees before their roots can fully establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa cacao tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to build high mounds of dirt to plant my yams instead of planting them in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa sũ ni nɔ kwɔ koni mikɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down into the earth. Building loose, high dirt mounds makes it easy for the roots to expand freely and prevents rain water from pooling around the seed yam and rotting it.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya, ni ehaaa nugbɔ nu lɛ abua amɛhe naa. Sweet potato dumɔwui ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from my hybrid maize harvest for the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest will produce weaker plants, smaller cob sizes, and much lower yields overall.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ aba. Cob dalɛ ji bibioo ni nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a vital food for crop growth. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant steals nutrients from its older, lower leaves to keep its new top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Abele juɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ koni eha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize help my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This process feeds the soil and acts as a natural fertilizer for nearby crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves to save water during dry conditions. Dropping leaves reduces water loss through evaporation, allowing the tubers underground to stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruits when the heat gets very high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ aduawai kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from being pollinated. Without successful pollination, the plant drops the flower stems instead of producing tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi pollination naa Kɛji pollination lɛ yeee omanye Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔii ashishifãi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaawo tomato.

english: Why shouldn't I water my vegetable garden in the middle of the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ nu shwieɔ o-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering under hot afternoon heat causes most of the water to evaporate before reaching roots. Water drops left on leaves under intense sun can also encourage fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ awo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hewalɛ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from the undersides of leaves, or by a virus spread by those pests. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite tsei ahe tsei lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight and fresh air into the farm to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ duŋ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Koni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do vegetables grown inside a greenhouse structure mature faster than the ones I plant in my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ oya fe aduawai ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Greenhouses control the plant's environment by reducing extreme heat, wind, and heavy rain stress while keeping humidity steady. When crops spend less energy defending themselves against harsh weather, they direct all their energy into growing foliage and fruit much faster.
ga: Greenhouses kudɔɔ tso lɛ shihilɛ kɛtsɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, hulutsoo be fɛɛ be lɛ mlihiɛmɔ. Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa waa lɛ ahe. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii kɛha baai kɛ aduawai adalɛ oya kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any fruit when the afternoon heat becomes too strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, heat stress makes the pollen inside tomato flowers sterile, preventing fertilization. To save water and energy, the tomato plant naturally sheds these unfertilized flowers instead of letting them turn into fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Heat stress haa pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela. ni etsi fɔmɔ nii anaa Bɔni afee ni akɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ aba Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nɛkɛ fɔfɔi ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli nɛɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha efee nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn yellow and scorch when I remove all the surrounding shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees to filter the sun and keep the air humid, bright sunlight destroys the green chlorophyll in the leaves, burning them and stunt growth.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulu lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ klorofil eŋɔli ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. shãa ni ehaaa dalɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like narrow tubes during the dry, hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaf rolling is a survival trick used by maize plants to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun. By rolling its leaves, the plant traps moisture inside and slows down water loss through evaporation during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni abɛi tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛba baa lɛ nɔ hulu la shi. kɛtsɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛhaa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fiofio kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning light yellow while the top leaves remain dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen moves easily inside the plant, so when nutrients are low, the plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen lɛ nyiɛɔ yɛ tsei amli oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii faaa Tsei lɛ juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper fruits come out bent and misshapen instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efite moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Deformed peppers happen when small sap-sucking insects damage the flower buds or when the soil gets wet and dry unevenly during fruit development. Consistent watering and early insect protection ensure smooth, well-shaped peppers.
ga: Afeɔ ŋmeii ni efite lɛ kɛ́ kooloi bibii miinu amɛmli nu lɛ. Fɔfɔi ashishifãi ni fiteɔ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni egbi yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ kooloi ahebuu mra Eyeɔ ebuaa chili lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do white, powdery spots spread across my garden leaves after a heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei lɛ ahe yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: High moisture and damp air create the perfect conditions for fungal spores to germinate on leaf surfaces. The white powder is a living fungus that feeds on the leaf's food reserves, slowing down plant growth if not managed.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa fungal spores lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji ŋmei ni hiɛ ka ni yeɔ niyenii ni ato yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ ada blɛoo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves but leaves me with small, thin roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen causes the plant to put all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy tops above ground. For big tubers under the soil, cassava needs less nitrogen and more potassium to move starch down into the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ. Kɛha yitso agbo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, Cassava biɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium fioo ko pɛ koni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ aya shi kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does cutting off the side branches of my tomato plants lead to bigger tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ afo tomato tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ, ehaa tomato lɛ feɔ agbo lɛ?
