english: A plant has a limited amount of food and water. Removing excess side shoots stops the plant from wasting energy on extra stems and directs all nutrients into making the remaining fruits larger and healthier.
ga: Tsei bɛ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaaa tso lɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ adara ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do pest insects multiply so much faster inside a net house than they do in an open farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ebɔ he lɛ amli fe ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Net houses keep out rain and wind while trapping warmth, creating ideal breeding conditions. They also keep out natural insect predators like spiders and birds, allowing any pest that gets inside to multiply rapidly without natural enemies.
ga: Mesh greenhouses tsiɔ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ dɔlɛ mli. Enɛ haa fɔmɔ shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa. Amɛbuɔ mɔ he hu kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ okpoi ahe, ni amɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ babaoo oya ni adebɔɔ mli henyɛlɔi bɛ amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fall off during the dry season? Is my crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ani miŋmɔshi nibii miigbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to save water and protect itself from heat. The roots underground are still alive and healthy, and the plant will grow fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli koni akɛbu nu he ni ebu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ. Ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Extreme heat or irregular watering causes tomato plants stress. When the plant gets too hot or dry, it drops its flowers to save energy rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ mli edɔ loo egbi tsɔ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu aduawai.

english: Why do my watermelons crack open on the field before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: When a dry spell is followed by sudden heavy rain or overwatering, the inside of the watermelon absorbs water too fast and grows quicker than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to burst.
ga: Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa loo nu babaoo fa tsɔ nyiɛɔ hɔmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Watermelon lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ ni edaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. ha efo

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, or the ground is flooded with too much water, which stops the plant roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ mumɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper roots rot when rain sits on my flat farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need air in the soil to survive. When water collects on flat land without proper drainage, the roots drown and soil-dwelling fungi attack them, causing root rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia pepper shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatutua amɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What is chewing holes in the center leaves of my maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni atsɔ mli yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the hot day and crawl out at night to eat the tender growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni efoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni eyaye baai ni miida ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why does striga weed keep appearing in the same field where I plant maize every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ striga jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ ŋmɔji ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Striga, or witchweed, thrives in tired soils that have lost their nutrients from continuous planting of the same crop. Planting legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas helps rebuild the soil and starves out the weed.
ga: Striga, loo Witchweed lɛ, shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nii efo mli kɛtsɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground where they could rot and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni edɔ yɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo.

english: Why should I cut away the small shoot suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow around the main plant, they fight for the same water, light, and nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves more energy for the main stem to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ naa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my tomatoes when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje tomato dumɔ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ be lɛ bashɛ?

english: Wait until the rains become steady rather than planting after the very first rain. Planting during erratic initial rains can cause seedlings to dry out or get washed away by sudden heavy downpours.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shishijee nugbɔshiimɔ be ni bɛ faŋŋ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ ahoo amɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my new tomatoes in the exact same field where I just harvested my last tomato crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato hee yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa mi naagbee tomato ŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli pɛŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly in the same spot allows soil-borne pests and diseases like bacterial wilt to build up in the ground. Rotating tomatoes with crops like maize or cassava starves out these diseases.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tamɔ bacteria wilt aba. ebua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tomatoi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ. Ye obua ni atsĩ helai nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young tomato plants curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai bibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually caused by Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by extreme heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: What causes my tomato plants to suddenly wilt and die even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni haa mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease that blocks the movement of water inside the stem. It lives in the soil and thrives in warm, overly wet conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehiɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo fe nine yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turn dark brown or black before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering or dry spells while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo hulutsoo be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil gets too dry, or when insects like thrips attack the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutuaa fɔfɔii.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes split and crack open right on the plant before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miigba ni egbɛ eshwa tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani mikpa lɛ?

english: Cracking occurs when plants get a sudden heavy supply of water after a dry period, causing the inside of the fruit to expand faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Kpãmɔ baa kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo nu babaoo mli trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Is it better for me to water my crop early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because roots absorb water before the sun heats up the ground. Afternoon watering wastes water through evaporation and can shock the hot plants.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani hulu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ahe afee shoo yɛ latsaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: How does putting dried grass around the base of my plants help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛfataa tso shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Adding grass or leaf mulch keeps the soil cool, prevents weeds from growing, and retains soil moisture so you do not have to water as frequently.
ga: Jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ.

english: Should I pick my tomatoes while they are fully red or while they are still slightly green if I am sending them to market?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tomato be mli ni eyɛ tɔrɔmɔɔ kwraa loo be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ fioo lolo kɛji mikɛmaje jara nɔ?

english: Pick them when they are just starting to turn pink if you are sending them to far markets like Accra. Fully red tomatoes will crush easily and rot during long transport trips.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ amɛ be mli ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ pinki kɛkɛ kɛji ootsu amɛ kɛmiiya jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ tamɔ Accra. Tomato tsuru ni egbɔ lɛ mli gbalaa oya ni egboɔ yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when there is too much sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct, intense sun and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living umbrellas that shield the young cocoa from heat stress and help keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: Can I plant cassava in low-lying land that stays flooded during the heavy rains?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots will easily rot if left sitting in waterlogged soil for too long. Cassava grows best in well-drained, loose soil or on raised soil mounds where excess water can drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni etse ehe nɔ. aloo yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to start sowing my maize when the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives steady, deep rainfall over a few consecutive days rather than planting after the very first light shower, which can dry up and kill seed sprouts.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ, moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do people tell me to tie my growing yam vines onto wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso ni miida lɛ akpɛtɛ tso ko he lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs plenty of sunlight on its leaves to produce food for the root. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they catch maximum sunlight, stay healthy, and produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo koni eshɛ amɛbaai lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ aba mli babaoo. Ha oná hewalɛ ni ofɔ yitsoi wuji

english: Is it good or bad if I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field alongside my maize?
ga: Ani ehi loo ehiii kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi?

english: Planting beans with maize is very beneficial because legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into a natural fertilizer in the soil, which feeds the neighboring maize plant.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same spot on my farm every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up, leading to lower harvests over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does adding dried poultry manure to my farm soil make my vegetables grow so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbi fata shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ, ehaa mi-aduawai lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ?

english: Poultry manure is rich in essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, which give plants the fuel they need to build green leaves, strong stems, and healthy fruit rapidly.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium babaoo yɛ kooloi ashishifã mli. ni haa tso lɛ naa tsofa ni ekɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. tso ni mli wa kɛ aduawai ni mli wa oya

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants showing small holes and getting chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ ni aaaye lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Early scouting and applying appropriate biopesticides or organic treatments help prevent them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii mra. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds to grow in my field reduce the total harvest I get?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, groundwater, and plant food from your crops. When weeds compete with your plants, your crops cannot get enough nutrients to reach full yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Beni jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ miitswa akaŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn dark and rotten before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ ashishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani etsɔɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: Dark, soft bottoms on tomatoes are usually caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato ni shishi yɔɔ ediŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ mli baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. loo enine shɛɔ nu nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under direct hot sun. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without producing good fruit when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting them with proper spacing allows each plant to get enough light and food to grow thick stems and healthy fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔ ni akɛ gbɛ ni sa kpãa gbee lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni mli wa akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen or are sitting in waterlogged soil. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving drainage helps the leaves regain their green color and produce better grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli loo amɛta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni ooofee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field make my next season's maize grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants harvest, they leave this natural fertilizer in the ground, which feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa tsei lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and fall off during the hot dry season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, kɛ́ awo amɛ nu po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl during intense heat to conserve moisture. If temperatures are too high or watering is irregular, the plant drops its leaves because it is stressed and cannot move nutrients properly from the roots.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa be mli koni amɛbu fɛ̃i. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa Tsei lɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe ejɔ amɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which causes the plant to build leaves instead of holding onto blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings need to be planted at a slant in the soil instead of standing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ nɔ ni ja lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stem cuttings at an angle helps roots spread out wider and deeper in the soil, which allows the plant to produce larger tubers and anchor firmly against heavy rain and winds.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo ni eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and misshapen when the soil in my farm is hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni efite be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft earth to push downward and expand. Hard or compacted soil physically stops the tuber from swelling properly, leading to short, bent, or stunted tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛtsi kɛya shi ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ lɛ baatsi bulb lɛ naa koni ekafu jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ kuku, ebɔleɔ loo egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do armyworms show up and destroy my maize field right after the first heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay hundreds of eggs on soft green maize leaves immediately after the early rains start. The warm weather causes these eggs to hatch quickly, and young caterpillars begin feeding on the fresh leaves before they are easily spotted.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ haa wɔji nɛɛ fɔɔ oya. Ni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ baai heei yeli shishi dani anaa amɛ mlɛo.

english: Why does striga weed attach itself to my maize roots and make the plants dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ striga jwɛi lɛ miikpɛtɛ mi-abele shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa tso lɛ miigbi lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that cannot make its own food. Its tiny seeds lie in the soil and attach directly to maize roots to suck out water and nutrients, causing the maize plant to look stunted and dried out.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni nyɛɛɛ afee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii. Edumɔwui bibii lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛmu nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbi.

english: Yes, staking lifts yam leaves into direct sunlight so the plant can make more food. Yam vines that are allowed to trail on the hot ground produce much smaller tubers compared to vines supported by stakes.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Sweet potato wain tsei ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛnyiɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ baaha bulbs bibii kwraa fe wain tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei anɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying top-dressing fertilizers like NPK or urea gives the plant the energy it needs to form good ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo toi kpakpai.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or beans after harvesting my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Corn feeds heavily on soil nutrients and leaves the ground tired. Cowpeas and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing and restoring the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaa sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Cowpeas kɛ beans buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli kɛ hewalɛwoo kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does putting dry grass or leaves around my crops help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the soil during dry spells, stops weeds from growing, and turns into rich soil food as it rots.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi shwieɔ Dumɔwui ahe ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ kɛ́ egbo.

english: What is making small holes in the leaf stems of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: Small holes and chewed leaf edges on young corn are typically caused by Fall Armyworms hiding inside the central growth funnel. Spraying recommended pesticides early in the morning or late evening targets these pests effectively.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii kɛ baai ni ashɛreɔ yɛ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ baa. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baagbe kooloi nɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava root rot happens when water stays trapped around the roots for too long during heavy rains, allowing fungal diseases to grow. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets extra water drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking sap from the tender leaves, or by viruses they spread. Using neem oil spray or suitable insecticides helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ kooloi nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out suddenly, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ trukaa loo kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Extra suckers act like hungry children competing for the main plant's food and water. Leaving only one strong replacement sucker ensures your main plantain tree has enough strength to grow a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbekɛbii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oyɛ sucker kome pɛ ni he wa ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ, ebaaha o-plantain tso titri lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ efee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: When is the best time of year for me to plant new cocoa seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant is at the beginning of the major rainy season, usually around May or June in Ghana. Planting when the soil is naturally wet gives the roots enough moisture to establish strongly before the harsh dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ May loo June mli yɛ Ghana. Dumɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná hewalɛ dani hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ aba.

english: Is it okay for me to plant food crops like plantain or cassava alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makwɛ niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava? Mi kokoo tso ni mli tse lɛ nɔ

english: Plantain is great to intercrop because its large leaves provide vital shade and moisture for young cocoa. However, avoid planting heavy root crops like cassava too close, as their aggressive root systems steal water and nutrients from the young cocoa trees.
ga: Plantains hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni aduɔ yɛ amɛteŋ ejaakɛ amɛbaai wuji lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni shishifãi ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi ni boteɔ mli lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or permanent forest trees to act as living shields against heat and retain soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui loo koo mli tsei ni hiɔ shi daa. Koni etsu nii akɛ gãimlibii ni buɔ wala he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni eha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the cocoa plant is missing essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or it is getting too much direct sunlight without enough shade. Applying suitable organic manure or approved cocoa fertilizers usually fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ ni ebɛ hulutsoo be ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ kookoo mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsake naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off side shoots and extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo tso ko he ŋmeii kɛ niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-productive branches (like chupons) that drain energy away from the tree. It opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can circulate, which prevents fungal diseases and encourages the tree to grow bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni wooo yibii (tamɔ chupons) lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji ni shwieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Egbeleɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa lɛ naa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji.

english: How often should I clear weeds from around my cocoa plants?
ga: Esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Shii enyiɛ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Weeding should be done about 3 to 4 times a year, especially around the base of young trees. Removing weeds stops them from stealing fertilizers, nutrients, and water from your cocoa.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ shii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ afi mli, titri lɛ yɛ tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju ŋmɔshi nibii, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ okokoo lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, dark, and overly humid farm environments. Clearing tall weeds, pruning dense branches for airflow, and removing infected pods quickly helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be fe nine. tall weed removal Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: What causes tiny holes and chewed edges on the new leaves of my cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Kɛ ŋmeii ni ashɛre yɛ mi-kookoo baai heei lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: This damage is usually caused by pests such as capsids (mirids) or leaf-eating caterpillars. Regular farm monitoring and applying recommended, safe pest control measures help protect young foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ capsids (mirids) loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ ni afeɔ daa kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe.

english: How long will my new cocoa seedlings take before they start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ baahe dani amɛje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana typically start producing their first pods in about 2 to 3 years with good care, whereas older traditional varieties took 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baahe afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ.

english: Why do so many flowers drop off my cocoa tree without growing into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: It is normal for cocoa trees to produce far more flowers than pods. Drops happen because only a few flowers get pollinated by tiny insects called midge flies, or because the tree drops excess flowers during periods of water stress or nutrient shortage.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo kwraa fe ŋmeii. Nɔ ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa ejaakɛ fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛhe. Atsɛɔ amɛ midge ŋmeii. Aloo akɛni tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine yɛ be mli ni nu he naagba loo niyenii mli hewalɛ he ehiaaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn yellow and droop after heavy rain falls on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil or flood the roots so they cannot breathe. When roots drown or lack nutrients, the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛ nu abɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashɛ he ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ bote nu mli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon sun even though it rained heavily yesterday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ nyɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw moisture from the wet soil, causing temporary wilting until the temperature drops.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my farm right before a big rain comes or after the rain stops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba loo beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is better to apply fertilizer right after rain when the soil is moist. If you apply it right before heavy rain, the water will wash the fertilizer away before the crop roots can absorb it.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa Nu hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani tso shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots under the soil are thin and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes the cassava plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and tall stems above ground instead of storing energy in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ɔ ngɛ tso sisi nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Extreme heat, sudden changes in rainfall, or lack of water cause stress to the plant. To save its own life, the plant drops its flowers instead of spending energy to grow fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔshiimɔ tsakemɔi trukaa Loo nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei lɛ anɔ. Bɔni afee ni ehere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow thin, weak, and tall when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛfeɔ shwiili kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Vegetables need direct sunlight to make their food and grow strong. When shaded by tall trees, they stretch unnaturally upward to search for light, making their stems thin and fragile.
ga: Hulu la he miihia aduawai tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhoo ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Beni eyɔɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko shishi lɛ Ekpãa ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛtaoɔ la. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, and deep soil to expand downward easily. If the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, the tuber struggles to push through and becomes crooked and stunted.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛbaakoto ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster than my main crops right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ be fɛɛ be beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are tough and can stay alive in the dry soil for a long time. Once the rain hits them, they absorb water faster than cultivated crop seeds and grow quickly to grab available light and food.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wa ni amɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nu oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ. ni edaa oya koni ekɛ la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why did many of the maize seeds I planted fail to grow out of the soil after the rain fell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep in the soil, planted in waterlogged ground, or attacked by insects and fungi in the damp earth, they rot before they can sprout.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ tutuaa lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ baagbo dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do black spots and white powder appear on my crop leaves during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: High humidity and wet leaves create the perfect condition for fungal diseases to spread quickly. Fungi thrive in moist, cool air and easily infect damp leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Kwao lɛ shwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli edɔ mli ni eyeɔ baai ni efɔ lɛ hela oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Kɛjɛ be mli ni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need protection from harsh sunlight and heat. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides shelter, keeping the soil moist and protecting tender young cocoa leaves from scorching in the sun.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ baanyɛ aha mɔ ko aná wɔɔhe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebu kookoo baai bibii ahe koni hulu akashã amɛ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. The plant moves nitrogen to newer leaves at the top, leaving older leaves hungry, which can be corrected by applying nitrogen fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Shi baai momo lɛ hɔmɔ Abaanyɛ ajaje enɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What is eating holes in the middle leaf whorl of my young corn and leaving brown dust inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baa teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They crawl inside the central funnel of the maize plant to eat tender leaf tissue, leaving behind ragged leaf holes and brown waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛkplekeɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji. Amɛshiɔ bu yɛ baai ni etse kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: How do I know which end of a cassava stick to push into the soil when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ matsi kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings have small leaf nodes or buds along the stick. Look at these buds—they should point upwards toward the sky so the shoots grow straight up and roots develop properly in the soil.
ga: Cassava nine lɛ yɛ baai bibii. loo fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ lɛ Kwɛmɔ fɔfɔi nɛɛ—esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni shishifãi lɛ atsɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Staking gets yam leaves up into sunlight so they can absorb light to grow large tuber roots under the soil. Keeping vines lifted off the ground also protects the leaves from humidity and fungal diseases on wet soil.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ hulu la mli bɔni afee ni amɛŋɔ la ni amɛkwɛ̃ shishifãi ni tamɔ bulbous yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) take away soil nutrients, water, and sunlight from the main mother tree. Pruning back excess suckers to leave just one or two allows the main plant to yield a larger, healthier plantain bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo (tso lɛ tsei) kɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo aba tso titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. Without consistent water and mild weather, the plant cannot support fruit production.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ bɛ lɛ, Tsei nyɛŋ aye abua aduawai afeemɔ kɛkɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant lacks calcium while fruit is forming, which is usually caused by uneven or irregular watering that prevents roots from absorbing calcium.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji calcium bɛ tso lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be ni haaa shishifãi lɛ aná calcium lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts improve my farm soil for next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, this nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as natural food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground when I plant immediately after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by hot dry spells before regular rains start. If seeds absorb initial water but the soil quickly dries out and heats up, the germinating seeds dry out and rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwu lɛ ŋɔ shishijee nu lɛ shi shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ oya ni edɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is missing key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away and soaked the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-ŋmã lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ etsɔ nu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep dropping off before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ miida diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from very hot weather, dry soil, or a lack of plant nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso lɛ mli niyenii tamɔ calcium ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my tomato plants develop dark spots and rot away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboi lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by fungal diseases in the soil that splash onto lower leaves when it rains. Clearing the lower leaves and covering the ground with dry grass mulch prevents soil from splashing onto the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni shwieɔ baai anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni sũ akashwie tso lɛ nɔ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in root tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ starch kɛ woɔ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant cowpeas or beans on the same land with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil, which naturally fertilizes neighboring maize crops without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmãa babaoo.

english: Should I apply my fertilizer when the farm soil is completely dry or when it is wet?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi kwraa loo edɔ?

english: Fertilizer should always be applied when the soil is moist or just before a rain, because plant roots need moisture to dissolve and absorb the nutrients without burning the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo dani nugbɔ anɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ashishifãi lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛshãaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in weak, thin stems and a smaller overall harvest than properly spaced crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛkpaa nii fioo fe tso ni akɛtoɔ he ko jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long heatwave that dries up the ground, which will scorch tender seeds before the steady rains arrive to support them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shãa dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa koni ekɛfi amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when the rain is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil before your crop roots can reach them, essentially starving your crop despite plenty of rainfall.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy or rot after I seal it in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ewo muji loo egbo beni mikɛwo kotoku mli ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bagging maize before the grains are fully sun-dried traps internal moisture, creating a hot and humid climate inside the bag that encourages mold and fungi to ruin the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ wo kotoku mli dani ŋmeii lɛ agbi kwraa lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kotoku lɛ mli ni woɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hewalɛ koni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight with each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients, leaving them with less energy to develop big, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii, ni no haa amɛnáaa hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛbaawo aduawai wuji ni he wa.

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, protects the ground from strong sunlight, keeps moisture in the dirt longer, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and encourages crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ewo tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen fertilizer or water. The plant moves remaining nutrients to newer top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu. Tso lɛ baajie niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or severe dryness, causing it to shed blossoms to save water and stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi bɔni afee ni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb up high to expose maximum leaf area to the sun, which allows the plant to produce enough energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Waterlogged soil starves cassava roots of air and creates ideal conditions for soil fungus, which rots the tubers before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbo dani akpa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my cultivated crops as soon as the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ?

english: Wild weeds are native plants naturally adapted to local soils, allowing them to absorb nutrients and rainwater far more aggressively than cultivated crops.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough to plant maize on a large scale?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni da nɔ?

english: Good soil for maize feels soft, looks dark, and drains water well after rain. If water stands on your land like a pond for days after it rains, the maize roots will suffocate and rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ediŋ, ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Kɛji nu yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ nubu gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ. Abɛi shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same food from the soil until it is exhausted. It also allows specific pests and diseases to build up in that field, waiting to attack your next crop.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛbaafite. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi hu shwereɔ yɛ nakai he lɛ, ni amɛmɛɔ koni amɛtutua oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do planting beans or cowpeas make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Cowpeas and beans have natural helpers inside their roots that catch plant food from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that food stays in the soil to help your next crop grow strong.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbualɔi yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai niyenii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves on purpose to stop water from escaping through them when it is hot. The plant is not dead; it is protecting itself, and it will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ nu akaje mli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebuɔ ehe he Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and turn brown when planted in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are naturally forest plants that need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct hot sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain next to them acts like a living umbrella.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii ji koo mli tsei ni biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi lɛ Tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka

english: What actually happens to my crops if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are squeezed together, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, light, and soil food. This makes all the plants grow thin and weak, resulting in smaller yields than well-spaced plants.
ga: Kɛ́ atswa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi fe tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ lɛ.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains are regular. The very first rain is often followed by a long hot dry stretch, which will bake your newly sprouted seeds in the soil before they can settle.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa odumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn yellow and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiikpa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are stronger drinkers and eaters than your crops. They steal the moisture and soil nutrients away from your plants, leaving your crops starving and turning yellow from lack of food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ nuɔ nu ni eyeɔ nii waa fe oŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing. If you apply it during a dry spell, it can burn the plant, and if you apply it during torrential rain, it gets washed away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei miida jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ okɛtsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli Tsei baanyɛ ashã. ni kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baaho kɛya.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my young maize leaves so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ miifite mi-baby corn baai lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Armyworms target the softest, newest leaves at the center of young maize plants where it is sweet and tender. Because they hatch in large numbers and eat constantly, catching them early with control measures is critical to save the yield.
ga: Kplukai lɛ kwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ fe fɛɛ, ni ji ehee fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ, he ni amɛmli ŋɔɔ ni amɛhe jɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛfɔɔ babaoo ni amɛyeɔ nii daa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ gbɛjianɔtoi ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehe miihia waa akɛ abaato nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts makes my farm soil better for other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei dumɔ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a family of crops that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the plant dies or is harvested, this stored food stays behind in the soil to nourish the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei aweku ko ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tsei gboi loo akpa amɛ Niyenii ni ato nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, delicate leaves that lose water very quickly in direct heat. They need temporary shade plants like plantains or bananas above them to block harsh sunlight until their roots grow deep enough to drink water easily.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana, yɛ amɛyiteŋ koni amɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu nu mlɛo.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger tubers when I train them onto tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mitsɔseɔ amɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground using stakes allows their leaves to spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves create plant food, which travels down to grow a bigger yam tuber underground.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo sweet potato wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛbaai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tsei niyenii. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni ekwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat or irregular watering. When the plant feels stressed by drought or hot weather, it sacrifices its flowers to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ hɔmɔ loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ miigba amɛnaa lɛ Ekɛ fɔfɔi baashã afɔle koni ekɛhere nu ni eha ehe ahi wala mli.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if there is plenty of land around each plant?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛhe? Tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko?

english: Even if there is open land, weed roots travel underground to steal water and fertilizers away from your crops. Weeds grow much faster than crops and will drink up the nutrients before your crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ moŋ, shi jwɛi shishifãi hu fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛyaju nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ onibii amli. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛbaanu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot uses up the same soil nutrients year after year and gives pests that eat maize a permanent home to multiply. Changing crops breaks the pest cycle and gives the soil time to rebuild.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baatsu nii afi fɛɛ afi. Ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa shia ni amɛhiɔ shi daa ni amɛfɔɔ bii. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛsaa ehe.

english: Why do I see small worms inside my maize leaves even right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm hide deep inside the tight center leaves of the maize plant where rainwater cannot reach them. Rain alone cannot wash them away, so you need to check the leaf funnels directly for pests.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ he ni nugbɔ nu nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Nugbɔ pɛ nyɛŋ ashwie amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots go soft and rot after only two or three days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a tough outer skin to protect them once dug out of the ground, so air quickly spoils the crop. It is best to leave cassava tubers undisturbed in the soil until the exact day you plan to sell or eat them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi bɛ kponɔgbɛ nɔ ko ni wa ni buɔ amɛhe kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nɔ ko akagbala amɛ kɛyashi gbi ni oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ loo oye lɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the ground instead of sprouting if I plant right after a heavy flood?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ nu afua ni naa wa ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need air inside the soil to breathe and sprout. When soil becomes completely soaked with standing water, it squeezes out all air spaces, causing the seeds to drown and rot before they can grow.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etsɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ Ebaamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow strong green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves standing water in your field, stopping the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi yɛ oŋmɔji amli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap natural plant food from the air and put it into the ground. When you harvest them, that stored food stays in the soil to feed your next crop, like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei aniyenii amli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni okpaa lɛ Niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛye onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that create living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make food. Lifting the leaves off the wet ground keeps them healthy and helps the plant grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhoo nii. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If too many shoots grow from the same plant, they all fight for the same water and food in the soil. Leaving only the main stem and one or two strong suckers ensures you get larger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni jɛ tso kome mli lɛ miida lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ baawuu koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kome yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ koni ona plantains akuu ni da ni tsii.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that hide under the leaves and suck out the plant's juice. They can also spread plant sicknesses that stunt the growth of your pepper plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei ahe helai ni haaa o-pepper tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ hu amɛshwã.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on young maize leaves from the inside out. They hide inside the central leaf funnel during the day to stay cool.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves soil soaked for days without good drainage, the roots suffocate and soil fungi cause them to go soft and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbii babaoo ni nu kpakpa hoɔ kɛyaa jɛmɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛfee blɛoo ni amɛgboi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too hot or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells. Without a steady supply of moisture, the plant cannot support turning flowers into heavy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua kɛkɛ ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsake amɛhe ni amɛfee aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my crops with dry grass help them grow during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Placing dry grass or leaves around your plants acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks the hot sun, keeps the ground cool, and stops water from evaporating so your crops stay hydrated longer.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he Tsei lɛ baatsu nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ajɔ ni otsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. They need temporary shade plants, like plantains or leguminous shade trees, to shield them from sun scorch and keep the soil moist while their roots settle.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo ŋmeii. Bɔni afee ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why is my maize turning pale yellow instead of dark green even after I weeded the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jwɛi efo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for healthy leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the correct growth stage will help the leaves turn green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni he wa lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plants experience severe heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering during dry spells and using balanced fertilizer helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that cannot easily hold up the heavy weight of a maturing fruit bunch, especially during high winds. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden or bamboo stakes keeps the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni ekwɛ̃ ni tsii lɛ anɔ mlɛo. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning pale green and white?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ eyɛŋ lɛ?

english: Curled and pale leaves on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing infected plants early protects the rest of your field.
ga: Kasava baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are my pepper fruits rotting and dropping from the plant before they turn ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ miifite ni amɛmiigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Rotting pepper fruits are often caused by fruit flies laying eggs inside them or fungal infections during humid weather. Clearing fallen, rotten fruits from the field and applying the right crop protection product early prevents the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ pepper aduawai fitemɔ baa ji aduawai amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli loo ŋmeii ni baa mɔ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Yibii ni egbee shi ni efite lɛ anaabuamɔ mra kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ nibii ni sa ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ gbɛfaŋnɔ naa.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtee ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on young maize leaves and growing points. Spraying approved treatments early in the morning or late evening when caterpillars are active helps control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Planting maize on the same land repeatedly drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpea or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ ni ekɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ abele pɔtɛɛ he lɛ baa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground to catch maximum sunlight and prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ. ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee baai ni fiteɔ

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and small yields. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to yield heavily.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Can I use water from my fish pond to irrigate my vegetable crops like tomatoes and peppers?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ loo ŋshɔ mli lɛ afɔ aduawai tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ?

english: Yes, water from a fish pond is rich in organic nutrients from fish waste. Using it to water your vegetables acts as a natural liquid fertilizer that helps plants grow stronger and yield more without needing extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, loo ŋshɔ mli nu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jɛɔ loo sũ mli. Nu ni okɛwoɔ o-vegetables lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni yeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why should I leave space between my cassava plants instead of planting them as close together as possible?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand and grow thick. If you plant them too close together, the leaves block sunlight from each other and the roots fight for nutrients, resulting in many small, thin tubers instead of a good harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji odu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ yibiiwoo kpakpa najiaŋ.

english: What happens if I try planting my maize in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds randomly across my farm?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mika akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa hu?

english: Planting in straight, measured rows allows every plant to get enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much faster and easier, which increases your overall yield.
