ga: Dumɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni asusu he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, kɛ nikpamɔ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kwraa. ni haa onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why is burning my farm land after clearing it bad for my crops in the long run?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mishãa yɛ be mli ni mijie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ gbonyo ko yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich, dark organic layer on top of the soil along with helpful earthworms and beneficial microbes. While the ash gives a short temporary boost, the soil becomes dry, weak, and poor after a season or two.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ sũ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ be kukuoo ko moŋ, shi shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi, egbɔjɔ, ni ebaafite yɛ be kome loo enyɔ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight or high heat when they are small. They need plantains or shade trees planted beside them to act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ kɛ́ kakao tsei lɛ darako. Amɛmiitao tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Is it good if I plant beans or groundnuts together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛji mikɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei du yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps your maize grow greener and produce larger cobs.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Ebuaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know if my soil is soft and healthy enough to grow large yam tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji?

english: Good yam soil should be loose, well-drained, and rich in organic matter. If the soil is too hard or heavy with clay, the yam tubers cannot expand freely underground and will end up small or deformed.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii. Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbaafee bibii loo amɛbaafite.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off during very hot days without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely hot, tomato plants suffer from heat stress and drop their blossoms to conserve water. The high heat also damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing fruits from forming.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ baaná hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni amɛbaafɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwie shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ hu fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee

english: How can I tell when my cassava crop is mature enough for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: You will notice the lower leaves on the cassava stem starting to turn yellow and fall off, and the soil right around the base of the plant will begin to crack open as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni ŋmei lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do white powdery spots cover my pepper leaves when the weather gets damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ haa mi-pepper baa lɛ nɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: This is a fungal disease caused by high humidity and wet leaves. The white powder blocks sunlight from reaching the leaves, weakening the plant and causing flowers to drop before pepper fruits can grow.
ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni hulutsoo babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Pauda yɛŋ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmɔtɔ yibii lɛ baa.

english: Why do farmers in Ghana plant plantains next to young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, a major nutrient in soil, or that too much water is choking the roots. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo nu babaoo yɛ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings too close together in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots compete heavily for soil nutrients, space, and water. Proper spacing allows the underground roots to expand into large, thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ŋwɛi, kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant faces stress, such as very high temperatures, insufficient watering, or lack of insect pollination. Keeping the soil moist and providing light shade helps save the flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa kpe. nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ falɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa la kpɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: If I have land but cannot visit it every day, what crop can I plant that survives with minimal care?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miyɛ shikpɔŋ shi minyɛɛɛ mayasara jɛmɛ daa gbi hu? Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ ni baahi shi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Hardy crops like cassava or cowpeas are good choices. They are resilient, tolerate dry spells well, and do not require intense daily labor compared to delicate fresh vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni wa tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ji nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Amɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi jogbaŋŋ. Ni ebiii daa gbi nitsumɔ ni tsii kɛ akɛto aduawai heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: What causes the leaves of my cassava plant to curl up and turn yellowish-green?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ?

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by small insects called whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems prevents this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Strong afternoon heat causes plants to lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can absorb water. Mulching the soil with dry leaves helps trap ground moisture and keeps roots cool.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops actually stop my crops from growing big?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃?

english: Weeds steal the sunlight, water, and soil food meant for your crops. Removing weeds early allows your crops to get full nutrition and grow much faster.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu ni amɛdaraa oya kwraa.

english: How can I tell that my yams underground are ready for harvest without digging them up first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛtsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Yam plants signal maturity above ground: when the green leaves and vines dry up and turn yellow at the end of the rainy season, it means the tubers below have finished growing.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ miitsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishigbɛ ŋmei lɛ etsɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash plant food out of the soil or waterlog the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha tsei aniyenii je kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu ŋshɔi ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ amli.

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during high heat as a defense mechanism to reduce the amount of water escaping through their surfaces. However, if they stay curled even in the morning, it could be a sign of leaf curl virus.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛhiɛ lɛ aba shi. Shi, kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛfo amɛhe leebi lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee leaf curl virus lɛ he okadi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress caused by sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or receiving too much water at once. The plant discards flowers to preserve its energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ na haomɔ ni trukaa ŋmɔshi nibii, latsaa ni naa wa, loo nu babaoo ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛbaa shikome. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up when I plant them in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct sun. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains planted alongside them to act as natural umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Should I push my cassava stem cuttings straight into the soil or lay them flat under the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo makɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at an angle or vertically creates deeper root systems that anchor the crop against strong winds, while laying them flat creates shallower roots. Vertical or slanted planting works best in areas with moderate rainfall.
ga: Yucca tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ loo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni haa tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he lɛ baa. Yɛ be mli ni okɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee mlɛo. Dumɔ ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ loo ni etse ehe lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo yɛ lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning them away and leaving only one strong replacement sucker ensures your main plant yields large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ mli ni oshi tso kome pɛ ni mli wa lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ awo yibii babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do I see small holes in my corn leaves with yellowish powder inside the middle shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai ni powda ŋmɔŋ yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It crawls inside the central funnel (whorl) of the corn plant to feed safely on the soft young leaves before they unroll.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe shwieɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei (ring) lɛ mli koni eye baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shweshweeshwe dani ejie ehe kpo.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees snap or fall over completely after mild rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bibioo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains easily fall over when underground stem pests or root rots destroy their anchor roots. Propping heavy trees with wooden Y-sticks helps support the stem weight during fruit production.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi loo shishifãi ni egbo lɛ fite amɛshishifãi ni akɛfiɔ amɛhe lɛ. Tsei ni tsii ni akɛ Y-shaped bars fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni eye ebua tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yɛ aduawai afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field make my next maize crop yield much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ waa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the crop matures, this natural fertilizer remains in the soil to feed nitrogen-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tsei ni he hiaa nitrogen, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my yam plant growing plenty of green leaves above ground but producing very small tubers under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen fertilizer or receives heavy shade, the yam plant invests all its food into leaf growth instead of storing nutrients below ground to form large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli loo eyɛ hulutsoo waa. Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ebaa lɛ aya hiɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niyenii kpakpahi kɛ toɔ zugba a sisi konɛ a pee ngmɔkɔ nguahi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under the strong Ghanaian sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ Ghana hulu ni naa wa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow strong cobs. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ ŋmãa ni mli wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifã lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year yield smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haaa yibii babaoo aba lɛ?

english: Maize takes the same specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the field.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii daa be. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them for too long without draining. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps heavy rainwater run off so the roots remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Shika ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa hoɔ koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines to climb up long sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maye mabua sweet potato wain tso ko ni ekwɔ tso nine kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make tubers underground using energy from sunlight caught by their leaves. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves get maximum sun and stay clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tswaa amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha tso lɛ yibii lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he, ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat stress or irregular watering. When the plant feels too hot or dry, it drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ edɔ tsɔ loo egbi Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why should I space my maize seeds apart instead of planting many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu ŋmeii babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too close together fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing them out ensures every stalk gets enough resources to grow thick and bear large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ tso fɛɛ tso lɛ náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee bibioo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your plants. Even with plenty of rain, your crops will starve if weeds are drinking the fertilizer first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po baaye hɔmɔ kɛji jwɛi lɛ nu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Treating for insects early prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ atsa kooloi mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaafiteɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why should I wait until after it rains before putting dry fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Dry fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plant roots can drink it up. Applying fertilizer on dry soil under direct sunlight can burn the plant's roots or cause the fertilizer to evaporate into the air.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni egbi lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the sun gets very hot during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ wo amɛmli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat to conserve moisture. By rolling, the leaf reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and dry wind, which slows down water loss until the temperature cools or rain falls.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa be mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit when it gets too dry and hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai beni edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: High temperatures combined with low humidity cause tomato pollen to dry out and become sterile. When the flower cannot be fertilized, the plant sheds the blossom to save its limited energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa kɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ haa tomato pollen lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi ko fɔ Tsei baafɔ̃ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu fioo pɛ ato.

english: Why do my sorghum and millet crops survive dry spells much better than my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Sorghum and millet have deeper root systems and can naturally pause their growth during dry spells without dying. Once the rains return, they recover quickly, making them well-suited for hot and dry areas like Tamale.
ga: Sorghum kɛ millet yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpa shweremɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ni amɛgbooo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, ebaatsa oya. Enɛ haa ehiɔ kɛha hei ni mli edɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi tamɔ tamales.

english: How can I safely store my harvested grains in Tamale so that insects do not ruin them before the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ato tamales mli shweshweeshwe? Bɔni afee ni kooloi bibii akafite amɛ dani be ni baa lɛ aba?

english: Ensure your grain is thoroughly sun-dried until it is hard enough to crack between your teeth before storing. Storing dry grains in airtight containers or triple-layer PICS bags starves insects of oxygen and prevents weevils from multiplying.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni odumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛbaafee shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala dani okɛto. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo PICS kotoku ni mli fãi etɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni haaa amɛfɔ bii.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting inside my storage shed even when I do not water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wooo mli moŋ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally break dormancy when temperatures and humidity change in the storage room. Keeping your storage shed cool, well-ventilated, and checking yams regularly to break off early sprouts helps delay this process.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ wɔɔhe mli kɛji hulutsoo kɛ latsaa tsake yɛ nitoohe lɛ. Oshĩa lɛ mli ni oooha efee fɛ̃i Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ. Ni kɛ́ okwɛ sweet potatoes lɛ amli daa koni okɛgbala tsei bibii amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why does dark mold grow on my harvested groundnuts after I put them into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ diŋ miikwɛ mi-peanuts ni mikpa lɛ nɔ beni mikɛwo nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Mold grows when groundnuts are bagged before they are completely dry. Trapped moisture inside the sack creates warm, humid conditions that allow molds, including harmful aflatoxins, to grow on the nuts.
ga: Mold lɛ daa kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii wo kotoku mli dani amɛgbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i ni atsĩ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔɔ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fungus Aflatoxins ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ fata he.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize on the same field next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas work with beneficial soil bacteria to pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them enriches the ground naturally, providing free nutrients for the maize crop that follows.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize turning yellow in a V-shape down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main vein of older, lower leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant pulls nitrogen from its lower leaves to support new growth at the top, indicating that the soil needs manure, compost, or fertilizer.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli fãji titrii lɛ ahe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and crumpling into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and crumpled leaves on cassava are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings. Planting resistant cassava varieties and using clean stem cuttings prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava henɔi ni nyɛɔ hela lɛ ni aduɔ kɛ niji ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do small caterpillars chew holes into the center leaves of my young maize plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which target the tender central leaves (whorl) of young maize. Moths lay eggs early in the season, and the hatched caterpillars feed inside the leaf whorl, requiring early monitoring and treatment with neem oil or recommended controls.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo (rings) lɛ anɔ. Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ be lɛ mli mra. Ni ŋmeii ni fɔɔ lɛ baaye nii yɛ baai lɛ amli. Esa akɛ akwɛ enɛ mli ni akɛ neem fɔ atsu he nii mra. loo nibii ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akudɔ

english: What are these small white insects on my cocoa trees, and can they harm my crops?
ga: tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo Mɛni ji enɛɛmɛi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ? Ni ani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Those white insects are mealybugs. They feed on the sap of your cocoa tree and can carry dangerous viruses from sick trees to healthy ones, causing severe damage to your farm over time.
ga: Nakai kooloi yɛji lɛ ji mealybugs. Amɛyeɔ nu ni jɛɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Ni abaanyɛ ajie helai ni yɔɔ oshara kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Ekɛ naagbai ni mli wa aba oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do small insects like mealybugs move from tree to tree if they do not fly well?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs lɛ ajɛ tso kome mli kɛya tso kroko nɔ kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛfo jogbaŋŋ?

english: Mealybugs are often carried from tree to tree by ants, which farm them for their sweet secretions. They can also be carried by wind, farm tools, or by walking across touching tree branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii woɔ mealybugs kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. ni kwɛɔ amɛ nɔ kɛha amɛ shwiemɔi ni ŋɔɔ lɛ Abaanyɛ akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu awo mli. okwaayeli he nibii loo nyiɛmɔ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni taa he lɛ anɔ

english: Why do I see so many ants crawling around the branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii babaoo ni miiho yɛ mikookoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Ants are attracted to mealybugs because mealybugs produce a sweet liquid that ants like to eat. The ants protect the mealybugs from predators and carry them to new branches, helping spread crop diseases.
ga: Mealybugs lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmeii ejaakɛ amɛjieɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛye lɛ kpo. Akpɔlɔi lɛ buɔ mealybugs lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe, ni amɛkɛ amɛ yaa niji heei amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Can the large wild shade trees around my farm spread diseases to my cocoa plants?
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo he fɛɛ he Ani miŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, certain wild forest trees can host insects like mealybugs that carry plant viruses. When those insects move from the wild trees to your cocoa trees, they deposit the virus and infect your crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, koo mli tsei komɛi baanyɛ ahi kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs ni hiɛ tsei ahe helai lɛ amli. Kɛ nakai kooloi lɛ shi koo mli tsei amli kɛtee kooloi tsei amli lɛ Amɛbaabua helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa ni amɛbaatswa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does a wild tree near my cocoa look healthy even if it is carrying a crop disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mi-kookoo lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyɛ tsei ahe helai moŋ lɛ?

english: Some wild forest trees are natural hosts that can carry a virus without showing any signs of sickness. However, once insects transfer that same virus to cocoa trees, the cocoa trees quickly get sick and die.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɔi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ hela lɛ ni amɛjieee hela he okadi ko kpo. Shi, kɛ́ kooloi bibii gbɛ hela nɛɛ nɔŋŋ amɛshwã cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, Cocoa tso lɛ baaná hela oya ni egbo.

english: Why are the stems of my cocoa trees swelling up and the leaves changing color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fũuɔ ni baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su lɛ?

english: Swollen stems and yellowing leaves are key signs of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease. This virus is transferred to your tree by mealybugs and weakens the internal transport system of the plant.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ji okadii ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo bud virus hela lɛ eba. Nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ ji nɔ ni mealybugs tsɔɔ otsei lɛ amli. ni ehaa tso lɛ mli gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ

english: Why has my cocoa tree stopped producing pods even though I am giving it enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ ekpa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miha lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: When a cocoa tree gets infected with a virus from mealybugs, the virus attacks the tree from the inside. This prevents nutrients from moving properly, causing the tree to stop making pods regardless of water supply.
ga: Kɛji akɛ mealybugs lɛ ye cocoa tsei anɔ lɛ, hela lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli. Enɛ haaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɔɔɔ he eko he ni nu lɛ jɛɔ.

english: Does a cocoa tree recover on its own once a virus enters its stems?
ga: Ani cacao tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ kɛji hela ko ebote tso lɛ mli pɛ?

english: No, once a cocoa tree is infected with a virus, there is no chemical cure to heal it inside the plant. The virus will remain in the tree and continue to weaken it until the tree eventually dies.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli pɛ. Tsofa ko bɛ ni baatsa cacao tso lɛ mli. Virus lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli ni eyaa nɔ egbɔjɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ naagbee.

english: How does a virus actually get inside my cocoa tree in the first place?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni hela lɛ bote mi cacao tsei lɛ amli yɛ shishijee mli?

english: A virus enters your cocoa tree when an infected mealybug bites into the bark or leaves to feed. As the insect feeds, it deposits the virus directly into the tree's living tissues.
ga: Virus lɛ boteɔ o-cocoa tso lɛ mli kɛ́ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ŋmɔ tso lɛ yibii loo baai lɛ koni amɛtao niyenii. Kɛji kooloi ye niyenii Ekɛ hela lɛ woɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What is the best way to prevent a sickness on one cocoa tree from reaching the rest of my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ atsĩ hela ni jɛɔ cacao tso kome mli baa lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: To stop viral diseases from spreading, you must remove and destroy infected trees along with the immediate surrounding trees, and control the insects and ants that carry the disease across your farm.
ga: Bɔni afee ni helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ akagbɛ ashwã Esa akɛ ojie tso ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ kɛ tsei fɛɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. ni okwɛ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ helai baa lɛ anɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the tip inward, it usually means the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil, or the roots are suffocating from waterlogged soil. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed manure helps green up the leaves.
ga: Beni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee V su kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛtee mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows its leaves to capture full sunlight and produce large, well-filled cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I need to keep shade trees on my farm when planting new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli he hiaa mi beni miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from heat stress and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa canopy closes.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out suddenly during flowering, or when there is excessive nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and mulching help keep the plant stable so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying neem oil or appropriate organic control early keeps these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Neem fɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mi lɛ shwieee lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense midday heat, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can drink water from the soil, causing temporary wilting. Placing mulch around the base of the plants keeps soil cool and conserves water.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hu sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers small, hard, and woody when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii, amɛhe wa ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers become hard and woody if left in the ground too long past their normal harvest time, or if planted in hard, unplowed soil. Harvesting on time (usually between 10 to 12 months) and planting in loose soil yields soft, starchy tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ fe ŋmaakpamɔ be ni sa lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuuu nɔ lɛ nɔ Kpamɔ yɛ be naa (bei pii lɛ yɛ nyɔji 10 kɛyashi 12 teŋ) ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tamɔ powder baa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly after I store them in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly in storage if they were cut or bruised during harvest, or if stored in hot, unventilated spaces. Storing undamaged yams off the ground on raised wooden racks in a cool, shady, well-aired barn keeps them healthy longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ To sweet potatoes ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he lɛ yɛ tsei ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: You should wait until two or three heavy rains have soaked deep into the soil before planting. Planting right after the very first light rainfall often causes seeds to germinate and then dry up if a hot week follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani okɛdu. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji otsi ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is this purple-flowered weed making my maize turn yellow even when I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ jwɛi ni fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ haa mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli moŋ?

english: That weed is likely Striga, a parasitic plant that attaches its roots directly to maize roots under the ground and steals water and nutrients before the crop can use them. Uprooting Striga before it flowers and rotating crops helps clean the soil.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, ni ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii dani tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii. Striga ni ajieɔ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsuu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check for crop pests and diseases?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ tsei lɛ amli kɛji amɛyɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai?

english: You should walk through your farm at least twice a week. Inspecting crops regularly allows you to catch pests like fall armyworms or leaf diseases early before they spread and destroy your whole farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ onibii amli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni omɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa loo baa he helai mra. Dani amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do weeds growing close to my crops affect their growth?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal essential soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your main crops. Keeping your field clean ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii titrii amli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔji lɛ amli tse lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii kpakpai fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Yam vines need support to lift their leaves high into the sunlight. When leaves get full sunlight, they produce more food, which helps the yam tuber grow bigger underground.
ga: Yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ebaaha niyenii babaoo aba. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet, shaded conditions. Regularly removing infected pods and clearing overgrown branches to let in sunlight helps prevent it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni ajie tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba amɛnɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enaa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen or water in the soil. Adding top-dressing fertilizer like urea at the right stage keeps the plant green and healthy.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ urea fata he yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat or lack of water. Keeping the soil moist and using mulch around the stems helps protect the plant from heat stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why is it bad to plant cassava on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and builds up soil pests. Rotating cassava with legumes like cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Cassava ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpea tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough for growing healthy cassava tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Good soil for cassava is soft, rich in organic matter, and drains water easily. Heavy clay soil that stays too hard makes it difficult for roots to expand into large tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni nu lɛ hoɔ oya Shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii ni wa tsɔ lɛ haa ewaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop during the hot afternoon even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Pepper leaves wilt in intense afternoon heat because they lose moisture faster than roots can draw it up. As long as the soil is moist, the plant will recover by evening.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my garden eggs turn out small and bitter instead of large and sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee agboi ni ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Garden eggs become small and bitter when the plant experiences water shortages during fruiting or if the fruits are left too long on the stem before harvesting.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ tsei lɛ na nu ni faaa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ loo kɛji akɛ ashi yibii lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa amɛ.

english: Why can I only harvest maize during certain times of the year instead of all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ manyɛ makpa ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi pɛ amli moŋ fe afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize depends heavily on regular rainfall to grow and mature, making it a seasonal crop that only produces food during the rainy months.
ga: Abɛi damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekwɛ̃. Enɛ haa efeɔ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ niyenii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli pɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Maize seeds need moist soil to sprout; without sufficient rainfall or irrigation, the seeds will either fail to germinate or the young shoots will wither and die.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he hiaa abele dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛɛɛ loo nu shwieee nɔ bɔ ni sa Ekolɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: How do I know when it is the best time to sow my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa?

english: You should sow your maize right at the onset of the rainy season so the plants get enough water during their critical growth and flowering stages.
ga: Esa akɛ odu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ kɛ fɔfɔii ni he hiaa lɛ amli.

english: Why can I leave cassava in the soil and harvest it whenever I need food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ manyɛ mashi ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni makpa lɛ be fɛɛ be ni niyenii he baahia mi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots act as a natural underground storehouse, allowing the tubers to stay fresh in the ground for many months until you are ready to harvest them bit by bit.
ga: Cassava shishifãi tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ shishi nitoohei. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa amɛ yɛ kui bibii amli.

english: How come plantain plants can produce food continuously while maize dies after one harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui nyɛɔ amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa gboɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa shikome sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize is an annual crop that dies after producing its ears, whereas plantain plants produce suckers (young shoots) at their base that keep growing to produce new fruits continuously.
ga: Abɛi ji tso ko ni yeɔ daa afi ni gboɔ beni toi lɛ eje kpo lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui woɔ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni yaa nɔ amɛdaraa koni amɛwo yibii heei daa.

english: Why does cassava handle dry weather better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ etsui shi fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cassava has a strong, deep root system that stores water and nutrients, enabling it to survive long dry spells where shallower-rooted crops like maize would fail.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni toɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. He ni tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, nyɛɛɛ akwɛ.

english: How does a plantain tree produce a new crop after I cut down the old stem?
ga: Te plantain baafee tɛŋŋ ekwɛ tsei heei beni mifo tso lɛ shishifã momo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When you cut down a mature plantain stem after harvesting, side shoots called suckers grow up from the roots to take its place and produce the next bundle of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ofo plantain tsei ni eda lɛ beni okpa Lateral tsei lɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ, daa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛye amɛhe ni amɛfee plantain kuu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Which crops should I plant if I want my family to always have food to eat at home throughout the year?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ madu kɛji miisumɔ ni miweku lɛ aná niyenii yɛ shia afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Planting cassava and plantains gives you year-round food security because their harvests are not strictly tied to one specific season like maize.
ga: Cassava kɛ plantains ni ooodu lɛ haa onáa niyenii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kpamɔ lɛ damɔɔɔ be kome pɛ nɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do cassava and plantains sometimes become scarce in the market if they grow all year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ ewa akɛ aaana ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ jara nɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Even though they are non-seasonal, factors like prolonged dry spells, pest diseases, or heavy market demand can temporarily reduce their availability.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ jeee be lɛ ji moŋ Shi nibii tamɔ hulutsoo be lɛ mli helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ babaoo lɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aha nibii nɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Can I feed my farm goats with leftover leaves and peels from my cassava and plantain harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tooi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, plantain leaves, plantain peels, and dried cassava peels make nutritious feed for goats, allowing you to feed your animals while growing your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain baai, plantain ŋmɔji kɛ cassava ŋmɔji ni egbi ji niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛhaa tooi. Ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ kooloi yɛ be mli ni oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know if the land in my area is suitable for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Good land for cocoa has deep, dark soil that drains water easily without getting waterlogged. If food crops like plantain or yam grow thick and green in that soil, it shows the land is rich and fertile enough for cocoa.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha kookoo ji shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ oya ni nu bɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu kookoo.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when the soil gets too soaked with water after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When the soil stays flooded for too long, the roots cannot breathe air. Starved of oxygen, the roots stop taking up nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and eventually drop off.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ. kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ faaa lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baakpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni naagbee lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa plants have very delicate leaves and roots that cannot survive intense, direct sunlight. They require partial shade from temporary nurse crops like plantain trees to shield them and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni nyɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsu nii. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ dumɔwui, koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Trees drop flowers when stressed by long dry spells, sudden heat, or damage from sap-sucking pests. Keeping the soil covered and protecting the farm with windbreaks helps the tree retain its flowers so they turn into pods.
ga: Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hao amɛ. latsaa trukaa loo nibii ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ adɛŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Weed seeds are very tough and can sleep in the dirt for a long time. Once rain falls, they sprout immediately and pull water and light faster than cultivated crops, which need a little more time to settle.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛgbalaa nu kɛ la oya fe tsei ni etswa shi shiŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ heɔ be fioo ko dani anyɛɔ atsakeɔ ehe.

english: It is best to avoid planting cassava near young cocoa because cassava roots spread aggressively underground and suck up water and nutrients, leaving the young cocoa trees weak and starved.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain suckers when planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ he ko kɛji midu?

english: Plantains need about 3 meters (10 feet) of space between each plant. Giving them enough room ensures their large leaves do not block each other from sunlight and their roots don't compete for nutrients.
ga: Plantains he miihia aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha baai wuji lɛ akatsĩ hulu lɛ naa, ni shishifãi lɛ hu akatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai.

english: How does covering the dirt around my young plants with dry leaves help them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi ni mikɛhaa muji ni ebɔle mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves—called mulching—works like a sunshade for the soil. It holds moisture so the roots stay wet longer during dry days and gradually rots to feed the plants.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli, ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii aha tso lɛ.

english: Does trimming off some branches from my trees make them bear more fruits?
ga: Ani tso lɛ niji komɛi ni afolɔ lɛ baaha ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, pruning removes dead or unproductive branches that waste energy. Removing them allows the tree to direct its water and nutrients straight to healthy branches that produce bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ni fiteɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ tsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛyaa niji ni mli wa ni woɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: When is the best time of the year to plant maize in the forest zone?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ koo lɛ mli?

english: The ideal time is right at the beginning of the main rainy season, usually late March to early April. Planting when rains are steady ensures the seeds germinate quickly without burning in hot dry soil.
ga: Be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa March naagbee kɛyashi April shishijee. Dumɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni ashãaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why am I seeing tiny holes on my cocoa pods and tree trunks this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji kɛ tsei ahe yɛ be nɛɛ mli

english: Tiny holes are usually caused by pod borers or stem-boring insects that drill into the cocoa plant to feed or lay eggs. If left untreated, these holes allow rainwater and diseases like black pod to get inside, which can destroy the tree or pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pod borers loo stem-boring kooloi ni shwieɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli koni amɛye niyenii loo amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa bu nɛɛ haa nugbɔ nu kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji boteɔ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ afite tso lɛ loo eshishifãi lɛ.

english: What are those small capsules or pest traps that some cocoa farmers place directly on their trees?
ga: Mɛni ji kapsul bibii loo ŋmeii ni kookoo okwaafoi komɛi kɛwoɔ tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Those capsules contain targeted scents or localized chemicals designed to attract and trap specific pests like mirids (akate). Placing them directly on the tree helps control insects right where they gather without needing to spray the entire farm.
ga: Nakai tsofai lɛ amli tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko loo tsofa ko ni afee koni ekɛgbala kooloi komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ mirids (akate) lɛ ni emɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hei ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa yɛ lɛ, ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofa afɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe to place pest control caps or chemical protectors directly onto individual cocoa pods?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ nɔ ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsofai nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ baawo kookoo ŋmɔŋ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, targeted chemical capsules or protective covers can be safely attached near pods to protect them from direct insect attacks. This ensures the protective chemical stays right where pests feed and isn't washed away by rain.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ loo nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ akpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji koni tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ lɛ, ni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ.

english: Why is high heat so important when I am fermenting my harvested cocoa beans under plantain leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he hiaa beni mikɛ mi-kookoo ni akpa lɛ woɔ plantain baai ashishi lɛ?

english: During fermentation, high heat naturally builds up inside the bean heap to stop the bean from germinating and to kill bitter compounds. Reaching the right high temperature is what gives cocoa beans their rich chocolate flavor and brown color.
ga: yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ yaa nɔ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato lɛ mli koni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni egbe nibii ni yɔɔ mli ni mli edɔ lɛ. Nine ni ashɛɔ hulutsoo be ni sa nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ tsokolate ni mli wa waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know if my fermenting cocoa heap is getting too hot or if it needs more time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo ehe miihia be babaoo?

english: Fermenting cocoa needs to reach a high, steady temperature (around 45°C to 50°C / 115°F to 125°F) for several days. If it gets too hot for too long, the beans will burn and smell bad, so you need to turn the heap every two days to balance the heat.
ga: Cocoa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ ni ehiɔ shi daa (aaafee 45°C kɛyashi 50°C / 115°F kɛyashi 125°F) gbii babaoo. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baashã ni amɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ otsɔ stack fɛɛ stack nɔ. Gbii enyɔ ni akɛtsakeɔ hulutsoo lɛ mli

english: How many days should I allow my cocoa beans to ferment before taking them out to dry in the sun?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani anyɛ agbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Cocoa beans typically need 5 to 7 days of fermentation depending on the heat built up inside the heap. Once the temperature peaks and the internal color of the beans turns brown, they are ready to be moved to drying mats.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ gbii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani cocoa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni enɛ damɔ dɔlɛ ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ shɛ he ni eyɔɔ fe fɛɛ ni kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ amli su lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Amrɔ nɛɛ, esa akɛ ajie kɔfi yibii lɛ kɛya tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to use exact measuring cups when mixing chemicals for our farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ susumɔ kɔɔpoi ni ja atsu nii kɛ́ wɔmiifutu tsofai yɛ wɔŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Using exact measuring cups ensures you apply the correct strength of chemical to your crops. Using too little won't kill the pests, while using too much can burn your cocoa leaves and waste your money.
ga: Kɛ okɛ susumɔ kɔɔpoo lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa onaa nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ tsofa hewalɛ ni sa miitsu nii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsu nii lɛ, egbeŋ ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã kookoo baai lɛ ni efite shika.

english: Can leaving a pest treatment on my cocoa trees for too long or using too much heat harm the crop?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo mikɛ la ni mli edɔ babaoo tsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, applying chemicals incorrectly or exposing crops to excessive heat can damage the cocoa pods, burn plant tissue, and leave unsafe chemical residues that reduce the market quality of your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ la mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ afite kookoo ŋmeii. shã tso mli fãji ni eshi tsofai ni bɛ shweshweeshwe ni eshwɛ lɛ Enɛ baaha nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ jara nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: How does weather temperature affect how well my farm chemicals work on cocoa trees?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ mli latsaa lɛ saa bɔ ni tsofai ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Chemicals react differently depending on heat; high temperatures can cause liquid chemicals to evaporate too fast before doing their job, while the right temperature helps systemic treatments absorb effectively into the crop.
ga: Tsofai kɛ dɔlɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni ji nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ dani aje nitsumɔ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo ni sa lɛ haa tsofa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ boteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees during extremely hot weather when temperatures rise very high?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes cocoa trees to lose moisture rapidly through their leaves, leading to wilting and smaller pod sizes. Shade trees and mulching help keep the soil temperature down and protect your cocoa during very hot periods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa cacao tso lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa baa shi ni ebuɔ o-cocoa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do some of the groundnut seeds I plant fail to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnut seeds fail to sprout if they were damaged during shelling, kept in damp storage, planted too deep, or eaten by insects in the soil. Using intact, healthy seeds and planting them at the right depth helps them sprout evenly.
ga: Peanut dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ amɛfite yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ amɛ lɛ. Okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. adu mli tsɔ Aloo kooloi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii ni adu yɛ he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Can I save some of the groundnuts I harvest this season to use as seeds for next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmeii ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ato koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui kɛha afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Yes, you can save your own seeds by picking the largest, healthiest pods from your best plants. Keep them inside their shells in a dry, cool place until planting time to protect them from moisture and pests that destroy their ability to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ obu bo diɛŋtsɛ odumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni dara fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ otsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni ooohala lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi kɛyashi be mli ni aduɔ lɛ koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ amɛnyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛdaraa lɛ he.

english: How deep into the soil should I push my groundnut seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mashɛ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: You should plant groundnut seeds about 3 to 5 centimeters deep, which is roughly the length of the top joint of your thumb. Planting too deep stops the shoot from reaching the sun, while planting too shallow leaves the seed to dry out or be eaten by birds.
ga: Esa akɛ odu o-peanut dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5, ni ji aaafee oshishifã lɛ yiteŋ lɛlɛ. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la. yɛ be mli ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo okpoi aye amɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plant flowers bend down and push themselves into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have a unique way of growing where the flower blossoms above ground, but the fruit grows below. Once pollinated, the flower stem grows downward into the soil—a process called pegging—where the groundnut pod actually develops.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛdaraa yɛ he ni fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Shi aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ. Beni pollinated Fɔfɔi tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ pinning. Biɛ ji he ni beanstalk lɛ daa yɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: How can I know that my groundnuts under the soil are fully ripe without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ kwraa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You know groundnuts are maturing when the plant leaves begin turning yellow and drop off. To double-check, dig up two or three sample plants; if the inside of the pods has turned dark brown or black instead of white, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: O le kaa ngmlɛfia a hɛ mi be ke tso ɔ baai ɔmɛ bɔni blɔ nya tomi nɛ a ngɛ ngmlaae ɔ. Koni okwɛ ekoŋŋ Tsɔmɔmɔ tsei ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii enyɔ loo etɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young groundnut plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that heavy rain has logged the soil with water and choked the roots. Improving water drainage and applying organic manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni efo shishifãi lɛ amli. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my groundnut seeds too close to each other in a row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When groundnuts are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow lots of leafy stems but produces very small, empty pods underground.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa tso ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli. Mohu ɔ, a peeɔ ŋmɔtɔ nyafii wawɛɛ nɛ e be nɔ́ ko ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why is it harmful to weed my groundnut farm once the plants start showing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mafolɔ mi-peanut ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kpo lɛ?

english: When groundnuts flower, they send delicate growing stems called pegs down into the soil to form the nuts. Hoeing or weeding around the plants at this stage breaks these stems and destroys your yields, so weeding must be done before flowering begins.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛtsuɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni bɔle Tsei lɛ ahe loo ojie amɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaakumɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ni efite onibii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm where I plant maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which means their roots naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside or before maize feeds the soil naturally, helping your maize grow taller without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa he loo dani ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: What kind of soil makes groundnuts grow best and yield big nuts?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ haa ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Groundnuts grow best in loose, sandy loam soil that drains water easily. Soft soil makes it easy for the flowering stems to push underground and gives the growing pods room to expand fully without being squashed by hard clay.
ga: Peanuts kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa ewaaa akɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ baatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ehaa pod lɛ he lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kwraa ni shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ etswaaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is getting too much direct sunlight or lacks key nutrients like nitrogen. Providing shade trees like plantains and applying recommended organic or chemical fertilizer helps keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha tsei tamɔ dumɔwui kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛfataa he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: What causes the cocoa pods on my farm to turn black and rot before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, humid conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing tall weeds allows air to circulate, drying out the pods and preventing the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What causes the stems on some of my young cocoa trees to swell up?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ekomɛi ahe tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi?

english: Swollen stems are a key sign of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, a serious disease spread by small insects called mealybugs. Infected trees yield less cocoa and should be inspected by an extension officer to stop the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni ji hela ko ni naa wa ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi titri. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baawo kookoo fioo ni esa akɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ akwɛ mli koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does keeping shade trees on my cocoa farm help my crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Shade trees protect delicate cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist during dry seasons, and drop leaves that decay into rich natural fertilizer for your cocoa plants.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni okɛ baai ni miifite lɛ awo shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛha o-cacao tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss. It is a natural sign that the plant is experiencing heat stress or needs more soil moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miina dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo aba.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall and thin without producing large tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo ni efeee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Cassava plants grow tall and leggy when they are planted too close together or shaded by bigger trees, forcing them to spend energy growing upward for sunlight rather than storing food in their root tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ tsei wuji ashishi. Enɛ nyɛɔ enɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛdaraa koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants often shed their flowers when temperatures become too high or when there is a sudden dry spell. The plant drops flowers to save energy and survive the weather stress.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ hɔmɔ ba trukaa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛjo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe haomɔ naa foi.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil can happen when hot weather makes leaves lose water faster than the roots can take it up, or it can indicate a bacterial wilt disease in the soil affecting the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha baai lɛ amli nu lɛ fite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Aloo ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ bacteria ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni saa shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli.

english: What are these tiny white, powdery insects sticking to my cocoa pods and stems?
ga: powda bibii yɛŋ Mɛni ji enɛɛmɛi ni kpɛtɛɔ mi kokoo ŋmɔji kɛ mishishifãi lɛ ahe?

english: Those are mealybugs, which suck the sap from cocoa trees and can transmit viral diseases like Swollen Shoot. Keeping the farm clean and using approved target sprays will help control them.
ga: Amɛji mealybugs, ni nuɔ cacao tsei amli nu lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ amɛshwã. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is naturally suitable for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha adebɔɔ mli kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cocoa prefers deep, dark, well-draining soil rich in organic matter. If rainwater sits on top of your land for days without soaking in, the soil may be too clay-heavy and can cause cocoa roots to rot.
ga: Cocoa sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ta oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni eboteee mli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu baanyɛ afee nɔ ni tsii tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eha kookoo shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: What actually happens to the cocoa beans after I harvest and sell them to the buyer?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ beni mikpa amɛ ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After you sell your dried cocoa beans, they are exported and processed into products like chocolate, cocoa powder, cosmetics, cocoa butter, and beverage ingredients used all over the world.
ga: Beni ohɔ̃ɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yaa maŋsɛɛ ni afeɔ nibii tamɔ tsokolate, kookoo powda, tsofai ni akɛsaa gbɔmɔtso he, kookoo bɔta, kɛ nibii ni akɛnuɔ nii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ je lɛŋ he fɛɛ he.

english: Why is cocoa considered one of the best cash crops for supporting a family in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ kookoo akɛ eji shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛhaa weku ko niyenii yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ ekome lɛ?

english: Cocoa provides a reliable seasonal income that can fund major household expenses like school fees, housing, and healthcare, making it a reliable financial foundation for farming families.
ga: Cocoa haa shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ akɛwo shia shika wuji tamɔ skul nyɔmɔwoo, shĩa, kɛ helatsamɔ he nyɔmɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo feɔ shika he shishitoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛhaa okwaayeli wekui.

english: Can women in our community take full ownership and leadership positions in running cocoa farms?
ga: Ani yei ni yɔɔ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛhegbɛ kɛ hiɛnyiɛlɔi fɛɛ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ akwɛmɔ mli?

english: Yes, women can fully own, manage, and lead cocoa farms. Many of the most successful cocoa farmers and leaders in agricultural cooperatives across Ghana are women.
ga: Hɛɛ, yei baanyɛ afee kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔtsɛmɛi kwraa, amɛkwɛ nɔ ni amɛnyiɛ hiɛ. Kookoo okwaafoi kɛ hiɛnyiɛlɔi ni yeɔ omanye fe fɛɛ yɛ okwaayeli kuu mli yɛ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo ji yei.

english: How much cocoa harvest should I expect to get from a well-managed farm?
ga: Cocoa enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ko ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ mli?

english: A typical farm in Ghana can produce several hundred kilograms of cocoa per acre, while improved high-yielding varieties with proper fertilizer and care can reach up to one ton per hectare.
ga: Ghana ŋmɔ ko baanyɛ afee kookoo kilogram ohai abɔ yɛ acre kome mli. Yɛ be mli ni kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ, kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ewo yibii ni shɛɔ tɔn kome yɛ hectare kome mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers without developing into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛdarako ni amɛfeee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can support. Only a small fraction get pollinated by tiny insects, and the tree naturally sheds the excess flowers to save energy for developing healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Eyɛ fã bibioo ko pɛ Ekɛ ŋmeii bibii pɛ feɔ pollin. Ni tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni he wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants need shade trees around them to survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo abɔle mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he koni enyɛ ehi shi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily by direct sunlight. Shade trees act like giant umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool, preserving soil moisture, and protecting young plants from harsh weather.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela wuji. Ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni obu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe

english: Is it safe to grow food crops like plantain alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ niyenii tamɔ plantains yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe?
