english: Yes, growing plantains alongside young cocoa is beneficial because the plantains provide quick shade for the cocoa seedlings while producing food and early income for your family.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ baaha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, feemɔ niyenii kɛ shishijee shika kɛha oweku lɛ.

english: A cocoa pod is ready to harvest when its skin color changes completely, usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from red to an orange-yellow color.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji amɛhewolo nɔ su etsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. loo kɛjɛ etsuru nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ-ɔranji nɔ

english: Why is it important to ferment my cocoa beans before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afee kookoo ŋmeii dani agbi lɛ?

english: Fermentation kills the bean seed to prevent sprouting, removes bitter tastes, and develops the rich chocolate flavor and brown color that buyers look for.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃, ejieɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ, ni ehaa tsokolate ŋmeii ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the tree, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei anɔ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ aaatsɔ atsĩ naa?

english: Black pods are usually caused by a fungal disease that spreads in wet and dark conditions. Pruning your trees and clearing weeds lets sunlight in and air circulate, which prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji black pods lɛ baa. Tsei ni afoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are my maize stalks snapping and breaking even though I don't see any caterpillars on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miikumɔ ni amɛmiikumɔ lɛ? Ani onaaa ŋmeii komɛi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Stem borer caterpillars hatch on leaves and quickly chew their way deep inside the stalk to feed. Because they live hidden inside the stem, you won't see them on the leaves, but they hollow out the plant from the inside until it weakens and breaks.
ga: Stem borers lɛ fɔɔ baa nɔ ni amɛyeɔ oya kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ amli koni amɛtao niyenii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli. Onaŋ amɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ tso ɔ kɛ jeɔ e mi mi kɛ yaa si benɛ e gbɔjɔ nɛ e kuɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree branches dry up and die suddenly without any obvious pest attack on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ baatutua amɛ lɛ?

english: Stem borers and mirids often tunnel into the inner wood or suck sap from hidden branch joints. This internal damage cuts off water flow inside the branch, causing it to dry out before you notice any insects outside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ amli kɛ myrids lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli loo amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ haa nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso nine lɛ mli lɛ kpaa. Gbi lɛ dani ona kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ kpo lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my fresh green peppers with small worms inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-pepper eŋɔli hee lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli.

english: Fruit borer insects lay their eggs on young flowers or fruit. Once hatched, the tiny larvae burrow inside the pepper to eat the seeds, leaving entry holes that allow rot to set in.
ga: Fruit borers lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ fɔfɔi bibii loo aduawai anɔ. Kɛji amɛfɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye dumɔwui lɛ. Kɛtsɔ bu ni haa ŋmeii boteɔ mli lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young corn plants have ragged holes with tiny dirt-like droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Etamɔ muji yɛ emli.

english: This is typical damage from Fall Armyworm. The caterpillars crawl deep into the leaf funnel (whorl) where they hide from daylight while eating the soft, growing leaves from the inside out.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm fɔɔ fitemɔ. Kplukai lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ (rings) he ni amɛteɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: How can I get medicine to kill pests that are hidden inside the stems of my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahe tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtee miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: For pests inside stems or whorls, you need to apply systemic insecticides or direct liquid spray directly into the leaf funnels or holes. Systemic chemicals get absorbed into the plant sap, killing the insects when they bite into the stem from the inside.
ga: Kɛha kooloi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli loo oval lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ atsu nii loo okɛ nu lɛ afɔ cone loo baa bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsofai ni yɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli. ni egbeɔ kooloi bibii kɛ́ amɛjɛ mli amɛbote tso lɛ mli.

english: Should I wait until I see actual damage on my crop leaves before spraying medicine?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni mana nɔ ni efite diɛŋtsɛ yɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ dani mikɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ?

english: No, for many stem-boring insects and fungal diseases, early preventative treatment is best. Once the pest enters the stem or root tissue, it is much harder to reach and kill, and damage has already begun.
ga: Dabi Kɛha kooloi ni shwieɔ shi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo. Tsamɔ ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa mra lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ebote tso lɛ shishi loo shishifã lɛ mli pɛ. Ebaawa kwraa akɛ aaashɛ he ni agbe lɛ. Ni fitemɔ lɛ eje shishi.

english: Why does liquid medicine need to be sprayed directly into the funnels of young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afɔse tsofa ni ji nu lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like armyworms hide deep inside the funnel of the plant where surface leaf sprays cannot reach them. Pouring or directing liquid into the funnel fills the hiding space and reaches the pest directly.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Nu ni afɔseɔ loo afɔɔ ashwieɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ haa he ni akɛteeɔ lɛ eyiɔ obɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyaa jɛmɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers have dark rot inside even when the leaves above ground look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po.

english: Soil pests like nematodes or underground fungi attack tubers from beneath the dirt. Because the damage happens completely underground, the stem and leaves can look healthy while the tuber is rotting inside.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɔ ni efite lɛ ba shikpɔŋ shishi kwraa. Tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ amli egbo.

english: Why is the base of my vegetable stem turning soft and rotting right where it touches the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables tsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpe pɛ lɛ?

english: Soil-borne fungi enter plant stems at the soil line when there is too much moisture or stem damage. The fungus penetrates the stem base, cutting off food and water to the rest of the plant.
ga: Fungi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ boteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ loo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ efite. Fuji lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa niyenii kɛ nu laajeɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi amli.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers come out with deep holes and dark tunnels inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ yɛ bu ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ duŋ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam beetles and soil larvae feed on the tubers while they are developing under the soil. They dig deep into the tuber flesh, creating tunnels that damage the crop before harvest.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Amɛfo yitso loo lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Feemɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani akpa amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off when the sun gets too bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense sunlight and heat stress. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block harsh direct rays, the leaves scorch, lose moisture rapidly, and drop to protect the plant from dying of dehydration.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ Koni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ Baai lɛ baashã. Efiteɔ nu oya ni egbeeɔ shi koni ebu tsei ahe kɛjɛ nu ni faaa lɛ he

english: Leaving too many suckers creates heavy competition for water and soil nutrients. Pruning all extra suckers except one or two strong ones allows the main plantain tree to direct its energy into producing large, heavy bunches of fruit.
ga: Suckers ni ajieɔ lɛ fe nine lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai. Afoɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ ajie tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ ni mli wa lɛ, plantain titri lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do some of my planted cassava stems rot in the ground while others sprout quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings rot if they are planted upside down, cut from old or diseased stems, or placed in waterlogged soil. Planting healthy cuttings right-side up with the buds pointing toward the sky ensures quick leafing and strong root growth.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ shishi tsei ni afo lɛ baagbo kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Afolɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni egbɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. aloo akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa ninejurɔgbɛ, ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaawo baai lɛ adalɛ mra kɛ shishifãi ni wa lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them lie on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tsei koni makwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ekã shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up into the sunlight and improves airflow. When leaves catch maximum sunlight without touching the wet soil, they manufacture more food for the underground tuber to grow large and stay free from fungal diseases.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato lɛ naa hulu la ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Be mli ni baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ ni amɛtaaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he. Baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo koni eha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni ŋmeii helai akafee amɛ.

english: Yellowing starting from the lower leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen keeps crops green and growing; when the soil lacks it, the maize plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the fresh green leaves growing at the top.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ bɛ lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmãa baa momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ koni ekɛha baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have beneficial bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the roots decay after harvest, they leave behind free natural fertilizer for future crops like maize.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my plant leaves get burnt and brown if I place fertilizer right against the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts that draw water out of plant tissues upon direct contact. Placing fertilizer too close to the main stem burns the plant; it should always be buried a few inches away in moist soil where tiny feeding roots can safely reach it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ lɛ he ni kɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko. baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many flowers, but the blossoms fall off before growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off primarily due to heat stress or poor pollination. Extreme afternoon heat dries up the pollen, preventing the flower from forming fruit, which causes the plant to drop the unpollinated blossom.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji dɔlɛ haomɔ loo pollination ni ehiii. Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo yibii Enɛ haa fɔfɔi tsei ni awooo amɛ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or thrips. As these insects feed on the sap and spread plant viruses, the leaves deform and lose their ability to feed the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa. Baai lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii dɔŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to water my vegetable crops during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ nu yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under intense sun causes most of the water to evaporate immediately before root absorption. Additionally, standing water droplets left on hot leaves can scorch the foliage and create a warm, humid environment for plant diseases to multiply.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ nu lɛ. Kɛfata he lɛ, nu ni shwɛɔ yɛ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba koni tsei ahe helai aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and turn yellow when the sun gets very hot during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight because their root systems are small and cannot pull up water fast enough. They need temporary shade trees like plantains to protect them and keep the soil cool until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala nu oya bɔ ni sa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli baawo shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to trim off some healthy branches from my mature cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Trimming extra branches lets light reach the main trunk where pods grow and allows air to move freely through the canopy. This prevents moisture from getting trapped, which reduces the chance of fungal diseases developing.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa la shɛɔ tso titri lɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli oya Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ akabote mli. Enɛ baaha hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do small green cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, egboɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa.

english: When a cocoa tree has more pods than it can support with water and nutrients, it naturally sheds some of the young pods to save energy so the remaining pods can grow fully.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ, Ebaajie ŋmeii bibii lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛto hewalɛ he koni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ adara kɛyashɛ shweremɔ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers at specific times of the year instead of all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli moŋ fe afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond to seasonal weather changes, such as the return of rain after a dry spell. This change in water availability triggers the tree to flower so that pods can grow when moisture is available.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ be mli lɛ ahe nii, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ. Tsakemɔi ni baa nu ni yɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ yɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are getting too much water from heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: When water sits on the farm for too long without draining, the tree roots cannot get oxygen. This causes the leaves to droop, turn yellow, and can eventually lead to root rot.
ga: Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ baa ni laajeɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my cocoa farm has lost its natural food for the crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ efite adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Tired soil shows in the trees through slow stem growth, leaves that stay light green or yellowish instead of dark green, and a drop in the number and size of pods produced.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baajie ehe kpo yɛ tsei anɔ kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Baai ni eshwɛ ni ji eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmeii ni ajieɔ lɛ ayibɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ba shi.

english: Why is it harmful to plant my cocoa seedlings close together on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting too closely causes trees to fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and underground water. This competition results in tall, thin, weak trees that produce very few pods.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Can I plant cassava in the same plot together with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ kookoo tsei bibii?

english: Cassava has fast-growing, heavy roots that take up water and food from the soil, which can starve young cocoa trees and slow down their growth.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya, ni tsii ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛha amɛdalɛ aba shi.

english: Why do black spots appear on my cocoa pods and spread rapidly when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates damp conditions where the black pod fungus thrives. Raindrops splash water from infected leaves or soil onto healthy pods, spreading the disease fast.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa hei ni black pod fungus lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai loo shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: As cocoa trees age, their internal system for moving water and nutrients weakens, making it harder for the tree to support as many large pods as it did when it was younger.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ, gbɛjianɔtoi ni yɔɔ mli ni haa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso lɛ akɛ ebaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji anɔ tamɔ bɔ ni efee beni eji gbekɛ fioo lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main plant food for green leaf growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the newest leaves at the top, leaving the old bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baatsi ehe fioo kɛya baa hee fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Ha shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do extension officers ask me to apply fertilizer in a circle around my crop instead of dumping it right at the stem base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ kooyigbɛ, shi jeee yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Putting fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's skin and roots. Spreading it in a small ring around the plant puts the food right where the searching feeder roots can absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ agbɛ ashwã tso lɛ he yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko mli lɛ, ehaa niyenii lɛ hiɔ he ko ni shishifãi ni haa niyenii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Cassava tubers need loose soil to grow long and fat. Raising the earth into mounds loosens the soil so roots can expand easily and prevents heavy rainwater from sitting around the roots and rotting them.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee fɔ. Kɛ́ owó shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsɔ gɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ alɛɛ mli oya ni amɛtsi nugbɔ ni naa wa ni nɛɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why will my maize field produce smaller cobs if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves every plant weak and hungry, resulting in small, poorly filled cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daraaa, ni amɛyimɔɔɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny green worms eating the inner leaves of my young maize crop early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ mi-ŋmei gbekɛ lɛ mli baai lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Those worms are fall armyworms that hatch inside the central funnel of young maize plants. They feed on tender leaves before the cob forms, so catching them early with natural sprays or recommended chemicals protects your yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni afolɔ ni fɔɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani ŋmei lɛ feɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɔmɔ amɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do dark, watery spots appear on my tomato leaves after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii diji ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-tomato baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater splashes soil-borne fungal spores onto leaves, and the moisture allows the fungus to grow rapidly into leaf spots. Spacing your plants and trimming lower leaves keeps the foliage dry and prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔ lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni hulutsoo be lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ adara oya ni etsɔ baai amli ŋmeii. He ni tsei lɛ kɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ afolɔ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akagbi ni ehaa baa lɛ mli helai baaa.

english: Why do my garden pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any pepper fruits when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko baaa kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when heat and water stress become too severe. The plant drops flowers to save its own life because it feels it does not have enough water to grow mature fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ bafee nɔ ni naa wa tsɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala. Ejaakɛ enu he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baaha aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to prune off the small shoots growing at the bottom of my cocoa tree stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi.

english: Those low shoots, called chupons, steal water and nutrients away from the main cocoa trunk. Cutting them off directs all the plant's food into making flowers and pods on the main tree.
ga: Nakai tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo lɛ, ejieɔ tso lɛ niyenii fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso titri lɛ nɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I save hybrid maize seeds from my harvest to plant again next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ hybrid corn dumɔwui ni jɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one strong generation. If you plant the seeds saved from that harvest, the second-generation crop will grow unevenly and yield much smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha yinɔ ni he wa. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ tsei lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa.

english: Why do my stored dried cowpeas get filled with tiny holes and brown dust after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsina ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Tiny beetles called weevils lay microscopic eggs on dried beans, and the hatching larvae eat the inside of the seed. Storing your dry beans in airtight hermetic bags suffocates these insects and keeps your harvest safe.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni anaaa yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni baa lɛ baaye dumɔwu lɛ mligbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ wo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akagbɔjɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ni onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain nearby protects them from burning and drying out until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Enɛ baabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ shãa he ni ebaagbi kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do people cut off some of the extra shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from each other. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ ebɔle ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tso wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know it is safe to start planting my crop seeds after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the ground receives two or three heavy, steady rains so the soil is moist deep down. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then wither if dry heat returns.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji latsaa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow green leaves and process sunlight. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or decomposed animal manure gives the crop the food it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni abele akwɛ baai eŋɔli ni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Covering the ground, also known as mulching, keeps the soil moist by stopping the sun from drying it out quickly. It also prevents weeds from growing and keeps the crop roots cool.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo be mli ni ehaaa egbi oya lɛ nɔ. Ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same farm patch every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop pests build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like cowpea or groundnuts restores soil fertility.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ

english: Why does putting animal manure on my farm make my vegetables grow bigger than untreated soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ haa mi-aduawai lɛ daraa fe shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu he nii lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural organic matter and nutrients that break down slowly. It helps hard soil stay loose and hold water better, making it easy for crop roots to absorb food.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fiteɔ fiofio lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ niyenii oya

english: Why do caterpillars eat holes in my corn leaves mostly during the night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli buji babaoo gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm hide deep inside the plant stem or soil during the hot day to avoid drying out and escaping predatory birds. They come out at night when it is cool to feed on leaves.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni okpoi ni yeɔ mɛi lɛ akagbi ni amɛjo foi. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ koni amɛbaye baai lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava roots grow very fat while others stay thin like sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu egbɔjɔ tamɔ tsei lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, uncompacted soil to expand. If the soil is too hard, or if the cassava stems are planted too close together, the roots cannot swell into big tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni ehiɛɛɛ shi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo aduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashwere ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my garden egg flowers fall off the plant before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop off when the crop experiences water stress, extreme heat, or a lack of insects like bees to transfer pollen. Keeping the soil moist and avoiding heavy chemical spraying during flowering helps fruits form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nu mli haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie fɔfɔi lɛ kɛya. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai aba.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying proper fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore nutrients to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ aku sɛɛ aba tso lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I grow the same crop on it every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over time. Rotating crops or planting beans and groundnuts helps put natural nutrients back into the land.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaya nɔ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, loo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Curled and pale leaves on cassava are typically caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by small insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant stem varieties helps prevent this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ tso henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during severe heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What will happen if I plant my seeds very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to thrive.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda.

english: Why should I wait for the steady rains before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Maize seeds need continuous soil moisture to germinate and grow strong roots. Planting in dry soil before steady rains arrive causes the seeds to dry out and die.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ anɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Removing weak or crowded branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the inner tree, which reduces fungal diseases and directs energy into producing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni mli edɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela baa shi ni ekwɛɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, aggressive roots that steal water and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting shortly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot quickly if they suffer cuts during digging or are stored in warm, damp places. Harvesting carefully and storing tubers in a cool, well-ventilated structure helps keep them fresh.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ apila amɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ okpa bulb lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen when the soil is too wet, making it hard for the roots to breathe and take up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally feeds your maize crop and improves the soil without you having to buy extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni egbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha o-corn tsei lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long during heavy rains. Building raised mounds or ridges of soil before planting helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ dani adu lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are my ripe tomato fruits cracking open on the sides before I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbala yɛ afãi dani mikɛ amɛ shwie shi lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack when they go through a dry spell and then suddenly receive a large amount of water. The inside of the fruit grows very fast and splits the outer skin. Watering your tomatoes in small, regular amounts prevents this.
ga: Tomatoi baagbala beni amɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. Ni trukaa lɛ, enine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya waa ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli gbalaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu fioo fioo wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni okɛtsi naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Groundnuts are unique plants that flower above ground, but produce their pods underground. After the flower is pollinated, the stem grows downward into the soil so the peanut can safely develop hidden from heat and animals.
ga: Peanuts ji tsei ni yɔɔ srɔto ni fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Shi afeɔ pods lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollin sɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe, ni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ahe.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches at the top, which makes them easy for wind to tip over. Supporting the stems with strong wooden props or planting them close to windbreak trees keeps them standing.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni jwɛi ni mli tse yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baagbee shi oya Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ loo adu yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi.

english: Yams tell you they are ready when the vines and leaves above ground start turning yellow and completely dry up. This signals that the plant has stopped growing leaves and transferred all its energy into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato kɛɛ bo akɛ efee klalo beni wain tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ etee ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree is stressed by too much harsh sunlight, dry soil, or a lack of tiny insects called midges that pollinate the flowers. Providing gentle shade trees and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ hulu la babaoo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii anɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ. Tso lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and slowing down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiiya hiɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves. Clearing weeds around your field and spraying soapy water or neem oil can help control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem fɔ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops every time the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have adapted to quickly swallow up nutrients, water, and sunlight before farm crops can. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops a head start to grow strong without competing for food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛye niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la oya dani ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ye obua odumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye niyenii he akaŋ.

english: Where can I get good cocoa seeds to plant on my new farm in Ghana?
ga: Ma ná kookoo yibii kpakpai komɛi. Higbɛ abaadu nii yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli yɛ Ghana?

english: You should get certified hybrid cocoa seeds or seedlings directly from the Cocoa Health and Extension Division (CHED) of COCOBOD, as these are bred to be high-yielding and resistant to common local diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ onine ashɛ kookoo yibii loo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli nɔ kɛjɛ COCOBOD Cocoa Hewalɛ kɛ Nɔyaa Nitsumɔhe (CHED) lɛ tɛ̃ɛ, ejaakɛ atsɔse amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Can I just collect seeds from my old cocoa pods and plant them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua dumɔwui kɛjɛ kookoo tsei momo amli ni madu?

english: It is not recommended because seeds from older farm trees may carry hidden diseases or produce low yields; improved seeds supplied by extension officers give your farm a better chance of thriving.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli tsei ni etsɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aná helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ efee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ aná hegbɛ kpakpa ni ekɛshwere.

english: How can I tell if a young cocoa seedling is healthy before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ dani madu?

english: A healthy seedling has vibrant dark green leaves without yellow patches, a straight and firm stem, intact roots, and no unusual swellings or insect damage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse ni ŋmɔŋ bɛ he. Tso lɛ ja ni ehi shi shiŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ efiteee. ni shwiemɔ ni ejaaa loo kooloi ni efite lɛ bɛ.

english: Why does an extension officer need to inspect my land before I plant cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛdu kookoo lɛ?

english: An inspection helps officers check if the land has hidden crop viruses or poor soil conditions, ensuring you do not waste healthy seeds on land that could infect or kill them.
ga: Nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa onukpai lɛ ni amɛnaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ ni ehiii kwraa. Enɛ haa oshiɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baanyɛ aŋɔ hela loo egbe amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the job of the Cocoa Board's Extension Division on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nitsumɔi ni kã Cocoa Board Nɔyaa Nitsumɔhe lɛ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extension officers act as advisors who visit your farm to teach you proper planting methods, check your trees for early signs of disease, and guide you on how to protect your yield.
ga: Extension officers tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋaawolɔi ni baasara oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛtsɔɔ bo gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ mli koni ona hela he okadi mra. ni otsɔɔ gbɛi ni oootsɔ nɔ obu onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees have been attacked by a virus?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela ko etutua mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Look out for swollen stems or branches, reddened leaf veins, yellowish patterns on leaves, and abnormally small or misshapen pods, which are clear signs of a viral attack like Swollen Shoot.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo niji ni efuu, baa lɛ mli fãji tsuji, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baa lɛ nɔ. kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ Enɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko eba, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu.

english: How do crop viruses spread from one cocoa farm to another?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli?

english: Small insects like mealybugs carry the virus from infected trees to healthy ones, and the wind or contaminated farming tools can also move these pests across neighboring farms.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ mealybugs lɛ hiɛɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo okwaayeli he nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ baanyɛ ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by fungal infections like Black Pod disease or viral damage, which multiply quickly when the farm is too shaded or holds too much damp air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal hela, tamɔ black pod hela, loo hela ko ni fiteɔ nii kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛfɔɔ oya kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo hulutsoo tsɔ loo hulutsoo be tsɔ.

english: Why am I advised to cut down a cocoa tree if it catches a severe virus?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo kookoo tso kɛji akɛ hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ emɔ mli?

english: There is currently no chemical cure for plant viruses once they infect a tree, so cutting down the diseased tree is the only way to protect the rest of your healthy farm from catching it.
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛtsaa hela nɛɛ yɛ tsei amli kɛji hela lɛ ebote tso lɛ mli pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ obu oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he koni ekamɔ lɛ.

english: Can I immediately plant fresh cocoa seedlings where diseased trees were cut down?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, the soil needs time and proper treatment to ensure all virus-carrying pests and infected root pieces are fully gone before introducing new, delicate seedlings.
ga: Dabi, be kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ koni ekwɛ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ etee kwraa dani dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ aba.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow healthy leaves. The plant naturally moves the limited nitrogen it has up to its newer top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai ni wa akwɛ̃. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fioo kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha ni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛgboi.

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny helpers on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. When the cowpeas are harvested, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ yelikɛbualɔi bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa tsina ŋmei Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees shrivel up and drop off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed excess flowers when they do not have enough water or nutrients to support them. It can also happen if tiny insects called midges are not around to pollinate the flowers or during periods of dry heat.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ lɛ bɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Midge lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli loo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms when the heat becomes very intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants get heat stress when the sun is too hot. To save water and keep themselves alive, the plants drop their blossoms instead of using energy to grow fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ naa dɔlɛ mli haomɔ kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Koni okɛ nu ato ni oha ohe ahi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii lɛ, ewoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the farm without draining away, it suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungi to attack and rot the cassava underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Nu lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch sunlight, which they use to make food for growing big tubers. Lifting the vines off the ground also protects the leaves from damp soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. ni akɛfeɔ niyenii kɛha bulb agbo ni akwɛ̃ɔ Wein tso lɛ nɔ ni awoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Tomato leaf curling is often caused by tiny whitefly insects that pass a virus to the plant as they feed. It can also happen when the plant experiences extreme heat and tries to curl its leaves to prevent water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ tso ko na dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ ebaai lɛ abɔle ehe koni nu akaje mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow tall and thin instead of strong and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and block sunlight from reaching your crops. When crops are shaded by weeds, they stretch upward very quickly to search for sun, making their stems thin, weak, and easily broken.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ onibii ahe. Kɛ́ jwɛi ha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛyatao hulu la. Ehaa tso lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ feɔ mlɛo, egbɔjɔɔ ni efiteɔ oya.

english: Why does my plantain tree give a small bunch when many young suckers are growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young suckers drink water and steal soil nutrients directly from the mother plant. If you leave too many suckers attached, the mother plant will not have enough food left to make a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How can I tell if the soil has enough moisture for me to safely plant my seeds after the first rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui shweshweeshwe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Dig a small hole hand-deep into the soil and squeeze a handful of soil into a ball. If the soil holds together easily without dripping water, it has enough moisture for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Kɛ onine atsa bu bibioo ko kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ko afee bɔɔlu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he mlɛo ni nu shwieee shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They turn yellow and dry up if they do not have shade crops like plantains planted next to them to provide protective canopy shade during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbi kɛji amɛbɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha ni ebu ŋwɛitsu lɛ he yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over right when the fruit bunches start to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and high water content in their trunks. As the heavy bunch matures, the plant becomes top-heavy, so strong winds easily uproot it unless you brace the stem with a wooden prop stick.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni ŋmɔ lɛ da kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatswa ni ajie shishifãi lɛ. Ja okɛ tso ni fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ lɛ fĩ tsɔne lɛ he.

english: Why is my maize growing very tall but producing small cobs with missing grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? He ni dumɔwui bɛ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when maize plants are crowded too close together or lack key nutrients like phosphorus. When planted too tightly, they fight for sunlight and grow tall, but lack the energy needed to fill out full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ loo amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, kɛ́ adu amɛ tsɔ. Ebaatswa hulu la lɛ he akaŋ ni ebaada. Shi ebɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmei lɛ mli kwraa.

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below. Balanced soil nutrients and loose earth encourage bigger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ŋmei ato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my main grain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa titri lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them alongside grains naturally enriches the soil with food that helps your main crop grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmaa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa onibii titrii lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by high temperatures and irregular watering. When the ground gets too dry during hot spells, the plant drops flowers to save its water for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu koni amɛkɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small pods during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli

english: During the dry Harmattan season, hot winds dry out the soil quickly. The cocoa tree automatically sheds small pods (cherelles) to save water and keep the main tree alive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ oya. Cacao tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii (cherelles) lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso titri lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my yam setts taking a very long time to sprout after I plant them in mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ beni mikɛwo gɔŋ ko mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period called dormancy. If planted right after harvest or in mounds that are too hot and dry, the sett will wait until moisture and temperature conditions trigger its dormant shoot to break open.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo yɛ gɔŋ ko ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ Set lɛ baamɛ kɛyashi hulutsoo kɛ latsaa baaha tsei ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium due to uneven watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant carry nutrients evenly to developing tomatoes.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji blossom end rot, ni baa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ tomatoi lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crops' root zone. Even with good rain, crops will starve if weeds are allowed to consume the food in the soil first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ po lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii lolo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small ears even when I clear the weeds regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ toi bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ amɛ jwɛi daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize needs nutrients from the soil to produce large ears, not just weed-free space. If the soil lacks nutrients, applying the right fertilizer at the right growth stage gives the plant the food it needs to develop full, heavy cobs.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ toi wuji aba. Jeee hei ni jwɛi bɛ lɛ pɛ he ewieɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ etsɔ ŋmei ni he wa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my crop needs fertilizer or if it just needs more water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu babaoo?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves usually curl or droop during the hot sun. When crops lack nutrients, their leaves turn pale or yellow even when the soil is wet, showing they need fertilizer to grow healthy.
ga: Kɛ tsei bɛ nu lɛ Bei pii lɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Amɛbaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants grow lots of tall green leaves but very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to focus on growing leaves instead of flowers and fruit. Using a balanced fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium at the right time encourages the plant to produce high yields of fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do insects attack my farm more right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Warm and moist weather creates the perfect conditions for insect eggs to hatch, while fresh rain causes plants to grow tender young leaves that insects love to eat. Spraying an insecticide early prevents these pests from multiplying.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha koolooi awɔlɔi ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ehee lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kooloi bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ mra Ebaatsi kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: What causes the leaves on my crop to turn dark and rot when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ?

english: This rot is usually caused by a fungal disease that spreads easily when water sits on plant leaves for a long time. Applying a fungicide protects the plant tissue and stops the rot from destroying your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji nu ta tsei ahe baai anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii tsu nii lɛ, ebaabu tsei ahe fãji ahe, ni ebaatsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ anaa.

english: What is the difference between an insecticide and a fungicide?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ateŋ?

english: An insecticide only kills insects like caterpillars and beetles, while a fungicide protects crops against fungal diseases like leaf spots and rots. Using the wrong product will not solve your crop's specific problem.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii helai tamɔ baa mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe. Nibii ni ejaaa ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ haŋ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaagbai pɔtɛɛi lɛ aba naagbee.

english: Why is it important to spray my crops at specific weeks instead of whenever I have spare time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ otsii komɛi amli moŋ fe be fɛɛ be ni maná hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ?

english: Farm chemicals work best at specific plant growth stages or pest life cycles. Applying them too early or too late wastes your money because the plant cannot absorb the chemical properly or the pests have already caused irreversible damage.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ mli fãi pɔtɛɛ komɛi loo tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ wala be mli. Kɛ́ okɛwo mli mra loo okɛwo mli sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ofite shika ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ tsofai lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ efite nibii ni anyɛɛɛ asaa momo.

english: How can following correct farm care steps help me get double the yield from my small plot?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛjianɔtoi ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná yibiiwoo ni jɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli lɛ toi enyɔ?

english: Following proper guidelines for spacing, weed control, and accurate chemical timing ensures every single plant receives maximum nutrients and protection, allowing the plot to reach its highest possible production level.
ga: Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni sa ni kɔɔ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ he kɛ tsofafeemɔ be pɔtɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ hebuu ni fa fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsɔne ni tsakeɔ nii lɛ shɛɔ nibii ni afee lɛ he ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do crop buyers at the market reject some of my harvest while buying produce from other farmers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kpooɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi yɛ be mli ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Buyers look for clean, unblemished produce with uniform size and no insect holes. Protecting your crop with proper pest and disease control during its growth ensures your harvested yield meets the standards buyers pay top price for.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ nibii ni he tse, ni tɔmɔ ko bɛ he, ni amɛdalɛ yaa nɔ ekomekomei, ni kooloi bibii bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ, no haa onibii ni okpa lɛ baashɛ shishitoo mlai ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How does keeping my crops healthy right before harvest affect the price I get at market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ dani akpa lɛ, ebaaná jara ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Pest or disease damage close to harvest causes produce to rot quickly during transport to market. Healthy, disease-free crops stay fresh longer, giving buyers confidence to offer you better prices.
ga: Nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni bɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ fiteɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya beni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni hela bɛ mli lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ náa hekɛnɔfɔɔ ni amɛkɛ jara ni hi fe fɛɛ baaha bo.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small yields. Proper spacing allows each plant to grow big and produce heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Should I plant my cassava stem cuttings slanting into the ground or straight down?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo mikɛwo ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slant makes it easier for the roots to spread out and grow deeper into the soil, which helps the plant absorb water better and produce larger tuber yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better to burn the cleared weeds on my farm before planting, or should I leave them on the ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaashã jwɛi ni ajie yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani adu? Aloo esa akɛ mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cleared weeds on top of the soil as mulch keeps the ground cool, retains moisture during dry spells, and slowly breaks down into natural plant food.
ga: Shi jwɛi lɛ ahe tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. Spraying the leaves early with neem oil extract or proper crop protectants helps stop the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo nɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ashwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa nɔ ni efite lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the soil gets too dry, temperatures are extremely high, or the plant lacks nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. eyɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa loo tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ muji ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crops look limp and wilted during the hot afternoon even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During intense sun, leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can pull from the ground. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing more water, but recovers as the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni nu babaoo akafite. Shi ebaahi shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does my groundnut plant bend down and push its flower stems into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miikoto shi ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ miitsi shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts grow their pods underground. Once the flowers are pollinated above ground, the plant naturally produces long stems called pegs that push into the soil so the nuts can safely swell and mature.
ga: Peanuts kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ pods amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afuu ni amɛdara shweshweeshwe.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce a high yield for one harvest only. If you plant the seeds saved from that harvest, the new crop will grow unevenly and yield much smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛha kpamɔ kome pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nibii heei baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii bibii kwraa.

english: Why is my land giving me smaller maize harvests today compared to when my ancestors worked on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ amrɔ nɛɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛhaa mi lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni miblematsɛmɛi lɛ tsuɔ okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the earth every season. Over many decades, continuous farming without adding manure, organic compost, or giving the soil time to rest drains the ground's natural energy and strength.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ amli fɛɛ Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he loo ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ afite.

english: Why do my leafy crops grow so much greener and faster after rain accompanied by thunder and lightning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daa ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa oya babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ sarawagbamɔ fata he lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Lightning creates electrical energy in the air that converts natural nitrogen into a form that dissolves into rainwater. This gives your crops an instant boost of natural fertilizer directly through their roots.
ga: Lasuogbelemɔ feɔ srawa hewalɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛtsake adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ ewo nɔ ko ni shwieɔ shi tamɔ nugbɔ nu. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and burn when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like soft saplings that burn easily under full sun. Without shade trees or plantains acting as living umbrellas, the heat dries out the leaves and steals moisture from the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii tamɔ dumɔwui bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni baatsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni ejuɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of protecting itself from losing water during dry weather. The plant goes to sleep to keep its underground tubers alive until the rains come back.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji yucca lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ he. Tso lɛ yaa wɔɔhe koni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my yam vines try to climb onto bushes instead of just growing flat on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants naturally reach upward to catch direct sunlight, which gives them the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Staking them lifts the leaves off the damp ground where diseases live.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa anáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do new suckers keep shooting up around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei miikwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Mi plantain shishitoo lɛ?

english: Plantain stems grow underground and naturally send up baby suckers so the crop can multiply and continue producing food after the main stem bears fruit and dies.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛtsuɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aya nɔ afɔ ni ewo niyenii beni tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ewo yibii ni egbo sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your corn is running out of nitrogen food in the soil. The plant moves whatever food it has left from the older bottom leaves up to nourish the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ ashishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms falling off the stem before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when water supply is irregular. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out under stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi yɛ haomɔ shishi.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up into tight cups and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ kɔɔpoo ni mli wa ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by insects that disturbs leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni kooloi bibii ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli.

english: Why does my maize grow thin and weak when I plant it right next to cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ mli tsɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ waa kɛ́ midu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava has thick, greedy roots that take up a lot of water and food from the soil. Planting corn too close creates competition that starves the maize of the nutrients it needs to grow strong.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli tse ni yeɔ nii babaoo ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii baa ni haaa abele lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the proper way to prepare seeds before putting them into the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa dumɔwui dani aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Proper seed preparation involves selecting clean, undamaged seeds and sometimes soaking or treating them against soil pests so that a higher percentage of them sprout into healthy seedlings.
ga: Dumɔwui ahe saamɔ kpakpa biɔ ni ahala dumɔwui ni he tse ni efiteee. Ni bei komɛi lɛ, afɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai woɔ mli bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ amli oha mlijaa 100 ni fa fe nakai lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the best distance to leave between seeds when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni kã dumɔwui ateŋ beni aduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Giving crop seeds proper spacing ensures their roots do not fight for water and soil nutrients, allowing each plant enough sunlight and air to grow strong and produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkaye nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he akaŋ. Ehaa tso fɛɛ tso hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How does planting seeds in neat rows help my crops produce more food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo niyenii babaoo?

english: Planting in rows gives every crop plant equal space and light, while making it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and care for the plants without damaging them.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okwɛ otsei lɛ anɔ ni ofiteee amɛ.

english: Why do some farms yield a large harvest while others on the same size of land produce very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: A large harvest depends on using healthy seeds, correct planting depth, good spacing, and feeding the soil properly, rather than just the total amount of land you farm.
