ga: Nikpamɔ babaoo damɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni ja he ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Jeee shikpɔŋ fɛɛ ni otsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ.

english: How can I help a small number of crop plants yield a lot of produce?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: You can maximize yield from a few plants by planting them in fertile soil, keeping them free of weeds, ensuring proper watering, and feeding them nutrients at the right stages of growth.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ tsei komɛi amli kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Tsi jwɛi Naa Nu ni sa ni aha tsei ni yɔɔ dalɛ be ni sa mli lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my crop plants grow lots of green leaves but yield very few fruits or grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi aduawai loo dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much leaf growth with little fruit usually means the soil has too much nitrogen but lacks nutrients like phosphorus and potassium, which crops need specifically for flowering and fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo tsɔ. Shi niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium bɛ mli. ni tsei he hiaa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo

english: Is clearing weeds and clearing the land enough to prepare my field for planting?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaa lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛsaa he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing is only the first step; loosening or tilling the soil allows crop roots to spread deep into the ground to collect water and food easily.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ loo atsuɔ he nii lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛhiɛ nu kɛ niyenii amli.

english: Crops getting enough nutrients display deep green leaves, sturdy stems, and steady growth, whereas yellowing leaves or thin stems usually show that the soil lacks essential nutrients.
ga: Tsei ni nine shɛɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ baajie baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpo. tso lɛ yitso ni mli wa kɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow well at first but stop growing before flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli shi ekpaa dalɛ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Crops need extra food and water when transitioning from leafy growth to producing flowers; if nutrients run out at this critical stage, growth will stall.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii kɛ nu krokomɛi beni amɛtsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ adalɛ mli kɛyaa fɔfɔii afeemɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ fite yɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ, Dalɛ baakpa.

english: How does removing weeds early in the season help my crops grow stronger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhe awa?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil food, so clearing them early ensures your young crops get all the resources they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts in my maize farm makes the soil better for my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have special bacteria in their roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When groundnut roots and leaves decay, they leave this free plant food in the soil for nearby crops like maize to feed on.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmei shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fite lɛ Amɛshiɔ tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛye tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why do weeds make my cassava plants look so weak and yellow even after I put fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa ŋmei tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni awo amɛ ŋmei po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cassava and aggressively steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your cassava. If you do not clear them early, the weeds consume all the plant food before your cassava roots can reach it.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei ni ekɛ hiɛdɔɔ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmei lɛ. Kɛji ojieee lɛ mra lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaye tso muu lɛ fɛɛ dani ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ashɛ he.

english: What is this purple-flowered weed that attaches itself to my guinea corn roots and stops it from growing?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ jwɛi ni fɔfɔii yɔɔ mli ni miikpɛtɛ mi guinea ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi ahe ni ekpa edalɛ?

english: That weed is called Striga or Witchweed. It behaves like a parasite by attaching its roots directly into your crop's roots to suck out water and nutrients, leaving your crop stunted and dried up.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi nɛɛ akɛ Striga loo Witchweed. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛtsɔ eshishifãi ni ekɛkpɛtɛɔ tsei ashishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛmu nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ nɔ. Ha otsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their leaves during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trees lose most of their water through their leaves. Dropping leaves during dry months is the tree's natural defense to save moisture so it does not dry up completely and die before the rains return.
ga: Tsei fiteɔ amɛnu lɛ babaoo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ kwraa ni egboɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do extra side shoots grow out from the base of my maize stalks, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii miikwɛ̃ kɛmiijɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie loo esaaa akɛ majie?

english: These side shoots grow when the maize plant gets extra nutrients or moisture. They steal food and water from the main stalk, so removing them helps the main stalk produce larger, healthier ears of corn.
ga: Nɛkɛ afã tsei nɛɛ daa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ nine shɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔtɔ kroko nɔ. Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why must I train my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible with their leaves. Catching sunlight allows the leaves to produce energy, which travels down to swell and grow large yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛjɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efuɔ ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why did my yellow maize crop produce cobs with mixed white and yellow grains after my neighbor planted white maize nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ efutu mli lɛ? Beni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ du ŋmãa yɛŋ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Wind carries pollen floating in the air from neighboring fields. When pollen from your neighbor's white maize blows onto your yellow maize flowers, it fertilizes those grains, turning some of the seeds white on the same cob.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa pollen kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Beni pollen ni jɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ lɛ mli lɛ tswa oŋmãa ŋmɔŋ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Ekɛ nakai ŋmaa lɛ baafɔ bii. ni ehaa dumɔwui komɛi feɔ futafuta yɛ ŋmei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli

english: When weather gets extremely hot or dry, tomato plants get stressed and drop their flowers to save water and energy. Keeping the plants watered and cooler helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ loo edɔ waa lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ ni edɔ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ he ni etsɔ aduawai.

english: How does planting a cover crop like Mucuna help clear my land of stubborn weeds?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ Mucuna ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ajie jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Mucuna spreads rapidly and forms a thick green blanket over the ground. This blanket completely blocks sunlight from reaching the soil underneath, suffocating weeds so they cannot grow.
ga: Mucuna lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsɔne nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa kwraa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops get rotten spots or mold when the weather becomes hot and rainy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ he tsɔi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Heat combined with moisture creates the perfect environment for fungi to grow and multiply quickly, causing mold, dark spots, or decay on your crops.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni kɛ hulutsoo fata he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ adara ni amɛshwere oya. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ baa onibii anɔ.

english: Why do leaf sicknesses attack my farm faster during the rainy season than the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa helai tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fungi need water and warmth to survive and multiply, so warm rainy periods give them the continuous damp conditions they need to invade plants.
ga: Fungi hia nu kɛ dɔlɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛfɔ bii. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ bei ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ naa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ etutua tsei lɛ.

english: Why does moisture staying on my crop leaves cause them to decay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni kpɛtɛɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛgboi lɛ?

english: When water sits on leaves in warm weather, tiny fungal spores sprout in the wetness and feed on the plant, making the leaves wither and rot.
ga: Kɛ nu ba yɛ baai anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Fungal spores bibii Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni eyeɔ tsei. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why does plant sickness spread so fast when I plant my crops very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, diseases easily jump from leaf to leaf, while close spacing traps heat and damp air around the stems where fungi thrive.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, helai baanyɛ ajɛ baa kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Is it better to leave space between my crops or plant them tightly to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ loo madu babaoo koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: Leaving proper space allows fresh air to move between plants and keeps them dry, preventing dangerous fungal diseases from wiping out your entire crop.
ga: He ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ ni ehaa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ akafite onibii fɛɛ.

english: How can I stop one sick crop from destroying all the rest of my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmɔshi nibii kome ni hela mɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Spacing your plants well and removing infected leaves quickly keeps fungal spores from hopping across the field to healthy crops.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ tsei jogbaŋŋ ni ojie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it easier to stop a fungal disease if I spot it on just one plant early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaaa akɛ makpa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko kɛji mina yɛ tso kome nɔ mra lɛ?

english: Removing an infected plant early destroys the disease before warmth and close spacing allow spores to spread to nearby crops.
ga: Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ekpataa hela lɛ hiɛ dani hulutsoo kɛ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do plants inside covered green shade houses still get leaf molds and fungi?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shĩai ni amɛyiteŋ eŋɔli lɛ amli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Enclosed structures naturally trap heat and moisture inside, creating an ideal breeding ground for fungus even if air is moving through.
ga: Nɔ ni agbe naa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ miitsɔ mli moŋ.

english: What causes white or dark mold to grow on my vegetable crops even when I care for them inside a structure?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ loo ediŋŋ shwereɔ yɛ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Mold is caused by fungi that thrive when warm air and dampness stay trapped around closely planted vegetables inside an enclosed space.
ga: Fungi ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ebɔle ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni afo he

english: If I grow my vegetables inside a greenhouse, do I still need to leave space between the plants?
ga: Kɛji midu aduawai yɛ ŋmɔ mli Ani ehe miihia ni mashi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lolo?

english: Yes, because greenhouses trap warmth and humidity, planting too closely makes it very easy for a single fungal infection to ruin the entire house.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsũi ni mli tse lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo waa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela kome pɛ baafite oshia muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient that keeps plants green and healthy. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color and improve yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the soil remains flooded or waterlogged for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, creating conditions for rot-causing fungi and bacteria to attack the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Be mli ni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo loo nu ehi mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off the topsoil before the crop's roots have a chance to absorb it, wasting your investment and washing useful nutrients into nearby streams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ. Enɛ haa ofiteɔ oshika ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ, ni ekɛ niyenii ni jara wa tsuɔ nii kɛyaa faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to leave some big trees standing on my farm when planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu kookoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Large shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist while protecting young cocoa plants from severe heat during the dry harmattan season.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat or irregular watering. When temperatures get too high or water is scarce, the plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa titri yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa hewɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu faaa Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry very heavy stems and fruit bunches. Propping up the stems with strong wooden poles gives them structural support and prevents them from snapping or uprooting during storms.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii waa kɛ aduawai akui. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ, ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the wet soil, exposing leaves to sunlight and reducing leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ baai lɛ awo hulu la mli ni eha baai helai aba shi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the juices from young leaves, or viruses spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that compete aggressively with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops get all the available resources to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ekwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow at the bottom while the top remains green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ kã he eji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. The crop naturally steals nutrients from older lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top when the soil lacks enough plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. Tsei juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with bushy leaves, but producing small underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When cassava soil has too much nitrogen or excess water early on, the plant puts all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of storing starch in its roots. Pruning some leaves and balancing soil nutrients helps direct growth to the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo nu babaoo yɛ shishijee mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ starch ato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, baai lɛ ekomɛi ni ooofolɔ ni okɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afee ekome lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers encourage me to plant groundnuts or beans alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko woɔ mi hewalɛ koni madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special root nodules that draw nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally enriches the land and feeds neighboring crops without needing extra inputs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ nibii krokomɛi awo mli.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the trees experience water stress, excessive heat, or poor pollination by tiny insects called midges. Providing shade trees and keeping the soil moist helps flowers stay attached and turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. hulutsoo ni fe nine loo ŋmeii bibii ni haaa ŋmeii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb instead of spreading on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight, which generates the food energy needed to grow large underground tubers. Keeping the leaves off the damp ground also protects them from rot and fungus.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛha baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo he. Enɛ haa niyenii hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops droop and look dead in the hot afternoon sun, but look fresh again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni gboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi obaaku osɛɛ kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi?

english: In the hot afternoon, leaves lose water to the air faster than the roots can pull water from the soil, causing the plant to temporarily wilt to save moisture. During the cooler night, roots catch up and refill the plant with water.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ tso lɛ agbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Gbi gbɛkɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baa ni amɛkɛ nu fataa tso lɛ he.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars only seem to eat my young maize at night or early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworm ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa pɛ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms dislike direct sunshine because it dries out their skin. They hide deep inside the central whorl of the maize leaves during the day and come out to feed when temperature drops at night and dawn.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ sumɔɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ ehaa amɛhewolo lɛ gĩɔ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye niyenii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ kɛ leebi.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and squishy before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady prevents the fruit tips from starving and rotting.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ tsiɔ aduawai ayitsei lɛ anaa koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ ni amɛkafite.

english: Why do pepper plant leaves curl upwards and stop the whole plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or viruses spread by these insects. They drain the plant's juices, causing leaves to warp and stunting overall growth.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Amɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why does spear grass keep coming back even after I clear and burn the surface of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa lɛ? Kɛji mijie ŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ ni mishã lɛ po?

english: Spear grass has tough underground stems called rhizomes that remain alive beneath the soil even when the top foliage is burned or cut. The plant quickly uses stored food in these roots to push up fresh shoots.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni wa ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes. Eyaa nɔ ehiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji ashã ŋwɛi baai lɛ loo afolɔ amɛ po. Tsei kɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ shishifãi nɛɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya koni amɛkɛtsi ŋmeii heei kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: How can I keep part of my maize harvest safe from insects so my family can eat it throughout the year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ ekomɛi akafee nɔ ko ni kooloi kɛbaa amɛnɔ koni miweku lɛ aye afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: To protect stored maize from insects like weevils, ensure the grains are thoroughly dried in the sun until hard, then store them in airtight hermetic bags (like PICS bags) or clean drums in a dry, covered space.
ga: Bɔni afee ni abu ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ahe lɛ, kwɛmɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ agbi waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku mli) loo baagi ni akɛjieɔ muji lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni egbi ni nɔ ko eha nɔ.

english: Is it better to harvest all my cassava at once or leave some in the ground until my family is ready to eat?
ga: Esa akɛ abua ŋmei fɛɛ naa yɛ be kome mli. Aloo ashiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni weku lɛ baaye nii?

english: Cassava roots spoil within two to three days after being dug up. Leaving the mature roots living in the soil acts as natural storage, allowing you to harvest gradually as your family needs food.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ baafite yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛji atsa amɛ. Shishifãi ni eda ni ashiɔ koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nutoohe. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii bibii bibii beni niyenii he miihia oweku lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same field, or will they fight each other for food?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaatswa niyenii he akaŋ?

english: You can safely plant them together because maize grows fast and is harvested in about three to four months, leaving the slow-growing cassava with plenty of space and sunlight to finish maturing over the rest of the year.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ he kome shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3-4 mli, ni ehaa ŋmãa ni daa blɛoo lɛ náa he ko kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees take over a year to produce fruit while my maize produces in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize is a fast-growing annual cereal crop designed to produce seeds quickly, while plantain is a longer-term crop that spends its first year building a huge stalk and underground stem before it can support a heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Abɛi ji afi ŋmaa ni daa oya ni afee koni ewo dumɔwui oya. Shi plantains ji tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua aduawai babaoo.

english: Why does planting maize on the same plot every season make my soil produce less food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ haaa niyenii babaoo aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize is a heavy feeder that pulls large amounts of nitrogen and nutrients out of the earth. Continuous planting exhausts the soil unless you add organic manure, fertilizer, or rotate the land with crops like beans or groundnuts.
ga: Abele ji niyenii ni tsii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛ niyenii mli nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee shoo. No ji ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How does growing plantains on my farm help protect the soil during hot, sunny months?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Plantain plants have broad, leafy canopies that shade the ground, reducing soil moisture loss from evaporation and keeping the root area cool during periods of intense heat.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ mli nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ

english: Why do cassava plants survive dry weather much better than maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep roots that reach water far below the surface and can shed its leaves during dry spells to save moisture, whereas maize has shallow roots and wilts quickly when rains stop.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ nu he kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ, ni ebaanyɛ ejie amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ lɛ, egboɔ oya.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ripe and ready to harvest for dry grain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi?

english: Maize is fully mature when the leaves turn dry and brown, the cobs droop downward, and a tiny black mark forms at the base of each hard kernel.
ga: Abɛi lɛ eda kɛji baai lɛ egbi ni amɛfee blɔfo, ŋmeii lɛ efo shi, ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwui ni wa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi.

english: Leaving too many young shoots (suckers) forces them to steal food and water from the main tree, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only two or three healthy shoots ensures larger fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji niji bibii Kɛji akɛ ahiɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaawo yibii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily when strong winds and rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and soft rather than woody, making the heavy plant top-heavy. Supporting main stalks with bamboo props or wooden poles prevents them from uprooting during strong storms.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe yɛ blɛoo fe tso shishifãi. Ehaa tsei ni tsii lɛ tsiimɔ wa waa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fi tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli.

english: Can I plant maize and rice together on the same piece of land, or will they fight each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaawu?

english: Maize and rice have different water and soil needs. Maize prefers well-drained soil and rots in standing water, while rice usually needs very wet or lowland soils, so planting them in the exact same spot often leads to low yields for one or both.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmãa yɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ he hiamɔ nii sɔrɔtoi. Abele sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, yibiiwoo ni jɛɔ ekome loo enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: If I add a new crop like cowpeas to my existing corn field, how does it affect the soil?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei, tamɔ tsina ŋmei fata ŋmãa ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ momo lɛ he. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ebaaná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas are special because their roots pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, which acts as natural fertilizer and actually helps feed your corn.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas ji nɔ krɛdɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ ni ekwɛɔ ŋmãa.

english: You should wait until the rain penetrates deep into the soil for several consecutive days. Planting right after the very first light rain can burn and destroy your seeds if a long dry spell follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite dumɔwui kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my corn seeds fail to come up out of the dirt after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if the soil is too dry, if they are buried too deep where air cannot reach them, or if soil insects and birds eat them before they can germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he. Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ye lɛ dani ekwɛ̃.

english: What will happen to my land if I keep planting corn on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Corn is a hungry crop that quickly drains nitrogen and nutrients from the earth. If you do not rotate it with other crops or add manure, the soil becomes tired, and your yields will decrease every year.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni ekɛ nitrogen kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tsakeee loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni onibii ni obaawo lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Yellow leaves mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen or their roots are suffocating from too much trapped water in the soil.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen loo amɛshishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ kɛjɛ nu babaoo ni ekpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my rice and corn after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi ŋmãa kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants adapted to survive easily, so they quickly steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your young crops before the crops have a chance to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe oya koni amɛhi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii bibii lɛ oya. Dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛdara waa

english: Why is it bad if I plant my corn seeds very close together just to squeeze more onto my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛnyɛ dumɔwui babaoo nɔ kɛbote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they block sunlight from each other and fight for soil nutrients, causing them to grow thin and produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko.

english: How does clearing and burning bushes on new land affect the crops I plant there?
ga: Te brɔshi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ ni ashãa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Burning gives a quick ash boost for the first season, but it damages organic matter and kills beneficial bugs in the soil, making the soil dry out faster in future seasons.
ga: Shãa ni ashãa lɛ haa sũ yaa hiɛ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ wɔsɛɛ bei amli.

english: Why does lowland soil feel different to farm on compared to high upland soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛ akɛto gɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Lowland soil holds onto water and washed-down nutrients from hills, making it rich and wet for water-loving crops like rice, while upland soil drains quickly and dries out faster.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔji lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ oya ni egbiɔ oya.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and healthy. Adding manure or fertilizer helps restore their normal color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ lɛ su lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ehaa bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yams expand underground, so if the soil is hard, compacted, or rocky, the tubers struggle to push through, causing them to stay small or become twisted.
ga: Atomɔ mli shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsɔnei lɛ feɔ bibii loo amɛtsakeɔ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests that prefer that crop to build up in the ground, leading to poor yields.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon weather gets extremely hot or when they lack sufficient water, as a natural way to save energy during stressful conditions.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ shwane mli loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ hewalɛ toɔ yɛ haomɔ bei amli.

english: Why does cassava manage to stay alive during the dry season while other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep roots that reach water far below the surface and can shed its leaves to stop losing moisture, allowing it to survive harsh dry spells.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ nu he kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ, ni ebaanyɛ ejie amɛbaai lɛ koni ekɛkpa ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. ni ehaa ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa shihilɛi amli

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose water faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil, so the plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects sucking the juice out of young leaves or spreading a sickness that prevents normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haaa amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield fewer pods when the farm is bushy and overgrown with shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ?

english: Too much bush traps moisture and blocks sunlight, creating a humid environment where diseases like black pod thrive and flower growth is reduced.
ga: Tsoi bibii babaoo baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni amɛtsi hulu la naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ yaa hiɛ ni fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to your local soil, allowing them to drink water and absorb nutrients much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni amɛduɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain bunch stay small if I leave all the young shoots growing around the mother stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ? Mami kotoku lɛ?

english: When too many young suckers grow around one mother plantain stem, they steal food and water from her, leaving less energy to produce a large, healthy bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ dumɔwu kome tso lɛ he lɛ Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ edɛŋ. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ babaoo aba koni akɛfee kuu agbo ni mli wa.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn easily under direct, harsh sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living shade and traps soil moisture, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the young suckers to grow around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Midumɔwu titri lɛ

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning away extra suckers and leaving just one or two allows the parent plant to direct all its energy into growing a bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Plantain kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso nyɛ lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛya dumɔwui wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and remain small when I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi bibioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain after a dry season often washes away loose topsoil nutrients and can be followed by a short dry spell. Waiting until the rainy season is fully established ensures the soil stays consistently moist and warm enough for young maize roots to feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni etse lɛ mli lɛ. ni hulutsoo be kuku nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Ni aaamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa naagbee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni ŋmãa shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year if I keep planting maize in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Maize is a heavy feeder that quickly drains essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts the ground, whereas rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas restores nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ji niyenii agbo ni baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become watery and rot if I harvest them during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ kɛji mikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During intense rains, cassava plants soak up excess water instead of storing starch in their roots. Soil that stays soaked with water starves the roots of air, causing the tubers to spoil and turn soft before harvest.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baato ŋmei yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni edɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbo ni amɛfee blɛoo dani akpa.

english: Why do I need to put tall stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food that gets stored underground as big yams. If the vines crawl along the ground in the shade of weeds, they cannot capture enough light, leading to very small, thin tubers.
ga: Taakɛ sweet potato agbo ji lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni akɛto shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji wain tsei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ jwɛi lɛ ashishi lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔmɔ la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛkɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo waa ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from sudden high heat, dry soil, or too much fertilizer. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its blossoms to save energy rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaafɔlɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. It usually happens when watering is inconsistent, as the plant needs steady moisture to move calcium from the soil into the developing tomatoes.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛjie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya tomatoi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my vegetable garden during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mikɛhaa mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛhaaa mi lɛ?

english: Watering under mid-day sun causes water on leaves to evaporate rapidly or scorch the tender foliage. The sudden change from hot air to cool water also shocks the root system, so watering early in the morning or late evening is much safer for the plants.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la shishi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔ oya loo ebaaha baai bibii lɛ ashã. Tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa kɛjɛɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ hu haa shishifãi lɛ amli fãji lɛ fiteɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa kɛha tso lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea pods as soon as the flowers finish dropping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ efo pɛ?

english: Young cowpea pods are soft, sweet, and rich in moisture, making them an easy target for pod-boring insects. Inspecting the field during flowering allows you to protect the crop early before pests lay eggs inside the developing pods.
ga: Cowpea ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli ŋɔɔ, ni amɛmli nu babaoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha kooloi ni boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe mra. Dani tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ baawo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense direct sunlight. They need temporary shade trees like plantains to act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting tender cocoa leaves from burning while they establish roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he beni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Will planting maize too close to my young cocoa plants slow down their growth?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni madu yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha edalɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, maize grows rapidly and consumes a large amount of soil nutrients and surface water. Planting it too close competes directly with young cocoa trees, leaving the seedlings malnourished.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa daa oya ni ekɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ekɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ baabɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ anaaa niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why should I use my Cocobod farm grant specifically for cocoa inputs instead of starting a poultry business?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ Cocobod ŋmɔ mli shika ni akɛhaa lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛha kookoo nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeje kooloi akwɛmɔ nitsumɔ shishi lɛ

english: Cocoa support funds are calculated to cover specific crop survival needs like weed control, pest sprays, and fertilizers. Diverting these funds to livestock starves your cocoa crop of care, reducing overall pod yield and income.
ga: Abuɔ kookoo yelikɛbuamɔ shika he akɔntaa koni akɛtsu ŋmɔshi nibii ashihilɛ he hiamɔ nii, tamɔ jwɛi akudɔmɔ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Shika nɛɛ ni okɛaawo kooloi adɛŋ lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye o-cocoa tso lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, pod feemɔ kɛ shika fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ ba shi.

english: Why does old cocoa land stop producing good yields even when I keep clearing weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo shikpɔŋ momo lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai eyɛ mli akɛ miyaa nɔ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally decrease pod production as they reach 25 to 30 years of age, and old soil loses vital minerals. Replanting aged farms with fresh hybrid seedlings restores yield potential far better than just weeding around old trees.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ amɛye afii 25 kɛyashi 30, ni shikpɔŋ momo lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ fiteɔ. Gbɛjegbɛi momoi ni akɛ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ duɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa amɛ yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi jogbaŋŋ fe jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ. tso momo

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in high moisture and excessive shade. Frequent harvesting of ripe pods and pruning excess branches helps keep air moving to prevent the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa kɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ daa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni ekɛtsi ŋmeii anaa.

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rains often indicate waterlogged soil where roots cannot breathe, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen. Improving farm drainage and applying cocoa fertilizer restores healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ, ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Okwaafoi amli nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only tiny flying insects called midges can pollinate them. Unpollinated flowers naturally drop off, which is normal for the tree's natural growth cycle.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi kooloi bibii ni foɔ pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midges pɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ pollen lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ tso adebɔɔ mli dalɛ mli.

english: Why does pruning extra branches from my cocoa tree help it produce more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni abaakpa lɛ baaye abua ni ewo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-productive stems, allowing sunlight to penetrate the foliage and directing the tree’s energy away from growing excess leaves and into producing healthy flowers and large pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni wooo yibii lɛ. Ha hulu la lɛ akpɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ gbɛ kɛjɛ baai lɛ adalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ he. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do capsids attack my cocoa farm more severely in areas where the forest canopy is open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ capsids miitutua mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ waa yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Capsid pests prefer warm, sunlit pockets in the canopy. When large shade trees are removed too quickly, it creates sunny gaps that attract capsids to feed on tender young cocoa shoots and pods.
ga: Capsid tsɛŋemɔ helai sumɔɔ hei ni mli edɔ, ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli kɛji ajie tsei ni eda lɛ oya tsɔ. Ehaa hei ni hulu la lɛ gbalaa capsids lɛ koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii kɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce a heavy harvest in the main season but very few pods during the light season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be titri lɛ mli lɛ? Shi pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa pod development depends heavily on rainfall cycles. The main harvest season follows the long rainy season when trees have abundant moisture to support many pods, while the light season follows shorter rains.
ga: Cocoa pod lɛ shweremɔ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ waa. Nikpamɔ be titri lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Beni tso lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔtɔi babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when I plant them right after burning the bush on my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ beni mishã jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Burning the bush destroys organic matter and beneficial microbes in the topsoil, leaving the ground starved of nutrients. Yellow leaves show that the young maize lacks nitrogen, which can be fixed by adding compost or manure to nourish the soil.
ga: Tsoi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa bibii amli. Abaanyɛ atsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear wild weeds and thick bush before planting my cassava stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie koo mli jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni mli tse lɛ dani madu ŋmei tsei lɛ?

english: Clearing bush properly gives cassava roots space to expand in light soil and ensures young sprouts do not have to fight aggressive wild weeds for water, fertilizer, and sunlight right from the start.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei bibii amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ naa gbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ nɔ. Ni ehereɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa lɛ ni amɛkɛaawuu koni amɛná nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ shishijee tɔ̃ɔ lɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my maize if I drop four or five seeds in a single hole to save space?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu kome mli koni mikɛ he akafite?

english: Planting too many seeds together causes crops to crowd each other out. They end up competing for the same soil nutrients and light, resulting in thin, weak stalks and tiny cobs instead of strong, healthy yields.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee shoo. Amɛbaagbe naa ni amɛmiitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ la lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ yiblii nɛ mi wa nɛ e ngɛ he wami.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing very tall and skinny without producing many leafy branches or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miida ni efee mlɛo ni niji loo pepper babaoo bɛ he lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are set too close together, they stretch upward searching for light. This forces the plant to waste all its energy on height rather than spreading out branches to bear fruit.
ga: Kɛji pepper tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni efite ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eniji lɛ eshwa koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up shortly after I transplant them onto my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee miŋmɔ lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and strong winds. Without shade trees like plantains to cover them and keep the ground moist, their tender roots quickly dry out.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains bɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are just thirsty from the afternoon heat or actually sick with a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kumai miiye mi-tomato tsei lɛ kɛkɛ kɛjɛ shwane latsaa lɛ mli loo hela miipiŋ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Thirsty plants will perk back up in the cool evening after watering. Sick plants will remain limp, show spots or yellow patches on their leaves, and fail to recover even when given plenty of water.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli beni awo amɛ nu sɛɛ. Tso ni hela mɔ lɛ baaya nɔ agbɔjɔ. Ayɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. ni enyɛŋ ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nu babaoo po

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by severe heat or irregular watering. The plant sheds flowers to preserve its own life until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with huge leafy stems, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus all its energy on growing top leaves and stems instead of storing food underground in the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida kɛ ŋwɛi ŋmei lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ zugba a sisi ngɛ tso ɔ sisi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up and turn brownish during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ harmatta be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains roll their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to dry winds, protecting themselves from losing water until the rain returns.
ga: Okɛ baai lɛ abɔle he koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ aba shi. Buu ohe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea crop suddenly as soon as the flowers open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛji amɛwo fɔfɔi pɛ?

english: Cowpea blossoms produce sweet scents and nectar that attract pests looking for food. Protecting the farm right at the start of flowering prevents insects from damaging the developing pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni gbalaa kooloi ni taoɔ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ abu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ fɔfɔii ashishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite fɔfɔi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray chemical medicine on my whole mango farm as soon as I see a few insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashwieɔ tsofai yɛ mango tso lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛji ana kooloi komɛi pɛ?

english: You do not always need to spray the entire farm. Cutting off affected branches and damaged fruits physically removes the insects and their eggs, controlling the pest problem naturally without spending money on unnecessary chemicals.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be ehe hiaa ni okɛ tsofa afɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Niji ni ena hela kɛ aduawai ni efite lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaye abua ni ajie kooloi bibii lɛ kɛ amɛwuji lɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ. ni amɛye tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛfiteee shika yɛ tsofai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe.

english: How does trimming my mango tree branches help control insect pests?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mango tsei ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ejie tsɛŋemɔ helai?

english: When you trim your tree, you cut away the specific branches where insects are living and breeding. Removing these infested parts destroys the insects' home and reduces the overall pest problem on your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ oofo tso lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oofo tso niji pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni kooloi bibii lɛ hiɔ ni amɛfɔɔ bii yɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie nɛkɛ hei ni hela emɔ amɛ nɛɛ, efiteɔ kooloo lɛ shia lɛ, ni ehaa kooloo lɛ he naagba fɛɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it important to pick off and throw away insect-damaged mangoes from the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie mango ni kooloi efite lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving damaged mangoes on the tree allows insects to stay, feed, and multiply. Removing those affected fruits gets rid of the insects inside them so they cannot spread to your healthy mangoes.
ga: Mango ni efite ni ashiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi, amɛyeɔ nii ni amɛfɔɔ bii. Kɛ́ ojie tso yibii ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ, ebaajie kooloi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni ekagbɛ eshwa o-mango ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What is the best way to get rid of insects hiding deep inside my fruit tree?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi aduawai tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Trimming overcrowded branches and cutting away diseased parts is the best method. This removes the hidden pests directly and opens up the tree to sun and air, which keeps insects away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo tsei niji ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli ni ojie hei ni hela yɔɔ lɛ. Gbɛ nɛɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. ni ogbele tsei lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akabote mli.

english: How do I stop insects from spreading from one bad mango to the healthy ones near it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã kɛjɛ mango fɔŋ kome mli kɛya mango ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should immediately cut off and remove the bad mangoes from the tree. Taking away the infested fruit removes the source of the insects before they can move to neighboring healthy fruits.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ ni ojie mango ni ehiii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ he ni kooloi lɛ jɛɔ lɛ dani ekɛ amɛ yaa yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Does cutting off damaged branches and fruits hurt the growth of my mango tree?
ga: Ani niji kɛ aduawai ni efite lɛ ni majie lɛ baafite mi mango tso lɛ?

english: No, it actually protects the tree. Cutting off damaged parts removes pests that steal nutrients, allowing the tree to focus its strength on growing healthy leaves and good fruits.
ga: Dabi, ebuɔ tso lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ afo hei ni efite lɛ, ebaajie kooloi ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama hewalɛ nɔ koni ebaakwɛ baai kpakpai kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do insects keep coming back to my mango trees every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa mango tsei lɛ anɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Insects often stay on the farm if old, damaged fruits and infested branches are left on the trees after harvest. Removing these affected parts cleans the tree so insects have nowhere to live for the next season.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi bibii baahi ŋmɔji amli kɛji akɛ aduawai ni egbɔ ni efite kɛ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ tee nɔ amɛhi tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ojie hei ni ena hela nɛɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsumɔ tso lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni kooloi bibii lɛ akaná he ko ni amɛhi kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Can pruning my fruit trees really reduce my reliance on expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Ani mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, pruning removes the exact places where pests live. By simply trimming bad branches and picking off infested fruits, you control the pest population naturally without needing to spray chemical medicine on everything.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ lɛ. Kpãa tsei niji ni ehiii lɛ ahe kɛkɛ ni ojie aduawai fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ayibɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ nɔ.

english: Is it better to cut off a sick branch or just spray it with insect medicine?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafolɔ tsei niji ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ loo akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ amɛnɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Cutting off the sick branch is often better because it completely removes the insects and their breeding site from the farm, solving the problem directly without the cost of spraying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei niji ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ejieɔ kooloi bibii kɛ he ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kwraa. Enɛ tsuɔ naagba lɛ he nii tɛ̃ɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni awo nyɔmɔ kɛha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: What should I do first when I notice insect pests attacking my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ mina akɛ ŋmeii miitutua mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Before reaching for chemical sprays, start by trimming the tree to remove affected branches and plucking off damaged fruits. This clean-up step gets rid of the pest source quickly and safely.
ga: Dani oookɛ tsofai ashwie nɔ lɛ Je shishi kɛtsɔ tso lɛ ni ooofo lɛ nɔ koni ojie niji ni efite lɛ ni ojie aduawai fɛɛ ni efite lɛ. Nɛkɛ hetsemɔ gbɛ nɛɛ baajie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ oya ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need phosphorus fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he hiaa ni akɛ fɔsfɔs awo mli lɛ?

english: Phosphorus is an essential nutrient that helps plant roots grow strong, enables the tree to transport energy quickly to where it is needed, and directly supports the formation of healthy flowers and pods.
ga: Fosfɔs ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛdaraa waa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ yaa he ni ehe hiaa lɛ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tɛ̃ɛ ni afeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni he wa

english: How does fertilizer actually help nutrients move inside a crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ ni amɛyaa?

english: Certain nutrients like phosphorus act as energy transporters inside the plant, creating fast internal pathways so food and water from the soil can easily reach the leaves, flowers, and growing pods.
ga: Niyenii mli nibii komɛi, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, tsuɔ nii akɛ hewalɛ ni akɛyaa tsei amli. Ehaa mligbɛ gbɛ ni hoɔ oya baa. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe oya.

english: Why is my cocoa tree producing plenty of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Trees use nitrogen mainly for leaf growth, but they need phosphorus for fruiting. If the soil lacks phosphorus, the tree will put all its energy into growing leaves instead of making pods.
ga: Tsei kɛ nitrogen tsuɔ nii titri kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Shi fɔsfɔs he miihia amɛ koni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs lɛ Tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii.

english: Flowers fall off when the tree does not have enough stored nutrients, particularly phosphorus, to nourish the flower and convert it into a developing pod.
ga: Fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ato yɛ mli. titri lɛ phosphorus Ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aná hewalɛ ni etsɔ amɛ ŋmeii ni miida.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to stay small and fail to mature properly?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ efee bibioo ni enyɛɛɛ eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pods remain small when the tree lacks sufficient nutrients during the early development phase, as nutrients like phosphorus are needed to feed the pod and help it expand fully.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ bibii kɛ́ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ eshishijee be mli ni edara lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs he miihia koni eha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kwraa.

english: What kind of special care or nutrients do my cocoa trees need once flowering starts?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiaa mi-cacao tso lɛ beni fɔfɔi jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees begin to flower, they require a boost of nutrients, especially phosphorus, to ensure the flowers stay attached and smoothly transition into healthy pods.
ga: Beni kookoo tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ He miihia amɛ niyenii babaoo. titri lɛ fɔsfɔs Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What can I do to stop my young cocoa pods from shriveling and dying early?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ akagbo ni amɛgboi oya?

english: Ensuring your trees have adequate phosphorus early in the season strengthens the pod attachment and provides the steady nutrient flow needed to prevent young pods from drying up.
ga: Kɛ́ akwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewaje ŋmeii lɛ ni eha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ aya nɔ koni ŋmeii bibii lɛ akagbi.

english: Why is it important to give nutrients to cocoa trees when they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aha kookoo tsei lɛ niyenii kpakpai beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees store critical nutrients like phosphorus early on to build efficient internal transport systems, preparing the tree to carry heavy food loads once it starts bearing fruit.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs toɔ mra. Bɔni afee ni afee mligbɛ gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ahe saamɔ kɛha niyenii ni tsii beni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer early in a tree's growth or wait until it starts fruiting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo tso lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli loo mamɛ ni ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: It is best to apply key nutrients early because building strong roots and nutrient transport channels ahead of time ensures the tree is ready to support flowers and pods when fruiting begins.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ awo mli mra. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ ama shishifãi ni wa kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa lɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni efee klalo ni ekɛfi fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛ beni yibiiwoo jeɔ shishi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is missing the right nutrients for good pod development?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa ni baaha pod kpakpa aya hiɛ?

english: Signs of missing nutrients like phosphorus include weak flower growth, frequent flower dropping, slow pod growth, and pods that stay tiny or misshapen.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ lɛ he ji fɔfɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi shii abɔ, fɔfɔi ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, kɛ fɔfɔi bibii loo ni ehiii.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for green leaves, so adding compost, poultry manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea early in the season will help them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas are special plants that can pull nitrogen food from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them alongside corn feeds your soil naturally, gives you two crops from one field, and saves you money on commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei ji tsei pɔtɛɛ ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen nibii kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa onine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli. ni ekɛ shika toɔ bo yɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo he.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and dry out easily under full sunshine. Fast-growing plantains provide big, temporary leafy umbrellas that shield young cocoa from harsh sun and heat during their first two years until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa, ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa baai agbo ko ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining, especially in flat or heavy clay soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli tse mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Water your tomato plants consistently and add wood ash or agricultural lime to the soil before planting to keep the fruit firm.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Okɛ nu awo o-tomato tsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu koni aduawai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: How does covering my soil with dry leaves and grass stop weeds from taking over my farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi awo mli lɛ atsĩ jwɛi ni yeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa?

english: Covering the dirt with dry plant material (called mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds in the ground. Without sunlight, weed seeds cannot sprout, and the cover also keeps moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Mulching kɛ tso nibii ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Kɛji hulu la bɛ lɛ Jwɛi dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What is eating tiny holes in my young corn leaves and leaving sawdust-like dirt inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the corn plant. Inspecting your field early and putting neem leaf extract or recommended control powders straight into the leaf funnel kills the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo powder ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ fata tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to burn the dried bushes on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã jwɛi ni egbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter, earthworms, and useful microbes that hold water and food in the soil. Leaving cleared weeds to rot back into the dirt feeds your soil naturally, keeping it rich and moist for better yields.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvested hybrid corn to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields only in their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest will produce weak, uneven plants with smaller ears; buying fresh certified hybrid seeds each season guarantees strong, uniform crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ aba. Dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe hewalɛ, po.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sun, which boosts tuber growth and prevents leaves from rotting due to soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli. Enɛ haa tuber lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ helai ahewɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field under direct heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a protective canopy that provides shade and traps moisture until the young cocoa trees are strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Adumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my elders advise me to plant groundnuts together with maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Different crops help each other when planted together. Groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the neighboring maize grow taller and stronger without draining all the nutrients from the land.
