ga: Aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he kome. Peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ daa ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ ejɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow and stay small when I plant them on the same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ bibii kɛ́ adu yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Soil gets exhausted when the same crop draws the exact same nutrients from it year after year. Rotating your crops or giving the soil a break allows natural nutrients to recover so future crops can grow healthily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsake loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ fite lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shi ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do aggressive weeds cause my crop plants to produce very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ yibii fioo pɛ baa miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil food. When weeds are allowed to take over, they steal essential nutrients away from your crops, leaving the plants weak and unproductive.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛye nɔ lɛ Amɛbaaju niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ onibii amli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make the soil better for my next crop of yam or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei dumɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei loo ŋmei dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have microscopic organisms in their roots that fix nitrogen into the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer that enriches the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees produce fewer pods now even though the trees are very large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni kookoo tsei lɛ dara waa nɛkɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their internal pathways become less efficient at moving food and water, and they spend most of their energy maintaining thick wood rather than making new pods. Replacing or pruning old trees helps keep the farm productive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ Amɛmli gbɛi ni akɛyaa niyenii kɛ nu he lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmeii heei. Tsei momo ni atsakeɔ loo afoɔ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii.

english: Why should I pinch off some of the leafy extra shoots on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Excess leafy shoots consume water and nutrients to grow leaves instead of fruit. Removing unnecessary branches forces the plant to send its energy and food straight into developing large, healthy tomatoes.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa baa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ gbɛ koni ená tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What happens to my cassava plants if I plant the stems too close to each other on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots fight for underground space and nutrients. Instead of growing fat, starch-filled tubers, the plants will produce long, thin roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, mo ha bulbs nɛ a ngɛ fɔ, nɛ a ngɛ starch ɔ. Tso lɛ baawo shishifãi kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up during the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha amɛ mra moŋ?

english: When the sun is hot, leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it from the soil. Curling their leaves is a natural mechanism plants use to shrink their exposed surface area and stop water from evaporating.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ afee bibioo ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho.

english: Why does a crop disease spread so fast across my farm when I plant only one single type of crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso hela ko miigbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya nɛkɛ lɛ? Akɛni miduɔ tso henɔ kome pɛ hewɔ lɛ

english: When an entire field consists of only one crop, pests and diseases can easily jump from plant to plant without barriers. Mixing crops or creating boundaries makes it harder for diseases to sweep through the whole farm.
ga: Beni kpokpaa muu lɛ fɛɛ ji tso henɔ kome pɛ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai baanyɛ ajɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ oya ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ loo husui ni atoɔ lɛ haa ewaa waa akɛ helai baagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do the cocoa pods on parts of my farm with less shade turn yellow faster than those under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ hei ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya fe kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight warms up the cocoa tree and speeds up the ripening process. Trees under heavy shade receive less heat and light, which delays ripening, making pods in open areas mature sooner than those in shaded spots.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaa amɛshwereɔ oya. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa shishi lɛ naa dɔlɛ fioo kɛ la fioo. ni haa shweremɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: How does having too much shade on my cocoa farm affect how much harvest I get?
ga: Te hulutsoo be babaoo ni miyɔɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While cocoa trees need some shade when young, dense shade on mature trees blocks sunlight, which reduces flower production and creates high humidity that encourages pod rot diseases, leading to a smaller harvest.
ga: Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hulutsoo he miihia kookoo tsei kɛ́ amɛdara. Shi hulutsoo ni mli wa ni yɔɔ tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi ni afeɔ lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ni haa pod lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why do strong winds make my cocoa flowers and young pods drop to the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa haa kookoo fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy winds dry out the air around your trees and physically shake the branches, breaking the delicate stems that hold young flowers and small pods before they can mature.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ Otso lɛ egbi. ni ekpokpoɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ Ekpãtãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hiɛ fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahiɛ. dani eda kwraa

english: What can I plant around the edges of my cocoa farm to protect my trees from dry winds?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ makwɛ yɛ ehe? Ani abaanyɛ atsɔ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni akɛbu mitsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he?

english: You can plant tall, fast-growing trees like plantains, citrus, or forest trees around your farm borders to act as windbreaks, slowing down harsh winds before they hit your fragile cocoa trees.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni daa oya tamɔ plantains, citrus, loo koo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa koni amɛtsu nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsii. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ aba shi dani etswa o-cacao tsei ni waaa lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during dry, windy conditions to reduce water loss. Dropping leaves helps the tree conserve moisture in its stem and roots to survive the dry season.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ egbi, koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are some cocoa pods ready for harvesting while others on the exact same tree are still small and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ? be mli ni pods krokomɛi lɛ Afee bibii lolo ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso kome lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Cocoa trees produce flowers over a long period rather than all at once. Because the flowers are fertilized at different times, the pods develop and ripen in stages throughout the season.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli moŋ fe ni amɛbaafɔ shikome. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ fɔmɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is it okay for me to harvest green cocoa pods if I want to finish harvesting early?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmɔji kɛji miisumɔ ni magbe mikpamɔ lɛ naa mra?

english: No, harvesting unripe green pods yields flat, low-quality beans that will not ferment properly. Plucking only fully yellow or ripe pods ensures good bean quality and better weight when selling.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni eshɛko ni akpaa lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii kwraa lɛ aba, ni amɛshwieee jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsiimɔ aya hiɛ kɛ́ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why is harvesting cocoa in dense, shaded areas so much more exhausting than in open field areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ni akpaa yɛ hei ni mɛi babaoo yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe waa fe hei ni mɛi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Shaded areas retain high humidity, damp air, and thicker undergrowth. Working in humid, enclosed environments makes the body tire faster, and navigating dense foliage requires more physical effort.
ga: He ni shade yɔɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ shishi tsei ni mli tse lɛ yaa hiɛ. Nitsumɔ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni ŋmɛlɛtswaa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa gbɔmɔtso lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe oya. Ni tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli nyiɛmɔ biɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo.

english: How often should I clear weeds under my cocoa trees during the peak harvesting season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni kpamɔ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds every 6 to 8 weeks during harvest makes walking through the farm easier, helps you spot fallen pods quickly, and prevents weeds from hiding pests that damage ripe pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi daa otsii 6 kɛyashi 8 yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyiɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa onaa ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ oya. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akatee.

english: Why do cocoa pods rot more quickly during heavy rains in heavily shaded farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Rain combined with thick shade creates trapped moisture and prevents airflow around the pods. This damp environment allows black pod fungus to multiply rapidly and destroy your crop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ahe lɛ naa. Shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ nɛɛ haa black pod fungus lɛ faa oya ni efiteɔ onibii lɛ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and will it help my crops grow better in our hot weather?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: A greenhouse is a frame covered with clear material that protects crops from heavy rain, winds, and pests. However, in hot regions like Ghana, heat gets trapped inside very quickly, so the structure must have open sides with insect mesh to let hot air escape and prevent your crops from burning.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsɔne ko ni akɛ nɔ ko ni mli tse ehà nɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Shi, yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tamɔ Ghana lɛ, Heat ŋmɛɔ oya yɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ tsũ lɛ ahiɛ fãi ni agbele naa ni ŋmeii awo mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ajɛ mli ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni shãa lɛ anaa.

english: Can I use plastic sheets to cover my vegetables during the hot afternoon to protect them from the sun?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ plastic aha aduawai ahe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he?

english: Clear or solid plastic sheets actually trap sunlight and heat underneath them rather than blocking it, creating extreme heat that cooks your plants. It is better to use woven shade netting or palm fronds that block harsh sunlight while allowing air to flow through freely.
ga: Plastic ni mli tse loo ni wa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ yɛ shishi moŋ fe ni eeetsi amɛnaa. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni shãa otsei lɛ baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ shade net loo tso tso baa ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ oya lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why do some farmers put netting on the sides of crop shelters instead of solid plastic?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋshɔŋlooi tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ahe yɛ plastic ni wa najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Netting allows fresh air and breeze to pass through the structure continuously, which lowers the temperature inside. Solid plastic blocks airflow completely, turning the shelter into an oven that burns any crop planted inside.
ga: Mesh lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tsɔne lɛ mli daa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji mligbɛ latsaa lɛ shibaa. Plastic ni wa tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa kwraa. Tsɔɔmɔ shĩa ko ni yɔɔ mli lɛ flɔnɔɔ ni baashã ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetables look withered and burnt even though I am giving them water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo ni eshã lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu haa daa gbi?

english: When the air temperature gets extremely hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Very high heat damages the leaf tissues directly, causing them to scorch and dry up regardless of how moist the soil is.
ga: Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ baafite baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ ha.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from too much heat during the day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miidɔ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Crops show heat stress when their leaves droop or roll up during the peak sun hours, turn yellow or crisp brown at the edges, or shed their blossoms before fruits can form.
ga: Tsei jieɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpo kɛji baai lɛ gĩ loo amɛkpãtã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa be mli. Baai lɛ anaa tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. loo egbee shi dani aduawai lɛ aje kpo

english: How does extreme heat inside a garden structure affect how my plants produce fruit?
ga: Te dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni yɔɔ abɔɔ ko mli lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive air temperature inside a closed structure damages the pollen inside crop flowers. When pollen dies from high heat, the flowers drop off the plant without ever forming fruits like tomatoes, peppers, or garden eggs.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ fe nine yɛ tsɔne ni agbe naa lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ pollen ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollen gbo yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee yibii, tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, loo abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔi.

english: Why do my young pepper seedlings keep dying when I keep them inside a fully covered shade structure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby pepper dumɔwui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ toɔ shĩa mli lɛ?

english: Fully enclosed structures trap heat from sunlight without giving it a way to escape. Young pepper seedlings are very sensitive to temperature, and the trapped heat bakes their tender stems and roots until they wither and die.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwo mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajoɔ foi haaa. Pepper dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa ni dɔlɛ ni amɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: How can I lower the temperature around my nursery seedlings without spending a lot of money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã hulutsoo ni bɔle dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ aba shi ni mikɛ shika babaoo tsuuu nii?

english: You can build a high shade roof using local palm branches or grass raised high above the plants, while leaving all four sides completely open so natural breezes can blow through and cool the air.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsei aniji loo jwɛi ni awó nɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ afee ŋwɛi ŋta ni nɔ kwɔ. Egbeleɔ ehe yɛ efãi ejwɛ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ koni adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ.

english: Does moving air really matter for crop growth, or do plants only care about sunlight and water?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ he hiaa diɛŋtsɛ kɛha tsei adalɛ, aloo hulu la kɛ nu pɛ tsei sumɔɔ?

english: Moving air is essential because it sweeps away trapped heat and moisture around the plant leaves. Fresh airflow helps plants cool down, breathe properly, and prevents harmful fungal leaf diseases from taking hold.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ he hiaa ejaakɛ ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle tsei ahe lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni ehaa amɛhe jɔɔ. Mumɔ jogbaŋŋ ni otsi fungal leaf helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ anaa.

english: Is direct sunlight always good for all crops in Ghana, or can too much sun hurt them?
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ be fɛɛ be. Aloo ani hulu la ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: While plants need sunlight to make food, intense tropical afternoon sun can overheat and scorch delicate crops. Many young seedlings and leaf vegetables need a balance of gentle light, good ventilation, and partial shade to stay healthy.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la he miihia tsei koni amɛfee niyenii moŋ, shi hulu ni naa wa ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ adɔ fe nine ni eshã tsei ni nuɔ he waa lɛ. Tsei bibii kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai babaoo biɔ la ni ŋmɛɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ blɛoo. kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulutsoo fã ko kɛha hewalɛnamɔ kpakpa

english: Why does adding plant food make my soil stronger and help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei aniyenii ni mikɛfataa he lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa ni eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the ground to grow, just like people need food to stay strong. Over time, the soil loses this food, and adding fertilizer or manure restores those missing nutrients so plants can thrive.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃. Taakɛ niyenii he hiaa gbɔmɛi koni amɛhe awa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Sũ lɛ baafite niyenii nɛɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What causes my farmland to yield less and less crop every harvest season?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ kpamɔ be fɛɛ kpamɔ be mli?

english: Every time you harvest, you take nutrients away from the soil. If you keep planting without giving the land a rest or adding manure, the soil becomes exhausted and can no longer support strong plants.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa Obaajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji oya nɔ odu nii ni ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do some soil inputs work much faster on my vegetables than organic manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii komɛi tsuɔ nii oya yɛ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers dissolve quickly in soil moisture and reach plant roots almost immediately for fast growth. Organic manure breaks down slowly, building long-term soil strength over time rather than giving an instant boost.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli ni eshɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe aaafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni eha amɛdara oya. Organic ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ fiofio. Wajemɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli moŋ fe ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help from starving plants that lack nitrogen. Even with enough water, plants need proper soil nutrients to stay green, make energy, and grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ ni jɛ tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni nitrogen bɛ amɛhe lɛ adɛŋ. Kɛji nu fa bɔ ni sa po Tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli, amɛfee hewalɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting enough strength from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy plants have deep green leaves, sturdy stems, and steady growth. If your crops look pale, remain stunted, or drop leaves early, the soil is likely lacking necessary nutrients.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa. tso ni mli wa kɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow unevenly across different parts of the same farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ? ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ

english: Soil strength is not the same everywhere on a farm. Areas with lower organic matter or poor drainage hold fewer nutrients, causing crops in those spots to grow slower than in richer parts of the field.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ jeee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli he fɛɛ he. Hei ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ baaná niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nakai hei lɛ daa blɛoo fe hei ni nii yɔɔ babaoo lɛ.

english: Why is it better to put fertilizer near the base of the plant instead of spreading it everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo tso lɛ shishigbɛ moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Roots need to easily reach the nutrients you put down. Placing fertilizer close to the plant base ensures your crops absorb it before rain washes it away or nearby weeds steal it.
ga: Ehe miihia ni shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni okɛfataa he lɛ mlɛo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aŋɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ aho lɛ loo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aju lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after I feed the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo niyenii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that quickly steal food and water from the ground. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the strength from the soil inputs you apply.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ náa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nibii ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ amli.

english: How does well-fed soil help my plants survive short dry spells without wilting?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni awoɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mitsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Healthy soil rich in nutrients and organic matter acts like a sponge that holds water longer. Weak soil dries out rapidly, causing crops to wilt quickly when rains take a break.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big bushy leaves but small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi shi bulbs bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen makes plants spend energy building thick leaves instead of root tubers. Plants need balanced nutrients, including potassium and phosphorus, to make heavy, healthy food underneath.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai ni mli tse yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ najiaŋ. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Potassium kɛ phosphorus fata he koni akɛfee niyenii ni tsii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow big leaves in the valley but end up rotting at the roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ baai wuji yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli shi amɛmiifite yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Valleys collect washed-away nutrients and water, which makes plants grow quickly at first. However, during heavy rains, water settles in the valley and stays trapped, starving the plant roots of oxygen and causing them to rot.
ga: Jɔɔ lɛ buaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa oya yɛ shishijee mli. Shi, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Nu baaho yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli ni ebaatsi ehe. Ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains spoil and turn soft within just two days of cutting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, plantains release natural ripening gases. If they are left under the hot sun or piled tightly together on the field, the trapped heat speeds up ripening and causes rapid spoilage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa Daring lɛ, ebaajie adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ shwereɔ lɛ kpo. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo ato amɛhe shi shiŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni amɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baaha amɛhoo oya ni amɛfite oya.

english: Can I leave my cassava tubers unharvested in the soil for months while waiting for buyers?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmei shishifãi ni akpaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo, ni mamɛ mɔ ko ni baahe?

english: Cassava can stay in the soil for a short while, but leaving it too long makes the roots woody, tough, and vulnerable to underground pests and rot from rain.
ga: Yucca baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fioo. Shi kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei, amɛhe wa ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do all my tomatoes mature at the exact same time, forcing me to harvest everything at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miida yɛ be kome mli, ni no haa mikpaa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ?

english: If you plant all your tomato seeds on the same day, they will finish growing together. Staggering your planting dates every two weeks allows your crops to mature in stages so you do not have too much harvest at one time.
ga: Kɛji odu o-tomato dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ Tomato dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekome. Kɛ́ otsi gbi ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ daa Otsii Enyɔ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Enɛ ji koni okakpa nibii babaoo shikome.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn black and moldy when I pile it on the ground after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛto shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize holds inside moisture. When piled directly on wet soil, heat and humidity get trapped, creating the perfect environment for dangerous mold to grow.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ ato shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mɔɔ shi. Ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ adalɛ baa.

english: Why is my pepper plant producing tiny flowers when it is still very short and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Beni eji kuku ni ebɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ?

english: When a pepper plant experiences stress from heat or poor soil, it panics and flowers early to produce seeds before it dies, rather than focusing on growing a strong stem.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ Ebaafee gbeyei ni ebaafɔ mra koni ekɛ dumɔwui aba dani egbo. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ o juɛmi kɛ ma tsohi nɛ a he wa nɛ a ngɛ wae ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting and shrinking before I can take them out for sale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ dani ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that wake up from dormancy as temperatures change. When sprouts grow, they draw water and nutrients out of the yam itself, causing the tuber to shrivel.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be tsake. Kɛji ŋmei lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ Ebaagbala nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mli. ha yitso lɛ agbi

english: Why do crops planted under large tree canopies produce thin stems and small fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ ashishifãi yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Large trees block essential sunlight and their roots steal water and nutrients from the soil. Crops need direct sunlight to produce food for growing heavy fruits.
ga: Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa lɛ naa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Hulu la he miihia tsei tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha aduawai ni tsii ni amɛduɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my garden eggs smaller this year when I planted them in the exact same field as last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa afi nɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ saatso kome nɔ tamɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows soil pests that feed on that specific crop to build up.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa.

english: Why are my young papaya fruits dropping off the tree long before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya bibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Papaya trees drop young fruits when they experience sudden water shortages or intense heat, reducing their load so the main plant can survive.
ga: Papaya tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛna nu ni faaa trukaa loo latsaa ni naa wa waa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jatsu lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I wash my freshly harvested leafy greens before taking them to the market or cooking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ mi-ŋmɔji ni mikpa ehee lɛ ahe dani mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ loo mahoo lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested greens carry soil, dirt, and tiny pests from the farm field. Washing them removes these contaminants, making the produce safe to eat, hygienic, and much more attractive to market buyers.
ga: Baai ni akpa ehee lɛ kɛ muji, sũ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ afɔ he lɛ, ebaajie nɛkɛ muji nɛɛ. Enɛ haa nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyeli, ehe tse, ni ehaa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ waa.

english: How soon after cutting my leafy crops should I wash and handle them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafɔ he oya ni matsu he nii beni mifo tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wash and process leafy crops right after harvesting them while they are still fresh. Handling them immediately prevents wilting and helps the leaves retain their crisp texture, nutrition, and market quality.
ga: Esa akɛ ofɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe ni otsu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji okpa amɛ be mli ni amɛji ehee lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii oya lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa ni ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛ jarayeli mli nibii ni hi

english: Is it better to cut my leafy vegetables into small pieces before washing them, or should I wash them whole?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofolɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli bibii bibii dani ahoo, aloo ehi akɛ ooofɔ baa muu lɛ fɛɛ he?

english: Chopping leafy vegetables into smaller pieces before washing allows water to reach hidden dirt and pests trapped deep inside folded leaves, ensuring a thorough clean.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ ni afoɔ mli bibii bibii Pre-rinsing haa nu lɛ shɛɔ muji kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ baai ni afolɔ mli lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ahe. Koni ena nɔmimaa akɛ ehe tse kwraa.

english: Why do experienced farmers add salt to the water when washing fresh leafy crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ ŋoo woɔ nu mli kɛ́ amɛmiifɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa ehei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Salt acts as a natural cleaner that draws out hidden worms, small insects, and soil microbes clinging to the undersides of leaves without damaging the produce.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni tsuɔ he nii. Ejieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, kooloi bibii kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Will washing my harvested vegetables in plain tap water remove all insects and dirt?
ga: Ani mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ pɔmpi nu mli daa lɛ baajie ŋmeii kɛ muji fɛɛ kɛjɛ mihe?

english: Plain water removes loose mud, but adding a little salt helps detach tiny insects and tiny eggs that stick tightly to leaf surfaces.
ga: Nu lɛ baajie muji ni etse ehe lɛ. Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmei fioo fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni egbɛɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to dry my leafy vegetables after washing them before I store or cook them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli beni mifɔ amɛhe sɛɛ dani mikɛto loo mihoo lɛ?

english: Excess water left on leaves trapped in bags or baskets creates moisture that causes rapid bacterial decay and rot. Drying them first keeps the leaves fresh and extends their shelf life.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ashiɔ yɛ baai ni akɛwo kotokui loo tsɛnsii amli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni haa helatsɛmɛi amli helai fiteɔ oya lɛ baa. Kɛ́ agbi amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ehee, ni ehaa amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested greens turn soft and slimy quickly if I pack them while wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya kɛji mikpa amɛ ni efɔ lɛ?

english: Trapped water on harvested leaves encourages mold and decay bacteria to grow quickly, turning healthy greens into unusable waste within a short time.
ga: Nu ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ baai ni akpa lɛ he lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ adalɛ oya lɛ he hewalɛ. Tsɔmɔmɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee jwɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: What happens to harvested leafy vegetables if I leave soil sitting on them for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa aduawai ni yɔɔ baai ni akpa lɛ anɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi sũ lɛ yɛ nakai aduawai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ hu?

english: Soil contains rot-causing fungi and bacteria that digest leaf tissue. Leaving dirt on leaves causes yellowing, spotting, and quick spoilage.
ga: Fungi ni kɛ fitemɔ baa kɛ muawai ni yeɔ baa fãji yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Muji ni ashiɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: How does cleaning and drying my harvested greens increase my farm profits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ ahe saamɔ kɛ amɛgbimɔ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛnamɔ aya hiɛ?

english: Clean, well-dried produce looks fresh, lasts longer on the market shelf, and builds buyer trust, allowing you to charge better prices than sellers with dirty or wet produce.
ga: Nibii ni he tse ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni ehe tse. Abaanyɛ akɛto jarayeli hei be kakadaŋŋ. ni oha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ahe amɛye Enɛ haa onyɛɔ obiɔ jara ni hi fe nihɔɔlɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli ewo muji loo efɔ.

english: What are the essential steps I should take after cutting leafy greens to get them ready for cooking?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii ni he hiaa ni esa akɛ mafee beni mifolɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni mikɛsaa mihe kɛha nihoomɔ?

english: Immediately after harvesting, wash the leaves thoroughly in clean water with a bit of salt, chop them if desired, and let them dry completely before cooking or packaging.
ga: Kɛji akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, okɛ nu ni mli tse ni akɛ ŋoo fioo ewo mli lɛ afɔ baai lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. Kpɔ̃ɔ mli bibii bibii bɔ ni osumɔɔ. ni oha egbi kwraa dani ohoo loo okɛwo tsɔne mli.

english: Young cocoa plants get sunburned easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Hulu shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize regain its green color and grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmei lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda oya.

english: If I plant my crop seeds closer together, won't I harvest more food from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. When crowded, plants stay small and weak, producing a smaller overall harvest than properly spaced crops.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli beni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ Tso lɛ baafee bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi fe tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like mites, thrips, or aphids, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with organic sprays like neem oil or recommended pest treatments stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites, thrips, loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ nɔ. Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it so critical to clear weeds when my crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your food plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop establishes strong roots without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛha oniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy, which sends food down into the ground to build big tubers. Staking lifts the vines high off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight and stay away from wet soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee hewalɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee bulb agboi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil year after year and builds up maize-specific pests. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil nutrients naturally and breaks insect life cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɔɔ ŋmãa he lɛ baa ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ kooloi bibii lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, prevents hot sunshine from drying out the soil water. It keeps the roots cool, conserves water, and stops weed seeds from receiving light to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ, ehiɛɔ nu mli, ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ aná la koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of protecting itself during dry weather. By shedding leaves, the plant loses less water to the hot air, going quiet until the rains return to sprout new leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ŋmei he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Tsei lɛ baafite nu fioo kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ. Ni ofee dioo kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ kɛ baai heei baaba.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures get too hot, water supply is irregular, or there are no insects to pollinate them. Regular watering during dry spells and keeping soil cool helps flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it true that rice needs a lot of water to grow well, and why?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ nu babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ? Ni mɛni hewɔ?

english: Yes, rice requires much more water than most crops. Water acts as its main nourishment and protection, helping the plant absorb nutrients from the soil while naturally preventing weeds from choking the crop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu babaoo he miihia ŋmãa fe tsei babaoo. Nu tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛ hebuu titri. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ jwɛi hu naa koni amɛkafite adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Will my corn crop die if water sits on the field for a long time like it does for rice?
ga: Ani mi ŋmãa lɛ baagbo kɛji nu lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmãa nu lɛ?

english: Yes, corn roots need air to breathe. Unlike rice, which thrives in flooded conditions, standing water will rot the roots of corn plants and cause them to yellow and die.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia ŋmãa shishifãi koni amɛmu. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni nu afua yɔɔ mli lɛ he. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baafite ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Where is the best place on my land to plant rice so that it gets enough moisture?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa koni maná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Rice grows best in low-lying areas, valley bottoms, or swampy fields where water naturally collects and stays in the soil for long periods.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, jɔɔ lɛ shishi, loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: How many months does it usually take for rice to mature and be ready for harvest after planting?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ ni ebaanyɛ akpa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most common rice varieties take about three to four months from the day you plant them until they are fully mature and ready to be harvested.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni oduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni omɔ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: How can I tell when my rice is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains on the farm turn golden-yellow and feel hard when you bite down on them.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. ni enuɔ he waa kɛ́ eeye ŋmãa

english: What usually causes sudden trouble or damage to planted corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni fɔɔ naagbai loo fitemɔ trukaa baa ŋmãa ni adu lɛ nɔ?

english: Sudden leaf damage on corn is commonly caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm or stem borers, which eat the leaves and central shoots of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm loo stem borers ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni fiteɔ trukaa yɛ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ baa. ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛteŋ ŋmeii lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn lacks nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that the soil is either too dry or soaked with too much standing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ kɛ nu ni ekã shi.

english: How can joining a local farmer group or district association help me manage my farm better?
ga: Te okwaafoi akuu loo kpokpaa nɔ kuu ko ni mikɛ mihe woɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Farmer groups give you early warnings about farming issues, teach you proper crop schedules, and make it easier to get farming advice, seeds, and better market prices together.
ga: Okwaafoi akui baatswa bo adafi yɛ okwaayeli he saji ahe kɛtsɔ hiɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa ni oha efee mlɛo akɛ onine ashɛ okwaayeli he ŋaawoo nɔ dumɔ dumɔwui kɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to plan my crop activities before the planting season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mato dumɔ nitsumɔi ahe gbɛjianɔ dani dumɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Planning early helps you prepare your land on time, buy good quality seeds, and align your planting with the start of the rains so your crops don't fail.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo mra Eyeɔ ebua bo ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be naa. Hemɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ Ni oto dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔ koni ekɛ nugbɔ be lɛ shishijee lɛ akpã gbee bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Can I plant corn and rice together on the exact same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: It is better to plant them in different fields because rice needs very wet or flooded ground to grow well, while corn needs well-drained land where water flows away easily.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amɛ yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efɔ loo nu eyi nɔ babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. He ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ ni nu baanyɛ ajɛ mli oya lɛ he miihia ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Big trees act as living umbrellas, providing shade, keeping the air cool, and holding moisture in the soil so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ hɔɔŋ, ni amɛhaa hɔɔŋ ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a vital nutrient in the soil. Without enough nitrogen or water, the plant cannot make the green chlorophyll it needs to grow strong corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji nitrogen loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil eŋɔli ni he hiaa koni aná ŋmãa toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Fertilizer is concentrated like salt, and putting it right against the stem can burn the plant's delicate skin and roots. Placing it a few inches away allows the roots to safely reach out and drink up the nutrients.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle ehe tamɔ ŋoo. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aya jɛmɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every year if I plant maize on the exact same patch of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and lets soil diseases build up. Rotating with beans or groundnuts restores nutrients and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni akwɛɔ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oooha amɛbua amɛhe naa Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, dry soil, or insect attacks. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap out of young leaves, or by a virus spread by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with bushy leaves but yielding tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava puts all its food energy into growing leaves above ground instead of sending that energy into the roots to build large tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ Cassava heɔ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ jamɛ a he wami ɔ yaa sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ a pee bulb nguahi.

english: How does spraying agricultural oil on my crops help stop insect pests?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaayeli mli fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa?

english: Crop oils work by coating insects and their tiny eggs with a thin layer of oil that blocks their breathing holes, smothering the pests safely without using harsh chemical poisons.
ga: Mu ni akɛwoɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. ni akɛ mu bibioo ko ewo mli lɛ. ni tsi amɛmumɔ bu lɛ naa Jiemɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shweshweeshwe ni okɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni mli wa tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my vegetable crops rot faster when bright sunshine comes right after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Warm, wet conditions create a hot environment where fungal diseases multiply quickly. The damp leaves combined with heat create perfect conditions for fungi to grow and cause soft rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Baai ni mli efɔ ni akɛ dɔlɛ fataa he lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni amɛdaraa ni amɛkɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even when I water the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Even with water, your crops stay weak because the weeds are consuming the plant food first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nu po yɔɔ mli lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ tsei lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Yellowing and curling cassava leaves are typically caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension agents helps protect your farm from this disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni o-extension agent lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ hela nɛɛ he.

english: What is causing small green and brown worms to eat the leaves inside the tops of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of young maize plants to feed. Early detection and applying approved organic or chemical sprays into the leaf funnel will stop them before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Organic sprays loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ anaa mra ni akɛtsuɔ nii. kɛya baa lɛ mli koni okpa amɛ dani amɛfite onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and leaves that cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa gives them cover and keeps the air humid during the Harmattan.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ tsei bibii loo shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ harmattan beaŋ.

english: Why should I remove some of the small stems growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: If too many sucker shoots grow at the base, they steal water and nutrients from the main tree. Removing extra shoots and leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ahi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the plant to produce food, which flows down to the roots and builds large, healthy yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia pilamɔi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii, ni hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to high heat, irregular watering, or a lack of plant food in the soil. Giving your plants steady water and mulching the base helps keep the roots cool so flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains all the nitrogen from the soil and allows maize pests to settle in the land. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie nitrogen fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. and allows corn pests to colonize the soil. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very tiny fruits when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for space, light, water, and soil food. Spacing your seeds properly gives every individual plant enough room to grow strong and bear heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo yibii ni tsii.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has run out of nutrients and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Soil lacking nutrients shows clear warning signs: plants grow slowly, leaves turn light green or yellow instead of deep green, and harvests get smaller each year. Adding compost, animal manure, or balanced fertilizers restores the soil's strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ jieɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo, tamɔ tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. And the harvest will be less each year. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: You should not plant immediately after the very first rain because the ground underneath is still hot and dry. Wait until two or three heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the soil, ensuring steady moisture for your seeds to germinate.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni edɔ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa be fɛɛ be koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How many years can my cocoa trees keep producing pods before I need to cut them down and replant?
ga: Afii enyiɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii dani ehe baahia ni afo lɛ ni adu ekoŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees can live and bear fruit for 25 to 30 years or more if properly maintained. You do not need to replant them every season like maize or tomatoes; the original trees you plant will yield harvests year after year.
ga: Cacao tsei baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehe ehiaaa ni odu tsei heei daa be, tamɔ ŋmãa loo tomato. Shishijee tsei ni odu lɛ baawo kpamɔ yibii afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Is it better to clear my entire farm and replant new cocoa trees when trees get old, or keep working with the old ones?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ majie miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni madu kookoo tsei heei beni tsei lɛ egbɔ lɛ? Aloo oya nɔ okɛ kookoo tso momo lɛ atsu nii?

english: If only a few old trees are struggling, you can plant new seedlings in the empty spaces while keeping the producing trees. However, if the whole farm is over 30 years old, diseased, or yielding very little, clearing and replanting the entire land with improved hybrid varieties gives a better long-term yield.
ga: Kɛji tsei momoi fioo komɛi pɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ yɛ be mli ni okwɛɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ lolo. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ eye fe afii 30, hela emɔ lɛ loo ewooo yibii fioo ko pɛ. Kɛ́ atsumɔ he muu lɛ fɛɛ he ni akɛ tsei ni afee amɛ srɔtoi lɛ adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If my old cocoa trees start giving me fewer pods, do I have to cut them down or can I refresh them?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso momo lɛ bɔi ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ Esa akɛ afo lɛ loo abaanyɛ aku sɛɛ afee lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: You do not always have to cut them down. You can perform 'pruning' and 'rehabilitation' by cutting back overgrown branches, clearing shade, and applying proper cocoa fertilizer to encourage fresh shoots and new pod growth from the same tree.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be ehe baahia ni ofolɔ amɛ. Obaanyɛ ‘ofolɔ’ ni ‘oha amɛfee ehee’ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni ooofolɔ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni okɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii ni okɛwo tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli ŋmeii heei kɛ ŋmeii heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is too old to produce good pods anymore?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmeii kpakpai dɔŋŋ?

english: An aging cocoa tree that needs replacing will usually have a very thick, hollow trunk, produce tiny or misshapen pods, have sparse leaf growth, and fail to flower heavily even after the rains start.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni egbɔ ni esa akɛ atsake lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse waa, ni ŋmeii yɔɔ mli ni ŋmeii bibii loo amɛhe bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli. Baai ni gbɛ eshwa lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Ni fɔfɔii babaoo bɛ ni fɔɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ po sɛɛ.

english: How long do I have to wait after planting cocoa before the land starts yielding pods?
ga: Kɛ́ odu kookoo lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: Traditional cocoa trees take about 3 to 5 years to start producing their first pods, while modern hybrid cocoa seedlings can begin yielding fruit in as little as 2 to 3 years with good care.
ga: Kusum mli cacao tsei lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I harvest cocoa pods from the same trees multiple times in a single year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ shii abɔ yɛ afi kome mli?

english: Yes, cocoa trees bear fruit continuously, but in Ghana, there are two main harvest periods: the main crop season from October to February (which yields the biggest harvest) and the minor crop season from May to June.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii. Shi yɛ Ghana lɛ, kpamɔ bei titrii enyɔ yɔɔ: Be titri ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ ji kɛjɛ October kɛyashi February. (ni woɔ yibii babaoo fe fɛɛ) kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ ni ji enyɔ kɛjɛɔ May kɛyashi June.

english: Why is my cocoa farm giving me fewer bags of cocoa this year compared to when the trees first started producing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ miiha mi kookoo kotokui fioo ko pɛ afi nɛɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni wɔbɔi kookoo feemɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ he.

english: Every harvest removes nutrients from the soil. Over time, without fertilizer or manure, the soil loses its richness, and the trees produce fewer pods. Lack of rainfall, poor pruning, or pest attacks can also reduce yield.
ga: Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite hewalɛ. kɛ tsei ni woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo, nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ, tsei ni afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ Loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi hu.

english: Now that my young cocoa farm has started producing its first pods, do I need to care for the trees differently?
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ, kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo ko yɛ jɛmɛ. Minɔ lɛ ebɔi eklɛŋklɛŋ pods lɛ feemɔ. Ani ehe miihia ni makwɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ?

english: Yes, once trees start producing pods, they require more nutrients and sunlight. You should prune excess branches to allow sunlight to reach the trunk, remove mistletoe parasites, and regularly pluck off diseased pods to protect the healthy harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni tso lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Niyenii babaoo kɛ hulu la he miihia amɛ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Jiemɔ mistletoe mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa koni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Can I just take seeds from my current cocoa harvest and plant them to start a new farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ni mikpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli ni madu koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: While seeds from your current harvest will grow, it is much better to buy certified hybrid seedlings from approved nurseries. Hybrid plants resist local diseases better and start yielding pods much faster than seeds saved from ordinary pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ okpamɔ ni okpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ po Shi ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ. Hybrid tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii folo mli lɛ.

english: If I start a cocoa farm now as a young person, can it continue to feed me for the rest of my life?
ga: Kɛji mije kookoo ŋmɔ shishi bianɛ beni miji oblanyo fioo lɛ Ani obaanyɛ oya nɔ okwɛ mi yɛ miwala be fɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, a cocoa farm is a long-term investment. Because cocoa trees can yield crops for decades, starting a farm early in life can provide you with reliable seasonal income well into your old age as long as you maintain the trees and soil health.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ji nitsumɔ ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, cacao tsei baanyɛ awo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Kɛ́ oje ŋmɔ shishi yɛ ogbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha oná shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ be mli kɛyashi obaagbɔ, kɛji akɛ okwɛ tsei lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods have many big beans inside, but others on the same tree only have a few small ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ekomɛi yɛ dumɔwui wuji babaoo yɛ mli lɛ? Shi kookoo ŋmeii krokomɛi Yɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. only a few seeds

english: This usually happens because of uneven pollination. Cocoa flowers need insects like midges to carry pollen; if only a little pollen reaches a flower, fewer seeds will form inside that pod, leaving it with fewer and smaller beans.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ pollination ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ hewɔ. Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii koni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ shɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ, Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ baa shi. Beans ni eshwɛ lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why do my maize cobs have empty spaces on them instead of full rows of corn grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Empty spaces on a cob mean those parts of the flower were not pollinated properly. Hot dry winds or drought during flowering can dry up the corn silk before pollen reaches it, leaving bare spots on the cob.
ga: He ni nɔ ko bɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ fãi srɔtoi lɛ. ni kɔɔ fɔfɔii ahe ni anyɛɛɛ ashɛre amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ he Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa loo hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa siliki lɛ agbi dani fɔfɔi lɛ ashɛ he. Ekɛ muji baa cob lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are some peppers on my farm growing very large while others on the same plant remain tiny?
ga: Why do some peppers on my farm grow so large? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii henɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ bibii lɛ.

english: Plants send most of their water and nutrients to the first fruits that open. If you remove damaged or tiny peppers early, the plant will share its energy evenly among the remaining fruits so they all grow well.
ga: Tso lɛ kɛ enu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo majeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii ni gbeleɔ lɛ. Kɛji ojie ŋmeii ni efite loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ mra lɛ, Tso lɛ jaa ehewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do many flowers on my tomato plants fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot sunny days or irregular watering. The plant sheds flowers to save its energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ gbi ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Tsei baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why did only two seeds sprout out of the four seeds I planted in each hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ejwɛ ni midu yɛ bu fɛɛ bu mli lɛ ateŋ enyɔ pɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, if the soil is too dry, or if soil insects eat them before they germinate. Planting seeds at the proper depth and keeping the soil moist improves sprout rates.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Aloo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is water flowing strongly at the beginning of my irrigation pipe, but barely dripping at the far end of the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hoɔ waa yɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shishijee lɛ? Shi ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko kɛkɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: This happens when dirt or sand collects inside the pipe or when water pressure drops over a long distance. Opening the end caps to flush out trapped sediment usually restores proper water flow.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ muji loo ŋã bua ehe naa yɛ paipii lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu lɛ mli hewalɛ ba shi yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛ. Bei pii lɛ, naagbee tsɔne lɛ ni agbeleɔ koni akɛjie sũ ni emɔ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I check if my farm water pipes are blocked when my vegetables start looking dry?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu paipii lɛ efo beni mi-aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Turn on your water supply and walk along the pipe line to check the ground around each outlet. If some spots stay dry while others are wet, or if water is building up in one area, there is a blockage or leak in that section.
ga: Sumɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni onyiɛ paipii lɛ mli koni okwɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle nu ni jɛɔ mli lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he lɛ. Kɛji akɛ hei komɛi egbi yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu edɔ. aloo nu ebua ehe naa yɛ he kome Tsɔɔ akɛ nɔ ko etsĩ loo nu miiho yɛ nakai fã lɛ mli.

english: Why are muddy pools forming around only a few rows of my crops where the water pipes run?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ŋmɔtɔ ko babɔle ehe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi pɛ ji he ni nu paipii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Muddy pools indicate a leak or crack in that specific part of your water pipe. Fixing these leaks quickly stops water waste and prevents crop roots in that spot from rotting in standing water.
ga: Nubu ni mli ewo muji lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu miiho loo egbɛ eshwa o-nu paipi lɛ fã pɔtɛɛ ko mli. Kɛ́ asaa nu ni hoɔ nɛɛ, ebaaha nu ni afiteɔ lɛ akpa oya, ni ebaatsi tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell whether my yellowing maize leaves are caused by a lack of fertilizer or by a disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni bɛ loo hela ko hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni ji yellow lɛ baa lɛ?

english: If the yellowing starts at the bottom leaves and forms a 'V' shape down the center, the plant needs nitrogen fertilizer. If you see scattered yellow spots, rings, or powdery dust on the leaves, it is caused by a crop disease.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ je shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ ni efee ‘V’ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, no lɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji ana ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ loo sũ ni egbɛ eshwã baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso hela ji nɔ ni kɛba.

english: What steps should I follow if my cassava plants suddenly stop growing and drop their leaves?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ kpa dalɛ trukaa ni ebaa lɛ fite?

english: First inspect the undersides of the leaves for insects like mealybugs or spider mites, then check if the root soil is dry or waterlogged. Cassava drops its leaves to protect itself during prolonged dry spells or severe pest attacks.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji kooloi tamɔ mealybugs loo spider mites yɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, kwɛmɔ kɛji shishifã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Yucca shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa waa lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow fast. It can also happen if excessive rain washes away soil nutrients or drowns the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ ha niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fite loo eha shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up with yellowish patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled, spotted leaves are a sign of the Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus prevents the plant from making enough food, resulting in smaller tubers underground.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and burn when I remove all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Large trees provide shade that lowers the temperature and keeps moisture in the soil, protecting delicate cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni haa hulutsoo baa shi, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Ebuɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Plantain plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from the intense sun. By hiding part of the leaf surface, the plant stops water from evaporating too quickly during hot, dry spells.
ga: Dumɔwui shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ baa lɛ nɔ fã ko ni ekɛteeɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: When weather gets extremely hot or dry, tomato plants get stressed and drop their flowers to save energy. Once the temperature cools down or watering improves, the flowers will stay and turn into fruit.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ loo edɔ waa Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ hi lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baahi shi ni ebaatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I space my cassava stems far apart instead of crowding them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala ŋmei tsei lɛ amli moŋ fe ni mafee amɛ ekome?

english: Cassava roots need room under the dirt to swell into big tubers. If you plant them too close, the roots will fight for water and soil nutrients, leaving you with thin, weak tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji odu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, obaaná yitso ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do people advise planting beans in the same field as maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans have a special ability to pull invisible nitrogen food from the air and put it into the dirt. Maize feeds heavily on nitrogen, so growing them together naturally fertilizes the maize.
ga: Beans yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni ekɛjieɔ nitrogen nibii ni anaaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi yeɔ nitrogen akɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa lɛ ekome lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa.

english: Why does adding dried animal manure to my farm make my crops grow better than using soil alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi fata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ pɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the tiny living organisms in the ground and helps the soil hold onto rainwater longer. It acts as a slow-release food that builds strong roots and stalks.
ga: Koolooi ashwiei haa bɔɔ nii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni jieɔ ehe blɛoo ni haa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa baa.

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark dirt inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni mli edɔ kɛ muji ni mli edɔ yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center funnel of the plant to eat soft leaves. The dark dirt is its waste, indicating an active infestation.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Muji ni tsuɔ waa lɛ ji jwɛi. ni tsɔɔ basabasafeemɔ ni eba lɛ

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts under the soil are mature enough to pull up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: You can check by harvesting one test plant. If the insides of the shells have turned dark brown or black and the seeds are full and firm, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ kaa tso kome ni oookpa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the soil and prevent the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni etsĩ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu ni amɛye nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big leaves, but produce tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are given too much fertilizer, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in its roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei baato niyenii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai kɛ tsei ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with weak stems when I plant them close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. They stretch upward rapidly to reach light, making their stems thin and easily broken by wind.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have soft leaves and short roots that cannot handle direct sunlight and dry winds. They need temporary shade plants like plantains to shelter them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛha amɛha amɛhe aahu kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo shɔŋŋ.
