english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when there is a sudden change from very dry to very wet soil. The plant gets stressed and discards the flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsakemɔ ko ba trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa nɔ. Tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I plant maize on the exact same land repeatedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the specific nutrients that crop loves from the soil. It also allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ helai hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer on my field when the heavy rain is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ afɔseɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔji amli kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash fertilizer off the field before the plant roots can drink it in. This wastes your money and can wash the chemicals into nearby drinking water.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. This will cost you money and can leach chemicals into nearby drinking water.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps moisture during hot dry days, stops weeds from growing, and decays into natural plant food.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Helps keep the soil cool Locks in moisture during hot, dry days Prevents weeds from growing and decomposes into natural plant food

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juice from young leaves, or by viruses carried by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ

english: Why is it important to weed my farm early while the crops are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli mra lɛ? Enɛ he miihia yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ.

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will quickly steal the sunlight, water, and soil food your crop needs to establish strong roots early in life.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Ni ejuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ oya koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli mra.

english: Why do my tomato and okra plants produce fruits at different times of the year instead of a fixed month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato kɛ okra tsei woɔ yibii yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Vegetable crops like tomatoes and okra rely heavily on specific weather conditions like rain and sun. Because rain patterns change each year, the exact time these plants grow, flower, and produce fruit will shift with the weather.
ga: Aduawai ni aduɔ tamɔ tomato kɛ okra damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi tamɔ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo nɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ tsakeɔ daa afi. Be pɔtɛɛ ni tsei nɛɛ daa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ naa.

english: Can I start land preparation and planting as early as January, or must I wait for the main rainy season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛ dumɔwui yɛ January shishijee gbɛ loo esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ?

english: You can start your farming activities in January. Preparing land and planting certain hardy crops early allows them to catch the first light rains and establish roots before the heavy rain season begins.
ga: Obaanyɛ oje okwaayeli nitsumɔi lɛ shishi yɛ January mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ mra Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: How can I keep my farm productive throughout the entire year instead of farming only in the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔ lɛ awo yibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ, shi jeee yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli pɛ?

english: To farm year-round, you can mix long-season crops like cassava with fast-growing vegetables and hardy grains, and stagger your planting times starting from early January so you harvest continuously.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni ofee okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei afutu aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ dumɔwui ni wa. Ni oja dumɔ be lɛ mli kɛjɛ January shishijee mli koni onyɛ oná ŋmaa ni yaa nɔ.

english: What is the 'one woman 1000' crop variety, and why do farmers choose to plant it?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘Yei Akpe’ tso henɔ lɛ ni mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi halaa akɛ amɛbaadu lɛ?

english: One woman 1000' is a local variety named for its high productivity and reliability. Farmers plant it because it produces continuously throughout the year, providing a steady supply of food and income.
ga: One woman 1000’ ji maŋ lɛ mli tsofa ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ yɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo kɛ hekɛnɔfɔɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. Okwaafoi duɔ lɛ ejaakɛ abaanyɛ afee lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ha niyenii kɛ shika ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do millet and sorghum stay green and survive hot dry spells much better than corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Millet and sorghum have deep roots and tough leaves that trap moisture inside the plant. This allows them to withstand extreme sun and drought where corn would normally dry up and wilt.
ga: Sorghum kɛ sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni wa ni mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ ni bei pii lɛ ŋmãa gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do heavy rains sometimes spoil my tomato farm while my corn thrives in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ mi-tomato ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ miida lolo yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have delicate leaves and flowers that easily catch fungal diseases and rot when hit by heavy rain, whereas corn has strong, water-loving leaves and stalks that grow rapidly with plenty of rainfall.
ga: Tomato yɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baanyɛ atswa lɛ oya, ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, egboɔ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa yɛ baai ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ. ni daa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant groundnuts and beans alongside my corn field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that pull natural nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This enriches the soil and provides free nutrients for heavy-feeding crops like corn.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehaa niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Can I grow root crops like yam and cassava together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ shishifãi tamɔ sweet potato kɛ cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, yam and cassava can grow on the same land. While yam requires high soil mounds for its tubers, cassava is hardier and can grow around the edges or between mounds, maximizing your land space.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ he miihia ŋmeii babaoo moŋ, shi yucca ŋmeii lɛ wa fe tsutsu lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi loo amɛteŋ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ aya hiɛ kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛɔ

english: Why do many farmers plant a mix of grains, legumes, and root crops on one farm instead of just one single crop?
ga: Why do so many farmers grow grain? ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi ni akɛfutu mli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli Yɛ tso henɔ kome pɛ ni abaadu lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Planting a mix of crops like corn, beans, millet, and cassava protects you from total loss. If bad weather kills one crop, the tougher crops will still yield food and income for your household.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa ni ooodu lɛ baabu ohe kɛjɛ fitemɔ kwraa he. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii kpata ŋmɔshi nibii kome hiɛ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa lɛ baaya nɔ aha niyenii kɛ shika aha oshia lɛ.

english: Why do my okra plants drop their flowers without forming any pods when the weather suddenly turns hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi trukaa ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? The weather is hot and dry?

english: Okra plants get stressed when water is low and heat is high. To protect themselves from dying, the plant drops its flowers to conserve water and energy until the moisture returns.
ga: Gumbo tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ kɛji nu lɛ faaa ni dɔlɛ hu fa. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so all leaves catch sunlight easily and stay safe from moisture and diseases on the soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ anyɛ ana hulu la lɛ mlɛo. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main stem, they steal water, nutrients, and sunlight from the mother plant. Cutting off extra suckers leaves just one or two strong ones, allowing the mother plant to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ awo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and thin without producing big ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo waa ni ŋmãa toi wuji ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for light and soil food. They stretch upwards trying to reach sunlight, making them weak and unable to invest energy into forming big, full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei baawuu amɛhe koni amɛná la kɛ shikpɔŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe koni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmãa toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which traps natural nitrogen fertilizer from the air and leaves it in the soil. Planting them first enriches the soil so the maize you plant next grows stronger and yields better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ mra lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni obaadu be kroko lɛ baawa ni ebaawo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops start turning yellow after very heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away key nutrients like nitrogen deep down into the soil where roots cannot reach. Excess water also fills up air spaces in the soil, preventing roots from breathing properly to take up food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing green and yellow patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ he mfoniri lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making food through its leaves, resulting in small, poor cassava roots.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Kooloi bibii eyɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei atsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfee niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraaa, ni amɛhe ehiaaa.

english: Why do I see tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms that hide inside the central funnel of young maize plants to eat tender leaves. If left unchecked, they can destroy the growing point of the crop, so early control with recommended insecticides or organic methods is needed.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ akudɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without turning into fresh tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato hee lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the crop suffers heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. When the plant feels stressed by bad conditions, it sheds its flowers to save energy for basic survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihe dɔlɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni tsei nuɔ he akɛ shihilɛi ni esaaa miigba amɛnaa lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Why shouldn't I spray chemical insecticides on my pepper farm while the plants are flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays during flowering kill friendly insects like bees that visit flowers to help them form fruits. Without these insects transferring pollen between flowers, many flowers will wither without producing peppers.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii anɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo tamɔ ŋmeii ni baa fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni baanyɛ ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Fɔfɔi babaoo baagbo kɛkɛ ni amɛjieee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field with no shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Planting them near shade trees or plantains protects them from harsh heat while their roots develop fully.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my maize in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives each plant enough space to capture sunlight and root nutrients without fighting its neighbors. It also makes it much easier to walk through the farm to clear weeds and apply fertilizer evenly.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baajɛ eshishifãi amli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. It also makes it much easier to walk through the farm to weed and fertilize regularly.

english: How far apart should I space my tomato plants when putting them in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Spacing tomatoes about two feet apart allows air to flow freely between the plants, which keeps leaves dry and prevents fungal diseases from spreading quickly during the rainy season.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tomatoi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee ninetalɔi enyɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii helai agbɛ ashwã oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do people tell me to cut off some of the extra branches on my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning excess stems forces the cassava plant to direct its energy down into the ground, which makes the food roots grow larger and thicker instead of wasting energy on too many leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, enyɛɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ amaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii lɛ shishifãi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai babaoo nɔ lɛ

english: Should I cut down old crop stalks right after harvest or leave them on the land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ashishifãi momoi lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akpa amɛ loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Leaving healthy crop stalks on the soil helps shade the ground, trap moisture, and build rich soil as they decay. However, if the old plants were sick, you should cut and remove them so the disease does not spread to your next crop.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ahe tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii baa be mli ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ. Shi, kɛji tsei momo lɛ hela mɔ amɛ lɛ, Esa akɛ Ofolɔ amɛ ni ojie amɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks or iron stakes next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ loo dade tso ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to make food. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes keeps the leaves healthy and leads to bigger tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewaje baai lɛ, ni ebaaha ŋmeii wuji aba shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Can I use sharp metal tools close to the base of my crops when clearing weeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dade nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ atsu nii kɛ́ miikpa jwɛi?

english: Weeding too close to the stem with metal tools can accidentally cut the shallow feeder roots of your crop. It is safer to scrape gently further away or pull weeds near the main stem by hand.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dade nibii jieɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ afo onibii lɛ yɛ oshara mli. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji okɛ ŋmɔlɔ shwie nɔ. Je kpo loo okɛ onine agbala jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ tso titri lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves roll up slightly in intense heat as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing too much water, but if they remain tightly curled during cool mornings, it means tiny pests are attacking the leaves.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe lolo yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso hu? Etsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni tutuaa baai

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. The crop moves whatever food it has left up to its newest top leaves to survive, telling you that the field needs fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ekɛɛ bo akɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ahe miihia ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What causes my bean plants to drop their flowers before producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Bean plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat or dry soil, as the plant tries to save water and energy until weather conditions become favorable again.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing when water sits on the farm for many days after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When excess rain covers the soil for too long, the roots choke from a lack of air and cannot take up nutrients, causing the plant to turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ babaoo nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to grow green and healthy. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or keep the soil waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hole niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo eha nu ewo mli.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny beneficial helpers on their roots that trap natural food from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize and keeps the soil healthy without extra cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bɛ yelikɛbuamɔ fioo ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛmɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Yam leaves need to catch direct sunlight to produce energy for expanding the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and letting air flow freely.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi helai anaa ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose their leaves when I cut down all the big shade trees on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi beni mifo tsei wuji ni haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli shade lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa plants naturally prefer scattered light. Without protective shade trees, direct hot sun scorches the leaves, dries out the plant, and leaves it vulnerable to destructive insect attacks.
ga: Cocoa tsei sumɔɔ la ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã baai lɛ. egbiɔ tso lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo akɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atutua lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upwards and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips that suck the sap from tender new leaves, spreading viruses that make the leaves wrinkle and stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Egbɛɔ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Root rot happens when water sits in the soil for too long around the roots, or when infected stem cuttings are planted, allowing soil fungi to soften and spoil the tubers.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ adu tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afee blɛoo ni ebaafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do I see small ragged holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ.

english: This is a sign of pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hide inside the tight center of the growing maize plant to eat tender leaves before they unfurl.
ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ ni mli wa lɛ he okadi koni amɛye baai bibii dani amɛjie amɛhe kpo.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they get stressed by high heat, sudden drought, or lack of water, dropping the blossoms to save their energy until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa hao amɛ. hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa loo nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli Gbalamɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ koni okɛ hewalɛ ato kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods on my trees turn black and dry up while they are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbi beni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ?

english: While cocoa trees naturally drop some tiny pods they cannot support, widespread blackening is caused by fungal diseases like Black Pod or damage from sap-sucking insects like capsids.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ cacao tsei jieɔ ŋmeii bibii moŋ, shi anyɛɛɛ aye abua nakai yɛ adebɔɔ naa Shi nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa ji ŋmeii helai, tamɔ ŋmeii ni etsɔ diŋ, loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ ŋmeii, tamɔ capsids lɛ fitemɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct, scorching sunlight. Leaving some large shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ yaa nɔ edaa lɛ baa.

english: Yellow lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK early in the season helps restore the leaves to green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ aku sɛɛ afee amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Look for ragged holes chewed into the leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the central funnel of the plant, accompanied by sawdust-like droppings. Catching them early makes pest control treatments much more effective.
ga: Taomɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ. Ekɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ŋmɔɔ Ekɛ ehe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli. kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ebaaha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need room underground to swell into large tubers. If you plant them too close together, the roots compete with each other for water and nutrients, resulting in many small, thin roots instead of big tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛshwere ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji odu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ bulb wuji najiaŋ.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. The very first rain is often followed by a dry heat spell, which can scorch and kill newly sprouted seeds before the main rain season truly begins.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. Planting them with maize naturally feeds the maize and improves soil quality without extra cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli abele duɔ lɛ haa abele lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Saving seeds from hybrid maize usually leads to a much smaller harvest the following year. Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields in their first generation, so buying fresh seeds each season gives you the best crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni ooohe daa afi lɛ baaha oná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a plant virus carried by tiny whiteflies. Controlling these insects early and removing severely infected plants stops the disease from spreading through your whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ni tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch or watering helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaatsumɔ?

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and begin to dry naturally. This shows that the vine has finished storing all its energy down into the root tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛje shishi amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto shishifã lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees drying up and turning brown in the sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very tender and cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to block the intense sun and keep the soil moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: This rot is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning dense branches lets in sunlight and air, which keeps the pods dry and helps prevent the disease.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stay small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make leaves green and healthy. Rain supplies water, but the plant still needs manure or fertilizer to grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Nugbɔ ji nu jɛɛhe. Shi ŋmeii he miihia tsei lolo koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I place fertilizer directly near the plant roots instead of scattering it across the whole field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Placing fertilizer near the roots ensures your crop absorbs the nutrients immediately before weeds can steal them or heavy rains wash them away from the field.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani jwɛi lɛ juɔ amɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the soft growth center of maize plants. Spraying approved treatments directly into the plant center early in the morning or late evening helps protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni daraa yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties stops this disease from destroying your yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha hela lɛ akpa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field with my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-cassava lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and feeds it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil and helps your cassava grow larger roots without extra expense.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-cassava lɛ ni ekwɛɔ shishifãi wuji ni ekɛ shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly even if I clear them late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mifoɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ be ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa naagbee lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. If you clear them late, they have already stolen the food your crops needed during their most important growing period.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ojie lɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaaju niyenii ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are my plantain bunches growing very small compared to other farms in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwereɔ fioo kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji krokomɛi ahe lɛ? yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ

english: When too many young shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal nutrients and water from the main plant. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only two or three stems, allowing the main stem to produce a bigger, heavier bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Ebaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii 2-3 pɛ, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ afee ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Providing consistent water at the root area during hot days helps the blossoms stay attached and develop into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and rotting before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifite dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf yellowing and rotting are often caused by fungal diseases or waterlogging in the soil. High moisture creates an ideal environment for fungi to feed on your crops and cause decay.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii helai loo nu ni hiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ fitemɔ baa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni yeɔ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: How can I tell if my crop problem is caused by insects or by a plant disease like fungus?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ahe helai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe naagbai lɛ baa?

english: Insects usually leave visible signs like chewed leaves, holes, or sticky fluids, whereas fungal diseases often appear as powdery patches, dark spots, or soft rotting areas across stems and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi shĩɔ okadii ni anaa, tamɔ baai ni amɛye, bu, loo nu ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo hei ni egbo ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops suddenly wither and droop even when there is enough water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ lɛ? He ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo yɛ?

english: Sudden withering despite adequate moisture is usually a sign of root rot or stem disease. Fungi or parasites in the soil attack the roots, stopping the plant from taking up food and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ trukaa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ ji shishifãi ni egbo loo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe hela he okadi. Fungi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Can I use natural solutions from my community to fight pests without buying expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni jɛ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛwu ashi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ aheee?

english: Yes, natural treatments like sprays made from crushed neem tree leaves, wood ash, or soap solutions can repel pests and control mild fungal infections without harming your crops or soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa, tso mli sũ, loo samla ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashwie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni eye tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ ni eyeee onibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ awui.

english: Will chemical sprays damage my crops or soil if I do not use them properly?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baafite miŋmɔshi nibii loo mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, applying chemicals at the wrong strength or at the wrong time can burn your crop leaves, kill good soil organisms, and leave dangerous residues on the food you produce.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni falɛ ni esaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã otso lɛ baai lɛ. Egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshiɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ niyenii ni ofeɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I protect myself and my land when applying chemical treatments on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mihe kɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsu nii?

english: Always wear protective clothing like boots and long sleeves, mix chemicals strictly according to instructions, avoid spraying against the wind, and keep chemicals far away from drinking water sources.
ga: Wo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ atadei kɛ nine kakadaŋŋ agboi be fɛɛ be. Futumɔ tsofai pɛpɛɛpɛ taakɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni oooshwie lɛ he. ni okɛ tsofai akabote nu ni anuɔ lɛ he

english: Why do pests attack my farm heavily in some months but seem to disappear in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ etutua miŋmɔ lɛ waa yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli shi etamɔ nɔ ni amɛlaajeɔ yɛ ŋmɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Pest and fungal populations change with the weather; humidity and high heat during rainy seasons help pests multiply quickly, while dry weather slows them down.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii ayibɔ tsakeɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daraa fioo.

english: How does changing my planting date help protect my young crops from pest attacks?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbi ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ tsakemɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: Planting slightly earlier or later in the season shifts your crops' vulnerable growing stage so it doesn't align with the peak arrival time of common local insects.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ mra fioo loo sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsake tso lɛ dalɛ be lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ehiii nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ be ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fɔɔ baa lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: Why should I inspect my crops regularly even when they appear healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa kɛji akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ po lɛ?

english: Catching pests or disease spots early makes treatment much easier and cheaper, allowing you to stop an outbreak before it spreads and ruins your whole field.
ga: Ni aaamɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo helai ahe hei mra Enɛ haa helatsamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni ejara hu waaa. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa dani egbɛɔ eshwaa ni efiteɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Does planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season cause disease problems?
ga: Ani tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ kɛ helai ahe naagbai baa?

english: Yes, growing the same crop repeatedly allows crop-specific insects and fungal spores to build up in the soil over time, leading to worse crop decay in future seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ. Enɛ baaha kooloi bibii kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli ŋmeii abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ yɛ bei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient plant need to grow leaves and stay green. Applying well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the base of the plant will help it recover its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛbɔleɔ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aku esɛɛ kɛba eŋɔli su lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny natural factories on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the ground and makes the maize growing next to them stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. amɛdara ni amɛhe wa

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crops with dry grass or dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Tsoi ni jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the ground cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, and blocks weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ latsaa be mli. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop in the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. Drooping is the plant's way of conserving moisture, and they usually bounce back once the sun sets and temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Drooping ji gbɛ kome ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛhaa tsei. Ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛyaa sɛɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers if they don't get pollinated by tiny beneficial insects called midges, or if the tree is stressed by drought or lack of shade. Ensuring adequate shade trees and protecting insect habitats helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ wooo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ehiɛɛɛ amɛhe. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Aloo kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ loo hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni tso lɛ aná hulutsoo ni sa kɛ kooloi ashihilɛhei ahebuu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that stay near the surface instead of going deep into the soil. If the soil is too wet or if tiny pests called nematodes eat the root system, the plant loses its grip and falls over easily.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ. Ewaaa akɛ tso lɛ baafee mɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ebaagbee shi.

english: Curling and yellowing tomato leaves are usually caused by a plant virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Keeping the farm free of weeds where insects hide and protecting young plants helps stop the virus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ he ni kooloi baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ lɛ, ni abuɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and rot in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for a long time, allowing fungal diseases to attack the tubers. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: What is making ragged holes in the middle whorl of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn plants lɛ miifee bu yɛ ring lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Ragged holes in the center leaves of young corn are usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant during the day and eat the fresh leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi mli. ni oye baai heei lɛ dani amɛje kpo

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly and look weak whenever there are weeds growing near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil that your crops need. When weeds are present, your crops suffer from starvation because the weeds consume the resources first.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ mli. Beni jwɛi yɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ he amanehulu ejaakɛ jwɛi yeɔ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Yellowing and falling leaves often signal Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease or a severe nutrient deficiency. When infected, the trees struggle to transport food and water, causing leaves to discolor and drop before the tree gradually dies if left untreated.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli fuumɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni naa wa waa. Beni hela lɛ emɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ nu aya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani tso lɛ baanyɛ abɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Ebaagbo kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: If my cocoa farm gets infected by a bad crop disease, how long will it take for the land to heal so I can plant safely again?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii lɛ emɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli hu? Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani shikpɔŋ lɛ baatsa dani abaanyɛ adu lɛ ekoŋŋ shweshweeshwe?

english: Severe cocoa diseases like Swollen Shoot Virus require cutting down infected trees and waiting about 3 to 5 years while applying proper soil treatment and planting disease-resistant varieties before full production can safely resume.
ga: Kookoo helai ni naa wa waa, tamɔ Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ biɔ ni afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛmɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5, ni akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsofai ni sa awo mli ni adu tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ dani amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba nitsumɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Can traditional concoctions completely cure my cocoa trees if they catch a plant virus?
ga: Ani kusum mli niyenii ni ahoɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsa mi-cacao tsei lɛ kwraa kɛji akɛ tso mli hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ emɔ amɛ?

english: Traditional mixtures might help ward off some farm pests, but viral diseases inside a cocoa tree's stem cannot be cured by external mixtures. Stopping a virus usually requires cutting out infected branches or whole trees to prevent the disease from spreading.
ga: Kusum nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu he kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi komɛi ahe Shi anyɛɛɛ akɛ nibii ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ atsa helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ ni abaatsi naa lɛ biɔ ni afo tsei niji loo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot whenever the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates high humidity, which helps the Black Pod fungus spread rapidly through splashing water droplets. Spraying approved fungicides before the heavy rains start protects the pods from rotting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ haa blackpod tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Why can my cocoa trees survive harsh dry seasons better than my maize or vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa mli jogbaŋŋ fe mi ŋmãa loo aduawai lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees develop a deep taproot system that reaches water far below the ground during dry spells, whereas shallow-rooted crops like maize dry out quickly when rain stops.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ abele lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya.

english: Why do some cocoa trees on my farm survive an insect attack while others nearby die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ wala kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi yeɔ wala lɛ? yɛ gbele he lɛ

english: Individual cocoa trees have different genetic strength and root vigor. Trees with stronger roots and better access to soil nutrients can resist pest damage much better than weaker neighboring trees.
ga: Cacao tso fɛɛ tso yɛ fɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ kɛ shishifã hewalɛ sɔrɔtoi. Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe amɛkutsoŋbii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Is direct afternoon sunlight good for my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani shwane hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight burns tender young cocoa leaves. Seedlings need shade from larger plants like plantain or shade trees during their first two years to trap moisture and protect them until they mature.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa kookoo baai bibii. Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara.

english: Why does my old cocoa farm yield much fewer pods now than it did ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kwraa fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, they pull essential minerals out of the ground year after year. Without replacing nutrients using organic manure or fertilizers, the soil becomes depleted and pod production drops.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ Amɛjieɔ nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni akɛtoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii lɛ najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know if a sick cocoa tree can still recover or if I should cut it down completely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kookoo tso ni hela mɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ lolo loo esa akɛ afo lɛ kwraa?

english: If a cocoa tree shows swollen stems, severe branch dieback, or consistently produces fewer than 10 pods a season despite good feeding, it cannot recover fully and should be cut down to protect nearby healthy trees.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ jie shishifãi ni efuu kpo lɛ Nine lɛ gboɔ waa. aloo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni shɛɛɛ 10 yɛ be fɛɛ mli yɛ niyenii kpakpa ni amɛhaa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Kookoo tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsa kwraa kɔkɔɔkɔ. ni esa akɛ afo koni akɛbu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster on my land than my actual crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi miida yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe mitsei diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients aggressively, allowing them to outgrow cultivated crops like cocoa if the farm is not weeded regularly.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkɛ ekãa aju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo kɛji akɛ ajieee jwɛi kɛjɛɛɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa.

english: Why do pests keep climbing up my cocoa trees and destroying my pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kwɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfiteɔ mi-pods lɛ?

english: Pests like squirrels and insects attack cocoa trees because the pods contain sweet moisture and food. Regularly inspecting your farm and pruning low-hanging branches makes it harder for climbing pests to reach and destroy your fruit.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii tutuaa cacao tsei lɛ ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni ŋɔɔ yɔɔ amɛmli. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni ofolɔ tsei niji ni shwieɔ shi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha amɛ akɛ amɛaakwɔ koni amɛyashɛ oyibii lɛ ahe ni amɛfite.

english: What will happen to my farm if I am not constantly checking my crops for pests?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikwɛɛɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli be fɛɛ be koni mana kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli?

english: If you are not vigilant, pests will quickly multiply and spread across your entire farm, eating your pods and causing massive crop loss before you even realize there is a problem.
ga: Kɛji okwɛɛɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, kooloi ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Eyeɔ o-pods lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fiteɔ dani oleɔ po akɛ naagba ko yɛ.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to keep pests from ruining my cocoa?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite mi-kokoo lɛ?

english: You should inspect your farm at least once or twice a week. Being watchful allows you to spot pest attacks early and take action before they destroy your whole yield.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Nɔ ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni oyɔseɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra. Ni ofee nɔ ko dani efite onibii fɛɛ.

english: What simple steps can I take to stop pests from climbing onto my cocoa trees?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni mafee koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akakwɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Clearing thick weeds around the trunk, pruning branches that touch surrounding bush, and removing infected pods helps block pests from easily moving onto your cocoa trees.
ga: Ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ, ni afoɔ tsei niji ni kɛ tsei bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kpeɔ lɛ. kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Enɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkabote o-cacao tsei lɛ amli mlɛo.

english: Can I fix or improve damaged cocoa pods after I have already harvested them?
ga: Ani manyɛ masaa loo masaa kookoo ŋmeii ni efite lɛ beni akpa amɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, once cocoa pods are damaged by pests or harvested poorly, you cannot change or restore their quality; the defect remains permanent throughout the entire post-harvest process.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ loo akpaaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Onyɛŋ otsake loo okɛ esubaŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Tɔmɔi lɛ hiɔ shi daa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why does the quality of bad cocoa beans stay low even after I dry them for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni ehiii lɛ ahe ehiii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ egbi be kakadaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Drying only removes moisture; it cannot repair damage caused by pests or poor harvest timing. Cocoa quality is locked in at the moment of harvest, so bad beans stay bad forever.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛ. Enyɛŋ esaa nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo ŋmaakpamɔ be ni ehiii lɛ efite lɛ. Akɛ kookoo lɛ kpakpa lɛ ŋmɛɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔfi yibii ni ehiii lɛ baakã he ahi shi akɛ nɔ ni ehiii kɛya naanɔ.

english: How does harvesting pest-damaged cocoa affect my crop for the rest of the year?
ga: Te kookoo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni eshwɛ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Harvesting damaged or diseased pods lowers the overall quality of your whole cocoa batch, resulting in permanent price deductions or rejection by buyers throughout the sales season.
ga: Pods ni efite loo hela emɔ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha o-cocoa kuu muu lɛ fɛɛ mli kpakpa lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa ajieɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ jara loo akpooɔ amɛ jara daa yɛ jarayeli be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do extension officers repeat the same farming instructions to us every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ tsuɔ kusum naa okwaayeli he nii lɛ? Kɛ wɔ daa be?

english: Good crop care requires daily discipline and consistent routines; repeating the teachings ensures farmers remember to apply basic pest management and farm checks every day.
ga: Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ daa gbi tsɔsemɔ kɛ nifeemɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Nitsɔɔmɔ ni afeɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛkaiɔ ni amɛkɛ shishijee tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ kɛ daa gbi ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ atsu nii.

english: Why is continuous learning important for me as a farmer if I already know how to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nikasemɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ he hiaa mi akɛ okwaafonyo lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mile bɔ ni aduɔ tsei momo hu?

english: Pests and field conditions change constantly, so continually learning new protection techniques helps you prevent unexpected losses and keep your crop yields high year after year.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛi heei ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa lɛ akasemɔ Hekwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ nibii ni baafite ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ anaa, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why does my crop output remain poor if I only apply farm management advice once in a while?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ he ŋaawoo tsu nii yɛ bei komɛi amli pɛ.

english: Crops require continuous protection and proper handling throughout their growth cycles; ignoring advice or slacking on farm monitoring even for a short period gives pests enough time to ruin your output.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ hebuu ni yaa nɔ kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli. Ŋaawoo ni oooku ohiɛ oshwie nɔ loo ni oooku ohiɛ oshwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ nɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli po Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ aná be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava growing next to them while young to protect their delicate leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. be mli ni eji gbekɛ lolo Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni shãa, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops hot sunlight from drying out the soil, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow. Applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season keeps the leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do weeds make my crop yield small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for nutrients hidden in the soil. Even if there is enough water, weeds steal the plant food before your main crops can consume it.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po lɛ, jwɛi hu baaju niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baanyɛ aye.

english: Does it matter which direction I slant cassava stem cuttings when inserting them into the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: Yes, the small growth buds on the stem must point upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots struggle to reach the surface, leading to weak growth or plant death.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ, Shoots lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei baanyɛ agbɔjɔ loo amɛgboi.

english: Why do extension officers advise making high soil mounds for planting yams instead of flat soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha sweet potatoes dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep soil to expand downward without hitting hard ground. Mounding also allows excess heavy rainfall to drain away so the yams do not rot in waterlogged soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. Muji ni abua naa lɛ hu haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded. Keeping soil moisture consistent prevents flowers from falling off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why should I cut away small sucker shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: When too many sucker shoots grow together, they fight for nutrients and water, resulting in small plantain bunches. Keeping only one or two suckers allows the main tree to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ fee ekome kɛdara tsɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantain tsei bibii Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ to he lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside leaf funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely fall armyworms, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves. Applying approved treatments directly into the center leaf funnel early stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baatsɔ asraafoi ŋmeii. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii Kɛ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ awo baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ haa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects sucking sap from the underside of leaves or spreading viruses. Removing affected plants early and managing sap-sucking insects helps protect the rest of the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei ni ena hela lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni abu he ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and moist air the young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa cacao tsei bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa.

english: Yellowing leaf tips on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. Adding manure or the right fertilizer will help the leaves turn dark green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland yield fewer crops every year even though I use the same seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Every crop draws food out of the ground to grow. If you plant the same crop year after year without adding organic manure or fertilizer, the soil gets tired and empty of nutrients.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ he feɔ shoo ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a tiny fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather, especially when cocoa trees are crowded and air cannot flow through. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight in and helps keep the pods dry.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛ ŋmei bibioo ko mli. No gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ cacao tsei lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit a plant virus, or by extreme heat and uneven watering. Clearing weeds around the farm helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaaa ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ mli Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Okwaafoi yeɔ ebuaa ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are packed too closely, their underground roots compete with each other for water and soil nutrients, resulting in many thin, useless tubers instead of large, heavy ones.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni he ehiaaa yɛ yitso agbo ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get too hot, face a dry spell, or receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves rather than fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji edɔ tsɔ. Ni akɛkpeɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naa loo enine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to sprout after I sowed them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds usually fail to sprout if the soil is too dry after planting, if insects or birds ate the seeds underground, or if the seed was stored in a hot, damp place before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii loo okpoi yeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi loo kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ dani adu.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up in the late afternoon or under heavy heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants fold their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water when the weather is hot, saving moisture so the plant does not dry out and die.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni tsei lɛ akagbi ni amɛkagboi.

english: How can I tell when my sweet potatoes are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Sweet potatoes are usually ready when the vines start turning yellow and drying up. You can also dig up one root and cut it; if the milky sap inside dries white without turning dark, the crop is ready to harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ kɛ́ wain tsei lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ otsa shishifã kome ni ofo mli. Kɛji mliki ni yɔɔ mli lɛ gĩ eyɛŋ ni etsɔko ediŋŋ Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa.

english: When does cocoa flowering and pollination usually begin in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana?

english: Cocoa flowering and pollination typically start around February as early weather changes trigger the tree to open flowers for the new cropping season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Coco fɔfɔi kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ February mli. Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa mra lɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛha shweremɔ be hee lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa flowers need to be pollinated before I can harvest cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli dani abaanyɛ akpa kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Pollination transfers pollen to the flower, which acts as the trigger that allows the flower to develop into a full, seed-bearing cocoa pod rather than dying off.
ga: Pollination kɛ pollen yaa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni kanyaa fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbo

english: Why do so many of my cocoa flowers drop off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when they are not successfully pollinated by tiny insects or when the tree lacks sufficient nutrients and water to support all its flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii ba amɛnɔ. Enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ loo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ aye abua lɛ.

english: Why do extension workers recommend hand-pollinating cocoa flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ kookoo fɔfɔi ni akɛ niji feɔ lɛ he ŋaa lɛ?

english: Hand pollination ensures that a higher percentage of flowers are successfully fertilized, leading to significantly higher pod yields than relying on natural insects alone.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ amli oha mlijaa ko baaye omanye yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa pod yibii babaoo baa fe adebɔɔ mli kooloi pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo kookoo tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Fertilizer is best applied right after pollination begins in the early season, giving the tree the essential nutrients needed to grow and hold onto developing pods.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni pollination je shishi yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: What does fertilizer actually do for my cocoa trees once flowering starts?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ kɛji ebɔi fɔfɔi?

english: Fertilizer feeds the tree key nutrients like potassium and phosphorus, which strengthen the branches, reduce pod loss, and help pods grow large with healthy beans.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niji lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ. Ha pod ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi Ni eyeɔ ebuaa pods lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can joining a farmer cooperative help me get fertilizer for my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi akuu ko ni mikɛ mihe baawo mli lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cooperatives organize groups of farmers to buy inputs together, making it easier and more affordable to procure genuine fertilizers distributed by agricultural programs.
ga: Kuu ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome lɛ toɔ okwaafoi akui ahe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛfee ekome kɛhe nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo ni shika hu waaa akɛ aaaná ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ ni okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoi hɔ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: How many years can a single cocoa tree continue producing pods on my farm?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cacao tso kome baanyɛ awo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A cocoa tree can remain productive for well over 14 to 30 years if it receives proper care, regular pruning, pest control, and soil nutrients throughout its life.
ga: Kookoo tsei baanyɛ awo yibii afii 14 kɛyashi 30 kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe nitsumɔ daa yɛ wala be fɛɛ mli

english: Can I grow only cocoa on the same farm plot for over ten years without destroying the soil?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu kookoo pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋma ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, cocoa can be grown continuously on the same land for decades, provided you replenish lost soil nutrients using fertilizers and maintain good farm sanitation.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu kookoo be fɛɛ be yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Ebaabi ni okɛ niyenii ni elaaje yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii kɛ ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ kpakpa nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Why does cocoa production follow specific seasonal months like February instead of fruiting heavily all year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo feemɔ nyiɛɔ be pɔtɛɛ ko sɛɛ, tamɔ February, moŋ fe ni afee lɛ babaoo yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees follow natural rainfall and temperature patterns, which naturally trigger flushing leaves and flowering in months like February to align with the main growing season.
ga: Cacao tsei nyiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ dɔlɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa baai kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nyɔji tamɔ February mli koni ekɛ be titri ni amɛdaraa lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Why shouldn't I apply all the pest medicine to my crops at once if I want to kill the insects quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ fɛɛ wooo miŋmɔshi nibii amli shikome kɛji miisumɔ ni magbe kooloi lɛ oya lɛ?

english: Applying too much crop medicine at once can scorch and destroy your leaves, just like taking too much medicine harms a human. It also wastes money and can make the pests resistant to the spray over time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso tsofa babaoo wo mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã ni efite. Taakɛ tsofa ni anuɔ fe nine lɛ ji oshara kɛha adesai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eji shika fitemɔ hu ni ebaanyɛ eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akafee nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow when the plants get sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ hela mɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling in tomato leaves are signs that the plant is under attack by small insects like whiteflies or is suffering from a virus. The plant curls its leaves to conserve water and protect itself from stress.
ga: Tomato baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies etutua tso lɛ loo hela ko emɔ lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔi ahe.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and weak without big cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii wuji beni midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the maize plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Instead of putting energy into making big cobs, they spend all their energy stretching upwards to reach the light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abele tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baatsu nii kɛfee ŋmeii wuji Moŋ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsu nii ni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baaná shishifãi ni wa.
