english: This is a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. The maize plant naturally pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves and growing cobs, causing the lower leaves to yellow first.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Excess rain fills up all the tiny air spaces in the soil, effectively drowning the cassava roots. Without oxygen, the roots cannot breathe and fungi quickly spread, causing the tubers to decay underground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Ni ŋmei lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing peppers during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the pepper plant and damages the pollen inside the flowers, preventing fruit from forming. The plant drops its useless flowers to save energy and water until temperatures drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee Tsei lɛ baashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ ashwie koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops can reach them. Feeding a farm full of weeds means the weeds get stronger while your crops starve.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ oha ŋmɔ ni jwɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ niyenii lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ jwɛi lɛ baaná hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves high into the air where they can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight gives the leaves energy to make food, which is then stored underground to grow large tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it bad to spray insect medicine on my crops during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mafɔ̃ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Spraying under strong afternoon heat causes the medicine to evaporate quickly before it can work. Additionally, water droplets on leaves can act like magnifying glasses in direct sunlight, burning holes in the foliage.
ga: Tsofa lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ la ni naa wa shishi yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsofa lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani etsuɔ ​​nii. Kɛfata he lɛ, nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa shãa bu yɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my land stop producing good food after I plant on it for a few years straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ekpa niyenii kpakpa baa lɛ? Beni mikwɛ nɔ afii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Just like a person getting tired after heavy work, land loses its strength when crops take up nutrients season after season. Resting the land, adding animal manure, or growing crops like beans helps put strength back into the soil so your farm can thrive again.
ga: Tamɔ gbɔmɛi ni nitsumɔ ni wa etɔ amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ yɛ be mli, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ, kɛ kooloi ashishifãi. Aloo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ewaje shikpɔŋ lɛ koni oŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my seeds too close together on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Giving them proper space helps each plant grow strong stems and produce bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ekwɛ̃ɔ tso lɛ shishi ni wa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some crops need to be planted in a small nursery bed first before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ tsei komɛi yɛ ŋmɔji bibii amli dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ?

english: Young seeds are delicate like newborn babies and can easily die from harsh sun, strong rain, or insects on the open field. A nursery bed protects them until they are strong enough to survive on the main farm.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ gbekɛbii ni afɔɔ amɛ ehee lɛ, ni hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baanyɛ agbo oya. Nursery saatsoi lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my young plants in the nursery are ready to be dug up and taken to the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni midumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaatsumɔ ni akɛya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Seedlings are usually ready when they have grown 3 to 4 strong leaves and their stems look firm, which typically takes a few weeks depending on the crop. Digging them up when they are too small can cause them to die from shock.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwu ko efee klalo kɛji eyɛ baai 3 kɛyashi 4 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshishifã lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ shiŋŋ. Enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ afu amɛ beni amɛdarako tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛgboi kɛjɛ shoofeemɔ mli.

english: What should I do if the roots of my plants break when I dig them up from the nursery?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fã beni mifoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: To prevent broken roots, water the nursery bed very well before digging so the soil becomes soft. If roots break, keep the plant in shade, plant it quickly in moist soil, and water it immediately so it can recover.
ga: Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akakumɔ lɛ Nu awo dumɔhe lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani otsa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ efo lɛ, ha tso lɛ ahi hulutsoo be mli. Dumɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. kɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni eha ehe ajɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when there is enough rain falling on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crops are hungry for soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the ground has too much water around the roots, making it hard for the plant to breathe and absorb food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu babaoo ni ebɔle eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Why do my plants droop in the afternoon heat even if the soil was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: When the afternoon sun is very hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. The plant droops to protect itself from losing more water, and it usually stands back up when the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Kɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, edamɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ hulu lɛ enyɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my crop is sick from a disease or if it just lacks water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo nu efo mli?

english: A thirsty plant will dry up evenly and rise again after you water it. A diseased plant will often show strange spots, dark patches, mold, or rotten spots that do not go away even when watered.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ baagbi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shi beni okɛ nu ha amɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni sɛɛ efooo kɛji awo amɛ nu po sɛɛ lɛ kpo.

english: What simple precautions can I take to stop disease from destroying my crops before I plant?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma pee blɔ nya tomi komɛ nɛ ngɛ mlɛo. Mɛni abaanyɛ afee koni helai akafite ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu?

english: You should clear out sick crop remains from the previous season, use healthy seeds from a trusted source, and wash your farm tools with soap and water so you do not carry sickness from one plant to another.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ hei ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. ni okɛ samla kɛ nu afɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe. Enɛ ji koni okɛ hela akajɛ tso kome mli kɛya ekroko nɔ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to plant different crops on the same land instead of just one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ fe ekome pɛ lɛ?

english: Planting different crops together or changing them every season confuses pests and stops diseases from building up in the soil, while also keeping the land fertile and protecting you from losing your whole harvest if one crop fails.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei srɔtoi yɛ he kome loo atsake amɛ daa be lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai afutu, ni ebaaha helai akabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii, ni ebuɔ ohe koni onibii fɛɛ akafite kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite.

english: Why does it cost me so much money to farm tomatoes in Ghana compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ shika babaoo tsuɔ tomato abɔɔ mli yɛ Ghana kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Tomatoes are delicate crops that require expensive inputs like fertilizers, pest management chemicals, and artificial irrigation during dry periods to survive and produce good yields, making their production costs high.
ga: Tomato ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni biɔ nibii ni jara wa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi. kɛ nu ni akɛ nibii fee ni akɛwoɔ nu mli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni anyɛ ahi shi ni aná yibii kpakpai. ni kɛ nibii afeemɔ he nyɔmɔwoo babaoo baa

english: Why do tomato crops perform better in dry climates like Burkina Faso than in humid parts of Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi tamɔ Burkina Faso fe hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Tomatoes prefer sunny, dry conditions with controlled watering. High humidity and heavy rain promote fungal diseases and leaf rot, which reduces yields and increases the need for costly spray treatments.
ga: Tomato sumɔɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ akudɔɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni fiteɔ baa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa atsu nii kɛshwie nɔ.

english: High daytime temperatures and excessive humidity can stress tomato plants, causing their flowers to dry up and fall off before pollination takes place.
ga: Gbi mli latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: This condition, called Blossom End Rot, happens when the plant lacks calcium or experiences inconsistent watering, preventing nutrients from reaching the bottom of the developing fruit.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Blossom End Rot lɛ baa kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my tomatoes split or crack open on the vine right before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miitswa loo amɛmiitswa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cracking occurs when tomato plants receive a sudden surge of water after a dry spell, causing the inside of the fruit to grow faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Kpojiemɔ baa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ná nu ni yaa hiɛ trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do I need to tie my tomato vines to wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi tomato wain tsei lɛ fĩɔ tsei ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking keeps leaves and fruit off the wet soil, which improves air circulation around the plant and prevents soil-borne fungi from destroying the crop.
ga: Staking baaye abua ni ebaatsi baai kɛ aduawai ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified tomato seeds instead of planting seeds saved from market tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe tomato dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni makwɛ tomato dumɔwui ni jara waaa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Market tomatoes are often hybrids, meaning seeds saved from them will result in weak, disease-prone plants with low fruit yields. Certified seeds guarantee uniform growth and disease resistance.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛfee nɔ ko. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ oya kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ aba. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli haa amɛdalɛ daa kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect my tomato plants during the growing season?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excess rain washes away soil nutrients, damages delicate flowers, and creates damp conditions that spread bacterial leaf spots and blights very quickly across your farm.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Efiteɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni gbɛɔ bacteria leaf spot kɛ blight oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I keep my tomato field moist during the dry season without spending too much money on water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-tomato ŋmɔji lɛ amli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ni mikɛ shika babaoo akafiteee yɛ nu he?

english: Covering the soil around your tomato plants with dry grass or straw (mulching) reduces water evaporation, keeps the soil cool, and cuts down the amount of irrigation needed.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi (mulching) shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle o-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and spoil quickly before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes harvested fully ripe under hot conditions continue to produce heat and moisture, which speeds up decay. Harvesting them at the 'breaker stage' (just as red color starts showing) extends their market shelf life.
ga: Tomato ni akpaa ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lolo. ni haa fitemɔ yaa oya. harvest at ‘Circuit breaker period’ (tamɔ bɔ ni su tsuru lɛ jeɔ shishi ejieɔ ehe kpo lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ) baaye abua ni eha esɛɛ atsɛ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I remove all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving larger trees or planting plantains around them creates shade that keeps the soil cool and moist, protecting the young plants until they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni ajieɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually show that the crop is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their healthy green color, so applying fertilizer or compost early helps keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra. Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni ebaawo yibii kpakpai.

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the underground tubers swell up.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei lɛ egbɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stems before forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or lack of water. Watered regularly during dry periods, the plant stays cool enough to hold onto its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ he. Nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baakã he afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why is it important for me to put wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves off the ground and spreads them out to catch sunlight. When leaves get plenty of light, they generate more food for the plant, resulting in much larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaafee niyenii babaoo aha tsei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Which young shoot should I take from my old plantain tree if I want to plant a new one?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmeii bibii esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii kɛjɛ dumɔwu momo mli kɛji miisumɔ ni madu ehee?

english: You should pick a sucker that has narrow, sword-like leaves and a strong, wide base. Avoid suckers with broad, flat leaves because they grow into weaker trees with smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ klante kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛbaatsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni aduawai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and shrinking into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on young leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage and keeps the leaves growing flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ afitemɔ naa ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater collects in the soil for days, it smothers the roots and allows rotting organisms to attack the tubers. Planting on mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Dumɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Will planting cowpeas together with my maize stop my corn from growing well?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa baadu lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, planting cowpeas alongside maize actually helps the corn. Cowpeas naturally feed nitrogen into the soil, which acts like free food for the maize while the maize stalks give cowpea vines a structure to climb.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Cowpeas kɛ nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei haa cowpea wain tsei lɛ anáa gbɛjianɔtoo ni amɛkɛkwɔɔ.

english: Why do groundnut flowers appear on top of the stems if the nuts grow underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔi jeɔ kpo yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛji ŋmei lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers bloom above ground, they drop special shoots called pegs that grow downwards into the dirt. Once those pegs push into loose soil, they swell up to form the groundnut pods underground.
ga: Beni ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Eshiɔ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ tsi amɛhe kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni etse lɛ mli lɛ Amɛfuɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why is it bad to plant my maize seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the stalks to grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in smaller cobs and lower harvest yield.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why should I plant cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of straight down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a 45-degree angle encourages roots to branch out closer to the fertile topsoil, which leads to larger tuber development and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji 45-degree lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji baa, ni ehaa ŋmeii akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell. If seeds sprout during this dry period, the young roots will dry out in the hot soil and die before the major rainy season actually begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nɛkɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle extreme heat. They require shade crops, such as plantains, to shield them from burning sun while their root systems mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he beni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or waterlogging around the roots. Nitrogen is essential for crops to produce green leaves and energy for growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni ehiɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Nitrogen he hia koni tsei afee baai eŋɔli ni amɛha hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why does my soil produce less yield when I plant maize on the same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding and eating deep inside the funnel of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender center leaves of corn plants. If ignored, they destroy the plant's growing point before it can produce cobs, so early treatment is needed.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ, amɛbaafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ dani ebaanyɛ ewo ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni atsa lɛ mra.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow poorly even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that suck up water and fertilizer faster than your crops can. Clearing weeds ensures your crops actually receive the food you give them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni okɛhaa amɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms dropping off the plant instead of forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, water supply is irregular, or the soil lacks nutrients like calcium. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant hold its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. Aloo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I place solid fertilizer right against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is concentrated and acts like salt; touching the plant stem directly can burn the outer tissue and destroy roots. Placing it a few inches away allows fine side roots to take up nutrients safely.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ ŋoo. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã fãji ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil and turn soft so quickly before I can transport them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya dani akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes naturally continue to breathe and release water vapor after being picked. If they are harvested when fully ripe, packed tightly in deep crates, or left in hot sunlight, they produce ethylene gas which speeds up decay and causes them to rot rapidly.
ga: Tomato baaya nɔ emu ni ejie nu mli lasu kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ akpa beni ekwɛ̃ kwraa Akɛwo adeka ni mli kwɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. loo shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli Ejieɔ ethylene gas, ni haa fitemɔ yaa oya ni ehaa fitemɔ baa oya.

english: Why do all my tomato plants produce their fruit at the exact same time instead of giving me a steady supply to sell over several weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ fɛɛ woɔ yibii yɛ be kome mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha mi nibii ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ daa otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Certain crop varieties are naturally programmed to grow to a fixed size, flower, and ripen all their fruit at once. To spread out your harvest and avoid market gluts, you can plant varieties that fruit continuously or plant your seeds in batches a few weeks apart.
ga: Ato ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi komɛi ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛdara kɛyashɛ he ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ, amɛwo fɔfɔi, ni amɛwo amɛyibii lɛ fɛɛ shikome. koni akɛkpamɔ nii lɛ afee srɔtoi ni akafee nɔ ni fa fe nine. Obaanyɛ odu henɔi ni woɔ yibii be fɛɛ be loo odu dumɔwui yɛ kui amli ni otsii fioo komɛi kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee.

english: Why do some of my harvested tomatoes get squashed and damaged at the bottom of my carrying crates?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ ekomɛi efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efite yɛ mi-shipping crates lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have soft skin that cannot support heavy weight. Stacking too many layers of fruit in deep containers puts pressure on the bottom layers, cracking the skin and allowing rot-causing bacteria to enter.
ga: Tomato yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ nibii ni tsii nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ aduawai babaoo to tsɛnsii ni mli kwɔ amli lɛ, ehaa shishigbɛ fãi lɛ feɔ nɔnyɛɛ, ni ehaa hewolo lɛ mli gbalaa ni ehaa helai ni haa mɔ fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ mli.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my growing tomatoes turning black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni midu lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani amɛshwereɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It occurs when the crop cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by uneven watering or dry spells while the fruit is growing rapidly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa loo be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open on the vine right when they are almost ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ trukaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ beni kpamɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: Fruit cracking happens when a heavy rain or heavy watering follows a long dry period. The inside of the tomato absorbs water quickly and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Yibii amli fãmɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu babaoo nyiɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why are my ripening tomatoes developing white or pale patches on the side facing the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ fã ni kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is sunscald, which is similar to sunburn on human skin. It happens when hot, direct sunlight hits exposed fruits after the plant loses its leafy shade due to disease, heavy pruning, or dry weather.
ga: Enɛ ji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa. Enɛ tamɔ hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ gbɔmɔ hewolo nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ebaa kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tswa aduawai lɛ beni tso lɛ ehiɛ edɔ yɛ ebaai lɛ ahe yɛ hela hewɔ lɛ sɛɛ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi

english: If I apply extra chemical fertilizer to my crop, will it make the fruits bigger or can it cause harm?
ga: Ani tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaha amɛfee wuji loo amɛbaaye amɛ awui?

english: Applying too much fertilizer, especially nitrogen, burns the plant's roots and causes leaves to turn yellow or brown. It also forces the crop to spend energy growing big leaves instead of developing healthy fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine titri lɛ nitrogen Ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Enyɛɔ tsei anɔ hu koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛɔ baai wuji lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do small green tomatoes fall off my plants before they have a chance to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young fruits drop off when the plant experiences sudden stress, such as intense heat during flowering, a lack of soil nutrients, or severe pest damage, causing the crop to shed fruits it cannot support.
ga: Yibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ trukaa, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ beaŋ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii waa Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye abua nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wilt during the afternoon even when there is moisture in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect the plant from drying out, and usually recover in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my crop turn yellow and drop off after a week of heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa otsi kome sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain leaves the soil completely soaked, water fills all the air spaces around the roots. Without air, the roots cannot breathe or absorb food, causing the lower leaves to starve, turn yellow, and drop.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, sũ lɛ mli fɔ̃ɔ. Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ amli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii. ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ aye hɔmɔ Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi

english: Why do my crops turn pale green and grow slowly on land where topsoil was dug away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsa nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Topsoil contains most of the natural food and organic matter that crops need. When topsoil is removed during digging, crops are left in nutrient-poor subsoil and starve unless enriched soil or fertilizer is added back.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he hiaa tsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Beni ajieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ashiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni niyenii he hewalɛ kɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ mli. Ja akɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my seeds struggle to grow after heavy digging machinery compacts my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛtaoɔ shika tsuru lɛ efo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy equipment squeezes air out of the soil and packs it tight. Hard, compacted soil makes it very difficult for tiny roots to push through and search for nutrients and water.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii miimiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni amɛhaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shishifãi bibii kwɛ̃ɔ. Ewa akɛ ooobote mli ni ona niyenii kɛ nu

english: Why do my yam tubers grow better on raised soil mounds rather than flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ fe nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds provide loose, deep soil that gives yam tubers room to expand freely without pushing against hard ground, while also preventing excess water from collecting around the roots.
ga: Gɔji haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛtsiii shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off when rainwater collects on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: When water sits on the field for too long, it cuts off air from the soil and drowns the roots, causing root rot so the plant can no longer feed its leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii kɛtsɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: How do I test if my farm's soil can hold enough water for crops during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Squeeze a handful of moist soil into a ball in your hand; if it holds its shape without crumbling immediately or leaking water, it has a good balance for holding moisture for crop roots.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ko nɔ ofee bɔɔlu yɛ onine mli. Kɛji akɛ tsɔne ni akɛtoɔ shi lɛ gbeeee shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo nu lɛ hoɔ lɛ, ebaaná tsɔne ni akɛtoɔ shi lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiɛ mli kɛha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli.

english: Will digging shallow drainage channels around my plot help save my crops during heavy rains?
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ mli ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ mli ni akuɔ Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, shallow channels guide excess surface water away from crop roots, preventing soil from becoming waterlogged and keeping roots healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛjegbɛi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli. Etsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Is it better to apply water to my vegetable crops early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows roots to absorb moisture before the afternoon sun causes the water to evaporate from the warm soil.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ shwane lɛ haa ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during high winds when planted in deeply dug soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akumɔ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots spread wide near the surface rather than growing deep down. If the surrounding soil is freshly dug and too loose without firming, the roots cannot anchor the heavy tree against strong wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo yɛ nu lɛ hiɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaya shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ atsa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni akɛtswaaa shi shiŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛfi tso ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the middle of the day even when the soil feels damp underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ amɛshishi moŋ lɛ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water faster through the hot air than the roots can pull up from the ground, causing temporary wilting to protect the plant from losing more moisture.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha tso lɛ agbi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo akafite lɛ.

english: How deep should I dig when transplanting young tomato seedlings into my field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo mli kɛya shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tomato dumɔwui bibii miiwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Dig deep enough to bury the seedling stem up to its lower leaves, because tomato stems grow extra roots under the soil, making the plant stronger and better able to drink water.
ga: Tsɔmɔmɔ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni okɛfu dumɔwu lɛ shishigbɛ kɛyashi baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi krokomɛi ni fata he yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛnuɔ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need for green leaf growth. Adding NPK fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nitrogen they need to turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adara. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná nitrogen ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize grow much better when I plant groundnuts on the land first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ wo shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the groundnut harvest is done, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil, serving as free natural food for the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ agbe ŋmeikpamɔ lɛ naa lɛ, Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant plantains on the same field with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, shielding the cocoa from harsh sun and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can capture direct sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food through photosynthesis, which then travels down to build large, heavy yam tubers in the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la haa baai feɔ niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii agboi ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become woody and hard to boil when I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tso ni ewaa akɛ aaaho kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store food in the form of starch, but once the plant reaches full maturity, it starts consuming that starch and converting it into tough woody fiber. Harvesting at the right age keeps the tubers soft and starchy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ niyenii toɔ yɛ ŋmei gbɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ dara kwraa lɛ Ebaabɔi ŋmei lɛ yeli ni etsɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ yɛ afii ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tamɔ ashikishaŋ aba.

english: Why do my sweet potato plants produce mostly thick leaves and thin roots when I apply too much manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ baai ni mli tse kɛ shishifãi ni mli tse babaoo kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo fata he lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen from excessive manure tricks the plant into spending all its energy growing leafy vines above the ground, leaving very little energy to swell the roots into big potatoes.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni jɛɔ ŋmeii babaoo mli lɛ lakaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ wain tsei ni baai yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ ni eshwɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ shishifãi lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and humid conditions. High rain and heavy shade trap moisture on the pods, allowing fungal spores to splash around and destroy the cocoa crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa. Trap moisture yɛ pods lɛ anɔ Enɛ haa fungal spores lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛbɔleɔ he. ni efite kookoo tsei lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small tightly packed cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by microscopic insects like mites or thrips sucking the sap from the underside of fresh leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extremely hot temperatures make tomato pollen dry and sticky, preventing flowers from being fertilized. When a flower is not fertilized, the plant drops it to save water and energy.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tomato pollen lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpɛtɛɔ he. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo fɔ Kɛji fɔfɔi ko wooo fɔ Tsei baashwie shi koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in flooded land while maize rots and dies in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu afua yɔɔ lɛ? Beni ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems that carry oxygen down to their roots underwater, whereas maize roots lack these air tubes and suffocate when flooded.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tsui krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei nɛɛ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛji nu shwie amɛmli.

english: Why is it important for me to weigh my harvested crops instead of just counting the bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu mikpamɔ lɛ he moŋ fe ni makane kotokui lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Weighing your crops gives you an accurate measure of your actual yield because bag sizes can vary and moisture content changes weight. Knowing the exact weight helps you negotiate fair market prices, track soil performance year to year, and know if your hard work is paying off.
ga: Kɛ́ osusu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ehaa osusuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaawo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baagi lɛ dalɛi baanyɛ afee srɔtoi. ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ falɛ baatsake shwiili lɛ shwiili lɛ shwiili lɛ shwiili lɛ ni ole lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ jara ni sa baasusu he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nitsumɔ nɔ afi kɛ afi Ni ole kɛji onitsumɔ ni wa lɛ miiwo yibii.

english: How can I safely try out a new farming method on my farm without risking my whole harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka okwaayeli gbɛ hee ko makwɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wooo oshara mli?

english: You can set up a small trial plot on a tiny corner of your land to test new practices, such as a new fertilizer or planting space. Comparing that small section to the rest of your field allows you to see if the new method works well in your soil before applying it to your entire farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ oto kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fã bibioo ko nɔ koni oka nifeemɔi heei, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo hei heei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ okwɛ. Fãi bibii kɛ hei krokomɛi ni akɛtoɔ he Ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kɛji gbɛ hee lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ. dani okɛtsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of green leaves but very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi tomato fioo pɛ?

english: This usually happens when plants get too much nitrogen, often from over-using certain fertilizers or fresh manure. High nitrogen makes the plant focus all its energy on leaf growth instead of developing flowers and fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turn black and soft while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni miida lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo be mli ni eyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is a condition called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering. Keeping your soil moisture steady with regular watering and mulching helps the plant absorb calcium continuously.
ga: Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛhe calcium.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to reduce water loss when moisture leaves their leaves faster than roots can draw it up. Watering early in the morning allows plants to build up water reserves to withstand the midday sun.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ shi kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ shi baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni efeɔ nu jɛɛhe ko ni baanyɛ adamɔ hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ naa.

english: Can I feed leftover tomato plants and crop residues to my sheep after harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha mitooi lɛ tomato tsei ni eshwɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: While some crop residues like maize stalks or legume vines are great fodder, leaves and stems from tomato plants can actually be toxic to sheep. It is better to turn tomato waste into compost rather than feeding it directly to your animals.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi ni etse amɛhe, tamɔ ŋmãa tsei loo ŋmãa tsei ji niyenii kpakpa lɛ, baai kɛ tsei ni jɛɔ tomato tsei amli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni gbeɔ tooi diɛŋtsɛ. Ehi akɛ oootsɔ tomato ni etse lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ mli moŋ fe ni oookɛha okooloi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is manure from my sheep safe to put directly around my growing crops?
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ mitooi lɛ amli lɛ awo he fɛɛ he. Ani manyɛ maná miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh sheep manure is too high in ammonia and heat, which can burn plant roots and damage young crops. You should let sheep manure rot and break down in a heap for a few weeks to turn it into safe compost before adding it to your soil.
ga: Too ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli ammonia yɛ mli, ni edɔ tsɔ. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii bibii Esa akɛ oha too ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbo ni efolɔ otsii fioo komɛi koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe dani okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How does keeping farm animals near my vegetable fields help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni mikɛ amɛ toɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Livestock produce manure that enriches the soil with organic matter, which helps the ground hold water and feed the plants. In return, safe crop byproducts can feed the animals, creating a cycle where your crops and animals support each other.
ga: Koolooi feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa tsei niyenii. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ enɛ lɛ, abaanyɛ aha kooloi niyenii ni jɛ tsei amli ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Feemɔ sɛɛkuu ko ni oŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kooloi lɛ yeɔ amɛbuaa amɛhe.

english: Does the side of the field where I plant my light-sensitive vegetables like tomatoes really matter?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni miduɔ aduawai ni haa la kpɛɔ tamɔ tomato lɛ he hia?

english: Yes, crops need full sunlight to make food and grow fruit, but extreme afternoon heat can scorch young plants. Planting them where they receive adequate morning sunlight while being sheltered from strong afternoon heat keeps them healthy and productive.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛwo yibii. Shi latsaa ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ odu otso lɛ yɛ he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ leebi lɛ, yɛ be mli ni shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ hu kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why should I plant my crops in neat rows instead of scattering seeds across the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ

english: Planting in rows ensures every crop gets equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without overcrowded competition. Row planting also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ni akaŋshii lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ tsɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ hu haa jwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why should I remove and destroy a single diseased plant instead of leaving it in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tso kome ni hela emɔ lɛ ni makpãtã hiɛ moŋ fe ni mashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Removing a single sick plant immediately stops the disease from spreading to surrounding crops, effectively eliminating the source of infection before it destroys your entire farm.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni ebaajie he ni hela lɛ jɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani ekpata oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why is it recommended to mix crop medicine into the irrigation water for all my plants at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu nu ni akɛshwieɔ mitsei lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ mli shikome lɛ?

english: Mixing liquid treatment or fertilizer directly into irrigation water ensures that every plant receives equal protection and nutrients through its roots simultaneously, resulting in uniform farm health.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ futu nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hebuu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ be kome mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my neighboring farmers and I need to control pests on our farms at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi kɛ okwaafonyo ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ wɔŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Pests move freely between fields, so if only one farmer treats their farm, the pests will simply migrate to neighboring crops and return later. Combining efforts destroys the pest population completely.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyiɛɔ ŋmɔji ateŋ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji okwaafonyo kome pɛ ji mɔ ni kwɛɔ eŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Pests hu baafã kɛya side effects tsei amli ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba sɛɛ mli. Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ baafite kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ kwraa.

english: Should I apply disease treatment to crops that do not look sick yet?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa atsu nii yɛ tsei ni hela emɔko amɛ lolo lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, applying preventive treatments to all crops protects healthy plants before symptoms appear, ensuring the disease cannot establish itself in your field.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe dani hela lɛ he okadii lɛ aba. Enɛ haa hela nɛɛ baaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How does applying liquid fertilizer through water help my crops grow better than dry fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi?

english: Liquid fertilizer dissolved in water is immediately accessible to the roots, allowing plants to absorb nutrients faster and more evenly across the entire field.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya ni amɛfeɔ ekome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my crop treatment was successful and my field is in good health?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsu nii lɛ ye omanye, ni miŋmɔji lɛ hu yɛ hewalɛ?

english: Overall crop wellness is visible when all plants show uniform growth, vibrant leaf color, strong stem development, and an absence of pest damage across the entire plot.
ga: Abaanyɛ ana tsei lɛ ahewalɛ fɛɛ kɛji tsei lɛ fɛɛ dara yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ, amɛbaa lɛ su mli tse, amɛshishifãi lɛ wa, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why do young crops struggle to grow when planted too close to older, established crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei ni edara ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Older crops have larger root systems and taller leaves that take away sunlight, water, and nutrients from younger plants, effectively smothering their growth.
ga: Tsei ni edara yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai kakadaji ni gbalaa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. ni ehaa dalɛ baa shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why must I dig out the deep roots of stubborn weeds instead of just cutting the tops off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni mafolɔ amɛyitsei lɛ?

english: Cutting only the top of a weed leaves the underground root intact, allowing the weed to quickly grow back and continue stealing food and water from your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo jwɛi lɛ yiteŋ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahi shi. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni eyaa nɔ ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Is it better to treat only the sick plants on my farm or treat the whole field together?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ matsa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ loo matsa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ ekome?

english: If an outbreak is isolated to one spot, targeting only that area saves money, but if the threat is widespread, treating the entire field ensures total protection for all plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hela lɛ je shishi kɛyashɛ he kome lɛ, hei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔɔ nɔ lɛ baaha okɛ shika akafite. Shi kɛji akɛ gbeyeishemɔ lɛ gbɛ eshwa lɛ, jɛmɛ fɛɛ ni abaatsa lɛ baaha abu tsei fɛɛ ahe kwraa.

english: How does working together with other farmers to clear land help prevent crop damage?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi ni akɛ amɛ baatsu nii kɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Clearing large areas of land quickly as a team removes wild pest habitats all at once, giving your newly planted crops a clean, safe environment to establish strong growth.
ga: Kuu lɛ jie he ko ni da waa oya, ni ejie koo mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛhei fɛɛ shikome. Ha onibii ni odu ehee lɛ shihilɛ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe koni amɛkwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why do my crops produce much less harvest when the weather is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaaa nii babaoo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive heat stresses plants and prevents flowers from developing into full fruits, which can drop your harvest weight down to as little as 1.5 kilos per plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ kwraa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai. Enɛ baaha okpamɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ aba shi kɛyashɛ kilogram 1.5 pɛ yɛ tso kome mli.

english: Does cooler weather help my crops give a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Yes, when heat subsides, plants retain more of their flowers and convert them into heavy fruit, allowing you to harvest up to 5 or 6 kilos per plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ latsaa lɛ ba shi lɛ Tso lɛ hiɛɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni etsɔɔ aduawai ni tsii. Ehaa okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shɛɔ 5 loo 6 kg tsuɔ nii yɛ tso kome mli.

english: Why are the fruits from my hot-season farming much lighter than those grown in cooler months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yibii ni jɛɔ mi hulutsoo be mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli waaa fe yibii ni jɛɔ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High temperatures during the growth cycle drain the plant's energy, resulting in lighter produce compared to cooler periods where conditions are ideal for maximum crop weight.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ beaŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ waaa kɛ akɛto nyɔji ni mli ejɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛɛmɛi ji shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii fe fɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to make sure my crops have enough water when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa beni amɛjeɔ fɔmɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Water during the flowering stage helps the plant cool down and gives it the nutrients needed to transform flowers into heavy, healthy produce.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: At what stage in my crop's growth will a lack of water damage my final yield the most?
ga: Nu ni bɛ lɛ yeɔ minaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui fe fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ be mli?

english: The flowering stage is critical; if plants lack water when flowers appear, many flowers will fall off, leading to a much smaller harvest.
ga: Fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ he hiaa waa. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu beni fɔfɔii jeɔ kpo lɛ Fɔfɔi babaoo baagbee shi. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: What key things should I check in my farm when my crops start flowering?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa esa akɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ?

english: When flowering starts, make sure there is sufficient moisture in the soil and check that extreme heat has passed so the flowers can turn into full fruits.
ga: Be ni esa akɛ oje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ni kwɛmɔ akɛ la ni naa wa lɛ eho bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai ni eyi obɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How much harvest weight can I reasonably expect from a single crop plant?
ga: Nikpamɔ mli tsiimɔ enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ kɛjɛ tso kome mli?

english: Depending on weather and water availability, a single plant can yield as low as 1.5 kilos under hot, dry conditions, or up to 5 to 6 kilos under cool, well-watered conditions.
ga: Edamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Tso kome baanyɛ awo yibii ni baa shi tamɔ kilogram 1.5 yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli loo kilogram 5 kɛyashi 6 yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ mli.

english: How can I increase the total weight of crops I harvest from each plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ tso fɛɛ tso mli lɛ fɛɛ mli tsiimɔ aya hiɛ?

english: Providing adequate water and timing your planting so flowering happens during cooler periods will help each plant reach a yield of 5 to 6 kilos.
ga: Nu ni fa kɛ be ni akɛbaadu nii lɛ ni akɛaaha Bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii aba yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso woɔ yibii ni tsiimɔ ji kilogram 5 kɛyashi 6.

english: Why did I get very low output per plant even though my crops produced flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii ni baa shi kwraa yɛ tso kome nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi moŋ lɛ?

english: If flowers face extreme heat or lack of water after emerging, they fail to develop properly, leaving you with small yields like 1.5 kilos per plant.
ga: Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ afɔmɔ sɛɛ lɛ Dalɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, onine shɛɔ yibii fioo ko nɔ, tamɔ kilogram 1.5 yɛ tso kome nɔ.

english: Will watering my crops regularly during hot weather bring my yield back to normal levels?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: Sufficient water helps reduce heat stress during flowering, which protects the flowers and helps restore your harvest weight closer to its full potential.
ga: Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa baaye abua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Enɛ buɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni okɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa he ni eshɛɔ he ni eshɛɔ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, protecting them from heat and helping the soil retain moisture during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak stalks that yield tiny or empty corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes inside the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a major pest affecting maize in Ghana. They hide in the growing point (the central leaf whorl) to feed on young leaves, and they require early treatment with approved insecticides or bio-controls to protect your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii wulu ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa nɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ (baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta) koni amɛye baa bibii. Ni ehe miihia ni atsa amɛ mra. kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ koni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food. Guiding the leafy vines up tall wooden stakes lifts them off the ground, maximizing sunlight exposure and resulting in significantly larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ wein tso ni yɔɔ baai lɛ wo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ayi fa babaoo

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and prevent themselves from drying out. As long as the stems remain green and alive, new leaves will sprout as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi enaa koni ekagbi. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baafee eŋɔli ni ehiɛ kã lɛ, baa heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil every year and causes crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: How do weeds actually reduce my harvest if they are just growing in the soil next to my crops?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Weeds act like competitor plants that steal food, water, and sunlight directly away from your crops. If weeds are left unchecked, your crops will stay stunted because they are not getting enough nutrients to grow properly.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ jwɛi lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã he ahi shi ejaakɛ amɛnáaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the very first rain of the season is enough for me to start sowing seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: The first rain often only wets the surface layer while the soil underneath remains dry. Sowing immediately is risky because a dry gap after one rain can kill sprouting seeds; it is safer to wait until the soil is moist at least hand-deep and rains become regular.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ pɛ. be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo lɛ Dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara. Ejaakɛ hei ni egbi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ shikome sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agboi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baawo mli bɔ ni abaanyɛ, ni nugbɔ eba be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers drop off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi efoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting mainly due to stress caused by intense heat, uneven watering, or a lack of insect pollinators like bees during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii lɛ jɛɔ haomɔ ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛbaa lɛ mli titri. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo pollinators tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Can I put solid fertilizer directly into the hole with my seeds when planting?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa afata dumɔwu lɛ bu lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ midu?

english: No, placing fertilizer directly against seeds can chemical-burn the delicate seeds and prevent them from germinating. Fertilizer should always be applied a small distance away from the seeds or around the base of living plants.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa ashã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha amɛkakwɛ̃. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo loo yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he.

english: Why are my garden egg leaves turning yellow and dropping off before fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your garden egg plants lack nitrogen in the soil, or they are getting too much water around the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or compost gives them the nutrients they need to stay green and produce healthy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ eggplant ni yɔɔ obɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu babaoo ebɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Garden egg flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Regular watering and applying good compost keep the plant healthy enough to hold flowers until they form fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ hao tso lɛ. Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaawo yibii.

english: What causes small holes in my garden egg fruits and makes them rot on the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ baa ni ehaa amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes are usually caused by fruit borer insects that lay eggs on flowers or young fruits. Clearing away infested fruits quickly and rotating your crops each season helps stop these pests from multiplying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni yeɔ aduawai ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ fɔfɔi loo aduawai bibii anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa. Yibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafa babaoo.

english: Why do my young corn leaves roll up tightly during the sunny mid-day hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves curl up in intense sunlight to protect themselves and conserve water. As long as the leaves unfold again during the cooler evening hours, the plant is simply managing heat stress naturally.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baaje kpo ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baanyɛ atsu dɔlɛ he haomɔ he nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know the right distance to space my corn seeds when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Spacing corn about 25 to 30 centimeters apart along rows gives each plant enough soil nutrients, sunlight, and root space to grow strong stalks and produce full ears.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, hulu la kɛ shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa ni wa ni ekɛ toi ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why are some of my corn cobs only half-filled with grains at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ fã pɛ eyi kɛ ŋmãa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Empty spots on corn cobs usually happen when hot, dry weather prevents proper pollination while the silks are emerging. Planting corn in square blocks rather than long single rows helps wind spread pollen evenly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, he ko ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu egbi lɛ tsiɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii ni sa lɛ anaa yɛ be mli ni siliki lɛ miije kpo lɛ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ sqɛɛ blɔki mli moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kakadaŋŋ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aja pollen lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing that forms a V-shape starting from the tip of lower leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding composted poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore leaf color and support cob development.
ga: Yellowing ni feɔ V su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi a-compost loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua cob lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Why do my carrots grow with split roots or strange twisted shapes instead of growing straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi karɔt lɛ miida kɛ shishifãi ni ekumɔ loo amɛhe mfoniri ni etsake yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooda yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ?

english: Carrots split or twist when the soil is hard, stony, or heavily fertilized with unrotted fresh manure. Loose, deeply tilled sandy soil allows carrot roots to push straight down easily.
ga: Karɔt baagbala loo ebaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ tɛi, loo akɛ ŋmeii heei ni egbooo ewo mli babaoo. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ woɔ karɔt shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shi tɛ̃ɛ. mlɛo

english: Why do my carrot seeds take so long to sprout compared to my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi karɔt dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ akɛto mi tsei krokomɛi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Carrot seeds are small and need steady moisture near the surface of the soil to break open. Covering the seedbed lightly with clean grass straw helps retain ground moisture until green shoots appear.
ga: Karɔt dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛtswa. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi jwɛi ni he tse ha dumɔwui lɛ asa lɛ nɔ fioo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or straw, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ

english: How do my cocoa flowers actually turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ bafeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects, mainly midges (tiny flies), to carry pollen from one flower to another. Without these tiny insects visiting the flowers to pollinate them, the blossoms will simply dry up and drop off without forming any pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Nɔ ni amɛteŋ babaoo ji ŋmeii. (fɛ̃i bibii) ni amɛkɛ pollen baajɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli Kɛji kooloi bibii bɛ Enɛɛmɛi baa koni amɛbasara fɔfɔi koni amɛbawo pollen. Kɛkɛ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when there aren't enough insect pollinators around to fertilize them, or when the tree is stressed by hot sun and lack of water. Creating a shaded, moist environment on your farm keeps these tiny insects alive so more flowers turn into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ pollinators ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. Aloo be mli ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ofee shihilɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi bibii ni amɛhiɔ shi. Mɛnɛɛmɛi yɛ wala mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ bafeɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: What is hand pollination, and can it help increase the harvest on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni ani ebaaye ebua ni nibii ni afeɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Hand pollination is when you manually transfer pollen from one flower to another using a small brush or tool. It guarantees fertilization and can significantly increase your yield, especially if natural pollinating insects are low in your area.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ ji be mli ni okɛ onine shwieɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ brɔsh loo dɛŋdade bibioo ko nɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli ni ebaanyɛ eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ waa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ faaa yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Will spraying heavy chemical pesticides on my cocoa farm reduce my crop yields?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni tsii ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, if used incorrectly. Heavy chemical sprays kill harmful pests, but they also kill the friendly midges and tiny insects that pollinate your cocoa flowers. Without those pollinators, your trees will produce far fewer pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ. shi egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo kɛ kooloi bibii ni haa o-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hu Kɛji kooloi ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ Otso lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ fioo kwraa.

english: How does nearby illegal mining (galamsey) affect the growth of my cocoa trees?
ga: Te shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ (Galamsey) ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ saa mi kokoo tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Galamsey pollutes nearby water sources with mud and dangerous chemicals, strips away healthy topsoil, and destroys the natural habitat of pollinating insects. This makes it hard for your cocoa roots to drink clean water and leads to poor pod formation.
