ga: Galamsey kɛ muji kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara fiteɔ nu gbɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhei ni kooloi ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa kookoo shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaanu nu ni mli tse, ni ehaaaa ŋmeii lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: What can I plant around my farm boundaries to protect my cocoa trees from external pollution and dust?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ makwɛ yɛ ehe? Okwaafoi husui baanyɛ abu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ mujiwoo kɛ sũ ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ he.

english: Planting a boundary line of fast-growing shade trees or tall food crops creates a green buffer zone. This barrier traps dust, blocks harsh chemical drift from nearby land, and provides a safe refuge for crop-friendly insects.
ga: Shade tsei ni daa oya loo niyenii tsei kakadaji ni aduɔ yɛ husu ko mli lɛ feɔ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɛkɛ gbɛtsii nii nɛɛ mɔ̃ɔ sũ. Etsiɔ tsofai ni mli wa ni jɛɔ shikpɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ anaa. ni eha kooloi bibii ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do extension officers recommend keeping shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni sɛɛkwɛlɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect delicate cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight, keep the soil moist during dry spells, and create a cool shelter where beneficial pollinating insects can live and multiply.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni amɛfee shĩai ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛfɔ bii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and wilting in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight without enough soil moisture. They need temporary shade cover and steady water to build strong roots before they can handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛ nu daa koni amɛto shishifãi ni mli wa amɛma shi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I clear away all the dead leaf litter off the ground under my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijieɔ baai ni egboi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Leaving a layer of dead leaves on the soil creates a natural carpet that retains soil moisture, breaks down into rich compost nutrients, and provides the dark, damp breeding ground that cocoa-pollinating midges need to survive.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egboi lɛ eko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli kapɛti ni yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ baa. Efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔ mli niyenii ni fa babaoo. Ni ehaa ŋmeii ni woɔ kookoo mli ŋmeii lɛ fɔmɔ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni mli edɔ ni ehe hiaa koni amɛhi shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do farmers plant plantain trees alongside new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa seedlings the shade they desperately need during their first few years while also providing food and extra income.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii kɛ shika kroko ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my maize as soon as the very first rain falls in the year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli pɛ?

english: No, the first rain is often a temporary shower. It is better to wait until two or three steady rains have soaked the soil so your seeds do not dry out and die after germinating.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kukuoo ko. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baatsi odumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm gets enough rain during the year to grow good corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa yɛ afi lɛ mli koni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kpakpa?

english: Corn needs continuous rainfall over about three to four months. You can ask local extension officers about your district's average rainfall, as corn requires reliable rain throughout its growing stage to fill the ears.
ga: Abɛi he miihia nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ. Obaanyɛ obi okpokpaa lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ mlijaa mlijaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ he miihia ŋmãa yɛ edalɛ be fɛɛ mli koni ekɛwo etoi amli.

english: Why does corn grow much better in some regions of Ghana than in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kpokpai komɛi anɔ fe he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Different regions get different amounts of rainfall and have varied rainy season lengths. Areas with longer rainy seasons give corn the steady water it needs, while drier regions may cause the plants to stunt.
ga: Kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ falɛ srɔtoi kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei srɔtoi. Hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aná nu ni he hiaa lɛ daa. yɛ be mli ni hei ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How can I choose the best crop to plant based on the rainfall in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: You match the crop's water needs to your local weather pattern. Heavy rain regions are great for crops like cocoa and maize, while drier areas with short rains are better suited for crops like millet or sorghum.
ga: Okɛ nu ni he hiaa onibii lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kpãa gbee. Hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo kɛ ŋmãa. yɛ be mli ni hei ni egbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Are there special corn seeds I can buy if the rains in my district do not last long?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ ni manyɛ mahe kɛji nugbɔ enɛko yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ?

english: Yes, there are early-maturing and drought-tolerant seed varieties bred specifically for regions with shorter rainy seasons, allowing you to harvest before the dry period begins.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni shwereɔ mra, ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ yɛ ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ aha kpokpai ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa yɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up and turn yellow during a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku mli lɛ?

english: Corn plants curl their leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation when soil moisture drops. It is the plant's natural way of protecting itself until the next rainfall.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he kɛyashiɔ nugbɔshiimɔ gbi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I keep rainwater in my soil longer so my crops don't dry out quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha nugbɔ nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akagbi oya?

english: Adding compost or leaves as mulch on top of the soil helps block the sun, preventing rainwater from evaporating quickly and keeping the plant roots moist between rains.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai fata he akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu he kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Etsiɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya. ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my crops look weak even though a heavy rain fell on my farm last week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli otsi ni eho lɛ?

english: One heavy downpour can run off the surface without soaking deep into the ground. Crops need consistent, light to moderate rainfall over time rather than a single sudden flood.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ efo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, fioo kɛyashiɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli. Yɛ nu afua kome pɛ ni baaba lɛ najiaŋ

english: How do modern farming methods help farmers get higher crop yields than traditional methods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe blema gbɛi lɛ?

english: Modern methods use precise planting measurements, improved seeds, and rainfall tracking to ensure crops make full use of the water and nutrients available in your specific region.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi kɛ dumɔ susumɔi pɔtɛɛ tsuɔ nii. Dumɔwui ni atsake kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ koni ana akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miitsu nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I do to protect my corn crop if the rain stops completely earlier than normal?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni sa?

english: If rains end early, practice water conservation techniques like mulching, clear weeds that steal soil water, and consider using small-scale irrigation or planting short-duration crop varieties next season.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba naagbee mra lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ gbɛi ni akɛbuɔ nu he tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ jwɛi ni juɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ajiemɔ. ni osusu nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi bibioo loo be kukuoo mli dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Should I pick the biggest maize seeds from my current harvest to plant for the next season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahala ŋmãa ni da fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli koni madu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Selecting just the largest seeds from a harvest does not guarantee a good crop. A seed might be big simply because it got extra water or space, not because it has strong genetics. Buying certified seeds ensures you get high yields and protection against common plant diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui wuji ni ahalaa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ haaa aná nɔmimaa akɛ abaawo yibii kpakpai. Dumɔwui baanyɛ afee wuji yɛ nu babaoo loo he ko ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hewɔ kɛkɛ. Jeee yɛ fɔmɔ su ni mli wa hewɔ Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ baaye abua bo ni oná yibii babaoo ni obu ohe kɛjɛ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are some of my cassava roots growing very big while others on the same farm stay small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miida waa nɛkɛ lɛ? be mli ni shishifãi krokomɛi Yɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, ebatsɔ bibioo ni efite?

english: Cassava roots grow unevenly when the soil in some parts of the farm is too hard or compacted for the roots to expand. Uneven watering or early pest damage on certain plants can also cause abnormal root growth.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei komɛi amli be fɛɛ be loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ amɛ mra lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛshishifãi lɛ ada yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Why do my yams start sprouting and rotting shortly after I store them at home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ bɔi shweremɔ kɛ fitemɔ beni akɛto shia be kukuoo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when they are kept in warm, humid places because the warmth signals to the tuber that it is time to grow again. Rotting happens if the yams were bruised during harvest; keeping them in a cool, dark, and well-ventilated barn prevents early sprouting and decay.
ga: Atomo baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa tsɔne lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ eda ekoŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ sweet potatoes lɛ fite yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ, fitemɔ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite oya.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my crops closer together so more can fit on my farm?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting crops too close together actually reduces your total yield. When plants are crowded, they fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with small fruits instead of fewer, healthy, high-yielding crops.
ga: Kɛ́ odu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛwuɔ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa. Yɛ tsei ni faaa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. The plant steals nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season keeps the entire plant green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ afee eŋɔli ni ewo yibii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. When stressed by heat or drought, the plant drops its blossoms to save its own strength instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ latsaa loo hɔmɔ hao amɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei lɛ baawo yibii lɛ, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, overly shaded, and wet conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches lets sunlight in and lowers moisture, which helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ Shade babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kpãa kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni eha fɛ̃i aba shi. Enɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it recommended that I cut off extra stems and branches from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɔ akɛ mafolɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifã lɛ kɛ tsei niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ?

english: Removing non-essential side branches helps the plant direct all its food and water toward growing larger, healthier peppers instead of wasting energy on growing extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ eniyenii kɛ enu lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni okɛbaakwɛ baai krokomɛi

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have naturally adapted to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing the food your crops need to survive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔi ni baaha amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why do my garden eggs become smaller and bitter when I grow them in the exact same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same spot every year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating your crop with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and improves harvest quality.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai akaboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ebaanyɛ ebua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Leaving some large trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that keep the seedlings cool and moist until they are strong enough.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei komɛi ni eda ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ hu baanyɛ aha hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni haa dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruits compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need proper selection and care. If you do not cut off extra suckers growing around the main plant, they fight for nutrients and water, which delays fruit production. Removing extra suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to grow faster and fruit earlier.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ahala plantain tsei lɛ ahe ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji ofolɔɔɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛbaatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ baaha aduawai ni anáa lɛ asɛɛ afo. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo koni eda oya ni ewo yibii oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before they produce any corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛwo abele lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for green leafy growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure early in the season will restore the green color and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ ahe afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is tired and needs a rest from planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ etɔ ni ehe miihia ni majɔɔ mihe kɛjɛ dumɔ mli?

english: Tired soil shows signs like stunted crop growth, pale leaves, and low harvest yields even when rain is good. Planting nitrogen-fixing crops like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore essential nutrients naturally without leaving the land completely empty.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ okadii tamɔ tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ, baai ni tsuɔ, kɛ ŋmaa ni baa shi lɛ kpo kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ jogbaŋŋ po. Nitrogen-fixing nibii tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts ni aduɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaaa he lɛ afee efolo tsɔ.

english: Curled, yellowing leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny whiteflies. The best solution is to plant improved, disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers rather than taking cuttings from infected fields.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nibii yaa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Tsabaa ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ adu ŋmei henɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaafolɔ tsei niji kɛjɛ shikpɔji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: What causes the bottoms of my tomatoes to turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo dani ekwɛ̃?

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps prevent this condition.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ shihilɛ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why is it risky to cut cassava stems for my new farm from a field that had sick plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mafolɔ ŋmei tsei kɛha miŋmɔ hee lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava diseases stay inside the stem cuttings even if the stem looks dry or tough. Planting stems from a diseased field spreads the sickness into your new soil and reduces your total yield at harvest time.
ga: Cassava hela lɛ yɛ lolo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi loo ewa po. Tsei ni ooodu kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ni hela lɛ emɔ mli lɛ baaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oshikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ onibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ aba shi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds as soon as the very first rain falls in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat spell or dry period before the main rainy season starts. Planting too early means seeds will germinate, but the young roots will dry up and die in the hot soil before the steady rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ be ni mli edɔ waa loo nugbɔshiimɔ be mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or sudden changes in soil moisture. Providing shade during hot spells and watering the soil evenly near the base stops the flowers from falling off.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakemɔi trukaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa, ni afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Yam tubers rot when rain accumulates in the soil without draining away, or when tiny pests in the soil wound the tuber skin. Planting yams on high mounds or ridges ensures excess water drains away from the roots, protecting the tubers from rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ mli. aloo beni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tswa bulb lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Tsi yitso lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot hours to reduce their surface area, which prevents the plant from losing too much water through evaporation. It is an early warning sign that your crops are experiencing heat stress and need soil moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Eji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi mra akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miina dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia amɛ.

english: Spreading dry grass, or mulching, acts as a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool under direct sunlight and stops water from evaporating quickly, protecting delicate roots from heat damage.
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya. Ebuɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cowpea plants drop their flowers without producing any pods during hot dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop flowers as a survival response so it can conserve water and energy rather than spending it on developing seeds.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi akɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ hetoo. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ ato nu kɛ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ moŋ fe ni akɛbaatsu dumɔwui ahe nii.

english: Is it safe to sow my vegetable seeds when the ground is extremely hot from days of bright sun?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu aduawai dumɔwui beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hewɔ?

english: Sowing seeds in extremely hot soil can scorch the tender seeds before they sprout or burn the fresh young roots as soon as they emerge, leading to poor germination.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ loo eshã shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ ehee lɛ kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even though I irrigate them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Overwatering fills all the small air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots so they cannot absorb water or food, and creates ideal conditions for soil-borne diseases that kill the plant quickly.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛŋɔ nu loo niyenii mli nibii. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa kɛha helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni baanyɛ agbe tsei oya lɛ.

english: Why do crop leaves turn yellow and stems turn soft when rainwater stands on my farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Standing water deprives the roots of oxygen, causing them to rot. When roots decay, they can no longer take up nutrients, which turns the leaves yellow and weakens the whole plant.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ji oxygen lɛ aná shishifãi lɛ, ni no haa amɛgboiɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ miifite lɛ nyɛŋ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ dɔŋŋ Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: What are the pros and cons of planting my crops under large shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi kɛ naagbai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Shade trees protect young crops from harsh sun and keep the soil moist longer, but too much shade prevents crops from getting the sunlight they need to grow strong and make fruit.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Shi hulutsoo be babaoo haaa tsei lɛ aná hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What does it mean when the lower leaves of my cassava plants start turning yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mi shishigbɛ cassava baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya. Mɛni enɛ ɔ tsɔɔ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually an early sign that the crop is suffering from a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that it is reacting to early drought stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji mra be mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miina shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ eetsu mra be mli hɔmɔ he haomɔ he nii.

english: Why do my crop plants get tall and thin with very few leaves when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni miduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When planted too closely, crops compete aggressively for sunlight, causing them to stretch upward quickly while remaining weak, slender, and less productive.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya yɛ be mli ni amɛshwɛɔ ni amɛhe waaa, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra branches growing at the bottom of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Removing bottom branches improves air circulation around the base to prevent fungal diseases and directs the plant's energy away from useless leaves and into producing larger fruits.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ aya hiɛ. cones koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ekɛ tso hewalɛ lɛ aya he ko kɛjɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe ni ekɛ aduawai wuji aba.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early gives the plants the strength to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa lɛ bɛ o-abele tso lɛ mli. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra. Ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any fruit appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get steady water. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing balanced nutrients helps flowers stay on the plant to turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant sap. Spraying neem water or appropriate insecticides early protects the foliage from damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do I need to use tall sticks to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei kakadaji duɔ sweet potato wain tsei moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight for growth while keeping them away from damp ground where rot and leaf diseases spread, leading to much larger tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni amɛdara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ekɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ akabɔ he. Ekɛ yitso ni da kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ baa

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms that target young maize leaves. Checking the central shoots early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract into the plant funnels stops them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ. Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ awo tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ kpaa shi dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Groundnuts and beans capture nitrogen gas directly from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When the plants finish producing, that natural fertilizer stays in the ground to nourish the next crop you plant.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ gbe nitsumɔ naa lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I select sword suckers with narrow leaves instead of broad-leaf suckers when planting plantain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala klante tsei ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ fe tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ beni miduɔ plantains lɛ?

english: Sword suckers have strong root bases and food reserves, allowing them to grow faster and produce larger bunches of plantains compared to broad-leaf suckers, which are weaker and produce small yields.
ga: Klante ŋmeii yɛ shishitoo ni wa kɛ niyenii ni ato. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ plantains babaoo kɛ akɛto broadleaf shoots ni bɛ hewalɛ ni wooo yibii babaoo lɛ ahe.

english: Why does letting weeds grow in my field during the first month reduce my harvest so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔji amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi waa lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and must compete with aggressive weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crop gets all the nutrients it needs to build a strong stem and deep roots.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Is it better for me to start farming on a small plot of land before expanding to a large farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mabɔi okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ dani mikɛ mihe awo ŋmɔ wulu ko mli?

english: Starting small allows you to learn proper crop care, manage costs, and handle pests without risking big losses. Once you master a small plot and make a profit, you can use that experience and money to expand safely.
ga: shishijee bibioo Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okaseɔ bɔ ni esa akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ, bɔ ni okwɛɔ shika nɔ, ni otsuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nii ni okɛ ohe wooo osharai wuji amli. Kɛji ole shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni oná sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ nakai niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ shika lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe ni okɛgbala onitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds very close to each other to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin plants and a smaller harvest overall compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Yes, maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly underground. Once you harvest the maize, the cassava takes over the extra space without losing yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ fiofio yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, kɛ́ okpa ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmãa baahe he kroko ni ŋmãa baafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient out of the soil away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛjie shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, the roots suffocate and rot from excess moisture.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper and tomato plants falling off without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or a lack of water. It can also happen if you give the plant too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing it to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha otsei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How do weeds in my farm actually slow down the growth of my main crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haaa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your crops need. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What are these small caterpillars eating the leaves inside my maize funnel, and how do they damage the crop?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-corn cones lɛ amli nɛɛ? Ni te amɛfeɔ tɛŋŋ amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the central leaves of young maize and eat the growing point, which prevents the plant from forming healthy stalks and ears of corn.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworms ji enɛɛmɛi. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afee ŋmãa ŋmeii kɛ toi ni mli wa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry period. If your seeds germinate after that single rain and find no soil moisture in the following weeks, the young seedlings will dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ ni anaaa ŋmɔtɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ otsii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why do my crops give a very good harvest on new land at first, but produce much less food after farming the same spot for three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpa nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ he hee lɛ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi niyenii ni anáa lɛ faaa kwraa beni atsu okwaayeli yɛ he kome afii etɛ sɛɛ.

english: Crops feed on natural nutrients in the dirt to grow. When you plant on the same land repeatedly without giving the soil a break or adding organic manure, the plants eat up all the food in the dirt, leaving the soil tired and poor.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji odu yɛ he kome shii abɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieee shi loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ Tsei lɛ baaye niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ.

english: Why does planting beans or cowpeas on my land make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have special microscopic partners in their roots that pull food (nitrogen) directly from the air and store it in the soil. When the beans are harvested, that leftover food remains in the dirt to feed hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ srɔto, ni anaaa kɛjɛɔ hiŋmɛi nɔ. Enɛ gbalaa niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nakai niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and survive tough weather better than the actual food crops I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa mli jogbaŋŋ fe niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have adapted over centuries to survive with very little water and poor soil. Domesticated food crops are weaker because they put all their energy into making large fruits and seeds, making them rely more on human care.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii mli. Shia niyenii tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ejaakɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ aduawai kɛ dumɔwui wuji. Enɛ haa amɛhiɛ kã adesai akwɛmɔ nɔ babaoo.

english: When the sun gets too strong, crops lose water through their leaves just like humans sweat. Maize rolls its leaves tightly to hide the flat surface from the hot sun, stopping water from evaporating so the plant does not dry out and die.
ga: Kɛ hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tamɔ gbɔmɔ latsaa. Abɛi shwieɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛtee ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsi nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa koni tso lɛ akagbi ni egbo.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean the tubers are dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egboi?

english: Cassava plants deliberately drop their leaves in dry weather to save moisture inside their stems and roots. The plant is not dead; it goes to sleep temporarily to protect the tubers growing underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebaawɔ be kukuoo ko koni ebu bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming any tomatoes during very hot months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: High temperatures make the pollen inside tomato flowers dry and sticky, preventing them from reproducing properly. When a flower cannot form a seed due to extreme heat stress, the plant drops the flower to save its energy.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashi amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground when there is heavy rainfall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When heavy rains flood the farm and water stays on top of the soil, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing the yam tubers to drown, suffocate, and rot in the waterlogged soil.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ ni nu shwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛmuɔ, ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain suckers planted right beside them on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide leafy shade umbrellas that shield the cocoa trees from excessive heat while keeping the soil moist during their tender early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. ni bɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, air, soil water, and nutrients. They stretch upward as tall as possible to catch light, wasting all their strength on tall stems instead of building big, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, kɔɔyɔɔ, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛmɔ kane lɛ. Kɛtsɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ yiblii nguahi nɛ a he wa.

english: Why do my orange and mango trees produce very few fruits when big wild trees shade them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange kɛ mango tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ tsei wuji ewo amɛhe shade lɛ?

english: Fruit trees use sunlight as fuel to manufacture the energy needed for blooming and fruiting. If larger trees block the sun, the fruit tree cannot make enough food energy, causing it to produce mostly leafy branches instead of sweet fruit.
ga: Yibii tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii akɛ tsofa koni amɛkɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo. Kɛji tso agbo ko tsi hulu la lɛ naa Yibii tsei hu nyɛŋ aha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, niji lɛ ateŋ babaoo ji baai yɛ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ najiaŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to plant my maize so that the early rains do not spoil the seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ akafite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plant your maize right after the first two major continuous rains of the season when the soil is properly moist. Planting in dry soil before steady rains start can cause seeds to rot or get eaten by birds before they sprout.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo okpoi aye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, helping the young cocoa survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry periods to save water and protect themselves. As long as the stem remains green inside, the plant will produce fresh leaves as soon as rain returns.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baahi shi akɛ eŋɔli lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Yam plants make their food through leaves exposed to sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground to capture more sun, prevents leaf diseases, and encourages the roots to form larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei hoɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni emɔ hulu la babaoo. Tsi baa helai anaa ni okanya shishifãi lɛ koni amɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their blossoms before any small peppers grow out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ dani pepper bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they suffer from stress, such as very hot days, irregular watering, or a lack of key soil nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛmiihao, tamɔ yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs.

english: Why do small ragged holes suddenly appear in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ miije kpo trukaa yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding and feeding inside the central leaf funnels. Inspecting plants early allows you to treat them before the growing point is destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ji fall armyworm lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tsu lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa amɛ dani he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the green pods on my cocoa tree turning completely black and rotting on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛmiifite yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in damp, heavily shaded conditions. Pruning excess farm branches lets in sunlight and airflow, which stops the moisture that the fungus needs to grow.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ waa lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ adara lɛ akpa.

english: What causes my tomato leaves to curl tightly upward and stop the whole plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni ehaaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ada?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by extreme heat stress. Keeping insects away and watering regularly keeps the plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ mli Kooloi akwɛmɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the topsoil. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ pɛ mli. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if a plantain sucker is healthy enough to dig up and plant in a new garden?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sucker dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa ni adu yɛ abɔɔ hee mli?

english: Select suckers that have narrow, sword-like leaves, strong undamaged bases, and clean white insides without dark spots or insect tunnels when cut.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ klante. Shishitoo lɛ mli wa ni efiteee. Ni emli he tse ni eyɛ futafuta ni nɔ ko bɛ he ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo kooloi bibii agbɛjianɔtoo kɛji afo.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect their tender leaves from harsh sunlight and severe heat stress. Keeping large shade trees or interplanting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a cooler environment and retains soil moisture so cocoa seedlings can survive.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be fioo ko koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he haomɔ he. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground, exposing them to light while preventing soil-borne fungal diseases from destroying the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha baai lɛ aná la ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for keeping leaves green and healthy, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure restores plant greenness and boosts growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia koni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does adding decomposed leaves or poultry manure to my field improve crop yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egboi loo kooloi afɔfɔi ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Decomposed organic matter feeds the soil with essential nutrients, improves the soil's ability to hold onto water during dry stretches, and helps plant roots spread and absorb food easily over a longer period.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo ni amɛŋɔɔ niyenii yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli

english: Why should I weed my farm thoroughly before applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will absorb most of the applied fertilizer if left in the field. Clearing weeds first ensures that your crops get direct access to all the nutrients in the fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ babaoo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes in the funnels of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ a-kone lɛ mli

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on tender growing leaves. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract inside the plant funnel prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ yitsei lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft, watery, and rotten inside during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, nu ni fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stagnates around them in flat or poorly drained soils, encouraging fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe kɛbɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afite. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant them close together instead of leaving space between them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe moŋ fe ni mashi gbɛ yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow strong and produce larger yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my seeds right after the very first short rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ kuku lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat spell before the main rainy season fully sets in. Seeds planted after the first rain may sprout, but the young seedlings will dry up and die if follow-up rain does not fall soon enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Shi dumɔwui lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ enɛɛɛ oya bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their yellow flowers without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme heat or dry soil, which prevents pollination. Keeping soil consistently moist through regular watering and mulching helps lower ground temperature and keeps flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. ni tsiɔ pollination naa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa aba shi ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct heat and strong sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa from sun damage, keeps the soil cool, and helps the plants survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient it needs to grow. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant turn dark green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them for too long because the soil does not drain well. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to run off, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when they do not get water consistently. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting at the right time helps the flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo amɛnáaa nu daa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni aduɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani mana yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients from the soil. Giving each plant proper space lets it grow larger and produce a bigger overall harvest.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eda ni ekɛ ŋmaa babaoo aba yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the underside of the leaves. Clearing nearby weeds and applying recommended insect treatments stops these pests from damaging your peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite o-peppers lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and preventing diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Okɛwo la mli ni otsi helai anaa.

english: How do weeds growing around my maize reduce the size of my cob harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tɛŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ dalɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil that your maize needs to grow. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the nourishment required to form full, heavy ears of maize.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ sũ ni he hiaa bo koni o-abele lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmãa ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do certified seeds from the store give better yields than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akpɛlɛ nɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to resist local diseases, endure weather changes, and grow uniformly. Saved seeds gradually lose these strong traits over time, resulting in smaller crops and lower yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpeɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ daa Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafee fiofio Efiteɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ kɛ be hoɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my main crop make the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the ground, helping nearby crops grow healthier without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ kwraa.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are getting too old to produce good yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Cocoa trees usually produce their highest yield between 10 and 20 years of age. After 20 years, the tree's internal transport system slows down, leading to fewer pods and smaller harvests even if you care for them well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ he beni amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 20 lɛ. Yɛ afii 20 sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ mli gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi, kɛji okwɛ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Why are my 20-year-old cocoa trees producing fewer pods than they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso ni eye afii 20 lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 years, their root systems grow weaker and become less efficient at pulling nutrients and water from the soil, which reduces their energy to make new pods.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei ye fe afii 20 lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee pods heei lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is a 10-year-old cocoa farm usually more productive than a much older farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni eye afii 10 lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmɔji ni etsɛ lɛ?

english: At around 10 years old, a cocoa tree is in its prime stage of life with strong roots and active branches, allowing it to use nutrients efficiently and bear maximum fruit.
ga: Beni cacao tsei lɛ eye aaafee afii 10 lɛ, amɛyɛ amɛshihilɛ mli be ni fe fɛɛ. Eyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ niji ni tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ atsuɔ niyenii mli nibii ahe nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: How many years after planting should I expect my young cocoa trees to start bearing fruits?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni midu lɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: With modern hybrid cocoa varieties, trees usually start flowering and bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take up to 5 years.
ga: kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa henɔi Bei pii lɛ Tsei jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema cocoa henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 5.

english: Why do some new cocoa varieties start fruiting after just two years while traditional ones take longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo henɔi heei komɛi jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ be babaoo lɛ?

english: Improved hybrid seeds are bred specifically to grow faster roots and stems, allowing the plant to reach mature flowering stage in about two years instead of waiting many years.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ oya. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shɛɔ fɔfɔi babaoo he yɛ aaafee afii enyɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehe baahia ni amɛmɛ afii babaoo lɛ

english: What signs should I look for to know it is time to cut down old trees and replant my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ matao koni male akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ mafo tsei momoi ni madu miŋmɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: You should consider replanting if your harvest drops permanently for several seasons, if branches die back continuously, or if trees reach over 25 years old and no longer respond to fertilizer.
ga: Esa akɛ osusu dumɔwui ekoŋŋ he kɛji akɛ okpamɔ lɛ eba shi daa yɛ bei babaoo mli. Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ tee nɔ amɛgboi loo kɛji tso lɛ eye fe afii 25 ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii dɔŋŋ.

english: Will heavily pruning my very old cocoa trees make them produce like young trees again?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei ni egbɔ waa lɛ ni mafolɔ waa lɛ baaha amɛwo yibii tamɔ tsei bibii ekoŋŋ?

english: Pruning removes dead wood and gives old trees a temporary boost, but it cannot fix aged roots; full replanting is still necessary once trees pass their peak lifespan.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni egboi lɛ, ni ehaa tso momo lɛ náa hewalɛ be kukuoo ko. Shi enyɛŋ esaa shishifãi momoi. Ehe miihia ni adu tso lɛ ekoŋŋ kwraa hu beni tso lɛ eshɛ ewala be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the trunk without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree lacks sufficient moisture, nutrients, or shade, or if small beneficial insects like midges are not present to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa, niyenii mli hewalɛ loo shade. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ bɛ.

english: Can keeping very old cocoa trees on my farm harm the young trees I plant near them?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni egbɔ waa ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye tsei bibii ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awui?

english: Yes, old trees often harbor hidden pests and diseases like swollen shoot virus or black pod, which can easily spread to young, sensitive plants nearby.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ni egbɔ lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni efuu loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni etsɔ ediŋŋ. ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya

english: Why does my soil seem to stop supporting my cocoa trees after they have been producing for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ ekpaa mi cacao tsei lɛ ayelikɛbuamɔ beni amɛwo yibii afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Every pod harvested takes nutrients out of the earth; over 15 to 20 years, the soil becomes depleted of essential minerals unless organic matter and fertilizers are put back.
ga: Pod fɛɛ pod ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ afii 15 kɛyashi 20 sɛɛ lɛ, sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ laajeɔ. ja akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I grow my seeds in a nursery first instead of planting them directly on my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings are very delicate when they first sprout. A nursery lets you protect them from harsh heat, heavy rain, and pests until they grow strong roots and are ready to survive on the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ waaa kwraa kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ. He ni akwɛɔ tsei yɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaahi shi yɛ oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young seedlings look weak and wilted right after I dig them up and move them to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo amɛ ni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When you dig up seedlings, their tiny root hairs get damaged and cannot soak up water easily for a few days. Giving them shade and extra water helps them recover from this transplant shock.
ga: Kɛ́ otsa dumɔwu ko lɛ, eshishifãi bibii lɛ efite ni enyɛŋ eŋɔ nu mlɛo gbii fioo komɛi. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu kroko ha amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛjɛ nɛkɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he gbeyeishemɔ nɛɛ mli.

english: How do crop diseases get into my field soil in the first place?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai boteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli yɛ shishijee mli?

english: Diseases can travel into your farm soil through dirty cutlasses and tools, infected seedlings bought from elsewhere, flowing rainwater from neighboring farms, or by planting the exact same crop in the same spot year after year.
ga: Helai baanyɛ abote shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmeii kɛ nitsumɔ dadei ni mli ewo muji nɔ. Dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ ni ahe yɛ hei krokomɛi Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli loo kɛtsɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Crowding also blocks air movement, creating a damp environment where plant diseases spread rapidly.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to remove old crop roots and dead plants before setting up a new farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei shishifãi momoi kɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ dani mafee ŋmɔ hee ko?

english: Old crop remains can carry hidden pests and fungal spores from the previous harvest. Clearing them away prevents those hidden diseases from attacking your fresh seedlings.
ga: Nibii ni etsɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaatsi helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua odumɔwui heei lɛ.

english: Why do my crops get rotten roots when water stays trapped on my land for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shishifãi fiteɔ beni nu hiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like people do. When water stays on the land without draining away, it drowns the roots and creates the perfect environment for root-rot fungus to destroy the plant.
ga: Taakɛ gbɔmɛi ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejeee kpo Nu lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ aha shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ni baafite tso lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees grow better when I plant plantain stems around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have big leaves that act as living umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moisture in the soil while the young trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall with lots of green leaves but no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miida ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo aduawai bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or insufficient sunlight, they put all their energy into growing tall leaves instead of flowering and bearing fruit.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ náa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ. Amɛbaatsu amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he nii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai kakadaji lɛ akwɛmɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Why do my crops suffer more from pest attacks when I plant late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Insect populations build up as the rainy season progresses. If you plant late, your tender young crops face a massive population of hungry bugs that have already grown and multiplied on early-planted farms.
ga: Kplukai ayibɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Kɛji odu sɛɛ Otsei bibii lɛ baaná kooloi babaoo ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni miida momo ni amɛmiifɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a seedling is healthy enough to be dug up and planted in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: A healthy seedling has dark green leaves, a thick firm stem, and bright white roots without any dark spots, yellowing, or signs of insect damage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii ni tsuɔ, tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ futafuta ni nɔ ko bɛ he ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi efite.

english: Why do my crops stop growing or taking in food when the weather turns cold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ loo amɛyeɔ nii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ?

english: When temperatures drop, a plant's metabolism naturally slows down to conserve energy. During these cold periods, crops temporarily stop feeding and growing until warm sunlight returns, which is a normal protective behavior.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ, tso lɛ mli nibii ni tsakeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he. yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakpa niyenii yeli kɛ amɛdalɛ be kukuoo ko kɛyashi hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba. Enɛ ji hebuu subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ.

english: Should I stop working on my farm and applying inputs when heavy rain starts falling?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makpa nitsumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Yes, you should pause field activities. Heavy rain washes away applied fertilizers and chemical sprays before plants can absorb them, wasting your money and compacting wet soil around the roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ okpa oshiɛmɔ nitsumɔi lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ dani tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ amɛ. Eji shika fitemɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do insects stay on my crops during cold weather even when they are not actively eating the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyeee baai lɛ moŋ?

english: Cold weather lowers the body temperature of pests, making them sluggish. They seek shelter on your crops to protect themselves from harsh conditions and remain resting there until warm weather restores their energy.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ agbɔmɔtso mli dɔlɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ mɛi ni bɛ jwɛŋmɔ. Amɛnaa he ko ni amɛhiɔ yɛ onibii amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai ahe ni amɛhiɔ jɛmɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa amɛhewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it normal for my plants to look droopy and inactive after several days of continuous rain?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mitsei lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi ni amɛfeee nɔ ko yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbii babaoo sɛɛ?

english: Yes. Continuous rain saturates the soil, reducing oxygen around the root zone. Without oxygen, roots temporarily stop absorbing nutrients, causing the plant to rest and look inactive until the soil drains.
ga: Hɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baakpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ŋmɔmɔ be kukuoo ko. Ha tso lɛ hejɔɔmɔ ni okwɛ akɛ etsuuu nii kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu baaho.

english: Is it bad if I apply extra fertilizer to force my slow-growing crops to grow faster?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he koni mikɛnyɛ mitsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara oya?

english: Forcing plants with extra fertilizer when they are not ready to feed can burn their roots and scorch leaves. Crops take up nutrients at their own pace based on natural sunlight, temperature, and moisture levels.
ga: Kɛ́ anyɛ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he beni amɛfeee klalo akɛ amɛbaaye niyenii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ashã. Tsei nine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ oyaiyeli mli ni damɔ hulu la, latsaa kɛ adebɔɔ mli latsaa nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I fertilize my crops during cold or heavily overcast weather?
