ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ fɛ̃i loo atatu be mli?

english: Crops need warmth and sunlight to process plant food. If you feed them during cold or dark periods, the plants cannot absorb the nutrients, leaving high chemical concentrations in the soil that can damage root tips.
ga: Tsei hia dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la koni amɛtsu tsei niyenii ahe nii. Kɛji oye niyenii gbɛkɛ loo duŋ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsofai ni baanyɛ afite shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I keep adding chemical inputs to a crop that is stressed by bad weather?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai fata ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa waa lɛ egba amɛnaa lɛ ahe?

english: Applying strong chemicals to an already weather-stressed plant causes severe chemical shock. Instead of helping, it overpowers the plant's weakened defenses and can kill the foliage or stunt future growth.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛwoɔ tso ko ni ehao momo lɛ mli lɛ kɛ tsofafeemɔ he gbeyeishemɔ ni naa wa baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua lɛ, eyeɔ tso lɛ hebuu nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ kunim, ni ebaanyɛ efite tsei lɛ ahe tsei loo eha ekwɛɛɛ wɔsɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are actively feeding or just sitting dormant in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiye nii loo eta shi kɛkɛ ni ehiɛ edɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Active plants display firm, upright new growth and bright leaves during warm, sunny periods. If leaves look static, dark, or closed during cold or overly wet spells, the crop is resting and not actively taking up food.
ga: Tsei ni tsuɔ nii baatsɔɔ dalɛ hee ni mli wa kɛ baai ni kpɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni baai lɛ efee dioo, amɛyɛ ediŋ, loo amɛmli gbɛkɛ loo amɛmli edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ewɔ ni eyeee nii.

english: What should I do when my crops pause their growth after a sudden weather change?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpa shweremɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ba trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Give the crops time to adjust on their own. Avoid adding extra fertilizers or chemicals during this adjustment period, as natural rest helps the plant recover without causing unnecessary root burn.
ga: Ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai krokomɛi ni okɛbaafata he yɛ nɛkɛ tsakemɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi ni he ehiaaa lɛ shãaa.

english: Why does forcing my plants with extra water during cold weather cause root damage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ minyɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ nu kroko afata he yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, efiteɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ?

english: Plants drink very little water when it is cold. Adding extra water during cool periods leaves roots sitting in stagnant moisture, which suffocates them and encourages harmful root diseases to develop.
ga: Tsei nuɔ nu fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu kroko fata he gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa amɛmuɔ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ shishifãi helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize make the maize grow greener and stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa ehe waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer for the neighboring maize, helping it grow thicker stalks and greener leaves without needing extra chemicals.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsofai krokomɛi he ehiaaa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my pineapple plants turning pale yellow and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pineapple tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on pineapples usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen or potassium in the soil, or that tiny root pests like mealybugs are damaging the roots and preventing the plant from drinking water and taking in nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo potassium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi bibii tamɔ mealybugs miifite shishifãi lɛ. ni etsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkanu nu ni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Cassava plants fold and droop their leaves during peak heat to protect themselves. By reducing the leaf area exposed to the sun, the plant slows down water loss and protects its moisture until the evening cool arrives.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. Kɛtsɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die after heavy rains flood the farm for two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbo trukaa ni egbo beni nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu eyi gbii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need oxygen from the soil to survive. When water covers the farm floor for too long, the roots drown and suffocate, making it easy for soil fungi to attack and rot the base of the plant.
ga: Pepper shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu ha ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua tsei ashishi ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stem before any fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from high afternoon temperatures or irregular watering. The plant sheds its blossoms to save its own energy when the weather becomes too harsh.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi bafee nɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees give very small bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around the mother stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ panicles bibii waa kɛ́ mishɛrɛ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ ashwie lɛ? Tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ shishifã lɛ?

english: All the extra shoots, or suckers, fight with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning away the weaker suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the mother tree to put all her energy into growing a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii krokomɛi fɛɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ amli lɛ, tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ, ni enɛ haa tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tso kuu agbo ko.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees yield fewer pods when they are heavily shaded by big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ewo ehe ŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ?

english: While young cocoa plants need shade to survive the hot sun, fully grown cocoa trees need controlled sunlight to make food and produce flowers. Too much shade starves the mature trees of energy, leading to low pod production.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hɔnɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni akudɔ amɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛwo fɔfɔi. Shade babaoo baaha tsei ni eda lɛ aná hewalɛ ni hɔmɔ aye amɛ. Enɛ haa pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my pineapple plants growing very long leaves but refusing to produce fruit after over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-anana tso lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi ewooo yibii yɛ afi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages the pineapple plant to keep growing tall leaves instead of forming fruit. The plant needs a balance of potassium and specific maturity signals to shift its energy into flowering.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhiɛ baai kakadaji amli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii. Tsei hia potassium ni sa kɛ dalɛ he okadi pɔtɛɛ ko koni amɛtsake hewalɛ kɛya fɔfɔii anɔ.

english: Why do fall armyworms always attack the tender leaves inside the central heart of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ tutuaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The central funnel of young maize plants holds tender, moisture-rich leaves that are easy for caterpillars to eat. The deep funnel shape also shelters the armyworms from hot sunlight, heavy rain, and natural predators.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ tsu lɛ hiɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmeii yeɔ amɛ oya. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hu buɔ asraafoi akuu lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting green shoots in the barn even without soil or water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu bɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living stems with an internal biological clock. After a few months of dry storage, the tuber's natural dormancy ends, prompting it to use its stored food and moisture to shoot out new buds in search of light.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ amɛmli. Beni akɛto he ko ni egbi nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe lɛ baa naagbee. Wo lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni ato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ tsei heei ni ekɛtao la.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains nearby protects young cocoa trees from harsh sun while their root systems develop.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my cocoa seedlings too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close together, their roots compete heavily for water and soil nutrients, and their tops block sunlight from each other. Proper spacing gives every tree room to spread its leaves and produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli. ni kookoo tsei lɛ ayitsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni egbɛɔ ebaai lɛ eshwaa ni ekɛ yibii kpakpai baa.

english: Why do tiny bugs attack my cocoa branches and cause the tops of the trees to dry up and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua mi-kookoo niji lɛ ni amɛmiiha tsei lɛ ayiteŋ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: These insects, commonly known as Akate or capsids, bite young green stems and suck out plant juices, injecting toxic saliva that kills the branches. Using an approved chemical sprayer during their peak season protects the tree canopy from dying off.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ, ni afɔɔ amɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ Akate loo capsids lɛ, ŋmɔɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ shwieɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ shishi kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: What causes the small black spots that spread quickly and ruin my cocoa pods after rain?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ baa? ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni efiteɔ kookoo ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, wet conditions. Weeding regularly and pruning dense branches lets air flow through the farm, drying out dampness and reducing the spread of the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe daa kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli ni oha ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aba shi

english: Why shouldn't I spray insect chemicals on my crops in the middle of a hot sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ?

english: Spraying in intense heat causes the chemical liquid to evaporate too quickly into the air before it can work on pests. High heat can also cause liquid chemicals to scorch and damage the plant leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shwie nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsofai amli nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashã tsofai ni ji nu lɛ ni efite tsei lɛ ahe baai.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the small pods even start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ? Ani ebaaje shishi eda?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they are under stress from poor soil nutrients, water shortages, or pest attacks. Feeding the soil with fertilizer and controlling pests helps the tree retain its flowers long enough to form healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyɛ haomɔ mli kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli. nu ni faaa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni efee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my crop leaves look yellow and weak even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the soil is low in nitrogen and other essential plant foods, or that the root zone is waterlogged and unable to breathe. Adding nutrients or improving field drainage helps leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen kɛ tsei ahe nibii krokomɛi ni he hiaa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛfataa he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua baai lɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing good pods when their upper branches get too thick and overcrowded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii kpakpai feemɔ beni eniji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Overcrowded upper branches block sunlight from reaching the lower trunk where cocoa pods grow, and they waste the tree's energy. Pruning extra branches directs the plant's strength into growing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ, he ni kookoo tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Ni amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ atsake tso lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do weeds growing around the base of my crops reduce my final yield?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te baafee tɛŋŋ ni mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ aha mi naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds act like hidden thieves by rapidly sucking up soil water, fertilizer, and sunlight intended for your main crop. Keeping the ground around your crops clean allows them to absorb all available nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛtsɔ sũ mli nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha otsei titrii lɛ ni amɛmuɔ oya lɛ nɔ. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe tsemɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ.

english: How does the dry Harmattan wind affect the way my cocoa trees behave?
ga: Te Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ saa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ajeŋba he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind pulls moisture out of plant leaves and soil rapidly, forcing cocoa trees to shed their leaves to conserve water. Covering the soil around the tree base with dry leaves helps hold moisture in the ground during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ oya. Esa akɛ cacao tsei lɛ ajie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which acts as primary food for the plant. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the plant stay green and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei aniyenii titri Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of the same specific nutrients every season and allows pests and diseases that target that specific crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa nakai tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I let fresh cow or chicken manure dry out before putting it on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã tsina loo tsina ŋmei hee lɛ agbi dani madu lɛ?

english: Fresh manure releases strong gases and heat as it breaks down, which can burn plant roots. Composting or drying it first makes the nutrients safe and easy for plants to absorb.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ kɛji efite. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Kɛ́ afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo agbi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ.

english: Wait until the soil receives two or three steady, deep rains rather than planting after the very first light shower, ensuring the soil holds enough deep moisture to keep germinating seeds alive.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii aya nɔ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose water faster than roots can suck it up from the soil. The plant intentionally wilts to shrink its surface area and save moisture, usually recovering by evening.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ajɛɔ tsui mli agbiɔ tsei koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shi ni akɛto ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe feɔ shoo yɛ gbɛkɛ mli

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or water supply is uneven because the plant gets stressed and tries to save its energy rather than making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni jɛɔ mli lɛ ejaaa ejaakɛ tso lɛ haoɔ ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do I need to trim off the extra small shoots growing on the trunk of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Removing these extra shoots, known as suckers, stops the tree from wasting food on unnecessary leaves so it can send all its strength into growing heavy cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ajiemɔ Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii ni he ehiaaa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛwo kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Weeds act as competitor plants that steal sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients directly away from your crops' roots.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the funnel of leaves during the day and chew through them before the leaf unfolds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni okɛ amɛ atsɔ mli dani baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground if rain stays heavy near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa ni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ?

english: When soil remains soaked for too long, oxygen cannot reach the underground cassava roots, causing the tubers to suffocate and rot in the wet soil.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green so the crop can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yams struggle to grow straight when planted in hard, compacted, or stony soil. Loosening the soil deeply and building soft, high mounds or ridges allows the tubers to expand downward easily.
ga: Ewa akɛ abaadu atomo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ, loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni afee gɔji loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shi oya.

english: Cassava draws a lot of nutrients out of the soil over time. Planting it continuously on the same plot weakens the soil and leads to smaller harvests, so rotating with legumes like cowpeas or resting the land helps restore soil health.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛjɔɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to build strong stalks and produce full, large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni mli wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do some of my groundnut seeds rot in the soil without sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, if the soil is overly waterlogged, or if soil insects attack them before germination. Planting seeds at a shallow depth in well-drained soil protects them.
ga: Peanut dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Aloo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Shedding leaves is cassava's natural way of surviving dry weather. By dropping leaves, the plant stops losing water through evaporation, keeping the underground stem and roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni ŋmei tsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpaa. Enɛ haa tso shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants look wilted in the afternoon heat but look fresh again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi etamɔ nɔ ni ehiɛ ejɔ ehe leebi lɛ?

english: Plants droop slightly during hot afternoon hours to reduce water loss from direct sunlight. As temperatures cool down overnight, the roots catch up on drawing moisture from the soil, restoring the leaves by morning.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni nu ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ nyɔɔŋ kome Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ he jɔɔ amɛ leebi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the plant sap and spreading viruses. Managing these pests early prevents leaf damage and keeps the plant growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off mainly due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollination. Keeping soil moisture steady and providing partial shade during severe heat helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to steal water and soil nutrients faster than crop seedlings. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crops the chance to grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli oya fe tsei amli dumɔwui. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii ni odu lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛdara ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in an open field with no big trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight because their leaves lose water too quickly and burn. Planting shade crops like plantains around them provides a natural canopy that retains moisture and protects the cocoa until it grows stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu lɛ baaje baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ ni amɛbaashã. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebaawa.

english: Why do my yam vines need long sticks to climb up instead of just spreading across the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa niji kakadaji koni enyɛ ekwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to catch maximum sunlight to convert energy into large underground tubers. Staking the vines keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal leaf diseases and allowing better exposure to light and airflow.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛtsake hewalɛ amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ naa ni oha la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant actively moves the remaining nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves up to nourish the young leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess water, cassava puts all its growth energy into top-leaf and stem production rather than transferring surplus food energy down into root development.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ ni haa eda lɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋwɛi baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, ajieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow stronger when I plant them on a plot where I harvested groundnuts or cowpeas last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas work with natural soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, leaving behind enriched soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni ashiɔ ahaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my corn stalks grow thin and fall over easily when I put four or five seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ to bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds share one hole, the young roots compete intensely for limited soil nutrients, water, and root space. This forces the plants to grow tall, weak, and thin as they fight for light.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe he ni faaa lɛ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara, amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛhe afee mlɛo be mli ni amɛwuɔ koni amɛná la lɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout when I plant them very deep in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need warmth, air, and light soil pressure to sprout. Planting too deep causes the young shoot to exhaust all its stored food energy underground before it can reach the surface sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia dɔlɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔnyɛɛ fioo koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii bibii lɛ atsu niyenii ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he nii dani amɛshɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, extreme dryness, or a lack of wind and insects to shake pollen inside the blossom to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, ŋmɔlɔ ni fe nine, loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi ebaawo yibii.

english: Leaf curling is a response to sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or a sign of a plant virus transmitted by whiteflies.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji hetoo ni akɛhaa kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ. loo tso mli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadii.

english: Why do weeds make my maize turn pale and weak even when there is plenty of rain falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb soil fertilizer and nutrients much faster than maize roots, starving the crop of essential food despite adequate water.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya fe ŋmãa shishifãi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ náaa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ po.

english: Why are my plantain trees taking so long to produce fruits these days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ?

english: Plantains require constant moisture and rich soil nutrients to fruit quickly. During extended dry spells or when soil nutrients are low, the plant slows down its growth to conserve energy, which delays flowering and fruit production.
ga: Ehe miihia ni plantains lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa babaoo koni ewo yibii oya. Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ Tsei haa amɛdalɛ baa shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo asɛɛ afo.

english: How can I make my small plot of farmland yield more crops without having to acquire extra land?
ga: Mafee ŋmɔ bibioo ko. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo nibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe shikpɔŋ kroko kɛfata he?

english: You can maximize a small plot by practicing intercropping—planting compatible crops like maize and beans together. Beans add nitrogen to the soil while maize uses the vertical space, helping you harvest more food from the same land.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha he bibioo ko aya hiɛ babaoo kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔ. Beans kɛ nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa yeɔ he ko ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do crops grow so much bigger on freshly cleared forest land than on my old farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo yɛ mi koo shikpɔŋ ni migbele ehee lɛ nɔ fe miŋmɔ momo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Forest soil is rich because years of decayed leaves and natural compost have built up a heavy bank of nutrients. Old farm plots lose these nutrients over time as crops continually feed on them without being replenished.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii babaoo ejaakɛ afii babaoo ni eho lɛ amli baai ni fiteɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ebua niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo naa. Okwaayeli ŋmɔji ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii nɛɛ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛ niyenii haa ŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be ni akɛ nɔ ko wooo mli ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young plantain shoots turn yellow and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil. Adding animal manure around the base or improving drainage usually helps them recover.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ emɔ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ashishifã ni akɛwoɔ A base loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe waa.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily whenever a heavy rain or wind comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the earth. When the plant grows a heavy bunch of fruit, it becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with a strong bamboo or wooden pole prevents it from uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ tso lɛ wo aduawai ni tsii Ebaana muji babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni mli wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekaje shishi.

english: Maize plants curl their leaves as a self-defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, stopping water from evaporating out of the plant during intense heat.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. ni etsĩ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ

english: How do I tell if my farmland is getting tired and needs a rest or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni mafo mli loo awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Tired soil shows signs such as crops growing unusually slow, leaves turning light green or yellowish instead of dark green, and harvest sizes becoming smaller every year despite good rainfall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baajie okadii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ kpo. Baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Ni kpamɔ lɛ dalɛ baa shi daa afi yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Where do new plantain plants come from if they do not produce seeds like maize or peppers?
ga: Nɛgbɛ plantains heei lɛ jɛɔ kɛji amɛwooo dumɔwui, tamɔ ŋmãa loo chili ŋmãa?

english: Plantains reproduce through underground stems that push up young shoots called 'suckers' around the mother tree. You can carefully dig up these suckers and replant them elsewhere to grow new trees.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni tsiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘ŋmeii’ lɛ anɔ kɛbɔleɔ tso nyɛ lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ahe nii ni okɛwo he kroko koni tso hee ko akwɛ̃.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the cassava I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to survive on very few nutrients and water. They aggressively steal sunlight, space, and soil food from your cassava crops, which grow at a more controlled pace.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ niyenii fioo kɛ nu fioo mli. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, ŋwɛi, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ o-cassava tsei lɛ amli lɛ kɛ ekãa. ni daa yɛ gbɛ ni akudɔɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ

english: Why are my crops growing tall and skinny under big trees, but giving me very little harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ? Shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: Crops need sunlight to make food for growing fruits. When planted under heavy shade, the crop spends all its energy stretching upwards to reach light, leaving no energy left to grow proper fruits or roots.
ga: Hulu la he miihia tsei koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha aduawai ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii koni amɛná la. Hewalɛ ko eshwɛɛɛ ni baaha adu aduawai loo shishifãi ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of holes and looking like somebody chewed them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni etamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko ŋmɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Fall Armyworm caterpillars feed inside the center leaves of young maize, leaving behind ragged holes and waste that looks like sawdust. Catching them early with appropriate organic treatments or recommended sprays protects the growing point so the corn can still produce healthy cobs.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe baai. Eshiɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ esɛɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni sa ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ abu he ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ he koni ŋmãa lɛ aya nɔ awo ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with many big leaves, but when I harvest, the tubers are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi kɛ́ akpa bulb lɛ, ani amɛbafeɔ bibii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy building thick stems and green leaves instead of root tubers. Balancing the soil food allows the plant to redirect its sugars downward into growing long, heavy roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ni mli wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkuɔ sugar lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa amɛshishifãi kakadaji ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Extreme afternoon heat combined with dry soil makes tomato plants stressed, causing them to drop their blossoms to preserve water. Giving tomato plants consistent watering and light shade during peak heat helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy fruit.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fata he lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ ajie fɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni nu ahi mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa ni okɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Harmattan dry winds pull moisture out of cocoa leaves faster than the root system can drink from dry soil. Planting shade trees like plantains or shade-giving forestry trees keeps humidity near the trees and protects leaves from harsh dry winds.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he.

english: How do I stop my seed yams from rotting in the soil before they even sprout?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Raw cut edges of seed yams allow fungus and soil pests to enter and rot the yam before sprouts can form. Dusting the cut yam pieces with dry wood ash seals the cut surfaces and prevents rot while the seed lies in the damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii ni afolɔ ni afee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ okɛ tso sũ ni egbi lɛ shwie sweet potato fãi ni afo lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ sũ ni afo lɛ awo mli, ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip and spreads along the center vein of older leaves shows that the crop is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer. Applying nitrogen near the plant roots turns leaves dark green again so the crop can feed itself and build full corn cobs.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ashishigbɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aye niyenii ni ewo ŋmãa babaoo.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get a much bigger harvest from my small field?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ manyɛ maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Ani minɔ ni?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks with very small fruit. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets full sunlight and food, giving you bigger individual fruits and a higher total harvest.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii waa baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa onáa yibii wuji kɛ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upward and droop in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to shrink their leaf surface so they lose less water under the hot sun. If the leaves recover by early morning, the plant is managing heat, but if they stay limp, the soil needs deep watering near the root area.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha baa lɛ hiɛ afee bibioo bɔni afee ni nu fioo pɛ amɛfite yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ he wa lɛ leebi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ hulutsoo lɛ miikpe. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he miihia nu ni mli kwɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that drink up rain water and steal soil nutrients much faster than young crops can. Removing weeds early stops them from starving your crops, allowing your plants to use all the water and soil food to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni nuɔ nugbɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baanyɛ afee. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akaye hɔmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do extension officers encourage me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi hewalɛ koni madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer inside their roots. When planted alongside maize, these crops feed the soil naturally, helping the maize grow strong without relying entirely on bought fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Tsei nɛɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ ŋmãa ni aheɔ lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees lose water faster than their roots can take it up when exposed to severe heat and the Harmattan winds. Planting shade trees like plantains nearby and putting dry grass around the base of the stem keeps the soil moist and protects the leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbɔleɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa baa lɛ ashã.

english: This black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives when your farm is too damp, dark, and crowded. Clearing weeds, pruning excess branch leaves to let in sunlight and air, and removing affected pods early will protect the healthy ones.
ga: Nɛkɛ black pod hela nɛɛ jɛɔ ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ beni oŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, edɔ ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. weeding Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. kɛ ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark powders inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse ehe lɛ? Ni powda fioo ko ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ mli?

english: This leaf damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest eating the growing point of the maize plant. Catching them early and spraying safe bio-pesticides or neem leaf extract directly into the plant whorl prevents them from ruining your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: A V-shaped yellowing starting from the leaf tip means your soil lacks nitrogen nutrient. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure near the roots when the plant is knee-high provides the energy it needs to produce large ears.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ aaafee amɛnaji ahe lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee toi wuji.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy, soggy soil. Planting your cassava cuttings on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni mli efɔ nɔ Ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to produce energy and feed the growing tuber below. Without stakes, leaves stay bunched on the dark ground, leading to leaf spot diseases and very small tuber yields.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ leaf spot hela baa ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a plant virus. Controlling these insects early with soapy water sprays or appropriate insecticides keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ mli Mra be mli ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ Kɛ akɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Watering your plants consistently at root level and providing light shade during peak heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni aha lɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during light rain even when there is no storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ ahum ko bɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when invisible microscopic worms (nematodes) or banana weevils destroy the roots underground. Dip your new suckers in hot water for a few minutes before planting to kill pests and ensure strong root anchorage.
ga: Dumɔwui gbeeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni anaaa amɛ lɛ anɔ. (Nematodes) loo banana ŋmeii fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi. Okɛ oshishifãi heei lɛ awo nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli minitii fioo komɛi dani odu koni egbe kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni ekwɛ koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry palm leaves or cut grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni akɛ ŋmei baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni afolɔ ewo mli?

english: Covering soil with organic materials—called mulching—acts like a blanket that stops sunlight from baking the ground, keeps moisture in the soil longer during dry periods, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ko ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn and dry out quickly in full sunlight. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains to act as natural umbrellas until their roots grow deep enough to handle the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ latsaa lɛ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves high up to catch sunlight. Lifting the vines off the damp ground allows them to make more food through sunlight, which helps the plant grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa wain tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil food needed for green growth. Continuous farming or heavy rain washes nitrogen away, causing the plant to starve from the bottom up.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my field make the maize I plant next grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, the maize feeds on that leftover natural plant food in the soil.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa yeɔ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so fast right after the first rain after a long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During the dry season, fallen leaves and organic matter build up in the warm soil. The first rain causes soil microbes to break down this material rapidly, releasing a sudden burst of nutrients that gives crops an immediate growth spurt.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Baai ni egbee shi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ oya. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ajieɔ trukaa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya.

english: When too many young shoots grow around a single plantain tree, they steal water and soil nutrients from the main stem. Removing extra shoots ensures the main tree gets enough energy to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Tso lɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ niji agboi ni tsii baa.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even if there is plenty of space between the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ gbɛ babaoo kã amɛteŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that spread quickly under the soil to drink up water and fertilizer before your crops can reach them. Even if there is space above ground, weeds are secretly starving your crops below.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi oya koni enu nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ he. Kɛji akɛ he ko ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po. Jwɛi hu baanyɛ aha hɔmɔ aye onibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ yɛ teemɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when left in flooded soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil for long periods, the roots drown from lack of air, allowing rot fungi in the wet soil to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or dry conditions. The plant drops its blossoms to save its limited energy and moisture to stay alive instead of spending it on growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ fioo kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite shika yɛ aduawai akwɛmɔ mli lɛ

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into tight cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni ekpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking juice from the undersides of the leaves. This feeding damages the leaf cells and can spread plant viruses that stunt overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Niyenii nɛɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli wala yibii ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tso mli helai ni haa tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ eshwa.

english: Is cocoyam a difficult crop for a beginner like me to cultivate on my land?
ga: Ani kookoo ji tso ko ni wa kɛha mɔ ko ni jeɔ shishi tamɔ mi akɛ ebaadu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoyam is a straightforward and resilient crop that does not require extraordinary techniques, making it easy for any farmer to plant and maintain successfully with routine care.
ga: Cocoyam ji tso ko ni yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni enyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe ni ehe ehiaaa ŋaa krɛdɛɛ ko. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa okwaafoi lɛ akɛ amɛaadu ni amɛkwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa.

english: Can I grow cocoyam under the shade of bigger trees on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi?

english: Yes, cocoyam is shade-tolerant and thrives well under partial shade, which makes it ideal for intercropping alongside food trees like plantains or under young cocoa trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulutsoo naa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be fioo mli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains ahe loo yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ashishi.

english: What kind of soil do I need to get big, healthy cocoyam tubers?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ he hiaa mi koni maná kookoo yitsei wuji ni mli wa?

english: Cocoyams prefer loose, rich, well-draining soil filled with organic material, which allows the underground tubers room to expand easily without trapping excess standing water.
ga: Cocoa sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa tuber chamber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ehiɛɛɛ mli.

english: Why is it necessary to mound soil around the base of my growing root crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato shikpɔŋ abɔle mishishifãi ni miida lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Heaping soil around the base covers exposed tubers from sunlight, retains moisture around the roots, and provides soft earth for new tubers to grow underground.
ga: heaping dirt around Shishitoo lɛ baaha yitso ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo koni bulbs heei akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to plant cocoyam?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu kookoo?

english: The best time to plant cocoyam is at the onset of the main rainy season so the roots get enough consistent moisture to establish strong stems and leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛfee tsei kɛ baai ni wa.

english: Why do my cocoyam leaves droop and turn yellow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoyam leaves droop and dry up during dry periods to conserve water, reducing leaf surface area to keep the underground tuber alive until water returns.
ga: Kokoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni akɛbu nu he. Enɛ haa baa lɛ nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nu lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds around my cocoyam crop?
ga: Ehe miihia ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ. Shii enyiɛ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Weeding is important in the early months until the broad leaves of the cocoyam grow large enough to naturally shade the ground and suppress weed growth on their own.
ga: Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ he miihia yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli. Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsi jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: What causes my cocoyam tubers to rot while still in the ground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo bulbs lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Tuber rot is usually caused by waterlogged soil that lacks good drainage, or from wounded tubers caused by sharp farming tools during weeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tuber rot baa. aloo kɛjɛ yitsoŋ pilamɔi ni okwaayeli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛbaa yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell when my cocoyams are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kookoo lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoyams are typically ready for harvest when the leaves naturally begin to turn yellow and die back, usually around 8 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Can I save part of my harvested cocoyam to plant for the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ eko ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can save small side tubers or the top cuttings of the main tuber with intact buds and keep them in a cool, dry place until the next planting season.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okpa sɛɛ bulb bibii loo bulb wulu lɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ŋmeii lɛ bɛ mli lɛ. ni okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi kɛyashi be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the roots are drowning from excess water. Applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu babaoo miiho shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plant leaves curl up like narrow tubes when the afternoon sun gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ tsɔnei bibii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural survival reaction to save water. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to hot air, preventing fast water loss.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo koni ekɛbu nu he. Tsei haa he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni nu akafite oya

english: Why do my garden vegetables look droopy and wilted in the afternoon but stand up fresh again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi obaaku osɛɛ kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. At night, the roots catch up by absorbing moisture, making the plants fresh by sunrise.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. gbɛkɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ te shi

english: How do I know which side of a cassava cutting should face up when I plant it in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male mi-cassava lɛ fã ni esa akɛ ekwɛ ŋwɛi beni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or leaf nodes along the stem. The buds should point upward toward the sky like small arrows so the roots and shoots can grow in the right direction.
ga: Kwɛmɔ hiŋmɛii bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. loo baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi tamɔ akpɔlɔi bibii. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adara yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ.

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition produces weak, skinny plants and significantly lowers your harvest.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. ni okɛ okpamɔ lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden poles to climb on instead of growing flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akwɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can spread out to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build large underground tubers. Staking also keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko ni baaha amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers to save water and energy when weather conditions become too hot or dry. Planting shade trees like plantains protects young cocoa from heat stress and prevents flower drop.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he, ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when stressed by sudden dry soil, extreme heat, or pest damage. Spreading dry grass mulch around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and holds moisture in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai fitemɔ hao amɛ. Mulch ni egbi ni bɔleɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning black and soft on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miida lɛ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, often brought on by uneven watering. Consistent soil moisture helps the plant transport calcium from the soil into the fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to heap soil over my cassava and yam tubers if they start pushing out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ muji toɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ? Kɛ amɛbɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ?

english: Exposing tubers to direct sunlight turns them green, tough, and bitter, while making them easy targets for pests. Covering them with earth protects them from sun damage and burrowing insects.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ bulb lɛ wo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha etsɔ eŋɔli, ehe wa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ be mli ni ebaaha amɛfee nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ha amɛhe lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ bu lɛ ahe.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting my maize before it is ready to harvest?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmãa lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani efee klalo akɛ obaakpa?

english: Most maize varieties in Ghana take between 3 to 4 months (about 12 to 16 weeks) to mature fully and be ready for harvesting, depending on whether you plant early-maturing or late-maturing seed.
ga: Abele babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 (aaafee otsii 12 kɛyashi 16) dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ. Edamɔ dumɔwui ni shwereɔ mra loo dumɔwui ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How many years after planting cocoa seedlings will I start seeing cocoa pods grow on the trees?
ga: Afii enyiɛ beni odu kookoo dumɔwu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ obaaje shishi ona kookoo ŋmeii ni miikwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually take about 2 to 3 years to start producing pods, while traditional older varieties can take up to 4 or 5 years before yielding their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 dani ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé aaafee afii 4 loo 5 dani amɛwo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if my plantain bunch is ripe enough to harvest from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain tso lɛ ekwɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A plantain bunch is ready to harvest when the individual fruits look rounded and full rather than sharp and angled, and the dried flowers at the tips easily rub off.
ga: Plantain ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko efee kokroo ni eyi obɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ, eyɛ mlɛo akɛ abaajie.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the soil is short on nitrogen, so the plant is pulling nitrogen out of its older bottom leaves to keep the top growing leaves alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off mainly when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when bees and air currents are not available to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi babaoo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen.

english: How do I know if my crops are drooping from lack of rain or from a pest attacking the roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbee shi yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ahewɔ?

english: If crops droop during the hot afternoon sun but recover and stand tall by early morning, they need water; if they stay wilted overnight, insects or disease are likely damaging the roots.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Shi ehiɛ ba shi ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ leebi maŋkpa. amɛmiitao nu Kɛji amɛgbo nyɔɔŋ kome mli Etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii loo helai hu baafite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop have lush green leaves, but the roots underground are very thin and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛji bibii?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing heavy leaf foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Should I start planting immediately after the very first rain of the season drops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until two or three heavy rains have fallen so the soil holds enough deep moisture, preventing young seedlings from drying out if there is a short dry spell right after.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be kuku ko ba ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong direct sunlight, so plantains grow quickly and provide wide leaves that shade and protect the cocoa trees while they get established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa kookoo tso lɛ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ebuɔ ehe be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans helps improve the soil for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, leaving natural plant food behind that feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii lɛ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I measure my farmland in hectares so I know the exact size of my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ hectares mli? Bɔni afee ni manyɛ male bɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ da ha pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Measuring land in hectares helps you buy the exact amount of seeds and fertilizer needed without waste. One hectare is roughly equal to the size of a standard football field, or about 2.5 acres of land.
ga: Kɛ́ osusu he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he yɛ hectares mli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ oheɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii abɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ nɔ ko fiteee. Hectare kome dalɛ tamɔ bɔɔlutswaa he ko ni afɔɔ feemɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni feɔ acre 2.5.

english: How do I calculate how many cocoa seedlings I need to buy for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu kookoo dumɔwui enyiɛ ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You calculate seedling requirements by taking your total land size in hectares and dividing it by the recommended spacing; for cocoa planted at 3 meters apart, you will need about 1,110 seedlings per hectare.
ga: Obuɔ odumɔwui ahe hiamɔ nii ahe akɔntaa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ hectares mli lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛto lɛ mlijaa nɔ. Kɛha kookoo ŋmɔji ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 3 lɛ, obaahiɛ aaafee dumɔwui 1,110 yɛ hectare kome mli.

english: How much land space do I need to clear if I want to start a small commercial plantain farm?
ga: Shikpɔŋ enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mafo kɛji miisumɔ ni mabɔi jarayeli plantain ŋmɔ bibioo ko shishi?

english: A beginner can start with just one acre, which is about 0.4 hectares. This size can fit around 600 plantain suckers, making it easy to manage by yourself while still giving a good harvest.
ga: Mɛi ni jeɔ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi kɛ acre kome pɛ, ni ji aaafee hectares 0.4. Nɛkɛ dalɛ nɛɛ baanyɛ ashɛ plantains aaafee 600 he, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ obaakwɛ nɔ shi ewoɔ yibii kpakpai lolo.

english: Why do my maize crops yield less when I plant them very close together on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves them thin and weak, resulting in smaller cobs compared to well-spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmei bibioo ko baa kɛ akɛto tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do crops grow tall and healthy in one portion of my farm, but look small and weak in another portion?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛhe wa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi etamɔ nɔ ni eji bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fã kroko mli.

english: Soil quality and water retention vary across the same farm field. Some portions have rich, deep soil that holds moisture, while other spots may have rocky, poor soil that starves the plant roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. Mɛi komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli. yɛ be mli ni otii krokomɛi Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, ni ehiii ni haa tsei shishifãi yeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my crop yields drop every year if I keep growing the exact same crop on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year while allowing specific pests and diseases to build up and attack your future harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛtutuaa onibii ni obaadu wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does mixing beans with my maize crop help improve my farm land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛfutuɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ?

english: Legumes like beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This natural soil food stays in the ground to nourish your maize plants without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ niyenii nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa tso lɛ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry spells to reduce water loss through evaporation. It is a defense trick to keep its roots alive until the rains return to sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Eji teemɔŋ sane ko ni kɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni abuɔ he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baatsɔ amɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: In extreme afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can drink it from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself and usually recovers by evening when it cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni edɔ lɛ.

english: How do heavy rains affect the fertilizer I put around my plantain suckers?
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ he lɛ ahe. Te ofeɔ tɛŋŋ okɛ dumɔwui?

english: Heavy downpours can wash loose fertilizer off the topsoil or push it too deep into the ground past where plant roots can reach, so it is best to apply fertilizer in smaller amounts when rains are moderate.
