ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ he loo ekɛwo sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko awo mli beni nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ fioo lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily scorch under direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living cover and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii ewo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing on lower maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make leaves green. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant recover and form healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ ni ehaa toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Cassava is usually mature when the leaves at the bottom of the plant begin to turn yellow and drop off, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety you planted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda beni baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat is too intense or when the plant does not get enough regular water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from extreme heat helps fruits set.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ la lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ daa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛmaa shi.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines instead of letting them crawl on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã ekplekeshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up off the hot ground so they can catch more sunlight. When leaves get full light, the plant produces more food and grows much larger tubers underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la babaoo ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa lɛ Tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni amɛyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara kwraa.

english: Too many small shoots (suckers) steal water and food from the main mother plant. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which results in larger plantain bunches.
ga: Tso bibii (tso) babaoo tsɔ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa plantains lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and shrink?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi nɛɛ ni akudɔɔ amɛ mra lɛ baaye abua ni akafite tsei ahe tsei.

english: How does planting cowpeas help improve the soil for my next crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, that nitrogen stays in the soil, serving as free fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ fite Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my watermelons rot on the side that rests directly on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ fite yɛ fã ni akɛma shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Watermelons rot on the bottom when moisture from wet soil encourages bacteria and fungi to attack the skin. Placing dry straw or leaves under developing fruits keeps them dry and prevents rotting.
ga: Watermelons fiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛtutua hewolo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo aduawai ni miida lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ni eha ehiɛ akafite.

english: Why does my rice crop grow poorly when the soil stays dry for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Rice plants require a steady supply of moisture to build strong stems and fill their seed heads. Dry periods stress the plant, causing shallow root growth and empty grain husks at harvest time.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ taoɔ nu daa koni amɛfee tsei ni wa ni amɛwo dumɔwui ayitsei lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. Be ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ dumɔwui ahe tsɔi ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate the direct, harsh sun and hot winds of the dry season (Harmattan). Without shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them, their tender leaves dry out, turn yellow, and fall off.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ (harmattan) lɛ naa kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ebuuu amɛhe. Amɛbaai bibii lɛ baagbi. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi

english: Why do my young maize leaves have holes in them with tiny caterpillars hiding inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which lays eggs on corn leaves. Once hatched, the caterpillars crawl into the central growing leaves (the whorl) to feed on the tender stem, causing visible hole damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa baai anɔ lɛ. Beni ŋmei lɛ fɔɔ lɛ ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ baai ni miida yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (whorls) koni amɛye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. ni kɛ fitemɔ ni anaa baa

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but the roots in the soil stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or leafy manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above the ground instead of sending starches down to form thick tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shi kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark, soft, and rotten before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil. It usually occurs when watering is irregular or when the soil dries out completely between rainfalls.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and becoming tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni efee bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the young leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies that distorts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. ni fiteɔ baa lɛ dalɛ ni sa lɛ

english: Why did my maize seeds die in the soil after I planted them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ gboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often a 'false rain' that moistens the topsoil just enough for seeds to start sprouting, but if no more rain follows for weeks, the soil dries up completely and kills the tender germinated seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji ‘nugbɔ amale’ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi kwraa ni ebaagbe dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do my crops get dry, burnt leaves when I apply chemical fertilizer during a period without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii gĩɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are strong salts that need moisture to dissolve safely. If applied when the ground is dry, the fertilizer draws water out of the plant roots instead of feeding them, causing the leaves to dry up and burn.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni biɔ nu ni mli edɔ koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛtsu nii be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso shishifãi amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every year even though I plant the exact same crop in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? Kɛji akɛ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome po.

english: Planting the exact same crop in the same soil every season repeatedly removes the same nutrients without replacement, while allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be ni Seasons jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. without replacement Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa tsofai fɔji kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots and turning soft inside my barn before I sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living stem tissue that naturally break their resting phase when exposed to warmth and light. As new sprouts grow, they draw water and nutrients from inside the yam, making it light, soft, and spongy.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ wala mli ni amɛyaa wɔɔ kɛji akɛ amɛwo dɔlɛ kɛ la mli. Kɛji ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ Ejieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ sponji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during small windstorms even when the main stem does not break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum bibioo ko mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne titri lɛ ekuuu po.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that are easily damaged by microscopic worms (nematodes) or root weevils in the soil. When those pests destroy the roots underground, the plant loses its anchor and falls over under light wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. (nematodes) loo shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Kɛ́ nakai kooloi lɛ kpata shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahiɛ Tso lɛ laajeɔ eshishifãi lɛ ni egbeeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow better and yield more when I hire a tractor to plow the land deep before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ miha trakta koni mikɛtsu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani mikɛdu nii lɛ?

english: Deep plowing breaks up hard soil, allowing plant roots to spread easily, reach deep groundwater, and breathe. It also buries weeds and mixes natural nutrients into the root zone where crops can easily feed.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ baagbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. Eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he, ni enyɛɔ emuɔ. Efuɔ jwɛi hu ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii futuɔ shishifãi lɛ amli he ni tsei baanyɛ aye nii yɛ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with tiny harvests when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ŋmaa fioo pɛ ji nɔ ni mikpaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, crops fight each other for sunlight, soil moisture, and nutrients. Instead of making big fruits or grains, they waste energy stretching upward to compete for light.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni jɛɔ amɛhe Moŋ lɛ ebɔɔ aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji. Amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛmiitswa la he akaŋ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential food for growth. The plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves to nourish new growth, signaling that you need to apply fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha dalɛ hee lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ fɔ awo mli.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off without ever turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of bees and insects to pollinate them. Consistent watering during hot spells helps the plant hold onto flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. aloo ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni bɛ ni baaha tso lɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Weed seeds are wild and tough, resting ready in the soil to sprout instantly at the first drop of rain. Your crop seeds take more time to break their shell and establish roots before they can start growing upward.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛhe wa. Eheɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ. Odumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛgbalaa amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why does my rice crop need so much water in the field compared to my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto mi ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rice plants have shallow root systems that thrive in wet soil, which also smothers competing weeds. Maize has deeper roots designed to hunt for moisture underground and will rot if left standing in too much water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ hu kɛyaa. Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni afee koni ekɛtao ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ nu babaoo mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rains flooded the farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the ground for too long, it pushes all the air out, causing the roots to drown and turn soft and rotten.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛje kpo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their special strength in the second generation. Planting them results in uneven growth, smaller harvests, and weaker resistance to local pests compared to buying fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni fa fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ dumɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa fioo kɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen stays behind to naturally feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shi koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does my harvested rice break into tiny pieces when I take it to the mill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akumɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli bibii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be akɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rice grains break easily during milling if they dried too fast under harsh direct sunlight or were harvested too late when the grains were already brittle. Proper shaded drying keeps the grains strong.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛji amɛgbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Aloo kpamɔ sɛɛ tsɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ egbɔjɔ momo lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Adding balanced fertilizer like NPK or compost early in the season gives the maize the strength it needs to stay green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi ŋmɔŋ ni eda oya.

english: What causes my maize cobs to have missing kernels when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ bɛ ŋmeii kɛji mikpa amɛ?

english: Missing kernels happen when pollination fails, often because of dry weather or extreme heat when the silks are emerging. Ensuring the plants get enough water during flowering helps the pollen reach every silk to fill out the cob completely.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa beni siliki lɛ miida lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ehaa pollen lɛ shɛɔ siliki fɛɛ siliki he koni ekɛwo ŋmei lɛ mli kwraa.

english: How do I know if my crop leaves are curling up because of the sun or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hulu la loo hela hewɔ ni mitso lɛ baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaves often roll inward during the hot afternoon to prevent water loss, but they will relax once the sun sets. If the leaves stay curled up permanently or look wrinkled and sticky, it is usually caused by pests or a viral infection.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni nu akafite. Shi ejɔɔ ehe kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi. Kɛji baai lɛ ebɔle ehe daa loo ebɔle ehe ni ekpɛtɛ ehe Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: This black rot is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant pull calcium from the ground up into the tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tomato lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall with lots of big green leaves but very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai wuji eŋɔli shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them focus entirely on growing stems and leaves instead of flowers. Using fertilizers higher in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to bloom and set more fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot lets soil-borne diseases and pests build up in the dirt over time. Rotating your land with crops like maize or beans starves out tomato pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tomato yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baatsake lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ejie tomato mli ŋmeii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my mango trees drop most of their small green fruits right after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Bei pii lɛ, beni fɔfɔi lɛ ewo sɛɛ?

english: Mango trees naturally drop excess young fruit because they cannot support every flower that blooms. However, sudden severe fruit drop is often worsened by strong winds, dry spells, or sap-sucking pests like thrips that attack the flower stems.
ga: Mango tsei shwieɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo babaoo tsɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi fɔfɔi fɛɛ ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, hulutsoo be, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ haa aduawai ni shwieɔ shi trukaa waa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: What is the black powdery substance covering my mango leaves, and how does it harm the tree?
ga: Mɛni ji powda diŋ ni haa mango baai ahe lɛ? Mɛɛ hewalɛ gbonyo eyɔɔ yɛ tsei anɔ?

english: That black powder is sooty mold, a fungus that grows on the sweet liquid left behind by insects like mealybugs and scale insects. Washing off the pests stops the liquid, allowing rain to clean the leaves so the tree can absorb sunlight again.
ga: Pauda diŋ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs kɛ scale kooloi shwieɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ akpa. Ha nugbɔ lɛ atsumɔ baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow better when I plant cowpeas or beans near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When these roots decompose, they naturally enrich the surrounding soil with nitrogen for neighboring crops to feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anyɛ ana.

english: How can I check if my soil has enough moisture for planting without expensive equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ nii ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Dig down about a hand-length into the soil, grab a handful, and squeeze it into a ball; if it holds its shape without dripping excess water, the soil has ideal moisture for planting seeds.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ aaafee tso kome kɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okɛ onine awo mli ni okɛmimɔ mli ni efee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni ekɛ nu shwieee shi fe nine. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ.

english: Why do many farmers say plantain farming brings good profit compared to other food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo kɛɔ akɛ plantain dumɔ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ni aduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains yield high crop volume per acre and mature relatively quickly within 12 to 15 months. Because plantains are a staple food eaten daily across Ghana, there is constant market demand, allowing farmers to earn a strong and steady income.
ga: Plantains woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli ni edaa oya yɛ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 mli, ejaakɛ plantains ji niyenii titri ni ayeɔ daa gbi yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ yaa nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do people recommend planting plantain alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and conserving soil moisture for the cocoa trees during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei lɛ aná hulutsoo ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why does my plantain farm start growing very well in the beginning, but becomes harder to manage after the first harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ da jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi ebafeɔ nɔ ni wa waa akɛ aaakwɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: At first, a single plant uses all the soil's nutrients. After the first harvest, the plant leaves behind multiple new shoots (suckers) that compete for light, water, and food. Without regular pruning and pest management, the soil gets tired and management becomes difficult.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, tso kome yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Kɛji akɛ afolɔɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe daa ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tsei lɛ baashi ŋmeii heei babaoo (ŋmeii) ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa la, nu, kɛ niyenii he akaŋ yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baagbɔjɔ ni nɔkwɛmɔ baafee nɔ ni wa waa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that do not go very deep into the soil. As the heavy bunch grows at the top, strong winds or wet soil can easily knock the plant over. Supporting the stems with wooden poles helps keep them upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Beni kuu lɛ da yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei agbo oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi jaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain plants turning yellow and drying up before the fruits are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or that diseases like Black Sigatoka are spreading. Removing dead leaves and applying manure or fertilizer helps keep the leaves healthy so the fruit can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium, loo akɛ hela ko tamɔ Black Sigatoka miigbɛ eshwa. Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni egboi lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni aduawai anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain stems look weak and shrink during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants are made mostly of water. During dry periods, they lose water faster than their shallow roots can draw it from the dry ground. Mulching around the base with dry grass helps keep moisture in the soil during dry spells.
ga: Nu ji nɔ ni akɛfeɔ dumɔwui babaoo. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Amɛbaafite nu oya fe shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How do I choose the best plantain shoots to plant when starting a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu kɛji mije ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Choose 'sword suckers'—these are young shoots with broad bases and narrow, spear-shaped leaves. They have strong energy reserves and grow faster than 'water suckers,' which have broad leaves early on but produce weak stems and small fruit bunches.
ga: Halamɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni ji tso bibioo ko ni shishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ lance. Amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni mli wa ni amɛtoɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe ‘ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ mra lɛ. Shi tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii ni abua naa lɛ baahi.

english: Why do the fruit bunches from my plantain trees get smaller with every new harvest cycle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai akui ni jɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ amli lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ kpamɔ hee fɛɛ kpamɔ hee lɛ?

english: Over time, the mother plant leaves behind many suckers that exhaust the soil's nutrients and attract underground pests like stem borers. Pruning down to one or two strong suckers per plant and adding fertilizer restores bunch size.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ baashwie ŋmeii babaoo, ni no baaha sũ mli niyenii lɛ afite ni ebaagbala shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ stem borers. Kɛ́ afo tso kome loo enyɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kuu lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if pests are attacking my plantain plants from inside the stem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua mi dumɔwui lɛ kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: If the leaves wilt suddenly, the main stem breaks easily near the ground, or you see tiny holes with dark sap oozing out, stem borers or nematodes are tunneling inside the plant and cutting off its supply of food and water.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ gboi trukaa lɛ Tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ fãa mlɛo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Aloo onaa buji bibii? ni mliki ni mli edɔ miiho kɛmiijɛ mli lɛ Stem borers, loo nematodes, miifo tso lɛ mli ni amɛmiifo niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad to dig deeply with a hoe around the base of my plantain trees when weeding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmei baafo mi plantains lɛ ashishi kɛya shɔŋŋ beni mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Plantain feeder roots spread out very close to the soil surface. Deep hoeing cuts these roots, making it hard for the plant to absorb food and water, which slows down fruit growth and weakens the tree.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛ eshwa kɛbɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ waa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nitsumɔ ni mli kwɔ baafo shishifãi nɛɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ daraaa oya, ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: What does it actually mean when someone tells me a crop variety is 'drought-resistant'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ akɛ mɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ tso ko ‘nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa’?

english: It means the crop has special traits—like deep roots or hardier leaves—that allow it to survive and still produce yield even when there is very little rainfall or dry weather.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔ nii lɛ yɛ sui krɛdɛɛi, tamɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni wa. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi po.

english: If I plant a very strong and tough crop variety, do I still need to use fertilizer on my field?
ga: Kɛji midu tso ko ni mli wa waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mishia lɛ mli lolo?

english: Yes, even strong crops need nutrients to produce a good harvest. While a tough crop can survive poor soil better than a weak one, adding fertilizer ensures it reaches its full yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po he miihia niyenii kpakpai koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni egbɔjɔ moŋ, Shi kɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha oná yibiiwoo ni fa.

english: If I apply fertilizer to my farm once, will I need to keep adding it every single season?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome pɛ Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli daa be?

english: Yes, because growing plants consume the nutrients from the soil, and heavy rains can wash remaining nutrients away, so you must replenish the soil regularly to keep getting good yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei ni miida lɛ heɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa koni oya nɔ owo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crops sometimes grow very tall with lots of green leaves but produce very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛhiɛɔ baai babaoo shi niyenii fioo pɛ amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the plant gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or not enough balance of other nutrients, causing it to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of fruits or seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo amɛnáaa niyenii krokomɛi ni fa bɔ ni sa, ni no haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ ni jɛɔ ebaai lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ eyibii loo edumɔwui lɛ najiaŋ.

english: I want to expand my farm from 2 acres to 20 acres; is it just a matter of buying more seeds?
ga: Miisumɔ ni magbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ acre 2 kɛyashɛ acre 20 nɔ. Eji dumɔwui babaoo ni aheɔ kɛkɛ, aloo jeee nakai?

english: No, expanding requires much more labor, water, fertilizer, and time to manage pests. Without enough resources for the whole area, you risk crop failure across the entire expanded field.
ga: Dabi, shweremɔ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo, nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ be kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ. Kɛji nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha kpokpaa muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo oshara mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafite yɛ kpokpaa ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: As a small-scale farmer with limited money, what is the safest way for me to try a new crop variety?
ga: Ákɛ okwaafonyo bibioo ni shika fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maka tsei heei akwɛ?

english: Start by planting a small test section of your land first so you can observe how the crop behaves under your local weather and soil before spending all your money on a large area.
ga: Je shishi kɛtsɔ kaa he bibioo ko ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ amɛnii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ shishi. Dani obaafite oshika fɛɛ yɛ he ko ni da

english: Why do crops sometimes fail completely even when a farmer buys high-quality seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ kwraa eyɛ mli akɛ okwaafoi heɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Good seeds are only one part of success; if the crop lacks sufficient water, proper soil food, or protection from pests and diseases, it can still dry up or produce nothing.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai ji omanyeyeli fã ko kɛkɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa loo hebuu kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe Ebaaya nɔ ehi shi ni egbi loo ewooo nɔ ko kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are struggling from a lack of water before they actually die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni faaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miipiŋ dani amɛgboi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Look for early warning signs such as leaf curling, yellowing, or wilting during the cooler morning hours when plants should normally look fresh.
ga: Taomɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii mra tamɔ baai ni ebɔle, ni efee ŋmɔŋ loo ni egbo yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ ji be ni esa akɛ tso lɛ afee ehee tamɔ bɔ ni eji daa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to dry out so fast on hot days even if I watered them recently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo mli nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ moŋ.

english: Hot sun and wind cause moisture to evaporate rapidly from both the soil surface and the leaves, forcing the plant to drink up ground water much faster than on cool days.
ga: Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei nuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu oya fe gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ.

english: Can a small-scale farm produce as much food per acre as a large commercial farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔji bibii baanyɛ ajie niyenii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli tamɔ jarayeli ŋmɔji wuji lɛ?

english: Yes, small farms can match or exceed large farm yields per acre if the farmer gives close, careful attention to soil health, weed control, and proper plant feeding on that smaller plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔji bibii baanyɛ afee ŋmɔji wuji amli yibiiwoo yɛ acre kome mli loo amɛfee nakai. Kɛji okwaafoi kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ma shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tsei niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which acts as food for leaf growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: When beans get too much nitrogen from overly rich soil or heavy fertilizing, they focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of flowers. Less nitrogen encourages the plant to start flowering and producing pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii fe nine loo ŋmeii ni fa babaoo mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ baama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Nitrogen ni faaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that create living shade, protecting young cocoa trees while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy water collects and stays in the soil without draining, the roots drown and rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni muji bua ehe naa ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagboi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open on the vine just before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they get a sudden large amount of water after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit absorbs water quickly and expands faster than the skin can stretch, causing it to burst.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛ́ amɛná nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: What happens if I plant my yam setts too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Planting yams too close makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, space, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant room to spread its roots and form larger, heavier tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu sweet potatoes yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ tsu fɛɛ tsu mli gbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni efeɔ bulbs wuji ni tsii.

english: Sweet potatoes are naturally creeping vines. Spreading across the ground helps the plant shade the soil to hold moisture, suppress weed growth, and form tubers at different nodes along the stem.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa. Tsi jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ofee bulbs yɛ hei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites under the leaves. Their feeding weakens the plant and can spread viruses that prevent the pepper plant from growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo baa mli ŋmeii ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛ niyenii lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni haaa pepper tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ ashwã.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely high or when soil moisture changes too drastically. Heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake tsɔ. Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my maize stalks break easily during high winds before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani akpaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks weaken when stem borer pests chew holes inside the stem or when the soil lacks nutrients like potassium. Pest control and good plant food help build thick, strong stalks.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ stem borer kooloi lɛ shwie tsei lɛ amli buji loo kɛ́ niyenii tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei aniyenii kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa tsei ni mli tse ni wa.

english: Does tying my yam vines to tall wooden poles really make the tubers growing underground bigger?
ga: Ani sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, staking lifts yam leaves up toward the sunlight so the plant can make more food. That extra energy travels down to build much bigger yam tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking haa sweet potato lɛ woɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Nakai hewalɛ kroko lɛ fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee sweet potato tuber ni da kwraa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your corn lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baabii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is making small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the whorl?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by fall armyworm caterpillars feeding on the growing center of the corn plant. Catching them early with appropriate treatments stops them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi ni yeɔ ŋmei tso ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Kɛji okwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, obaanyɛ otsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and curl up during heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain and high humidity cause fungal diseases like leaf blight to spread quickly on damp leaves. Spacing plants further apart lets air dry the leaves faster and slows down disease.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ blight, gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ baai ni mli efɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbi oya, ni ebaaha helai aje shishi sɛɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil moist longer during hot days, stops weeds from taking over, and prevents rain from washing away rich topsoil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the small flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when soil gets too dry, temperatures get too hot, or nutrients are missing. Consistent watering and adequate soil nutrients help flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I know if my cassava under the ground is ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Cassava is generally ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize crop to plant again next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only in the first generation. Replanting saved seeds from that crop results in much smaller ears and weaker plants in the second year.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni adu lɛ ha toi bibii babaoo kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ba yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I plant them out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside cocoa provides a natural leaf canopy that shields the young trees and retains soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Enɛ kɛ kookoo lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli baai ni buɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land produce fewer bags of maize when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize draws heavy nutrients out of the soil every season. Rotating your plot with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns vital nitrogen back into the dirt, keeping the soil fertile naturally without relying only on expensive fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa pɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot in the dirt before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when heavy rainwater collects around the roots in flat or poorly drained soil. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess water to run off, keeping the roots healthy and firm.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nu buaa amɛhe naa lɛ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers. Lifting the leaves off the wet ground also protects the plant from soil-borne diseases and mold.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛkwɛ bulb agboi lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why are the center leaves of my young maize plants showing small holes and ragged edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii kɛ amɛhe ni etse lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize foliage are typically caused by pests like fall armyworms feeding inside the growing shoot. Checking your crop early in the morning helps catch the caterpillars before they damage the plant's main growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɔmɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite hei titri ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly into the hole with my seeds when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ bu ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ midu?

english: Concentrated fertilizer touching fresh seeds directly can burn the seed and kill the tender sprout. It is better to place fertilizer a few centimeters away from the seed or wait until the seedling has sprouted strong roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni kɛ dumɔwui heei kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui lɛ ni egbe tsei bibii lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 2-3 loo amɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baatsɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when heat is too intense, water levels change drastically, or there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering early in the morning helps the plant hold onto its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu lɛ mli ŋwɛi tsake kwraa. aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes shrinking and curling up into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking sap from the undersides of the leaves. Removing severely affected leaves early stops the insects from spreading to neighboring plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. Baai ni efite waa lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ amɛshwã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and tall with tiny cobs when I put seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete aggressively with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures strong stems and larger cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I clear weeds while my crops are still tiny instead of waiting until the weeds grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni jwɛi lɛ agbɔ lɛ,.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and quickly steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil. Clearing weeds while crops are small prevents the weeds from choking the young plants during their most critical growing phase.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lɛ baatsi jwɛi ni tsiɔ tsei bibii anaa yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow big. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from environmental stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Keeping soil moisture steady and protecting plants from pests helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he amanehulu. loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: When heavy rains flood the soil, water fills up all the air spaces underground. Without oxygen, the cassava roots suffocate and rot, which is why planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu baayi shikpɔŋ shishi kɔɔyɔɔ he fɛɛ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Kasava shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why does putting dry leaves or grass around the base of my crops help them survive hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi wo mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around plants, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the ground too quickly. It keeps the soil cool, retains moisture longer, and eventually rots into natural plant food.
ga: Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ Tsei ahe, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching Enɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei niyenii

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and dry winds. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted next to them to block the heat and retain soil moisture while their root systems grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough light and food to produce strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tsei ni wa kɛ tsei wuji.

english: Why do dark brown spots appear on my tomato leaves during the rainy period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Wet and humid weather encourages fungal diseases like blight to spread. Raindrops splashing on the leaves carry fungal spores from the soil, causing spots and rotting the leaves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baai ni fiteɔ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce less yield even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger root systems than most crops, so they steal the fertilizer and water before your crops can absorb them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients you apply.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu dani otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: The small shoots, called suckers, take water and food away from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two healthy suckers allows the mother plant to focus its energy on producing a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains babaoo ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that can draw nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies and rots, that stored nitrogen stays in the ground to fertilize the next crop, such as maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛfite Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus damages the leaves, preventing the plant from making food efficiently and severely reducing the size of the roots you harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Akɛni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, efiteɔ baai lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahoo nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa shishifãi ni okpaa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: How do I know the correct amount of water to mix with crop medicine before spraying my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nu abɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofa afutu tso mli dani mikɛshwie nɔ?

english: Mixing chemicals requires following the specific dosage instructions on the container using a measuring cup. Adding too little water can scorch and burn your leaves, while adding too much water dilutes the medicine, making it ineffective against pests.
ga: Esa akɛ tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ anyiɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ tsɛnsi lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛtsɔ susumɔ kɔɔpoo nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu fioo pɛ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã ni amɛshã. yɛ be mli ni nu babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha tsofa lɛ afee mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves with small dark droppings inside the funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm infestation. The caterpillars hide deep inside the central funnel of the plant during the day to feed on the soft, growing leaves, leaving behind waste that looks like coarse sawdust.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm hela ko eba. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni amɛdara. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ ni ashiɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight without protection. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains to act as natural umbrellas to keep the leaves cool and retain soil moisture while the cocoa roots grow deeper.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli kɛji akɛ abuuu amɛhe. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo koni amɛha baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if my maize crop does not get rain when the tassels start showing at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mi-abele lɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: The tasseling stage is when the maize plant forms its cobs and grains. If the soil is dry during this critical time, pollination fails and the plant produces empty cobs with very few grains.
ga: Brushing stage lɛ ji be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ nɛkɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ, Pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii ni tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko kɛ dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why are the yellow flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Flower dropping usually happens when the plant suffers from sudden water stress or extreme heat. When the plant becomes stressed, it sheds its flowers to conserve energy and keep the main stem alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji nu he haomɔ ni baa trukaa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ba tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei miihao lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni eha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I not pour fertilizer directly against the stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can burn the stem and kill the tender roots near the surface. It should always be applied in a ring a few inches away from the stem where the outer roots can safely feed on it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ahe ni efite shishifãi bibii ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛtsu nii be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ ŋta lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi. Ehi akɛ ayeɔ kponɔgbɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts together with my maize help my land grow better crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant decays, this nitrogen turns into natural fertilizer in the soil, which helps heavy-feeding crops like maize grow taller and produce larger cobs.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei fite Nitrogen nɛɛ bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa wuji.

english: Planted too tightly, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition causes the plants to grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in smaller cobs and a lower overall harvest.
ga: adu babaoo tsɔ Tsei kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after I clear my land with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dade shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Slashing only removes the top green part of the weed, leaving the roots untouched under the ground. Many weeds quickly send up new shoots from these live roots, especially after a fresh rainfall.
ga: Slashing jieɔ jwɛi lɛ ŋwɛi fã ni ji eŋɔli lɛ pɛ. ni etaaa shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Jwɛi babaoo kwɛɔ ŋmeii heei kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni hiɛ ka nɛɛ amli oya. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ hee sɛɛ

english: Why does it take so many years for my young cocoa trees to start producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to build a strong root system and sturdy branches capable of supporting heavy pods. With proper weeding, shade management, and care, young cocoa trees usually start fruiting within three to five years.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ niji ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ekwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei bibii jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ mli.

english: How long do I need to wait after planting before my oil palm trees produce palm kernels?
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii ogbe naa lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani okɛ ŋmei dumɔwui aba?

english: Oil palm trees generally take about three to four years after field planting to produce their first fruit bunches containing palm kernels. Regular weeding and fertilizing during these early years ensure healthy, high-yielding trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu mu tsei yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, amɛheɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani amɛfeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ tsei akui. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Enɛɛmɛi baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Can I grow oil palm trees alongside cocoa on my land to make extra money?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu mu tsei yɛ kookoo masɛi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni maná shika babaoo?

english: Yes, maintaining separate sections for both cocoa and oil palm helps diversify your income so you can earn money from palm kernels and palm oil while waiting for or alongside your cocoa harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, mlijaa kɛha kookoo kɛ mu tso fɛɛ lɛ baaha oshika ni onáa lɛ mlijaa aya hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oná shika yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmei fɔ nɔ beni omɛɛɔ loo yɛ o-cocoa kpamɔ lɛ masɛi.

english: How do palm kernels generate income for a farmer compared to just selling palm fruit?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei dumɔwui haa okwaafoi náa shika? Kɛ akɛto ŋmei tso yibii pɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ he?

english: Palm kernels contain valuable oil used for cooking, cosmetics, and soap, while the leftover cake is sold for animal feed. Crushing and selling the kernels creates an additional, high-value source of farm profit beyond the outer fruit pulp.
ga: Mu ko ni jara wa ni akɛhooɔ nii, tsofai kɛ samla yɛ palm ŋmeii amli, ni ahɔ̃ɔ keeki ni eshwɛ lɛ akɛ kooloi aniyenii. Dumɔwui lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛhɔ̃ɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli sɛɛnamɔ kroko ni he hiaa baa. Kɛfata aduawai lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ he lɛ

english: Is there a standard way to plant cocoa that works on any farm in Ghana?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ kookoo ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, using proper recommended spacing (usually 3 meters by 3 meters), creating temporary shade with plantains, and applying correct weed control works reliably across different soils and regions in Ghana.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ nɔ (bei pii lɛ mitai 3 x mitai 3), ni akɛ plantains feɔ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo. Ni jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aná yibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ shikpɔji kɛ kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ yɛ Ghana.

english: What basic steps do I need to follow to get maximum yield from my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi titrii esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: To get high yields, you must prune dead or overcrowded branches, clear weeds regularly, apply fertilizer to feed the soil, and spray to protect your pods from pests like capsids and black pod disease.
ga: koni onine ashɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ Ehe miihia ni ofo tsei niji ni egboi loo nɔ ni egbɔjɔ tsɔ lɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe daa. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. Ni okɛ tsofa awo mli koni obu o-pods lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids kɛ black pod hela lɛ ahe.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but many drop off due to incomplete pollination, dry weather stress, or limited nutrients. Proper pruning, shading, and soil feeding help the tree retain more developing pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ pollination ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ hewɔ. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ Tso lɛ he ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni akɛhaa hulutsoo, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ayibɔ babaoo mli.

english: Why do cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during hot, dry weather to reduce water loss and protect themselves from drought. Planting shade trees or plantains alongside cocoa protects young and mature trees from extreme heat.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni obu ohe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii kɛ wuji ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: What causes oil palm fruits to turn bad and fall off before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa oil palm yibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa?

english: Premature fruit drop in oil palms is usually caused by severe drought, nutrient shortages in the soil, or fungal diseases. Keeping the base of the palm clear and supplying adequate nutrients helps prevent fruit loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ mu tsei amli yibii ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baa. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ shishi tse ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa baaha lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni yibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do extension officers say that proper farming methods give the same good results on any land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ gbɛi ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ haa yibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baa yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi fɛɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Crops have universal biological needs for sunlight, water, space, and nutrients. When you follow proven agricultural techniques—such as correct spacing, pruning, and soil care—the crops respond with good yields regardless of the farm's location.
ga: Tsei yɛ jeŋ muu fɛɛ wala yibii ahe hiamɔ nii kɛha hulu la, nu, ŋwɛi kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji onyiɛ okwaayeli gbɛi ni ana he odaseyeli tamɔ ŋwɛi ni ja lɛ sɛɛ. ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha hetoo kɛ yibii kpakpai ekɔɔɔ he eko he ni ŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are healthy and producing as much as they should?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo bɔ ni sa?

english: Healthy cocoa trees should produce consistently high yields. If your farm is unable to produce up to ten bags of cocoa during a harvest, it is a sign that the trees are struggling and your crop growth is not progressing well.
ga: Esa akɛ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ awo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be. Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie kookoo kotokui nyɔŋma yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ No ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees failing to bring in a good harvest season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ wooo be mli ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Low harvests usually happen when the trees are neglected at the roots, attacked by diseases, or growing in poor soil conditions, which slows down pod production and reduces overall yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji aku hiɛ ashwie tsei anɔ kɛjɛ shishijee. Hela ko ni naa wa waa yɛ jɛmɛ. loo ni edaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ Enɛ haa pod lɛ feemɔ baa shi ni ehaa yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: What is a good benchmark harvest target to know my cocoa farm is doing well?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmaakpamɔ oti kpakpa ni akɛtoɔ he koni male kɛji mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ miiya nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A well-managed farm should aim for at least ten bags of cocoa per harvest season; anything less indicates that your crop management needs improvement to prevent financial loss.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, ebaaná kookoo kotokui nyɔŋma yɛ kpamɔɔ be fɛɛ mli. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni baa shi fe nakai lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni oya hiɛ yɛ bɔ ni okwɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ohaa lɛ mli koni shika akafite.

english: What does it mean to rehabilitate the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ mikɛ mi-cacao shishitoo lɛ baawo hewalɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Rehabilitating the base means cleaning up the soil area around the tree roots, removing parasitic weeds, improving soil nutrients, and treating damaged bark so the tree can feed properly and grow strong.
ga: Shishitoo lɛ ni aku sɛɛ akɛba lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaatsumɔ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ he, ni ajie jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli. Ha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni otsa tso lɛ yibii ni efite lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni eda waa.

english: How does fixing the ground around my cocoa roots help the trees produce more pods?
ga: ni ehiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Te mi-kookoo shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When the base of the farm is restored, the cocoa roots can absorb water and nutrients without competing with weeds, allowing the tree to direct its energy into growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aku sɛɛ asaa ŋmɔ lɛ shishitoo lɛ Cocoa shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ yeee akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees lose their productivity as the farm gets older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ yibiiwoo baa shi beni ŋmɔji lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Over time, soil nutrients at the base of cocoa trees get exhausted and overgrown brush can choke root systems, causing pod production to drop unless the farm base is actively restored.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ baafite. Ni tsei bibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi. Ja asaa ŋmɔ lɛ shishitoo lɛ kwraa.

english: When is the right time to start restoring the base of my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ shishitoo lɛ saamɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: You should rehabilitate the farm base as soon as you notice a dip in harvest yield or see that the ground around your trees is overgrown and failing to support healthy crop growth.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shishitoo lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛji ona akɛ okpamɔ lɛ eba shi pɛ. aloo kwɛmɔ akɛ he ni ebɔle ohe lɛ Otsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ adalɛ.

english: How can I prevent my cocoa pods from rotting or dying off before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite loo amɛkagbo dani akpa?

english: Protecting your crop starts at the base of the tree by keeping the ground clean, ensuring proper airflow, and managing soil health to stop fungal diseases from climbing up into the pods.
ga: Oŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni ooobu lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha ehe atse lɛ nɔ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya mli jogbaŋŋ. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ nɔkwɛmɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akakwɔ kɛbote ŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: What causes cocoa crops to suffer losses even when the trees look tall and green?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei lɛ naa amanehulu eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛhe tse moŋ?

english: Trees can look green but still produce very few pods if the roots are unhealthy or if pests destroy flowers at the base, leading to empty harvests and severe losses for the farmer.
ga: Tso lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ eŋɔli shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ lolo kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ waaa loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahiɛ. Ekɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛ fitemɔi ni mli wa baa okwaafoi anɔ.

english: Why is my neighbor getting more bags of cocoa from their farm than I get from mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nine shɛɔ kookoo kotokui babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛŋmɔ lɛ mli fe mi kɛjɛɔ minɔ lɛ?

english: Differences in harvest output usually come down to field care; farms that actively rehabilitate the base of their trees prevent pod decay and support higher bean production per tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli yibiiwoo mli lɛ damɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ahaa lɛ nɔ. Okwaafoi ni kɛ ekãa saa tsei ashishitoo lɛ tsiɔ pod lɛ fitemɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa nut ni fa babaoo yɛ tso fɛɛ tso mli.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves in maize are usually signs of nutrient shortage in the soil, such as nitrogen, or an attack by pests like fall armyworms. Adding compost or manure can help nourish the crop and revive its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ahe baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, bɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ etutua amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are suffering from a sickness or just dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛkɛ?

english: Dry weather makes leaves dry out evenly and drop off, while swollen shoot disease or pod rot causes strange leaf patterns, swollen stems, or black spots on pods that do not go away even when it rains.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni efuu loo ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, ŋmeii ni efuu, loo ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by bacterial wilt or root fungal sickness trapped in the soil. The sickness blocks the plant's internal water pipes, making the leaves collapse even if the soil is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ji bacteria wilt loo fungal hela ko ni ebote sũ lɛ mli. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.
