english: What simple steps can I take to save my cassava crop if a sickness starts spreading and I have no money for chemical medicine?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni ji nibii komɛi ni baaye abua mi ni makwɛ mi-cassava lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ hela lɛ bɔi gbɛfaŋnɔ ni mibɛ shika kɛha tsofa ni akɛ tsofa tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ hu?

english: When medicine is unavailable, you can cope by quickly uprooting infected plants, burning them away from the farm, and using only healthy, sickness-free stem cuttings for your next planting.
ga: Kɛ́ tsofa bɛ lɛ, obaanyɛ otsu he nii kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie oya lɛ nɔ. Shã nakai tsei lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he. Ni okɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela mɔ amɛ pɛ atsu nii kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can sprinkling wood ash on my vegetable crops help protect them from pest damage when I do not have spray?
ga: Ani tso sũ ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe be mli ni mibɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, wood ash acts as a natural protective barrier that irritates and smothers soft insects like caterpillars and aphids, making it a good low-cost way to reduce pest problems.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso mli sũ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni haa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli fuɔ ni eyeɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai shi yɛ shika helɛtemɔ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before growing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani eduɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme sun heat, improper watering, or poor soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save its strength until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hao amɛ. nu ni esaaa loo niyenii ni esaaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and twisted underground instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛtsi amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow twisted when the soil is too hard for them to expand easily, or when tiny soil worms called nematodes attack the growing roots. Mounding soft topsoil helps them grow straight.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo. Aloo kɛ́ sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua shishifãi ni miida lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋtayaai amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many days after spotting a sick plant in my field should I remove it to protect the rest of my farm?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ majie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni mikɛbu miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he?

english: You should remove a sick plant on the very same day you notice it. Delaying even for a few days allows insects or wind to carry the sickness to healthy neighboring crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ gbi nɔŋŋ ni oyɔse amɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ gbii fioo komɛi po sɛɛ fo lɛ, ebaaha kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ aŋɔ hela kɛya tso lɛ nɔ, ni enɛ baafite gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ.

english: Is it good practice to plant cowpea together with my maize in the same farm field?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛaadu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa?

english: Yes, cowpeas trap good air nutrients and feed the soil, which helps maize grow stronger. Cowpea leaves also spread over the ground to shade the soil and keep moisture from drying out quickly.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ niyenii kpakpai yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa. Cowpea baai lɛ hu gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekagbi oya.

english: How does changing the type of crop I plant on my field every season help prevent crop sickness?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsakemɔ daa be lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai akamɔ mi?

english: Crop rotation starves pests and sicknesses left in the soil. Sicknesses that feed on crops like maize cannot survive when you plant a completely different crop like groundnuts the following season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni hɔmɔ yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Hela ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa nyɛŋ ahi shi kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm in the Ashanti Region is loamy and good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ji sũ ni hi kɛha okwaayeli?

english: Loamy soil feels soft, slightly moist, and crumbles easily in your hands. It is neither too sticky like hard clay nor too loose like pure sand, which makes it perfect for holding the right amount of water and plant nutrients for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ. ŋmɔlɔ fioo ni efoɔ oya kɛ́ eyɛ nine mli Ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ tamɔ ŋã krɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni sa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atomɔ.

english: What kinds of crops can I grow if my land has good loamy soil?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ kpakpa?

english: Loamy soil is very versatile and supports almost all major crops in Ghana, including maize, cassava, plantain, cocoa, tomatoes, and pepper, because it provides a healthy balance of drainage, air, and plant food.
ga: Loam shikpɔji lɛ yɛ srɔtoi waa ni eyeɔ ebuaa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ. Nɔ ni fata enɛɛmɛi ahe ji ŋmãa, ŋmãa, plantain, kookoo, tomato kɛ ŋmãa ejaakɛ amɛhaa nu ni hoɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ tsei aniyenii ni sa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry out much faster in sandy soil compared to loamy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kwraa yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ akɛto ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large spaces that let rainwater wash straight through before crop roots can drink it. Loamy soil acts like a gentle sponge, holding onto moisture near the roots so plants stay green longer during hot days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni nugbɔ nu lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Loam tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important for me to plan my farm layout before buying seeds and starting to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ dani mahe dumɔwui ni mabɔi dumɔ?

english: Planning helps you match the right crops to the right sections of your land, budget your labor and money wisely, space plants properly, and prevent waste of time and seed.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo yeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ kpãa shikpɔŋ lɛ fã ni sa lɛ he. Okɛ onitsumɔ kɛ oshika ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ nilee mli. Too he ni abaadu tsei yɛ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni atsĩ be ni afiteɔ kɛ dumɔwui adumɔ naa

english: How do I choose which crops to farm if I only have a few workers on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni madu kɛji nitsulɔi fioo pɛ miyɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: If labor is limited, pick low-maintenance crops like cassava or plantain that require less daily attention, rather than delicate vegetables like tomatoes that need constant weeding, pruning, and spraying.
ga: Kɛji nitsumɔ faaa lɛ Halamɔ tsei ni esaaa akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei, ni ehe ehiaaa ni akwɛ amɛ daa gbi. Mohu ɔ, hla aduawai nɛ a he waaa kaa tomato nɛ biɔ nɛ a je jwɛi ɔmɛ a nɔ daa, nɛ a kpa mɛ, nɛ a ngɔ nu kɛ pue a nɔ be fɛɛ be ɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific plant food from the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli niyenii komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: How can I improve my farm soil if it feels too hard or too sandy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ kɛji minuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋã tsɔ?

english: You can mix in organic materials like decomposed crop leaves, poultry manure, or compost. Over time, adding organic matter transforms heavy clay or loose sand into rich, dark, loamy soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ tsei ahe baai ni egboi, kooloi afɔfɔi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii afutu mli. Beni be hoɔ lɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo ŋã ni etse ehe lɛ feɔ sũ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do plant roots grow much deeper and stronger in loamy soil than in compacted soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ daa ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Loamy soil is soft and porous, allowing young plant roots to easily push through and spread out to search for deep underground moisture and nutrients without suffocating.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ boteɔ mli oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛyatao ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni amɛtsiii amɛhe.

english: Is the land in the Ashanti Region naturally suitable for vegetable farming all year round?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ sa kɛha aduawai akwɛmɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, many areas in the Ashanti Region have fertile soil and good rainfall, but to farm vegetables year-round, especially in dry periods, you will need a nearby water source or basic irrigation.
ga: Hɛɛ, hei babaoo ni yɔɔ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo. Shi yɛ aduawai abɔɔ mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli Titri lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Obaasumɔ nu jɛɛhe ni bɛŋkɛ loo shishijee nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How deep should I push my crop seeds into loose, loamy soil when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli kɛyashɛ tɛŋŋ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: A general rule is to plant seeds at a depth that is two to three times their size. Planting too deep makes the seedling waste its energy trying to reach sunlight, while planting too shallow leaves seeds exposed to drying sun and birds.
ga: Mla ni yɔɔ ji ni adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ fe amɛdalɛ toi 2-3. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ afite hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he lɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ ni ehaa okpoi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Why should I use drip irrigation instead of just pouring water on my crops with a bucket?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ drip irrigation atsu nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ baagi baafɔ nu awo miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Drip irrigation delivers water drop by drop directly to the crop roots. This saves water, keeps leaves dry to prevent diseases, and ensures the plant gets a steady supply of moisture without wasting water on weeds.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaye abua ni nu akafite. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ koni helai akamɔ amɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be ni amɛfiteee nu yɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: What makes drip irrigation better for my crop's health than spraying water with a sprinkler?
ga: Mɛni haa nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ hi kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fe nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ?

english: Sprinklers spray water over leaves and open soil, which can cause fungal diseases and waste water through evaporation. Drip irrigation targets only the base of the plant, keeping the leaves dry and healthy.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ shwieɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ ni agbele nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ nu fɔŋ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ pɛ. Koni baai lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to dig a base hole around my crops when I am setting up irrigation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo bu yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ́ mikɛ nu miiwo mli lɛ?

english: A base hole creates a small basin around the crop's stem. It catches and holds irrigation water in place so it can sink deep down into the root zone instead of washing away across the field.
ga: Shishi bu lɛ feɔ ŋshɔ bibioo ko ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifã lɛ he. Emɔɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ni ehiɛɔ mli bɔni afee ni enyɛ ebote shishifã lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does water wash away off my field before my crops can drink it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu miiho kɛmiijɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midumɔ nii lɛ anu lɛ?

english: When ground is hard or sloping, water runs off before soaking in. Digging base holes or small mounds around your crops traps the water so the soil has time to absorb it for the roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo ejɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nu baajɛ mli dani ebote mli.Buji ni atsaa yɛ shishitoo mlai loo gɔji bibii ahe lɛ. Akɛ nu toɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná be ni ekɛjie lɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I loosen the dirt around my crop stems before watering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie muji ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ dani mawo amɛ nu lɛ?

english: Loosening packed soil breaks up the hard crust, allowing water and air to easily travel down to the root system rather than pooling on top or running off.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ mli ni etseɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli fãa. Enɛ haa nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli mlɛo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee poo yɛ ŋwɛi loo eeeho kɛya

english: Can I use borehole water that tastes a bit salty to water my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni ŋmei fioo yɔɔ mli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli?

english: Salty water can harm your crops and spoil the soil over time. If you must use it, methods like drip irrigation help deliver controlled amounts directly to roots to reduce salt buildup in the soil.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ baanyɛ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ ehe miihia lɛ, gbɛi tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni akudɔ lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛba ŋmei ni buaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi.

english: How does salty water affect the growth and yield of my crops?
ga: Te ŋmei nu lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Salt in irrigation water makes it hard for plant roots to drink, causing crops to look thirsty, turn yellow, and grow poorly even when the soil looks wet.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaanu. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni kumai miiye amɛ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ Ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ po.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, crops lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it. Ensuring water reaches deep into the root zone helps plants stay strong through the heat.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nu ni aaaha eho kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Is it bad if irrigation water stays standing around my crop stems for a long time?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ hi mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yes, standing water smothers crop roots by cutting off their air supply. This causes the roots to rot and can kill the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbe tso lɛ.

english: How can I stop the water in my plant's base hole from drying up quickly under the hot sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nu ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi bu lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi?

english: Covering the moist soil around the base hole with dry grass, leaves, or straw acts like a blanket, keeping the sun off the soil so moisture stays in the ground longer.
ga: Mulching shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni ebɔle Shishi bu ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo jwɛi ewo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he Koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: When bottom leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, your maize is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food that makes leaves green and healthy; without enough in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the new leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, no lɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ Tso lɛ baajie nibii lɛ fioo kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crop with dry grass help my plants grow better during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It blocks direct sunlight from drying out the dirt, keeps the plant roots cool, and holds water in the soil much longer so your crops do not dry up.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekagbi muji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni ehiɛɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ otsei lɛ akagbi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting fast-growing food crops like plantain gives the young cocoa shade, keeping the air cool and soil moist so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ Aloo niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha kookoo lɛ afee blɛoo. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tuber underneath the ground. Raising the vines on stakes gets the leaves off the hot ground, catches more sunlight, and prevents diseases from spreading.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baaha tsei ahe tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ. Na hulu la babaoo ni otsi helai anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot stems growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong stems, which allows the plant to produce a much bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Plantain muu lɛ fɛɛ baatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why does removing lower leaves from my tomato plants make the fruit grow larger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ajie shishigbɛ baai lɛ kɛjɛ tomato tsei amli lɛ, ehaa aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Trimming old or lower leaves stops the plant from wasting water and food on parts that do not produce fruit. The plant then sends all its energy directly into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai ni egbɔ loo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite nu kɛ niyenii yɛ hei ni wooo yibii lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rain falls for several weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ waa otsii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because heavy soil traps the water and suffocates the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away quickly so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do the flowers on my garden egg plants dry up and fall off without producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden water stress or extreme heat. If the plant does not get enough steady moisture while flowering, it gets weak and drops its blossoms to save its own life.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu mli haomɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa trukaa lɛ na tso lɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ be fɛɛ be beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, Ebaagbɔjɔ ni ebaagbee shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do tiny insect holes in the leaves of my pepper plants reduce the amount of pepper I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii abuji yɔɔ lɛ? yɛ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ, ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi

english: Leaves are like food factories for your crop, using sunlight to make energy. When insects eat holes in the leaves, the plant loses energy and cannot make as many peppers.
ga: Baai lɛ tamɔ niyenii nitsumɔhei kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji kooloi ye bu yɛ baai amli lɛ Tsei lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee chili ŋmeii babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves get curled and sticky with tiny green insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abɔleɔ ŋmãa baai ahe ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ?

english: Those tiny insects are aphids that suck the sweet juices out of the leaves. As they feed, they weaken the maize and leave behind a sticky substance that can attract black mold, hurting the crop's growth.
ga: Nakai kooloi bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ wuo mli nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ Amɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛshiɔ nɔ ko ni shwieɔ shi ni baanyɛ agbala ŋmãa diŋ. ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ awui

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo.

english: Wait until the rains become regular and steady for about two weeks so the soil holds enough moisture for seeds to sprout without drying out.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa ni ebaa shi aaafee otsi enyɔ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen nutrients, which you can fix by adding fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen niyenii. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my land if it used to grow crops naturally without it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Beni tsutsu lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they pull nutrients out of the soil. Over time, the soil becomes exhausted, and fertilizer puts those nutrients back so your future crops can grow big.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ nakai niyenii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni owɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes extremely hot or when plants suffer from water stress, which prevents proper pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking sap from the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays soaked with excess water for too long without good drainage, allowing fungal rot to take over underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ nu ni fa fe nine wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu kpakpa hoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi sũ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if the fall armyworm insect is attacking my corn field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ cutworm ŋmeii lɛ miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: You will notice ragged holes chewed into the leaves and dark, sawdust-like droppings inside the central growing funnel of the corn plant.
ga: Obaana buji ni ekpɔtɔ. Anaa baai ni ashɛre kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni miida lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce much less harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikpa nii fioo kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need to develop full fruits and heavy grains.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: Why do my maize plants need a different type of fertilizer when they start showing flowers compared to when I first planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi beni amɛjeɔ fɔmɔ shishi lɛ fe be mli ni midu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Just like animals need different food as they grow, young maize needs nitrogen early on to build strong leaves and stalks. Once flowering begins, the plant needs more potassium and phosphorus to form healthy, heavy grains instead of growing more leaves.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii srɔtoi he hiaa kooloi be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nitrogen he miihia abifao hu mra. Koni afee baai kɛ tsei ni wa Be ni esa akɛ aje fɔfɔii ashishi Tsei he miihia potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo koni amɛwo dumɔwui ni tsii ni wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehe baahia ni adu baai krokomɛi

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of big green leaves but fail to produce actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ewooo tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much leaf-building fertilizer early in their life, they spend all their energy growing tall and bushy. To produce fruit, plants need a shift in nutrients to signaling minerals like phosphorus and potassium that encourage flower and fruit development.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, amɛwoɔ baai babaoo tsɔ yɛ amɛshihilɛ shishijee mli. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. yɛ aduawai afeemɔ mli Ehe miihia ni tsei atsake niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni ekɛ okadi nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium. ni haa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai daa lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Why shouldn't I give my young cocoa trees the same fertilizer that full-grown cocoa trees carrying pods receive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni cacao tsei ni eda ni hiɛ ŋmeii lɛ naa lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa trees focus on building deep roots and strong stems, so they require nutrients suited for vegetative growth. Mature cocoa trees require extra nutrients specifically tailored to support pod formation, grain filling, and pest resistance.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ená niyenii ni sa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Cacao tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ niyenii krɛdɛɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ pɔtɛɛ koni eye ebua pod lɛ feemɔ. dumɔwui ni eyi mli obɔ kɛ bɔ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai

english: Why do extension officers tell me to apply fertilizer in two or three split doses instead of throwing it all on the farm at planting time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ 2-3 mli moŋ fe ni mashɛrɛ fɛɛ ashwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Plants cannot absorb all their lifetime food when they are small seedlings. Giving crops fertilizer in stages ensures they get fresh nutrients right when their growth demands change, such as during early sprouting and again during flowering.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli kɛ́ amɛji dumɔwui bibii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa wo tsei amli yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa niyenii heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛdalɛ he hiamɔ nii tsakeɔ, ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants stop growing big once small flower buds start appearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ beni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani ebɔi kpojiemɔ?

english: When a crop matures and enters its flowering phase, it naturally redirects its food energy away from producing new leaves and focuses on growing flowers and ripening seeds into peppers.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ da ni ebote fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Etsɔɔ niyenii hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli baai heei ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ he. ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa fɔfɔii ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ni akwɛɔ koni amɛfee chili ŋmɔtɔ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my plantain plants turn yellow and dry up when the fruit bunch starts coming out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: When plantains produce a fruit bunch, the plant mobilizes stored nutrients from its older, lower leaves and transfers them up into the developing bunch, causing the lowest leaves to naturally turn yellow and wither.
ga: Kɛ plantain tso lɛ wo aduawai akui Tso lɛ buaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ebua naa kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ naa ni ekɛyaa akui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do my bean plants drop their flowers on hot days without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: High heat causes stress in crops, making them conserve water and energy. If heat is too severe during flowering, plants will shed flowers to survive rather than trying to feed developing pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Ehaa nu kɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi. Mohu ɔ, a bɔɔ mɔde kaa a maa hla niye ní kɛ ha ŋmɔtɔhi nɛ a ngɛ wae ɔ.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings droop and look sickly right after I move them from the nursery bed into the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni hela mɔ amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Nursery beds shelter young plants from harsh sun and wind. Moving them to the open farm disturbs their roots and exposes them to bright heat, causing temporary transplant shock until their roots establish in the main soil.
ga: Nursery saatsoi lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ ko ni agbele naa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaahao amɛshishifãi lɛ ni ebaaha amɛná hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he shoofeemɔ baa be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Does my crop need the same amount of water when it is just sprouting as when it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Ani nu ni he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛkɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni he hiaa beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, water needs change as plants mature. Sprouting seedlings need light, frequent moisture for tender roots, while fruiting plants need larger volumes of water to plump up fruits and prevent drying out.
ga: Dabi, ehe miihia ni nu atsake be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ he miihia la kɛ nu ni mli edɔ shii abɔ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi blɛoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni woɔ aduawai lɛ he miihia nu babaoo koni aduawai lɛ ahi shi ni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do cassava plants need constant weeding in their first few months, but almost no weeding after half a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmeii tsei amli be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli, shi eshwɛ fioo ni ajie jwɛi yɛ afi fã sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cassava grows slowly and easily gets choked by weeds competing for sunlight and soil food. After several months, cassava forms a wide canopy of broad leaves that shades the ground and naturally blocks weeds from growing.
ga: Yucca bibioo lɛ daa blɛoo, ni jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ lɛ yeɔ enɔ oya. Yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, Cassava yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cocoa flowers rely on tiny insects like midges to transfer pollen from flower to flower. If there are not enough midges on your farm or if weather conditions prevent them from flying, most flowers will not get pollinated and will fall off naturally without forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii, tamɔ midges, anɔ koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii babaoo bɛ loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafo lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo bɛ pollination ni amɛbaagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: How does hand pollination help my cocoa trees produce more yields?
ga: Te nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Hand pollination involves manually moving pollen from one flower to another using small brushes or forceps. Because wild insects miss many flowers, doing this by hand guarantees that a much higher percentage of flowers get pollinated and grow into full cocoa pods.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ he ji ni akɛ niji ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ brɔsh bibioo loo pliers nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, koo mli kooloi bibii shweɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Enɛ ni akɛ niji feɔ lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli oha mlijaa 100 ni fa babaoo lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa flowers to dry up and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: During dry weather, cocoa trees try to save water to survive. If the soil does not have enough moisture, the tree drops its flowers because it cannot afford the water and energy needed to turn them into pods.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná nu kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do the local seeds I save from last year's harvest produce smaller yields than improved seeds from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved local seeds naturally lose their vigor over generations and can carry hidden diseases from the previous season. Improved or hybrid seeds are specially bred to resist diseases and produce stronger, higher-yielding crops.
ga: Kuu mli dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ he waaa yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aba. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ loo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do new hybrid crop varieties grow faster than the traditional local varieties we used years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni wɔkɛtsu nii afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds combine the strongest traits of two different parent plants. This gives them extra vigor, allowing their roots to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than traditional seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ kɛ sui ni mli wa fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ fɔlɔi tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli lɛ feɔ ekome. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhe wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui krokomɛi.

english: In intense afternoon sun, leaves lose moisture to the air faster than the roots can pull water from the soil. The plant intentionally wilts its leaves to reduce surface area and conserve water until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsɔɔ yiŋtoo ko nɔ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu nu lɛ he kɛyashi gbɛkɛ mli hulutsoo baa.

english: Extreme heat or dry soil causes heavy stress to tomato plants. When stressed, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy for survival rather than spending energy on growing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa tomato tsei anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ kɛdu aduawai

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize prioritizes new growth, so it pulls nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi sumɔɔ dalɛ hee. No hewɔ lɛ, egbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall and bushy with big leaves, but produce almost no peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji ni baai wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii ko kwraa bɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer makes plants put all their energy into leafy growth instead of flowers and fruit. Balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium encourages fruiting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛkwɛ baai yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Nitrogen kɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper crops turn yellow and rot when rainwater stays pooled on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the air inside the soil to survive. Standing water drowns the roots, preventing them from breathing, which causes root rot and turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu. tsiɔ mumɔ naa Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small when I plant them in shaded areas under large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ akwɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct sunlight to create food in its leaves through photosynthesis. When shaded, the plant cannot generate enough energy to store away and swell its root tubers.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii yɛ ebaai lɛ amli kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Beni eyɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛtoɔ shishifã lɛ he ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and stronger on my farm than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over centuries to thrive in poor soils and harsh conditions, allowing them to steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during storms right before the fruit is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli dani eyibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and become top-heavy as the heavy bunch grows. Supporting the main stem with wooden stakes helps distribute the weight and protects against strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei fiɔ ŋtayaa titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ejaraa muji lɛ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my maize when the rain comes unpredictably these days?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa? Akɛni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli hewɔ lɛ.

english: Rainfall patterns can change from year to year. Instead of planting on a fixed calendar date, wait until the soil receives at least one or two days of deep, continuous rain so there is enough moisture in the ground for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsake kɛjɛ afi kɛya afi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ gbi pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ Mɛɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: What happens to my crop seeds if I plant them in dry soil before the rains actually start?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ je shishi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Planting in completely dry soil can be risky because if a tiny rain falls and stops, the seeds may start to sprout and then die from heat and lack of water. It is safer to plant right after the soil is properly wet.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ fioo ni ekpa Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ hewɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear and prepare my farm weeks before the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni masaa he otsii komɛi dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ?

english: Preparing your land early ensures that as soon as the first proper rains fall, you can plant immediately. This gives your crops a strong head start to grow deep roots before weeds take over the land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akwɛɔ koni kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ, Obaanyɛ okwɛ tsei amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi dani jwɛi lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt so quickly during a short dry spell even after I have watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ewo mli moŋ.

english: When soil lacks organic matter like dry leaves or manure, it cannot hold water for long. Covering the soil around your crops with mulch traps moisture in the ground so the roots can drink even during hot dry spells.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa po lɛ, enyɛŋ ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like concrete when there is no rain for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ kɔnkrit be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard when it lacks organic matter and structural richness. Adding animal manure or decayed plant compost breaks up hard soil, allowing air, water, and roots to move through easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni wa kɛ́ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Koolooi amli ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo tsei amli ŋmeii ni akɛfataa he lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ shishifãi tsɔɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Can planting cover crops like cowpea help keep my soil moist during hot seasons?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cover crops spread across the ground like a natural blanket. Their leaves block direct sunlight from drying out the earth, keeping the soil cool and preserving moisture for main crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni gbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehaaa sũ lɛ agbi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa tsei titrii lɛ.

english: How can I water my small vegetable farm during dry periods without buying expensive water pumps?
ga: Mawo aduawai abɔɔ bibioo lɛ mli nu. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi nu lɛ atsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni miheee nu pɔmp ni jara wa?

english: You can use simple drip systems made from clean plastic containers or perforated hoses connected to water barrels. Gravity pushes the water slowly to the plant roots with minimal waste.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Akɛ plastic tsinsii ni mli tse loo paipi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu baagi ko feɔ nakai. Nibii ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ nu fiofio kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. kɛ jwɛi fioo ko pɛ

english: Why do my young crop seedlings burn and dry up even when I give them water every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Very young crops have delicate stems and leaves that can be scorched by intense, direct sunlight before their roots grow deep. Creating simple temporary shade using palm fronds protects them until they grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii waa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei ahe tsei fee be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Do my crops need the same amount of water when flowering as they did when they were young shoots?
ga: Ani nu ni falɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ amɛmiiwo fɔfɔi?

english: No, crops need much more water when flowering and forming fruits or grains. This is the period when the plant works hardest, and a lack of water at flowering can drastically lower your harvest yield.
ga: Dabi, nu babaoo he miihia tsei kɛ́ amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii loo dumɔwui. Be nɛɛ ji be ni tsei tsuɔ nii waa fe fɛɛ. Ni nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge green leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil or heavy rain early on can cause cassava plants to put all their energy into leafy top growth instead of storing nutrients below ground in the roots.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mra. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ebaa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my maize turn yellow and stay small if I do not put fertilizer in the soil when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi bibioo kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Maize plants are heavy feeders that need plenty of food from the very start. Fertilizer provides essential nutrients like nitrogen that keep the leaves deep green and give the plant the energy it needs to grow tall and produce big cobs.
ga: Abɛi tsei ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ shishijee. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do some farmers put fertilizer into the soil at the exact same time they plant their corn seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be kome too mli lɛ? Ni nɛgbɛ aduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ?

english: Putting fertilizer near the seed at planting ensures that as soon as the seed sprouts tiny roots, it immediately finds rich food. This early boost helps the seedling grow strong stems and roots quickly before weeds can take over.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe beni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ pɛ lɛ, shishifãi bibii baa. Obaana niyenii babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni akɛfataa he kɛjɛɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdaraa shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa oya dani jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young crops sometimes burn or dry up when fertilizer touches them directly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ baai lɛ shãa loo amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts. If it touches tender green leaves or stems directly instead of going into the soil, it draws water out of the plant tissue, causing the leaves to scorch and wither.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ baai loo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni eeebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni egboɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller corn yields after I plant on the same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmãa fioo beni midu ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Corn draws a lot of nutrients out of the ground. When you plant it repeatedly on the same land without adding fertilizer or rotating with crops like beans, the soil becomes exhausted and can no longer feed the plants well.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeee lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni enyɛŋ eha tsei lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil or get eaten by insects when I keep them inside my house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo kooloi yeɔ amɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo shĩa mli lɛ?

english: Grains stored at home often trap heat and moisture, which attracts dangerous mold and insect pests like weevils. Proper storage structures keep grains dry, cool, and sealed off from pests so they stay fresh.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ shia lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i mli. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii. Gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmaa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ mli egbiɔ, ehaa edɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli koni ehi shi ehee.

english: Why is it necessary for me to dry my harvested corn thoroughly before taking it to a storage warehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi kwraa dani mikɛto he ko ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ?

english: Damp corn rots quickly and develops dangerous molds like aflatoxin. Sunshine-drying the corn until the grains are hard ensures it will stay safe and high-quality for many months in a warehouse without spoiling.
ga: Abɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aflatoxins baa. Abele ni akɛwoɔ hulu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa abele lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni ehi jogbaŋŋ nyɔji babaoo yɛ nitoohe lɛ ni efiteee.

english: How does storing my harvested crops in a proper warehouse help me make more money?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni mikpa lɛ ni mikɛtoɔ nitoohe ni sa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná shika babaoo?

english: Right after harvest, everyone is selling and market prices are very low. Storing your crops safely in a warehouse prevents spoilage, allowing you to wait a few months and sell when prices rise.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbe naa lɛ, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hɔ̃ɔ ni jara lɛ baa shi waa. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ to nitoohe shweshweeshwe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekafite. Ehaa omɛɔ nyɔji fioo komɛi, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, kɛ́ jara lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my corn plants need specific spacing between each seed when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-abele tso lɛ aná gbɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: If corn seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for soil food and water, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another, resulting in weak plants with tiny cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛna niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why do my corn crops begin to wilt so quickly when the rain stops for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: Corn has relatively shallow roots that depend on moisture near the soil surface. Under the hot sun, topsoil dries out fast unless there is organic matter or ground cover to help trap moisture.
ga: Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni damɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baagbi oya. Ja nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ ni baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli lɛ yɛ.

english: Weeds are native plants that are adapted to survive in tough conditions, so their seeds sprout and spread roots instantly. Crops need extra care, good soil preparation, and early feeding to outgrow the wild weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tso lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa mra Koni jwɛi lɛ ada oya fe jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout if I plant them before the main rain season starts in April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ je shishi yɛ April mli lɛ?

english: Maize seeds need steady soil moisture to break their dormancy and grow. Planting into dry soil before regular rainfall begins causes the seeds to dry out, rot, or get eaten by birds and ants before they can germinate.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛfo ŋmiŋmi ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi, amɛgboi, loo okpoi kɛ ŋmeii aye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there are no plantain trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Fast-growing plantain trees provide canopy shade and lower surrounding temperatures, keeping the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain tsei ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava roots staying small and thin even though the leaves above ground look healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, uncompacted soil to expand into thick tubers. If the soil is too hard or heavy with clay, the roots cannot push through to grow thick, even if the plant gets plenty of sunlight.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli tse he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsii tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant conserve water and prevent drying out during hot periods.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. He ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he, ni ehaaa amɛgbi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience heat stress, extreme dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei baafɔ kɛji dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why does weed grass growing near my young maize turn the maize leaves light green and slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miida yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ masɛi lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-spreading roots that steal nitrogen and water from the soil before the young crop can reach them. Without enough nitrogen, maize leaves lose their deep green color and cannot produce energy to grow tall.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni juɔ nitrogen kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Abɛi baai lɛ hu fiteɔ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie hewalɛ ni fa babaoo kpo.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are mature and ready to dig up from under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and drying up. You can test a few pods by opening them; if the inside of the shell has dark brown veins and the seeds fill the shell tightly, they are ready.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka pods fioo komɛi okwɛ kɛtsɔ amɛgbelemɔ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ ebɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain suckers droop down during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves droop in high heat to reduce direct exposure to sunlight and conserve internal moisture. As long as the plant gets enough water in the morning or evening, the leaves will bounce back when temperatures cool down.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ baagbo yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi ni eha emli hulutsoo lɛ ahi shi. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi.

english: Why does adding wood ash from my cooking fire around my vegetable beds help the crops grow stronger?
ga: No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ tso sũ ni jɛɔ la ni akɛhooɔ nii amli ni akɛfataa Vegetable ŋmɔji ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa lɛ.

english: Wood ash contains potassium and calcium, which lower soil acidity and provide essential nutrients. Potassium helps plants build strong stems, develop healthy root systems, and resist common garden diseases.
ga: Potassium kɛ calcium yɛ tso mli ashwishwɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ acidity lɛ baa shi ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa ŋmeii ni wa. Feemɔ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ abɔɔ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe hewalɛ

english: When crops are planted too close together, they shade each other out and compete for limited soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to search for sunlight, wasting energy on tall stalks instead of growing big ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni faaa lɛ. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehe koni etao hulu la. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni afiteɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ yɛ ŋmãa toi wuji ni aduɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and drop off when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the soil gets soaked with too much water, the roots cannot breathe air. This causes root suffocation and rotting, which prevents the crop from absorbing nutrients and leads to yellow leaves.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ, ni no haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do crops planted in low-lying parts of my field die after heavy downpours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Low areas collect standing water easily. Most crops cannot survive with their roots fully submerged for long periods, so digging simple drainage channels helps excess water flow away.
ga: Hei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ buaa nu ni damɔ shi lɛ anaa oya. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo nyɛŋ ahi shi kɛji akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ bote nu shishi be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni oootsɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Is it bad to apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Ani ejaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: Yes, heavy rain can wash the fertilizer off the field before the plant roots can absorb it, wasting your money and leaving the crop without food.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa afiteɔ shika ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ niyenii.

english: Can leaving old crop waste and debris on my land cause problems for my new crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii momoi ni eshwɛ kɛ sũ ni efite yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ naagbai aba miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ anɔ?

english: Leaving old plants and rotting debris on the soil can hide pests and crop diseases, allowing them to attack your new seedlings as soon as they start growing.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei momoi kɛ sũ ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai ato. Ha amɛtutua odumɔwui heei lɛ kɛji amɛbɔi damɔ pɛ.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow when I plant them in hard, unplowed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Hard soil makes it difficult for young plant roots to push through and search for nutrients and water, which keeps the crop small and weak.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi akɛ amɛaatsɔ mli ni amɛna niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: If I pull out diseased plants from my farm, should I leave them on the ground between the crop rows?
ga: Kɛji mijie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ dumɔwui akutsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: No, rain splashes and wind can carry diseases from those dead leaves back onto your healthy plants. It is best to collect infected plants and burn or bury them far away.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai kɛjɛ baai ni egboi lɛ amli kɛba otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobua tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anaa ni ashã loo afu amɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and fall off during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves naturally when it gets very dry to save water inside their stem and roots until the rainy season comes back.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛgbi waa koni amɛkɛ nu ato amɛshishi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my maize plants staying short and pale green even though I planted them on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ kuku lolo ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ be naa moŋ lɛ?

english: Pale and stunted maize is usually a sign that the soil is low in nutrients like nitrogen, meaning the plants need compost or fertilizer to grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni mli tse ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ agbo.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster than my main crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are very strong and efficient at stealing water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil before your main crops can get them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ baanyɛ aná.

english: Can direct hot afternoon sunlight kill my delicate young crop seedlings?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ agbe mi dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Yes, hot sun can dry out and burn young seedlings before their roots grow deep enough to find groundwater, which is why temporary shade can help them survive early on.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni eshã dumɔwui bibii dani shishifãi lɛ mli aba bɔ ni sa ni amɛna shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Nɔ hewɔ ni be kukuoo mli hulutsoo baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi mra lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant it in hard ground without plowing the soil first?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Hard, unplowed soil makes it difficult for young plant roots to spread out and search for water and food, which leaves the crop stunted and weak.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko he nii lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable plants with dried grass help them grow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi duɔ mi-vegetables lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Dried grass acts as a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly into the hot air, allowing plant roots to stay moist longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds always grow back so much faster than the crops I plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds produce thousands of hardy seeds that stay asleep in the dirt for years, and as soon as you clear the ground and water touches the soil, those weed seeds wake up and grow before your crop seeds can catch up.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ woɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Ni kɛji ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni nu lɛ ta shikpɔŋ lɛ he pɛ kɛkɛ Nakai jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ baate shi ni amɛdara dani odumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do tiny insects appear on my pepper plants as soon as they start bringing out fresh flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛbɔi fɔfɔi heei feemɔ pɛ?

english: Insects are drawn by the sweet smell and soft tissue of fresh flower buds, which offer easy food and water for the pests as the plant enters its fruiting stage.
ga: Fɔfɔi heei ahe muji kɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ gbalaa koolooi. Enɛ haa niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe beni tsei lɛ boteɔ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cabbage seedlings wither and die when I plant them directly in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Baby plants have very tender roots that cannot drink water fast enough to replace the moisture their leaves lose under direct sunlight, so they quickly dry out without shade protection.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni nyɛɛɛ anu nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛto ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ laajeɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ najiaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya ni hulutsoo bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why is it important to use net covers or mesh over my young seedbeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ trellis loo ŋshɔŋloo baatsu nii yɛ mi-nursery saatso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Net covers act as a physical barrier that keeps heavy raindrops from beating down young seedlings while preventing flying pests from laying eggs on the tender leaves.
ga: Ŋshɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekatswa tsei bibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ kooloi ni fɔ̃ɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmeii yɛ baai bibii anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my green crops turning yellow while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei eŋɔli lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is starving for key soil nutrients like nitrogen, which plants use to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye oŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants look droopy in the hot afternoon but stand upright again by early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil, causing temporary wilting until the air cools down at night.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my seeds very close to each other to save space?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and ground water, resulting in thin stalks and smaller harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni akpaa nii fioo.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt season after season, making the soil poor and allowing specialized soil pests to multiply.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ohiafo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi krɛdɛɛi babaoo feɔ babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning brown and burning even though I added a lot of fertilizer to help them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiishã lɛ? Ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli koni eye ebua lɛ?

english: Crops have a limited capacity to absorb nutrients at one time. Giving them too much fertilizer at once overwhelms the roots and causes fertilizer burn, which damages the plant and prevents it from taking up food and water.
ga: Tsei bɛ nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be kome mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aye nɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashã. Enɛ fiteɔ tsei ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants grow very big while others right next to them stay small, even when I give them the same manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi miida waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ha amɛ po.

english: Just like people, individual plants have different capacities to absorb nutrients depending on their root strength and health. Giving every plant the exact same amount doesn't always mean they will absorb it equally.
ga: same as humans Tsei srɔtoi yɛ nyɛmɔi srɔtoi ni amɛkɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Edamɔ shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei fɛɛ ha lɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ, no etsɔɔɔ akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ amɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Can giving too much manure or fertilizer to my pepper plants actually reduce the number of peppers I harvest?
ga: Ani mi-pepper tsei lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ amɛmli loo mikɛwoɔ amɛmli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes. Over-assisting your plants with excess food causes them to put all their energy into growing thick leaves instead of producing and supporting healthy fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛ́ aye tso lɛ niyenii fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ baai ni mli tse ni miida lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ yiblii kpakpahi nɛ e woɔ nɔ he wami.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so my crops actually absorb it instead of wasting it?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aŋɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ moŋ fe ni eeefite?

english: The best time is when the plant is actively growing and the soil is moist, usually a few weeks after germination or just before flowering. Applying fertilizer at the right moment ensures the roots are ready to take in the nutrients.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be mli ni tsei lɛ miida ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ loo dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaasaa shishifãi lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai.

english: How can I make sure I am giving my crops just the right amount of fertilizer without guessing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miiwo miŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ bɔ ni sa mli ni misusuuu he?

english: Using precise measurement tools—such as a specific bottle cap of fertilizer per plant—ensures you feed your crops according to what their roots can actually absorb without damaging them.
ga: Kɛ susumɔ dɛŋdadei pɔtɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii, tamɔ tɔ mli ŋmɔshi nii pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso fɛɛ tso mli. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ ooha tsei lɛ niyenii ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni efiteee tsei lɛ.

english: How can I tell by looking at the leaves and fruits of my crops if they are getting enough food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛtsɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛyibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ nɔ akɛ amɛmiiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Your crops show clear signs on top. Pale or yellowing leaves often mean the plant is hungry, while dark green leaves with falling fruits or burnt leaf tips mean the plant has been over-fed or stressed.
ga: Akadi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋwɛi. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai eŋɔli ni aduawai egbee shi loo baa lɛ naagbee shãa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eye niyenii fe nine loo eyɛ haomɔ.

english: Why are the flowers and tiny fruits on my tomato plants dropping off before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii No hewɔ lɛ yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ amɛgbee shi dani amɛdara.

english: Fruit drop happens when a plant is overloaded or stressed—often from too much fertilizer or irregular watering—causing it to shed its top fruits because it cannot absorb enough resources to support them.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ he ejɔ fe nine loo ehao. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Amɛgbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaha nakai tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my yam plants grow very bushy vines on top but produce only small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ wain tsei babaoo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e woɔ bulb nyafii pɛ ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: When crops receive too much fertilizer early in their growth, they spend all their energy building top leaves and vines rather than storing nutrients down in the tubers.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ ná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baato eyitso lɛ mli lɛ

english: Should I feed my young seedling crops the same amount of fertilizer as my mature crops that are fruiting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha tsei bibii lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei ni eda ni woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: No. Young plants have smaller root systems with lower absorption capacity. They need smaller, precise doses, while mature plants producing fruit require higher amounts of nutrients to support their top growth.
ga: Dabi, tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ faaa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu. Amɛbiɔ tsofai bibii ni ja jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni eda ni woɔ yibii lɛ biɔ niyenii babaoo koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does heavy rain after applying fertilizer seem to stop my crops from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haaa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Excess water can wash nutrients past the roots or saturate the soil so much that roots cannot breathe. When roots cannot breathe, they lose their ability to absorb the nutrients in the soil.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nu aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Ebaafee nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaaŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What does it mean when people talk about applying a 'base' fertilizer before or during planting?
ga: Kɛ́ mɛi miiwie ‘shishijee’ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli dani aduɔ loo yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ he lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: Base or basal fertilizer is applied to the soil before planting or right at planting time. It mixes into the soil to feed the early root system so your young crops have immediate nutrients as soon as they sprout.
ga: Okɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii loo shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani odu loo yɛ dumɔ be mli. Akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha shishifãi lɛ niyenii yɛ eshishijee fãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aná niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What is the proper step-by-step order for applying fertilizers to my crops from start to finish?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛjɛɔ shishijee kɛyashiɔ naagbee?
