english: You typically begin with a base fertilizer at planting to support early root growth, followed by top-dressing fertilizers like NPK a few weeks later to support leaf and crop growth, and finally specialized nutrients during flowering or fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ adalɛ mra. Nyiɛmɔ sɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi tamɔ NPK yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ koni eye ebua baa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ. Ni naagbee lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ yɛ fɔfɔi loo yibiiwoo be mli.

english: How deep into the soil should I bury my fertilizer so my crop roots can reach it easily?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he oya?

english: Fertilizer should be placed about 3 to 5 centimeters deep near the plant roots and covered with soil. This prevents heavy rains from washing it away and stops the heat of the sun from reducing its effectiveness.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shɔŋŋ sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni akɛ sũ aha nɔ. Enɛ ji koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafɔ otadei lɛ. ni etsĩ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ naa koni ekaha nitsumɔ lɛ aba shi

english: What is NPK fertilizer, and what specific work does it do for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi eyɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: NPK stands for Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium. Nitrogen builds green leaves and strong stems, Phosphorus develops healthy roots, and Potassium helps your crops resist diseases and produce heavy fruits.
ga: NPK damɔ shi kɛha naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam. Nitrogen feɔ baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei ni wa. Fosforo haa shishifãi ni mli wa baa. Ni potassium yeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my crops turning yellow even though I clear weeds regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mishwieɔ jwɛi daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying an NPK fertilizer provides the necessary nitrogen to restore the green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha nitrogen ni he hiaa koni ekɛha tsei lɛ ahiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I apply too much NPK fertilizer at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii yɛ be kome mli?

english: Over-applying NPK fertilizer can 'burn' your crop roots and leaves due to high chemical salt concentration. This turns leaf tips brown, stunts plant growth, and can even kill the crop.
ga: NPK ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ‘ashã’ otsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai. Ejaakɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ ashishigbɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. etsĩɔ tsei adalɛ naa, ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii po.

english: How long does NPK fertilizer stay in the soil to feed my crops after I apply it?
ga: Be enyiɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii beni mikɛwo mli sɛɛ?

english: Once NPK dissolves into the soil with water, it actively feeds your crops for at least one month, during which you will notice faster growth and healthier leaves.
ga: Kɛ NPK lɛ kɛ nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaaha onibii lɛ niyenii kɛ hoo lɛ nyɔŋ kome. Yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, obaana akɛ amɛdaraa oya ni amɛbaa lɛ hu yɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why can't I just put all the fertilizer my farm needs on the day I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa miŋmɔ lɛ awo mli yɛ gbi ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young plants cannot consume large amounts of fertilizer at once. Applying everything at planting means heavy rains will wash away the excess nutrients before the crops are big enough to use them.
ga: Tsei bibii nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo shikome. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ dani tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii.

english: Will fertilizer still work for my crops if there is no rain after I apply it?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baatsu nii lolo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ beni mikɛwo mli sɛɛ?

english: No, solid fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so crop roots can drink it up. Without water or rain, the fertilizer stays dry in the soil and cannot help the plant grow.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa lɛ he miihia ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛji nu loo nugbɔ bɛ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi ni egbiɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei ni amɛdara.

english: How many times do I need to give fertilizer to my crops during one farming season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be kome mli?

english: Most short-term crops need at least two applications: a base fertilizer application at planting, and a second top-dressing application with NPK about four to six weeks later when the crops are growing fast.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo biɔ ni akɛ nibii enyɔ atsu nii: shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ; kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ ni akɛ NPK woɔ mli lɛ aaafee otsii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ sɛɛ beni tsei lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Is it helpful for me to mix crops like beans and maize together in my small garden space?
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni akɛfutuɔ he yɛ abɔɔ bibioo ko mli Ani minɔ lɛ baaye abua bo?

english: Yes, planting beans next to maize is very beneficial. Beans absorb nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer to help your maize grow stronger.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shia ni masɛi lɛ. Abele he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Why should I clear weeds from around my vegetable crops while the plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi aduawai lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii waa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing them early ensures your young crops get all the nourishment they need to build strong roots and produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ni oootsi ohe mra Ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do seeds I planted in my backyard garden fail to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu yɛ mishia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, if the soil dries out completely before they germinate, or if the soil is packed so tightly that the delicate sprout cannot push through.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa dani ekwɛ̃ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ waa aahu akɛ tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ abote mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves during heavy rains often mean the soil is waterlogged. Excessive water drowns the roots, making it impossible for them to breathe and draw up nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi. Enɛ haaa anyɛ amu ni ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience stress, usually caused by extreme heat, inconsistent watering, or a lack of key nutrients in the soil like calcium and potassium.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli nibii titrii tamɔ calcium kɛ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomatoes get dark, rotten spots on the bottom while they are still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Dark spots on the bottom of growing tomatoes are caused by a condition called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant lacks calcium or experiences irregular watering, which prevents calcium from reaching the developing fruit.
ga: Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato ni adu lɛ shishi lɛ baa. Ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haaa calcium lɛ ayashɛ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain plant turning brown and drying up while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Older plantain leaves at the bottom naturally turn brown and dry up as the plant matures. The plant redirects its energy and nutrients upward toward developing new green leaves and forming the fruit bunch.
ga: Plantain baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaagbi be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Tsei tsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛfeɔ aduawai akui.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is suffering from a lack of water during a dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu ni faaa yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: When maize plants are thirsty, their leaves roll inward like narrow tubes during the hottest part of the day to conserve moisture. If the leaves stay wide and open in midday heat, the plants have sufficient water.
ga: Kɛ́ kumai ye ŋmãa tsei lɛ Ebaai lɛ shwieɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa bibioo ko. yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi Kɛji baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbele yɛ gbi lɛ mli Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How does adding organic compost help my crops grow better than using plain dirt?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?

english: Compost works like a natural sponge that holds moisture around the roots while keeping the soil loose. It also continuously releases essential organic food that feeds your crops over time.
ga: Kɔmpost tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji, ni emɔɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ bɔɔ nii amli ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be lɛ hu kpo.

english: Why do some of my crops need direct hot sunlight while others prefer to grow under tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tɛ̃ɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tsei ashishi lɛ?

english: Sun-loving crops like maize and tomatoes require direct light to create the heavy energy needed for producing fruit. Shade-loving crops like cocoyam have sensitive leaves that scorch in direct sun and thrive best in filtered light.
ga: Tsei ni sumɔɔ hulu tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ tomato he miihia la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni tsii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai afeemɔ. Tsei ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ kookoo yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. ni edaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ la ni ajieɔ mli lɛ mli

english: How do I know which trees to cut down when preparing my land for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni esa akɛ mafo beni miisaa kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: When preparing land for cocoa, you should cut down large, thick-canopy trees that block all sunlight, but leave a few beneficial shade trees to protect young cocoa plants from harsh sun and direct wind.
ga: Kɛji oosaa he ni abaadu kookoo yɛ lɛ Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei wuji ni ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsiɔ hulu la fɛɛ naa lɛ. Shi shi tsei fioo komɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ he. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ

english: Does clearing all the big trees from my field help my young crops grow faster?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya?

english: No, removing every tree leaves young crops exposed to intense heat and hot winds, which dries out the soil quickly and can scorch delicate seedlings like cocoa.
ga: Dabi, tso fɛɛ tso ni afoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya, ni ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo.

english: What is the very first step I should take when setting up a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ ni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ miito kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: The first step is clearing the weed underbrush and planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava to create a protected environment before planting your delicate cocoa seedlings.
ga: Nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni esa akɛ afee ji ni ajie jwɛi tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Koni afee shihilɛ ni abuɔ he dani okɛ o-cocoa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ adu

english: Why do extension officers tell me to prune or cut back branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ofolɔ loo ofolɔ kookoo niji lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches so sunlight and air can reach inside the tree, which stops fungal diseases from breeding and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ mligbɛ. Enɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ akafɔ, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo.

english: How do simple farm maintenance practices help protect my cocoa pods from black pod disease?
ga: Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha ŋmɔ mli saamɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua ni abu mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ black pod hela he?

english: Simple steps like removing diseased pods, clearing weeds around the tree base, and maintaining good spacing reduce excess moisture, making it harder for fungal diseases to survive and spread.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ Jwɛi ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akɛ amɛaahi shi ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is holding enough water for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You can test your soil by squeezing a handful taken a few inches below the surface; if it forms a soft ball without dripping water, the soil has good moisture for roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni oootsi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aaafee 2-3 inch lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi kɛha shishifãi lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if they suffer from lack of water during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nu bɛ amɛmli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves wilt, turn brown, and drop, which reduces their ability to produce food, causing young pods to wither and yields to fall.
ga: Kɛ nu bɛ tsei lɛ Baai lɛ baagboi. Etsɔɔ blɔfo ni egbeeɔ shi, ni no haa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi. Ehaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Can heavy rain hurt my cocoa trees and flowers?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aye mi kokoo tsei kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awui?

english: Yes, excessive heavy rain can knock open flowers off the trees, flood the roots so they cannot breathe, and create damp conditions where fungal diseases bloom.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ ajɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Nu ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ aahu kɛyashi amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops still fail even after I spend money buying fertilizers and chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mifite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ahe moŋ?

english: Inputs only work if applied at the right time, in the right amounts, and alongside good field sanitation; improper timing or unmanaged weeds will waste your money without improving yields.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hi kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli pɛ. yɛ falɛ ni sa mli kɛ hetsemɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fata he Be ni sa loo jwɛi ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha ofite shika ni yibiiwoo lɛ eyaaa hiɛ.

english: Can I use basic household pans or basins to measure and apply inputs on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shia pan loo sinki ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ asusu nibii ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ni mikɛtsu nii?

english: While pans can carry dry materials like compost, precise farm chemicals need specific measuring tools to prevent under-dosing or over-dosing, which can damage crops.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ pans baanyɛ atere nibii ni egbi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ, shi tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ nibii pɔtɛɛ ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe koni akakɛtsu nii fe nine loo akɛtsuuu nii fe nine. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell, which can dry out soil and scorch seeds that have just started to sprout.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni eshã dumɔwui ni miije shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of the exact same nutrients and allows specific pests to multiply. Rotating with groundnuts or cowpeas puts nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi feɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Officer, why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an important food for growth. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives the plants the strength to stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Applying fertilizer a few weeks after planting—once the seed has sprouted and formed roots—ensures the young plant can actually absorb and use the nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ—kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni amɛshishifãi etswa shi lɛ—eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need taller plants like plantains growing right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ aná tso kakadaŋŋ tamɔ plantain ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense tropical sunshine. Fast-growing plantains provide shade and keep the soil moist, acting as natural umbrellas for cocoa trees in their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛha kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: When too many shoots grow together, they fight for the same soil water and nutrients. Removing extra shoots leaves one main plant to get all the energy, resulting in bigger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa tso titri kome mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ yɛ jwɛi wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the air, off the damp ground, which prevents leaf rot and helps tubers grow large.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. kponɔgbɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekafite ni eye ebua bulbs lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: How do I know if my cassava plants are growing tubers underground or just big leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii loo baai wuji kɛkɛ?

english: Healthy green leaves manufacture food using sunlight and send it down to store as starch in the roots. If the leaves are healthy and free of pests, the plant is actively building large cassava tubers underground.
ga: Baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa shi koni akɛto akɛ starch yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miifee ŋmei shishifãi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants suffer from excessive heat, sudden dry soil, or attacks from tiny insects. Keeping the soil moist with mulch protects the flowers so they can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Trukaa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi. loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii adɛŋ Kɛ́ okɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking the juices from fresh shoots. Spraying neem oil solution or approved farm medicine gets rid of the insects so new leaves can grow flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo ŋmɔ mli tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi bibii lɛ koni baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Without shade crops like plantain or tall trees to shield them, their leaves lose water faster than their roots can absorb it, causing them to burn and dry out.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei kakadaji ni buɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ, Amɛbaai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛshãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow starting from the middle to the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for green growth. When nitrogen is lacking in the soil, the plant pulls it from older leaves to feed newer growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my pepper plants wilting and dying even though the soil around them is very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ waa moŋ lɛ?

english: Too much water standing around the roots stops them from breathing and causes root rot. When roots rot, they can no longer send water up to the rest of the plant, making it wilt as if it were in a drought.
ga: nu ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Shishifãi babaoo tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkamu ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ egbo lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo nu kɛya tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ tamɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava cuttings too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the roots compete underground for space, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin stems above ground and small, poorly developed tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu kɛ niyenii, ni no haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ bibii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii ni edako jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and space that your crops need. Even with good rain, your crops will grow slowly if weeds are taking away their food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ he ni otsei lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii hu baakwɛ̃ fiofio kɛji jwɛi kpata amɛ niyenii lɛ hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without forming fruit when the air gets too hot, when the plant lacks water during flowering, or when there is an insect attack damaging the flower stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahiɛ

english: Why is it helpful to trim off some of the lower branches on my garden egg plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mafolɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Trimming extra low branches helps the plant direct its energy into producing bigger, healthier fruits instead of wasting strength on leaves that are too close to the dusty soil.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ fioo fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni baai ni bɛŋkɛ sũ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sũ lɛ baafite lɛ,.

english: Does my cassava plant stop growing tubers when it starts showing flowers on top?
ga: Ani mi yucca tso lɛ kpaɔ bulbs lɛ shweremɔ beni ebɔi fɔfɔii shweremɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The plant does not stop completely, but flowering causes the cassava to send extra energy up into seeds and stems, which can slow down how fast the tubers grow beneath the ground.
ga: Tso lɛ ekpaaa kwraa. Shi fɔfɔi ni baa lɛ haa ŋmei tsuɔ hewalɛ kroko kɛyaa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. ni baanyɛ aha bulb ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why are small holes appearing on the young leaves inside the funnel of my corn plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ anɔ.

english: These holes are usually caused by caterpillars, such as fall armyworms, which hide inside the central leaves of the young corn plant and eat them while they are soft and fresh.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Akɛ amɛ teeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni ayeɔ amɛ be mli ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo.

english: Why shouldn't I spray liquid medicine or fertilizer on my crop leaves right before a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain will wash the medicine or fertilizer off the leaves into the ground before the plant has time to absorb it, wasting your effort and money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Hewalɛ kɛ shika ni afiteɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die if I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong direct heat. Leaving large shade trees or planting plantains keeps the soil cool and moist, acting as a shield against full sunlight until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei wuji kɛha hulutsoo loo plantains ni odu lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves filled with small holes and powdery dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds on the growing center of maize plants. Catching it early allows you to treat the plant before the worm destroys the growing point and ruins your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ adalɛ he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa otsei lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Controlling these pests early stops the curling and allows the plant to flower and fruit normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant groundnuts or beans on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil to grow. Beans and groundnuts are legumes, which means they naturally trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring fertility for your next crop without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃. Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Fertilizer feeds every plant in the ground, and wild weeds absorb nutrients much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds before applying fertilizer ensures your crops get the nutrients instead of feeding the weeds.
ga: Fertilizer haa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii. Ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya kwraa fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi dani awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai moŋ fe ni amɛaaha jwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often a 'false rain' followed by days or weeks of dry heat. Planting immediately means seedlings dry out before establishing deep roots, so it is safer to wait until the rains become consistent.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji ‘nugbɔ amale’, ni gbii loo otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi tsɔne titri lɛ

english: When too many shoots grow around a single plantain plant, they compete for water and nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the main plant gets enough food to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ dumɔwu kome Tsobii lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be tied up on tall wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and fungal diseases while exposing maximum leaf surface to the sun so the plant can grow big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛye amɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha hulu la ashɛ baa lɛ nɔ bɔ ni ooonyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody even when the plant above ground is tall and full of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji tsei lɛ? Tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ po kɛlɛ ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ baai.

english: If the soil is too hard or packed, cassava roots cannot expand easily. Loose, well-tilled soil allows the roots to spread and swell into thick tubers rather than remaining thin and hard.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee mlɛo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes during periods of high heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages tomato pollen, preventing flowers from being fertilized. When flowers fail to pollinate, the plant drops them to conserve energy, so providing light shade or watering early in the day can help protect them.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Ehaa fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen lɛ Tsei baashi amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha fɔfɔi lɛ mra yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Cocoa trees shed leaves during dry spells to conserve water, but severe leaf drop usually happens when young trees lack sufficient shade from larger trees or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shi bei pii lɛ, baai ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baa kɛji tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji lɛ adɛŋ. aloo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I remove some of the young shoots coming up around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many young shoots, or suckers, forces them to compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients, which results in smaller, lighter plantain bunches.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii amli fe nine Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa plantains bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small worms inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli buji egbɛ eshwã ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which feed on the growing centers of maize plants and weaken the stem if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa, ni amɛhaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and show yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that stops the plant from growing properly.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haaa tsei adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the roots underneath stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded, the cassava puts most of its food and energy into leaf growth rather than storing energy in big root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ. Cassava kudɔɔ eniyenii kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa ebaai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi wuji amli lɛ

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots while sitting in storage long before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ beni mita nitoohe be kakadaŋŋ dani nugbɔ lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Yams naturally go through a resting phase after harvest, but as temperatures rise, internal chemical changes trigger the yam to sprout seeking soil to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɛɛɛ shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ Tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli tsakemɔi woɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ koni amɛtao shikpɔŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are turning pale because of poor soil or because of lack of rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ?

english: Dry plants usually wilt and curl up during hot hours, whereas plants lacking soil nutrients like nitrogen turn light green or yellow starting from the lower leaves, even when the soil is damp.
ga: Tsei ni egbi lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛgboi ni amɛkpokpo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up in the field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds as close together as possible to get more plants in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes crop roots and leaves to fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients, producing weak plants with tiny or empty cob heads.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop to the ground without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when temperatures get extremely hot, when the air becomes very dry during Harmattan, or when the plant receives uneven amounts of water.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa yɛ harmattan beaŋ loo be mli ni tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees look weak even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for the tree to produce pods. Cocoa trees need specific nutrients to create energy; if the soil lacks key minerals, the tree struggles to move energy up into flower buds and young pods.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa bɔ ni tso ko baanyɛ afee tsɛŋemɔ helai. Cacao tsei biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ minerals ni he hiaa lɛ Tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ awo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli.

english: What does a liquid foliar spray actually do to help my cocoa crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ?

english: Foliar sprays are liquid nutrients applied directly to the leaves, allowing the plant to quickly absorb energy and feed developing cocoa pods faster than waiting for root absorption.
ga: Foliar sprays ji niyenii ni ji nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ oya ni ehaa niyenii haa kookoo ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ oya fe bɔ ni eeemɛ ni shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa flowers drop off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When a tree does not have enough energy or food reserve, it naturally drops flowers to protect itself from overworking, keeping only the number of pods it has the energy to support.
ga: Beni tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo niyenii ni fa lɛ Bei pii lɛ, eshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ nitsumɔ ni fe nine lɛ he. Ebaato pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ ayibɔ pɛ.

english: How does trimming extra leaves and branches help energy reach my cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa hewalɛ ni eshɛɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ahe?

english: Pruning removes dead or unnecessary foliage so the tree stops wasting food on unwanted growth and instead directs all available energy directly to growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii yɛ dalɛ ni ataooo lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ a he wami tsuo kɛ yaa kookoo tso nɛ ngɛ he wami nɛ a ngɛ he wami ɔ mi.

english: How do I know if a growth booster or chemical is safe to use on my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ko ni haa mɔ daa loo tsofa ko yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Always look for products officially approved by the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD), as they test products to ensure they help crops grow without damaging the trees or cocoa beans.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, taomɔ nibii ni Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) lɛ ekpɛlɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛkaa amɛnibii lɛ amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfiteee tsei loo kookoo yibii lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid buying crop chemicals from unauthorized chemical vendors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahemɔ kɛjɛ tsofai ajalɔi ni ahaaa amɛ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Unapproved sellers often sell fake or adulterated chemicals that can burn your crops, ruin long-term tree health, and leave bad residues on your cocoa beans.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nibii ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ tsofai ni ji amalei loo tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ewo mli ni baanyɛ ashã onibii. Efiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ. ni eshiɔ nibii gbohii yɛ o-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why does COCOBOD restrict which sprays cocoa farmers are allowed to use?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ COCOBOD tsiɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo okwaafoi anɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: COCOBOD regulates sprays to protect crop health and ensure Ghanaian cocoa remains safe for export, keeping harmful or banned chemicals out of the international market.
ga: COCOBOD kudɔɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hewalɛnamɔ he ni ekwɛ koni Ghana kookoo lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe koni akɛya maŋsɛɛ. Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara loo ni agu ni atsiɔ naa koni amɛkashi majimaji ateŋ jarayelihe lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the best time of day to apply liquid fertilizers to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ nu awo kookoo tsei amli?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is ideal because the leaf pores are open to take in the nutrients, and the mild temperature prevents the spray from evaporating quickly in the sun.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Enɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ egbeleɔ amɛhe waa koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ni hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ haaa nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli.

english: Can spraying my crop leaves completely replace putting fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Ani mitsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahe tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: No, leaf sprays provide a quick energy boost, but solid fertilizers added to the soil feed the main root system that builds long-term tree strength and deep root networks.
ga: Dabi, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ baa nɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ haa shishifãi titri ni haa tso lɛ he waa be kakadaŋŋ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: What are the early signs that my cocoa trees are receiving enough energy and nutrients?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-cacao lɛ miiná hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Healthy, well-nourished cocoa trees produce dark green shiny leaves, fresh leaf flushes, strong flower retention, and steadily growing green pods without premature yellowing.
ga: Kakao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni niyenii kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ baai ni kpɛɔ, ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ, baai heei, kɛ fɔfɔi ni mli wa. kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni daa be fɛɛ be ni amɛfeee ŋmɔŋ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa beans get moldy and dark inside after I dry them on my wooden mats?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmli feɔ ediŋŋ beni migbi amɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa beans need to be fermented in banana leaves for about six days before drying. If you skip or rush fermentation, moisture stays trapped inside the beans, causing mold to grow and ruining the taste inside.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ banana baai amli aaafee gbii enumɔ dani amɛgbi. Kɛji otsi ohe loo okɛ oyaiyeli fee fermentation lɛ Moisture lɛ boteɔ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmei daa ni efiteɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ kɔfe yibii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods so the beans inside turn out good?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ koni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahi?

english: You should harvest cocoa pods when their color changes completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn orange. Picking pods too early means the beans won't ferment properly, while picking them too late causes beans to sprout inside.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa cocoa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛhe su etsake kwraa lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni shwiemɔ blɛoo tsɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cocoa beans take so long to dry properly during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani egbiɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High air humidity slows down evaporation. Spreading the beans in a thin, single layer on raised drying mats and turning them frequently helps air circulate around every bean so they dry evenly without spoiling.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa la ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi. Gbalamɔ kɔfi yibii lɛ amli yɛ fã bibioo mli. Gbimɔ yɛ tsɔne nɔ ni otsake shii abɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ abɔle he. kɔfi ŋmei fɛɛ Koni dumɔwui lɛ agbi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. Plantain trees or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, giving the young plants the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai. Enɛ haa tso bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are my yam plants growing very long leaves and vines above the ground but giving me small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji kɛ wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much foliage-building nutrients like nitrogen, the yam plant spends all its strength building leaves rather than roots. Using balanced organic manure encourages the plant to store energy underground.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa baai feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai amli moŋ fe shishifãi. Organic ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What causes dark brown rot spots to spread across my healthy cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This rot is caused by a fungus known as Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet and dark conditions. Pruning excess leaves and removing infected pods from the farm helps sunlight and fresh air reach the trees to stop the rot from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod hela. ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ kɛ duŋ mli Baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii akagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Applying fertilizer or compost around the stem restores nutrient levels, helping the plant grow green and produce heavy corn cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baabɔle Tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and tough to boil when I leave them in the ground for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ ashi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ waa ni amɛhoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: As cassava plants grow older than 12 months, they turn their soft root starch into hard fiber to support the plant. Harvesting them between 9 and 12 months ensures the tubers remain soft and easy to cook.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tsei eye fe nyɔji 12 lɛ, amɛtsakeɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa koni amɛkɛye amɛbua ŋmei tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ehoɔmɔ waaa.

english: Why do the flowers on my chili pepper plants drop off before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from heat or lack of water. Keeping the ground around the roots covered with dry grass mulching helps keep the soil moist and saves the flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Shishifãi ni awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my fresh tomatoes split open on the vine right when they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato heei lɛ tswaa trukaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato skins crack when the plant absorbs a sudden heavy flush of water after a dry period. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, so watering your plants consistently prevents cracking.
ga: Tomato hewolo lɛ mli fãa kɛ́ tso lɛ shwie nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha ekagbala.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient plants need to make food. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure supplies the soil with the nutrients needed for the leaves to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe hiaa ni tsei kɛtsu nii yɛ niyenii feemɔ mli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa koni eha baai lɛ aya nɔ afee ŋmɔji ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does putting dried animal manure on my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure adds natural nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus to the soil while improving its ability to hold water during dry weather. It acts as a slow-release food source that keeps your crops nourished throughout the season.
ga: Manure kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ yaa hiɛ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo blɛoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: This leaf damage is commonly caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the tender central leaves of young maize plants. Finding them early allows you to apply recommended pest control methods before the pest destroys the main growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsuɔ nii dani kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ hei titri ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when excessive rainwater sits in the soil without draining away, suffocating the roots and causing fungal infections. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily and protects the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu babaoo ta shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni ebuɔ ŋmei lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as protective shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until it becomes strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa edɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: When pepper plants are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and small yields. Crowding also blocks airflow, creating damp conditions where plant diseases easily spread.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mli oya.

english: The small shoots (called suckers) steal food and water from the main mother plantain tree. Removing extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones ensures all the nutrients go toward making a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers) lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ahiɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ aya ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, inconsistent watering, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant retain its flowers so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ tomato lɛ mli.

english: How do weeds in my field reduce the final harvest I get from my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa naagbee ŋmaa ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that your crops need to grow big and healthy. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get full access to all the food and water in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot completely drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize pests and diseases to multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwraa. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ehaa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: How can I tell if a yam tuber is healthy and good for eating or selling before buying it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ dani ahe?

english: A healthy yam tuber feels firm to the touch, has clean skin without soft spots or wet patches, and shows no foul smell, which indicates it is free from internal rot or disease.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ amɛta he. Ha ohewolo lɛ he afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo ko bɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛhe bɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo mligbɛ hela.

english: Why do yams rot quickly after harvest, and how can I keep them fresh longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya lɛ? Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yams rot when left in hot, damp places or directly on damp soil; storing them off the ground on raised bamboo racks in a well-ventilated shade barn prevents moisture buildup and spoilage.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji ashi yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛto shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ fitemɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots even when they are not in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Yams naturally break their sleeping period after a few months and use the water inside the tuber to sprout, which can be slowed down by keeping them in a cool, dark place.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be lɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ ni amɛkɛ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Abaanyɛ aha enɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛtsɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni duŋ ewo mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do yams need to be planted on raised soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu sweet potatoes yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen the soil so roots can expand into large tubers easily, while also draining away excess rainwater so the tubers do not sit in water and rot.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shwiemɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ akahi nu mli ni amɛkagbo.

english: Is it harmful to leave my harvested maize cobs lying directly on the bare ground?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ mashi mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, leaving maize on the ground allows soil moisture and insects to enter the cobs, which quickly causes mold, grain darking, and crop loss.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii abote ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ mli ŋmãa baa ni efiteɔ ŋmãa oya

english: How can I check if my harvested maize is dry enough to store in sacks safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto kotokui amli shweshweeshwe?

english: Maize is dry enough when the kernels feel glass-hard, make a sharp ringing sound when dropped, and cannot be dented with your thumbnail.
ga: Abɛi lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ mli wa tamɔ glase. Ehaa gbee ni tamɔ nɔ ni etswaa kɛ́ ashɛ shi ni esaaa akɛ ekɛ otsitsii shwieɔ shi.

english: What is the advantage of planting local Ghanaian maize varieties over unverified market seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa henɔi ni aduɔ lɛ he fe jarayeli dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Local varieties are bred to withstand local weather conditions and soil types, giving reliable yields and better resistance to native pests.
ga: Afɔ maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi lɛ anaa. Ehaa yibiiwoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do tiny insects bore holes into my stored dry maize, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These insects are maize weevils that feed on dry grains; storing your dried grain in airtight hermetic bags prevents them from surviving and destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni egbi. Dumɔwui ni egbi ni okɛtoɔ kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ haaa amɛhi shi ni amɛfite oŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate that heavy rains have washed nitrogen nutrients out of the soil away from the roots, which can be corrected by applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtee shishifãi lɛ ahe. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does measuring maize by volume using small containers give different results when selling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ akɛ tsɛnsii bibii tsu nii kɛsusu ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ, ehaa yibii sɔrɔtoi baa kɛ́ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Volume measurements vary because wet or loosely packed grains take up more space; properly dried and clean grains pack tightly, giving accurate volume and better grain quality.
ga: Volume susumɔi baasoro amɛhe yɛ dumɔwui ni efɔ loo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahewɔ. Eheɔ he babaoo Akɛ ŋmaa ni egbi ni he tse lɛ woɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsofa lɛ falɛ ni ja kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully ready to be harvested from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base of the plant starts to crack open due to the swollen tubers expanding beneath the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmei ni efuu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my plantain bunch is mature enough to cut for cooking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantains lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafolɔ kɛha niyenii?

english: Plantains are mature and ready to harvest when the individual fruits look plump and rounded rather than sharp and flat-sided, and the dry flower ends at the tips rub off easily.
ga: Plantains lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko egbɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ fãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi lɛ naagbee yɛ naagbee ni ajieɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do my new oil palm trees take several years before they start producing fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso hee lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi aduawai akui feemɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palms spend their first three to four years building a thick trunk and an extensive root network to store energy and support the heavy weight of mature fruit bunches later in life.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani amɛfeɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ shishifãi babaoo ni amɛkɛtoɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛyeɔ amɛbua sɛɛ mli aduawai akui ni eda lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ.

english: Can I still plant cassava and maize on the same piece of land after I plant young oil palm trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni midu mu tsei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, you can grow short-term food crops like maize or cassava between young oil palms for the first two to three years, but once the palm branches expand and create heavy shade, food crops will no longer get enough sunlight to produce well.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni heɔ be kuku tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. mu tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli Shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ mli gbala ni amɛfee hulutsoo ni tsii, Niyenii tsei lɛ naaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdu nii jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ.

english: How does switching my farm land from food crops to oil palm trees affect my soil?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii ni mitsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛyaa ŋmei fɔ nɔ lɛ saa mishikpɔŋ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Oil palms cover the ground continuously and protect the soil from heavy rains, but because they remain in the ground for over twenty years, they constantly draw nutrients from the soil, requiring regular compost or fertilizer to stay productive.
ga: Mu tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Shi ejaakɛ ŋmei fɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, mu tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii daa koni nibii ni anáa lɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning around the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily when exposed to direct, harsh sunlight without shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia to protect them while their tender root system establishes.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni tsei tamɔ plantains loo gliricidia bɛ ni buɔ amɛhe be mli ni amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow down the middle while the plant stays short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ yɛ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing down the middle of a maize leaf usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a key plant food that helps crops make green foliage and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil causing the plant to put energy into leaf growth instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upwards and twist tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ekome lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies that distorts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea and bean leaves fold up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas kɛ pea baai lɛ miifo ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans fold their leaves during the hottest hours of the day to reduce the leaf area facing the direct sun, which naturally helps the plant save water and stay cool.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Koni akɛba he ni baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and cannot withstand full, direct sunlight because their roots are small and cannot drink enough water quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees creates a cool canopy that protects young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa shade be kukuoo mli lɛ adumɔ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to keep vegetable seeds in a nursing bed before moving them to my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ aduawai adumɔwui ato helatsɛmɛi akwɛmɔhei lɛ dani mikɛwo mishikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny seeds and young shoots are very delicate, like newborns. A nursery allows you to give them special care, light shade, and protection from heavy rainfall and pests until the plants develop strong roots and stem power to survive in the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa, tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee. Gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ haa bo kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. Ha hulutsoo be ni mli tse ni obu he kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crop turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking food in the soil, specifically nitrogen. Rain provides water, but plants also need soil nutrients to stay green and grow strong, which you can fix by applying fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Titri lɛ nitrogen, nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu he miihia niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant maize on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnut helps put natural food back into the soil and breaks crop disease cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii baatsake Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekpa tso helai lɛ asɛɛkuu.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same farmland at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, cassava and maize are excellent farming partners. Maize grows fast and is harvested in about three to four months, leaving plenty of space, light, and soil room for the cassava to mature slowly over the rest of the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ji okwaayeli hefatalɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ, la kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ fiofio. yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops regularly instead of letting them grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ daa Moŋ lɛ, ha amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and water intended for your crops. Clearing weeds ensures your main crops get all the food they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my plantain leaves fold up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves fold up during hot weather as a natural self-defense action. By folding, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to the sun, preventing moisture from escaping and protecting the plant from drying out.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ akaje mli, ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress or drought. When conditions are too dry or hot, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy and water so that the main plant stays alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ mli baa lɛ he. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: What happens if I harvest my cassava tubers too early while the plant is still very young?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ mra tsɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Harvesting cassava too early results in thin, watery tubers because the plant has not had enough time to build up starch in the roots. Waiting until full maturity ensures heavy, firm, and starchy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei mra tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmei bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli ejaakɛ tsei lɛ bɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaafee ŋmei yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Mɛɛ ni ehoo jogbaŋŋ koni onine ashɛ yitso ni tsii, ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ.

english: How do I stop my seed yams from rotting before the next planting season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ akafite dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aje shishi?

english: Seed yams rot quickly when kept in warm, damp, or airless environments. Storing them off the ground in a shaded, cool, and well-ventilated traditional yam barn keeps them dry and prevents rot-causing fungi from destroying them.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni edɔ, edɔ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Okɛ sweet potato ato shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ blema sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha amɛhe agbi, ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ akafite amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants droop in the afternoon even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up from the soil. This temporary wilting is a natural defense to protect the plant from heat, and the leaves will normally bounce back by late evening or early morning.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa be kukuoo nɛɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plants do not get consistent water. High temperatures disrupt pollination, causing the plant to shed unpollinated flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Ha tsei afɔ fɔfɔi ni pollination bɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to reduce water loss. The plant is not dying; it enters a resting state and survives on energy stored in its underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tso lɛ gbooo, eboteɔ hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning dense branches to let sunlight and air circulate through your farm helps keep the pods dry and reduces the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's leaf funnel. Applying approved organic treatments like neem oil or recommended insecticides directly into the funnel early in the morning kills the pests before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ wo ŋmei lɛ mli leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmei lɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over at the base before the fruits are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miigbee shi yɛ shishigbɛ dani aduawai lɛ afee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when microscopic worms called nematodes or banana weevils destroy their roots underground. Without strong roots to anchor the plant, the heavy weight of the growing plantain bunch causes the stem to snap or uproot.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana moths lɛ fite amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni baaha tso lɛ ahi shi lɛ Plantains kuu ko ni miida lɛ tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akumɔ loo ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ ajɛ.
