english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips and moving down the center in a V-pattern indicates that your soil lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will restore healthy green growth.
ga: Yellow jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni etsɔɔ teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil with nutrients that make the maize grow stronger without needing as much synthetic fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmãa daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa seedlings cool and moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing short, twisted, and hard instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kukuji, amɛtsiɔ amɛhe, ni amɛhe wa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-drained soil to expand smoothly underground. If planted in compacted clay or shallow, stony soil, the growing tubers meet resistance and become distorted as they force their way through the hard earth.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Bulbs ni miida lɛ feɔ shitee-kɛ-woo ni amɛfiteɔ beni amɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for green leaf growth, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-decayed manure can help fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer helps nearby maize grow stronger and reduces the amount of chemical fertilizer you need to buy.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa, ni ehaa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow plenty of leafy green leaves but produce very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ pepper fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to put all their energy into leafy growth instead of flowers and fruits. Switching to a fertilizer richer in phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering and fruit set.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ he moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo aya hiɛ.

english: Which direction should I insert cassava stem cuttings into the soil for them to grow best?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted at a 45-degree angle or vertically with the growth buds pointing up toward the sky. Planting them upside down slows growth and reduces tuber yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu tsei ni afo lɛ yɛ 45-degree angle loo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ fioo ni ebaaha tuber yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as temporary shade umbrellas, protecting cocoa trees from harsh sun and retaining soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli shade. Buu kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and stopping the crop from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa tsei lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by tomato leaf curl virus, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. It can also happen when the plant experiences severe heat stress and drought.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the exact same field where I just harvested garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikɛ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwie mli kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and share the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them consecutively allows pests and fungal spores to build up in the soil and attack the new crop.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ tsei aweku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutua ŋmɔshi nibii heei.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their tiny flowers before pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani pods lɛ baafee?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrition, or attack by pests like capsids. Ensuring adequate shade and soil moisture prevents excessive flower loss.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Atutuaa sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite fe nine.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yams so they don't rot in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii? koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up. This signal shows the plant has finished storing energy in the tuber and stopped active growth.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ bulb lɛ mli lɛ naa, ni ekpa dalɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice crop require standing water in the field during early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ biɔ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ?

english: Shallow standing water smothers competing weeds that try to steal nutrients and sunlight, while ensuring the water-loving rice roots remain continuously hydrated.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ miɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni miitao niyenii kɛ hulu la he akaŋ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmãa ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why is it necessary to cut off some healthy-looking branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes crowded branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach the inner parts of the tree. This prevents fungal diseases, stops energy waste, and helps the tree focus its nutrients on growing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ mli. Gbɛ nɛɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa. Kpaa hewalɛ ni ofiteɔ lɛ ni oye obua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Should I cut off the thin shoots growing straight up from the bottom of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? Ani ajie nakai shweremɔ ni jɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, those vertical shoots—called suckers or chupons—drain valuable water and food away from the main fruiting branches. Removing them early ensures the tree puts all its strength into pod production.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ akɛ suckers loo chupons. Koni ejie nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ tsei niji titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli. Ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to trim my cocoa tree branches?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei?

english: The best time to trim cocoa trees is right after the main harvest season before the heavy rains begin. Light pruning done twice a year keeps the tree canopy open and ready for new flower growth.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei ji yɛ kpamɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ, dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli fioo shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ shishigbɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha fɔfɔi heei ni baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do flowers grow directly on the thick trunk of my cocoa tree instead of on the leaf twigs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? ni ji mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower on mature wood so the trunk and thick branches can support the heavy weight of full-grown cocoa pods without snapping under pressure.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ tso ni mli tse lɛ kɛ eniji lɛ baanyɛ aye abua kookoo tso ni eda lɛ muji ni tsii lɛ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli yɛ nɔnyɛɛ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do many flowers drop off my cocoa trees without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if tiny pollinating insects do not visit them, or if the tree lacks enough water and nutrients. Proper shade control and branch care help attract natural pollinators to fix this problem.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ eyasaraaa amɛ loo kɛji nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tso lɛ he. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ niji akwɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni egbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛbaa naagba nɛɛ mli.

english: Hand pollination means using a small tool or brush to manually transfer pollen from one flower to another. Doing this helps trees produce significantly more pods when natural pollinating insects are scarce.
ga: Nine nɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ dɛŋdade bibioo loo brɔsh tsuɔ nii ni akɛ niji jieɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi lɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo waa kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ faaa lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my growing cocoa pods turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pods turn black because of a fungal disease that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and overgrown farm conditions. Pruning excess leaves lets in sunlight and air, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Pods lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ hewɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce many pods one year but very few pods the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli shi ewoɔ fioo yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees become exhausted after a heavy harvest if they do not receive proper nutrients and care. Regular pruning and feeding the soil help the tree maintain a steady yield every season.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni wa sɛɛ kɛji akɛ ahaaa amɛ niyenii kpakpa kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ mli daa be mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and short roots that burn quickly in harsh heat. Planting shade crops like plantains near young cocoa protects them from direct sun and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: How does clearing weeds around the base of my cocoa trees help them produce more fruit?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Weeds steal soil moisture, fertilizer, and light away from your cocoa roots. Keeping a clean ring around each tree trunk ensures all soil nutrients go straight into feeding your cocoa tree.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ sũ mli nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli. Ni aaaha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he atse Tso lɛ shishi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii fɛɛ yaa kookoo tso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know which end of a cassava stem cutting to push into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes on the stem cutting. Plant the cutting with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the stems and leaves grow up properly and the roots form healthy tubers beneath.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. loo nodes bibii Yɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he mfoniri ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ Dumɔ niji lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi koni tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. Ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ bulb ni mli wa yɛ shishi.

english: How do I choose the right plantain shoots from my old farm to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantains ni sa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad bulb at the base. They grow faster and yield heavier bunches than shoots with wide, broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword bud’, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ yitso ni mli kwɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ kui ni tsii fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle harsh direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them protects their leaves from scorching and holds moisture in the soil.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip usually mean the maize is hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure gives the crop the nutrients it needs to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which gives them maximum sunlight and prevents soil-borne rot.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha ená hulu la babaoo ni ekɛtsi fitemɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme hot weather, dry soil, or poor nutrients. Regular watering and adding compost help the plant retain its flowers to form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛna haomɔ ni jɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni esaaa mli. Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by tiny whitefly insects that spread a virus, or by severe heat stress. Controlling whiteflies and keeping soil evenly moist prevents leaves from twisting and stunting growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli lɛ Kɛ́ akudɔ ŋmeii yɛji kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkakwɛ amɛdalɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight dry out the farm, and removing damaged pods keeps the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha hulu la ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Ni ŋmeii ni efite lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from washing away my farm soil on sloping ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting your crops in horizontal ridges across the slope rather than up and down slows down rainwater. This holds the topsoil in place and lets water soak into the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are tiny insects destroying my dried maize inside my storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi-abele ni egbi ni yɔɔ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Grain weevils lay eggs inside maize kernels, which hatch after harvest if the grain is not fully dry or sealed. Drying maize thoroughly in the sun and storing it in airtight bags or containers starves insects of oxygen.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmei fɔɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli. Amɛbaafɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa loo amɛtsiii amɛhe. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛto kotokui loo tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi lɛ ni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: Why should I use black plastic bags for my nursery seedlings instead of clear, transparent bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ plastic kotokui diji atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui yɛ kotokui ni mli tse ni mli tse lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Seed roots naturally need complete darkness to grow and absorb nutrients properly. Black plastic bags block out sunlight, protecting fragile roots from getting burned or dried out, whereas clear bags allow light inside which damages the roots.
ga: Dumɔwui shishifãi biɔ duŋ kwraa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛdara ni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ. Plastic kotokui diji tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Ebuɔ shishifãi ni waaa lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã loo amɛkagbi. yɛ be mli ni kotokui ni mli tse lɛ haa la kpɛɔ yɛ mli ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do young crop seedlings need a shade canopy over them in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa ni amɛná ŋwɛi ŋta yɛ ŋtayaa he lɛ?

english: Tender young sprouts do not have deep root systems yet to drink enough water. Shading protects them from intense sun heat, keeping the soil moist and preventing the young stems and leaves from scorching.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shading yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi tsei bibii kɛ baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã

english: How can I tell if my oil palm nuts are healthy enough to sprout before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-oil palm ŋmeii lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ dani amɛdu?

english: You can place the nuts in a container of water. Good, heavy nuts with healthy kernels inside will sink to the bottom, while hollow, damaged, or dry nuts will float to the top and should be discarded.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo nu tsɛnsi mli. Beans kpakpai ni tsii ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baagbee shi kɛya shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji, ni efite, loo ni egbi lɛ baafo kɛya ŋwɛi ni esa akɛ ashɛrɛ ashwie.

english: Why do my oil palm seeds fail to sprout when I leave them sitting in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji miha amɛtara shi yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palm seeds require darkness, heat, and moisture to break their outer shell and sprout. Leaving seeds exposed to direct light dries them out and signals to the seed that it is not in the safe underground environment needed for growth.
ga: Mu tso dumɔwui lɛ he miihia duŋ, dɔlɛ, kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛkumɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ ashi dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbi ni etsɔɔ amɛ akɛ amɛbɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ mli.

english: Why do some hard seeds need to be soaked in water before placing them in nursery soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ dumɔwui komɛi ni wa awo nu mli dani adu amɛ yɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soaking hard seeds softens their tough outer shell and allows water to penetrate inside. This wakes up the seed embryo and speeds up the time it takes for the seed to germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui ni wa ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ haa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa nu shwieɔ emli. Enɛ teɔ dumɔwu lɛ fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ shi ni ehaa be ni heɔ dani dumɔwu lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ yaa oya.

english: Why is it important to cover seeds completely with soil instead of leaving them on top of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aha dumɔwui anɔ moŋ fe ni aaashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Burying seeds under soil protects them from direct light, preserves essential moisture around the seed, keeps them safe from birds or insects, and gives the emerging root dark dirt to grip into.
ga: Kɛ́ afu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni bɔleɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ hiɔ shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ okpoi loo kooloi adɛŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa muji ni tsuɔ diŋŋ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe

english: How deep should I plant palm seeds in the soil so they grow properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛ ha tɛŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Palm seeds should be planted deep enough so they are fully covered by dark soil and protected from light, but not so deep that the young shoot exhausts its energy before reaching the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ aha amɛhe kwraa ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ la he. Shi jeee ni mli kwɔ tsɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahewalɛ baaho dani amɛshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ.

english: If full grown crops need sunlight to produce yield, why does direct light hurt roots underground?
ga: Kɛji tso ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la koni ekɛwo yibii Mɛni hewɔ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Leaves and roots have different jobs. Leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant, but roots are designed purely to seek water in the dark underground. Light damages delicate root tissue and prevents them from spreading.
ga: Baai kɛ shishifãi yɛ nitsumɔi srɔtoi. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha tso lɛ. Shi afee shishifãi lɛ koni amɛna nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi duŋ mli pɛ. La lɛ fiteɔ shishifã ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaaa egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why does dark, damp soil make seeds sprout faster than light, dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ haa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe shikpɔŋ ni mli egbi ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Dark soil traps gentle heat and retains humidity around the seed. This warm, moist environment triggers chemical changes inside the seed that tell it it is safe to break open and grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ waa lɛ hiɛɔ dɔlɛ ni mli jɔ fioo. ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi dumɔwu lɛ he. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ haa tsofa tsakemɔi baa dumɔwu lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ebaanyɛ ekwɛ̃ ni eda shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do seedling roots turn yellow or stop growing when light hits the soil in my pots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ la tswa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mitsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Roots naturally turn away from light to protect themselves. When light reaches the root zone inside a pot, root growth slows down or stops, leading to stunted plants that cannot absorb water effectively.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, shishifãi tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ la he koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. Kɛji la shɛ shishifã lɛ he ni yɔɔ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ Shishifã lɛ dalɛ baa shi loo ekpaa. Enɛ haa tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea near the base can help.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he ni bɛŋkɛ shishitoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua.

english: Yams become deformed when the soil is packed too tight or contains rocks that stop the tuber from expanding. Building high, loose soil mounds gives the roots plenty of soft space to grow smooth and large.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo tɛi komɛi yɛ ni tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa gbɛ babaoo ni amɛdaraa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying wood ash mixed with water or neem oil can help push these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Tso mli sũ ni akɛ nu loo neem fɔ efutu mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ashwie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: What is making small tiny holes all over my garden egg leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ahe baai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: Small holes in garden egg leaves are usually caused by flea beetles chewing on them. Keeping the farm free of surrounding weeds reduces their hiding places and protects your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ eggplant baai amli yɛ abɔɔi amli lɛ baa. Ni oooha jwɛi ni ebɔle ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ akafee nɔ ko Ebaaha he ni okɛ ohe baawo mli lɛ aba shi ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why are my cowpea pods turning black and shriveling up before the beans form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmeii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Shriveled pods are caused by pod-sucking bugs that pierce the young pods to drink the juice inside. Checking your field early in the morning and applying recommended insect treatments protects the harvest.
ga: Kplukai ni nuɔ pod ni amɛfoɔ pod bibii amli koni amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pod lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli leebi ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress or uneven watering. Watering your tomatoes regularly at the roots and placing dry grass mulch around the stem helps keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Akɛ nu woɔ tomatoi amli daa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe, ni akɛ sũ ni egbi shwieɔ amɛhe. Tso lɛ tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them for too long in flat, poorly drained land. Planting your cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows rain water to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why does my groundnut crop produce flowers, but no nuts grow under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ miifɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii komɛi bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they must push a peg down into the dirt to form the nut. If the soil is baked hard by the sun, the pegs cannot enter, so loosening the soil around the plants helps the nuts form.
ga: Beni amɛfee ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ Ehe bahia ni akɛ ŋmei ashwie amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmei lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ shã ni hulu lɛ ha ewa lɛ, Pin lɛ nyɛɛɛ abote mli No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ afee.

english: How can I tell that my maize is completely ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready when the outer green leaves turn papery dry and brown, and the silk at the tip becomes dark. You can also press a grain with your thumbnail; if it is hard and no milky liquid comes out, it is ready.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo beni kponɔgbɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ batsɔ wolo, egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. ni siliki ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ baatsɔ ediŋŋ. Obaanyɛ okɛ oshishifã lɛ hu anyɛ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji eyɛ shiŋŋ ni nu ko ni tamɔ atatu ejeee kpo lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo.

english: I planted my field two weeks ago, but some spots have no shoots coming up. Should I go back and put new seeds in those empty spots?
ga: Midu tsei lɛ otsii enyɔ ni eho nɛ. Shi yɛ hei komɛi lɛ, ŋmeii komɛi ejeee kpo kwraa. Ani esa akɛ maku misɛɛ kɛyadu dumɔwui heei yɛ nakai hei lɛ?

english: Yes, this practice is called refilling or supply planting. Some seeds fail to germinate due to dry soil, insects, or poor seed quality. Re-planting empty spots early ensures your field is fully populated so weeds do not take over the open spaces.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ infill loo supply dumɔ. Dumɔwui komɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, koolooi, loo dumɔwui ni ehiii hewɔ. He hee ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ooodu mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni gbɔmɛi ayi obɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ heŋ he ni agbele lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my entire 20-acre farm all in one week, or spread the planting out over a few weeks?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ madu miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli acre 20 yɛ otsi kome mli? Aloo gbɛmɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Spreading out your planting reduces your risk from unpredictable rainfall. If a sudden dry spell occurs, only a portion of your crops will be affected, and it also spreads out your harvest work so your crop does not spoil before you can harvest it.
ga: He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ baaha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ aba shi. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba trukaa lɛ Onibii lɛ fã ko pɛ baaná he sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni egbɛɔ okpamɔ lɛ eshwaa. Enɛ ji koni onibii akafite dani onyɛ okpa.

english: I want to clear a large new piece of land to expand my farm next season. How can I tell if the soil there is good for crops?
ga: Miisumɔ ni majie shikpɔŋ hee agbo ko nɔ koni mikɛgbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Look at the natural wild plants growing there first; tall, lush vegetation and dark, soft topsoil usually signal fertile land. Avoid rocky areas or soils that stay flooded for days after rain, as most crops need deep, well-draining soil to thrive.
ga: Kwɛmɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni tɛi yɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ he gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii pii biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops grow well on the land I cleared this year, but seem weaker on the land I have been farming for three years continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mifo afi nɛɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ afii etɛ etsu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every time they grow and produce a harvest. Without adding compost, manure, or fertilizers, or letting the soil rest, continuous farming depletes the soil's natural food supply over time.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni aduɔ amɛ ni akpaa amɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo ahaaa sũ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe. Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together than recommended, won't I get a bigger harvest because there are more plants on the farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe fe bɔ ni awo he ŋaa lɛ, Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo ejaakɛ tsei babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too closely causes plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Overcrowded plants grow thin and weak, producing tiny cobs or no yield at all, whereas proper spacing gives each plant room to produce maximum yield.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baatsɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔ. ni kɛ ŋmei bibioo ko baa loo ekɛ nɔ ko kwraa baaa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha tso lɛ tsu fɛɛ tsu lɛ aná yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some farmers plant cassava inside their maize fields instead of planting only one crop on the whole field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmãa yɛ amɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli moŋ fe ni amɛduɔ tso kome pɛ yɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called intercropping. Maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slower and takes over the space after the maize is cleared, giving you two harvests from the same land in one season.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli. Abɛi daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why does the soil around my young crops dry out so quickly after it rains, and how can I keep it moist longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya waa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nu be babaoo?

english: Direct hot sunlight causes water in bare soil to evaporate quickly. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves—known as mulching—acts as a blanket that traps moisture in the ground and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Mulching (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my planted crops after the first major rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and can lie dormant in the soil for years waiting for rain. Once water hits the ground, weeds sprout aggressively to seize sunlight and soil nutrients before your crops can establish themselves, which is why early weeding is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo, ni amɛmɛɔ nugbɔ Kɛ́ nu lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ lɛ Jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛŋɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ ama shi. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: My crop leaves are turning yellowish instead of staying dark green. What is wrong with my plants?
ga: Mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Mɛni ba mi tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your crop is missing nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make food and leaves. It can also happen when soil is too waterlogged, which suffocates the roots and stops them from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii kɛ baai Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: What will happen to my crop if a short dry spell hits right when the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ko ba? Kɛ tsei lɛ bɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Flowering is the most sensitive stage of crop growth because plants need high amounts of water to produce pollen and seeds. A drought during flowering causes flowers to drop off or fail to form full grains and fruits, severely cutting your yield.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ yɛ tso dalɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu babaoo he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee pollen kɛ dumɔwui. Hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi loo nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ dumɔwui kɛ aduawai kwraa. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because their leaf tissues burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving some large shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains alongside cocoa creates a cooler environment that protects the young seedlings until they mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ amɛbaai amli fãji lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ baa.

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' along the cassava stem cutting. These buds must always point upwards toward the sky so that the plant can easily sprout leaves above ground and build healthy roots underneath.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifã lɛ he lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo ni efee shishifãi ni wa yɛ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their healthy green color and leaves, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves green up again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa baai ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my dry fertilizer on the field right before a very heavy rain fell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes granular fertilizer off the soil surface into drainage streams, or washes it down too deep into the earth beyond where plant roots can reach, wasting your money and nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe kɛyaa faai ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Aloo etswaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he. Ehaa shika kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fiteɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture suddenly swings from very dry to very wet. Providing steady watering and mulching around the roots keeps the soil cool and stops the flowers from falling off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛyaa nɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb up on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on wooden stakes to spread their leaves toward maximum sunlight. Sunshine allows the plant leaves to make food, which flows down to swell the subterranean yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ anɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ahe baai ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why shouldn't I allow too many suckers to grow around one single plantain stool?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he lɛ? Plantain tso kome pɛ shishi

english: When too many suckers grow around one main plantain stem, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Removing extra suckers and keeping only one or two leaves all the soil nourishment for producing big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ baa kome loo enyɔ toɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa koni ekɛ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii aba.

english: Curled pepper leaves are caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves, or viruses spread by whiteflies. Controlling these small insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. loo helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: How does growing cowpea or groundnuts help make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and roots decay, that nitrogen remains in the soil to naturally feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does my harvested maize get small holes and fine powder inside the bags after sitting for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni powda kpakpa yɛ kotoku lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Holes and fine white powder inside grain bags mean maize weevils are eating the stored corn. Drying maize thoroughly until it is completely hard before sealing it in airtight sacks or silos stops weevils from surviving and damaging the grain.
ga: Bu kɛ powda yɛŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ dumɔwui kotoku lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii miiye ŋmãa ni ato lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa dani akɛwo vacuum kotokui loo ŋmãa ŋmãa mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmãa lɛ naa koni ekahi shi ni efite ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to use long sticks to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on sticks allows all the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow big tubers underground. It also keeps leaves off damp ground, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ naa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are packed too closely together, cassava puts all its energy into growing stem and leaf vegetation instead of storing food in its roots to form tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves curl and turn yellow when they get too much direct sunlight and lose water faster than their roots can drink. This is heat stress, which means the plants need shade trees or plantains nearby to break the intense light.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe tsɔ. ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu Enɛ ji dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ehe miihia ni tso lɛ aná hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ koni ekɛtsi la ni naa wa lɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to high heat stress, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit sets.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my plantain plants falling over easily once the fruit bunches start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support the heavy weight of a maturing fruit bunch, especially in high winds. Propping the stems with sturdy wooden poles prevents them from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai akui ni ekwɛ̃ ni tsii lɛ. titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why do experienced farmers spread dry grass and leaves around the base of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai amɛshwieɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under hot weather, traps moisture so you water less, and smothers weed seeds so they cannot grow.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni okɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ato koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why does my young maize crop turn pale green or yellow after several days of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ etsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes nitrogen—the main nutrient for leaf greenness—out of the root zone, and waterlogged soil stops roots from breathing. Applying fertilizer once the heavy rains stop helps restore health.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lɛ kɛyaa. kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe Ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli beni nugbɔ ni naa wa lɛ kpa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the leaves and funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed heavily on young maize leaves and growth tips. Catching them early allows you to use targeted controls before they destroy the crop's ability to grow.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni daraa lɛ waa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite nyɛmɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my stored harvested beans turn into powder and full of holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans ni mikpa lɛ miitsɔ powder ni bu eyi mli obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called bean weevils lay eggs on stored seeds, and their larvae burrow inside to eat the beans. Storing well-dried beans in airtight, sealed bags suffocates these pests and protects your yield.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ bean weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ anɔ. Ni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ baafo bu koni amɛye ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii nɛɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaabu onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Can I actually grow new seed yams using green stem cuttings instead of burying valuable tubers?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ adu dumɔwui heei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafu ŋmeii ni jara wa lɛ?

english: Yes! Yam vine propagation technology allows you to cut small green stems from a healthy plant and root them to produce clean seed yams, saving your harvested tubers for eating or selling.
ga: hɛɛ! Sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ he ŋaalee haa onyɛɔ ofoɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni shishifãi yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ kɛyashi sweet potato ni he tse nɔ. Akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ toɔ koni aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend using nursery baskets to grow young seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔji atsu nii ni akɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ?

english: Using nursery baskets makes it easier to control soil quality, protect delicate roots, and maintain the right moisture level, allowing a small setup to rapidly produce thousands of healthy planting materials.
ga: Dumɔwui tsɛnsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ebuɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni ehaa hulutsoo be ni sa lɛ hiɔ shi mlɛo Enɛ haa gbɛjianɔtoi bibii feɔ tsei ahe nibii akpei abɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ oya.

english: Is it true that I only need a very small amount of starting material to generate enough yam seeds for my farm?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ shishijee nibii fioo pɛ he miihia mi koni manyɛ mafee sweet potato dumɔwui ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, because a single healthy yam plant can provide hundreds of vine cuttings, allowing you to build up a massive quantity of seed yams from just one starting plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmei kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii ohai abɔ kɛjɛ wain tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ shishijee tso kome pɛ feɔ sweet potato dumɔwui babaoo.

english: What does 'foundation seed' mean when we are talking about yams?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘dumɔwui ashishitoo’ tsɔɔ kɛ wɔmiiwie ŋmeii ahe?

english: Foundation seeds are early-stage, disease-free mini-tubers produced under careful conditions specifically to serve as clean starting material for growing future crops.
ga: Foundation dumɔwui ji ŋmeii bibii ni hela bɛ mli yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli. Afee yɛ shihilɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ titri mli koni etsu nii akɛ niyenii ni he tse kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my traditional seed yams often get disease after a few growing seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, mi-kusum ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔɔ amɛ yɛ be fioo komɛi ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Traditional seed tubers carry over pests and diseases from previous soil cycles; producing clean seed yams from fresh vine cuttings in controlled nurseries breaks this disease cycle.
ga: Kusum dumɔwui ayitsei hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛi ni eho lɛ amli. Sweet potatoes ni he tse ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ wain tsei heei ni afolɔ mli yɛ ŋmɔ ni akudɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ hela nɛɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: How long does it take to produce seed yams if I start from vine cuttings?
ga: Kɛji akɛ aje shishi kɛjɛ wain tso ni afolɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ ebaahe dani anyɛ afee sweet potato?

english: It takes about six months to go from planting a vine cutting to harvesting healthy small seed yams ready for the next planting season.
ga: Akɛ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ tsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ adumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji dumɔwui bibii ni asaa he kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akpamɔ nɔ.

english: How many seed yams can I expect to harvest from a single batch of yam vine cuttings?
ga: Sweet potatoes enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ sweet potato wain tsei akuu kome mli?

english: From one good batch of vine cuttings, you can easily produce around 500 vines that go on to yield up to 1,000 seed yams within six months.
ga: Kɛjɛ wain tsei kpakpa kome ni ooofo lɛ mli Obaanyɛ oná wain tsei aaafee 500 kɛ ŋmeii ni shɛɔ 1,000 yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli.

english: How fast can a small yam nursery expand within a full year?
ga: Te sweet potato ŋmɔ bibioo ko baanyɛ alɛɛ oya yɛ afi muu kome mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: With proper container methods and continuous vine cutting cycles, a single starting setup can multiply into thousands—or even massive quantities—of clean planting materials within 12 months.
ga: Kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ awoɔ tsɛnsi mli kɛ wain tso lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shishijee gbɛjianɔtoo kome pɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe nibii ni he tse lɛ aya hiɛ ashɛ akpei abɔ—loo babaoo po—yɛ nyɔji 12 mli.

english: Do young yam vine cuttings need different care compared to normal yam mounds in the main farm?
ga: Ani sweet potato wain tsei ni afolɔ lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto fe sweet potato wain tsei ni abua naa daa yɛ ŋmɔ wulu ko mli lɛ?

english: Yes, fresh vine cuttings are delicate and need nursery protection, good moisture, and shaded container setups before they are strong enough to yield full seed tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, wain tsei heei ni afolɔ mli lɛ he waaa ni ehe miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ he. eyɛ hulutsoo kpakpa Ni esa akɛ afee tsɛnsi lɛ mli hulutsoo dani ewa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni eyi obɔ aha.

english: Can I turn seed yam multiplication into a main business on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsɔ sweet potato shweremɔ nɔ afee nitsumɔ titri ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, clean, disease-free seed yams are in high demand by other farmers, and using rapid vine multiplication allows you to produce high volumes at a low starting cost.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni okwaafoi krokomɛi taoɔ. Ni kɛ okɛ wain tsei ni yaa hiɛ oya tsu nii lɛ, ehaa onáa babaoo yɛ shishijee shika fioo mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They require shade from fast-growing plants like plantains during their first couple of years to keep them cool and protect soil moisture.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la gbɛ kwraa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Koni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he

english: Watering early in the morning gives plants time to drink before the sun gets hot. Afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate quickly into the heat before the roots can absorb it.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛnuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ oya ni etsɔɔ dɔlɛ dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer fixes this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts or beans on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes, which means their roots pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer for maize and improves soil richness.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the ground, keeps root areas moist for longer, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Ebaatsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep into the soil, making heavy bunches pull the tree down. Cutting away extra shoot babies (suckers) and supporting the main trunk with a strong wooden pole helps keep it standing.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Feemɔ jwɛi ni mli tse ni gbalaa tsei kɛyaa shi. Abifabii ni yɔɔ suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ooofolɔ amɛ ni okɛ tso ni wa fiɔ amɛgbɔmɔtso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi.

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanted angle helps the roots push deep into the soil and directs plant energy into forming larger, well-shaped tubers underneath.
ga: Yucca niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛkɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo.

english: What is making ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown powder inside the leaf whorl?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni eshiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baa lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that hides inside the central leaf funnel of maize plants and eats the growing shoots before leaves open up.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ. ni oye ŋmeii ni miida lɛ dani baai lɛ afɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers fall off before they turn into small tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium, causing the plant to shed flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ, ni haa tomato tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing normally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by very small insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap of young leaves or spreading a plant virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii waa tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ loo helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea around the base will help the maize turn healthy and green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ urea fata shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei lɛ ni efee hewalɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing plenty of big green leaves but produces very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ woɔ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi dumɔwui bibii fioo pɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen, they put all their energy into growing foliage instead of flowers and fruit. Adding nutrients rich in phosphorus, such as wood ash or recommended phosphorus fertilizers, encourages the crop to produce flowers and fill up heavy pods.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Akɛ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔsfɔs tamɔ tso sũ loo fɔsfɔs ŋmɔshi nibii afata he. Ebaaha tso lɛ awo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni tsii eyi mli obɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long, especially in heavy clay soil during rainy weather. Planting cassava stems on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. kɛha be kakadaŋŋ Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni tsii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants dry up and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants lose moisture very quickly under intense, direct heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains planted nearby to block the direct midday sun, cool the air, and retain soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛdu tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni eha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is healthy and ready for planting without sending it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esaa kɛha dumɔ ni mikɛyaaa laboratori ko mli?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well after rain, and contains living earthworms. If the soil is very pale, forms hard dry crusts, or lets water run right off, it needs organic material like dry leaves and manure mixed in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi baa. loo ha nu lɛ ajɛ mli Ehe miihia ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu mli.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and powdery dirt inside the central funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the growing funnel of the plant during the day to feed. Inspecting your farm early and spraying neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides directly into the plant funnel stops them from destroying the leaf growth.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra kɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni oooshwie tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or mites that feed on plant sap and transmit plant viruses. Spraying the plants early with soapy water solutions or mild insecticides controls these pests and keeps the leaves expanding normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni ekɛ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ shwieɔ tsei anɔ mra Nu ni akɛ samla fee loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli ejɔ baaye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni eye ebua baa lɛ ni egbɛ eshwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist using grass mulch around the base protects the root system from high heat and allows the flowers to turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛbɔleɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaabu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be damaged by tiny root-eating worms or weakened by heavy bunches of fruit. Mounding extra soil firmly around the trunk base and supporting the main stalk with sturdy wooden Y-props prevents the tree from tipping over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ afite. loo okɛ aduawai ni akɛwo mli shiŋŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ. Okɛ shikpɔŋ kroko abɔle tso lɛ shishi shiŋŋ ni okɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y ni akɛfiɔ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: How can I prevent my stored seed yams from sprouting too early in the barn before planting time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi sweet potato dumɔwui ni ato lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani dumɔ be aba?

english: Seed yams start sprouting early when stored in warm, dark, and humid spaces. Storing yams off the ground on raised wooden slats inside a cool, well-ventilated shade barn allows air to circulate around them, delaying early sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Afolɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei ni awó nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔleɔ ohe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shweremɔ oya lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. It can also happen when the soil has too much standing water, which prevents roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant groundnuts or beans after harvesting maize from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei beni mikpa ŋmãa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of food from the soil. Groundnuts and beans are special because they pull nitrogen out of the air and put it back into the soil, natural fertilizing it for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii ji nɔ krɛdɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: How do I put fertilizer on my crops so that the heavy rains do not wash it all away?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ ni naa wa akanɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist but not during torrential rainfall. Burying the fertilizer a few centimeters into the soil near the plant stem rather than leaving it on top prevents rain from washing it away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli sɛntimitai fioo komɛi moŋ fe ni oooshi yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ.

english: How do weeds actually reduce the final yield of my crops if I leave them to grow together?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi? Kɛji miha efee ekome kɛdara?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds are present, your crops get less food and water, which causes them to stay small and produce much less harvest.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Beni jwɛi yɔɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná niyenii kɛ nu fioo. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: What is causing tiny holes in the leaves of my young corn plants that look like shot marks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii ni tamɔ tu buji lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ.

english: This type of leaf damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the soft inner leaves of young corn, especially at night or early in the morning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni ji ŋmãa lɛ baa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baa. Titri lɛ, gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantain trees planted next to them during their early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? yɛ be mli ni edaa oya lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that easily dry out and burn under strong sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide wide leafy shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until it grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa shade kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to lift their leaves up to capture maximum sunlight for growth. Staking keeps the leaves dry and off the ground, which prevents leaf rot and leads to bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛshwere. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa baa lɛ afite ni ehaa bulbs wuji baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot inside the soil when the rainy season becomes too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain fills all the spaces in the ground for too long, the roots suffocate and rot due to excessive moisture and soil fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he fɛɛ he be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before they can grow into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when daytime heat becomes extremely hot, when the soil gets too dry, or if there are no insects around to help fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bɛ he ko ni ebɔle ehe Koni eye ebua ni ekɛ fɔfɔi afɔ

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetables roll up and droop in the heat of the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss during the hottest hours. If the soil has enough moisture, the leaves will naturally unroll and stand strong again by evening.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni elaajeɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ baa shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly when I pile them on top of each other after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto amɛhe nɔ beni mifo amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that produce heat and moisture. When piled tightly without air flowing between them, warmth and humidity build up, creating the perfect conditions for rot and fungi to destroy your harvest.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ko bɛ amɛteŋ lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baabua amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni baafite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why do bruised or cut yams spoil so fast when being transported to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni atswa loo afo lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ akɛtee jara nɔ lɛ?

english: A cut or bruise breaks the skin of the yam, creating an open wound. Bacteria and fungi enter through these wounds and cause quick decay, especially when yams bump against each other in moving vehicles.
ga: Kɛ́ afo loo atswa lɛ, ebaaha sweet potato lɛ hewolo lɛ akumɔ. kɛ pilamɔ ni agbele naa Bacteria kɛ fungi boteɔ pilamɔi nɛɛ amli ni ehaa fitemɔ baa oya. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ sweet potatoes tswa amɛhe yɛ tsɔnei ni miiho lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight for their leaves. More sunlight helps the plant make food to grow large tubers underground, while keeping leaves off the damp ground prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ni fa babaoo aba tsei lɛ ahe. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii koni ekɛ bulb agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ahe koni akafee baai lɛ ahe helai.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting green shoots on their own even when kept in a dry room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miije shishi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmiikwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli egbi mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have an internal natural clock called dormancy. Once that resting period ends—usually around the time rainy season approaches—the tuber naturally uses its stored energy to sprout and try to grow a new plant.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Kɛ nakai hejɔɔmɔ lɛ ba naagbee (bei pii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli) lɛ, Tubers kɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ tsei heei.

english: Why do my yam leaves turn yellow and dry up prematurely when there is a short drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ be kukuoo mli hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yams need steady soil moisture to carry nutrients from roots to leaves. During dry spells, the plant sheds leaves to save water, which stops tuber growth early if moisture isn't restored.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi amli kɛya baai amli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ baatsi tuber lɛ dalɛ naa mra kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cover my planted yam mounds with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi aha sweet potato ni abua naa lɛ nɔ?

english: Strong sun heats up bare soil mounds and dries out the buried yam seed pieces before they can sprout. Covering the mounds with grass acts like a protective blanket, keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Hulu ni naa wa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ sweet potato dumɔwui ni afu lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Jwɛi ni akɛhaa gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: How does planting my yam mounds too close together affect how big the tubers grow?
ga: Te ŋmeii ni abua naa ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ saa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When mounds are spaced too close together, plant roots fight each other for soil nutrients, water, and space underground, leading to thin and small tubers.
ga: Kɛji gɔji lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse shishifãi wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi hei lɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni eyɛ bibioo.

english: If I cut a yam into pieces for planting, does the top head piece sprout faster than the bottom tail piece?
ga: Kɛji ofolɔ sweet potato mli bibii bibii kɛha dumɔ. Ani ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya fe shishigbɛ ŋtayaai lɛ?

english: Yes, the head end of a yam tuber naturally contains more active growing buds and hormones, making it sprout faster and grow stronger shoots than the tail end.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei yitso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni haa mɔ daa lɛ momo. Enɛ haa edaa oya ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni he wa yɛ etsitsi lɛ naa.

english: Why does my yam crop produce huge bushy green leaves but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the yam plant direct all its food into growing tall stems and thick foliage instead of storing energy down in the tuber where you need it.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ haa sweet potato tso lɛ tsuɔ niyenii ni eyɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifãi ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ hewalɛ ato oyitsoŋ bɔ ni he hiaa bo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds around my yam mounds reduce my harvest yield even if I add plenty of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni bɔle mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ haa mi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crop vines and steal the fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight before your yam plant gets a chance to absorb them, starving the developing tuber.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe wain tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la dani sweet potato tso lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi. ni hɔmɔ aye bulbs ni miida lɛ.

english: How can I tell early on if my maize crops are sick before the whole field gets ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male enɛ mra? Ni mi-ŋma lɛ hela mɔ lɛ dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ fite?

english: Early signs of crop illness include yellowing leaves, dark spots, or stunted growth. Checking under leaves and along stems every few days helps you catch pests or fungal infections early so you can treat them before they spread to your entire farm.
ga: Mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso hela miiye lɛ ekomɛi ji baai ŋmɔŋ, he ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, loo dalɛ ni eyaaa hiɛ. Kwɛmɔ baa fɛɛ baa shishi kɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Gbii fioo komɛi baaye abua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai mra. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsa amɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.
