english: Leaf curling and yellowing in cassava are often caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems and pulling out infected plants early stops the virus from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Okɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baatsu nii ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does rotating my crops every season keep my farm free from diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsakeɔ daa be lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni helai akabote miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crop rotation breaks the life cycle of pests and soil diseases that target specific plants. Switching between grains like maize and legumes like groundnuts starves pests and naturally enriches the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ wala shihilɛ kpaa. Kɛ́ otsake ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I protect my cabbage crop from caterpillars without buying expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cabbage tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: You can prevent insect attacks by planting strong-smelling crops like onions around your cabbages or spraying leaves early with a natural mixture made from crushed neem leaves and water.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsĩ kooloi ni baatutua bo lɛ anaa kɛtsɔ tsei ni shãa mɔ waa, tamɔ sabolai, ni ooodu yɛ kaabe he loo kɛtsɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ mra lɛ nɔ. Kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa kɛ nu fee lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during the afternoon heat even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Pepper plants temporarily droop their leaves during peak afternoon heat to slow down water loss. If they bounce back in the evening, they are fine; placing dry grass mulch around the stems keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni nu lɛ akafite fioo. Kɛ́ oku osɛɛ oba gbɛkɛ lɛ, no lɛ ehi. Ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, water supply is uneven, or the plant lacks nutrients like calcium. Water consistently at the base of the plant and shade young crops during harsh afternoon heat to keep flowers healthy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. aloo tso lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ calcium. Okɛ nu awo tso lɛ shishi daa ni okɛ hulutsoo aha tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Yam rot is caused by fungi that thrive in waterlogged soil or enter through pest damage. Planting yams on raised mounds with good drainage prevents standing water from rotting the tubers before harvest.
ga: Sweet potato fitemɔ jɛɔ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛbaa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu ni ekã shi lɛ naa koni ekafite ŋmeii lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing tall with plenty of green leaves but producing very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants spend all their energy growing leaves instead of fruits. Switch to a balanced fertilizer high in phosphorus and potassium to encourage flower and fruit development.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai amli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Tsakemɔ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni eha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning a purplish color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is suffering from phosphorus deficiency, often because cold or wet soil prevents the roots from taking up nutrients. Adding well-rotted manure before planting prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ tso lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ loo ni efɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around my young crops while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle mitso lɛ he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your plants need. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crop gets strong enough to withstand pests and drought later on.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii titri lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hɔmɔ naa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do some foreign seed varieties fail to produce good yields on my farm compared to our local Ghanaian seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi wooo yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto wɔ maŋ Ghana dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Foreign seeds are usually developed for different climates and soil types. While they may have high yield potential, local seeds are naturally adapted to local weather, soil, and pest conditions in Ghana.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi. Eyɛ mli akɛ nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ baanyɛ aná yibiiwoo babaoo moŋ, shi maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ ji nɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, shikpɔŋ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ Ghana lɛ amli.

english: What does it mean when agricultural officers talk about cross-breeding crop varieties?
ga: Kɛ́ okwaayeli he onukpai miiwie ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ?

english: Cross-breeding means combining two different plant varieties—like a high-yielding foreign variety and a disease-resistant local variety—to produce a new seed that has the best qualities of both parents.
ga: Krosbreeding tsɔɔ tsei srɔtoi enyɔ ni akɛaafee ekome, tamɔ maŋsɛɛ tso ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ maŋ lɛ mli tso ni helai nyɛŋ eye lɛ. Koni ekɛ dumɔwui heei ni hiɛ fɔlɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ asui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why do crops grown from seeds I saved from last year's hybrid harvest produce smaller yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi ni ji hybrid kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Hybrid crop varieties are specially bred for one generation. If you plant seeds collected from that harvest, the crops lose their special strength and uniform traits, leading to lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha yinɔ kome. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛ amɛhefɛo kome. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers encourage farmers to visit local research stations?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ okwaafoi hewalɛ koni amɛyasara niiamlitaomɔ hei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Research stations test new crop varieties and techniques under local conditions first, allowing farmers to see which crops perform best before spending money on new seeds.
ga: Nibii amlitaomɔ he lɛ baaka tsei srɔtoi kɛ ŋaai heei ekwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ dani amɛwoɔ dumɔwui heei ahe nyɔmɔ.

english: How can I test a new crop variety safely without risking my whole farm's harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka tsei srɔtoi heei lɛ makwɛ shweshweeshwe ni mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni mifeɔ lɛ wooo oshara mli?

english: You can plant a small demonstration plot on a section of your land using the new variety alongside your traditional crop to compare their growth, pest resistance, and yield.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu nɔkwɛmɔnɔ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni fata blema ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ atsu nii ni okɛto dalɛ he. Pest ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ kɛ yibiiwoo

english: Why do my crops flower early when the rainy season is short or delayed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ fɔɔ mra be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa loo esɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: When crops experience water stress from poor rain, they go into a survival mode and produce flowers early to try to make seeds before the plant dries up entirely.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii na nu mli haomɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ lɛ Tsei yaa wala shihilɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi mra. Koni aka akɛ afee dumɔwui dani tsei lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall with thin stems and small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa babaoo kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe

english: When plants are overcrowded, they compete for sunlight and nutrients, spending all their energy growing tall to reach light instead of developing strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni fata he lɛ tsuɔ nii koni eshɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ tsohi agbohi.

english: How does cross-pollination from my neighbor's farm affect the crops on my field?
ga: Te cross-pollination ni jɛɔ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Wind and insects carry pollen from nearby fields to your crops. If your neighbor grows a different variety, the pollen can mix with yours and alter the grain quality or seed characteristics of your harvest.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii kɛ pollen kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa onibii amli. Kɛji okutsoŋnyo lɛ du tso kroko lɛ, Pollen baanyɛ ekɛ o-pollen lɛ afutu. ni ebaanyɛ etsake ŋmaa lɛ su loo ŋmaa lɛ su ni okɛkpaa nii lɛ.

english: Why do some new crop varieties resist insect attacks better than my traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei komɛi nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe mi blema dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved varieties are often bred to have natural defenses, such as tougher leaves, thicker husks, or natural chemical compounds that deter local insects and diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛná adebɔɔ mli hebuu, tamɔ baai ni mli wa. Kpoji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do crop varieties perform differently when moved from one region in Ghana to another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ kpokpaa kome nɔ yɛ Ghana kɛtee kpokpaa kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Different regions have varying rainfall patterns, temperatures, and soil compositions. A variety that thrives in the coastal savanna may struggle in the forest zone due to higher humidity and different diseases.
ga: Hei srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa, dɔlɛ, kɛ sũ lɛ mli nibii sɔrɔtoi. Kooloi srɔtoi ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋshɔnaa savannah lɛ baanyɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ kooi amli yɛ hulutsoo ni fa kɛ helai ahewɔ.

english: Why do I need to buy extra fertilizer for my crops when they are already growing in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahe ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni amɛmiidara yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ momo lɛ?

english: Soil is like a kitchen pantry; over time, crops eat up all the nutrients stored in it. Adding fertilizer puts fresh food back into the soil so your crops have enough energy to grow strong and produce a good harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tamɔ ŋtayaa. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fɛɛ ni ato yɛ mli lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii hee kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What is the difference between putting dry fertilizer in the ground and spraying liquid food on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Soil fertilizer feeds the plant slowly through its roots for long-term strength, while leaf sprays act like a quick energy drink that the plant absorbs immediately through its leaves.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii fiofio. kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛha hewalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hewalɛ ni anuɔ oya ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ baai lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and leafy but fail to produce big ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miida ni eyɛ baai shi ewooo abele toi wuji lɛ?

english: This usually happens when plants get too much leaf-building food (nitrogen) but not enough fruit-building food (phosphorus and potassium). Crops need a balanced diet to turn leafy growth into actual food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso ko nine shɛ niyenii ni feɔ baai (nitrogen) babaoo nɔ shi enáaa niyenii ni feɔ aduawai ni fa bɔ ni sa. (Phosphorus kɛ Potassium) Niyenii ni ja he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛtsake fɔfɔi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ewo niyenii diɛŋtsɛ mli.

english: How does spraying chemical medicine on my crops actually protect them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe?

english: Crop medicines work like treatments for humans. Some sprays coat the outside of leaves to kill pests on contact, while others get absorbed into the plant's sap to stop insects and diseases from eating it from the inside.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛ tsofa tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ bɔ ni gbɔmɔ tsofa tsuɔ nii pɛpɛɛpɛ. Spray komɛi haa baai lɛ asɛɛ koni egbe kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ kɛji amɛshɛ amɛhe. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai komɛi ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli koni kooloi kɛ helai akaye lɛ kɛjɛ emli.

english: Why do insects come back to my farm even after I have sprayed medicine on the crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ moŋ?

english: Spraying usually kills adult insects, but eggs hiding under leaves or in the soil can hatch days later. Rain can also wash the medicine away, making it easy for new pests from neighboring fields to move in.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baagbe kooloi bibii ni eda lɛ. Shi wɔji ni akɛtee baai ashishi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Nugbɔ hu baanyɛ afɔ tsofa kɛya. ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai heei baa Ewaaa akɛ abaajɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli aba.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray my crops with medicine?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Early morning or late evening is best because the air is cool and calm. Hot afternoon sun can evaporate the spray before the plant absorbs it or cause the liquid to scorch the leaves.
ga: Leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ afee la dani tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ loo eha nu lɛ ashã baai lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the plant medicine or spray I used is actually working on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso tsofa loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baatsu nii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You will notice new leaves coming out bright green and healthy, fewer holes or spots on the leaves, and insects dropping off or disappearing within a few days of application.
ga: Obaayɔse akɛ baai heei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ. Buu loo ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. ni kooloi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛlaaajeɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akɛtsu nii sɛɛ.

english: How long does it usually take to see changes in my crops after applying fertilizer?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani minaa tsakemɔi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most crops show darker green leaves and faster growth within 7 to 14 days after soil fertilizer is applied, while leaf sprays can show noticeable changes in as little as 3 to 5 days.
ga: Tsei babaoo yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 mli beni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nii sɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsakemɔi ni kadiɔ mɔ kpo yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 pɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign that the plant is starving for nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe and absorb food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ miiye nitrogen. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Can applying too much crop medicine or spray harm my plants?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye mi tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, using too much spray or mixing it too strong can burn the plant leaves, turn them brown, or stunt crop growth. Always mix the exact amount recommended for your field size.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi babaoo loo akɛfutu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã. tsɔ blɔfo loo ebaanyɛ etsĩ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa Be fɛɛ be lɛ, futumɔ bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee kɛha o-cavity lɛ dalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow much better on land where I planted cowpeas or beans the previous season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This nitrogen acts as a free natural fertilizer that feeds heavy-eating crops like maize during the next planting season.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa tsei ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies or spread when planting infected stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this yellowing and stem damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ loo amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛji amɛmiida tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees dry up and fall off before growing into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛmiidara ni amɛmiifee cacao ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from water stress during dry spells, insect attacks, or lack sufficient nutrients in the soil to feed all the pods at once.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ kpe amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, kooloi bibii tutua amɛ, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the right time to apply chemical fertilizer to my maize so it doesn't wash away or burn the plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ awo ŋmãa mli? Ani jeee ni afɔ loo ashã tsei lɛ?

english: Apply the first dose of fertilizer about two weeks after planting when the seedlings sprout, and the second dose when the maize reaches knee-height, putting it a few centimeters away from the plant stem.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli klɛŋklɛŋ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃, aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ nɔ beni ŋmei lɛ shɛɔ aaafee tsitsi nɔ lɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo tso lɛ shishi sɛntimitai fioo pɛ.

english: What is eating holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms that hide inside the central leaf funnel. Spraying recommended biological or chemical treatments directly into the plant centers early in the morning or late evening effectively controls them.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwo mli lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha enyɛ eye nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting while they are still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This black rot at the bottom of tomatoes is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering where the soil gets extremely dry and then soaked.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi waa ni edɔ waa lɛ

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and pale yellow if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Clearing weeds early stops them from starving your crops of food and light.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi otsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii kɛ la ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight to make food for the growing tuber underground, while keeping leaves away from moist soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛha niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my maize seeds very deep under the soil when sowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ waa lɛ?

english: If seeds are buried too deeply, they exhaust all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil and may die before reaching sunlight or emerge as weak plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, Hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ egbo dani hulu la ashɛ enɔ loo ebatsɔ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around my crops help them during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te fee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ye ebua amɛ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: How can I keep my crops from drying up when the rains stop earlier than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akagbi be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: You can use mulching, which means covering the soil around your plants with dry grass or leaves. This acts like a blanket that shades the soil, trapping moisture in the ground and keeping the plant roots cool during dry spells.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mulching atsu nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding animal manure or the right fertilizer feeds the soil and turns the leaves healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the best way to store my harvested grains so insects do not eat them before my family gets food?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mikɛ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ato koni kooloi akaye amɛ dani miweku lɛ aná?

english: Dry your grains completely in the sun until they are hard, then store them in airtight bags (like PICS bags) or sealed drums. Without air and moisture, storage insects cannot survive to spoil your crop.
ga: Gbimɔ ŋmaa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) loo baagi ni atsĩ naa mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo bɛ Storage insects lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi kɛkɛ ni amɛfite onibii.

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the water soaks deep into the roots before the hot afternoon sun can evaporate it, helping your vegetables stay strong all day.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ nu lɛ baabote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ dani ebaatsɔ la yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni o-vegetables lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Planting cassava stems too close together forces them to fight for sunlight and soil food, so they grow tall instead of swelling their roots. Giving each plant about one meter of space allows big tubers to develop underground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, edaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni miihe ashɛ mita kome lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts on my farm help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts pull goodness from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When you plant crops like maize on that same land later, they feed on that natural soil richness.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Egbalaa kpakpafeemɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛmɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni sɛɛ mli lɛ oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ. Amɛbaaye shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adebɔɔ mli nibii ni baa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from a disease or just thirsty from the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo hulu la he kumai miiye lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Thirsty plants usually droop in the hot sun but recover in the cool evening. If the leaves stay curled, spotted, or burnt even overnight, your crop is facing a pest or disease problem.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi ebaatsa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ mli kɛji akɛ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ, etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ashã lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome po. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai miikpe.

english: Should I plant seeds saved from my last harvest or buy certified seeds from the market?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli loo mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ jara nɔ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to survive local dry spells and resist diseases, giving you a bigger harvest. Saved seeds lose their strength over time and produce weaker crops.
ga: Ahala dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli ni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Ehaa okpaa nibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my farm soil turn into hard rocks after a few days without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ tɛ ni wa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic material like decayed leaves and compost. Mixing compost or animal manure into your farm soil breaks up hard earth, allowing it to hold water like a sponge.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo sũ mli lɛ, ebaagbala sũ ni wa lɛ mli. Ehiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji

english: Young crops have small roots and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water and plant food. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ tsei niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when there is no big tree near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby keeps the seedlings cool and retains moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Shade tsei loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I plant my cassava cuttings slanted in the ground instead of straight or flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei niji yɛ koŋ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ loo amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle helps roots grow deeper into the soil for bigger tubered yields, while keeping the stem steady against strong winds.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji 45 degree lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishi damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food for growing heavy tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves off the damp ground, which also protects them from leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ hu buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe helai ahe.

english: Removing extra shoots leaves only two or three strong stems per mat. This prevents the plants from fighting each other for water and food, allowing the main stem to produce a much bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ mat kome mli. Koni tsei akatswa akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii he. Ehaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ woɔ dumɔwui babaoo.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize help my soil stay rich?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow alongside maize, they naturally fertilize the soil with nutrients that the maize needs to grow green and tall.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa fee ekome lɛ Amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my maize so the rain doesn't waste it?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo ŋmãa koni nugbɔ lɛ akafite lɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a gentle rain, about two to three weeks after the maize stems sprout. Avoid applying right before heavy downpours that can wash the chemical away before roots absorb it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Aaafee otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ, Tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni okɛbaatsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba, ni baanyɛ ajie tsofai lɛ kɛjɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: How do I know if the first rain of the year is enough for me to start planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛje dumɔ shishi?

english: Wait until rain has soaked the soil deep enough that it stays wet for a few days straight. A single early rain is often followed by a hot dry stretch that can kill newly germinated seeds.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shikome lɛ nyiɛɔ dɔlɛ ni mli egbi ni baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the sun from drying out the soil, prevents weeds from growing, and turns into rich soil manure as it rots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: What are those tiny caterpillars eating the centers of my young maize leaves, and how do I save the crop?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ yɛ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extract in the leaf funnel before they grow large will save your crop.
ga: Amɛji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani amɛdara lɛ baaye abua ni ahere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are usually caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on when the plant experiences irregular watering or very dry spells while growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ahãa tsei lɛ nu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo amɛgbi waa beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: What kind of living fence can I plant around my farm to stop wandering cattle from entering and eating my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbogbo manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he koni tsinai ni elaaje lɛ akabote mli ni amɛye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Planting dense hedges of jatropha, thorny acacia, or vetiver grass around your farm boundary creates a tough physical barrier that deters farm animals like cattle and goats while clearly marking where your land begins.
ga: Jatropha jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ, acacia loo vetiver jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ Oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ni mli wa ni tsiɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ tsinai kɛ tooi anaa, yɛ be mli ni etsɔɔ he ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ lɛ faŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or compost will help the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot survive intense direct sun because their leaves dry out quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields them until they grow mature and strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ aba kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many green leaves, but when I harvest, the tubers are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ? Shi kɛ́ akpa bulb lɛ, ani amɛbafeɔ bibii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess fresh manure, cassava uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves above ground instead of swelling its roots below ground. Balanced soil nutrients help cassava produce large tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmeii heei babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: My tomato plants have plenty of blossoms, but why are the flowers dropping off without producing fruit?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or sudden dry conditions. Keeping the soil consistently moist by mulching around the plant base helps hold moisture and stops flowers from falling.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in weak plants with small yields. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures every plant grows full and yields more.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsei fɛɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets pests that feed on that crop build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaves. Spraying early with neem water or recommended extension remedies helps control these insects before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo, tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot when rainwater sits on my field for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the air inside the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits on the land and saturates the soil, it suffocates the roots and causes them to rot; creating small drainage mounds or channels helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi lɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha amɛgboi. Gɔji bibii loo nu homɔ gbɛi ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to steal fertilizer, water, and light much faster than cultivated farm crops. Clearing weeds early in the first few weeks gives your crops the head start they need to grow tall and shade out late weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ la oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛsaa amɛhe koni amɛdara ni amɛha jwɛi lɛ aná hulutsoo yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants still survive even when I don't give them as much fertilizer and care as my yam farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli ni mikwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Cassava is a naturally resilient crop with a strong root system that can draw nutrients from poor soils, whereas yams are more delicate and require rich, well-prepared soil and extra care to produce good tubers.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ shi ni eyɛ shishifãi ni wa ni baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Shi sweet potato lɛ, eyɛ mlɛo fe tsutsu lɛ, ni ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ, ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ, kɛ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii kpakpai.

english: Can I plant cassava along the borders of my yam field, or will it steal nutrients from my yams?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ naa? Aloo ebaaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can plant cassava on the borders of your yam field without issue, as long as you give enough spacing so the fast-growing cassava leaves do not shade the young yam vines.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ ko naa ni naagba ko bɛ he. Shii abɔ ni okɛ ohe aaabɔ he ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ ji koni akatsi ŋmei baai ni shwereɔ oya lɛ atsĩ yam wain tsei bibii lɛ anaa.

english: How should I position a cassava stem in the ground when planting so that it grows strong roots?
ga: Te esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oha tɛŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ awa?

english: Plant cassava stem cuttings about 20 to 30 centimeters long at an angle or horizontally into moist soil, making sure the buds on the stem point upward so the shoots can easily emerge.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛtsɔ amɛ ni ooofo yɛ koŋ loo ŋwɛigbɛ, aaafee sɛntimitai 20 kɛyashi 30, kɛya shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do yams need large soil mounds to grow well while cassava can grow on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ŋmɔji wuji he hiaa sweet potatoes koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need high, soft mounds so their long tubers can expand downward easily without meeting hard soil, while cassava roots are strong enough to penetrate flatter, harder ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato lɛ aná gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii kakadaji lɛ anyɛ ashɛ shi oya ni amɛtaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ he. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni wa mli.

english: How do shade trees on my farm affect the growth of my food crops like cassava?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While light shade from trees keeps the soil cool and moist, too much heavy shade slows down cassava growth because cassava needs full sunlight to develop big tubers.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ahe hulutsoo haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa moŋ, shi hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha yucca lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia cassava koni ekɛ bulbs wuji aba.

english: Why do cassava leaves yellow and drop during the dry season, and is my crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egboi?

english: Your crop is not dying; dropping leaves during the dry season is cassava's natural way of saving water, and it will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbooo. Abuɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ akɛ eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni ŋmei tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei.

english: Why does a cut cassava stem sprout new leaves so quickly after being planted in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ woɔ baai heei oya beni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems store stored food energy and water in their tissues, allowing them to shoot out new leaves and roots rapidly even without an existing root system.
ga: Kasava tsei toɔ hewalɛ, niyenii, kɛ nu yɛ amɛ fãji amli. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akwɛɔ baai kɛ shishifãi heei oya kɛji shishifã ko bɛ jɛmɛ po.

english: Why do my cassava tubers go bad within a few days of harvesting while my yams can stay fresh for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers lack a protective outer bark and begin to break down rapidly once exposed to air after harvest, whereas yams enter a dormant state with tough skins that preserve them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni buɔ amɛhe. Ni ejeɔ shishi efiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, sweet potatoes yaa shihilɛ ko ni mli wa mli kɛ ŋmei ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig up without harvesting too early?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa ni akpaaa amɛ mra tsɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the lower leaves dry up and drop, or by carefully test-digging one root to check its size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ole be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. aloo kɛtsɔ shishifã kome ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is cassava considered a good security crop for my family during lean seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ji ŋmãa kpakpa kɛha miweku lɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava can be left safely underground in the soil for months after it matures without spoiling, allowing you to harvest it bit by bit whenever your family needs food.
ga: Abaanyɛ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo beni ekwɛ̃ ni efiteee lɛ sɛɛ. Ehaa okpaa nii bibii bibii be fɛɛ be ni niyenii he baahia oweku lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and can burn. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves, providing crucial shade and conserving soil moisture for the young cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai wuji. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow strong green leaves. It can also happen when the soil is too waterlogged, preventing roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It keeps the ground cool under hot sun, stops water from evaporating quickly out of the soil, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. Planting them first enriches the soil naturally, reducing the amount of chemical fertilizer your next crop will need.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ mra lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni he hiaa bo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ baa shi.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the central funnel of young maize plants and chew on fresh leaves, reducing plant strength if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: It is best to wait until your land receives two or three steady, heavy rains so the soil absorbs enough moisture deep down. Planting after just one light rain often causes seeds to germinate and then dry up.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shishigbɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ pɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose as many leaves as possible to sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves catch, the more food the plant produces to feed and grow large tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Babaoo ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients, causing the plant stress that prevents fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni tsiɔ aduawai anaa lɛ baa.

english: Can I leave my mature cassava in the ground if buyers are not ready to purchase it yet?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashɛ ŋmei momo mafɔ shikpɔŋ kɛji mɔ ni heɔ lɛ efeko klalo akɛ ebaahe?

english: Yes, mature cassava roots can safely remain underground for several months, using the soil as natural storage until you are ready to harvest and take them to market.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nutoohe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa ni okɛya jara nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, mites, or thrips, or by viruses spread by whiteflies that distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites loo thrips, loo helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need taller crops like plantain planted right beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he hiaa mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and can burn easily. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides essential shade, keeps the soil cool, and retains moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã oya. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves upward toward sunlight to create energy for tuber growth. Elevating the leaves off the damp ground also protects them from fungal diseases and lets the plant catch maximum sunlight to produce bigger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ahe helai ahe, ni ehaa tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: When too many suckers grow around a single plantain tree, they compete with the main stem for water and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what remains to its newer top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie baai ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which works with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into plant food. When cowpeas grow and decay in the soil, they leave this natural fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii. Kɛji tsina ŋmeii kwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaashi nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii nɛɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cabbage in the exact same field where I harvested cabbage last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kaabɛji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa kaabɛji yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously in one spot allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up over time. Changing to a different crop family starves those pests and stops diseases from lingering in your soil.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai aba babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee tsei aweku kroko mli lɛ, ebaaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ, ni ebaaha helai akahi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when plants experience drought stress. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination inside the flower, causing the plant to shed the flower to conserve its energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on leaf sap. As they feed, they damage the delicate leaf tissue, causing the leaves to warp and curl inward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ Ebaafite baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa mli.

english: Why does cassava start to rot and spoil so quickly within a few days of harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ni egboɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpa lɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots lack a durable outer bark once removed from the ground. Minor cuts and exposure to oxygen trigger a rapid, natural decay process, making it necessary to process or consume the tubers shortly after harvest.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ bɛ kponɔgbɛ nɔ ko ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Nibii bibii ni afolɔ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ baaha nibii ni fiteɔ oya lɛ aba yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni atsu ŋmeii lɛ ahe nii loo aye amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa amɛ.

english: Why does rice grow much better when the field is kept shallowly flooded with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ nu eyi ŋmɔji ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air passages that allow their roots to breathe underwater while competing weeds get smothered. Keeping the field shallowly flooded ensures a steady supply of moisture and keeps weed growth low.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ mligbɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni haa amɛshishifãi lɛ muɔ yɛ nu shishi yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu afua ni baa ŋmɔji ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛ baaha hulutsoo be aba daa ni eye ebua ni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I leave some large trees on my farm instead of clearing everything down to the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni majie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Keeping certain shade trees protects delicate young crops from harsh sun heat, prevents soil from drying out too fast, and provides falling leaves that decompose into natural manure for your crops.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni abu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa baa ni egbee shi lɛ ni efiteɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: How do I know which trees will help my food crops and which ones will spoil them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baaye abua mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mɛɛ tsei baagboi?

english: Trees with light branch canopies and small leaves usually let enough sunlight through and add nitrogen to the soil, whereas trees with very dense leaves or greedy surface roots block light and drain groundwater away from crops.
ga: Tsei ni aniji ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛha hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ atsɔ mli ni amɛkɛ nitrogen awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa loo amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ hiɛjoomɔ lɛ haa la sɛɛ foɔ ni amɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Is burning bushes after clearing land bad for my soil in the long run?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ashãa beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ náa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: While burning gives a quick boost of ash fertilizer and clears land fast, it kills beneficial organisms living in the ground and destroys organic matter that holds moisture, leaving your soil tired and dry faster.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ oya ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ oya. Shi egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu, ni efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni egbiɔ oya.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of dirt after I completely clear my farm on a hillside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ shwie muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ beni mijie ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots and fallen leaves act like anchors and sponges holding the dirt together. When you clear all vegetation completely, heavy rain easily sweeps away the rich topsoil.
ga: Tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋshɔkei kɛ sponji ni ŋmɛɔ muji he. Kɛ́ ojie tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Will planting cassava close to my young cocoa seedlings slow down the growth of the cocoa?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ adalɛ aba shi?

english: If planted too close, cassava roots will fight with young cocoa for water and soil nutrients. However, if spaced properly, cassava can provide valuable shade that helps cocoa seedlings survive their early years.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ kɛ cocoa bibii lɛ baawu koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ akɛ he ko ni sa lɛ, Yucca baanyɛ aha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: What food crops can I grow to feed my family while waiting for long-term tree crops like oil palm or cocoa to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu koni mikɛha miweku lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ mu loo kookoo lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Fast-growing food crops like plantain, cocoyam, and vegetables can be intercropped with young tree seedlings to provide quick food and income while giving necessary shade to the cash trees.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ dumɔwui bibii adu niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains, cocoa, kɛ aduawai koni eha niyenii kɛ shika aba oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shika tso lɛ náa hulutsoo.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together, will I harvest more food from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and smaller cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to give a full yield.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ekpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield when I plant the same crop on the same farm year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt every season. Rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly right after I clear fresh forest land in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni ajie koo mli shikpɔŋ hee yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Clearing land exposes bare soil to direct sunlight and rain, which wakes up dormant weed seeds resting in the topsoil and causes them to germinate rapidly.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jɛmɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ akwɛ̃. Eteɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: How can I keep my farm soil moist during dry spells without using expensive watering systems?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni mikɛ nu ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Covering bare soil between your crops with dried leaves, grass, or crop stalks (mulching) shields the ground from direct sun and prevents water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ni okɛ baai ni egboi, jwɛi loo tsei ahe tsei (mulch) baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni etsĩ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight because their leaves scorch easily and the soil loses moisture quickly. They need temporary shade trees like plantains or food crops to act as natural covers until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo niyenii tsei. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other so I can have more trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Overcrowding cocoa trees makes them compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak trees that produce very few pods and spread diseases quickly between overlapping branches.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa tso kakadaŋŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ, ni egbɛɔ helai eshwaa niji ni tsɔɔ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ oya.

english: Why should I cut off green, healthy branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi cacao tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning unnecessary branches allows the tree to focus its energy and nutrients on growing pods rather than excess leaves. It also lets sunlight and air pass through the tree canopy, which reduces dampness and prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ maa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeehiɛ baai babaoo lɛ Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni ehaaa ŋmeii helai aba.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast around my cocoa trees and how does that affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mihe lɛ? mi koko tso lɛ Ni te enɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that quickly steal soil nutrients, fertilizers, and water away from your cocoa trees. Leaving weeds uncleared also creates a damp environment that hides pests like mirids and rodents.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli oya. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni ajieee kɛjɛ mli lɛ hu haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii teɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa tree fall off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree is stressed by lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks. Maintaining balanced soil fertility and protecting trees from sap-sucking insects helps flowers develop into full pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni abuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do cocoa flowers turn into pods if I do not see bees visiting my farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii kɛji minaaa ŋmeii ni baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa flowers are pollinated by tiny insects called midges rather than large bees. These midges live and breed in cool, moist leaf litter on the farm floor, which is why keeping organic mulch on the ground helps pod production.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ ji mɛi ni woɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ, shi jeee ŋmeii wuji. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ baai ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni organic mulch ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ pod feemɔ mli lɛ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet conditions and dark shade. Clearing weeds, pruning extra branches, and harvesting ripe pods promptly help air circulate and stop the moisture that allows the fungus to spread.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hei ni duŋ ewo. weeding additional pruning Ni ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ekpaa ŋmeii ni baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ akpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa tree curling up and showing brown patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with brown patches are often caused by mirids (capsids), small insects that feed on the sap of cocoa shoots and pods. Spraying at the right time of year and maintaining shade balanced with sunlight keeps mirid damage low.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, capsids, ni ji kooloi bibii lɛ kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. ni yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli, ni oha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa lɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo nibii ni efiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed many of their leaves during the dry Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves during severe dry weather is the cocoa tree's natural way of saving water to survive. Covering the soil around the base of the trunk with dry leaves or husks helps keep the roots cool and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ ji gbɛ ni cacao tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ koni ehi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmãa ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is it bad practice to harvest cocoa pods while they are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ abaakpa kookoo ŋmeii be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Unripe green pods contain flat, underdeveloped beans with very little sugar content. Beans from unripe pods cannot ferment properly, leading to bitter, poor-quality cocoa that buyers will reject.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni edako lɛ amli ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni edako ni sugar fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Beans ni jɛ pods ni edako lɛ amli lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ kookoo ni ehiii ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baakpoo lɛ baa.

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Clearing weeds and cutting excess tree branches helps air and sunlight dry out the pods, preventing the fungus from multiplying.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkafee babaoo

english: Why are the branches of my cocoa trees swelling up and the leaves changing colour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ niji lɛ efuu ni baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su lɛ?

english: This is a sign of swollen shoot disease, which is caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Because the virus cannot be cured with chemical sprays, infected trees must be removed so the disease does not spread to nearby healthy crops.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ he okadi, ni hela ko ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsa hela lɛ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do fungal diseases spread much faster on my farm during the rainy season than during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kwraa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fungi that cause crop diseases need water droplets and high humidity to hatch and infect plant leaves or fruits. Hot, dry weather dries up moisture, making it much harder for these disease spores to survive.
ga: Fungi ni gbeɔ helai yɛ tsei amli lɛ biɔ nu mli nu ni hoɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo koni enyɛ efɔ ni ekɛ hela aba tso lɛ baai loo aduawai lɛ anɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ mli egbiɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kwraa kɛhaa nɛkɛ helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akɛ amɛaahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the plant is missing essential nutrients in the soil, particularly nitrogen, or that the roots are overwhelmed by waterlogging and cannot feed properly.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛna niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa flowers and small pods keep falling off before growing into big pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani minɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji?

english: Trees shed young flowers and small pods when they experience stress, such as dry spells, lack of nutrients, or attacks by sap-sucking pests like mirids.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai, fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ haomɔ tamɔ hulutsoo be, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen tutuamɔ,

english: Why does cutting off some branches of my tree help it produce more fruit later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ fã ko ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or unproductive branches so the tree does not waste energy on them, allowing it to send extra food and nutrients directly to developing pods and fruits.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni wooo yibii lɛ. koni tsei akafite hewalɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo aya ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa plants need big shade trees around them, while maize needs open sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei wuji he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa he hiaa hulu la yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Different crops have different light needs; young cocoa naturally grows under forest canopies and gets sunburned without shade, whereas maize needs direct sunlight to generate energy for heavy grain cobs.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ kane he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Kookoo bibioo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni hulutsoo lɛ shãa lɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ ehe. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ kɛha ŋmãa ni tsii lɛ.

english: Fertilizer requires water to dissolve so that crop roots can absorb it. Applying it to dry soil can waste the fertilizer or even burn the plant's roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite loo eshã tso lɛ shishifãi.

english: How do weeds damage my crops if they are just growing in the same dirt next to them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii? Ni kɛji akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ hu?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they compete aggressively with your crops for the same soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight, leaving less food for your crops to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do insects eat my crop leaves much more during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates ideal conditions for insects to breed and hatch, and the soft new leaves that grow during the rains provide fresh food for young pests.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni kooloi afɔ ni amɛfɔ amɛwui. Ni baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ niyenii hee.

english: Why do some farmers in my village plant their crops in December before Christmas instead of waiting for the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ December mli dani Blonya baashɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ?

english: Some farmers take advantage of late minor rains or residual soil moisture to plant quick-maturing crops like vegetables or late maize, allowing them to harvest early in the new year when market prices are often high.
ga: Okwaafoi komɛi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ miitsu nii koni amɛkɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ aduawai loo ŋmãa. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa nii yɛ afi hee lɛ shishijee mli yɛ jara ni bei pii lɛ ejara wa waa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if it is too late in the year for me to start planting new seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ afi nɛɛ eshɛ sɛɛ tsɔ ni mikɛje dumɔwui heei adumɔ shishi?

english: You should check your soil moisture and rain patterns rather than just the calendar. If rains are stopping completely and you do not have irrigation, seeds planted late will lack the water needed to germinate and survive.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa. Jeee kalanda lɛ nɔ kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa kwraa ni obɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ bɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up and turn yellow during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry Harmattan, low humidity and strong dry winds strip water from plant leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil, forcing the plant to curl or shed leaves to preserve moisture.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ, hulutsoo be ni baa shi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa ni naa wa lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe loo eshwieɔ ebaa lɛ koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Will my seeds survive in the soil if I plant them before the dry season starts but the rain stops coming?
ga: Ani midumɔwui lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu amɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi shi nugbɔ lɛ kpa?

english: Seeds require consistent moisture to sprout. If a seed receives enough moisture to begin germinating but the soil dries out completely afterward, the fragile seedling will die under the hot dry soil.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji dumɔwu lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛje shishi ekwɛ̃ shi shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ, Fragile dumɔwui lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow much slower during the hazy December weather compared to April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kwraa yɛ December ni afua yɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛ akɛto April he lɛ?

english: Crops need direct, strong sunlight for photosynthesis to make food and grow quickly. Dust and haze in December block sunlight, which naturally slows down crop growth rates.
