ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la ni naa wa, tɛ̃ɛ kɛha fotosintɛsis ni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara oya. Muji kɛ lasu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ December mli lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Is it good for me to clear my farm land in December if I plan to travel home and plant later?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie midumɔi lɛ amli yɛ December mli? Ni kɛji akɛ mito gbɛjianɔ koni maku misɛɛ kɛya shia ni mayadu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli hu?

english: Clearing land early helps clear weeds and prepare the plot, but leaving the bare soil exposed to intense dry-season heat can bake away vital nutrients and moisture unless you leave a layer of organic mulch on top.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie jwɛi ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛaawo dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ akabote mli. Ja oshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ eko yɛ nɔ.

english: How can I keep my young crops from dying of thirst if I need to leave my farm for a few days during the holidays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni kumai akaye amɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ ehe bahia ni mashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi yɛ gbijurɔyelii lɛ amli hu?

english: You can cover the soil around the bases of your plants with a thick layer of dry grass or crop leaves (mulch), which traps soil moisture and shields root zones from intense heat.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tso baai ni mli edɔ (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he, ni no ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Which crops are best for me to plant if I am starting near the end of the year in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ kɛji mije shishi yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: Short-duration crops like pepper, tomato, and garden eggs do well if you can provide light watering, while drought-tolerant crops like cassava can establish roots before the dry period sets in fully.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo, tamɔ ŋmeii, tomato, kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji obaanyɛ okɛ nu awo amɛnɔ fioo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa, tamɔ ŋmei, baanyɛ afee shishifãi dani hɔmɔ be lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa.

english: Why does my soil dry out so much faster late in the year compared to the middle of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kwraa yɛ afi lɛ naagbee fe afi lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Late in the year, high temperatures combined with dry winds drop atmospheric humidity, causing water to evaporate rapidly from both the plant leaves and the surface of the soil.
ga: Beni afi lɛ baa naagbee lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi fata he lɛ ha kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa lɛ ba shi. Ehaa nu shwieɔ shi oya kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: If I plant cassava stems in the dry soil late in the year, will they rot before the next rain comes?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee Ani ŋmei tsei lɛ baagboi dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Hardy stems like cassava do not rot easily in dry soil; instead, they remain dormant until soil moisture increases, at which point they will begin producing root shoots and leaves.
ga: Tsoi ni he wa tamɔ ŋmei lɛ fiteee oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Shi amɛbaakã he amɛhi shi akɛ mɛi ni bɛ wɔɔhe. Kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ baaya hiɛ, ni no mli lɛ amɛbaabɔi shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ feemɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them directly in an open field without any tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn under direct heat. Planting them near fast-growing shade plants like plantains protects them from harsh sunlight and keeps the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa, ni la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods on my farm turn black and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, which thrives in cool, overly damp shade. When branches are too bushy and block airflow, moisture stays trapped on the pods, allowing fungal spores to grow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni jɛmɛ ejɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔji tsɔ ni amɛtsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa lɛ, Fɛ̃i baakpɛtɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa fungal spores lɛ daa.

english: When cocoa trees are overcrowded, their roots fight over water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching the lower branches. Overcrowding also stops air movement, creating conditions for diseases to spread.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni ebaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni kɛ shihilɛi ni helai srɔtoi baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mli baa

english: Why do I need to cut off the thin shoots growing out from the bottom of my cocoa tree trunks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal essential water and nutrients away from the main trunk. Removing them ensures the tree directs all its energy toward producing healthy foliage, flowers, and heavy pods.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are starving for nitrogen, a key food crop plants need to stay green. It can also happen when heavy rainfall washes away nutrients from the root area.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why does using too much fertilizer cause my cassava plants to grow big leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baa agboi shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen fertilizer encourages the plant to put all its food into growing leaves and stems above ground. Because the plant is busy expanding top growth, it stores very little starch down in its roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛ niyenii fɛɛ awo baai kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehe miiwo ehiɛ ni edaa lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ ato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the land with plant food, helping heavy-feeding crops like maize grow better in the next cycle.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsei niyenii yɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni ayeɔ nii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛkuu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by intense dry heat that bakes the topsoil. If steady rains have not officially set in, seeds will germinate partially and quickly dry up before their roots reach deep water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ daa Dumɔwui lɛ fã ko baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi oya dani shishifãi lɛ ashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without developing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi ni etswaaa ŋmɔtɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to pollinate them before fruit can form. High temperatures, lack of ground moisture, or strong chemicals can drive away these insects or cause stress that makes the tree drop its flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni ekɛ pollination woɔ mli dani ewoɔ yibii. Teats ni mli wa, ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo tsofai ni mli wa baanyɛ ashwie nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ loo ekɛ haomɔ ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and harm my crop plants much more when the crop plants are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui waa be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: Young crops have shallow root systems and small leaves, making them weak competitors. Weeds naturally grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil food before the young crops get established enough to defend themselves.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii. ni haa efeɔ akaŋshilɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ Jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei bibii lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize so the heat does not burn the young crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa? Koni la ni tsoɔ lɛ akashã dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Maize needs consistent moisture during germination. Planting immediately after the first major, steady rain ensures the young roots get enough moisture to establish deep root systems before mid-season dry spells occur.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛto shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ama shi dani hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why is my farmland producing far fewer cocoa pods today than it did during my father's time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmeii fioo kwraa fe mitsɛ beaŋ lɛ?

english: Over many years, crops absorb vital nutrients from the soil with every harvest. Without putting nutrients back into the soil using organic compost, shade management, or fertilizers, the land becomes exhausted and can no longer feed full crops.
ga: Yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa amɛ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ hulutsoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall with lots of green leaves but produce very few flowers and fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ebaa eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes plants to focus all their energy on leaf and stem growth instead of fruiting. Balancing the soil with nutrients like phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to form strong flowers and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛaato he pɛpɛɛpɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni mli wa.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I harvest more bags at the end of the season?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani makpa baagi babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: No, planting too closely creates heavy competition for sunlight, water, and soil food. The plants grow weak and thin, producing tiny cobs or no cobs at all. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ loo ŋmeii ko kwraa baaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: This is usually Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus prevents the plant leaves from converting sunlight into food, which stops the cassava roots from growing big under the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ lɛ. Virus lɛ tsiɔ tsei ahe baai anaa koni amɛkatsake hulu la amɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ adara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do seeds I save from last year's harvest yield smaller crops than new seeds bought from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Many modern crop seeds are high-yielding hybrids designed for maximum strength in their first generation. Saved seeds lose these special genetic traits in the next planting cycle, leading to uneven growth and lower yields.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei dumɔwui babaoo ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni afee koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ fɔmɔ sui krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do so many flowers drop off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or dry soil as a defense mechanism to preserve water. Keeping the soil moist with organic mulch cools the roots and helps the flowers stay attached to form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛ yashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ okɛ organic mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii amli.

english: Why do the outer leaves of my plantain trees turn yellow and droop during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ asɛɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains lose water quickly through their massive leaves. During a drought, the plant intentionally sheds its lower leaves to conserve water and protect the main stem and growing fruit bundle from drying out completely.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai wuji lɛ anɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ aduawai akui ni miida lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Yam rot is caused by fungi or small soil pests like nematodes, often triggered by waterlogged soil. Excess water around the roots prevents air from reaching the tuber, making it easy for decay organisms to invade.
ga: Fungi loo sũ mli kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ baa, ni bei pii lɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe Shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ bulb lɛ he. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ bɔɔ nii ni miifite lɛ baatutua amɛ.

english: Why do weeds slow down my young cassava growth so drastically during the first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ ha mi yucca lɛ dalɛ ba shi waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young cassava and consume the topsoil water and fertilizer first. Clearing weeds during the first three months allows the young cassava to establish its roots without competing for food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei bibii lɛ ni amɛyeɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmei klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei bibii lɛ aná shishifãi ni amɛkɛ niyenii he akaŋ akaŋ.

english: How does using drip irrigation help my vegetables grow better than watering them with a bucket?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe nu ni akɛ baagi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drip irrigation delivers water slowly and directly to the crop roots where it is needed most. This prevents water loss through evaporation and keeps the soil consistently moist so crops grow faster without stress.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu lɛ yaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli fiofio. ni oya he ni ehe hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ Enɛ baatsi nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei daa oya ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Is borehole water safe and good for watering my crops all year round?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, borehole water is a reliable and clean source of underground water for crops during dry seasons. It provides a steady supply so your plants do not wilt, though it is good to make sure the water does not contain harmful salts.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu ji shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni he tse kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Ehaa nu daa bɔni afee ni otsei lɛ akagbo. Shi ehi hu akɛ ooona nɔmimaa akɛ ŋoo ni yeɔ mɔ awui bɛ nu lɛ mli.

english: What is the best time of day to give water to my crops so they get the most benefit?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni maná he sɛɛ babaoo kɛjɛ mli?

english: The best time to water crops is early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Watering during these cooler times prevents the sun from quickly evaporating the water before the roots can drink it.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu ji leebi loo shwane. Nu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ lɛ haaa hulu la lɛ afee nu lɛ oya dani shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why do my crops produce more yield when given small amounts of water regularly instead of heavy watering once a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ amɛnáa nu fioo daa lɛ? Instead of watering once a week

english: Crops prefer a steady supply of moisture to grow evenly. Heavy watering once a week creates cycles of severe drought followed by root flooding, which causes stress and can make flowers or young fruits drop off.
ga: Tsei lɛ hia ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa baa ni shishifãi lɛ amli nu afua nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa, ni ebaanyɛ eha fɔfɔi loo aduawai bibii agbo.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the hot sun, which helps the plant conserve moisture inside its leaves when water is scarce.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ baa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛ́ nu bɛ.

english: When crops get too little water, they wilt, their leaves dry out, and growth slows down. When they get too much water, the roots drown from lack of air, causing leaves to turn yellow and fall off.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu fioo tsɔ lɛ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, baai lɛ egbiɔ, ni amɛdalɛ baa shi. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do deep-rooted crops survive dry spells better than shallow-rooted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: Deep-rooted crops can push their roots deep down into the ground where moisture remains hidden, whereas shallow-rooted crops rely on the top soil which dries out very quickly under heat.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ, ni egbiɔ oya waa yɛ latsaa be lɛ shishi.

english: Will using heavy machines to dig boreholes or irrigation paths spoil my farm soil for crops?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛfo nubui loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Heavy machinery can compact the soil if used carelessly, making it harder for roots to grow. However, properly using machines to create lasting water sources helps your crops produce more in the long run, provided you till the compacted soil afterward.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ okɛ tsɔnei tsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni okɛfee nu jɛɛhe ni sɛɛ baatsɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni oooha otsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii ni okɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Which crops should I plant if I have limited water available during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu kɛji nu faaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpeas, and sorghum naturally need less water to survive. Vegetables like peppers and tomatoes can also do well with limited water if you use targeted watering methods like drip tubes.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ biɔ nu fioo koni amɛhi shi. Aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nu ni hoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, tamɔ hose ni hoɔ nu lɛ tsu nii lɛ,.

english: Why do fewer weeds grow when I use drip lines instead of flooding the whole field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ fioo kɛ́ mikɛ drip line tsu nii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ nu baawo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Drip lines only wet the soil directly around the crop roots, leaving the soil between the plant rows dry. Weed seeds need water to sprout, so keeping the surrounding soil dry prevents them from growing.
ga: Drip line lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Wet tso shishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tsei akui lɛ ateŋ lɛ agbi. Nu he miihia jwɛi dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ ni aaaha egbi lɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing when rainwater collects in my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air just like humans do. When water fills all the empty spaces in the soil for too long, the roots suffocate, cannot take up food from the ground, and cause the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi hu he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Enyɛɛɛ eye niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I check if my soil has enough water for my vegetables without buying expensive equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha mi-vegetables lɛ ni miheee nibii ni jara wa?

english: You can push a dry wooden stick or your finger into the soil about two inches deep. If it comes out clean and dry, your crops need water; if damp soil sticks to it, there is already enough moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tso ni egbi loo onine awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee inchi enyɔ. Kɛji ehe tse ni egbi Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia nu. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kpɛtɛ he lɛ, no lɛ nu ni mli efɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Watering early in the morning gives plants time to absorb moisture before the sun gets hot, whereas afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can use it.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ mli edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Should I try digging manual water channels on my farm before hiring big machines?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ maka nubu ko mafo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani maŋɔ tsɔne agbo ko?

english: Yes, testing simple hand-dug gutters first allows you to see how water naturally flows across your field without spending a lot of money on heavy equipment right away.
ga: Hɛɛ, nubu ni akɛ niji atsa lɛ kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona bɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔji amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni afiteee shika babaoo yɛ nibii ni tsii ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my field become hard like rock after a heavy machine drives over wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ beni tsɔnei ni tsii tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy machinery presses wet soil particles tightly together, squishing out all the air pockets and forming a hard crust that plant roots and water cannot easily pass through.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii haa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome jogbaŋŋ. Mimɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ mli ni ofee ŋmei ni wa ni tsei shishifãi kɛ nu nyɛŋ atsɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do I get very low prices when I take my tomatoes to the market at the same time as everyone else?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ jara ni baa shi nɛkɛ nɔ beni mikɛ tomato baa jara nɔ yɛ be kome mli kɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ lɛ?

english: When every farmer harvests and sells at the same time, the market becomes full or saturated. Because supply is higher than what buyers need, prices drop sharply.
ga: Kɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ kpa ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli Ani jara lɛ baayi loo ebaayi? Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa fe nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, jara lɛ ba shi oya.

english: Why do my harvested peppers rot quickly on the way to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ni mikpa lɛ fite oya yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Peppers picked in the hot sun keep carrying internal heat, which speeds up decay. Picking them during the cool morning and keeping them shaded slows down spoilage during travel.
ga: Chili ŋmeii ni ajieɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baajie amɛmli dɔlɛ lɛ kɛya. Enɛ baaye abua ni efite oya. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli ni akɛ amɛ to shia lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛfitemɔ aba shi yɛ gbɛfaa mli.

english: Why do my crops drop their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho baai yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Losing leaves is a plant's natural defense trick to survive dry winds and intense heat, as most of a plant's water leaves through its leaf surface.
ga: Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu teemɔŋ sane koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni yɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ateŋ babaoo tsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open after a heavy rain that follows a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ tswaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When thirsty tomato plants suddenly get a large amount of water, the inside of the fruit grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Kɛ́ tomato tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ ná nu babaoo trukaa lɛ tso yibii lɛ mli loo lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings die when planted in an open field without big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse ni tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tender young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them protects the young cocoa from heat while they build strong roots.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ebu cocoa tso lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi ni wa baa.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant maize and cassava together on the same piece of land instead of separately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is ready for harvest in a few months, while cassava takes almost a year to mature. Planting them together lets you harvest maize early while giving ground cover that reduces weed growth and protects soil moisture for the slower-growing cassava.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni eshɛɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmei heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. Companion planting haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa mra ni ehaa ŋmãa ni haa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ baa shi ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛha ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for producing green leaves that feed the plant, so adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baai eŋɔli ni haa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ afeemɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni eha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam tubers grow small or misshapen when the soil is hard and compacted. Creating deep, loose, soft mounds or ridges gives the roots plenty of room to expand downward freely into large, smooth tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi kɛya shi ni amɛfee ŋshɔŋloo agbo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy rain in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soaked, stagnant water because the water cuts off air to the roots. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away quickly so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛta nu ni ekã shi ni edɔ mli. Ejaakɛ nu ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Dark spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium inside the fruit, which often happens when soil moisture fluctuates between very dry and very wet. Regular, steady watering helps the plant absorb calcium smoothly from the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake yɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ waa teŋ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ calcium ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pruning opens up the center of the tree to let sunlight and fresh air pass through. This reduces humidity inside the canopy, which stops fungal diseases like black pod disease from spreading and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni ekanyaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing organic manure helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni maye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which target the tender growing heart of the maize plant. Inspecting your farm regularly and applying recommended natural or chemical controls directly into the leaf funnel early in the morning stops them before they kill the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ tsui ni miida blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛkudɔɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsu nii leebi. Abaatsi nakai ŋmɔji lɛ anaa dani akpata amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Plantain suckers struggle to grow if old roots and pests are left on the bulb before planting, or if planted in dry, unmulched soil. Trimming old root tissue and placing organic mulch around the base keeps the root zone moist and triggers fast leaf growth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baaná naagba akɛ amɛaada kɛji shishifãi momo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tee nɔ ehi bulb lɛ nɔ dani adu. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni sũ ehàaa nɔ. Afoɔ shishifãi momo lɛ ni akɛ organic mulch shwieɔ he. Shishitoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ daa oya.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ready for harvesting so it does not spoil on the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the leaves and husks turn brown and dry, and the kernels become hard enough that you cannot easily dent them with your fingernail.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsɔ otsitsii lɛ anɔ atsɔ mlɛo.

english: Why does my land produce less food when I plant maize on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my corn turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the soil is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Why do vegetables wither in the afternoon sun? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil, so they temporarily wilt to protect themselves from the intense heat.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei gboiɔ be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: What causes my cassava roots to stay thin and small even after spending many months in the ground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii beni mikɛ nyɔji babaoo ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay small if the soil is too hard and packed for the tubers to expand, or if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium that help roots swell.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee bibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ potassium ni yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to the local soil and climate, allowing them to absorb water and nutrients much faster than planted domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛnáa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ amɛmaŋ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily in direct sunlight, so they need temporary shade trees like plantains to shelter them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ anɔ kɛha wɔɔhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants will compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in weak stems and small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or by severe heat stress and irregular watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper flowers drop when temperatures become too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil causing the plant to produce leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa tsei woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Can I prepare my farm land and let it sit for a few weeks before planting my crops when the rains start?
ga: Ani manyɛ masaa he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ni mashi otsii fioo komɛi dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Yes, preparing your land weeks early allows cleared weeds to decompose into rich organic matter and gives the soil time to settle. When the rains arrive, the soil is ready to absorb moisture immediately and support healthy seed germination.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni asaa he otsii komɛi kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ agbala mli ni etsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná be ni ekɛba shi. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo amrɔ nɔŋŋ akɛ ebaaŋɔ nu ni eha dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How soon after planting cocoa seedlings should I check my farm to see if they are surviving?
ga: Beni adu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ tɛŋŋ? Ani esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo?

english: You should inspect your farm within the first one to three months after planting. This early check allows you to spot dead or struggling seedlings that need replacing and ensures young plants get enough shade and water before weeds overtake them.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji kome kɛyashi etɛ mli yɛ be mli ni odu nii lɛ sɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ haa onaa dumɔwui ni egboi loo ni miitao ni ehe miihia ni atsake amɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa dani jwɛi lɛ yeɔ amɛhe.

english: Can I put animal manure on my farm weeks before I actually sow my vegetable seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata miŋmɔ lɛ he otsii komɛi dani madu aduawai lɛ amli dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, applying well-rotted manure a few weeks before planting gives beneficial soil micro-organisms time to break down the nutrients, making them readily available for young seedlings as soon as they germinate.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii otsii fioo komɛi dani adu lɛ, ehaa sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛgbala niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Feemɔ klalo kɛha dumɔwui bibii kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: What special care do my maize plants need once they start flowering and producing tassels?
ga: Ani mi-abɛi tso lɛ he miihia ni akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji ebɔi fɔfɔii ni ebɔi fɔfɔii ni ebɔi fɔfɔi?

english: When maize starts flowering, it enters a critical reproductive phase requiring extra nutrients and moisture. Applying top-dressing fertilizer and keeping the field weed-free during this period helps the plants fill out large, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ bɔi fɔfɔi lɛ Eboteɔ fɔmɔ be ni he hiaa waa ni biɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ krokomɛi lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii ni aha jwɛi akafee jɛmɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cassava plants need extra weeding and care during their first three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko kɛjɛ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first three months are crucial because cassava plants are establishing their root systems underground. Keeping the farm clean early on prevents weeds from stealing light, water, and nutrients needed to form strong tubers later.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ he hiaa ejaakɛ ŋmei tso lɛ miito eshishifãi ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni oooha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ bulbs ni hi jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ mli.

english: What special attention do my cocoa trees need when small green pods start growing on the tree trunks?
ga: Mɛɛ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ he hiaa mi-cacao tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe? Ejeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei akutsei anɔ

english: When young pods appear, you need to inspect the trees regularly for black pod disease and mirid insect damage. Pruning excess shade branches during this phase also ensures good air circulation around the developing pods.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii je kpo Esa akɛ okwɛ tso lɛ mli daa kɛji ŋmeii diji hela kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni efite lɛ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebɔleɔ tso lɛ he. Pods lɛ hu miiya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I do to protect my tomato plants while the green fruits are growing larger?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe be mli ni aduawai eŋɔli lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: As tomato fruits expand, the plants need regular watering, staking to keep fruit off the wet ground, and protection against insect borers to prevent rotting and ensure high-quality produce.
ga: Beni tomato yibii lɛ mli lɛɛ Ehe miihia ni afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa. Okɛ tsei lɛ ama shi bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ akajo foi kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ni etsĩɔ kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni amɛha nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: How long does it take for a plantain sucker to yield a bunch after I plant it in the farm?
ga: Beni adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii kui?

english: Plantain suckers usually take between 9 to 12 months from planting to harvest, depending on soil fertility and rainfall. Proper mulching, weeding, and removing extra side suckers help the plant produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain ŋmeii lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 kɛjɛ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ. Ni kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why are my cashew trees dropping their flowers without setting any nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmeii ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Flower drop in cashew trees is usually caused by pest attacks, fungal diseases like anthracnose, or dry weather stress during the flowering period. Spraying approved protective treatments and pruning infected branches help save the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ yɛ cashew tsei anɔ lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose, loo haomɔ ni jɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ shwie nɔ, ni afolɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are getting enough nutrition to carry their fruits to full maturity?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii ni eda?

english: Healthy, well-fed pepper plants have dark green leaves, steady new growth, and hold onto their blossoms. If the leaves turn yellow or flowers drop early, the crop is lacking water or vital soil nutrients.
ga: Pepper tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Dalɛ hee ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ. Ni eyɛ fɔfɔi lolo. Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo fɔfɔi lɛ shwie shi oya Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my land has good soil for starting a cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni mikɛjeɔ kookoo ŋmɔ shishi?

english: Good soil for cocoa should be deep, dark in color from organic matter, and able to hold water well without becoming waterlogged, which can rot the plant's roots.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha kookoo lɛ mli kwɔ. Eyɛ su ni tsuɔ ni jɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli amli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu ato jogbaŋŋ ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: When is the best time of the year to clear land and plant my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli ni esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni adu nii?

english: It is best to clear land late in the dry season and plant right at the start of the main rainy season so young plants get steady water to build strong roots before the heat returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi he lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee ni odu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli koni eha tsei bibii lɛ aná nu ni hoɔ daa koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa dani hulutsoo be lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Can I plant cassava in the middle of my cocoa farm, or will it hurt the cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ ko teŋ loo ebaafite ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cassava roots grow large and take up a lot of nutrients and water from the ground, which can starve young cocoa plants. It is better to use plantains or food crops that do not compete as aggressively for root space.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛnáa niyenii kɛ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha hɔmɔ aye kookoo tsei bibii. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ plantains loo niyenii tsei ni kɛ hiɛdɔɔ etswaaa shishifãi ahe akaŋ lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crop trees turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or it is getting too much direct sunlight without enough shade and ground moisture.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ ni hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many small flowers, but most of them fall off without making pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lack of nutrients, or because insects like midges were not available to pollinate them. The tree naturally drops excess flowers it cannot support.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo akɛni kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo tso lɛ mli fɔfɔi lɛ ha tso lɛ haoɔ lɛ hewɔ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ kpo.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to prune or cut away branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ofolɔ loo ofolɔ kookoo niji lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or dead branches, allowing sunlight and air to flow through the tree. This reduces fungal diseases and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni egboi lɛ. koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai baa shi ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do black spots appear on my cocoa pods when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains increase humidity, which helps the fungus that causes Black Pod disease spread rapidly through splashing water drops from one pod to another.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔ nu ni eshwieɔ kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds lower the money I can make from my farm if I leave them growing?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha shika ni manyɛ maná kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi kɛji miha amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. They also hide farm pests and diseases that can destroy your harvest before you pick it.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Amɛkɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni baanyɛ afite onibii lɛ hu teeɔ dani okɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color from green or deep red to a clear yellow or orange, and make a hollow sound when you tap them gently.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse nɔ. Ni efeɔ gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ otswa nɔ fioo.

english: Why does my harvested local rice always have small stones and dirt mixed inside it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa lɛ hiɛ tɛi kɛ muji be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Stones and dirt get mixed into rice when the crops are threshed directly on the bare ground. Threshing your harvest on clean tarpaulins or mats keeps the grains clean and free of debris.
ga: Tɛi kɛ muji futuɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛ́ ashwie ŋmãa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmaa lɛ shwie tarp loo tsɔne ni he tse nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmaa lɛ he atse ni sũ akafee nɔ ko.

english: How do I know if my harvested rice is dry enough to be bagged for the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo kotoku mli ni mikɛmaje jara nɔ?

english: You can test grain dryness by biting a grain kernel—if it snaps sharply without bending, it is properly dried. Well-dried rice prevents mould and stays fresh during storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni ŋmaa lɛ egbi ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmaa lɛ ni oooye lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwu lɛ efo ni efooo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ, etsĩɔ ŋmãa naa ni ehiɔ shi ehee yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Does leaving my cut rice on the open soil for a few days hurt its quality?
ga: Ani kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ mli afee fɛo?

english: Yes, leaving cut crops directly on the soil exposes them to moisture, insects, and dirt, which stains the grains and lowers the price buyers will pay for them.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ, kooloi bibii kɛ muji baa amɛnɔ, ni no haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ muji ni ehaa jara ni mɔ ni heɔ lɛ baawo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my stored rice sometimes turn dark or smell bad after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmãa ni ato lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ loo eŋɔɔɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Dark color and bad smells happen when grain is bagged while still damp, allowing mould and bacteria to grow. Drying your grains thoroughly in the sun before bagging stops this spoilage.
ga: Su ni tsuɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii baa kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo kotoku mli be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, fungi kɛ bacteria baanyɛ ada. Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ hulu mli dani awoɔ kotoku mli lɛ haa nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ kpaa.

english: Why does my local rice break into small pieces when I take it to the grinding mill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akuɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa lɛ mli bibii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be akɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rice breaks easily during milling if the grains were dried too quickly under hot sun or if the moisture was uneven. Drying paddy rice slowly in light sun keeps the kernel strong and whole.
ga: Omɔ fãa oya yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ gĩ oya tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. aloo eyɛ hulutsoo ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee Omɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbiɔ blɛoo Yɛ hulu la ni mli jɔ lɛ mli Eyeɔ ebuaa omɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛyeɔ emuu.

english: What is the benefit of soaking and steaming my rice paddy before taking it to be milled?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ nu mli ni ashãa dani ashɛreɔ lɛ he?

english: Steaming or parboiling rice before milling hardens the grain so it does not break, makes the outer husk come off cleanly, and locks vitamins inside the grain.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa shã loo okɛshã parboil dani okɛ ŋmãa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni amɛkumɔɔɔ. Ha kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ ajie ehe fɛo. ni okɛ vitamini ato ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli

english: Why do some grains in my rice field mature faster while others are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi daa oya yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi daa lɛ? Eŋɔli lolo?

english: Uneven ripening happens when seeds of different varieties are mixed together at planting. Using certified single-variety seeds ensures your whole field grows and matures evenly.
ga: Nibii ni shwereɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi futu dumɔwu ko mli. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi kome pɛ ni awo he odaseyeli tsu nii lɛ, ehaa ogbɛhe muu lɛ fɛɛ baashwere ni eshwere jogbaŋŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do buyers in town prefer imported foreign rice over the local rice I grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ fe maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers prefer imported rice because it is thoroughly cleaned, uniform, and free of dirt or stones. When local rice is harvested and processed cleanly, it can match or exceed imported quality.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ ejaakɛ atsuuɔ he jogbaŋŋ, efeɔ ekome, ni muji loo tɛi bɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmãa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli ni atsu he nii yɛ gbɛ ni he tse nɔ lɛ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmãa ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ akpã gbee loo eteke nɔ.

english: How can an extension officer like you help me get better prices for my crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni extension nitsulɔ tamɔ bo lɛ aye abua mi ni maná jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Extension officers teach practical techniques for planting, harvesting, and cleaning crops so your farm produce meets high market standards and earns top market prices.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni aduɔ nii ahaa. ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe saamɔ Bɔni afee ni okwaayeli nibii lɛ ashɛ jarayeli he mlai ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ahe ni amɛná jara ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers do practical field demonstrations instead of just talking to us?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ feɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ wɔ baawie kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Field demonstrations allow you to see and practice new farming techniques step-by-step, making it easy to master proper crop handling without risking mistakes on your own farm.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa onaa okwaayeli he ŋaai heei ni okɛtsuɔ nii fiofio, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooole bɔ ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ohe wooo tɔmɔi amli yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How much annual rainfall do my cocoa trees need to produce a good harvest?
ga: Nugbɔ enyiɛ he hiaa mi-cacao tso lɛ daa afi koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Cocoa trees generally thrive best with around 1,500 to 2,000 millimeters of rainfall spread evenly throughout the year, as consistent soil moisture is needed for healthy flowering and pod growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ji 1,500 kɛyashi 2,000 mm ni aja mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Afi muu lɛ fɛɛ Enɛ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ pod ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry out much faster now during dry spells compared to past years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ oya kwraa yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Shortfalls in annual rainfall combined with rising temperatures cause soil moisture to evaporate quickly, leaving less water stored in the ground for plant roots to drink.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa afi kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Enɛ haa nu fioo pɛ atoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants curling up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves inward during dry spells to trap moisture and reduce surface area exposed to the sun, which slows down water loss while they wait for rain.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ nugbɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize crop if the rain suddenly stops right when the plants begin to flower?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa beni tsei lɛ bɔi fɔfɔi?

english: Flowering is the most sensitive stage for maize. A shortage of water at this time prevents proper pollination, which results in cobs with missing kernels or empty cobs.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa. Nu ni faaa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ mli dumɔwui bɛ loo ŋmei lɛ feɔ efolo.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even though the leaves above ground look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli moŋ?

english: When there is a shortfall in rainfall, cassava plants use their limited water to keep their leaves alive for survival instead of sending energy down to expand the underground tuber roots.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ nu fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ehi shi. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ kɛ yaa si konɛ e ha nɛ tuber sisi a mi nɛ wa.

english: When soil moisture drops too low during hot weather, pepper plants get stressed and drop their flowers to save energy and water for their own survival.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi tsɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛha amɛwala.

english: How can I check if there is enough water in my soil before I sow my crop seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Dig down a few inches, scoop a handful of soil, and squeeze it; if it forms a moist ball that holds together without dripping water, the soil has enough moisture for seeds to germinate.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shi inchi fioo komɛi. Kpɔ̃ɔ muji ni okɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni okɛmimɔ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ko ni mli edɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi lɛ yɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops turn pale yellow after a week of non-stop heavy rainfall that floods the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsi kome ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni ekpaaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Too much standing water drowns the soil by pushing out air, which suffocates plant roots and prevents them from taking up essential nutrients like nitrogen that keep leaves dark green.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eeetsi kɛya he kroko lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli waa.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open when heavy rain falls after a long dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: After a dry spell, sudden heavy rain causes tomato plants to take up water rapidly, making the inside of the fruit expand faster than the dry skin can stretch, which causes cracking.
ga: Beni etsɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. ni kɛ ŋmeii baa

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and snap during the dry windy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ yɛ nyɔji ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ baa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Strong, dry winds pull water out of broad plantain leaves much faster than the roots can draw water from dry soil, causing the stems to lose internal water pressure and break.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni efoɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to direct its energy into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni oha tsei kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives the plant the food it needs to grow green and healthy.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my land better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have roots that pull nitrogen directly from the air and deposit it into the dirt. When the roots decay, they leave this free plant food behind in the soil for future crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, amɛshiɔ tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: If I buy high-yielding hybrid seed once, why can't I just save seeds from my harvest to plant next season?
ga: Kɛji mihe dumɔwu kome pɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent plants to give high yields. The seeds you harvest from those crops lose that special strength, resulting in smaller cobs and much lower yields if planted again.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni okpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii baa, ni kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields every year even when I plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ nii yɛ be kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every time they grow. Without adding fertilizer, manure, or rotating crops with legumes, the soil becomes exhausted over time and can no longer nourish healthy crops.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni adu amɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ tsuuu nii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli, ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or lack of water. When the weather is too dry or hot, the plant sheds flowers to conserve energy and survive rather than spending energy growing fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ he. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why does my cassava take several months before the tubers start growing big under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: During its early months, a cassava plant spends all its energy developing strong roots to anchor itself and growing leaves to capture sunlight. Only after establishing plenty of leaves does it store extra food underground to swell the roots.
ga: yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa ni ekɛbaatswa ehe shi ni ekɛ baai akwɛ̃ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Beni baai babaoo eba pɛ kɛkɛ ni akɛ niyenii krokomɛi toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the young leaves. This damages the leaf tissue and can spread plant viruses, causing leaves to twist and stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baa fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tso lɛ hela lɛ eshwã. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛdara.

english: Why should I clear and burn old stems from my field before planting fresh seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei momoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mashã amɛ dani madu dumɔwui heei?

english: Old plant stems and leftover roots often harbor hidden pest eggs and fungal spores. Clearing or composting old crop residue breaks the life cycle of pests and prevents diseases from jumping directly onto your new seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso shishifãi momo kɛ shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai. Tso momo mli nibii ni efite lɛ ni ooofɔ loo okɛwo mli lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ashihilɛ gbɛ, ni ehaa helai shwieɔ odumɔwui heei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaf tips usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the food they need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plants recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cassava plants shed leaves during dry weather to conserve water and protect themselves from drying out. Once the rains return, the plants will naturally sprout fresh green leaves again.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely high or when the soil goes from very dry to overly wet. Keeping soil moisture steady and providing partial shade during hot peaks helps the fruits form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo fã ko ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ fa babaoo lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai aba.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant maize seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When planted too close, crops compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leads to weak, thin stalks and much smaller cobs than plants given proper spacing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bibioo kwraa fe tso lɛ ni sɛɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sun to manufacture food that builds large tubers underground. Staking lifts leaves off the ground toward sunlight while keeping them safe from rot and damp soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni feɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking elevator lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants turn soft and rot when rainwater sits in my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ gbii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess water sits on the field for too long, it cuts off air to the roots, causing them to suffocate, turn soft, and die.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ehaa amɛmuɔ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does maize grown from my saved seeds produce smaller yields than certified seeds bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni adu kɛjɛ mi dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high yield and vigor in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and hard on the trees before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Dark, dry cocoa pods are a sign of Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, cool air. Clearing excess farm shade and removing infected pods helps stop the spread.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ diŋ hela he okadi. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli ejɔ mli kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔ mli hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops actually reduce the size of my final harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mihaa tɛŋŋ ni mi naagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ dalɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing them early gives your crops full access to the resources needed to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ Ajiemɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo amɛnibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide natural shade and conserve moisture in the soil to help the cocoa seedlings survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi koni eye ebua kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and snap during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkuɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves have a large surface area that loses water rapidly in dry, windy weather. When the soil lacks moisture, the plant intentionally shuts down and lets older leaves collapse to protect its core stems.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ yɛ he ko ni da ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ amli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ yiŋtoo ji ni eŋmɛɔ ehe ni ehaa baai momoi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu eshishigbɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my small maize plants turning purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the plant cannot take up phosphorus from the soil. This often happens when the soil is too cold, too wet, or lacks proper nutrients early in the growing season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie fɔsfɔs kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ, edɔ tsɔ, loo niyenii ni sa bɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do some of my maize cobs have missing kernels and empty spaces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii kɛ he ko ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Missing kernels happen when hot temperatures or dry spells destroy the pollen while the maize is flowering. Without proper pollination, the seeds on the cob cannot form.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be kpata pollen ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa bɛ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ cob lɛ nɔ lɛ hu nyɛŋ afee.

english: Curled and yellow leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny whiteflies that suck the sap from the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long without good drainage. Excessive water suffocates the roots and allows underground fungi to attack the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu kpakpa hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Nu babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or high nitrogen levels. Under stress, the plant sheds its blossoms to save its own energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo. yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing tall and thin instead of bushy and full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miidara ni amɛmiifee bibioo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmɔji ni amɛyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants stretch upward and become leggy when they do not receive enough direct sunlight. They expend all their energy growing taller to reach for light rather than growing thick leaves and stems.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛbaatsɔ naji kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛkɛ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ baai kɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa.

english: When crops do not get enough nitrogen from the soil, they move whatever nitrogen they have left from their older, lower leaves up to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ejieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops remain short and stunted even though I cleared all the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee kuku lolo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ moŋ?

english: Stunted growth usually means the soil lacks essential plant nutrients, is packed too tightly for roots to spread, or has tiny worm-like pests called nematodes attacking the root system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are my young maize seedlings turning yellow and looking weak shortly after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crops are extremely delicate when they first germinate. Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or has too much water around the fragile roots, which prevents the young plant from getting the energy it needs to grow strong stems.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo ebɔle he. Shishifãi ni waaa Enɛ haaa tso bibioo lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ tso lɛ shishifã ni wa.

english: How deep should I put my seeds in the dirt when planting so they grow properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Seeds should generally be planted at a depth about two to three times their size. If you bury a seed too deep, the young shoot uses up all its stored energy before reaching the surface and dies; if planted too shallow, the sun dries it out.
