ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee amɛdalɛ toi enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ. Kɛji ofu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ dani amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaagbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to build a shade cover over my new cocoa nursery plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa shĩa kɛha mi-kookoo tso hee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants in their first stage of life are very sensitive to harsh sunlight. Shade protects their tender leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist until the plants are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshihilɛ shishijee mli lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Shade lɛ buɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: How do I know if my cassava plants are putting their energy into the roots instead of just growing tall leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ miiwo shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe baai kakadaji lɛ pɛ?

english: If cassava plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy making thick, tall leaves above ground while leaving the tubers underneath small. Balancing fertilizer ensures the plant shifts its vitality to growing heavy tubers in the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbaashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ tsei bibii lɛ ashishi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛyaa bulbs ni tsii ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: When is the most critical time to feed fertilizer to my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi tomato tsei lɛ amli?

english: The most important stage to nourish tomato plants is right when they transition from growing stems to producing their first flowers. Feeding them at this delicate stage gives the plant the extra strength needed to turn flowers into heavy fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ yɛ tomato tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mli ji be mli ni amɛtsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi ni miida lɛ amli kɛyaa amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ niyenii yɛ nɛkɛ be ni mli wa nɛɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ kroko ni amɛkɛtsakeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amɛfeɔ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or sudden dryness. The plant drops its flowers to save its own life because it doesn't have enough water and strength to support fruit development at that moment.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ shweremɔ bɛ nakai beaŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra leaves or weak shoots from my growing garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo baai loo tsei bibii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes extra shoots that drain food away from the fruit. By cutting weak leaves, you help the plant direct all its nutrients into making the remaining fruits larger, heavier, and healthier.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Baai ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni eha aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ adara, etsii ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when the plantain bunch starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbee shi beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and as the fruit bunch gets heavy, the top weight pulls the delicate root system out of the moist soil. Supporting the trunk with a sturdy wooden pole holds the heavy weight until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ tsii lɛ, tsiimɔ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ baagbala shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tso ni mli wa afi tso lɛ sɛɛ. Ebaanyɛ etere muji ni tsii kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves curl up in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural way of protecting itself from losing water in intense sun. It shrinks its leaf area to survive the hottest hours of the day, showing you that the crop is stressed for moisture.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ he. Ehaa baa he bibioo ko baa koni ehi shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsɔɔ bo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihao kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why should I pluck off some small, overcrowded fruits from my tomato crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ aduawai bibii ni eyi obɔ kɛ mi tomatoi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing a few small or damaged fruits allows the plant to send its full energy and weight to the remaining ones, ensuring you get larger, high-quality tomatoes rather than many tiny, weak ones.
ga: Yibii bibii ni akɛbaa loo ajieɔ yibii ni efite lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ egbɔjɔmɔ fɛɛ mli kɛyaa tomatoi ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ tomatoi wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, o náa tomato nyafii nɛ e he wami fuu.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and dry starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea early in the crop's life helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe awa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea tsu nii yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after I harvest my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛŋmɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to produce strong stems and full fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ená shishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on instead of leaving them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves into the sunlight so they can make more food for the root, resulting in larger yams. It also keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and disease.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli koni amɛfee niyenii babaoo amɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ baatsɔ agbo. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai hu anaa.

english: How does covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass help them during dry weather?
ga: Bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops moisture from evaporating in the sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from growing and taking nutrients from your crops.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: What causes small holes and dirt like sawdust inside the funnels of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii kɛ muji, tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn leaf cones lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds hidden inside the center of the maize plant. Catching them early and applying recommended pest treatments or an ash mixture directly into the leaf funnel helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni taoɔ niyenii ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo sũ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves develop dark spots and wither right after heavy rain showers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain splashes soil that contains fungal spores onto the lower tomato leaves, causing diseases like leaf blight. Planting on raised soil mounds and trimming lower leaves off the soil helps stop rain from splashing fungi onto the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ haa shikpɔŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ tomato baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ helai tamɔ baa mli tsɛŋemɔ baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ nɔ kɛ shishigbɛ baai ni afoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers and tiny pods when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛ fɔfɔii kɛ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ bɔi tswaa lɛ

english: Dry Harmattan winds suck moisture out of the air and soil, stressing the cocoa tree. The tree naturally drops young pods and flowers to save water and protect itself from dying during the dry weather.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ miihao. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ ŋmeii kɛ amɛfɔfɔi bibii lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛsu naa koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can check readiness when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, or by carefully scraping away soil near the base of one plant to check root size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji efee klalo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. Aloo kɛtsɔ sũ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ dara ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only in the first planting. If you save and replant those seeds, the second generation will grow unevenly and yield much less grain than the original seed.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji obua nakai dumɔwui lɛ anaa ni odu ekoŋŋ lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from intense heat. By rolling their leaves, the plants reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun, which stops water from evaporating too quickly during the hottest hours.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei haa baa lɛ nɔ hulu la lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaa lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my tomato plants without forming fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, making it impossible for the plant to produce seeds and fruit. When it gets too hot, the plant sheds its unpollinated flowers to conserve energy and moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛwo dumɔwui kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I cut down all the large shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mifoɔ cacao tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that get burnt by direct, harsh sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air cool and preserving soil moisture so young cocoa plants can build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ ji koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and drop early when planted in open fields without tall trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have huge leaves that lose water rapidly under strong sunshine and high heat. Without partial shade or proper windbreaks, heat stress drains moisture from the plant faster than its roots can pull it from the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo fã ko loo kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu ni sa bɛ lɛ, Heat stress lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and look burnt after I apply chemical fertilizer during a sunny dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer requires plenty of soil moisture to dissolve safely. In hot, dry soil, concentrated fertilizer draws water out of the plant roots instead of feeding them, which causes leaf burning and dehydration.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni sũ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i babaoo dani enyɛ etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni nu shwieɔ amɛmli.

english: Why does my fresh animal manure make my crops dry up when I put it directly around the plant roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei hee lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmei lɛ wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh manure undergoes a natural decomposition process that releases strong heat and gases. If placed directly against roots, this heat burns the root tips and prevents the plant from absorbing water.
ga: Manure hee tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ gbɛ ko ni jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kpo lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛwo shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ nɛɛ baashã shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaŋɔ nu.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables rot so quickly when I pack them tightly in closed sacks to send to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛwo kotokui ni aŋã mli jogbaŋŋ koni akɛya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested crops are still alive and breathing. When tightly packed without air movement, they generate heat and trapped moisture, creating a hot environment where mold and rot spread rapidly during transit.
ga: Nibii ni akpa lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛmiimu. Kɛji akɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tsiii ehe lɛ Amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ baa ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni akɛ nibii majeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn dark and spoil within two days of taking them out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ewo duŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots react with air and heat, initiating a fast oxidation process that breaks down the starch inside. Exposure to tropical sun and warm air speeds up this internal decay.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ, amɛfeɔ amɛnii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he. Enɛ haa oksideshin nifeemɔ ko ni yaa oya ni fiteɔ starch ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ haa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli fitemɔ yaa oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the day even when there is standing water on top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe. Standing water suffocates the roots, causing them to drown and stop pumping water up to the rest of the plant, which makes the leaves wilt despite the water.
ga: Tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa amɛshwieɔ nu mli ni amɛkpaa nu ni amɛkɛyaa tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ni no haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up completely above ground before the yam tubers under the dirt are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miigbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ afee klalo lɛ?

english: At the end of the rainy season, the yam plant naturally transfers all its food energy from the leaves down into the tuber. The dying vine above ground signals that the underground tuber is finishing its growth and maturing.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ, Sweet potato tsei lɛ jieɔ amɛ niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Wein tsei ni miigboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiidara.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up into tight rolls during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl during the heat of the day to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant conserve moisture and prevent water loss when the weather is extremely hot.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ehaaa nu lɛ afite kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without producing any peppers when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants experience heat stress and drop their flowers to save energy and water for their own survival rather than spending energy on growing fruits.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛha amɛwala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ kɛdu aduawai

english: Why is it better for me to harvest my vegetables early in the morning rather than late in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa mi-aduawai lɛ leebi moŋ fe shwane mli lɛ?

english: Vegetables harvested early in the morning are full of water taken up overnight and are cool. Harvesting in the afternoon heat makes produce wilt fast, lose weight, and spoil quickly before reaching the market.
ga: Akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai ni akpaa leebi lɛ amli lɛ woɔ mli, ni akɛnuɔ nyɔɔŋ kome ni ehaa edɔɔ. Nikpamɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni akpaa lɛ shwieɔ oya, egbɔjɔɔ ni efiteɔ oya dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have soft leaves that easily burn under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and provide broad leaf shade, protecting the young cocoa from heat and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa shade kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing huge green leaves above ground but very small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, cassava plants use all their energy to grow leafy stems instead of moving stored food down into the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ baa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my corn seeds fail to sprout when I plant them too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry limited food energy inside them. If buried too deep, the young sprout runs out of energy pushing through the heavy soil before it reaches the surface sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ amɛmli. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ baaho dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn pale yellow when rain water sits on my farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns crop roots by blocking air in the soil. Without air, roots cannot breathe or absorb nitrogen, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ nitrogen. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with seeds naturally adapted to wake up fast and absorb tiny amounts of rain, allowing them to outgrow domestic crops that need settled moisture.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa. Eyɛ dumɔwui ni etsake amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛte shi oya ni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ fioo ko. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya fe shia tsei ni he hiaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow and dry while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Fungal diseases often start near the damp soil on older bottom leaves. Water splashing from rain or watering transfers soil fungi onto lower leaves first before spreading upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai jeɔ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ masɛi. Nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛya baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ dani egbɛ eshwa kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why do I see more insect pests eating my crops early in the morning and late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi ni yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Insects hide during the hot afternoon sun to avoid drying out, coming out to feed when temperatures cool down during the early morning and evening hours.
ga: Kplukai baahi amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkagbi. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye niyenii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ leebi maŋkpa kɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: If the rains stop early this season, what will happen to my young maize plants?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Mɛni baaba mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: When rain stops early, maize plants cannot get enough moisture to fill their grain cobs, which causes the kernels to stay small or dry up completely before harvest time.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra Abɛi tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo ŋmaa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii loo amɛgbiɔ kwraa dani nikpamɔ be lɛ shɛɔ.

english: Excess water floods the soil and suffocates plant roots by cutting off oxygen, causing the roots to rot so they can no longer feed the plant.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua tso lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of the plant mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source plants need to stay green and build strong stalks.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ jɛɛhe titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛma ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help improve my field?
ga: Te cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha he ni miyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural food supply that helps the surrounding maize grow stronger without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ. Edaa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi awo mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and roll inward when the afternoon heat becomes very high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli beni shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves roll inward during hot periods to trap internal moisture and reduce water loss through their leaf surfaces, protecting the plant from drying out.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni ekɛba nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Buu tsei ahe koni amɛkagbi

english: Why are my garden eggs growing tall and skinny without making many fruits under large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo yɛ tsei wuji lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Vegetable plants need direct sunlight to produce flowers and fruit; when planted under shade, they waste all their energy growing tall toward the light instead of producing food.
ga: Aduawai tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo shishi lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ beni amɛkwɔɔ kɛyaa la mli yɛ niyenii ni amɛbaafee lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, light, and soil food, making all the plants weak and reducing overall yield.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow poorly even when the soil looks fertile?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni baa nii moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil, effectively starving your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young flowers during long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi bibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers during dry weather to save energy and water so the main tree can survive the dry season.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli.

english: How do armyworms cause my maize crops to stop growing new leaves?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii baafee tɛŋŋ amɛtsi ŋmãa ni baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ naa?

english: Armyworms hide inside the center growing funnel of the maize plant and eat the tender new leaves before they have a chance to open.
ga: Asraafoi amli ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo dani amɛnáa hegbɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: I grow only cocoa on my farm. Why is it risky for me to rely only on cocoa?
ga: Miduɔ kookoo pɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ kookoo pɛ nɔ?

english: Relying only on cocoa leaves you without income during the off-season or when diseases strike. Diversifying by planting food crops gives you extra food and steady income throughout the year.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ cocoa pɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha oná shika ko yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔɔɔ shi loo be mli ni helai baa lɛ. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooofee srɔtoi lɛ haa onáa niyenii kroko kɛ shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Can I plant food crops on the same land where I grow my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside cocoa maximizes your land use. It helps you harvest farm produce for family use and sale while your cocoa trees are growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii babaoo. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii ni jɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni oweku lɛ kɛtsu nii ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ be mli ni o-cacao tsei lɛ miida lɛ.

english: I planted a crop variety on my farm, but the rainy months ended before the crop was ready. Why did this happen?
ga: Miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi nyɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ ba naagbee dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bafee klalo. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: Different crop varieties need different lengths of time to mature. If the rainy season in your area is short, longer-duration varieties will not get enough water to complete their yield.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi biɔ be srɔtoi dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ Tsoi srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: What should I do if the rainy season in my area is too short for my usual crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ faaa tsɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ daa lɛ?

english: When rainy months are not long enough, switch to quick-maturing crop varieties that can finish growing before the water runs out, or buy improved seeds adapted for shorter seasons.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ tsɔ Moŋ lɛ, tsakemɔ kɛya tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni baanyɛ agbe dumɔ naa dani nu lɛ agbe naa lɛ anɔ. Aloo hemɔ dumɔwui ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni okɛ ohe awo be kukuoo lɛ mli.

english: I heard about the 'Colombia' cassava variety. Why might it fail to mature on some farms?
ga: Minu ‘Colombia’ ŋmei henɔ lɛ he. Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji komɛi nyɛɛɛ amɛdu lɛ?

english: The 'Colombia' cassava variety requires a specific number of wet months to yield fully. If planted in areas where the rain stops early, it won't have enough time to finish maturing.
ga: Columbia’ ŋmei lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmei lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni nugbɔ lɛ kpaa oya lɛ, enaŋ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Where can I get crop stems or seeds that will grow fast if my local ones take too long?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana ŋmeii loo dumɔwui ni baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji akɛ mimaŋ dumɔwui lɛ miihe be babaoo tsɔ?

english: You can visit approved agricultural input suppliers and dealers. They supply certified, fast-maturing planting materials that help you overcome short rainy seasons.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara mɛi ni kɛ okwaayeli nibii haa kɛ mɛi ni jaa amɛ lɛ. Amɛhaa dumɔ nibii ni yɔɔ odaseyeli, ni shwereɔ oya ni yeɔ ebuaa bo ni oyeɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ nɔ kunim.

english: If my neighbor gets better harvests during short rains using new crop varieties, how can I get the same?
ga: Kɛji mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ná ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku mli kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi heei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni efee nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: Your neighbor is likely using improved planting materials. You can achieve the same success by sourcing certified seeds or stems directly from recognized farm suppliers.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ dumɔ nibii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ miitsu nii. Obaanyɛ onine ashɛ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ahe ni ooohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli nihɔɔlɔi ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I make my daily farm work easier without spending a lot of money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi daa gbi ŋmɔ lɛ afee mlɛo ni mikɛ shika babaoo tsuuu nii?

english: Modern farming relies on working smart with natural resources provided in the environment. Using natural rainfall, good soil management, and proper crop selection reduces manual labor and costs.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli damɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛhaa shihilɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nilee mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ tsu nii shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni ahala lɛ baaye abua ni adesa nitsumɔ kɛ shika ni afiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: How do natural resources help make crop farming less stressful for farmers today?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni haoɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ okwaafoi lɛ?

english: By working in harmony with natural weather patterns and using natural soil nutrients, you spend less effort fighting nature and achieve better crop yields with less manual strain.
ga: Kɛtsɔ nitsumɔ ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpãa gbee nɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, Okɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ baawuu oshi adebɔɔ. ni oná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni haomɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli

english: How can I make sure I have farm produce to sell throughout the year instead of waiting for one season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ maná nibii ni mahɔ̃ɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ moŋ fe be kome pɛ?

english: Do not focus on a single cash crop like cocoa alone. Growing a variety of fast-growing food crops alongside your tree crops ensures you have produce to harvest and sell all year round.
ga: Kaaha ojwɛŋmɔ ahi shika ŋmɔshi nibii kome tamɔ kookoo pɛ nɔ. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ni ooodu yɛ otsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa onáa nibii ni obaakpa ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: What happens to my maize if I harvest it while it is raining?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋma lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpa beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting maize in the rain traps moisture inside the husks and grains. This dampness creates an ideal environment for mold to grow, causes grains to rot quickly, and drastically reduces the market quality and shelf life of your crop.
ga: Abɛi ni akpaa yɛ nugbɔ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni baakwɛ̃. Ehaa ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ oya ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ajarayeli kɛ amɛshihilɛ be baa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tall crops lie flat on the ground after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii kakadaji lɛ ekã shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Rainwater adds extra weight to the tops of mature plants while softening the wet soil around their roots. This combination makes crops like maize or sorghum top-heavy, causing them to fall over (lodge) and rot if they remain in contact with wet mud.
ga: Nugbɔ nu haa tsei ni eda lɛ ayiteŋ feɔ mlɛo, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ hu feɔ blɛoo. Nɛkɛ nibii ni akɛfutuɔ mli nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni tsii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi (efoɔ) ni egboɔ kɛji ekɛ muji ni mli efɔ lɛ tee nɔ ebɔ.

english: Why do my mature rice grains spoil so fast if heavy rains hit just as they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni eda lɛ miifite oya nɛkɛ? Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa be mli ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: When ripe grains get soaked by rain, they absorb water rapidly and can start sprouting directly on the stalk or drop off into the muddy soil, leading to severe crop loss.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ shwie dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ lɛ Eŋɔɔ nu oya ni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo egbeeɔ muji lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ waa.

english: Is it good for me to hire a big combine harvester for my small farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe tsɔne agbo ko ni akɛkpaa nii kɛhaa miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Combine harvesters are built for large, open fields. On a small plot, the machinery cost is high, it is hard for the machine to maneuver, and it may damage small crop patches, making manual labor or small shared machinery more cost-effective.
ga: Atswaa tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa nii ni akɛfataa he lɛ kɛhaa ŋmɔji wuji ni agbele naa. yɛ he ko bibioo nɔ Tsɔnei ahe nyɔmɔwoo babaoo Ewa akɛ aaatsi tsɔne lɛ he. ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔji bibii. Ehaa adesa nitsumɔ loo tsɔnei bibii ni akɛhaa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I drive heavy machinery on my farmland when the soil is very wet after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsɔnei ni tsii tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy machinery presses wet soil together tightly, crushing air pockets. This causes soil compaction, which stops water from draining properly and makes it very difficult for future crop roots to grow deep.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii haa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ feɔ ekome jogbaŋŋ. Kpɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ akɛ amɛaaya shɔŋŋ.

english: Will using a harvesting machine damage my grain seeds more than harvesting by hand?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baafite midumɔwui lɛ fe bɔ ni mikɛ nine baakpa amɛ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: If crops are harvested when they are too damp or if machine settings are incorrect, mechanical harvesters can crush or crack the seeds, making them easily rot or attract insects during storage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ tsɔne lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ejaaa. Tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ loo agbala dumɔwui amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ oya loo egbalaa kooloi kɛbaa amɛhe yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I take too long to harvest because I am working alone on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ be babaoo kpa ni mikpa ejaakɛ mikome too mitsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving mature crops in the field for too long exposes them to pests, wild animals, intense heat, and sudden rains. Grains will dry out too much and shatter onto the ground, resulting in high crop losses.
ga: Nibii ni eda ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Enɛ baaha tsei nɛɛ aná kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, koo mli kooloi, latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ. Ŋmaa lɛ baagbi tsɔ ni ebaagbala shikpɔŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni laajeɔ.

english: Why is it better for me to invite my neighbors to help me harvest quickly instead of doing it slowly over weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafɔ̃ mikutsoŋbii lɛ nine koni amɛbaye amɛbua mi kɛkpa nikpamɔ oya lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee lɛ blɛoo otsii babaoo lɛ

english: Harvesting rapidly as a group ensures all crops are collected at peak ripeness before unexpected bad weather or pests destroy them, keeping the quality and market value of your harvest high.
ga: Nikpamɔ oya yɛ kui amli lɛ haa abuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ anaa yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Dani kɔɔyɔŋ fɔŋ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Enɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ mli nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ jarayeli jara lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains develop a powdery mold on them during damp weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and humidity allow fungal spores to feed on the damp crop. Wet weather speeds up this mold growth, which ruins seed germination and can make the crops unsafe to eat.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ lɛ haa fungal spores lɛ yeɔ tsei ni mli efɔ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa oya. ni fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: How does sudden rain on my freshly harvested crops affect their safety for eating?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ saa niyenii he shweshweeshwefeemɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Unexpected rain rehydrates gathered crops, raising their moisture level and creating a warm, damp environment where harmful toxins like aflatoxins grow rapidly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni abua naa lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ. Ha fɛ̃i aya hiɛ ni ofee shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i. Biɛ ji he ni tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ yaa hiɛ oya yɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to need fertilizer to grow well these days when the land used to yield food without it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ? Be ko ni eho lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Farming the same piece of land continuously removes the natural food and nutrients from the soil over time. Fertilizer replaces those lost nutrients, giving your crops the strength and nourishment they need to grow healthy and give you a good harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ okwaayeli jieɔ niyenii kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ. Ehaa otsei lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough before I start planting my cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa dani mabɔi ŋmei dumɔ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels moist, and crumbles easily in your hands. If your soil is very hard, pale, or sandy, it lacks nutrients and organic matter, meaning it will need manure or fertilizer to support a healthy crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Henumɔ ni mli edɔ ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ oyɛ onine mli Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ ŋã lɛ, no lɛ niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii koni eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to grow leaves. It can also happen when too much water drowns the roots, preventing the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi, ni no haaa tso lɛ atao niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and dropping off the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or by a viral infection. Protecting the crop early with neem oil or suitable treatment keeps the leaves flat so the plant can produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ mli Abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsamɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ afee tso lɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni tso lɛ awo yibii.

english: The first rain after a long dry season is often a 'false start' followed by days of intense heat. Planting too early causes the dry soil to scorch the young seeds before the true rainy season established water in the ground.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ ji ‘Apasa shishijee’ ni gbi ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Dumɔ mra tsɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa dumɔwui bibii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ feɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to weed around my young crops as soon as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early ensures your young crops get all the food and space they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ waa. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baaha otsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ he fɛɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool moisture it needs to survive its early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground. This naturally enriches the soil, helping your maize grow better without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-ŋmã lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like potassium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil during flowering helps the blossoms turn into full fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize grain develop mold and spoil when I store it in my crib?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ kɛ́ mikɛto tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mold grows when maize is stored before it is completely dry inside. Leaving grain to dry thoroughly under the sun until the kernels are hard prevents dampness, which keeps fungi and grain-eating insects away.
ga: Mold lɛ daa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to dani egbi kwraa yɛ emli. Kɛ́ oha dumɔwui lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi kɛyashi amɛhe wa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmaa lɛ akashɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight while they are small. Large shade trees protect young cocoa from intense heat, reduce soil water loss, and help recreate the forest environment cocoa naturally needs to establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni amɛbuɔ kookoo yibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha nu ni laajeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni eye ebua ni afee koo shihilɛ ni kookoo he hiaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily right when the fruit bunches start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the surface of the soil. As the fruit bunch grows heavier, the plant becomes top-heavy, allowing strong winds and soft, wet rain-soaked soil to pull the root system right out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsii waa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plant leaves use to stay green. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the topsoil, or the soil may simply be tired and in need of compost or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei ahe baai kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: What is eating the soft inner leaves of my maize plants and leaving tiny holes and green dust inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ? mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli lɛ no sɛɛ lɛ eshiɔ bu bibioo ko kɛ sũ eŋɔli yɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Moths lay tiny eggs inside the central funnel of young maize, and once the caterpillars hatch, they feed on the tender growing leaves inside before the leaf fully unwraps.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ni woɔ wui bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Yɛ ŋmãa abifao lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛbaaye baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ mli lɛ dani baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe kwraa.

english: Why do I need to clear the grass and put long sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ ni mikɛ niji kakadaji awo mli koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make the food that grows big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves spread out into the light and off the damp soil, which also prevents soil diseases from infecting the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa la mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ akamɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground in the rainy season before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli dani akpaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away quickly. Too much trapped water suffocates the roots by cutting off air, allowing rot-causing fungi present in wet soil to infect and ruin the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli oya. Nu ni emɔ mli tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela awo ŋmeii lɛ amli ni efite amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up into tight cups during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a pepper plant's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, helping it conserve internal moisture and prevent excessive water loss during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ pepper tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ mli, ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ fe nine yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress or irregular watering. When temperatures get too hot or soil moisture changes rapidly from very dry to very wet, the plant cannot properly pollinate its flowers and sheds them to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa hewɔ. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ he ni egbi waa kɛyaa he ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ajieɔ amɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: How do weeds hurt my main crops if there is plenty of soil space for all plants to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ awui kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for invisible resources like underground moisture, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Because wild weeds often grow faster than crops, they consume these essentials first, leaving your crops weak and undersized.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nibii ni anaaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la, taakɛ koo mli jwɛi lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii No hewɔ lɛ amɛyeɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafee bibii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my land make my maize crop grow stronger the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa mi-ŋmei lɛ daa waa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the legumes finish growing, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as natural food for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ egbe amɛkwɛ̃mɔ naa Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-cornmeal ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and wither during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive, soft leaves that dry out and burn quickly under direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain or shade trees beside them keeps the air humid and protects the leaves until the cocoa roots grow deep enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ahi shi ni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ shishifãi lɛ baa mli bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible to make food. When the vines climb stakes, the plant leaves get maximum light, which fuels the growth of large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã ni hulu la ashɛ nɔ bɔ ni aaanyɛ koni ahoo. Kɛ wain tso lɛ kwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ baaná la ni fa fe fɛɛ. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ daa lɛ

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips in a V-shape is a classic sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to build strong, green leaves.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa yɛ V-shape mli lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests every year when I plant the same crop on the same farm continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi be mli ni miyaa nɔ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Every crop draws specific nutrients from the soil. Planting the same crop repeatedly drains those exact nutrients without giving the soil time to recover, causing yields to drop.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: How does adding animal manure or decomposed leaves help my crops grow better in sandy soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloo ŋmei loo baai ni egboi ni mikɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Organic matter like manure works like a sponge in sandy soil. It traps rainwater so roots can drink and slowly releases natural plant food over time.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ. Emɔɔ nugbɔ nu koni shishifãi lɛ anu ni ejieɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my young maize plants have small holes in the central leaves and dark sawdust-like dirt inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ yɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep center (whorl) of the maize plant during the day to feed on young leaves away from heat and predators.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ (rings) ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, the roots suffocate and rot away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without forming any tomatoes during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing the pollen inside flowers to dry up and become infertile. The plant drops the flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why does my plantain stem snap and fall over right when the fruit bunch starts to get heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ fãa trukaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ mli wa lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have strong woody trunks or deep taproots; their stems are made of soft, water-filled leaf sheaths. Supporting them with propping poles prevents heavy bunches from bending or uprooting the plant.
ga: Plantains bɛ tsei ahe tsei ni wa loo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Akɛ baai bibii ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ fee tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni fiɔ esɛɛ lɛ fiɔ esɛɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kuu ni tsii lɛ nyɛɛɛ abɔle loo eshishi.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and taller than my young crop seedlings after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with naturally aggressive root systems designed to grab water and soil nutrients instantly, outcompeting young crops that grow more slowly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Afee lɛ koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ehi fe tsei bibii ni daa blɛoo lɛ.

english: How should I arrange my crops when planting them outside in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mato minibii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ du yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: You should plant them outside in four neat lines to keep your field organized and easy to manage.
ga: Esa akɛ odu amɛ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ejwɛ mli koni oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee mlɛo akɛ oookwɛ nɔ.

english: What distance should I leave between the rows and individual plants when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ kɛ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ahi tɛŋŋ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: You should use a spacing of 75 centimeters between the lines and 20 centimeters between the individual plants.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni ji sɛntimita 75 atsu nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ kɛ sɛntimita 20 yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ.

english: Can I plant these crop seeds directly outside in the open field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui nɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, you can plant them directly outside in the open field, laying them out in four lines.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu yɛ kpo nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli. Ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ kui ejwɛ mli.

english: How far apart should one plant be from the next plant in the same row?
ga: Te esa akɛ tso kome kɛ nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ sɛɛkuu kome mli lɛ afee shɔŋŋ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: You should leave a space of 20 centimeters between one plant and the next along the row, while keeping 75 centimeters between the rows.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi aaafee sɛntimita 20 yɛ tso kome kɛ nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ teŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli, ni aaafee sɛntimita 75 ahi sɛɛ mli.

english: How many lines of crops should I set up outside in my plot?
ga: Tsei akui enyiɛ esa akɛ madu yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to plant them in four lines outside in your field area.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amɛ yɛ sɛɛkuu ejwɛ mli yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to leave up to 75 centimeters between my crop lines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafee nɔ ni fe sɛntimitai 75 lɛ?

english: Leaving 75 centimeters between lines gives enough room for the crops to spread out and allows space to work between the rows, while keeping plants 20 centimeters apart in four lines outside.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji sɛntimitai 75 lɛ haa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. ni gbɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ ateŋ Ha tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 20 yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋtayaai 4 lɛ anɔ.

english: How many seeds am I supposed to drop into a single hole during planting?
ga: Yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ, dumɔwui enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛwo bu kome mli?

english: You should plant the seeds one by one in each hole so that the growing plants do not compete heavily with each other.
ga: Esa akɛ odu dumɔwui lɛ ekomekomei yɛ bu lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli bɔni afee ni tsei ni miida lɛ akatswa amɛhe akaŋ waa.

english: Why shouldn't I drop two or three seeds together in one hole when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui enyɔ loo etɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Planting seeds one by one prevents overcrowding and ensures each crop gets sufficient food and sunlight to grow properly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ekomekomei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the correct standard spacing measurement to follow when planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ kɛ́ adu mi tsei lɛ?

english: The recommended planting distance is 75 by 20 centimeters, planting one by one in four lines outside.
ga: Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ aduɔ lɛ ji 75 x 20 centimeters, ni aduɔ ekomekomei yɛ kponɔgbɛ linei ejwɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I make sure my crops do not grow too close together and fight for soil nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛkaye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ?

english: To stop crops from fighting for nutrients, plant them one by one at a distance of 75 by 20 centimeters in four lines outside.
ga: Ani oosumɔ ni okpa tsei ni kɛ amɛhe wuɔ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he lɛ? Dumɔ amɛ komekomei yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 75 x 20, ni okɛ amɛ awo kponɔgbɛ linei ejwɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight so their leaves can capture solar energy. Exposing the leaves to maximum sunlight fuels the growth of larger and healthier tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ hulu hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ awo hulu la babaoo mli bɔ ni aaanyɛ lɛ, ebaawo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen in the soil, or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe and take up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛye nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce only tiny roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miiya hiɛ waa nɛkɛ? Ani oyɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi bibii pɛ yɔɔ mli?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in its underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the main tree for food and water. Removing extra suckers directs all the soil nutrients to the main tree, resulting in much larger bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi suckers babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa sũ mli niyenii fɛɛ yaa tso titri lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa kuu ko ni da kwraa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets extremely hot or when water supply drops suddenly. The heat and dryness stress the plant, causing it to abort flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ba shi trukaa. Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo haomɔ tsei. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akpa nitsumɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves look droopy in the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than roots can drink it from the soil. The droopiness is a temporary defense mechanism to conserve water until the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni haa mɔ wɔɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do people say that planting cowpeas or beans helps improve the soil for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny living organisms on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ tsei.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily when strong winds blow before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa dani akpa ŋmaa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over easily if plants are crowded together, if soil nutrients like potassium are low, or if root-feeding insects have damaged the root system that anchors the plant in the ground.
ga: Abɛi baanyɛ agbo oya kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ. Kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium lɛ faaa Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ shishifãi lɛ efite shishifãi ni ŋmɛɔ tso lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I lay dry wood pieces or dry leaves around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei ni egbi loo baai ni egboi abɔle he lɛ? miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishitoo

english: Laying dry wood or leaves (mulching) covers the soil layer to trap moisture during hot Ghanaian sunny days. As the wood rots, it also turns into rich food for the soil, helping your crops stay hydrated and strong.
ga: Ni akɛ tsei loo baai ni egbi (mulch) baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli yɛ Ghana gbii ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ miifite lɛ Ebafeɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa onibii ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: How does burying crop waste inside the soil help my plants grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni mikɛfuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Burying old crop waste creates a rich nutrient layer under the topsoil. As it decays, it softens the ground so crop roots can spread easily and draw up extra food and water.
ga: Nibii ni egbɔ ni aduɔ lɛ ni afuɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ egbo lɛ Ebaagbɔjɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shishifãi baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛha niyenii kɛ nu jɛɛhe kroko.

english: Are all the small creatures living in my farm soil bad for my crops?
ga: nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli Ani nakai shihilɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ miiná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: No, not all soil creatures are harmful. Useful organisms break down dead plants into quick soil food, while harmful pests attack live roots. Knowing the difference helps you avoid killing the good soil helpers.
ga: Dabi, jeee shikpɔŋ nɔ bɔɔ nii fɛɛ ji oshara. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ gbálaa tsei ni egboi lɛ amli oya ni amɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni hiɛ ka lɛ. Kɛ́ ole srɔtofeemɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okagbe shikpɔŋ yelikɛbualɔ kpakpa.

english: Why are pests eating the leaves of my young crops little by little every night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii daa gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Night insects chew leaves slowly to feed themselves. When plants lose their leaves bit by bit, they lose their ability to trap sunlight and make food, which slows down their overall growth.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kooloi ŋmɔɔ baai fiofio koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛna amɛ niyenii. Kɛ tso ko baai lɛ fite fiofio lɛ Ebaafee nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaamɔ hulu la ni ekɛbaahã niyenii lɛ. Enɛ haa dalɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do termites attack the plant stems and dry wood on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa tsei akutsei kɛ tsei ni egbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Termites naturally search for wood and dry plant matter for food. If there is no moisture or dead organic material in the soil, they will start feeding on your living crops instead.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii taoɔ niyenii yɛ tsei kɛ tsei ni egbi nɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ loo nibii ni egboi bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baabɔi tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ yeli.

english: What happens if I apply fresh animal manure directly to my plant roots?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh manure is too strong and hot for crops, which can burn root tissues and interfere with how plants absorb water. Always let manure dry and decompose before adding it to your crop layer.
ga: Manure hee mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni edɔ waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. ni baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ amli fãji ni etsĩ nu ni tsei lɛ nuɔ lɛ naa. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni efite dani okɛwo tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why does a pest attack cause my crops to produce small yields even if the plant doesn't die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ gbooo moŋ?

english: Even minor insect damage forces the plant to waste energy repairing its tissues instead of growing fruit or tubers. This disruption in its daily life leads to smaller harvests.
ga: Kplukai bibii po ni fiteɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛsaa fãji lɛ yɛ aduawai loo ŋmeii ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ. Nɛkɛ daa gbi shihilɛ mligbalamɔ nɛɛ kɛ kpamɔ bibioo baa.

english: How do I make sure the fertilizer I put in the ground actually gets to the plant roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shɛɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Fertilizer must be placed in the soil layer near the active roots and covered lightly with soil or mulch. Moisture then dissolves the fertilizer so roots can drink it up easily.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi ni tsuɔ nii lɛ ahe, ni akɛ sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko aha nɔ. Fɛ̃i lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ mlɛo.

english: How can I set up simple traps to catch insects destroying my farm without using expensive chemicals?
ga: Mafee amale ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mamɔ kooloi bibii ni miifite miŋmɔ lɛ ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can use bright yellow containers filled with soapy water placed around your field. Flying pests are attracted to the color, land in the water, and get trapped before they can damage your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsɛnsi ko ni mli tse ni mli tse ni nu ni akɛ saamɔ eyi mli obɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛbɔle he. o-rice ŋmɔji lɛ Gbalaa kooloi ni fɔ̃ɔ lɛ kɛyaa penti lɛ nɔ, amɛgbeeɔ nu lɛ mli, ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe dani amɛfiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my crops turn yellow and dry up during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Bottom leaves dry up when root pests or hard soil prevent the plant from getting enough food from below. Adding rotten organic material around the root layer helps restore healthy nutrient flow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ shishifãi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai loo shikpɔŋ ni wa tsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shishi. Nibii ni egbo ni akɛfataa he lɛ shishifã lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the difference between organic fertilizer and the chemical fertilizer I buy at the store?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni miheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Organic fertilizer comes from natural plant or animal matter and builds healthy soil over time, while chemical fertilizers feed the plant quickly with artificial nutrients but do not improve soil structure.
ga: Organic fertilizers jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei loo kooloi amli ni amɛmaa shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya kɛ niyenii ni akɛfee lɛ. Shi ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: When is the best time to start feeding fertilizer to my crops after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aje ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ shishi?

english: You should apply fertilizer once the seeds have sprouted and established roots—usually a few weeks after planting—so the young plant is actively growing and ready to absorb nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni amɛshishifãi etswa shi. (Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ) koni eha tso bibioo lɛ ada ni efee klalo ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ atsu nii.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my farm during heavy rainfall or wait?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli loo mamɛ?

english: It is best to wait for light rain or moist soil. Heavy rainfall can wash the fertilizer away before your crops have a chance to take it in.
ga: Ehi akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ fioo loo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ.

english: Can putting too much fertilizer on my crops actually harm them?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ awui?

english: Yes, using too much fertilizer can burn the crop's roots and leaves, causing the plant to wither or die instead of growing stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã otso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ loo egboɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I help my young cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand harsh weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ anaa?

english: Giving cocoa trees organic nutrients helps them build deeper root systems and stronger trunks, allowing them to absorb moisture and thrive during dry periods.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa kookoo tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhaa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi ni edaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Is organic fertilizer suitable for mature cocoa trees, or is it only for young plants?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sa kɛha kookoo tsei ni eda loo tsei bibii pɛ?

english: Organic fertilizer is great for mature cocoa trees because it slowly releases nutrients into the soil, keeping the tree energized to continuously produce pods.
ga: Organic ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hi kɛha kookoo tsei ni eda. ejaakɛ ejieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii be fɛɛ be.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by lack of nutrients, drought, or pests. Feeding the tree properly gives it the strength to hold flowers and turn them into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, hɔmɔ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ oha otso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ená hewalɛ ni ekɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔii ni efee ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves on my plants turning pale yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is struggling to feed the growing plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha tso ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if my soil needs fertilizer before I start planting my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had thin stems, or gave low yields, your soil nutrients are likely exhausted and need fertilizer to rebuild.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo, amɛshishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ, loo amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo Ekolɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu efo ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni etswa ekoŋŋ.

english: Do I need to clear the weeds around my crops before I put fertilizer down?
ga: Ehe miihia ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ dani awoɔ ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Yes, always clear weeds around your crops first so that your plants get all the nutrients rather than competing with weeds for the fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kɛya. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ. koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ jwɛi baatswa akaŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen nutrients or getting too much standing water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives the plants the food they need to turn green and grow strong.
