ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen niyenii loo eyɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize on that same land next season, the maize feeds on that stored nutrient to produce bigger yields.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baaye niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmãa babaoo aba.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from under the leaves. Spraying your crops early with soapy water or natural neem oil solution helps clear these pests before they ruin the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni ooofɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ mra Soap nu loo adebɔɔ mli neem mu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to leave large shade trees on our cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔshi tsei wuji yɛ wɔ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect young cocoa leaves from harsh sun, keep the soil cool and moist during dry spells, and help cocoa trees stay healthy and bear pods for many years.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni eda afii babaoo.

english: How does putting dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the hot sun from drying out the ground, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly rots into rich food for the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii babaoo kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight with their leaves. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more energy the plant sends down to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaji lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ, babaoo ni esa akɛ tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ awo sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: Wait until your soil receives at least two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the ground. Planting too early in dry, warm soil causes seeds to dry up and die before they can sprout.
ga: Mɛɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ aná oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Cassava roots rot when rain water sits in the soil without draining away. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess water drain off so roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejeee kpo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely during flowering. Regular watering at the base of the plant keeps flowers attached until fruits form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛmɔ be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi jɛmɛ kɛyashi aduawai baaje kpo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning brown and dry under the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaf surfaces that burn easily in direct sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them shields the young cocoa leaves from heat and preserves soil moisture while the trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛɔ Enɛ baabu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my vegetable seedlings with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle aduawai dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the hot sun from evaporating water in the ground, keeps the root area cool, and prevents weeds from taking light and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or have too much nitrogen in the soil, the plant puts all its energy into growing upper leaves to reach sunlight instead of storing carbohydrates in its underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛdaraa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ carbohydrates baato amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds when sowing?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu nii?

english: Spacing maize seeds roughly 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between plants ensures that each plant receives enough sunlight, root space, and soil water to form large, full cobs.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni miihe ashɛ sɛntimita 75 kɛ sɛntimita 40 yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yam plants are natural vines that need to climb upwards so their leaves can spread out and capture full sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground to prevent leaf rots and encourages bigger tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli wain tsei ni esa akɛ akwɔ koni baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni baa lɛ akafite ni eha bulbs wuji lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a clear sign that the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main element crops use to build green leaves and grow strong stems.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa shishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji nɔ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why should I wait a few weeks after applying fresh poultry manure before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni mikɛ kooloi aŋɔli hee efata he dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure generates strong heat and high chemical levels as it breaks down, which can burn tender plant roots. Letting it decompose in the soil for a few weeks makes the nutrients safe for young seeds to absorb.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ tsofai ni fa babaoo baa kɛji akumɔ mli. ni baanyɛ ashã tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ Kɛ́ oha egbo yɛ sũ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni dumɔwui bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Growing the same crop every season consumes the exact same soil nutrients over and over while giving crop-specific pests a permanent home. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa be lɛ biɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ shii abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe kooloi lɛ náa shia ni amɛhiɔ shi daa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the ambient temperature becomes extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet quickly. Maintaining steady watering during flowering helps the flowers form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ oya. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my chili pepper plants curling up into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ mi chili baai lɛ ebɔle kɔɔpoi bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early protects the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tips down the middle, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tso lɛ daa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: This leaf curling and discoloration is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by planting stems from sick plants. Uprooting infected plants early and planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties helps protect your farm.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ amɛhe su tsakeɔ. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo kɛtsɔ tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ ŋmei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Kɛ ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil switches abruptly from very dry to very wet. Giving your crops consistent water at the roots and providing light shade during extreme midday heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, overly damp, and shaded conditions during heavy rains. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let sunlight reach the crop and removing infected pods prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, edɔ tsɔ, kɛ shade yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my yam mounds early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young yam shoots grow slowly at first and cannot easily compete with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures the yam plant receives all the nutrients it needs to build big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato tso lɛ ni enáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny pests called nematodes or banana weevils can eat away at the roots and corm, making the plant weak. Packing soil tightly around the base and supporting heavy trees with bamboo or wooden props keeps them standing upright.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii, amɛbaanyɛ amɛye shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii. weaken the plant Okɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ abɔle shi shiŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmeii loo tsei afi tso lɛ sɛɛ waa koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops roll up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural way of saving water during heat, similar to how humans sweat or seek shade. As long as the leaves unroll in the cool evening or after watering, the plant is simply protecting itself from drying out.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ dɔlɛ be mli. Etamɔ bɔ ni adesai shwieɔ latsaa loo amɛtaoɔ hulutsoo. Shii abɔ ni ajieɔ baai lɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli loo beni afɔ amɛ nu sɛɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛkɛ koni ekagbi.

english: Why are the new leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and growing close together like a bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: This condition is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips, or a plant virus they carry. Controlling these pests early with appropriate sprays or soapy water treatments allows the leaves to open up and grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips kɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ baa. loo tsei amli helai ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni sa loo nu ni akɛ saamɔ fee lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛgbele ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants have plenty of big green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpeas receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves instead of flowers and pods. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen from the air, so they need much less fertilizer than crops like maize.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai wuji yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe tsei tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are the leaves on my sweet orange trees covered in a sticky black powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni mli tse ehà mi tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: The black powder is a mold that grows on the sweet waste left behind by sap-sucking insects like aphids or mealybugs. Spraying the tree to get rid of these insects clears up the sticky waste and stops the black mold from blocking sunlight on the leaves.
ga: Black powder ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ aphids loo mealybugs ni nuɔ nu lɛ eshiɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie tsei lɛ anɔ koni egbe kooloi bibii nɛɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie jwɛi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ, ni ebaatsi ŋmeii diji lɛ anaa koni ekatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I use a maize sheller machine instead of beating my dried corn with sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Beating corn with sticks cracks the grains, which lets insects and mold inside easily. A sheller gently removes kernels without breaking them, keeping your grain clean, intact, and ready to fetch a higher market price.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso tswa ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ fãa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii baahi mli. Kraki lɛ baajie dumɔwui lɛ fiofio ni amɛkumɔɔɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ ahe tseɔ, amɛhe tseee ni amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaahe jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding well-composted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my harvested corn spoil so quickly when I store it in woven sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛto kotokui ni akpɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Corn spoils quickly if it is put into storage before it is completely dry, or if moisture gets into the sacks. Drying your corn thoroughly and using airtight storage bags keeps insects out and prevents mold from growing.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ dani egbi kwraa. aloo kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bote kotoku lɛ mli Abele lɛ ni ooogbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni kooloi akabote mli ni ŋmɔtɔ hu akakwɛ̃.

english: Missing grains happen when the maize plant does not get fully pollinated, which often occurs if the crop lacks water or suffers from extreme heat during the flowering stage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛhe kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu efo tso lɛ mli loo hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miikpe yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without making big fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii wuji kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, spending all their energy stretching upwards to reach light rather than growing strong stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaawuu koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛshwieɔ ŋwɛi koni enine ashɛ la nɔ. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ hyɛɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ yiblii nɛ tsii.

english: Why do grain buyers pay less money for my corn if it has dark spots on the kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmaa lɛ woɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii diji yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots usually indicate mold infestation, which produces harmful toxins that make food unsafe for humans and animals. Buyers look for clean, spotless grains to ensure the crop is safe to eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko eba. Enɛ haa tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara ni haaa niyenii afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai kɛ kooloi baa. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ ŋmaa ni he tse ni nɔ ko bɛ he koni amɛkwɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: Will adding chemical fertilizer to my field make the food unsafe for my family to eat?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni mikɛbaafata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baaha miweku lɛ niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ?

english: No, chemical fertilizers simply supply essential soil minerals like nitrogen and phosphorus that plants naturally need to grow. When applied in correct amounts, they help produce safe, nutritious food.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus pɛ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei akwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ bɔ ni sa mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli baa.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds each season instead of planting grains saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du ngma nɛ i ngɔ ngɛ ye nyagbe ngmɔ ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Grains saved from high-yielding hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, producing smaller plants with lower yields. Certified seeds are specially bred to give strong, reliable harvests every time.
ga: Ŋmãa ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛwoɔ yibii babaoo amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii ni mli wa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the roots of my crops help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil, blocking direct sunlight from drying out the earth, keeping roots cool, and saving moisture so your crops stay green longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni onibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do worms attack my maize leaves right in the center funnel where the new leaves come out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi ŋmãa baai lɛ yɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ ni agbeleɔ he ni baai heei lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm target the central funnel because those young leaves are soft, moist, and tender to eat, while the deep fold protects the worms from heat and predators.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall flukes lɛ tsɔɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ. Ejaakɛ nakai baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli edɔ, ni amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛji aye. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ buɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily in harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade plants like plantain or cassava alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa trees from direct heat and retains soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya kɛji hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantain loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ baa. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do I need to stake my yam plants with tall wooden sticks as they begin to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji atswa mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ama shi be mli ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need physical support to expand their leaves toward sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot soil, reduces fungal disease, and helps the plant produce leaves efficiently so it can grow larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛgbala amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛ hulu lɛ akpee. Staking baaha baai akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi, ni eye ebua tsei ni amɛwo baai jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips backward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛyashi amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is a sign that your maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure early in the plant's growth restores leaf color and helps produce healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ́ ebaa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ baafata he yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ shishijee bei amli. Ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm field help the crop I plant there next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, they leave nitrogen in the soil, which feeds the next crop like maize without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite Amɛshiɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot branches growing straight up from the main trunk of my mature cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those fast-growing shoots, often called water sprouts, steal water and nutrients from the rest of the tree without producing cocoa pods. Removing them improves air movement to prevent disease and directs energy back into developing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛɛ akɛ nu mli tsei. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ hei krokomɛi. tso lɛ nɔ ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔi efeee lɛ Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni helai akabote mli. ni okɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ awo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afeemɔ mli.

english: How does covering the bare soil around my crops with dried leaves or dry grass keep them from wilting?
ga: Mulching bare soil around Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni egboi amli lɛ akagbo?

english: Covering the ground with dry plant matter creates mulch, which acts like a blanket over the soil. Mulch blocks hot sunlight from drying out the dirt, keeps crop roots cool, and retains moisture in the soil long after the rain stops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Muji lɛ baatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni ebaaha muji lɛ akagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ

english: Why do weeds in my field grow so much faster than my young crops during the early rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to survive tough conditions and rapidly steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight from young crops. Clearing weeds early within the first four weeks gives your crops a fair chance to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: When selecting plantain shoots to plant, why should I choose sword suckers with narrow leaves over water suckers with wide leaves?
ga: Yɛ plantain tsei ni esa akɛ adu lɛ halamɔ mli Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala klante tsei ni baai lɛ mli tseee lɛ fe nu tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ?

english: Sword suckers have strong root connections to the parent plant and large food reserves, allowing them to grow into sturdy plantain trees that produce heavy bunches. Water suckers look leafy early on but have weak root systems and yield small fruit.
ga: Swordsuckers yɛ shishifãi ni kɛ amɛ tsaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he kɛ niyenii jɛɛhe ni da fe no. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni he wa ni woɔ ŋmeii wuji. Nu ni shwieɔ nu lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ baai yɛ shishijee mli. Shi eyɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni ewoɔ yibii bibii.

english: Why does cassava spoil so quickly within a few days after I dig it up from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots are cut away from the main plant and exposed to air, chemical reactions trigger rapid decay within 48 to 72 hours. To avoid loss, leave tubers in the ground until you are ready to sell or process them into food immediately after harvest.
ga: Beni afoɔ ŋmei shishifãi kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni akɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. Tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa efiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli koni akafite. Shi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaahɔɔ loo obaatsu he nii ni ofee niyenii yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without setting any fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out flower pollen, preventing proper fertilization so the blossoms drop off unused. Providing partial afternoon shade and keeping the soil evenly moist during hot periods helps flowers develop into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi fɔmɔ ni sa lɛ naa No sɛɛ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni akɛtsuuu nii. Kɛ́ akɛ shwane mli hulutsoo fã ko ha, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like pencils during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ pensil yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat to reduce their surface area and prevent water loss. It is the crop's natural defense mechanism showing that it is stressed for water and trying to conserve moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nu he haomɔ shishi, ni eebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their lower leaves as soon as the dry season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ eshishigbɛ baai lɛ shi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its lower leaves when water becomes scarce to reduce the amount of water it loses through transpiration. This allows the plant to survive droughts by keeping its underground roots alive.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji nu faaa koni ekɛba nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ nu ni faaa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli kɛtsɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛhiɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Will spraying water directly over the leaves of my pepper plants during hot afternoon sunshine harm them?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaye amɛ awui?

english: Sprinkling water on leaves under intense sun can cause leaf burn, as water droplets act like tiny magnifying glasses. It also creates a warm, moist environment that encourages fungal diseases. It is best to irrigate early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu mli nui ni hoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hu baa ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ he hewalɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi loo shwane.

english: Why are my vegetables growing bigger near the center of my field than at the far edges where water barely reaches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ fe ŋshɔi lɛ anaa he ni nu shɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops need a consistent volume of water to absorb nutrients and grow properly. Crops further away from the main water source get less water coverage, causing them to grow slower than those receiving full water coverage.
ga: Tsei hia nu babaoo be fɛɛ be koni amɛnu niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ nu jɛɛhe titri lɛ he lɛ baaná nu fioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei daa blɛoo fe tsei ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato stems rot and collapse when I give them too much sprinkler water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛkuɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo mi-sprinklers lɛ amli fe nine daa gbi lɛ?

english: Excess water floods the small air spaces in the soil, starving the crop's roots of oxygen. This suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungal diseases that rot the stem at ground level.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ shoo, ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do crops in the transition zone dry out much faster than those grown in the deep forest areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ tsakemɔ hei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kooi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: The transition zone experiences higher temperatures, longer dry spells, and stronger dry winds than forest areas. These conditions strip moisture from both the soil and crop leaves at a much faster rate.
ga: Tsakemɔ he lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni nɔ kwɔ. Be kakadaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa fe kooi amli hei Shihilɛi nɛɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei ahe baai fɛɛ amli oya kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato plants start flowering early when I miss watering them for a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔmɔ shishi mra beni mikɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ otsi kome lɛ?

english: When a crop senses water stress, it panics and feels its life is threatened. It quickly produces flowers and seeds as an emergency effort to reproduce before it dries up completely.
ga: Kɛ tsei nu nu he haomɔ he lɛ Ebaafee gbeyei ni enu he akɛ ewala eba oshara mli. Ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui oya akɛ oyaiyeli mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni ekɛbaafɔ dani egbiɔ kwraa.

english: Does applying water to my dry soil help my crops take up solid fertilizer faster?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa tsuɔ nii oya?

english: Yes, crop roots cannot eat solid fertilizer directly. Water dissolves the fertilizer particles into a liquid form that the crop's roots can easily drink and use for growth.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa tɛ̃ɛ. Nu shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ efeɔ nu ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ anu ni amɛkɛtsu nii kɛha dalɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops whenever I turn on water sprinklers across the whole field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni matswa tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, aggressive plants with strong root systems that can steal water and nutrients faster than cultivated crops. When sprinklers shower water over wide open spaces, weeds take quick advantage of the moisture.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe yɔɔ gbeyei ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aju nu kɛ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu yɛ hei ni gbɛ eshwa lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ kɛ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii oya.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting the right amount of moisture in the soil without fancy tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni sa ni mikɛ nibii ni yɔɔ fɛo tsuuu nii?

english: Push a dry stick or your finger about three inches deep into the soil near the plant root. If it comes out clean and dusty, the crop is thirsty; if damp soil sticks to it, the crop has enough moisture.
ga: Tsɔ tso ni egbi loo onine mli aaafee inchi etɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ehe tse ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ Kumai ye ŋmɔshinii lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my mango trees produce so many more fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Mango trees thrive on high temperatures. Strong heat stimulates their flowering and accelerates fruit development, leading to a much larger harvest during hot weather.
ga: Mango tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ shi ni ehaa aduawai lɛ daa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, abaanyɛ akpa babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Is the natural hot weather we experience here in Ghana good for growing fruit trees like mangoes?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni wɔnaa yɛ Ghana lɛ hi kɛha tsei ni woɔ yibii tamɔ mango lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: Yes, Ghana's hot weather is ideal for mangoes because these trees rely on warm temperatures to fuel their growth and produce high yields of fruit.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mango ejaakɛ tsei nɛɛ damɔɔ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛha amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Does high heat help fruit crops grow better, or does it harm them?
ga: Ani dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ loo eyeɔ tsei awui?

english: For crops like mangoes, heat is essential. They use the warmth from the sun to drive their growth processes and build up energy for fruiting, so more heat generally leads to more fruit.
ga: Kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ mango Dɔlɛ he hia. Amɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ kudɔɔ dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ kɛha yibiiwoo. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ babaoo haa aduawai babaoo baa.

english: Why do mango trees bloom and set fruit during the sunny, hot season instead of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ fe nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ?

english: Intense sunshine and heat signal to the mango tree that it is the right condition to produce flowers and set fruit efficiently, leading to heavy fruiting.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ haa mango tso lɛ leɔ akɛ shihilɛi lɛ hi kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni tsii

english: Why do I see a sudden burst of young mangoes forming after a period of high heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango yibii lɛ shwereɔ trukaa kɛ́ akɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli be fioo lɛ?

english: Periods of strong heat act as a biological trigger for the mango tree, accelerating its natural development and causing a quick surge in fruit formation.
ga: Be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ko ni wala yɔɔ mli ni kanyaa mango tsei lɛ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli shweremɔ yaa oya ni ekɛ yibii ni jɛɔ mli baa oya baa.

english: Why does the main mango harvest always coincide with the hottest months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, afi lɛ mli nyɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli mango kpamɔ titri lɛ?

english: The timing of the harvest aligns with the hottest months because maximum warmth provides the continuous heat energy the tree needs to fully mature and yield an abundant harvest.
ga: Nikpamɔ be lɛ kɛ nyɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ kpãa gbee. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Should I plant my mango trees in full open sunshine or under the shade of bigger trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu mango tso yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ faŋŋ loo yɛ tso agbo ko shishi?

english: You should plant them in full open sunshine. Mango trees need direct heat and light to produce well, so keeping them under dense shade will lower your harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ odu yɛ he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ. Mango tsei lɛ he miihia dɔlɛ kɛ la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛwo hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ, ebaaha onibii ni obaawo lɛ aba shi.

english: Will my mango trees produce good yields if the weather stays cool and cloudy for a long time?
ga: Ani mango tsei baawo yibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ mli jɔ ni atatu ewo mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: No, cool and cloudy weather slows down the tree's growth processes. Mangoes require consistent heat to trigger flower production and develop healthy fruits.
ga: Dabi, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni atatu yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi. Mango he miihia dɔlɛ ni yaa nɔ daa koni eha fɔfɔii afeemɔ aya hiɛ ni ewo aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How exactly does heat help the mango fruits mature and ripen on the tree?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dɔlɛ yeɔ ebuaa mango ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Heat speeds up the natural internal chemical reactions inside the plant, allowing the fruits to grow faster, build up sweetness, and ripen on time.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ yaa oya. Ehaa aduawai lɛ daa oya ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni ahoɔ yɛ be naa

english: How do tropical fruit trees use weather heat to support their growth?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shikpɔji anɔ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛdalɛ?

english: Fruit trees like mangoes convert thermal energy from the hot tropical climate into growth energy, using it much like fuel to power fruit production.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ yibii tamɔ mango lɛ tsakeɔ dɔlɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ mli. Akɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa yɛ aduawai afeemɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving taller trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa from heat while they build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni kɛlɛ fe tsutsu lɛ loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to make leaves green and healthy. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plants regain their green color and grow bigger ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni amɛtoii lɛ hu dara.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts together with my maize help my soil?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This leaves extra nutrient-rich food in the soil for the maize plants, making the crops grow better without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up in the soil because the roots cannot breathe without oxygen. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the roots, preventing rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to spread their leaves toward the sun. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce energy, which moves down into the roots to produce larger, heavier yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ he. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Enɛ yaa shishi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences sudden drought stress. Keeping the soil consistently damp with regular watering and putting dry grass mulch around the base protects the flowers from extreme heat.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the sap out of young leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents the leaves from twisting and preserves fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anɔ nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young suckers growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain lɛ baai lɛ

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal water and food from the main plant. Cutting away extra suckers and leaving only one or two allows the main tree to produce a bigger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ekome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to the local environment, so they absorb rain and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crops the sunlight and nutrients they need to establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãa gbee. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛdara.

english: Why do my stored maize grains get tiny holes and white powder inside after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni powda yɛŋ yɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Tiny insects called grain weevils eat into stored dry maize to feed and lay eggs, leaving behind holes and fine dust. Drying the maize thoroughly before storage and keeping it in sealed airtight bags stops weevils from ruining the harvest.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ grain moths lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa ni egbi ni ato kɛha niyenii ni amɛwoɔ wɔji. Kɛtsɔ bu kɛ sũ bibii ni eshiɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ dani okɛto ni okɛwo kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafite ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up into tight tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water when the sun is harsh. It is a natural defense mechanism that helps the crop conserve moisture until the heat dies down.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ dɔlɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted around them to act as living umbrellas until their branches are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi eniji lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches high off the ground, making them top-heavy. Planting windbreak trees along your field boundaries blocks strong winds and keeps your plantains standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai akui ni tsii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ. cause a lot weight Kɔɔyɔɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ husui lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he ni eha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants snap and fall over when they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fãa ni egbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants have soft stems that get overloaded when branches fill up with heavy fruit. Tying the stems to wooden sticks driven into the ground gives them the structural support they need to stay upright.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni hoɔ kɛji akɛ aduawai ni tsii eyi tsei lɛ aniji amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ fĩ tso ko ni atsɔ mli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa enáa yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa koni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of green leaves but very small fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ baa eŋɔli babaoo shi amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. The plants spend all their energy fighting for survival and growing leaves, leaving very little energy to produce thick, healthy fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ wuɔ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛba lɛ adalɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshiɔ koni ekɛwo aduawai ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very thin like sticks even after growing for a whole year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ tamɔ tsei yɛ be mli ni mikwɛ amɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, soft soil to expand properly. If the soil is packed too hard or compacted, the tubers cannot push through the earth to grow thick and heavy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ Yitso lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsilɛ ni etsii.

english: Yam tubers grow straight down into the soil and need deep, soft earth to expand easily. High mounds create loose soil and allow excess rainwater to drain away so the young tubers do not rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni bulb bibioo lɛ akafite

english: Why do my cabbage plants rot at the stem when heavy rain sits on my flat field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ mi-kpãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Flat ground allows rainwater to collect around the base of plants without draining away. Cabbage stems sitting in stagnant water are starved of air, which causes stem rot and fungal diseases to set in quickly.
ga: He ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi ni efooo kɛyaa. Kaabaji tsei ni yɔɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa stem rot kɛ fungal helai yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves during the Harmattan is the cassava plant's way of surviving drought. By shedding its leaves, the plant stops water from escaping into the dry air and conserves energy until the rainy season returns.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ ji gbɛ ni ŋmei tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nu naa koni ekajo foi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ, ni amɛtoɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Cowpeas are natural soil improvers. Their roots take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into rich soil nutrients, leaving behind free food in the earth for your next crop of maize.
ga: Cowpea ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Amɛshishifãi lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha o-maise ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How long does it take for a fresh cocoa farm to start giving a full harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmɔ mli kookoo hee lɛ shɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu he?

english: Starting a fresh cocoa farm from traditional seeds can take 6 to 8 years to reach full production, but once the trees mature, you will get regular yields every harvest season for decades.
ga: Kɛ́ aje kusum naa kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ehe afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani eshɛ ŋmei lɛ he. Shi kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa Obaaná yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ kpamɔ be fɛɛ kpamɔ be mli afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why do my young maize plants turn yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer solves this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: How do beneficial insects protect my farm against pests without chemicals?
ga: Te kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ ni amɛkɛ tsofai tsuuu nii?

english: Helpful insects act as natural hunters that feed on destructive pests like caterpillars. Once established in your field, they control pest populations naturally season after season.
ga: Kplukai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛji amɛto amɛhe shi yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli pɛ. Amɛkudɔɔ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is poor pollination from wind and insects.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ

english: Why do my pepper fruits develop soft black spots on the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or consistent water while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas during the first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I avoid planting my crop seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Crops planted too close together fight for the same water, sunlight, and nutrients, resulting in thin plants and very small yields.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do cassava tubers rot underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water gathers in heavy soil during heavy rains without draining properly, suffocating the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. shwieɔ yitso lɛ nɔ

english: Why does planting groundnuts make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally captures nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in the soil, feeding whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Plantain leaves droop during hot weather to reduce water loss. Placing mulch around the stem retains moisture in the soil to help the plant survive heat.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Mulch ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How can I test my maize seeds before planting to know if they will actually grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ makwɛ dani madu koni mana kɛji amɛbaakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can do a simple germination test by placing 10 seeds in a wet cloth for a few days. If 8 or more sprout, your seeds are healthy and ready for planting; if fewer sprout, the seed quality is poor and you should get new seeds.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii 2-3 lɛ nɔ. Kɛji 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu. Kɛji akɛ fioo pɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ehiii kwraa. Ni esa akɛ otao dumɔwui heei.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the primary nutrient plants need to stay green and build strong stems. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps them regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli ni amɛma tsei ashishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under hot direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and maintaining soil moisture during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for too long, it drowns the roots and creates wet conditions where fungal decay thrives, causing the tubers to spoil before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni ŋmei baanyɛ afite yɛ mli lɛ aba. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and small or missing corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo ni bɛ lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when watering is uneven, or when there are no bees and insects to pollinate the blossoms, preventing fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bɛ ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ Haa aduawai lɛ akagboi.

english: Staking keeps yam leaves off the wet ground so they can catch direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers, while also protecting the foliage from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Staking baajie sweet potato baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛha niyenii aha bulbs wuji ni miida lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ sweet potato baai ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are there ragged holes inside the funnels of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ a-kone lɛ mli

english: Ragged holes inside young maize leaves are a key sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the growing tip of the plant and eat the tender inner leaves.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so much slower when weeds are left around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi eshwɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal food, water, and sunlight away from your crops, effectively starving your plants and slowing down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ ni ehaa amɛdaraa fioo.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ baadu tsina loo ŋmeii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they naturally fertilize the soil and nourish neighboring crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni amɛha tsei lɛ niyenii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni jɛɔ mli baa.

english: Why does my cocoa farm take several years before it starts giving me good money?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he afii babaoo dani ebɔi mi shika kpakpa hamɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need time to build strong roots and healthy branches before they can produce full pods. In their first few years, the trees spend all their energy growing leaves and roots rather than producing fruit.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia be koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa kɛ niji ni wa dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ baai kɛ shishifãi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing very few pods even after I put in so much hard work on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mitsu nii waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: A low yield despite hard work often happens if the soil lacks nutrients, if pests and diseases are attacking the trees silently, or if the trees are not getting the right balance of shade and sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ nitsumɔ ni wa fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai tutua tsei dioo Aloo kɛji tso lɛ naaa hulutsoo kɛ hulu la ni sa.

english: How do I know the right time of the year to harvest my cocoa to get the best crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo koni maná yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvesting when they turn from green or dark red to a clear yellow or orange color. Harvesting during the main peak season when pods are fully mature ensures heavy, high-quality beans.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛtsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. Nikpamɔ yɛ be titri ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa anáa kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes my cocoa beans heavy and good quality when I take them to be weighed and sold?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsii ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ misusu he ni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Proper fermentation for five to six days followed by thorough sun-drying makes the beans heavy, rich in quality, and free from mold, which ensures you get full value at the weighing scale.
ga: Kɛ́ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ gbii enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ ni hulutsoo be mli egbi lɛ, no haa kɔfi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli tsii, ehi jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ oskel lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before they are ready to be picked?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, overly wet, and damp conditions. Pruning excess branches and removing weeds helps airflow and sunlight reduce the wetness that causes it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Efɔ fe nine ni edɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ aba koni ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛbaa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but very few of them actually grow into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to pollinate them. If the farm is too dry, lacks moist leaf litter, or has been sprayed with harsh chemicals at the wrong time, the insects die and the flowers drop off without making pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Baai ni mli efɔ bɛ. aloo tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli Kplukai lɛ baagboi ni fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when the dry season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have short roots that cannot reach water deep in the soil during dry weather. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them shields them from harsh heat and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ amɛwo nu kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ tsei bibii, yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee dɔlɛ ni fe nine, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: How does clearing weeds around my cocoa trees help the trees yield better fruit?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ ajiemɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mitso lɛ ni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Weeds compete with your cocoa trees for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Keeping the farm clean ensures your cocoa trees get all the food and moisture they need to produce abundant pods.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ehaa cacao tsei lɛ náa niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why is it important for me to prune the extra branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine yɛ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing sunlight and fresh air to reach inside the tree. This prevents fungal diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni akɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni mli wa.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees stop producing as many pods as they used to when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ ekpa ŋmeii babaoo ni ewoɔ beni eji gbekɛ fioo lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older than 20 to 25 years, their ability to carry water and food up the trunk slows down. Older trees also become more prone to diseases, requiring side-grafting, heavy pruning, or replanting to restore high yield.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso eye fe afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛyaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ baa shi. Tsei ni edara lɛ hu helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya. Ebiɔ ni akɛ fã kroko awo mli. ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii loo dumɔwui heei koni ekɛ yibii babaoo aba

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers as a survival choice to save water and energy instead of growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛhi shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ aduawai.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly when the sun gets very bright around midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli aaafee shwane fintiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural self-defense action where the plant reduces its leaf surface area to trap moisture and prevent water from evaporating too quickly in hot sun.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do cassava plants drop their lower leaves when the dry season begins in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their bottom leaves naturally to reduce the amount of water they lose through transpiration, helping the plant stay alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ni amɛlaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ nɔ aba shi. Ehaa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: How does applying water directly to the crop roots through small pipes work better than pouring water on the leaves with a bucket?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛ hose bibioo ko shwieɔ tsei ashishifãi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe nu ni akɛ baagi shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Drip watering delivers moisture straight to the roots where the plant actually drinks, which prevents water from wasting in the hot air and keeps leaves dry so diseases cannot spread.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ni tso lɛ nuɔ nu diɛŋtsɛ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haaa nu afite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, ni ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ koni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cabbage roots turn soft and rot when I water them heavily every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli waa daa gbi lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air as well as water to breathe. Flooding the soil every day drowns the roots, suffocating them and creating a wet environment where rot-causing fungi thrive.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ daa gbi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ehaa amɛmuɔ, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ shwereɔ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them grow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil, keeping the ground cool and trapping moisture so the sun cannot dry out the earth quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Bɔni afee ni hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why do sweet peppers grow taller and look healthier under a wooden frame covered with plastic than out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ni akɛ plastic ehà nɔ lɛ ashishi fe ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: A shelter frame shields sensitive vegetables from harsh sunlight, direct heavy rain, and strong winds, creating a gentle environment where the plant spends energy on growth rather than fighting stress.
ga: He ni ahiɔ lɛ baabu aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli jɔ ni tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ haomɔ baawu lɛ baa.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings burn and die when I plant them straight into direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have delicate leaves and tender roots that cannot handle intense solar heat yet; they need temporary shade to build strength before facing full sunlight.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lolo. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni amɛná hewalɛ dani amɛkɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akpee.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow much faster than my cultivated crops after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with seeds that lie dormant in the soil, ready to absorb water instantly and outgrow cultivated crops that need time to establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa. Dumɔwui yɛ ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Efee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ni edaa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ, ni heɔ be dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my garden eggs taste bitter and stay small when there is a long break in the rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When garden egg plants suffer from water shortages and heat stress during fruit formation, they produce defense chemicals that turn the fruit bitter while stopping proper growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ na nu ni faaa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ yɛ aduawai afeemɔ be mli lɛ Amɛfeɔ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when there is too much heat from the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ fa tsɔ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that dry out and burn quickly in direct heat. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted next to them to act as living umbrellas and keep the soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ akɛwo la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ kã ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil does not have enough nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK will help the crop grow big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa. Eji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ NPK ni okɛfata he lɛ baaye abua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná toi wuji.

english: How do I know which direction to plant my cassava stick in the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni esa akɛ odu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small bumps (buds) where leaves used to grow on the cassava stem stick. These buds must point upward toward the sky when you put the stick in the ground so the plant sprouts correctly and forms strong tuber roots.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii (tsoji) ni be ko ni eho lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehe miihia ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi beni okɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ fɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crop roots with dead grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry grass or leaves (called mulching) blocks direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you do not need to water as often, and stops unwanted weeds from sprouting.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi woɔ tsei ahe (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Etsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means they take nitrogen gas from the air and naturally pump it back into the ground through their roots. This enriches the soil with free fertilizer that helps your maize grow better.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: That damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing funnel of the maize plant. Spraying approved insecticides or neem leaf water directly into the leaf funnel early in the morning will destroy them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa lɛ mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaakpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of nutrients like calcium and boron. Watering your tomatoes regularly at the base early in the morning helps prevent this.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium kɛ boron ni bɛ lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni okɛtsi naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Which young shoots should I cut away from the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei bibii esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi?

english: Cut away the small shoots with broad, wide leaves (called water suckers) because they steal food from the main tree. Keep only two or three shoots with narrow, sword-shaped leaves (sword suckers) to replace the main stem after harvest.
