ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ yibii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers) lɛ shiɔ ejaakɛ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kpãa tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni baa bibii tamɔ klante (klante tsei) koni akɛto tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ najiaŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves develop dark spots and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High rainfall and humidity create moist conditions where fungal diseases thrive and spread easily on wet leaves. Planting your crops with enough space between them lets wind blow through to dry the leaves quickly and prevent rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ haa hulutsoo baa. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ oya. Dumɔ he ko ni gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ aha baai lɛ agbi oya ni ekɛtsi fitemɔ naa.

english: Why is it a bad idea to plant pepper on the same plot where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ ooodu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mifo mi-tomato lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Peppers and tomatoes belong to the same crop family and attract the exact same pests and soil diseases. Planting them back-to-back on the same ground allows hidden soil diseases to build up and ruin your next harvest.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛgbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ abua amɛhe naa ni amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and wither when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight. Tall shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa leaves from scorching heat and keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant naturally moves the limited nutrients it has from its older lower leaves up to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo kɛjɛɔ baa ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it important for me to plant cassava stem cuttings with the buds pointing upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava buds are designed to push new branches up toward the sky and roots down into the soil. Planting stems upside down forces the plant to waste energy re-orienting itself, resulting in weak growth and poor tuber formation.
ga: Afee Yucca tsei lɛ koni amɛtsi tsei niji heei kɛya ŋwɛi ni amɛshishifãi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ da ni ekɛ ehe shwie shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ he waaa yɛ ehe ni ekɛbaatsake ehe lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber feemɔ ni ehiii baa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground allows more leaves to catch sunlight and prevents leaf diseases, sending more food energy down to grow large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaa lɛ baa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. ni atsĩ baa helai anaa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, atsuɔ niyenii hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants dropping off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot dry spells or inconsistent watering. The plant sheds its flowers to save water and energy just to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ko, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa, ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Tso nɛɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni ehi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I plant my seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together must fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Because none of the plants get enough food, they all end up small with low yields.
ga: Ehe baahia ni tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu fioo Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ eko kwraa enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ daraaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot under the soil instead of growing when I plant them right before the rains fully start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Seeds need steady moisture to sprout successfully. If planted in hot, dry soil with only light, unpredictable showers, the seed absorbs just enough water to swell and spoil without getting enough water to fully germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi ni nugbɔ baanɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛbaaŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛfuu ni amɛgboi.

english: The main plantain stem shares its food and water with all the suckers growing around it. Removing extra shoots leaves only one strong successor, allowing the main plant to focus its energy on growing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Plantain tso titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ jaa niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ sɛɛyelɔ kome pɛ ni he wa. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable roots with dry grass keep them greener during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks the sun from touching the soil directly. This stops water from evaporating quickly, keeps root zones cool, and retains soil moisture longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akafee lasu oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do weeds harm my crops much more when the crop plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui fe tsutsu lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop plants have small, delicate roots and few leaves, making them weak. Fast-growing weeds easily shade young crops from sunlight and steal soil fertilizer before the crops are strong enough to defend their space.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai fioo pɛ, ni no haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ afee hulutsoo be mlɛo ni amɛju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do some cassava varieties produce heavy tubers while others only grow tall leaves with small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi woɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ akwɛ srɔtoi komɛi kɛ baai kakadaji kɛ shishifãi bibii pɛ.

english: Different cassava varieties are bred for different purposes. Traditional or wild varieties often put their energy into growing tall stems and heavy leaves, while improved agricultural varieties are specifically developed to store energy into big, starch-rich tuber roots.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi Akwɛ amɛ kɛha yiŋtoi srɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, maŋbii loo koo mli tsei srɔtoi kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni tsii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, afee okwaayeli henɔi ni atsake lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛ hewalɛ ato ŋmeii agboi ni starch eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do hybrid maize seeds I buy from the store produce more cobs than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni miheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa babaoo fe ŋmãa ni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are created by crossing two specific parent plants to combine their strongest traits, like disease resistance and high yield. However, seeds saved from that harvest lose those combined strengths in the next generation, resulting in smaller cobs and uneven growth.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛtsakeɔ nibii ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ feɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni akɛ amɛsui ni mli wa fe fɛɛ, tamɔ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ afee ekome lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ mli lɛ baafite nakai hewalɛi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Why is it good practice to plant legumes like groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa fataa ŋmãa he lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the soil, especially nitrogen. Groundnut plants have special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is starving for nitrogen or that the roots are waterlogged from poor drainage. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving drainage helps restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni ooofee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring steady moisture and balanced fertilizer helps the plant hold its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli tsɔ Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and show light green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This curling and discoloration is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant stem cuttings from the extension service prevents this issue.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ baa. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Niji ni nyɛɔ helai ahe ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ sɛɛgbɛ nitsumɔ ko mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the branch before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, overly damp conditions. Pruning unnecessary tree branches lets in sunlight and air circulation, which stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fuŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ ni edɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does my stored maize get destroyed by small insects even when I keep it inside sealed bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli moŋ?

english: Insects like grain weevils often lay tiny eggs on the maize while it is still in the field or during drying. If the maize is not completely dry or treated with approved storage protectants before bagging, those eggs hatch inside the bag and destroy the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ ŋmãa nɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo loo yɛ be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa loo akɛ nɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ he lɛ tsu nii dani akɛwo kotoku mli. Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli ni amɛfiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot inside the mound before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Yam rot in the soil is caused by excess water standing around the roots or damage from soil pests like nematodes and fungi. Planting on high mounds with good drainage and selecting unblemished seed yams prevents underground decay.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes kɛ fungi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ahala ŋmeii ni bɛ muji lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii akafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the sun gets very strong during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ naa wa waa yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small roots that cannot withstand direct sunlight. Planting them alongside plantains provides shade, traps humidity, and keeps the soil cool so the young cocoa can establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ plantains ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni kookoo bibioo lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high moisture and low sunlight. Clearing weeds around the base and pruning unnecessary branches lets in sunlight and airflow to dry out the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ ni hulu la fioo pɛ shɛɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ ni ofolɔ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle he koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires nitrogen to stay green and produce food, so when soil nutrients are low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ niyenii aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young maize plants have ragged holes in the leaves with tiny caterpillars hidden inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu yɛ amɛbaai amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the leaf tissues inside the central funnel of the maize plant. Inspecting fields early and applying appropriate controls protect the growing shoot so the plant can form ears.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ baa mli fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe koni tsei lɛ afee toi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when there is heavy rain for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in heavy soil without draining away, it starves the roots of oxygen, allowing soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atutua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch direct sunlight, which fuels tuber growth underground. Lifting the vines on stakes maximizes sun exposure and prevents leaves from getting fungal diseases from damp soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni ji tsofa ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ daraa Wein tso lɛ nɔ ni awoɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or irregular watering. High temperatures combined with dry soil make the plant discard its flowers to conserve energy for basic survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fataa he lɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and turning hard and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies that suck plant sap and spread viruses, causing the leaves to distort and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do officers advise me to plant groundnuts on my farm to make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ mli onukpai lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules. When groundnut roots decay in the field, they leave behind natural nitrogen fertilizer that nourishes future crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmei koni ekɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi shwieɔ shi No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ye ebua amɛ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass is called mulching. It acts as a protective blanket that traps moisture in the ground, keeps root temperatures cool, and stops dry winds from evaporating soil water.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli latsaa lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: How can I test if the maize seeds I bought will germinate well before I plant them in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can perform a simple germination test by putting 10 seeds in a moist cloth for 3 to 5 days. If 8 or more seeds sprout, your seed batch is high quality and ready for full planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, odumɔwui akuu lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui fɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava cuttings rotting in the soil instead of growing green shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Cassava stems rot when they are planted in waterlogged soil or taken from diseased parent plants. Always select healthy stem cuttings and plant them in well-drained soil at the beginning of the rainy season.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ loo ajie kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Halamɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ be fɛɛ be ni odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate excessive water around the roots, poor soil drainage, or a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Improving drainage and applying proper organic or inorganic fertilizer will help them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni hoɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo nibii ni wala bɛ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the crop experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying phosphorus-rich fertilizer encourages fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni faaa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaawo yibiiwoo he hewalɛ.

english: Why are my groundnut pods coming out empty when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut pods lɛ efee efolo kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when the crop lacks calcium in the soil while the pods are developing underground. Adding agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil before planting helps pods fill out fully.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ayi dumɔwui lɛ amli obɔ.

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the central shoot. Inspecting the whorl early and applying recommended organic or chemical treatments helps protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ okwɛ band lɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my yam vines turn dark brown and die before the tubers are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani bulbs lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Premature browning of yam vines is often caused by a fungal disease called yam anthracnose, which spreads rapidly in warm, humid weather. Staking vines high off the wet soil reduces disease spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ sweet potato anthracnose lɛ kɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tsei wo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it important for me to plant cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. Rotating maize with cowpeas restores natural soil fertility and breaks the life cycle of pests that target maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Abɛi ni akɛ cowpea tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji ŋmãa lɛ yiŋtoo lɛ wala shihilɛ mli ni afoɔ.

english: What will happen to my plantain farm if I plant the suckers too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting plantains too close forces them to compete for sunlight and soil nutrients. This leads to tall, weak stems and small bunches that easily fall over in strong wind.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Egbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa leaves will look scorched, dry up along the edges, or turn pale when exposed to harsh direct sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa trees while they establish.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni eshã, amɛgbi yɛ amɛnaagbɛ, loo amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: This is usually a sign that your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green. When the plant cannot find enough nitrogen in the soil, it steals it from its older lower leaves to keep the new top leaves growing.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejuɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni ekɛ ŋwɛi baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and watery if I do not harvest them before the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. During heavy rains, water fills up all the small air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and causing rot-causing fungi to multiply quickly.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli Nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo oya.

english: Why are the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi kookoo tso lɛ nɔ koni egbee shi ni etsɔko kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to fertilize them, and the tree needs steady moisture. If the weather is too dry, or if chemical sprays kill off the good midges, the tree drops its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli. Ni tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Aloo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ mɔ diɛŋtsɛ ehe? Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark black spots on the bottom right before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot and happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the growing fruit. This usually occurs when watering is irregular—going from very dry soil to very soaked soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha yibii ni miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ—kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa nɔ.

english: Why does putting dry leaves or grass on top of the soil around my crops help them stay alive during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni nu lɛ mli egbi lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that shades the ground from the hot sun, keeps moisture from evaporating out of the dirt, and prevents root scorching.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily right when the fruit bunch is getting big and heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni aduawai akui lɛ miifee wuji ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are naturally shallow, but tiny worms called nematodes or stem borer insects can weaken them further. When the fruit bunch grows heavy, weak or damaged roots can no longer anchor the plant against strong wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, shi ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ babaoo. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ da waa lɛ Shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ loo efite lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ tso lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why does my young maize plant burn and die if I put the granular fertilizer directly against the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa ni ji granular fertilizer wo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is made of strong salts that suck moisture directly out of tender plant stems and roots when touched directly. You should always place fertilizer a few finger-widths away in a circle or line so roots can safely reach for it.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ feɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he aaafee 2-3 inches yɛ kooyigbɛ loo line mli koni shishifãi lɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips, mites, or aphids that attack young leaves and spread plant viruses. As these pests drink the plant's juices, the leaves grow distorted and twisted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni tutuaa baai bibii ni egbɛɔ helai eshwaa tsei amli Enɛ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu. Baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for my corn in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it into the ground. When you harvest them, that extra natural fertilizer stays behind in the soil for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ baajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa amɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wilt and die when I move them straight from my shady nursery canopy out into the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Young plants raised in complete shade are soft and weak against harsh direct sunlight and wind. They need a process called 'hardening off,' where you gradually expose them to direct sun for a few extra hours each day over a week before final planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kwraa lɛ baafee blɛoo ni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa amɛ. Amɛbiɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘hardening’ ni okɛ amɛ woɔ hulu la mli fiofio ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo krokomɛi ni fata he daa gbi yɛ otsi kome mli dani naagbee dumɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves often show that your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth, or that the ground is waterlogged and preventing the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ miiye nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ akwɛ̃ Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up completely above the ground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ egbi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally die off at the end of their growing cycle to signal that the plant has stopped growing leaves and moved all its remaining energy into storing food inside the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ naagbee, ni no tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii koni ekɛ niyenii ato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under full sun; plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm where I plant maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps hungry crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce big roots in some areas of my farm but only thin woody roots in other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi wuji yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii pɛ yɔɔ hei krokomɛi?

english: Cassava tubers need loose, soft soil to expand; hard or compacted soils prevent the roots from swelling into thick, starchy tubers, leaving them thin and fibrous.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafu ni amɛfee bulbs ni mli edɔ ni starch yɔɔ mli. Shi ni efee mlɛo ni efee fiber.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the cleared bushes on my field before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi ni ajie yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Burning destroys useful organic matter, kills beneficial soil microbes, and dries out the land, whereas leaving cleared vegetation to rot creates natural mulch that enriches the soil.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni ajie lɛ ni ashiɔ koni amɛgboi lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap out of new leaves, or by viruses transmitted by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without forming any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry winds, or irregular watering, as the plant tries to save water rather than produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very light yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When planted too closely, crops compete fiercely for limited sunlight and nutrients, causing them to stretch upward for light instead of developing strong stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhe la lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo ŋmeii ni wa kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong rains when they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches in wet soil, especially if soil pests like nematodes have damaged their root system.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes fite eshishifãi lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact size of my land in hectares, and how is it different from acres?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male mishikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ yɛ hectares mli? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ Acre he?

english: One hectare is equal to about 2.5 acres, or roughly the size of a standard football pitch. Knowing your farm size in hectares helps you calculate the right amount of seeds, fertilizer, and expected crop output.
ga: Hectare kome kɛ aaafee acre 2.5 yeɔ egbɔ, loo aaafee bɔɔlutswaa he ko ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ dalɛ. Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ da ha yɛ hectares mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni obu dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ ayibɔ ni sa lɛ he akɔntaa.

english: What does it mean when buyers measure my crop yield in metric tons instead of bags?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji mɔ ko ni heɔ nii lɛ susu miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ he yɛ mɛtrik tɔn mli yɛ baagi najiaŋ?

english: A metric ton is equal to 1,000 kilograms, which is roughly equivalent to 15 standard 64kg bags of produce. Large buyers use metric tons to measure very large harvests easily across big farms.
ga: Mɛtrik tɔn kome kɛ kilogram 1,000 yeɔ egbɔ, ni no kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kotokui 15 ni tsiimɔ ji kilogram 64 lɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Nihɔɔlɔi wuji kɛ mɛtrik tɔn tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛsusu ŋmaa ni akpaa babaoo waa yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ he mlɛo.

english: How much crop harvest should I expect to produce from one hectare of land?
ga: Nibii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ hectare kome nɔ?

english: Your yield per hectare depends on crop variety, soil quality, and rainfall, but proper planting distance and weed control can help you get maximum weight in tons per hectare.
ga: O yibiiwoo yɛ hectare kome mli lɛ damɔ tsei srɔtoi lɛ anɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua bo ni oná jatsui ni fa fe fɛɛ yɛ tɔn mli yɛ hectare kome mli.

english: How can I figure out how much crop output my farm can harvest and handle every day during peak season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male bɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa ni etsu he nii daa gbi yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Daily output depends on your land size, the number of farm hands or machines working, and how fast you can pick, clean, and dry your crop each day before it spoils.
ga: Nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli daa gbi lɛ damɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ nɔ. Okwaafoi adɛŋ niji loo tsɔnei ayibɔ ni tsuɔ nii kɛ bɔ ni obaanyɛ okɛ oyaiyeli akpãtã, otsumɔ, ni ogbi oŋmɔshi nibii daa gbi dani efite.

english: Why do buyers grade my crop harvest before setting the selling price?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miisusu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe dani atsɔɔ jara ni akɛbaahɔɔ lɛ?

english: Grading separates your harvest based on quality, size, moisture content, and cleanliness. Top-grade crops with no insect damage or mold fetch a much higher price in the market.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo gbalaa okpamɔ lɛ mli yɛ bɔ ni ehi ha, bɔ ni edara ha, bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ bɔ ni ehe tse ha lɛ naa. Nibii ni aduɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni kooloi loo ŋmeii efiteee lɛ lɛ jara wa waa yɛ jara nɔ.

english: How does sorting my crops into different grades stop me from losing money?
ga: Mi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli gbalamɔ yɛ grade srɔtoi amli Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi gbɛ koni mikafite shika?

english: If you mix damaged produce with good crops, buyers will price the entire batch based on the worst quality. Sorting allows you to sell your premium produce at top price.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite futu ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ, Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baadamɔ nɔ ni ehiii fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ jara. Nibii ni okɛhalaa lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my harvested crops to lose quality and drop to a lower grade?
ga: Mɛni haa mikpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ebaa shi kɛyaa shishigbɛ?

english: Poor drying, harvesting crops before they mature, storing them in damp rooms, and insect damage lower your crop grade and reduce its market value.
ga: poor drying Nibii ni akpaa dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Kɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli. kɛ nibii ni kooloi fiteɔ lɛ Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ baa shi ni ehaa jara ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can using machines for sorting and grading help my harvest compared to doing it by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔnei ni akɛhalaa nibii amli kɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mikpamɔ lɛ kɛ akɛto nikpamɔ ni akɛ niji kpaa lɛ he?

english: Machines process large quantities of crops much faster and more accurately than manual labor, removing dirt and bad grains without damaging the good crops.
ga: Mshinii tsuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ahe nii oya ni etsuɔ ​​nii pɛpɛɛpɛ fe nine nitsumɔ. Ejieɔ muji kɛ dumɔwui gbohii ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ.

english: Will using threshing or processing machines damage my harvested crops?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsɔne ni akɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baafite mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: When properly set up, modern processing machines are gentle on produce and actually reduce crop breakage compared to traditional beating methods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ feɔ blɛoo yɛ yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ kɛ akɛto blema gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atswaa nii lɛ ahe.

english: What equipment do I need if I want to scale up my harvest processing to handle large volumes every day?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii he hiaa mi kɛji miisumɔ ni mawo mikpamɔ nitsumɔ lɛ mli babaoo koni manyɛ matsu nibii babaoo ahe nii daa gbi?

english: To handle large daily volumes, you need mechanical cleaners, moisture meters, automated grading screens, and proper bagging equipment to prevent bottlenecks.
ga: Bɔni afee ni otsu woji wuji ahe nii daa gbi Ohe miihia ni okɛ tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ muji lɛ atsu nii. Fɛ̃i mita otomatik halamɔ tsɔne kɛ kotoku mli nibii ni sa ni baatsi bottlenecks naa.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is running out of nitrogen, which acts like food for the plant. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color and allows the corn ears to grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa toi lɛ ni amɛdaraa

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts on the same land where I harvested maize?
ga: Ani ebaahi aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, that is very good for your land. Legumes like groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil that the maize used up, naturally refreshing your field for future crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, no ji nɔ ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Legumes, tamɔ ŋmei, gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmei kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔji lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are there small worms eating holes right in the middle of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that loves to hide in the tender center leaves of young maize. Clearing weeds early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or chemicals when the worms are still small stops them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ amli. Ajie jwɛi lɛ mra ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ wala mli lɛ atsu nii be mli ni kooloi lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite onibii lɛ.

english: This black patch is called blossom end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or when watering is irregular. Watering your plants consistently every day keeps the soil moist and stops the fruit from spoiling.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa gbi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ akafite.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops actually stop them from bearing good fruit?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛkawo yibii kpakpai?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal water, sunlight, and plant food directly away from your crops' roots, leaving your main plants too weak to produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otso titri lɛ baagbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How do I know if a cassava stem is healthy enough to cut and plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afolɔ ni adu?

english: Choose stems from strong, disease-free plants that are about 8 to 18 months old. Good stems should be hard with brown bark and have visible, closely spaced eye buds along the stem.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai bɛ mli ni eye aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 lɛ ashishifãi. Esa akɛ tsei kpakpai lɛ afee nɔ ni wa, ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni anaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to raise my pepper seeds in a small nursery bed before moving them to the big field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli dani mikɛwo ŋmɔ agbo mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are tiny and fragile. A sheltered nursery bed protects the young seedlings from hot sun, heavy rain, and insects until they grow strong roots and are ready to survive out in the open field.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Tsoi akwɛmɔhei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaahi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by too much heat, lack of water, or attack by pests like mirids. Maintaining reasonable shade trees and protecting the farm from sucking insects helps the flowers turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine, nu ni bɛ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ atatu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ he hulu tsoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the weather gets a little windy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa fioo lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can easily be destroyed by microscopic soil worms called nematodes. Also, heavy fruit bunches pull the tree down, so farmers use sturdy wooden poles to support trees carrying big bunches.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Kɛfata he lɛ, aduawai akui ni tsii Abaagbala tsei lɛ kɛba shi, no hewɔ lɛ okwaafoi lɛ kɛ tsei ni wa tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ tsei ni hiɛ akui wuji lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to lift my yam vines off the ground using wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mikɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ awo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need full sunlight to produce the food that makes the tubers underground grow big. Lifting the vines up on stakes keeps the leaves in the light and off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Hulu ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli tseɔ, ni amɛjeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. This causes them to stretch tall to reach the sun without having enough energy to grow big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛgbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young pods during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry harmattan wind strips moisture from both the soil and the plant leaves. To protect itself from drying out completely and dying, the cocoa tree intentionally sheds its young pods to save water.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai fɛɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe he koni okagbi kwraa ni ogbo. Bɔni afee ni nu akafite lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbala ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow during the hot dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl and turn yellow when the plant suffers from heat stress, lack of soil water, or tiny insects like whiteflies that spread crop diseases during warm weather.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli, nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tso helai eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow and fall off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Lower cassava leaves drop naturally when the plant experiences drought or lacks nitrogen, as it diverts available food and water away from older leaves to keep growing roots underground.
ga: Cassava baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji tso lɛ na hɔmɔ loo nitrogen ni faaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ejieɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ahe koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my sweet potato roots stay thin and stringy instead of swelling into big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato shishifãi lɛ ji mlɛo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes need loose, soft soil to expand. If the soil is too hard or compacted clay, the roots cannot easily push the earth aside to swell into thick tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛje kpo kɛya afã koni efu ni etsɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without making peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Pepper flowers drop without forming fruit when temperatures become too high, water supply is irregular, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee yɛ jɛmɛ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of bushy green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Applying too much chemical fertilizer containing high nitrogen forces the cowpea plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and branches instead of making flowers and pods.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ tsei aniji amli yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rains even when the stem looks strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots near the surface of the earth. Heavy rains soften the topsoil, making heavy bunches pull the entire tree out of the loose ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ogbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni etse lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots even when I keep them inside a dark storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ tsũ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers with an internal biological clock. Once their natural rest period ends after harvest, changes in air humidity signal to the yam that the planting season is returning, causing it to sprout.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni wala yɔɔ mli. Beni adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ baa naagbee yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tsakemɔi ni baa kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ leɔ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ eba ekoŋŋ, ni no haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for planting coconut trees instead of food crops like maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei najiaŋ?

english: Coconut trees thrive best in warm climates with deep, well-drained sandy or loamy soils and good access to groundwater. While maize gives quick returns within a few months, coconut is a long-term investment that produces fruit for decades if your land has deep soil and regular sunlight.
ga: Kokoo tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa haa sɛɛnamɔ oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli moŋ. Kokoo ji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni baaha yibii aba afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ daa.

english: If I plant tree crops like coconut or cocoa, how long will I have to wait before I start harvesting?
ga: Kɛji midu tso tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mije ŋmei kpamɔ shishi?

english: Modern hybrid coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years, whereas traditional varieties can take 6 to 7 years. Cocoa trees typically begin producing pods in about 3 to 5 years, depending on the variety and care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmeii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 6 kɛyashi 7. Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmeii sɔrɔtoi lɛ kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ amɛ nɔ ahaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant crops like cassava or vegetables between my young coconut trees while I wait for them to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava, legumes, or vegetables between young tree crops is a smart practice. Since young trees have small root systems and do not block sunlight, planting short-term crops gives you food and income while keeping weeds down until the tree canopy closes.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa loo aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ tsei bibii ateŋ lɛ ji nilee nifeemɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifã bibioo ko, ni etsĩii hulu la lɛ naa. Be kukuoo mli dumɔ haa anáa niyenii kɛ shika kɛ agbɛnɛ hu jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ shishi tsɔne lɛ ŋmɛɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn under full sun and roots that dry out quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains or bananas next to young cocoa acts like a living umbrella, protecting the seedlings from extreme sunlight until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ shishifãi ni gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shade ni hiɛ ka. Ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crops turning yellow while the plants are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves near the bottom of a plant usually mean it lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding organic manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the crop maintain strong foliage and good growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ baai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young coconut trees drop their fruits before the nuts are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ woɔ yibii dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop in young coconuts is usually caused by water stress during long dry periods or a lack of nutrients like potassium in the soil. Mulching around the tree base to retain moisture and feeding the soil helps the tree hold its fruit.
ga: Kokoo aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya, bei pii lɛ, nu he haomɔ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ hewɔ. aloo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: What happens if I plant my tree crops too close to each other on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting trees too closely causes them to compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients. This leads to tall, thin trees with poor yields because their branches cannot spread out to catch enough sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɛlɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ejaakɛ amɛniji lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around the base of my trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and nutrients directly from your crop's root zone and can hide pests that attack the tree stem. Clearing a clean ring around the tree trunk ensures all water and fertilizer go directly to your crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa tsei akutsei lɛ ato. Klemɔ ring ni he tse ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I tell if a plant on my farm is suffering from a disease or just bad weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hela loo kɔɔyɔŋ ehiii?

english: Weather stress like drought usually affects all crops in the field uniformly by causing wilting. Diseases usually show specific signs on individual plants first, such as spotty leaves, rotting stems, sap oozing from trunks, or sudden yellowing of isolated trees.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔ, tamɔ hɔmɔ, fɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ hewalɛ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛbaa lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, helai jieɔ okadii pɔtɛɛ komɛi akpo yɛ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ, tamɔ baai ni etse, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni egboi, kɛ latɛs ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. Aloo tso ko ni yɔɔ ekome too lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa.

english: If I decide to clear an old crop field to plant tree crops, how should I prepare the ground properly?
ga: Kɛji mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ majie ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo lɛ koni madu tsei Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Start by clearing weeds and removing old, diseased plant residues so pests don't spread. Dig wide, deep planting holes and mix the excavated topsoil with well-rotted manure before planting to give the new roots a rich, loose environment to grow into.
ga: Je shishi kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tso momo ni hela emɔ lɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. Tsɔmɔmɔ dumɔ bu ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ. Ni okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni atsa lɛ afutu ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ dani odu koni eha shishifãi heei lɛ aná he ko ni baa nii, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for leaf growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers spread dry leaves and cut grass around the stems of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ baai ni egbi nɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, traps moisture so you water less often, and stops weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo oŋmɔji lɛ amli fioo ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that prefer maize to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the big trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn under harsh direct sunlight. Leaving or planting shade trees like plantains creates a cool umbrella that protects them until they are fully grown.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Will I harvest more food if I plant my seeds very close together in the ground?
ga: Ani makpa niyenii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak plants and a smaller harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibioo baa.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to grow so slowly even when rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like nutrient thieves. They quickly drink up water and steal fertilizer from the soil before your main crops have a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Amɛnuɔ nu oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: What is making tiny holes in my corn leaves and leaving small caterpillars inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on young maize leaves. Catching them early and spraying suitable organic or chemical controls can protect your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni sa ni haa wala yibii loo tsofai ni yeɔ wala nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu oyale lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or viruses they pass to the plant. Spraying insecticidal soap or neem oil can keep these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni amɛtsɔɔ tsei amli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ samla loo neem fɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsi kooloi nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before any small tomatoes can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato bibii lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather gets too hot, when watering is uneven, or if there are no bees around to pollinate the flowers into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii ni amɛbatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot under the ground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains water easily. When excess water sits around the roots without sinking into the ground, the roots drown and begin to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kpɛtɛ shishifãi ahe ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees from my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their delicate leaves and dries up the soil moisture around their shallow roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɔle shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ he lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rain and wind just when the fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy; propping the main stem up with strong bamboo or wooden poles prevents them from snapping.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fĩ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekakumɔ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from the agriculture office instead of planting seeds saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ i he kɛ je ye nyagbe ngma kpami ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Certified seeds are bred to resist local pests, tolerate dry spells, and yield more harvest, whereas saved seeds lose their strength and yield less with every season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo daa be.

english: Why does my maize turn yellow and stay small even when the rain is falling regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the soil is low in nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient plants need to build green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Is it good for me to plant groundnuts between my rows of cassava?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which enriches your farm naturally and helps the cassava grow better.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa sɛɛnamɔ baa oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize cobs so small when I plant seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii waa lɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni ekɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete for the same food and water in the soil, causing all the plants to remain weak and produce tiny cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow during the dry months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is typically caused by the cassava mosaic virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that multiply quickly in warm, dry weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into mounds before planting my yams instead of planting on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabua shikpɔŋ ŋmɔtɔ naa dani madu ŋmɔtɔ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounding loosens the soil so yam tubers can expand easily underground without hitting hard soil, and it keeps water from pooling around the tubers and causing rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaawo lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi oya ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. ni etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle bulb lɛ he ni eha egbo.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and softening so quickly inside my storage shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni efee blɛoo oya yɛ mi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when exposed to warmth and light because they sense it is time to grow; storing them in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated yarn barn delays sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo kɛ la he ejaakɛ amɛnuɔ he akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Baaha kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, causing the plant to drop its blossoms to conserve energy until conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ha tsei lɛ aba fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni akɛto hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is short on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen or plants are planted too close together, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei baato niyenii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ebaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my land make the maize planted after it yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa ni midu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means they extract nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the ground for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛha niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves or passing viruses to the plant. Inspecting leaf undersides and applying neem oil helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo amɛhaa helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni okɛ neem fɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that hides inside the whorl of maize stalks to feed on tender leaves. Checking farms early and applying neem extracts or recommended bio-pesticides stops their damage.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Akwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ atsu nii. lɛ baakpa nɔ ni efite lɛ

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant. It happens when watering is inconsistent or when dry spells prevent roots from drawing up calcium from the soil.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Ebaa kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilts and droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can absorb it. Drooping is a temporary self-defense mechanism that reduces sun exposure to preserve water until evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Drooping ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he yɛ be kukuoo mli ni haa hulutsoo be baa shi koni nu lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can make food efficiently, while keeping leaves off hot, damp soil where fungal rot and diseases spread.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers if they lack water, if shade is inadequate, or if tiny pollinating insects called midges are missing. Maintaining proper shade trees ensures pollinator presence and conserves moisture.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛji nu bɛ amɛmli. Shade ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Midge lɛ laaje. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha otsei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during mild rainfall and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni waaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally have shallow roots that can be destroyed underground by pests like nematodes or stem borers. Propping mature plants with wooden poles prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ afite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔ ŋmeii tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers nɔ. Tsei ni eda lɛ ni akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear the weeds and bush around the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni bɔle kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing the base removes weeds that steal valuable nutrients, water, and sunlight from young cocoa trees, while also preventing pests and diseases from hiding near the trunk.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shishigbɛ lɛ, egbeɔ jwɛi ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai akatee amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ he.

english: What kind of tools or machines should I choose when clearing heavy bush on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ dɛŋdade loo tsɔne esa akɛ mahala kɛ́ miijie jwɛi ni tsii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: For light grass and small weeds, cutlasses or motorized brush cutters work best, but for dense vegetation and woody stems, heavy-duty clearing machines save labor and create a cleaner planting bed.
ga: Kɛha jwɛi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ jwɛi bibii Atsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛha tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ tsei akutsei lɛ, jwɛi shwiemɔ ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ haa nitsumɔ baa shi ni ehaa he ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ he tseɔ.

english: Is it better to burn the bush after clearing my land or cut it down mechanically?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi lɛ beni mijie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo mikɛ tsɔnei baafolɔ?

english: Cutting down the bush without burning leaves organic matter on the soil, which decays into natural manure, keeps the soil cool, and preserves useful soil insects.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei bibii ni ashãaa lɛ, ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni baafite ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni sũ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɔ shi

english: What is the best time of the year for me to clear land for a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ hee?

english: Clearing is best done towards the end of the dry season so that your land is completely prepared before the main rainy season begins for planting.
