ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee koni osaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot survive intense, direct sunlight; they need shade from surrounding trees or crops like plantains to keep them cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ adɛŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Should I cut down every single plant on my plot before planting cocoa, or leave some standing?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso fɛɛ tso dani madu kookoo loo maha ema shi?

english: You should only clear harmful weeds and unwanted brush, but leave good shade trees standing to protect the young cocoa plants from heat stress.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ brɔshi ni ataooo lɛ pɛ. Shi shimɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and curling during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow, curling leaves usually indicate heat stress and water loss caused by excessive exposure to harsh sunlight and lack of protective shade trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ kɛ nu ni laajeɔ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ tsei ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli lɛ mli baa.

english: How does clearing the topsoil too deeply affect my farm's productivity?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni akuɔ mli tsɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔ lɛ mli yibiiwoo lɛ he?

english: Removing topsoil strips away the fertile layer rich in nutrients and organic matter, making it difficult for young cocoa roots to establish and absorb food.
ga: Sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaafee niyenii ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly right after I clear my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing removes the top vegetative cover, allowing buried weed seeds to receive direct sunlight and rain, which triggers rapid regrowth.
ga: Klearing jieɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa ŋwɛi lɛ. Ha jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ awo hulu la kɛ nugbɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe oya lɛ

english: How does using blunt tools during field clearing harm my crops?
ga: Te nibii ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Blunt cutlasses tear and damage plant roots and stems instead of making clean cuts, which delays land preparation and increases the risk of crop disease.
ga: Kakla ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ gbálaa tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni efiteɔ amɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofolɔ mli lɛ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha tsei ahe helai aya hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with large leaves that provide the necessary shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa tree's first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli.

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in high humidity. Pruning extra branches to let air and sunlight through, clearing weeds, and removing rotten pods helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ enɛ baa, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji fɛ̃i fa babaoo. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli, ni ajie jwɛi, ni ajie ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the roots swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to build high soil mounds for my yams instead of planting on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ maha mi-sweet potatoes lɛ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow long and thick underground, so they need loose, deep soil to expand properly. Mounding soft earth creates room for the tubers to grow big without hitting hard ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ato lɛ haa gbɛ haa bulb agboi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛnáaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the topsoil, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea restores green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ adara ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets too hot or when plants experience water stress. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing the plant from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ awo yibii

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on leaf sap, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. Sprays made from neem seed extract can help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Spray ni akɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu fee lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why can't I plant my orange trees close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu mi-orange tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maha amɛ gbɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: When orange trees are planted too close, their roots fight over nutrients and water, while their tall leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing them out allows every tree to produce bigger, healthier fruit harvests.
ga: Beni Aduɔ Orange Tsei ni Ebɛŋkɛ Tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. yɛ be mli ni baai kakadaji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni kã tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso woɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I grow cowpeas in the same field where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen nutrients out of the soil. Legumes like cowpeas have special root structures that capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, natural refreshing it for the next season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni aná hejɔɔmɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain stalks fall over so easily during stormy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground. As the fruit bunch grows heavy at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with a wooden prop or bamboo stake keeps it upright.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ bafee nɔ ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ baaná muji babaoo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ loo ŋmei tsei fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is good for growing vegetables before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko hi kɛha aduawai adumɔ dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: Good agricultural land usually has dark brown or black topsoil that crumbles easily in your hand and smells fresh. Soil that is sticky red clay or pure river sand usually lacks the organic matter and drainage needed for healthy crop roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni fiteɔ oya yɛ nine mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ hee. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔji ni ji shikpɔŋ tsuru loo faa mli ŋã ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nu ni hoɔ ni he hiaa kɛha tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. In low-lying areas or heavy clay soil, standing water drowns the root system, creating perfect conditions for fungal rots to destroy the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani akpa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow from the middle of the leaf down to the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya shishigbɛ kɛmiiya shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing down the middle of a leaf is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in soil. Maize requires nitrogen to make dark green chlorophyll; adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore the green color and crop strength.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee klorofil ni tsuɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ he afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When temperatures get too high and the air is very dry, tomato pollen dries out and becomes sterile, so the flowers cannot set fruit. Mulching around the roots and regular watering helps keep the plant cool enough to form tomatoes.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ. Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛto tomato shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield very little when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes intense competition between young plants for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving plants proper spacing ensures each stalk gets enough sunlight and root space to form full, heavy ears or tubers.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa dumɔwui ni he hiaa hulu la lɛ ateŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ he ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa hulu la kɛ shishifãi ahe he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ toi loo bulbs ni tsii, ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do cocoa trees dry up and die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally adapt to growing under forest canopy shade. Direct sunlight damages their delicate leaves and dries out the surrounding soil too fast, which is why farmers keep large canopy trees or plant plantains to provide shade.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ koo lɛ shishi shweremɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ okwaafoi adu tsei wuji ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi loo amɛdu dumɔwui koni amɛha hulutsoo lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting groundnuts alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special bacteria in its roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as natural fertilizer that helps the neighboring maize crop grow stronger.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he ni eyɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ eshishifãi amli ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do I need to put long sticks in the ground for my yam leaves to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ tso kakadaŋŋ atsu nii lɛ? Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines produce long runners that need to capture as much sunlight as possible to build large tubers underground. Staking holds leaves high above the ground where sunlight is abundant and prevents fungal diseases that thrive on wet leaves touching the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ foidalɔi ni yaa shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔɔŋ yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la yɛ lɛ, ni etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai ni efɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpeɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden pepper plants curling up into small twisted shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of young leaves. The insect feeding damages leaf tissue and can spread plant viruses that cause permanent curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kplukai ni ayeɔ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tso mli helai ni haa tsitsii lɛ shwieɔ shi daa lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why does paddy rice grow happily in standing water while my corn plants drown and die in water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ miishɛɛ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ? Beni mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels inside their stems and roots that transport oxygen down from the leaves into submerged roots, allowing them to thrive in waterlogged soil that would suffocate corn roots.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni baanyɛ aha ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can building a simple wooden roof or shed over my vegetables prevent them from catching diseases during the rainy season?
ga: Tso ni akɛfee tsũ yiteŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo ŋmɔ ni akɛwoɔ aduawai amli Ani ebaanyɛ etsĩ helai anaa diɛŋtsɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Yes, building an overhead structure keeps heavy rain from splashing dirty water and disease germs from the soil onto plant leaves. It keeps the foliage dry, which stops many common fungal and bacterial diseases from spreading.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋwɛi ŋta ni ama lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu ni mli ewo muji kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tsei ahe baai anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai babaoo ni afɔɔ namɔ ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ bacteria mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Will my crops still produce good fruit if I grow them under a shed, or do they need direct sunlight all day?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai lolo kɛji midu amɛ yɛ tsũ ko shishi? Aloo ani hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he miihia amɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Most crops need sunlight to make food, but partial shade can protect sensitive plants like tomatoes from extreme heat. However, if the shed is too dark, plants will grow tall and weak with very few fruits.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii. Shi hulutsoo be ko baanyɛ abu tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, tamɔ tomato, ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ tsɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do plants sometimes rot or wilt inside a covered farm structure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei fiteɔ loo amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tsũi ni aha nɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covered structures trap heat and moisture. If there is no good airflow or ventilation through the sides, the stagnant humid air causes heat stress and creates a breeding ground for mold and soft rot.
ga: Tsuji ni akɛ amɛyiteŋ eha nɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ bɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ekã shi lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Does putting a roof over my crops mean insects will stop attacking my farm?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛhaa lɛ baatsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii baakpa miŋmɔ lɛ tutuamɔ?

english: No, an overhead roof mainly protects against rain damage and leaf diseases. Flying insects and soil pests can still reach your crops unless you also use fine mesh netting around the sides.
ga: Dabi, nɔ titri ni buɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni efiteɔ nii kɛ tsei ahe helai ahe. Kplukai ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi baanyɛ ashɛ onibii ahe lolo. Ja okɛ ŋtayaa kpakpa hu ebɔle sɛɛgbɛ lɛ he.

english: How exactly does rain water cause my crop leaves to turn black and rot?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ?

english: Rain drops wash disease-causing fungi and bacteria onto leaves, and standing water on the leaf surface allows those germs to hatch and penetrate the plant tissue. Dry leaves rarely get infected.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ hoɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Ni nu ni damɔ baai anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa nakai helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ni amɛfɔɔ ni amɛboteɔ tsei lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, hela baaa baai ni egbi lɛ anɔ.

english: Is planting crops under a man-made shed better than planting them under large shade trees on my farm?
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsũ ni gbɔmɔ fee lɛ shishi Ani ehi fe tsei wuji ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: A man-made shed gives you shelter without stealing nutrients, because large trees have big root systems that take away water and fertilizer meant for your crops.
ga: Tsũ ni gbɔmɔ fee lɛ baaha oná wɔɔhe ni ojuuu niyenii mli hewalɛ nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei wuji lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii lɛ.

english: Why are my vegetable crops growing tall and thin with weak stems under my roof cover?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ miikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛshishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When crops do not receive enough sunlight under a cover, they stretch themselves upward searching for light. This uses up their energy, leaving the stems thin and incapable of supporting heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa amɛhe lɛ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyatao la. Enɛ baafite ohewalɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: How can I test a new farming technique from another country to know if it will work on my land in Ghana?
ga: Maka okwaayeli he ŋaa hee ko ni jɛ maŋ kroko nɔ lɛ makwɛ kɛji ebaatsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ lo.

english: Always try the new method on a small plot of land first. This lets you observe how local soil, hot weather, and rainfall affect the crops before spending a lot of money to change your whole farm.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, kaa gbɛ hee ko okwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ saa oŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa. Dani obaafite shika babaoo ni okɛtsake oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Is it worth the money for a small-scale farmer like me to build a shelter over my crops?
ga: Ani shika lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha okwaafonyo bibioo ko tamɔ mi koni ema shĩa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: It depends on the crop. High-value crops like tomatoes or sweet peppers that suffer high disease losses in the rainy season often yield enough extra healthy harvest to pay back the cost of the shelter.
ga: Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni jara wa waa tamɔ tomato loo bell pepper lɛ helai fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwoɔ shĩa lɛ shika ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english: How long should I wait to see if a new crop protection method is actually improving my yield?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ koni mana kɛji gbɛ hee ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You should observe the crops through at least one full growing season from planting to harvest so you can compare the final yield and quality against your traditional methods.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be kome mli fɛɛ, kɛjɛ dumɔ mli kɛyashi ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni okɛ naagbee yibiiwoo kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ ato gbɛ ni otsɔɔ nɔ otsuɔ nii shishijee lɛ he.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually shows that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK around the root area can feed the soil and fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni esaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that catch nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally fertilize the soil, helping the maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ekɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my tomato plants help them grow in hot weather?
ga: Bɔ ni jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves—called mulching—acts like a protective blanket over the ground. It traps moisture in the soil so it doesn't evaporate quickly in the sun, keeping root zones cool and hydrated.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ he. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ lɛ, efoŋ oya. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and fail to yield big cobs when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo ŋmãa wuji beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to develop strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food that builds big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun, preventing diseases from wet soil and helping the plant produce bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Tsi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji

english: Having too many small shoots (suckers) around the main stem drains food and water away from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main plant produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso bibii babaoo (tso) ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he. Enɛ baaha niyenii kɛ nu akashɛ dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining away, usually during heavy rains or in low clay soil. Planting on raised mounds or ridges allows extra water to run off, keeping the roots safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shi ni ejeee kpo. Bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ babaoo. ni oha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: What makes my pepper leaves curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny pests like whiteflies or mites sucking juices from the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Keeping the farm free of weeds and spraying approved insect remedies can protect the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu tsei ahe.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress, lack sufficient shade, or get attacked by sap-sucking pests like mirids. Maintaining adequate shade trees and protecting the farm from pests keeps the flowers on the branches.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. Shade ni sa ni bɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuaa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ni abu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my green pepper fruits fall off the plant before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili yibii ni ji green lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their young fruits when soil moisture changes too drastically—like going from very dry soil to heavy watering suddenly—or during extreme heat. Keeping soil moisture steady with regular watering prevents fruit drop.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛyibii bibii lɛ kɛji tsakemɔ ko ni sa kadimɔ ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, tamɔ tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛyaa nu ni mli wa nɔ. loo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential nutrient that maize needs to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nitrogen down into the soil beyond the reach of young roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa atsɔ eŋɔli ni efee hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie nitrogen lɛ nɔ kɛtee sũ lɛ mli ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I plant maize on the same piece of land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of its plant food and lets crop diseases build up; rotating your maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni ehaa tsei ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that burrows into the center whorl of young maize plants to feed on new leaves before the cob forms.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillar, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli koni eye baai heei dani ŋmãa lɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by extreme heat and lack of water causing the leaves to protect themselves from moisture loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ mli Enɛ haa baai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct, full sunlight. They need partial shade from larger trees or temporary shade crops like plantains to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can capture maximum sunlight to make food. Lacking stakes causes the leaves to crowd on the ground, leading to diseases and small underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Tso ni bɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Ekɛ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why are my hot pepper flowers falling off instead of growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is an imbalance of nutrients in the soil during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa loo be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground if I leave them in the soil during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa beaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains water easily. When heavy rains leave water sitting in the soil for days, the roots cannot get oxygen and begin to rot underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ sũ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛhe kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do plantain suckers with narrow leaves grow better than plantain suckers with wide leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe plantain tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ?

english: Suckers with narrow, needle-like leaves (called sword suckers) have strong attachments to the mother root and large food reserves, whereas broad-leafed suckers (water suckers) are weaker and yield smaller bunches.
ga: Sucker ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ ŋmeii. (ni atsɛɔ amɛ sword suckers) lɛ kpɛtɛɔ nyɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ niyenii jɛɛhei wuji lɛ ahe waa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ (suckers) lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: The season's first rain often only wet the surface layer of soil while underneath remains hot and dry. Seeds planted too early will sprout, but die quickly when a short dry spell follows that initial rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ lɛ kã he edɔ ni egbi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi egboɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ko ba. Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon sun even though I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense heat, tomato leaves lose water faster than their roots can drink it up. As long as the soil stays moist, they usually recover by evening, but putting dry grass around the base helps keep the soil cool and wet.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tomato baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ Bei pii lɛ, amɛhe baajɔ amɛ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. Shi kɛ akɛ jwɛi wo Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods like the harmattan to save water and protect themselves from dying. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves again.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ hulutsoo be mli, tamɔ Harmatta, koni eye ebua ni nu lɛ akafite ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable roots rot and turn soft when water stays on my land for days after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like they need water. When rain sits on the farm without draining, it suffocates the roots, causing them to decay and die.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow starting from the tip and moving down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant gets too much or too little water. Keeping the soil consistently moist without overwatering helps the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náa nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii amli.

english: Why did my young maize crops burn and dry up after I put fertilizer right at the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ shãa ni egbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmãa lɛ ewo ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong and draws water away from the plant if placed directly against the stem. Placing it a small distance away allows the roots to safely absorb it through the soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli wa waa ni ebaajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to amɛhe fioo lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without bearing good fruit when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni amɛfeɔ shwiili beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight for sunlight, soil food, and water. Spacing them properly allows each plant to get enough sunlight and nutrients to produce thick stems and healthy fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to make mounds of soil before planting my yams instead of planting in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ ni abua naa dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep under the soil. Making loose, soft mounds allows the yam roots to expand easily without fighting hard, compact ground, resulting in larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ aha gɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ he ko ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ abɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ baatsɔ agbo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even when I plant high-quality seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow aggressive roots that steal water, manure, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the soil's food so they can grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ woɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Koni amɛdara ni amɛhe awa

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing too much water in extreme heat. By rolling inward, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight, saving moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛfoɔ kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with big leaves but produce almost no tubers when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji, shi kɛ́ akpa lɛ, eshwɛ fioo ni ebaaba lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or foliage growth is overstimulated, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of storing food in the roots. Balanced soil nutrients ensure energy goes down into forming tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo ebaa lɛ shweremɔ fe nine lɛ, ekanyaa. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi kɛyaa bulb lɛ mli.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences sudden stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive water. When stressed, the plant sheds flowers to conserve its energy and survive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ ko trukaa, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu babaoo. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do young cocoa trees dry up and die if I clear all the tall trees on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. They require shade trees or plantains nearby to act as canopy umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the soft cocoa leaves while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛha amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ŋtayaa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe beni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need to reach maximum sunlight to generate energy for growing large underground tubers. Staking lifts leaves off the humid ground, boosting photosynthesis and reducing fungal diseases caused by wet leaves touching the soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ hia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ. Ajieɔ staking kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni fotosintɛsis yaa hiɛ. ni ebaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa ni efɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpeɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ shi

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay small and light when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When planted too closely, vegetable roots and leaves compete fiercely for water, air, and soil nutrients. Giving each cabbage enough space allows its leaves to expand fully and form a dense head.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Tsofai ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ nu, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli. Kɛ́ aha cabbage fɛɛ cabbage gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ebaa lɛ mli alɛɛ kwraa ni eyitsei afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my maize yield improve after I plant groundnuts on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ tee hiɛ beni midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut crop is harvested, the natural nitrogen left behind enriches the soil, feeding the next crop like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei tsei Adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ekɛ niyenii aha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my crops even after I apply fertilizer to the whole field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive, wild root systems designed to absorb nutrients faster than farmed crops. If weeds are not cleared before fertilizing, they steal most of the plant food meant for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni afee koni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji ajieee jwɛi kɛjɛɛɛ mli dani awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai jwɛi lɛ baaju tsei niyenii ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and collapse in the afternoon even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil is typically caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases that damage the water pathways inside the stem. Even though water is in the soil, the blocked stem prevents it from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni fiteɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ Shi tso ni etsi ehe lɛ tsiɔ enaa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow while the rest stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually indicates that the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant steals nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and tender leaves that burn easily under direct sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Maize leaves roll up to reduce leaf surface area and prevent water loss during intense heat. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni baa lɛ nɔ akafee nɔ ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa mli. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because water displaces air, starving the roots of oxygen. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily and prevents root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and capture maximum sunlight, which generates energy for tuber growth. Staking also keeps leaves off damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and weed competition.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa kɛha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ jwɛi akaŋshii naa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Providing consistent water and adding compost or manure helps the plant retain flowers and set healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Too many shoots around one plantain stem compete for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning away weaker suckers and leaving only one or two strong stems allows the main plant to produce a much larger, heavier bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni bɔle tso kome he lɛ kɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la miitswa akaŋ. Kɛtsɔ niji bibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni ashiɔ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii kwraa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil richer for future crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts work with natural soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the next crop you plant in that field.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ helai tsuɔ nii koni amɛjie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open right before they get fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ mli gbalaa dani amɛshwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when soil goes from dry to very wet suddenly, causing the inside of the fruit to expand faster than the skin can stretch. Keeping soil moisture steady throughout the growth cycle prevents cracking.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ haa tso yibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa yɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why are small ragged holes appearing inside the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like Fall Armyworms feeding inside the growing shoot. Identifying this damage early allows you to control the pest before it destroys the central growing point of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni efite lɛ ayɔsemɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ dani amɛfiteɔ he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Heavy rainwater washes fertilizer off the soil surface before crop roots have a chance to absorb it. Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist but heavy downpours are not expected, ensuring your crop gets full benefit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana sɛɛnamɔi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn yellow when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil. Planting plantains or leaving some tall trees provides temporary shade and holds moisture in the ground until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ loo tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer early in the season helps keep the leaves dark green and healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize make my soil richer?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa adu lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When these roots decay in the soil, they release natural food that feeds nearby crops like maize without needing extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛye tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Cassava buds are designed to grow upward toward the sun; planting them upside down forces the shoots to grow downward before bending up, which wastes the plant's energy and reduces the size and number of tubers you harvest.
ga: Afee Yucca ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛdara kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara kɛya shi dani amɛkoto amɛhe. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ hewalɛ afite. ni okɛ ŋmeii ni okpaa lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibɔ ​​aba shi.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small dark droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of maize plants. Checking your crops early and applying approved neem extracts or targeted treatments directly into the funnel kills the pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Ni oookwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛya tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ baagbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Staking raises yam leaves into the sunlight so they can make more food to produce large tubers underground, while also keeping the leaves away from wet soil that can cause fungal diseases.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhoo babaoo ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba lɛ he.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding excess nitrogen helps the flowers stay on the vine and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi wain tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers to transplant to a new plot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala banana tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: Choose 'sword suckers', which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad stem base, because they grow faster and produce larger bunches than 'water suckers', which have wide leaves and grow weakly.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud’, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ kui wuji fe ‘nu mli ŋmeii’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the base of my pepper plants with dry grass during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from evaporating soil moisture, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop field.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ, ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaha jwɛi akaye he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it better to water my vegetable leaves in the early morning instead of late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ oooha aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ nu leebi moŋ fe gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Watering late in the evening leaves the leaves wet all night, creating a warm, damp environment that encourages fungal diseases like leaf spot and rot to spread. Morning watering allows the sun to dry the foliage quickly.
ga: Nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he hewalɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya.

english: What is inside the blue fertilizer bags that extension officers distribute, and how does it help my crops?
ga: Mɛni yɔɔ bluu ŋmɔshi nibii ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ jaa lɛ amli? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: The blue bags usually contain NPK fertilizer, which provides three major nutrients: Nitrogen for leaf growth, Phosphorus for strong roots, and Potassium for healthy fruit and grain development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii etɛ haa lɛ yɛ bluu kotokui amli: Nitrogen kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Fosfɔs kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ potassium kɛha aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ.

english: Is chemical fertilizer the same thing as crop spray, or do they do different jobs on the farm?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ kome loo amɛtsuɔ nitsumɔi srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: They do different jobs. Fertilizer works as food to feed and strengthen your plants, while crop sprays act like medicine or protection to kill weeds, insects, and plant diseases.
ga: Amɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Tsoi ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa loo hebuu kɛjɛɔ jwɛi, kooloi bibii, kɛ tsei ahe helai ahe.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crops are hungry for key nutrients like Nitrogen. Adding the right fertilizer gives the soil the food plants need to stay green and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye oŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ nitrogen. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛshwere.

english: How do I know the best time to put fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer is most effective when applied to moist soil shortly after rain while plants are actively growing, allowing the roots to easily absorb the dissolved nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ beni tsei lɛ miida waa lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ mlɛo.

english: Should I place fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop or put it in the soil nearby?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifã lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should place fertilizer a few inches away from the main stem in small holes or rings so it doesn't burn the plant tissue while still reaching the spreading roots underground.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo bu bibioo ko loo ŋwɛi ŋtayaa ko mli kɛjɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he inchii fioo komɛi. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ akashã be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo lɛ.

english: Can putting too much fertilizer on my fields actually harm my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, applying too much fertilizer can 'burn' crop roots and leaves, causing them to dry up, turn brown, and potentially die instead of yield more harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ‘ashã’ tsei shishifãi kɛ baai. Ehaa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ gĩɔ. etsɔ blɔfo ni ebaanyɛ egbo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I rely on agricultural extension officers before using new chemical sprays on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ko nɔ dani mikɛ tsofa hee ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii?

english: Extension officers know the exact type, correct mixture, and right application timing for chemicals, protecting your crops from accidental damage and keeping you safe from harmful exposure.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi lɛ le nɔ̃ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli. nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ja kɛ be ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii Buu onibii ahe koni akafite yɛ oshara mli. ni eha ohe ahi ohe kɛjɛ osharai ahe.

english: What basic steps should I take to protect myself when applying sprays given by agricultural workers?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee koni mabu mihe kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛhaa okwaayeli nitsulɔi lɛ miitsu nii?

english: Always wear protective clothing like long sleeves, boots, and a mouth cover, avoid spraying against strong winds, and wash your skin and clothes thoroughly with soap right after spraying.
ga: Wo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ shɛɛti ni hiɛ nine kakadaŋŋ agboi, atadei kɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa bo. Ni okɛ samla afɔ ohewolo kɛ otadei ahe jogbaŋŋ kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How should I store leftover fertilizer bags so they do not spoil before the next planting season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ato koni amɛkafite dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Store fertilizer bags in a cool, dry room raised off the bare ground on wooden planks, keeping them tightly closed to prevent rainwater and damp air from turning the fertilizer into hard lumps.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kotoku lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi. Kɛtsɔ ewomɔ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ tso ko nɔ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ amɛ ŋmɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni nugbɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ akatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: Why does the government distribute specific fertilizers directly to smallholder farmers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ jaa ŋmɔshi nibii tɛ̃ɛ ehaa okwaafoi bibii pɛ lɛ?

english: The government provides tested, reliable fertilizers matched to regional soils at supported prices so farmers can safely increase crop yields without risking money on fake or harmful inputs.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aka amɛ akwɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni kɛ kpokpaa nɔ shikpɔji lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ haa yɛ jara ni yeɔ ebuaa nɔ. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛkɛ shika wooo oshara mli yɛ amalei loo nibii ni yɔɔ oshara ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense heat and direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees alongside cocoa keeps the soil moist and protects young trees from scorching.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ dumɔwui loo be kukuoo mli shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Should I trim away the small shoot leaves growing around the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Ani ajie plantain lɛ shishigbɛ?

english: Yes, removing excess suckers is important because too many suckers compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Keeping only two or three strong suckers per plant allows the main tree to produce larger plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ejaakɛ ŋmeii babaoo kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso kome mli ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is my maize crop turning yellowish with thin stems instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants use to build green leaves and grow strong stalks, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat hole patterns into the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the inner leaves of growing maize. Inspecting the field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts directly into the leaf funnels stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tswaa ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli baai lɛ. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ awo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my rice yield drop whenever the water in the field dries up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baagbi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Lowland rice requires steady moisture during its flowering and grain-filling stages to transport nutrients into the rice grains. When the field dries up prematurely, the plants become stressed and produce empty or light grains.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ biɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmaa ni eyiɔ mli lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya ŋmaa lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔji lɛ gĩ mra Tso lɛ haoɔ ni ewoɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are ready for harvest under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and cracks start appearing on the soil surface around the base of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ shwereɔ kwraa kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Eshi tsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko Ni ŋmeii bɔi baa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put long sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni mikɛ niji kakadaji awo mli koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce the energy required for large tubers to grow underground. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground and prevents diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe, ni ehaa helai baaa.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants get dark spots and dry up during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and high humidity encourage fungal diseases like tomato blight. Pruning the lowest leaves and spacing plants properly allows air to flow through, which keeps the leaves dry and reduces disease spread.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tomato baa mli tsɛŋemɔ baa. Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ni ashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or nutrient shortages. Keeping the soil consistently damp and applying balanced fertilizer helps flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-pepper lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why should I spread dried grass or dry leaves on top of the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi afɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, trap moisture in the soil, keeps the roots cool during hot days, prevents weeds from sprouting, and improves soil fertility as it decays.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why is cassava considered such a reliable crop to grow for feeding my farm workers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ ŋmei akɛ eji ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni aduɔ koni akɛha miŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ niyenii lɛ?

english: Cassava is very resilient because its thick roots store water and nutrients underground, allowing it to survive dry seasons and poor soil conditions where other crops might fail, ensuring a continuous food supply.
ga: Cassava nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi waa ejaakɛ eshishifãi ni mli tse lɛ toɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni tsei krokomɛi baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii baa daa.

english: Why do yam plants need high soil mounds to produce good tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ he hiaa sweet potato tsei lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand fully. Planting them in tall soil mounds allows the tubers to grow long, smooth, and thick without struggling against hard, compacted ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kwraa. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ akpee.

english: How long can cassava stay in the ground before it starts to spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ebɔi fitemɔ?

english: Cassava acts like a living storehouse underground. Its roots can remain safely in the soil for several months to a year after maturing, allowing you to harvest only what you need to feed workers or sell.
ga: Cassava tsuɔ nii tamɔ nitoohe ko ni hiɛ ka yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi afi yɛ amɛdalɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nɔ pɛ ni he hiaa bo koni oha onitsulɔi lɛ niyenii loo okɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: How do I know when my yams are mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni sweet potatoes lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: When the yam vines and leaves start turning yellow and drying up, it is a natural sign that the plant has stopped growing and the tuber underground is fully mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Beni sweet potato wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Eji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni eshishifãi lɛ edara ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why does my corn crop need more fertilizer and attention than cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hiɛdɔɔ babaoo fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Corn is a fast-growing, heavy-feeding crop with shallow roots, meaning it needs quick and rich soil nutrients, especially nitrogen, to build strong stalks and fill out full cobs.
ga: Abɛi ji tso ko ni daa oya, niyenii babaoo ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia amɛ oya. titri lɛ nitrogen Koni ekɛfee tsei ni wa ni eyi obɔ.

english: Can I plant corn and cassava together on the same field?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop them because corn matures quickly in three to four months, while cassava grows slower. By the time you harvest the corn, the cassava will take over the remaining space.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛwo mli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa oya yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo fe tsutsu lɛ. Kɛji okpa ŋmãa Cassava baaŋɔ he ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: What causes corn leaves to turn yellow early in the season, and how does it hurt my crop?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli? Ni te ebaafite minibii lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the corn plant lacks essential nitrogen from the soil, which stunts its growth and results in small cobs with missing grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraaa oya, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni dumɔwui bɛ amɛhe.

english: How can growing staple crops like corn and cassava give me both food and money?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ aha maná niyenii kɛ shika fɛɛ?

english: Corn yields a quick harvest that can feed your workers early in the season, while surplus corn and cassava can be taken to the local market for steady cash flow.
ga: Abɛi woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya ni baanyɛ aha onitsulɔi lɛ niyenii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni fa fe nine lɛ aya maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ koni shika ni yaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: How can crops like yams bring in foreign currency from international trade?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ sweet potato aba maŋsɛɛ shika kɛjɛ majimaji ateŋ jarayeli mli?

english: High-quality Ghanaian yams are heavily demanded overseas. When exporters buy your top-grade yams to sell in foreign markets, it earns foreign exchange for the country and higher income for growers.
ga: Ghana ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni ataoɔ waa yɛ maŋsɛɛ. Beni mɛi ni kɛ nibii majeɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ heɔ o-sweet potatoes ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋsɛɛ jarayeli hei. Ebaaha maŋ lɛ aná maŋsɛɛ shika, ni ebaaha mɛi ni duɔ nii lɛ aná shika babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil so fast, and how can I turn them into long-lasting profits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ sɛɛnamɔi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nɔ?

english: Raw cassava roots deteriorate within 2 to 3 days after harvest because of high moisture content. Processing them into dry cassava flour or gari preserves them for months and allows you to sell them at higher prices.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni ŋmɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo hewɔ lɛ Kɛ́ okɛfee ŋmei ashikishaŋ ni egbi kɛ gari lɛ, ebaaha ehi shi nyɔji babaoo ni eye ebua bo ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ.

english: Why do new improved seed varieties like Ghana 14 perform better than the traditional seeds I saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ tamɔ Ghana 14 lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seed varieties are carefully bred to withstand local dry spells, resist common plant diseases, and produce higher yields compared to saved seeds, which gradually lose their strength and purity over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ maŋ lɛ mli hɔmɔ shihilɛi lɛ anaa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe, ni fiofio lɛ, hewalɛ kɛ hetsemɔ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can locally grown corn varieties give me as good a harvest as imported grains?
ga: Ani ŋmãa srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ?

english: Yes, high-yielding local corn varieties are specifically adapted to Ghana's soil and climate, meaning they can equal or even beat imported crop yields when planted with proper spacing and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsake maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha Ghana shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ kpãa gbee loo amɛho he kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai.

english: How do I know if a specific crop variety will grow well in my local area's soil and weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ko baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crop varieties are tested in different zones; extension officers can tell you which varieties are bred specifically for your region's rainfall patterns and soil conditions.
ga: Aka tsei srɔtoi lɛ akwɛ yɛ hei srɔtoi. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akɛɛ bo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔ lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the corn is missing nitrogen in the soil, which often happens when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when planting in worn-out land.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ laaje. aloo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite nɔ

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural way of saving water; by curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to stop moisture from evaporating.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ŋmɔtɔ akafo.

english: Why are some of the corn cobs I harvested missing seeds on half of the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ fã ni elaaje lɛ?

english: Empty spots on a cob happen when hot, dry weather or pests damage the silks during pollination, preventing the individual grains from forming.
ga: He ni nɔ ko bɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi loo kooloi bibii kpata siliki lɛ hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui aŋkroaŋkroi afee.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni ŋmeii lɛ hu yɛ bibii.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my maize field so it grows strong?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-ŋmei lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Maize needs fertilizer early when it reaches knee-height to build strong stalks, and again just before flowering to help fill out the corn cobs.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛjɛ shishijee, kɛ́ eshɛ enaji ahe, koni efee ŋmeii ni wa. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu dani ewo fɔfɔi koni eye ebua ni ekɛwo ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow so slowly even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the plant food, water, and sunlight from the soil before your crop's roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ tsei niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he.

english: Why did many of the maize seeds I stored in my barn fail to sprout when I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ lɛ?

english: Stored seeds lose their power to germinate if they are exposed to heat, moisture, or insects, which damage the living embryo inside the seed before planting day.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo, hulutsoo loo kooloi ahe, ni baanyɛ afite fɔmɔ kotokui ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ dani adu gbi lɛ.

english: Why should I pay more attention to growing food crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama niyenii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ babaoo lɛ?
