english: Food crops provide quick food and income for your household, and they are often easier to sustain when you face challenges like shortages of water or inputs for other demanding crops.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ji niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe oya kɛha oshiabii lɛ. Ni bei pii lɛ, ewaaa akɛ oookwɛ amɛ nɔ kɛ́ okɛ naagbai tamɔ nu ni bɛ loo nibii krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ kpe.

english: Why is food crop farming recommended when water resources are limited on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Food crops often require less intensive chemical spraying schedules, which helps you avoid the heavy burden of fetching large amounts of water repeatedly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni mli wa fioo lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ jatsu ni ji nu babaoo ni okɛbaatsu nii shii abɔ lɛ he.

english: How long should I wait after transplanting my seedlings before I apply chemical sprays?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo he kroko lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ ni mikɛ tsofai afɔ amɛnɔ?

english: You should wait about two to three weeks after transplanting so the young plant has time to overcome transplant shock and settle into the soil before receiving chemicals.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ be mli ni okɛ tsofa lɛ ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛye shwiemɔ he gbeyeishemɔ nɔ kunim ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛná tsofai lɛ.

english: Can I spray my young crops with chemicals immediately on the day I plant them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ tsei bibii anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ gbi ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, spraying immediately can harm tender young plants because they are too weak and do not yet have enough developed branches or leaves to absorb the chemical safely.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnáko niji loo baai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofai lɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ awui.

english: How do I know when my newly planted crops are mature enough for chemical treatments?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mitsei heei ni midu lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai atsu nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Your crops are usually ready between the second and third week after planting, once they have started growing sturdy branches that can handle the application.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, onibii lɛ feɔ klalo yɛ otsi ni ji enyɔ kɛ etɛ lɛ teŋ yɛ odumɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛnáa niji ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Which part of my crop actually absorbs the chemical spray I apply?
ga: Mɛɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fãi diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: It is primarily the branches and leaves of the crop that absorb the chemical, which is why you must allow the plant to grow enough green foliage before spraying.
ga: Nɔ ni he hiaa ji akɛ, tso lɛ niji kɛ baai lɛ gbalaa tsofai. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni oha tso lɛ aná baai eŋɔli ni fa bɔ ni sa dani okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why won't my crop benefit from chemical spraying if I apply it too early in its growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ náŋ he sɛɛ kɛji akɛ mikɛwo mli mra tsɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ mli lɛ?

english: If you spray too early, the plant lacks sufficient branch and leaf surface area to absorb the chemical, causing the product to go to waste without helping the plant.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ oya tsɔ Tsei lɛ bɛ niji kɛ baai lɛ anɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofai. Enɛ haa nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ ni eyeee ebuaaa tso lɛ.

english: How does a lack of water on my farm affect my ability to protect my crops with sprays?
ga: Te nu ni faaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa nyɛmɔ ni miyɔɔ akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ lɛ buɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Chemical sprays must be mixed with significant amounts of water, so if fetching water is difficult, you will struggle to complete the required spraying schedule for your crops.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ afutu nu babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ ewa akɛ ooojie nu Obaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ogbe gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛshwieɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why is it difficult to complete a spray program that requires spraying my farm three times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ agbe tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ shii etɛ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Spraying three times requires finding and carrying heavy volumes of water to the field repeatedly, which becomes very hard to maintain if water sources are far away or labor is scarce.
ga: Bei etɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ biɔ ni atao nu babaoo shii abɔ ni akɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ abaakwɛ nɔ kɛji nu jɛɛhe lɛ yɛ shɔŋŋ loo nitsulɔi faaa.

english: What common challenges should I plan for before starting a crop that needs frequent spraying?
ga: Mɛɛ naagbai ni afɔɔ namɔ esa akɛ mato he gbɛjianɔ dani mabɔi tsei ni biɔ ni akɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ adumɔ?

english: You must plan for steady water availability and labor, as carrying water across the farm multiple times for repeated spraying is one of the hardest parts of crop maintenance.
ga: Esa akɛ oto gbɛjianɔ kɛha nu kɛ nitsumɔ ni yɔɔ daa. Enɛ ji akɛ, nu ni akɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli shii abɔ koni akɛshwie nɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni wa fe fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and intense heat. Tall shade trees protect the young seedlings from sunburn and help retain moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks in the soil for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they get more sunlight and protects them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni hulu la babaoo shɛɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing leaves in an inverted 'V' shape starting at the leaf tip is a common sign that the plant is short of nitrogen, a vital nutrient needed for healthy green leaves and strong stalk growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni feɔ ‘V’ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã ni wa.

english: Curled and distorted leaves with yellow patches are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease. Tiny whitefly insects spread this disease by carrying a virus from infected plants to healthy ones while feeding on the leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Nɔ ni kɛ cassava mosaic hela lɛ baa Whiteflies bibii lɛ gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa kɛtsɔ hela lɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ anɔ beni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or severe dry spells. The plant drops its flowers to save water and energy for basic survival during stressful weather.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni haoɔ mɔ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees yield very small bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Multiple young shoots compete with the main plantain tree for limited water, sunlight, and soil food. Pruning away excess suckers leaves the mother plant with enough energy to produce a large, healthy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu fioo, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak with tiny yields when I sow seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. They spend all their energy growing tall to reach light instead of building thick stems and strong fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ yiblii nɛ mi wa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests every year when I keep planting it in the exact same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ kpaaa ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? Be ni mikɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Maize consumes large amounts of specific nutrients from the soil. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains those nutrients faster than the soil can rebuild them, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ ama ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do the roots of my cowpea plants have small round bumps on them, and will they harm my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ, ni ani amɛbaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Those bumps are root nodules and are actually beneficial to your farm. They host helpful soil organisms that take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, naturally improving fertility for future crops.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ feɔ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ. Amɛhereɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves and stop flowering during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their leaves in dry weather to slow down water loss through evaporation. It is a natural protection mechanism to survive dry conditions until water becomes available again.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu baaje kpo ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees during their first few years to protect their delicate leaves and maintain soil moisture.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Koni abu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants have plenty of big green leaves but no fruits growing on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer causes pepper plants to spend their energy producing leaves instead of flowers and fruit. Balancing nutrients with phosphorus and potassium helps trigger flowering and fruit growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium toɔ he lɛ haa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai daa.

english: Cassava roots rot when soil remains waterlogged because roots need air to breathe. Planting on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, preventing fungal root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Etsiɔ fungal shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Why do my maize yields keep reducing every year when I plant on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize rapidly consumes nutrients from the soil. Planting it repeatedly on the same land drains the soil's fertility, so rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas helps put essential nitrogen back into the earth naturally.
ga: Abele yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn black and dry up after I spray them with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves burn if agrochemicals are mixed at too high a concentration or sprayed during the hottest part of the day. Spraying early in the morning or late afternoon with correct dosages prevents leaf scorching.
ga: Foji lɛ shãa kɛji akɛ akɛ okwaayeli tsofai futu mli babaoo tsɔ loo akɛshwie nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni sa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo shwane lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsofa ni baa lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings grow tall and thin like threads and then fall over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo tamɔ kpãai ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ?

english: Seedlings grow tall and weak when they are overcrowded or lack direct sunlight as they stretch to find light. Spacing seeds properly and ensuring good sunlight creates sturdy, thick stems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji amɛyi obɔ kɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ be mli ni amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛtao la lɛ. Kɛ́ gbɛ ni sa kã dumɔwui lɛ kɛ hulu la kpakpa teŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots near the soil surface that struggle to hold heavy fruit bunches in strong winds. Heap extra soil around the base and prop the plants up with wooden stakes to keep them stable.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛmɔ aduawai akui ni tsii amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Okɛ sũ krokomɛi ato shishigbɛ lɛ he ni okɛ tsei awo tso lɛ nɔ koni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the dirt instead of growing when I plant after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain after a dry season often creates high soil heat and is followed by short dry spells that dry out seeds before they establish. Waiting for stable, continuous rains ensures steady moisture for germination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔɔ waa. ni hulutsoo be kuku nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi dani amɛfee. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa ni eyaa nɔ lɛ mɛmɔ baaha ŋmɔtɔ aba daa koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves with yellow powder inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni powda ko ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the central leaves of the maize plant. Inspecting crops early and applying recommended controls protects the growing point of the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he ni aduɔ nii lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Why do my yam plants produce small tubers when I leave the vines to crawl on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ náa ŋmeii bibii beni mishiɔ wain tsei lɛ ni amɛkpãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight exposure to produce food for tuber growth. Staking the vines on tall sticks exposes leaves to light and keeps them free from soil-borne diseases, resulting in larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Kɛ́ adu wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nine ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aje kpo yɛ la mli, ni ebaaye ebua ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akamɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their tender leaves from scorching until their roots and branches are fully established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ buɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛniji lɛ yeɔ emuu.

english: Which suckers should I select from my plantain bush to plant on a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmeii esa akɛ mahala kɛjɛ dumɔwui ashishi koni madu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Choose 'sword suckers' that have narrow, needle-like leaves and strong bases. They grow much faster and produce bigger, healthier plantain bunches than suckers that already have broad leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud’ ni baai lɛ mli tseee ni tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ shishitoo ni wa. Amɛdaraa oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ plantain tsei ni dara ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ momo lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the top leaves and developing cob to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa baa lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii koni amɛhi shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, or when the plant doesn't get consistent water and nutrients. Without steady moisture, the plant cannot support turning flowers into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu kɛ niyenii nɔ daa Kɛji hulutsoo bɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aye abua ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsake ni amɛfee aduawai.

english: Why do my pepper plants stay small and bear very few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting pepper crops too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper space allows it to branch out and produce more pepper pods.
ga: Pepper tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni egbɛ niji ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo aba.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on sticks so their leaves can trap direct sunlight. Sunlight gives the plant the energy it needs to swell its roots into large yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni eshishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms that attack the sweet, growing middle part of the maize plant. Catching them early with proper treatment prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the stalk.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms ni tutuaa ŋmeii tsei ni ŋɔɔ ni miida lɛ ateŋgbɛ fã lɛ. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra kɛ tsamɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ yitsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crops with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass keeps water from evaporating in the sun, stops weeds from growing, and cools the roots so the crops can grow steadily even in warm weather.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ hulu la lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii aya nɔ akwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli po.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crops are fully ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare, thick main stem. You can dig up one plant to check if the roots have grown thick and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso titri ko ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni mli tse. Obaanyɛ otsa tso ko mli koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli tse ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to water my crops in the afternoon when the sun is hottest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering during hot afternoons causes most water to evaporate instantly before plant roots can drink it, and hot water droplets left on leaves can burn the plant and invite diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ ni ekɛ hela aba.

english: Cocoa yields often decline when soil nutrients are depleted, when trees become old, or when pests and diseases attack unseen. Proper pruning, shade management, and replenishing soil nutrients help bring pod production back up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Beni tso lɛ egbɔ Aloo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua lɛ ni anaaa lɛ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa Shade management Ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ podfeemɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How old does a cocoa tree get before it stops giving a good harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ kakao tso hiɔ shi dani ekpaa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: A cocoa tree usually reaches peak production between 10 and 25 years of age. After 25 to 30 years, pod production naturally declines as the tree becomes less efficient at absorbing nutrients, signaling that it may be time to replant or rehabilitate the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ afii 10 kɛyashi 25 kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ nii babaoo. Yɛ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 sɛɛ lɛ, pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ejaakɛ tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ be eshɛ ni abaadu ekoŋŋ loo abaawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop many flowers, but heavy flower loss occurs when the tree lacks enough water or soil nutrients, or when tiny pollinating insects like midges are absent due to bad weather or chemical sprays.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ midges lɛ laaje yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ fɔŋ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Dropping leaves during the dry season is a natural defense mechanism. Cocoa trees shed leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation, helping the tree conserve moisture and survive the harsh dry weather.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli wa mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle intense full sun. They need temporary shade, like plantain trees planted beside them, to protect them from heat stress until their roots and canopy mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantain ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛyashi shishifãi kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons, steal valuable water, food, and energy away from the main trunk and branches that produce pods. Removing them keeps the main tree healthy and productive.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hewalɛ ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi titri lɛ kɛ niji ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why is it bad for my crop yield if I plant cocoa trees too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too closely causes their branches and roots to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also blocks airflow, creating a humid environment where fungal diseases spread easily.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ niji kɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ hu naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa tree turning black and rotting before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excess shade and wet weather. Clearing weeds, pruning dense branches for better airflow, and removing infected pods helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo be mli. weeding Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni mli wa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes tiny holes in my cocoa pods with sticky liquid leaking out?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ, nu ko ni mli tse hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: This damage is usually caused by sap-sucking pests like mirids (capsids). They pierce the pod skin to feed, leaving wounds that leak sap and allow rot to enter, damaging the beans inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids), ni tsɔɔ pod lɛ hewolo lɛ mli koni amɛye niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Shi pilamɔ ko yɛ he ni nu lɛ etsɔ mli lɛ ni oha egbo. Kpata ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm soil is lacking nutrients for the crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If cocoa tree leaves look pale yellow instead of dark green, if new leaf growth is stunted, or if trees fail to produce healthy pods despite good rainfall, the soil is likely missing essential plant nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Kɛji akɛ baai heei lɛ egbɔjɔ Aloo kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Ekolɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and short roots, making them burn easily in full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains around them to block direct heat and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji. Ehaa shãa baa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ ehe. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with water, oxygen cannot reach the roots. This causes the cassava roots to drown and allows soil fungi to break them down, leading to tuber rot.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do farmers spread dry palm leaves or grass around the bottom of plants during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ ŋmei baai loo jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwieɔ amɛtsei lɛ ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that stops the hot sun from evaporating water out of the dirt, keeping the roots cool and wet longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to keep leaves green and help the crop grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdara.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans on my field make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as free, natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: When seeds are crowded together, the plants end up fighting each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients, leaving all of them weak and underdeveloped.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdarako jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do flowers fall off my pepper plants without turning into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or when tiny pests suck the juices out of the flowers before fruit can form.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii eba amɛmli. Ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a viral sickness spread by these sucking insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ hela ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly and allows pests and diseases that attack that specific crop to build up in the dirt.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa nibii ni adu lɛ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops, so they quickly steal the fertilizer and water out of the soil before your main plants get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya dani otsei titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there are no bigger trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he ko lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and dry out. Planting shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a canopy, giving the young cocoa trees the cool environment and moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛitsu Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ naa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for growth. The plant is moving its remaining food from the older bottom leaves to support the growing top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ. Tso lɛ miitsi niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛfi ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Ani nugbɔ miinɛ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain floods the land without proper drainage, water fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and causing rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms even when the tree looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that spread out near the top of the soil rather than going deep. When the plant carries heavy fruit bunches, strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the soft, wet ground unless you support the stem with wooden stakes.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shɔŋŋ. Beni tso lɛ woɔ aduawai babaoo Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi kɛjɛ hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ oya. Ja okɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsɔne lɛ fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, so the plant sheds the flower instead of growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster than the crops I carefully planted on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ duɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to the local environment, so their roots absorb water and nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. They quickly steal sunlight and space from your crops if you do not clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãa gbee. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjuɔ hulu la kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ onibii amli oya kɛji okɛjieee amɛ mra.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to erect wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso ko kɛha sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food that feeds the underground tuber. Lifting the vines off the ground on tall stakes helps the leaves catch maximum sunlight and keeps them safe from leaf diseases on wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛhe shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do pests attack my maize farm more severely when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli waa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year creates a permanent food supply for pests in your soil. The insects and their eggs stay in the soil through the dry season, ready to attack your new crop in huge numbers as soon as it sprouts.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ooodu afi fɛɛ afi lɛ feɔ niyenii ni hiɔ shi daa kɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Feemɔ klalo akɛ obaatutua oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ babaoo kɛji ekwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops droop and look dead during hot afternoons, but bounce back in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ mɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi obaaku osɛɛ oba gbɛkɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Drooping is the crop's natural way of resting and reducing leaf area to protect itself from losing more water.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejɔɔ ehe ni ekɛbaa baai lɛ anɔ shi koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu babaoo ni efiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight and intense heat. They need shade trees to act as living umbrellas, keeping the surrounding air cool and preserving moisture in the soil while the seedling establishes its roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the maize plant is missing nitrogen, which is its main plant food. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil beyond the roots' reach, so applying organic manure or fertilizer gives the leaves the food they need to grow green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nibii ni bɛ wala mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow tall with lots of leaves but leaves me with tiny cassava roots at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai shi eyɛ cassava shishifãi bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akpa?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or water, it puts all its energy into growing thick stems and leafy foliage above the ground instead of storing energy below ground to swell up the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami toɔ zugba a sisi konɛ e ha nɛ bulb ɔ nɛ bli.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my tomato plants fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when heat gets too high or when soil moisture swings from very dry to very wet. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to drop the flower because it cannot form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni egbi waa kɛyaa he ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily during rainstorms when they look so thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe wa?

english: Plantains have broad, heavy leaves and shallow roots that spread near the surface rather than going deep. When heavy fruit bunches grow at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, and strong winds on soft, wet soil can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ moŋ fe ni eeeshɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Beni aduawai akuu ko ni tsii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tswaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them crawl on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ekpã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food for the growing yam under the soil. Staking lifts the vines high into the sun and off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and rot caused by wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha sweet potato ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni ekɛ ehe jɛkɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tso helai kɛ fitemɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting into little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ kɔɔpoi bibii amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by a virus spread by those insects that disrupts healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsiɔ baai kpakpai adalɛ naa lɛ nɔ

english: Why does the flower at the top of my maize plant show up before the silks appear on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ dani siliki lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The top flower, called the tassel, develops first so it can release powder-like pollen into the air. By the time the sticky silks emerge lower down on the cob, pollen is already floating around to fall on them and form maize grains.
ga: Atsɛɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ akɛ tassel. Etsɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ejie pollen ni tamɔ powda kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ be shɛ ni siliki lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni shwieɔ shi yɛ cob lɛ nɔ Pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛbɔleɔ he. koni egbee nɔ ni efee ŋmãa ŋmeii

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt and droop during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mifeee nakai lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, water leaves the plant's leaves through evaporation faster than the roots can drink water from the soil. The plant intentionally wilts to reduce its surface area exposed to heat, recovering naturally when temperature drops in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ Nu shĩɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgboi koni amɛha he ni hulutsoo baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. ni ehiɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpea or beans make my soil better for growing maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have small nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food. When the cowpea plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii Kɛ́ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is a key food crops need to grow. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or animal manure helps restore the green color and produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni dara lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil is still moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: In strong afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it from the ground. They droop temporarily to protect themselves and conserve moisture, usually standing upright again by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛkotoɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants try to climb around wooden poles instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɔ kɛbɔle tso ko he moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Climbing bean varieties naturally wrap around supports to lift their leaves higher toward the sunlight, which gives them the energy needed to produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni kwɔɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ Support base lɛ he koni ewo baai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu la lɛ shɛ enɔ. Enɛ haa anáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni aná fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads during heavy rains and excessive shade. Pruning shade trees and clearing weeds lets air and sunlight in to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny insects always gathering underneath the leaves of my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ ashishi be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Insects like aphids hide under leaves to stay safe from hot sun and rain while sucking plant sap. Checking the undersides of leaves helps you spot and treat them before they spread diseases.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aphids kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi koni amɛná shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he be mli ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona amɛ ni otsa amɛ dani amɛgbɛ hela amɛshwã.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no insects like bees around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ he fɛɛ he. koni akɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen

english: Why are my cassava roots thin and small even after growing for a full year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii waa yɛ be mli ni midu amɛ afi muu fɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, soft soil to expand. If the soil is too hard or packed tightly, the tubers cannot swell into large, thick roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Bulb lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shishifãi wuji ni mli tse.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants need water without guessing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu he miihia mi-pepper tso lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni masusu he?

english: Push your finger about one inch into the soil around the plant; if the soil feels dry at that depth or the leaves feel soft instead of firm, your pepper plants need water.
ga: Nyɛɛ onine nɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee inchi kome ni bɔle tso lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ yɛ nakai shishigbɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi loo baai lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo moŋ fe ni eeefee mlɛo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia o-pepper tso lɛ.

english: Why do seeds planted at the very start of the rainy season grow faster than those planted later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni adu mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe nɔ ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: The early rains combine with the warm soil to release trapped nutrients like nitrogen, giving newly germinated seeds a quick boost to grow deep, strong roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ejie niyenii mli nibii ni emɔ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shwereɔ oya kɛha shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni wa.

english: Why should I plant cowpea on my farmland after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. Planting them after maize naturally replenishes the soil nutrients so your next crop grows well without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is short on nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to grow green and strong, so when nutrients are low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni efee hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and thin even though the vines above ground look big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eda ni eyɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the yam plant puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending nutrients down to build large tubers in the soil.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee bulb nguahi ngɛ zugba a mi.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches and picking ripe pods early allows air and sunlight to dry out the farm and stop the rot.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei aniji koni eha hulutsoo babaoo ni okpa tsei ni ekwɛ̃ mra. Ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ekpa fitemɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves and spreading viruses. Catching them early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts helps keep leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is a sudden lack of water. Excessive heat stresses the plant and prevents the flowers from pollinating properly, causing them to fall off.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu faaa trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves on purpose when the rain stops to save water. By dropping leaves, the plant stops losing moisture through transpiration and stays alive underground until the next rainy season.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ yiŋtoo ko hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ ashi baai lɛ, ehaaa tso lɛ mli nu lɛ afite kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔne yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up in intense sunlight to hide their surface from the sun's direct heat. This natural reaction helps the plant conserve water so it does not dry out during hot days.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli koni amɛkɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. Planting them alongside maize naturally adds fertilizer to the soil, helping the maize grow better without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over easily whenever there is a strong wind or rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over when roots are too shallow or planted too close together. Planting at the correct depth and mounding soil firmly around the base of the stems (earthing up) gives roots a stronger hold in the ground.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ he ni sa ni adu shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ nɔ) lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and bigger than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and adapted to pull water, sunlight, and soil food much faster than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing nutrients away from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛhe wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need special training just to pluck cocoa pods from my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɔsemɔ krɛdɛɛ he hiaa mi koni manyɛ majie kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plucking cocoa pods requires proper technique because damaging the flower cushion where the pod grows prevents future pods from forming there. Trained harvesting preserves these cushions so your tree continues yielding fruit every season.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ajieɔ lɛ biɔ ŋaa ni sa. Nɔ ni ha ebalɛ nakai ji fɔfɔii akushin ni yɔɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ fitemɔ. Enɛ baatsi pod lɛ naa koni ekadara wɔsɛɛ. Nibii ni akpaa ni atsɔse lɛ haa nɛkɛ kushɛji nɛɛ hiɔ shi. Enɛ baaha otso lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii daa be mli.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color, usually turning from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting pods when they are fully ripe ensures the beans inside are mature enough for proper fermentation.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛshwere kwraa lɛ, ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni sa.

english: Why is it bad to leave ripe cocoa pods on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaashi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes the seeds inside to start germinating or rot, which destroys the bean quality and reduces the weight and value of your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni ehaa okpamɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa shi.

english: Why should I harvest my cocoa early in the morning before the sun gets high overhead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa mi-kookoo lɛ leebi dani hulu lɛ ateshi yɛ miyitso nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting early in the morning protects you from extreme heat exhaustion and prevents harvested pods from sitting under scorching direct sunlight, which can dry out and damage the fresh beans inside.
ga: Nikpamɔ leebi lɛ baabu ohe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ebaatsi ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ anaa koni amɛkatara hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kɔfe yibii heei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ agbi ni efite.

english: Why does it cost me more money to harvest trees that are overgrown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika babaoo kɛkpa tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ?

english: Overgrown trees make pods difficult and dangerous to reach, requiring more time, effort, and specialized labor per tree. Keeping trees properly pruned makes harvesting faster and lowers your overall labor costs.
ga: Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashɛɔ he ni ewaa ni eyɛ oshara. Enɛ biɔ be babaoo, mɔdɛŋbɔɔ, kɛ nitsumɔ krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ tso fɛɛ tso nɔ. Tso nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa baaha kpamɔ lɛ aya oya ni ebaaha nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves look burnt and dry during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves burn easily under direct, intense sunlight because young and unshaded cocoa trees cannot handle strong heat without adequate shade from larger companion plants like plantains or forest trees.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tsei bibii ni bɛ hulutsoo lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa kɛji hulutsoo ni sa kɛjɛɛɛ nanemɛi tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei amli.

english: Why shouldn't I cut down all the large shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ shade tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Large shade trees protect cocoa plants from intense sun overhead, help retain soil moisture, and shield the cocoa trees from hot winds that cause leaf loss and stress.
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni jɛɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ he.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees produce many flowers but very few pods grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects like midges for pollination. If your farm loses shade or becomes too hot and dry under direct sunlight, these beneficial insects cannot survive to help the flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ kooloi bibii akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛfeɔ pollination. Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo bɛ loo edɔ tsɔ ni egbi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ po nyɛŋ aye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black while still attached to the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ lɛ? Ani ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lolo?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that thrives in overly wet and unpruned conditions. Removing infected pods quickly stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods on neighboring trees.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli ni afolɔɔɔ tsɔi tsɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ amli.

english: How soon after harvesting must I break open my cocoa pods?
ga: Yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Mɛɛ be ehe baahia ni magbele kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: You should break open harvested cocoa pods within 3 to 5 days. Delaying too long allows mold to grow inside the pod or causes the beans to sprout, ruining the crop.
ga: Esa akɛ ogbala o-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ni okpa lɛ mli yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli. Kɛ́ okɛ be babaoo shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli loo ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ

english: When water is scarce, maize plants roll their leaves to hide their surfaces from the sun. This stops water from evaporating quickly from the plant and helps the crop survive dry spells until the next rain.
ga: Kɛ́ nu faaa lɛ, Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la akashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ ni baa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my vegetable crops need extra water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu kroko he miihia mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Check your crops early in the morning; if the leaves look dull and wilted before the sun gets high, or if the top two inches of soil feel completely dry and powdery, your plants need extra watering.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli leebi. Kɛji baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ ni egbɔjɔ dani hulu lɛ shɛ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi inchi enyɔ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Nu babaoo he miihia otsei lɛ.

english: Is it better to water my crops in the afternoon when it is hot or in the early morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning. Watering in the heat of the afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate before roots can soak it up, and hot droplets on leaves can burn the plant.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ.

english: Why should I cut cassava stems at a slanting angle when preparing them for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afolɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishi kɛji asaa he koni adu lɛ?

english: Cutting stems at a sharp angle prevents water from sitting on top of the cut stem and causing rot, while also giving a larger surface area for strong roots to grow quickly once placed in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha nu akakpɛtɛ tso ni afo lɛ he ni eha egbo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ naa he ko ni da waa koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants stop producing well if I leave the lower leaves touching the wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ kpaɔ yibii kpakpai kɛji miha baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kpe lɛ?

english: Leaves that touch wet soil easily pick up diseases from mud and splash water, while wasting energy that the plant needs to grow fruit. Cutting lower leaves off keeps the crop healthy and productive.
ga: Baai ni taa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ helai ni jɛɔ muji kɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo yibii lɛ. Kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ baai lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why does the chemical weedkiller I spray fail to work when rain falls right after I apply it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ beni mikɛshwie nɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weedkillers need a few hours to be absorbed through the leaves. If rain falls immediately, it washes the chemical off into the soil before the weed can soak it in, making the chemical useless.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ heɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi dani etsɔɔ baai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ trukaa lɛ, ebaafɔ tsofai lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ehaa tsofai lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa

english: Will chemical fertilizer lose its power if I leave it on top of dry soil without covering it?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he?

english: Yes, fertilizer left uncovered on dry ground loses its strength to the hot air and can be blown away by wind. Covering it lightly with soil keeps the nutrients trapped where roots can reach them when water is present.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baafite ehewalɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, ni ekolɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa lɛ kɛya. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ hiɔ hei ni shishifãi baanyɛ aya kɛji nu yɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my bean plants turn yellow after I apply a large amount of chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ tsofa babaoo ewo mli lɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer creates high salt levels in the soil that pull moisture out of the plant's roots instead of feeding them. This burns the roots and causes leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmei babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ baa shã shishifãi lɛ ni eha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. The plant sheds flowers to preserve its energy for basic survival instead of producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow misshapen and small instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efite ni amɛji bibii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, deep soil to push downward as they grow. Hard or rocky soil blocks the tuber, forcing it to split, bend, or stop growing long, resulting in small, distorted tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ loo tɛi ni wa tsiɔ bulb lɛ naa, ni ehaa amɛmli gbalaa, amɛkotoɔ, loo amɛkpaa dalɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo ni efiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and need shade to survive intense sunshine. During the Harmattan dry season, direct sunlight scorches the leaves, turning them yellow and dry, which is why temporary shade plants like plantains or shade trees are essential protection.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛtaoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha hebuu lɛ.

english: Can I continue planting food crops like cassava inside my farm once the cocoa trees grow tall?
ga: Ani manyɛ maya nɔ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Beni kookoo tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ

english: Once cocoa trees mature and their leafy canopy closes overhead, they block out the sunlight that food crops like cassava need to grow. Therefore, food crops should only be intercropped during the first two to three years of establishing the farm.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ eda kwraa ni baai lɛ ashishifã lɛ ŋmɛɔ eyiteŋ lɛ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ loo etɛ ni ato ŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ mli pɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce a lot of small flowers, but most of them fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed over 90% of their flowers. A flower will only turn into a pod if tiny insects like midges pollinate it, and if the tree has sufficient water and nutrients to support the growing fruit.
ga: Cacao tsei ni fa fe 90% woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Fɔfɔi feɔ pods pɛ kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ midges wo amɛhe pollin kɛ kɛji tso lɛ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black while they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. It is a natural process where the cocoa tree intentionally discards excess young pods that it cannot feed due to a lack of water, nutrients, or environmental stress.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni cacao tso lɛ tsɔɔ etsuiŋ eshwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ yɛ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, loo shihilɛ mli haomɔi ahewɔ lɛ ashwieɔ.

english: What causes a cocoa tree to yield a huge harvest one year and very few pods the next year?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tso ko woɔ yibii babaoo afi kome shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Producing a heavy harvest drains the cocoa tree of its stored energy and soil nutrients. Without proper fertilizer application and pruning, the tree requires a recovery season to rebuild its strength before bearing heavy fruit again.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa babaoo lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa bɛ lɛ, Tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani amɛwo yibii ni tsii ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I recognize black pod disease on my cocoa trees before it ruins my entire harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji black pod hela lɛ yɛ cacao tsei anɔ dani efite miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ?

english: Black pod disease begins as small brown spots on the surface of the pod during wet weather. These spots spread rapidly until the whole pod turns dark black, rotting the cocoa beans inside if the pod is not removed quickly.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. yɛ pod lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya aahu akɛ pod muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni mli kwɔ. ni ehaa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ kɛji ajieee ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect my cocoa flowers and young pods?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa mi-kokoo fɔfɔi kɛ mi-pod lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While cocoa trees need moisture, excessive rain can wash away the tiny insects that pollinate cocoa flowers. High humidity and prolonged dampness also create the perfect conditions for fungal diseases like black pod to spread.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia kookoo tsei moŋ, Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ajie kooloi bibii. ni baanyɛ aha kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ hu haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune the extra branches off my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing sunlight and air to move freely through the canopy. This reduces the dampness that causes diseases and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds and rotten pods away from the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni egboi kɛjɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and nutrients from the cocoa roots, while rotten pods left on the ground harbor fungal spores and pests that can easily crawl or splash back onto healthy trees.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ atsɔ loo aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ oya.

english: Why do cocoa trees on dark forest soil grow better than those on hard clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ koo shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ nɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Dark forest soil is rich in decomposed organic matter, which holds water well while allowing roots to spread easily. Hard clay soil restricts root growth and makes it difficult for the tree to absorb water and nutrients during dry spells.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbo. Amɛhiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni ji shikpɔŋ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa. Ni enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaaná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings die so quickly when I plant them directly in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are delicate and burn easily under full sun and heavy rains. Starting them in a shaded nursery allows them to grow strong roots and stem resilience before being exposed to harsh field conditions.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shishi. Kɛ́ aje amɛ shishi yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛshishifãi ni wa kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe dani amɛyajeɔ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wa amli.

english: Why should I pinch off the top leaves of my pepper plants when they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ amli beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Removing the main growing tip stops the plant from growing tall and thin, forcing it to grow wider with more side branches that can carry significantly more flowers and peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii titrii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akakwɛ ni efee bibioo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni esɛɛ niji babaoo yɔɔ mli. ni baanyɛ atere fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo

english: What is the best time of day for me to move my vegetable seedlings from the nursery to the main farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie aduawai dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Transplanting late in the afternoon or on a cloudy day prevents the sun from wilting the tender shoots, giving the seedling the cooler night hours to recover from root shock.
ga: Kɛ́ atsake tsei lɛ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekagbe tsei bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni tswaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do some farmers build small palm-frond shelters over their vegetable beds after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi maa tsũi bibii lɛ? Ani okɛbaawo aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni odu sɛɛ?

english: Shade shelters protect delicate seeds and young shoots from severe heat stress and prevent heavy downpours from washing away topsoil and nutrients.
ga: He ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How can I catch early signs of disease on my cocoa trees before the whole farm gets infected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana hela he okadii mra yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli hela lɛ aba?

english: Look out for abnormal leaf yellowing, small spots, or swollen stems early on; pruning and treating affected branches immediately stops the disease from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ, ŋmeii bibii, loo tsei ni efu mra. Niji ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oookpa ni otsa amɛ lɛ baaha hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to put fertilizer into the soil at the same time I bury my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be kome too mli ni afuɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Raw fertilizer placed directly next to fresh seeds can burn the tender sprouts before they form roots; it is safer to apply fertilizer after the roots have established and can safely drink up the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui heei ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ŋmeii dani amɛwo shishifãi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shishifãi lɛ etswa shi lɛ sɛɛ, ni ebaanyɛ enu niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Rolling leaves is a crop's natural defense mechanism to conserve water; reducing the leaf surface exposed to the hot sun helps the plant hold onto moisture until cool evening temperatures arrive.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ni baa shi lɛ baa shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ baashɛɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without turning into actual tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?
