english: Extreme heat, lack of soil moisture, or absence of bees for pollination causes tomato plants stress, making them drop their flowers to save energy rather than produce weak fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ Loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: Why does cassava manage to grow well in poor soils while crops like cabbage fail?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kaabɛji yeee omanye lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep, hardy root systems designed to extract water and nutrients from tough soils, whereas shallow-rooted vegetables like cabbage require rich, constantly moist topsoil to produce edible heads.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni mli wa ni afee koni ejie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ sũ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, aduawai ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ kaabɛji lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛná ŋmeii ni ayeɔ.

english: Overcrowding forces neighboring crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough food energy to develop large, healthy cobs.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha etsɔ ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides natural shade cover and moisture, acting like an umbrella to protect the crop while it establishes strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi ni wa baa.

english: Why are small green worms eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-babi corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks the growing heart of maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extracts protects the main stalk so the crop can produce full cobs.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ atsui lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ bio-insecticide loo neem tso lɛ mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ awo cob ni eyi obɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and darkness. Pruning extra branches to allow sunlight and airflow into the farm helps dry out the trees and prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ duŋ fe nine yɔɔ lɛ. Nibii krokomɛi ni afeɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Which direction should I push my cassava sticks into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ atsɔ ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should always be planted with the raised leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the plant to waste energy turning its shoots around, resulting in weak growth and smaller tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi ni awó nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ ni edaa kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa efiteɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ eshishifãi ni etsakeɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyitsei lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Why should I space out my maize seeds instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Proper spacing gives each maize plant enough room to grow thick stalks and produce large, heavy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmãa tsoi wuji ni tsii baa.

english: How can I tell if my soil is weak and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: If your crops stay small, grow slowly, or turn pale yellow despite getting enough rain, the soil is low on essential nutrients like nitrogen and needs organic compost or fertilizer to regain its strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa lɛ, amɛdaraa blɛoo, loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa po sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli koni eha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans alongside my main crop help the ground?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they naturally feed the soil, making it richer for crops like cassava or maize planted nearby.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ fɛo waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long hot spell that can dry out the ground and kill germinating seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular before putting seeds in the soil.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ dani odu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce smaller yields even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the plant food, water, and sunlight that your crops need to grow. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes straight into making your crops strong and productive.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ koni nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop tiny holes and turn into dust when stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔɔ sũ kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotoku mli?

english: This damage is caused by weevils, which multiply quickly if grain is stored with remaining moisture. Thoroughly drying your maize under the sun until the grains are very hard before storing them in airtight bags prevents insect damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii. Amɛbaafa oya kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to ni ŋmɔtɔ eshwɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulu mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafite.

english: Why do my crops wilt and stop growing so fast when the dry weather begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Water works inside a plant like air inside a tire—it creates pressure that keeps the leaves up and nutrients moving. When the soil runs out of water, the plant loses its internal pressure, stops growing, and will quickly dry up and die if water is not restored.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ tai amli lɛ. Enɛ haa nɔnyɛɛ baa ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni niyenii mli nibii lɛ hu tsiɔ amɛhe. Beni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ mligbɛ nɔnyɛɛ lɛ baaje edɛŋ. ekpaa shweremɔ Amɛbaagbi oya ni amɛbaagboi kɛji amɛnáaa nu.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants keep them healthy?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni pepper tsei lɛ ashishi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass creates a protective cover that traps moisture in the ground. It prevents the strong sun from stealing soil water, so your crops always have enough water pressure to stay alive and green.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaju nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my young seedlings die so quickly when planted in open sunlight without any tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small roots and cannot drink water fast enough to replace what strong sunlight bakes out of their leaves. Without shade to slow down water loss, the seedlings drain out completely and dry up.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛwo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ he nyɔmɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ ni baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baaho kwraa ni amɛbaagbi.

english: Why is it better to treat worms on my farm when I first spot tiny ones instead of waiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ matsa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmeii bibii kpeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ?

english: Young insects are weak and easy to kill before they cause damage. If you wait until you see big worms or large swarms, their numbers increase rapidly, and they can eat the entire crop to death within days.
ga: Kplukai bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgbeɔ amɛ oya dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite nii. Kɛ omɛ kɛyashi ona ŋmei agbo loo ŋmei agbo Amɛyibɔ ​​baaya hiɛ oya. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii muu fɛɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: What causes my tomato stems to rot and collapse suddenly from the bottom upward?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi trukaa kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi?

english: This is usually caused by a soil sickness or mold that creeps up the stem and clogs the veins carrying water. Once the channels are blocked from the base up, water stops reaching the top and the entire plant dies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ hela loo ŋmei ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsiɔ lá fãji ni hiɛ nu lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsĩ gbɛ lɛ naa kɛjɛ shishigbɛ kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ Nu lɛ kpaɔ ŋwɛi shɛɛmɔ ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gboɔ.

english: Why do disease outbreaks spread so much faster across my farm during warm, humid periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai ni baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Warm, damp weather creates the perfect condition for crop diseases to multiply and rise rapidly. When heat and moisture stay high, fungal spores spread quickly from leaf to leaf, destroying plants if not controlled early.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa tsei ahe helai babaoo ni amɛyaa hiɛ oya. Kɛji latsaa kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, Fungal spores lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ baa nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ. Efiteɔ tsei kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why should I remove the extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: If you allow too many large shoots to grow together, they steal all the water and soil food from the main mother plant. Removing extra shoots leaves only small ones for next season and keeps the main stem strong.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii wuji babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ, Ejuɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi tsei lɛ fɛɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii bibii pɛ baashwɛ. kɛha be ni baa lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli waa

english: Why do extension officers advise us to pluck off some fruits if a vegetable plant produces too many small ones at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfo aduawai komɛi kɛji akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tso ko woɔ aduawai bibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: A plant has a limited supply of food and water to share. If it tries to feed too many small fruits, none of them will grow properly and the plant gets stressed; picking a few allows the remaining fruits to grow big and healthy.
ga: Tsei bɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni amɛkɛbaajara. Kɛji ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha aduawai bibii lɛ niyenii fe nine lɛ, aduawai lɛ eko kwraa edaŋ jogbaŋŋ ni eha tso lɛ haoɔ. Kɛ́ otsi fioo pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I harvest my okra pods when they are still small rather than waiting for them to grow very large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa okra ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii moŋ fe ni mamɛ ni amɛdara waa lɛ?

english: Okra pods are soft and tender when small, which is what buyers want. If you leave them to grow too big, the water leaves the pod, making it hard and woody, and the plant stops producing new flowers.
ga: Okra ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ amɛji bibii, ni no ji nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ. Kɛji oha efee agbo tsɔ Nu baaje pod lɛ mli. Ha efee nɔ ni wa ni efee tso. ni tso lɛ baakpa fɔfɔii heei womɔ.

english: What happens if I leave cassava in the ground too long past its mature harvest time?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi mi-cassava lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni miho kpamɔɔ be lɛ he?

english: As cassava gets too old, the plant starts drawing food back out of the tubers. The roots lose their soft starch, become tough and fibrous like wood, and eventually rot in the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei egbɔ tsɔ Tso lɛ baabɔi niyenii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baafite amɛ starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Ewa ni eyɛ tsɔi tamɔ tso ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains waterlog the soil and prevent the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for extended periods. Soggy ground prevents oxygen from reaching the roots and creates ideal conditions for soil-borne fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sun because their leaves burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains shields them from hot sunlight until their roots and branches mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he buɔ mɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ daraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and growing tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiida kɛmiibɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking plant sap from the underside of leaves, or by viral infections spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso mli nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: When seeds are planted too closely, individual plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving less energy to form large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso fɛɛ tso baawuu koni ená hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛfeɔ dumɔwui wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ faaa.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing underground tubers. Staking lifts the foliage into the light and keeps leaves away from wet soil pests.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ mli ni ehaa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Should I apply chemical fertilizer at the exact same time I plant seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli yɛ be kome too mli ni mikɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: It is usually better to wait until seedlings sprout and develop roots, or place fertilizer slightly away from the seed. Concentrated fertilizer directly touching a seed can burn the tender plant sprouts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ. Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he fioo kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when heat becomes too intense or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly, which stresses the plant and stops normal pollination.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsake waa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ekpaa pollination ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from heat and lack of water during dry months?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Water-stressed crops will roll or curl their leaves inward during the hottest part of the day, take on a dull or grayish color, and stop growing new shoots.
ga: Tsei ni nu haa amɛhe feɔ shoo lɛ baafolɔ loo amɛbaafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ebafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpaa ŋmeii heei adalɛ

english: What can I do with the dry plant leaves and farm waste left on my field after harvest?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Farm waste like dry leaves, husk, and stalks can be spread on top of the soil as mulch. Instead of throwing it away, this material covers the ground, traps moisture, and breaks down into natural food for your crops.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi tamɔ baai ni egbi, ŋmãa ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii atsu nii akɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ ashwie lɛ Nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa mli, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha onibii.

english: I don't have much money for chemical fertilizers; can I use leftover crop debris to help my farm?
ga: Mibɛ shika babaoo kɛha tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, using leftover plant debris costs nothing and acts as organic mulch. It enriches the soil as it decays, reducing the need for expensive chemical inputs while helping your crops grow strong.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei amli nibii ni efite lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he ehiaaa nɔ ko ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii beni efiteɔ lɛ. Ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa atsu nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Can every part of my harvested plant be reused on the farm for the next season?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ aku sɛɛ akɛ tsei ni mikpa lɛ fãi fɛɛ aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Almost every part of a harvested plant, including leaves, stalks, and husks, can be returned to the field. Using them as mulch feeds the soil and helps future crops grow better.
ga: Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tso ni akpa lɛ fã fɛɛ fã, ni baai, eshishifãi kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji fata he lɛ, abaanyɛ aku sɛɛ aya ŋmɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ tsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I cover the soil around them with dry plant materials?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ sũ wo amɛhe lɛ? Kɛ tso nibii ni egbi?

english: Covering the soil with plant materials acts like a protective blanket. It shades the roots from the scorching sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and keeps the soil cool so crops can feed continuously.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ tsei ahe nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii be fɛɛ be.

english: How does putting plant debris around my crops protect them during the dry season?
ga: Tsei amli jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Plant debris prevents the sun from drying out the earth. It creates a sponge-like layer that holds water in the soil longer, allowing crops to stay hydrated during dry spells.
ga: Tsei amli jwɛi yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Efeɔ nɔ ko ni tamɔ sponji ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Will my crops grow better if I clear all plant waste and leave the farm soil completely bare?
ga: Ani midumɔ nii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mijie tsei amli jwɛi fɛɛ ni mishi ŋmɔ lɛ mli sũ lɛ efolo kwraa?

english: No, bare soil dries out very fast under the sun and loses its nutrients when it rains. Leaving or spreading plant waste protects the soil surface and improves plant growth.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fiteɔ. Tsei amli jwɛi ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ shi loo agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I use leftover oil palm waste around my food crops?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ ŋmei fɔ ni eshwɛ ni ebɔle he lɛ atsu nii. Ani manyɛ madu miniyenii?

english: Yes, oil palm husks and empty fruit bunches are great for crop farming. When placed around your plants, they form a thick layer of mulch that retains soil moisture and gradually decays into nutrient-rich organic matter.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, mu tso mli ŋmeii kɛ aduawai akui ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni fiofio lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Is it safe to leave palm tree debris close to my vegetable roots, or will it damage them?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mashi ŋmei tso mli nibii ni efite lɛ yɛ mi-vegetables shishifãi lɛ ahe? Aloo ebaafite amɛ?

english: It is safe and beneficial as long as the palm debris is free from diseases. It stays on top of the soil, preventing weeds from growing and keeping the soil moist around vegetable roots.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he, be fɛɛ be ni hela bɛ tsei ni etse lɛ amli lɛ. Ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ aduawai shishifãi ahe.

english: What should I do with leftover palm fruit or crops that my family cannot finish eating?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ ŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni miweku lɛ nyɛŋ aye lɛ?

english: Leftover harvest can be shared with community food programs or preserved, while the unedible parts can be taken back to the farm to use as mulch to feed your soil for future planting.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmaa ni eshwɛ lɛ aha akutso lɛ mli niyenii he gbɛjianɔtoi loo akɛto he. yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ akɛ fãi ni ayeee lɛ aku sɛɛ aya ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni akɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does adding organic matter back into the ground change the way crop roots absorb water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ?

english: As plant leftovers decompose in the soil, they create rich organic matter that improves soil structure. This helps the soil hold on to rainwater much longer, making it easier for roots to absorb moisture.
ga: Kɛ tsei amli ŋmeii fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ nu.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Keeping mature shade trees protects young cocoa from sun damage, reduces water loss, and maintains the soil moisture needed for their survival.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ okɛ hɔɔŋ ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la lɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni laajeɔ lɛ shi ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips downwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn green again and produce strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni ewo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When cassava is planted too close, the plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak stalks and very small root tubers instead of a heavy harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi ayitsei bibii waa baa yɛ ŋmaa babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto tall stakes instead of letting them spread across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch more sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture food to build big tubers. It also keeps leaves away from wet ground where diseases and rot can easily spread.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa baai lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai kɛ fitemɔ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my land make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, this extra nitrogen stays in the soil and feeds the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni okpaa Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the central funnel of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves. Applying recommended treatments directly into the plant's funnel early on stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ baawo tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ mra. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of specific soil minerals. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo mineral pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl upwards and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by viral infections spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, or by severe water stress. Controlling insects early and watering regularly keeps the plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa loo nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ tomato mli. Kooloi ni yeɔ amɛhe mra Kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds early instead of waiting until my crop grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e he hia nɛ ma mɛ kɛ ya si benɛ ye ngmɔ ní ɔmɛ maa da.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, light, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Removing weeds during the first few weeks allows your crops to establish strong root systems without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli lɛ shishi.

english: Covering the soil with dry material, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating in the heat and keeps the root area cool. It also prevents weeds from sprouting and slowly enriches the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la kɛji akɛ edɔ. kɛ shishifã lɛ he ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fiofio.

english: Is it safe for me to plant crops on a piece of land where rubbish was cleared away?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he ni ashwieɔ sũ lɛ yɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, but you must remove non-biodegradable waste like plastics, metals, and glass first. Decomposed food scraps and organic waste can actually enrich the soil, but toxic trash can harm your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi ni nyɛɛɛ afite tamɔ plastic, dade, kɛ glase ashwie klɛŋklɛŋ. Niyenii ni egboi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo. Shi jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei baanyɛ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: How can I get a harvest big enough to feed my family and still have extra left to sell for my children's school fees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahã miweku lɛ niyenii, ni maná nɔ ni eshwɛ lolo ni mikɛwo mibii lɛ askulyaa he nyɔmɔ?

english: You can achieve a bigger yield by using certified high-yielding seeds, giving your crops proper spacing so they do not compete for nutrients, and applying the right fertilizer at the right stage of growth.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná yibii babaoo kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni awo he odaseyeli akɛ oootsu nii lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ni akɛ amɛ baabɔ he bɔ ni sa koni amɛkatswa niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ amli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to save water and protect itself from hot weather. The root in the ground is still alive, and fresh leaves will grow back once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why are my vegetables growing very tall and thin without producing any fruits under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii ko yɛ tsei wuji lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make the food required for producing fruits. Under heavy shade, plants stretch upward searching for light instead of spending energy on making fruits.
ga: Hulu la he miihia tsei tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛwo aduawai. yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Tsei baajie amɛhe kpo koni amɛtao la moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee aduawai.

english: How do I know if my soil is fertile enough to support crops without paying for expensive soil tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ shika ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni miwooo shikpɔŋ lɛ he kaa ni jara wa lɛ he nyɔmɔ?

english: Fertile soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well after rain, crumbles easily in your hand, and contains earthworms. If natural weeds grow thick and dark green on it, the soil is likely good.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ yɛ diŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ Efoɔ mlɛo yɛ oniji amli Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Kɛji adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ Etsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi.

english: Can I plant beans together with my maize in the same field, or will they destroy each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaafite amɛhe?

english: Planting beans with maize is actually beneficial. Beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa.

english: Will adding double the amount of fertilizer make my crops mature twice as fast?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ shii enyɔ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer can burn the roots and kill your plants. Crops can only absorb a specific amount of nutrients, so applying the recommended dosage gives the best result.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ. Tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Why are insects still destroying my crops after I cleared all the weeds from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ lolo beni mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds are not the only place farm pests live. Many insects travel by air from neighboring fields or nearby bushes to feed on crops, so clearing weeds reduces pests but does not stop them entirely.
ga: Jeee jwɛi pɛ ji he ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ. Kplukai babaoo fãa gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ loo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ koni amɛyaye ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai aba shi shi ekpaŋ amɛ kwraa.

english: If I save seeds from my best harvest this year to plant next season, will they produce the same big yield?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ afi nɛɛ kpamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ to ni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Ani dumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ?

english: Not always. Many improved or hybrid seeds lose their high yield strength and pest resistance in the second generation, so buying fresh certified seed gives a much more reliable harvest.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Dumɔwui babaoo ni atsake amɛ loo ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibiiwoo hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha anyɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ kpamɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I tell if my pepper plants are getting too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-pepper tso lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo eshɛɛɛ nu he?

english: If pepper plants lack water, their leaves wilt and droop during hot hours. If they get too much water, their leaves turn pale yellow and root rot sets in because the roots cannot get air.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ pepper tso lɛ he lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ mli ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to make green leaves and build strength. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores the green color and helps the maize grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why is my farm producing fewer tubers every year even though I use the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil every season drains specific nutrients without giving the land time to recover. Rotating your crops—like planting groundnuts or beans after maize—puts vital nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni ooodu yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know which side of a cassava stem cutting should face up when I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ madu mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the tiny raised buds where old leaves used to grow; these buds must point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoots will struggle to grow up and your harvest will be very small.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. ni kwɛ̃ yɛ he ni baai momo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ bɛŋkɛ Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ, Ewa akɛ eeekwɛ̃ ni ŋmaa lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers produce big bunches while others from the same farm grow weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni jɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Suckers with narrow, blade-like leaves (called sword suckers) have strong roots and produce healthy plantain bunches. Suckers with broad leaves early on (called maiden suckers) have weaker root connection to the mother plant and yield smaller bunches.
ga: Tsofɔi ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ ŋmei. (ni atsɛɔ lɛ klante ŋmeii) lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ plantain ŋmeii ni wa. Tsoi ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ Tsoi bibii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ maiden shoots) lɛ shishifãi fioo pɛ kɛ tso nyɛ lɛ kpãa gbee ni amɛfeɔ kui bibii.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight, which burns their leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving large shade trees or planting plantains beside them shields the tender cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Enɛ baa shã baai lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebuɔ cacao tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to send energy down to the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they could rot or catch diseases, allowing the plant to make bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba shi kɛya ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo hela aba amɛnɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaves brown dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center of young maize plants to feed. Spragging early with approved biological control like neem seed extract or recommended pesticides destroys the pest before it ruins the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli koni amɛye nii. mra ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ tamɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi. Ekpãtãa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahiɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off instead of turning into green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as very hot daytime temperatures, prolonged dryness, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly damp and balanced in nutrients keeps the flowers attached so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why did my seeds dry up and die even though I planted right after the first rain fell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: The very first rainy day of the year is often followed by a week or two of dry, scorching heat before the real rainy season starts. Planting during this false start causes seeds to germinate and then dry out before their roots reach underground water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, otsi kome loo enyɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Amale dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi dani shishifãi lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look thin and stunted even when rainfall is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔná nugbɔ kpakpa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your crops full access to the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: I keep hearing people in Kwaebibirem talk about Benson 8 oil palm, but why is this variety better for my farm than the wild palms?
ga: Miyaa nɔ minuɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ Gwebirem lɛ awieɔ Benson 8 mu tso lɛ he, shi mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ tso nɛɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ fe koo mli tso lɛ?

english: Benson 8 is a high-yielding hybrid oil palm developed by research institutions like OPRI in Kade. Unlike wild oil palms that take many years to bear small bunches with thick shells, Benson 8 grows faster, produces larger bunches, and yields far more oil with thinner shells.
ga: Benson 8 ji tso ni akɛwoɔ mu mli ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Nibii amlitaomɔ hei tamɔ OPRI ni yɔɔ Kade lɛ ji mɛi ni fee, ni esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ koo mli mu tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe. Kɛ ŋmei ni mli wa lɛ, Benson 8 lɛ daa oya. Ha yibiiwoo ni da ni ekɛ mu babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmei ni mli tseee lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the dry season when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn and lose water faster than their roots can absorb it. They need temporary shade crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower fronds of my young oil palm trees turning yellow and drooping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on oil palms usually indicate a lack of key nutrients like potassium or nitrogen in the soil, or stress from dry weather. Pruning old dead fronds and applying balanced fertilizer helps the tree focus its energy on growing healthy green leaves and fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ mu tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli baa lɛ Baai ni egboi lɛ ni afolɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai eŋɔli ni miida kɛ aduawai akui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily whenever a strong wind blows through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots, so their roots stay close to the surface. When a heavy bunch of plantains grows at the top, the plant becomes heavy, making it easy for winds to uproot it unless you support the stem with a strong wooden prop.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni plantains babaoo yɔɔ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa ni efo shishifãi lɛ. Ja okɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my sweet orange trees dropping small green fruits before they even get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Dani ebaashɛ po?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruit when they suffer from sudden changes in water supply, poor soil nutrients, or attacks from pests like fruit flies. Keeping the soil moist during dry spells and managing weeds helps the tree hold onto its fruit until harvest.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baafite amɛyibii bibii lɛ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ nu jɛɛhei ni tsakeɔ trukaa lɛ ahewɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni baatutua lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ ahi eyibii lɛ amli kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow straight out of the main trunk of the tree instead of on the thin branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ niji bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower directly on mature wood and thick trunks—a behavior called cauliflory. This structure allows the tree to support the heavy weight of full-grown cocoa pods without breaking fragile young twigs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei fɔɔ tsei ni eda kɛ tsei akutsei ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ji subaŋ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ kɔlifloa. Nɛkɛ gbɛjianɔtoo nɛɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ amli tsiimɔ lɛ mli ni ekuuu tsei niji bibii ni waaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing yellow patchy patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellow patterns are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to keep your crop healthy and maintain high yields.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ he mfoniri. Eji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ ni anáa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my plot is good enough for growing high-yielding crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, feels crumbly, and holds moisture well without staying flooded. If soil is very sandy, pale, or hard like rock, mixing in organic manure or compost improves its ability to feed your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ, enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ji ŋã, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi ni wa lɛ, Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ futu mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to plant maize together with cassava on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works very well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the space after the maize is cleared.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa dumɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. This is because corn grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look thin and pale even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Even with good rain, weeds will steal the food out of the soil before your crop roots can reach it, causing your plants to become weak.
ga: Weeds compete fiercely with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Weeds will take food out of the soil before the plant's roots can get to it. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: When maize leaves turn yellow, it usually means the crop is starving for nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged for roots to breathe. Nitrogen is the primary food crops need to stay green and manufacture their own food.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Nitrogen ji niyenii tso titri ko ni ehe hiaa ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants start curling up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in hot weather is a defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves tightly to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which stops precious water from evaporating out of the plant too quickly.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ amɛhiɛ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haaa nu ni jara wa lɛ ajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them in hard or flat soil. Planting cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like an umbrella for the ground. It keeps the blazing sun from drying out the earth, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and damp air they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam plants store energy in their leaves from sunlight to grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the hot ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant capture maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ toɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni edɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and weak when I put many seeds into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely together, the growing plants fight each other for soil nutrients, moisture, and sunlight. Giving each plant its own space allows roots to spread out and grow strong.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, moisture, and sunlight directly from your main crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get to consume all the nutrients in the soil without competition.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as very high temperatures or sudden soil dryness. The plant drops its flowers to save its own life until conditions get better.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛhere amɛhe yiwala kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small ragged holes keep appearing in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ amɛhe kpo yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize are typically caused by caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, eating their way through the tender leaves inside the funnel of the plant. Spotting this early helps treat the crop before the main growing tip is destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akai enɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala dani akpata ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How do I know if the fertilizer I am buying will ruin my farm land over time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ lɛ baafite nibii ni midu lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Fertilizers that protect the land work by feeding the crop without leaving behind harsh chemicals or damaging the natural soil life. Safe, balanced fertilizers keep your soil rich so it can produce good yields season after season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ tsei ni amɛhaa amɛ niyenii ni amɛshiuuu tsofai ni mli wa loo amɛfiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli wala lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Can using the wrong chemical inputs actually destroy my soil's ability to grow crops?
ga: Ani tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite nyɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛduɔ nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, certain harsh fertilizers can make your soil too acidic or strip away natural nutrients over time. Using fertilizers designed to be gentle on the land prevents long-term damage and keeps your field fertile.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni mli wa baanyɛ aha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee acid tsɔ loo eha adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee koni ekɛfee blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite shikpɔŋ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ, ni ebaaha oyale lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Are there specific fertilizers that help my crops grow strong without spoiling the soil for next year?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ ni baaye abua mitsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, land-friendly fertilizers supply essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus without leaving harmful residues, ensuring your soil stays healthy for future planting seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. ni eshiuuu nɔ ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ bei.

english: How can I help my exhausted farm land recover so my crops can flourish again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: You can restore tired soil by applying fertilizers that build up soil health, adding organic compost, and avoiding harsh inputs that strip away the land's natural richness.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baafata he lɛ nɔ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni jieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: What makes my maize crop grow fast and yield bigger cobs?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji?

english: Maize needs proper feeding early in its life. Applying safe fertilizers at the right growth stage, along with good weed control and moisture, helps maize plants flourish and grow large, full cobs.
ga: Niyenii ni sa he miihia ŋmã kɛjɛ egbekɛbiiashi tɔ̃ɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli kɛfata jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛ hulutsoo kpakpa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell if my maize plants are getting the right nourishment from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ miiná niyenii ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Healthy maize plants have deep green leaves, sturdy stalks, and grow evenly across the field. Yellowing leaves or thin stems usually mean the crop is lacking key nutrients from the soil.
ga: Abɛi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. tso lɛ mli wa ni edaa pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo tsei bibii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What is the best way to care for my maize crop during its early growing stage?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ makwɛ mi-kooloi lɛ anɔ yɛ shishijee mli?

english: During the first few weeks, maize needs protection from weeds and an early boost of soil-friendly fertilizer so it can build strong roots and absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehe miihia ni abu Abɛi he kɛjɛ jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe mra. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ efee shishifãi ni wa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops look weak even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If crops do not respond, the fertilizer might be the wrong type, applied at the wrong time, or the soil may be damaged. Using gentle, land-friendly fertilizers that match your soil's needs helps the crop actually absorb the food.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ haaa hetoo lɛ Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa awo mli, akɛwo mli yɛ be ni ejaaa mli, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpãaa gbee ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiamɔ nii kpãa gbee lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I try new farming tools and inputs instead of sticking to traditional methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka nibii heei kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ aka? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ehe akpɛtɛ blema gbɛi lɛ ahe lɛ

english: New agricultural technologies and inputs are specifically developed to solve common farming problems, helping you get bigger harvests while protecting your land better than old practices.
ga: Afee okwaayeli he ŋaalee heei kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni akɛtsu okwaayeli mli naagbai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe nii. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa nitsumɔ babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ fe blema nifeemɔi.

english: Is it safe for me to start using new crop technologies as soon as they arrive in my community?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii heei kɛ nitsumɔ kɛji ebashɛ mi akutso lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Yes, adopting proven new technologies early allows you to improve your yields and protect your soil health right away, giving your farm a strong advantage before problems set in.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔne hee ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Ehaa onáa yibiiwoo babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni obuɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he. Enɛ haa oŋmɔ lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ kpele dani naagbai baa.

english: Yam vines need to catch maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases and pests can easily destroy them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛha niyenii aha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai kɛ kooloi ni baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ oya lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil food, or the soil has too much water which is suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts on my land will make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts capture nitrogen directly from the air and store it in their roots and soil, acting like a natural fertilizer that feeds crops planted after them.
ga: Peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ni adu yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the plant lacks enough water during flowering, or when there is not enough food in the soil to support fruit growth.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. When plants lack sufficient water during flowering or when the soil does not have enough nutrients to support the growth of fruit.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgbi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. The plant wilts to protect itself, but usually recovers when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei gboɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants give very small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving no single plant with enough energy to make big cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long during rainy seasons, creating damp conditions where harmful soil fungi can easily attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. This creates moisture in which harmful soil fungi can easily attack the tubers.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Extra suckers steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Removing them leaves only the strongest shoots, helping the main tree produce larger and heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashwɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my young rice plants turn yellow a few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young rice plants usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or improper water levels. Applying nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right time helps restore their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does rice require so much standing water on the field compared to maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice plants thrive in wet conditions because flooding controls weeds naturally and keeps the soil soft, allowing the plant's shallow root system to easily absorb nutrients.
ga: Omɔ tsei yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli ejaakɛ nu afua lɛ kudɔɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and thin even though I weed my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: While clearing weeds removes crop competition, plants still need proper soil nutrients to grow tall. Short, thin stalks mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, which can be restored using organic manure or chemical fertilizers.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ, shi shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa he miihia Tsei lolo koni amɛdara. Tsoi kukuji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts on a plot where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔji ni akpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring fertility for future crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my crop leaves to curl up tightly during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Leaves curl during extreme heat as a survival mechanism to reduce sunlight exposure and minimize water loss through evaporation, protecting the plant until temperatures drop.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi oyitsɔi ni ebɔle ehe yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni hulu la ni baa shi lɛ aba shi, ni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Buu tsei ahe kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops wither and die if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry heat spell before regular rains start. Planting too early leaves young seeds without enough moisture once the initial rainwater dries up in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa ni mli egbi sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui bibii lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ akaná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa beni shishijee nugbɔ nu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I keep a specific distance between my cassava plants instead of planting them close together to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When planted too close, cassava plants compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛ adu Yucca tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ bulbs agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant stems turn black and rot when water stands around them for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu ta amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Excess standing water blocks oxygen from reaching the plant roots and creates ideal conditions for soil-borne fungi, causing root rot that kills the stem.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tsei shishifãi ahe. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ.

english: How can I tell if small holes in my crop leaves are caused by insects or a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ bu lɛ ji bibioo? yɛ mitso lɛ baai ni kooloi loo tsei ahe helai kɛbaa lɛ anɔ

english: Physical holes with clean or chewed edges are caused by insects eating the leaf. Disease usually causes brown spots, yellowing, or rotting patches on the leaf without visible bite marks.
ga: Kplukai ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ bu ni amɛhe tse loo amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni anaaa nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english: Why do my harvested grains like rice and maize spoil and get insects quickly inside my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa ni akpa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fiteɔ oya ni kooloi bibii boteɔ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Grains spoil in storage if they are not dried sufficiently before storing. High moisture content inside the grain creates a warm, damp environment that attracts pests and encourages mold growth.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ agbiko amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛtoɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ, ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa.

english: Why did the crop seed variety I bought fail to grow properly on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred for specific soil types, temperatures, and rainfall levels. If a variety is not suited to your local environment or current weather patterns, it will struggle to yield well even if it worked on a different farm.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi kɛha shikpɔŋ henɔi pɔtɛɛ, dɔlɛ, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ esaaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ, tso lɛ baaná naagbai ni ekɛbaawo yibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔji krokomɛi amli po.

english: How do I know if a new seed variety will adapt well to my local region before I buy it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei lɛ baatsake amɛhe jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ dani mahe amɛ?

english: You can check with local extension officers or test a small patch of land first, as seed varieties are tailored to specific ecological zones, soil types, and rainfall expectations.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ohegbɛ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ akwɛ loo oka he bibioo ko okwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ, ejaakɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ kɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kpãa gbee, shikpɔŋ henɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni baa lɛ he akɔntaabuu.

english: Why does the rain in my area seem to be changing its usual pattern compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ etsake bɔ ni eyɔɔ daa lɛ kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he lɛ?

english: Changing climate patterns are altering traditional weather cycles, causing rainy seasons in many regions to start earlier, later, or become shorter and less predictable than in the past.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi miitsake blema kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ kpokpai babaoo anɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi mra, sɛɛ mli, loo efeɔ kuku ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ nɔ ni baaba fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: How does planting my crops at the wrong time of the rainy season affect their growth?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be ni ejaaa mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he?

english: Planting too early can cause seeds to dry up in hot soil during dry spells, while planting too late means the crops will run out of water before they finish growing and producing food.
ga: Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔ ni aduɔ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu baaho yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani amɛgbe dumɔ ni amɛwo niyenii lɛ naa.

english: Why do agricultural experts advise planting in a specific month like March?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nilelɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu yɛ nyɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko tamɔ March mli lɛ?

english: March often marks the arrival of steady rains in certain regions, providing the necessary soil moisture for seeds to germinate and build strong root systems without dying of drought.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, March ji be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ kpokpai komɛi anɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Should I adjust my planting schedule if the rains start earlier or later than traditional months?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsake midumɔ be lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ je shishi mra loo sɛɛ mli fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Yes, you should adapt your planting schedule based on when the rains actually begin in a given year rather than relying strictly on fixed traditional dates.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ otsake be ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ nakai afi lɛ mli lɛ naa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaye kusum gbi lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ.

english: How can information from the Meteorological Services help me avoid crop failure?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ saji ni jɛ Kɔɔyɔŋ He Saji Ahe Nitsumɔhe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi koni mikakpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Meteorological Services monitor atmospheric conditions to forecast when rains will start and stop, helping you time your land preparation and planting for maximum water availability.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he nitsumɔhe lɛ kwɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli shihilɛ nɔ koni amɛtsɔɔ be ni nugbɔ baaje shishi kɛ be ni ebaakpa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otoɔ be he gbɛjianɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛ tsei ni aduɔ lɛ mli koni nu babaoo aba.

english: Who can I talk to in my area to get accurate weather forecasts before I start planting?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ mikɛ lɛ awie yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ koni maná kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji ni ja dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: You can consult local Agricultural Extension Officers, as they receive updated seasonal forecasts from Meteorological Services and translate that data into practical farming advice.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyabi okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛnáa be mli nibii ahe saji heei kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he nitsumɔhe lɛ. ni atsɔɔ nakai saji lɛ ashishi awo okwaayeli he ŋaawoo ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii mli.

english: Why can a crop variety perform very well in one part of the country but fail in my specific town?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ko baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ fã ko mli shi efeee nɔ ko yɛ mimaŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different towns and regions have distinct microclimates, rainfall amounts, and soil characteristics, meaning a crop variety that flourishes in one area may lack the specific conditions it needs in another.
ga: Maji kɛ kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi bibii, nugbɔshiimɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ sui srɔtoi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ aná shihilɛ pɔtɛɛ ni amɛtaoɔ yɛ he kroko lɛ.

english: What happens to my seeds if a dry spell occurs immediately after I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛgbi?

english: Newly planted seeds need consistent water to sprout; if a dry spell occurs right after planting, the seeds may dry up in the soil or produce weak seedlings that wither quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ biɔ nu be fɛɛ be dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ba yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui baanyɛ agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo eha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi oya.

english: Pruning removes weak or overcrowded branches so the tree doesn't waste energy on them. This allows nutrients to go straight into growing healthy cocoa pods and helps the farm stay productive for many more years.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni egbɔjɔ fe nine lɛ. koni tsei akafite hewalɛ Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ boteɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii babaoo.

english: Will trimming my cocoa tree branches hurt the tree or cause it to die?
ga: Ani kookoo tso ni afoɔ lɛ baafite tso lɛ loo ebaagbe lɛ?

english: Proper trimming does not harm the tree. Instead, it opens up the canopy to let in sunlight and fresh air, which prevents diseases from building up and actually prolongs the life of the tree.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeee tso lɛ awui. Mohu ɔ, a bliɔ gbogbo ɔ konɛ pu la kɛ kɔɔhiɔ kpakpa nɛ sɛ mi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akafee, ni ehaa tso lɛ wala sɛɛ tsɛɔ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees have too many branches and need to be pruned?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo tso ko yɛ niji babaoo ni ehe miihia ni afolɔ?

english: When the tree tops become so thick that sunlight cannot reach the ground or lower trunk, and when air cannot move freely through the farm, it is time to prune excess branches.
