ga: Be mli ni tso lɛ yiteŋ etse aahu akɛ hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ loo shishigbɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. ni be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya Be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to let my cocoa trees grow as tall and wild as they want?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nɔ fɔŋ akɛ maha mi-cacao tsei lɛ adara ni amɛfee koo mli bɔ ni amɛsumɔɔ lɛ?

english: Trees that grow too tall spend all their food on wood and leaves instead of fruit. Wild growth also blocks light from lower parts of the tree where pods grow and makes harvesting very difficult.
ga: Tsei ni shwereɔ tsɔ lɛ baaye amɛ niyenii fɛɛ yɛ tsei kɛ baai anɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Adebɔɔ mli dalɛ hu tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ daa lɛ naa. ni ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa waa

english: How does following the advice of cocoa extension officers help me make more profit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋaawoi ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ kookoo nɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ ni oooye nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni oná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo?

english: Extension officers share practical techniques on pruning, pest control, and farm maintenance that boost your crop yields and prevent lost harvests, leading to higher sales and profit.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ gbaa ŋaai ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ni kɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmɔmɔ he. tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni onibii ni oduɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaatsi yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ naa. Ekɛ jarayeli kɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni yaa hiɛ baa.

english: What is the main benefit of managing my farm using modern agricultural methods?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi titrii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi tsuɔ nii lɛ he?

english: Modern practices ensure your trees get the right care at the right time, preventing early farm breakdown and keeping production high season after season.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nifeemɔi haa otsei lɛ náa kwɛmɔ ni sa yɛ be ni sa mli. Tsi oŋmɔ lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ mra. ni ekwɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ babaoo nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do some cocoa farms stop bearing fruit early while others last for decades?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi kpaɔ aduawai oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hiɔ shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ?

english: Farms that are left unmanaged lose their vigor quickly due to overcrowded branches and disease, whereas farms that receive regular pruning and proper management stay healthy and continue yielding for generations.
ga: Okwaafoi ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli oya yɛ tsei niji ni eyi obɔ kɛ helai ahewɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔji ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaya nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kɛjɛ yinɔ kome mli kɛya yinɔ kroko mli.

english: What causes cocoa pods to grow bigger and healthier on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa pods grow larger when the tree gets direct sunlight, good airflow, and when energy is not diverted to unnecessary branches or heavy shade.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ daraa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ. Ni beni akɛ hewalɛ eyaaa tsei niji ni he ehiaaa loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: How does removing dead or unnecessary branches help my crop produce more yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Removing useless branches frees up water and soil nutrients so the tree can concentrate all its strength on producing more flower buds and pods.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔii babaoo ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I ensure my cocoa farm stays productive for many years into the future?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii babaoo ni baa lɛ?

english: Consistently applying proper care like routine branch pruning and following expert farming advice protects the trees from wearing out quickly, making the farm last longer.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ daa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ. Ni okwaayeli he ŋaawoi ni he esa waa lɛ ni oooye nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu otsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite oya. ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: If I see a few cassava plants with yellowing leaves on my farm, does it mean my whole crop will be ruined?
ga: Kɛji mina ŋmei tsei fioo komɛi ni baai yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ baafite?

english: Not necessarily. Just like with human sickness, seeing a few diseased plants does not mean your whole farm is lost. Usually, only a small percentage of infected plants go on to develop severe damage or die, provided you remove the sick stems early to protect the healthy ones.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Nakai nɔŋŋ eji yɛ adesai ahelai ahe. Kɛ́ ona tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, no etsɔɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ etee. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ateŋ oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ baafite waa loo amɛbaagboi. Kɛji ojie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ mra, Koni obu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe

english: Why do Fall Armyworms attack my maize farm so quickly after the shoots come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ oya beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fall Armyworms prefer young, tender maize plants because the leaves are soft and rich in moisture. Adult moths lay their eggs on young crops, and once the caterpillars hatch, they feed on the soft shoots to grow rapidly.
ga: Fall Armyworms sumɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ ji bibii ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Moths ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii koni amɛdara oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full, hot sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil they need to stay alive during their first years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for light, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to fight for sunlight instead of spending energy to build strong stalks and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la he akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛma ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn purple or light yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ purple loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Leaf colors tell you what the crop is missing in the soil. Light yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, while purple leaves show a lack of phosphorus. Plants need these specific food elements from the soil to stay green and healthy.
ga: Baai lɛ ahe su tsɔɔ bo tsei ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ mli. Tsei he miihia nɛkɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting tomatoes on the same patch of land where I just harvested eggplants or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tomato dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa eggplant loo pepper nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes, eggplants, and peppers belong to the same plant family and share similar pests and soil diseases. Planting them continuously on the same soil allows pests and fungal diseases to remain in the ground and easily attack the new crop.
ga: Tomato, eggplant, kɛ pepper yɛ tsei akuu kome mli, ni amɛyɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni tamɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutua ŋmɔshi nibii heei oya.

english: Why do some of my yams grow into strange, split shapes instead of single, smooth tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miida ni amɛmiitsɔ yitsei kome ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers change shape when the soil under them is hard, rocky, or full of clay. As the growing tuber tries to push down, it meets hard obstacles and bends or splits around them.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo shikpɔŋ eyi mli obɔ. Beni yitso ni miida lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eshɛ shi lɛ. Ekɛ gbɛtsii nii ni wa kpeɔ ni ekotoɔ loo egbalaa mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn hard like wood and become tough to cook if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa tamɔ tso ni kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ahoomɔ wa lɛ?

english: When cassava stays in the ground past its full maturity, the plant stops storing soft starch in the roots and begins building tough plant fiber instead, making the tubers hard and woody.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaada kwraa. Tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni ebɔi tso mli tsɔi ni mli wa feemɔ moŋ Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni efeɔ tso.

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress, dry soil, or insect pests like thrips attacking the blossom. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting the flowers from pests allows them to set fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ fɔfɔi ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism tomato plants use to protect themselves from hot sun and dry winds. By rolling leaf edges inward, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to heat so it loses less water.
ga: Leaf curling ji hebuu gbɛ ni tomato tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Baa lɛ naagbee ni aaatsɔ mli lɛ Tsei haa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo baa lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu fioo pɛ laajeɔ.

english: Which food crops can I grow on my farm to make sure my family gets a good, balanced diet to stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni miweku lɛ aná niyenii kpakpa ni sa kɛha hewalɛ kpakpa?

english: Combining starchy staples like cassava or plantain with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts, alongside green leafy vegetables like kontomire (cocoyam leaves), provides a complete balance of carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, and minerals that keep your family strong and reduce visits to the hospital.
ga: Ni akɛ starch tamɔ ŋmei loo plantain kɛ ŋmei tamɔ tsina ŋmei loo ŋmei baafee ekome. Kɛfata tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ contomir (kokoo baai) lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, protein, vitamini, kɛ mineral ni yeɔ emuu. Enɛ haa oweku lɛ náa hewalɛ, ni ehaa helatsamɔhe saramɔi hu baa shi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key plant food, or the soil is too soaked with water after heavy rains, which stops the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri Aloo akɛ nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ mumɔ ni amɛkpaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper plants often shed their flowers when they get too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil, causing the plant to panic and save its energy instead of making fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ he feɔ gbeyei ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ shi moŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why does cassava manage to stay green and alive even when the dry season comes and there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi kɛ́ fɛ̃i be lɛ ba ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep root systems that search far underground for water, and it drops some of its leaves during dry periods to save moisture, making it a very resilient food crop.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni taoɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni baai komɛi baagbee shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni anyɛɔ atsakeɔ waa.

english: Why do cocoa trees produce less fruit when all the large forest trees around them are cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ wooo yibii fioo beni tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ daraa lɛ? Afolɔ fɛɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally thrive under moderate shade because direct hot sunlight stresses the trees, dries out the soil quickly, and leaves them vulnerable to harsh winds and insect pests.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ anɔ.

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives pests and crop diseases a permanent home to multiply in your field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai náa shia ni hiɔ shi daa koni amɛfɔ yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do groundnuts make the soil better for the next crop I plant after harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni miduɔ yɛ be mli ni akpa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special tiny bumps on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: How does adding dried animal manure or compost help my crops yield better quality food?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Organic manure acts like a slow-release food bank for crops, improving how well the soil holds water during dry spells and feeding the crop essential nutrients needed to produce healthy yields.
ga: Organic fertilizers tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ jieɔ amɛhe blɛoo. Te eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ? ni amɛha tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil into the fruit, usually due to irregular watering where the soil goes from very dry to very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ agbala calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛtee nɔ ni edɔ waa nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops as soon as the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants natively adapted to the local environment, meaning their seeds lie dormant in the soil ready to burst open and grab available sunlight and nutrients faster than domesticated farm seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛjɛ fɔmɔ mli amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛdumɔwui lɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaatswa ni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ shia lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit, making them top-heavy. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden Y-sticks (staking) balances the weight and keeps winds from knocking them down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ Y-shape (staking) ni wa fi tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ tsɔne lɛ mli tsiimɔ lɛ afee ekome, ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground after heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when sitting in excess water because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rain water drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛbote nu babaoo mli ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ mawo tso ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking holds the leaves off the wet soil, giving them sun exposure while preventing ground fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking jieɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Okɛ amɛ awo hulu la mli kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen or the soil is too wet for roots to feed. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or improving farm drainage restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo afee nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and builds up corn pests. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa abele lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsuɔ nii kɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the centers of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft inner growth of corn plants. Catching them early and applying neem extract or appropriate insecticides keeps them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ anɔ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni sa tsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. Spraying with soapy water solution or neem oil clears the insects so new leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ koni baai heei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too hot, when soil moisture fluctuates wildly, or when the plant lacks phosphorus. Regular watering and light shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ waa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the middle of the day even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In hot sun, leaves lose moisture through evaporation faster than roots can drink from the soil, causing temporary drooping. As long as the soil remains damp, the leaves will naturally recover as temperatures cool in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ekɛ be kukuoo mli shigbeemɔ baa. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food plant uses to stay green and grow. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient deep into the soil where the shallow roots of young maize cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ eŋɔli kɛ amɛdalɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmãa bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Excessive heat stresses the plant, making it shed flowers to save energy rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Ha amɛfɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why does my cassava yield big tubers in sandy soil but small, crooked ones in hard clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ haa bulbs wuji yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil so they can easily expand sideways. Hard clay soil squeezes the tubers as they try to grow, keeping them small and bent.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã sɛɛgbɛ mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ baatsi bulb lɛ naa beni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda lɛ. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo ni ebɔleɔ ehe

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak when I put three or four seeds in one planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted together in a single spot, their roots fight each other for the limited water and fertilizer in that small area. Spacing them out allows each plant to get enough food to build a strong stalk.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he kome Shishifãi lɛ baawu amɛha nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni yɔɔ he bibioo tamɔ nɛkɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie gbɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tso lɛ yitso ni wa.

english: Why do worms always hide inside the middle leaf folds of my young maize during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, and they prefer the tender, moist center leaves of the maize plant because it gives them shelter from rain while they feed on the growing shoot.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni amɛsumɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ waa ejaakɛ amɛhaa nugbɔ lɛ he jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants dry up faster when elephant grass is growing near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya be mli ni shwuɔ jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Elephant grass has long, thick root systems that suck up moisture and soil nutrients much faster than pepper plants, leaving no water behind for your crop.
ga: Shɔshɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifã kakadaŋŋ ni mli tse ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe pepper tsei. ni oshiŋ nu ko kɛhaaa oŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big forest trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie koo mli tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, hot sunshine. Tall forest trees act like umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa seedlings need to build strong roots in their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and fold downward during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves fold downward during hot, dry weather to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun. This natural reaction helps the plant conserve the water stored inside its trunk.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ koni hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he.

english: Why does cutting off small side branches on my tomato plants make the remaining tomatoes bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ, ni no haa tomato ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ agbo.

english: Side branches consume food and energy to produce extra leaves. Cutting them off directs all the food from the soil straight into growing fewer, larger fruits.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛfee baai krokomɛi. Kɛ́ afo amɛ lɛ, niyenii fɛɛ ni jɛɔ sũ ni yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa aduawai bibii kɛ wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why do my yams rot quickly inside my barn after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot if they get bruised or cut during harvesting, or if the barn is too hot and closed off. Wounds let in air and fungi, while good air movement keeps harvested yams cool and dry.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite kɛji akɛ atswa loo afo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dɔ tsɔ ni egbe. Pilamɔi haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni egbiɔ.

english: If I only have access to a piece of land for less than a year, what type of crops should I plant?
ga: Kɛji akɛ minine shɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ni shɛɛɛ afi pɛ. Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu?

english: You should plant fast-maturing, short-season crops like maize, vegetables (like tomatoes, garden eggs, or pepper), or cowpeas. These crops mature within three to four months, allowing you to harvest and sell your produce before your land agreement ends.
ga: Esa akɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo, ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa, aduawai (tamɔ tomato, abɔɔ mli ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa) loo tsina ŋmãa. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa onibii ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ dani oshikpɔŋ he kpaŋmɔ lɛ baa naagbee.

english: Should I plant tree crops like cocoa, mangoes, or oil palm if I am only renting the land for a short time?
ga: Should I plant trees such as cocoa, mango or oil palm? Kɛji akɛ miha shikpɔŋ be kukuoo ko pɛ?

english: No, tree crops take several years before they start producing fruit and require permanent land ownership. On rented or short-term land, stick to annual crops like maize, cassava, or vegetables that yield within a single season.
ga: Dabi, tsei heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi, ni ebiɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi daa. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ahaa loo he ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii be kukuoo nɔ lɛ Kpɛtɛ afi mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo aduawai ni woɔ yibii yɛ be kome mli lɛ ahe.

english: Can I plant two different crops together on the same field to get more food before my short land access expires?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli koni maná niyenii babaoo dani shikpɔŋ kuku ni miyɔɔ lɛ aba naagbee?

english: Yes, intercropping fast-growing crops like beans or okra with maize allows you to harvest one crop quickly while the other matures, helping you maximize your harvest and income in a short amount of time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmei loo okra ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa kome oya yɛ be mli ni ekroko lɛ daa. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni onáa shika babaoo yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Is it safe for me to grow food crops on land that used to be a trash dump?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ eji jwɛi ashwiemɔ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Growing food on old dumpsites can be risky because broken glass, dangerous chemicals, and heavy metals from the waste can soak into the soil and contaminate your crops. It is best to have the soil tested before planting food crops there.
ga: Niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ shwɛmɔhei momoi lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara yɛ glase ni ekumɔ kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ ahewɔ. Ni dade ni tsii ni jɛɔ jwɛi mli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ dani odu niyenii yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land has good soil for farming just by looking at it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ kuku ko yɛ sũ kpakpa kɛha okwaayeli kɛtsɔ nɔ ni mikwɛɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Dark, moist soil that crumbles easily in your hand and has plenty of earthworms or natural green vegetation usually indicates fertile soil that can support healthy crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli efɔ ni fiteɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo adebɔɔ mli tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji babaoo yɔɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How will I know if my crops are suffering because the soil contains toxic waste or bad chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ ejaakɛ sũ ni yɔɔ gbeyei loo tsofai gbohii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops growing in contaminated soil often show stunted growth, unusual leaf yellowing, burnt leaf edges, or produce small and deformed fruits even when they receive enough water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji nɔ lɛ jieɔ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kpo. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, baa lɛ naa shãa, loo ewoɔ yibii bibii ni efite eyɛ mli akɛ amɛnáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ.

english: What is the best way for me to clear thick bush on my farm without destroying the quality of the soil?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ majie jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii?

english: Instead of burning the bush after clearing, practice slash-and-mulch by leaving the cleared grass to rot on top of the ground. This keeps the soil cool, retains moisture, and decomposes into natural fertilizer.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã jwɛi lɛ beni ajie amɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ bɔ ni ooofee okɛ jwɛi lɛ atswa kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ ni oooha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds grow back so fast right after I clear a new piece of farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he hee ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing the land exposes long-buried weed seeds to sunlight and rain, causing them to germinate quickly. Planting your crops immediately or covering the ground with mulch blocks sunlight and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu amɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ naa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ. Ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya Dumɔ onibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo okɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi hulu lɛ naa ni jwɛi lɛ akaye nɔ.

english: Can I use water running near industrial or utility sites to water my vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli ni bɛŋkɛ nitsumɔhe loo nitsumɔhe ko lɛ atsu nii kɛha aduawai?

english: Using untreated runoff or industrial wastewater can transfer dangerous germs and toxic chemicals into your vegetables, making them unsafe to eat and difficult to sell at the market. Always use clean water for irrigation.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ muji ni asaaa loo nitsumɔhei amli nu ni fiteɔ nii tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai kɛ tsofai fɔji awo o-vegetables lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ ayeɔ, ni ewaa akɛ aaahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ nu ni mli tse atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I figure out how much crop harvest I will actually get from my land before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni maná diɛŋtsɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: You can estimate your harvest by knowing the size of your land, the expected yield per acre for the seed variety you buy, and whether you have reliable soil and water. Proper spacing and fertilizer use will help you reach that expected yield.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu yibiiwoo lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ ni ooole lɛ nɔ. Yibiiwoo ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ abaaná yɛ acre kome mli kɛha dumɔwui srɔtoi ni oheɔ lɛ. Ni okwɛ kɛji oyɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lo. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua bo ni oná yibiiwoo ni okpaa gbɛ lɛ.

english: Please sir, why do my yam vines need long sticks to climb on instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ kɛ tsei kakadaji tsuɔ nii kɛkwɔɔ ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can reach full sunlight to make food. Climbing yams yield much larger underground tubers than vines left crawling on the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkɛhoo nii. Sweet potatoes ni kwɔɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara kwraa fe wain tsei ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Officer, why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to conserve water. By shedding leaves, the plant stops moisture from escaping into the hot air and protects its roots until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpaa, ni ebuɔ eshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Sir, why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient that keeps foliage green and healthy. Applying fertilizer like NPK or Urea gives the plant the food it needs to recover.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Officer, why do experienced farmers advise me to plant groundnuts together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally traps nitrogen from the air and feeds it into the soil. Planting groundnuts with maize helps enrich the soil so your maize grows better without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa duɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, o-abele lɛ baanyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Please sir, why should I spread dried grass on the soil around my young vegetable plants?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi mashwã shikpɔŋ ni mabɔle mitsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dried grass—a practice called mulching—keeps the soil cool under hot sunlight, traps moisture in the ground longer, and prevents weeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Hay ni agbɛɔ ashwãa—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Sir, why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Severe heat stress prevents the flowers from pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkawo yibii.

english: Officer, what causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Agent Mɛni ha mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This rot is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during cold, wet weather. Pruning extra branches and clearing weeds lets sunlight in to dry the pods and stop the sickness.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni afeɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hulu la babaoo aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni hela akpa.

english: Sir, why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight little balls?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bɔɔlu bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl when tiny insects like aphids or thrips suck the sap from new leaves, or when a virus is present. Using targeted pest control methods helps protect new shoots so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ nu nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ. aloo be mli ni hela ko yɛ Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei lɛ ashishifãi heei ahe koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: Officer, why do my mature cabbage heads split open right before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei ni eda kwraa lɛ mli gbalaa dani mikpaa amɛ?

english: Cabbage heads crack when they get a sudden heavy watering after a dry spell. The inside of the cabbage expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the head to burst.
ga: Kaabeji yitsei lɛ baagbala kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Kaabeji lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã, ni no haa eyitso lɛ mli fãa.

english: Sir, why do wild weeds grow much faster than my crop seedlings right after the early rains start?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi dumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapt to your local soil, allowing them to quickly absorb early rainwater and fertilizer. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops get the food and moisture they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛheɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from intense sun and conserve water. By curling, less leaf surface is exposed to heat, which reduces water evaporation until the cooler evening arrives.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ he ni amɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, baa lɛ hiɛ shɛɛɛ hulutsoo he tsɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔ kɛyaa fɛ̃i mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves during the dry season, and will the crop die because of this?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ? Ni ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagboi yɛ enɛ hewɔ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to stop water from escaping through the foliage. The plant is not dead; it goes into a resting state and will quickly sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebabote hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and burn when I clear away all the large shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and excessive heat. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young seedlings can establish strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their blossoms without forming fruit during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ otsi kome ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When flowers fail to pollinate due to high temperatures, the plant drops them to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaaa enyɛŋ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli Beni fɔfɔii lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn yellow and root stems rot after a heavy flood stays in the field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ be mli ni nu afua ni naa wa eba ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing root rot and preventing the plant from taking up food, which turns leaves yellow.
ga: Tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii. ni baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field make my maize grow better when I plant it there the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts work with natural soil organisms to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the legumes are harvested, this trapped nitrogen acts as natural food for the next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ nɛɛ baafee adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and thin with very small underground tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the leaves compete heavily for sunlight. The plant spends all its energy stretching upwards to reach light instead of sending energy down to develop large tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkpãa ŋwɛi koni enine ashɛ la nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a haa he wami kɛ baa si konɛ e pee yitso ngua.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable crops turn pale and weak even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and have aggressive roots that drink water and steal nutrients faster than your crops can. Even with added fertilizer, weeds absorb most of the nutrients before your vegetables can use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni nuɔ nu ni ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe otsei lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he moŋ, shi Jwɛi hu shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani aduawai baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do fall armyworm caterpillars stay deep inside the central funnel of my maize plant during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworm ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms avoid heat and bright daylight. The deep central leaves of the maize plant provide cool shelter and tender leaves, making it a safe place for them to hide and feed undetected.
ga: Fall armyworms tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ la he yɛ hulutsoo be mli. The deep center leaves of the corn plant provide cool shade and soft foliage. This makes it a safe place for them to hide and feed without being detected.

english: Why do lower leaves on my plantain tree turn yellow and dry up while the fruit bunch is maturing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai akui lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: As a plantain bunch grows, the plant draws stored food and nutrients out of its older leaves and sends them directly into the fruit. This natural process causes older leaves to yellow and dry up.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli ni ekɛmajeɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without plantains or shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive, tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that cool the air, protect the seedlings from intense heat, and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni nuɔ he waa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ mli jɔɔ. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread between plants by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing infected plants early stops the disease from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ ji mɛi ni hiɛɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa tsei ateŋ Akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ajieɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, cold, and overly wet conditions. Pruning dense cocoa branches allows sunlight and air to flow through the farm, which dries out excess moisture and prevents the fungus from attacking healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ hei ni efɔ tsɔ. Coco tsei ni afoɔ babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ agbi. ni etsĩ ŋmeii ni baatutua ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why does my young maize turn light green or yellow instead of deep green when it starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ beni ebɔi edamɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize are a clear sign that the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the growing stage or planting leguminous crops like cowpeas before maize helps restore the soil nutrients needed for healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Early application of nitrogen-rich fertilizer in the growth stage Or planting legumes, such as cowpeas, before corn will help restore nutrients in the soil needed for good green growth.

english: Why do my crops grow much stronger when I plant groundnuts or beans in the field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli wa waa nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can pull nitrogen from the air and store it inside the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the ground to naturally fertilize and nourish the next crop, such as maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji legumes, ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni okpa amɛ Nakai nitrogen ni aŋɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha amɛ hewalɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops are forced to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the roots to expand fully and absorb enough food to produce big, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ Dumɔwui anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kwraa ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when the soil is packed too hard or contains many stones that block the root from pushing downwards. Loosening the soil deep into ridges or mounds gives the growing tuber space to expand smoothly without obstruction.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi babaoo yɛ ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛya shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa ŋshɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii enaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot and dry or when the plant doesn't get a steady supply of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching protects the flowers so they can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that react instantly to moisture and are adapted to steal water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early in the season prevents them from choking your young crops before their roots can get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ba lɛ, amɛtsuɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni etsake ehe koni eju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbe otsei bibii lɛ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why do tiny beetles attack my harvested maize and cowpeas and turn them into dust inside storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miitutua mi ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ ni amɛmiitsɔ sũ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils lay eggs inside stored grains and feed on them from the inside out, especially if the grains still hold moisture. Thoroughly drying your grains in the sun and storing them in sealed, airtight bags starves the insects of air and stops destruction.
ga: Kplukai ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ amli edɔ lolo. Agbiɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu mli ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli. Ebaaye ebua ni eshwie kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekpa amɛhiɛkpatamɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of the heavy branches from big trees fall onto my farm during storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei wuji niji ni tsii komɛi gbee shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ ahum ko mli lɛ?

english: Big trees can drop dead or overgrown branches when heavy rains and strong winds start. Pruning old or weak branches early keeps your crops from getting crushed and allows just enough light to reach the farm.
ga: Tsei wuji baanyɛ agbee shi loo amɛniji lɛ baakwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Niji ni egbɔ loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni afolɔ mra. Ebaatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni ekakumɔ, ni ebaaha la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli ashɛ.

english: If I cut down all the big trees on my farm to let the sun in, will my crops grow faster?
ga: Kɛ mifo tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni hulu lɛ aba Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya?

english: While crops need sunlight to grow, removing all shade trees leaves them exposed to harsh heat and drying winds. Keeping moderate shade protects soil moisture and keeps young plants from getting scorched.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛdara moŋ, Shi kɛ́ ajie hulutsoo fɛɛ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ mli dɔɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha lɛ, ebaabu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he, ni ebaatsi tsei bibii anaa koni amɛkashã.

english: How do I know if the trees on my farm are planted too close together?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If you stand at the edge of your farm and cannot see through the plot because of thick foliage, or if sunlight never reaches the ground, your crops are too crowded. Overcrowding blocks breeze flow and encourages diseases.
ga: Kɛji odamɔ ŋmɔ ko naa ni onyɛɛɛ ona jɛmɛ yɛ tsei ahe tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ ahewɔ, loo kɛji hulu la lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa ni ewoɔ helai ahe hewalɛ.

english: What happens to my crops when bright sunshine suddenly turns into heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ amɛfite trukaa? Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa?

english: Rapid switches between strong sun and heavy rain create warm, humid conditions. This moisture on warm leaves can lead to fungal diseases like black pod in cocoa, so good field drainage and plant spacing are essential.
ga: Tsakemɔ ni yaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa teŋ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i shihilɛi baa. Fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ kookoo diji aba, no hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔ mli nu kpakpa kɛ gbɛ ni kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ he hiaa waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops wilting when the sun comes out strong after a rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crops wilt under strong sun because their small roots cannot absorb water fast enough to replace moisture lost through their leaves. Adding mulch around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and retains water.
ga: Tsei bibii baagbi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi yɛ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Amɛbaai lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛto ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ elaaje lɛ najiaŋ. Mulch ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi.

english: How should I prepare my land before the major rainy season begins?
ga: Dani abaabote nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli lɛ, te esa akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Before the rains start, clear overgrown weeds, clean out drainage pathways, and prune hazardous branches. This ensures rainwater flows off safely without flooding your field or breaking plant branches.
ga: Dani nugbɔ baanɛ Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ. Tsumɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ he ni ofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo shweshweeshwe ni nu afuaa ŋmɔji amli loo tsei niji akumɔɔ.

english: Does hot sunshine dry out the soil faster on a farm without shade crops?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: Yes, direct sunshine heats bare soil quickly, causing water to evaporate fast. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or keeping permanent shade trees keeps the soil cool and holds moisture for your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nu ni shwieɔ oya. Kɛ́ odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ akwɛmɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: What causes branches on my crop plants to break when the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni haa niji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ fãa kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: During the rainy season, strong winds combined with heavy rain soaking the leaves can make branches top-heavy and snap. Trimming excess foliage and supporting heavy branches helps prevent breakage.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa fataa he lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei niji atswa ni amɛkumɔ. Foji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ ni akɛfiɔ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛkumɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around the boundaries of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds along your farm edges gives you a clear view across your land to inspect crop health easily, while also preventing pests and bushfires from invading your field.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ, ebaaha ona oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni okwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ mli mlɛo Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ koo mli la naa koni amɛkatutua oŋmɔji lɛ.

english: Why do my crops develop leaf spots when warm sun follows a period of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heat combined with wet leaves creates ideal conditions for crop fungi to multiply. Spacing plants properly allows air to circulate so leaves dry out quickly after it rains.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni akɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ fataa he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni tso mli ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã tsei ateŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and shriveling up in the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and extreme heat. Without shade plants like plantains or canopy trees above them, the intense sun scorches their leaves and dries out the moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo kooyigbɛ tsei bibii bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ agbi.

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works well because maize grows fast and is harvested in about three months, while cassava grows slower and roots deeper, taking full advantage of the field after the maize is harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo ni eshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ. Kɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants start turning yellow from the tips downward before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ kɛyaa shi dani tsei lɛ daraa kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tips often mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient plants need to stay green. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa su kɛ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my corn leaves and small caterpillars hidden inside the middle of the plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ Mi nɔ ni akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves and growing points. Catching them early with recommended biopesticides or neem leaf extracts prevents them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii kɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a dry spell. Planting too early can cause your seeds to sprout and then die from intense heat when the rains pause.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point a cassava stem when sticking it into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tso ko miiwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ani etsɔɔ he ko?

english: Yes, the buds on the stem cutting must point upward toward the sky so the leaves can sprout naturally. Planting them upside down forces the plant to spend too much energy turning around, resulting in weak root production.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei niji ni afo lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ tso lɛ da ni ekɛ ehe shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo atsu nii ni ekɛtsɔ ehe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that blocks water movement inside the stem. Rotating your crops and not planting tomatoes in the exact same spot every season helps stop this disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ ni aduuu tomato yɛ he kome daa be lɛ baaye abua ni akpa hela nɛɛ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is already plenty of sunshine outside for all plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji tsei fɛɛ yɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa momo

english: Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, fertilizer, and water away from your crop roots under the ground. Even with plenty of sun, crops choked by weeds will stay weak because the weeds eat the food in the soil first.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la yɛ moŋ Dumɔwui ni jwɛi ehà nɔ lɛ hu bɛ hewalɛ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra baby suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Why should I cut back baby shoots growing around it? Ajie mi tsɔne titri lɛ

english: Multiple suckers compete directly with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the soil energy goes into producing a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni enɛ haa anyɛɔ akwɛɔ koni akɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni akɛwo tsei wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the heat is too severe or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Providing light shade during midday heat and keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ la lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane mli, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and burn easily in direct sun. They need shade from taller plants like plantain or shade trees to keep their leaves cool and preserve soil moisture while their roots are still small.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do small worms crawl deep inside the central funnel of my young maize stalks to eat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ kɛboteɔ mibi lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye nii lɛ?

english: These worms, often Fall Armyworms, hide deep inside the funnel because the tender inner leaves are easy to chew and the funnel protects them from hot sun, rain, and predator birds.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni bei pii lɛ amɛgbeeɔ shi akɛ asraafoi ŋmeii lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii amli shɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ŋmɔmɔ waaa ni ŋmeii lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ, kɛ okpoi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe.

english: The first rain often moistens only the top layer of soil. If a dry spell follows, the seeds will sprout and then dry up and die; it is safer to wait until the rains become steady and soak deep into the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli fũuɔ. Kɛji hɔmɔ nifeemɔ ko nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ, no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baafee shiŋŋ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize draws heavy amounts of specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those nutrients and lets soil diseases accumulate, reducing your yield over time.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, covering the soil like a blanket. It blocks direct sunlight from evaporating water out of the soil, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ atade Etsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without growing any fruits during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shwie efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ewooo yibii ko yɛ otsi kome ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages their pollen. When it gets too hot, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than trying to feed developing tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen lɛ. Beni edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha tomatoi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my cassava help improve my land?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in tiny knots on their roots. When the plant leaves and roots decay, that natural nitrogen feeds the surrounding cassava plants.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ebuaa amɛhe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli kɛ́ tso lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite. Nitrogen ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ aná niyenii.

english: Why do my yam plants need long wooden stakes for their vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food. When vines climb high on stakes, the leaves spread out into the sun, producing extra energy that gets sent down to build large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai he miihia hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ kroko baa shi koni ekɛfee yitso agbo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rain floods my field near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔji lɛ amli nu ni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Flooded soil seals out air, causing crop roots to suffocate. Without air, beneficial soil microbes cannot survive, allowing rot fungi to attack and break down the cassava tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi. Ha ŋmei lɛ atutua ni efite ŋmei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves that start from the tip and move inward along the center vein usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and produce food, so when soil nutrients are low, the plant pulls energy from its old leaves to feed the new ones.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni amɛyaa mli kɛtsɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ niyenii aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or organic manure without enough phosphorus, they put all their energy into growing tall stems and thick green leaves instead of making flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha tsei nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why does my farmland yield fewer crops every season even though I plant at the same time every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni midumɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ nii yɛ be kome mli daa afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Over time, the soil becomes tired and starved unless you rotate crops or add compost and manure.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye lɛ. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fold up and drop during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants curl and fold their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which stops water from evaporating too quickly. It is the plant's natural shield to stay alive until cooler hours or rain return.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ loo nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings quickly from very dry to very wet. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination, so the plant sheds the flower because it cannot support a growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛwo yibii ni amɛduɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my young pepper plants staying tiny and bushy without growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby pepper tso lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔ mli ni ebɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Stunted pepper plants usually suffer from hard, compacted soil that stops roots from spreading, or a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies. When roots cannot expand or when viruses attack, the plant stops growing upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ haa tsei ni ji dwarf pepper lɛ yeɔ amanehulu. Aloo helai komɛi yɛ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã loo kɛ́ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tutua lɛ lɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋwɛi shweremɔ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods on my tree turn black and dry up while still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Small cocoa pods turn black either due to black pod disease caused by heavy damp weather, or natural self-thinning, where the cocoa tree intentionally sheds excess pods it knows it cannot feed with available water and soil food.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii diji hela ni shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe He ni cacao tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ ejieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ele akɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛ nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ aha lɛ.

english: Why do holes appear all over my cabbage leaves even when I do not see insects on the farm during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji miije kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Many pests like caterpillars and beetles hide under the soil or in low shade during hot daylight hours and only come out at night to eat leaves. Inspecting under leaves at dusk usually reveals the hidden pests.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii, kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ni ebaaje kpo koni ebaye baai pɛ gbɛkɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, anaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my yam vines yellowing and drying up long before the harvest season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by fungal wilt or rot fungi attacking the roots and lower stem underground. When the underground stem is blocked by disease, water cannot reach the top leaves, causing early wilting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya ji fungal wilt loo rot ni tutuaa shishifãi kɛ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji hela tsi shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ anaa Nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔlɔ oya

english: Why did my green leaves turn brown and burn after I sprayed weed killer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical weed killers can burn crops if they are mixed too strong, sprayed on windless hot days where chemical drift touches crop leaves, or if a non-selective herbicide was used. Chemicals must be measured carefully and applied strictly around crop bases to avoid harming the plants.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akɛfutu mli waa tsɔ. Okɛ tsofai afɔ nɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ waa lɛ anɔ beni tsofai shwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ tsu nii Esa akɛ akɛ Tsofai atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwo he fɛɛ he. tso shishitoo nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni akaye tsei awui.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides in the growing head of young maize. They eat the tender central leaves, which prevents the plant from growing strong and producing healthy cobs.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa bibii ayitsei ni miida lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni haaa tso lɛ adara waa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa aba.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when temperatures get too high, when the soil lacks water during flowering, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing the plant to shed blossoms instead of forming tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Ehaa tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo tomato.

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or plants are spaced too closely together, cassava puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ. Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai eŋɔli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Dry Harmattan winds remove moisture from the soil and air. Cocoa trees naturally drop their leaves during severe dry spells to reduce water loss and protect the main trunk from completely dying.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli. Bɔni afee ni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu tso wulu lɛ he koni ekagbo kwraa.

english: Why do I need to use wooden poles to stake my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei atswa mi sweet potato tsei lɛ?
