english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to manufacture food for their underground tubers. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground so leaves receive full sunlight and stay safe from soil fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ sũ mli ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts together in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ afee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally captures nitrogen gas from the air and adds it to the soil. This helps nourish nearby heavy-feeding crops like maize and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ haa kooloi aniyenii ni tsii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: The very first rain is often followed by several hot, dry days before regular rains begin. Planting too early causes seeds to sprout and then wither from heat when the soil dries up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi kɛjɛ latsaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ lɛ.

english: Why did my young crop stems turn black and wither after I put chemical fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer too close to young plant stems or applying it when the soil is dry sucks moisture directly out of the roots, causing the plant to burn and dry out.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo tsei bibii lɛ ahe tsɔ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ, ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and steal vital soil nutrients, space, and sunlight from your plant roots, leaving your crops hungry despite abundant water.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋwɛi kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains develop tiny holes and turn to white powder inside my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni etsɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ mli.

english: Grain weevils lay tiny eggs inside maize that has not been dried properly or treated. Once hatched, the larvae eat the grain from the inside out, leaving behind empty shells and fine dust.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmei lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii. yɛ ŋmãa ni agbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo atsuuu he nii jogbaŋŋ mli Kɛji efɔ lɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Ashi ŋshɔŋloo ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ sũ bibioo ko yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa protects them from heat stress until they grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara waa.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce smaller and fewer peppers when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ pepper bibii kɛ bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, their roots fight over soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block light from each other. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough room and sunlight to branch out and produce abundant fruit.
ga: Beni pepper tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ naa He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ niji ajie ehe kpo ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or farmyard manure helps feed the growing plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ŋmãa babaoo koni ebaakwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why does my cassava farm have huge green leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shikpɔŋ shishi tsei bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing big leaves instead of expanding its underground roots. Adding wood ash or potassium fertilizer encourages bigger tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ faaa lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ tso sũ loo potassium ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua bulb lɛ ni edara.

english: Maize pulls a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts put nitrogen back into the dirt through their roots, naturally restoring fertility for the next season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo aba ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Too many shoots around one plantain stem fight for the same soil food and water, resulting in smaller bunches. Leaving only two or three healthy shoots ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce big, heavy plantain fingers.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni ebɔle plantain tso kome he lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Resulting in a smaller size Leaving only two or three healthy shoots will provide the main plant with enough food to produce large, heavy plantain fingers.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and provide stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni masaa tsei kɛha mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for the growing tuber below. Tall weeds block sunlight, while stakes lift the leaves high so they get maximum sun.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha bulbs ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Jwɛi kakadaji tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ená hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants have ragged holes in the leaves and powdery droppings inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni afee lɛ powder yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside tender maize leaves to eat them. Applying recommended organic or chemical treatments early in the morning destroys them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli koni amɛye amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaakpata amɛhiɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits developing black, rotten spots on the bottom while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by calcium deficiency, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots absorb calcium needed for strong fruit walls.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai gbogboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare dry soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the sun, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by your local extension officer keeps your crop healthy and protects your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Dumɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okpokpaa lɛ nɔ nitsumɔhe nine ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebuɔ onibii ahe.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when the heavy rains start coming late?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni nugbɔ ni naa wa lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants need adequate soil moisture to draw up nitrogen, which makes them green. When rains are delayed or soil lacks nutrients, the plant starves and its leaves lose their bright green color.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛjie nitrogen. which will make it green When the rain is delayed or the soil lacks nutrients The plant will starve and the leaves will lose their bright green color.

english: Why do my vegetable crops look strong in the morning but wilted by the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe yɛ hewalɛ leebi shi amɛgboɔ shwane lɛ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink from dry soil. Adding dry grass or palm leaves around the base of plants (mulching) holds water in the soil throughout the afternoon.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo ŋmei tsei ni egbi fata tso lɛ shishi (mulch) he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli shwane muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that multiplies in humid, wet weather. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets sunlight into the farm and stops moisture from building up around the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fungi ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i kɔɔyɔŋ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shi lɛ haa hulutsoo be kroko baaha hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni ebua ehe naa yɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the weather gets too hot, when soil moisture goes up and down sharply, or when insects damage the flowers. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps plants hold onto their blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ tsakeɔ oya loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: What makes my yam vines turn brown and die early before the roots grow big?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ daa?

english: Yam vines dry up early when attacked by a fungal leaf disease or when soil pests damage the roots. Staking your yam vines up high on sticks keeps the foliage dry and off the ground, reducing disease.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ fungal leaf helai emɔ amɛ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fite amɛshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ akagbi ni amɛkaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ni helai aba shi.

english: How deep should I bury my plantain suckers when setting up a new farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ beni miito ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers should be buried about 30 to 45 centimeters deep. Planting them at this depth keeps the roots firmly grounded and prevents strong winds from blowing the heavy mature plants over.
ga: Esa akɛ afu plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aaafee sɛntimita 30 kɛyashi 45 mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ nɛɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ, ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekatswa tso ni eda lɛ shi.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my pepper plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ pepper tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Spacing pepper plants gives every plant equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing also allows fresh air to move between plants, preventing leaf diseases from spreading easily.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã pepper tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Gbɛ ni sa hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Tsi baa helai anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo.

english: If previous crops grew slowly, stayed small, or had yellow leaves, your soil is low in nutrients. Adding compost or chemical fertilizer restores essential food so your next crop can grow strong.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ da blɛoo, eji bibioo, loo eyɛ baai ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do store-bought hybrid maize seeds perform better than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields and fight off common diseases. Seeds saved from last season lose these strong traits, resulting in weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ jarayeli mli lɛ amli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛkɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ awuu. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving mature shade trees or planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain creates a cool canopy that protects cocoa seedlings during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves in dry weather to save water and keep their roots alive. As soon as the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normal tuber roots.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ kɛkɛ lɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shishifãi tamɔ bɔ ni eji daa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants showing small holes and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni amɛkpãa amɛhe lɛ?

english: Holes and leaf curling on maize are usually caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm feeding on the young shoots. Identifying these early allows you to use appropriate controls before the insects damage the central growing point of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ, ni egbee shi ni eye ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmãa bu kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nibii nɛɛ ni oooyɔse mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni okɛ nɔyeli ni sa atsu nii dani kooloi bibii lɛ akpata tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every year when I plant it in the same field continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Maize uses up specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting maize repeatedly in the exact same spot exhausts the soil, so rotating it with legumes like cowpeas or beans helps put vital nitrogen back into the dirt naturally.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsuɔ nii daa be. Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaho. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Rotting at the bottom of tomatoes is usually caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent and adding organic compost helps produce clean, healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ calcium bɛ tomato tsei amli loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha tomatoi lɛ ahe atse, ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do extension agents tell me to plant cassava stem cuttings at an angle instead of straight down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei niji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slanting angle places several nodes shallowly under the soil, which encourages the plant to grow more tuberous roots evenly near the surface for a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu cassava tsei lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nodes lɛ ateŋ babaoo afee nɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ shishifãi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ koni ená ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing huge leafy branches but failing to produce any flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ niji kɛ baai wuji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi loo pepper lɛ?

english: Excess leafy growth without flowers often means the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer. Plants need balanced nutrients containing phosphorus and potassium to trigger strong flower blooming and fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni fɔfɔii bɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Niyenii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium fata he lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛwo fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to burn all the weeds and cleared stalks on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaashã jwɛi ni ajie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic material and helpful soil organisms that keep the ground rich and moist. Letting cleared vegetation decompose into the soil feeds future crops and protects the soil from sun damage.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ niyenii, ni ebaabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small, light bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ jwɛi bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting suckers too close forces them to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Giving plantains sufficient space ensures every plant gets enough energy to build big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee kuu agbo ni tsii.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning excessive cocoa branches and clearing ground weeds allows air and sunlight to dry the farm and reduce fungal infection.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Kookoo niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ mli egbiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Is there any real difference between planting red sweet potatoes and white sweet potatoes on my farm?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko diɛŋtsɛ yɛ ŋmeii tsuru kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Red and white sweet potato varieties behave differently in growth and use; red varieties often take a bit longer to mature and tend to be sweeter, while white varieties usually mature faster and are commonly used for basic staple dishes.
ga: Sweet potato tsuru kɛ eyɛŋ yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa kɛ bɔ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Henɔi ni tsuɔ lɛ fɔɔ be fioo dani amɛshwereɔ ni amɛfɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ futafuta lɛ shwereɔ oya ni bei pii lɛ akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa.

english: If I plant a rare crop variety that other farmers in my community are not growing, will it grow well in our soil?
ga: Kɛ midu tso ko ni anaaa lɛ ni okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ duuu lɛ, Ani ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: An uncommon variety can grow well if it is suited to your local soil and climate, but it may require special care because local pests might react differently to it compared to traditional crops.
ga: Henɔi ni jeee nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛsa shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Shi ekolɛ ebaabi ni akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ akɛto blema ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Are certain crop varieties naturally better at surviving diseases than others?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi baanyɛ ajo helai anaa foi yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe ekrokomɛi?

english: Yes, different varieties have different strengths; plant breeders specifically develop some varieties to resist common soil diseases and pests that easily destroy traditional crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, srɔtoi lɛ yɛ hewalɛi srɔtoi. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkɛte shi amɛwo helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ blema ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Where can a small farmer like me get reliable seeds or planting materials without spending too much money?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi baanyɛ ana dumɔwui loo nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni amɛfiteee shika babaoo yɛ?

english: Government agricultural extension offices, seed banks, and local farming cooperatives often provide certified, high-quality seeds for free or at subsidized rates to help farmers start strong.
ga: Nɔyeli Okwaafoi Ahe Nitsumɔhe lɛ dumɔwui atoohe Ni bei pii lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli kui kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli, ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa yaka loo yɛ shika ni akɛyeɔ abuaa amɛ koni eye ebua okwaafoi lɛ ni amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I safely store my harvested root crops like potatoes so they do not rot before I can sell them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ shishifãi ni akpa, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ato shweshweeshwe, koni amɛkafite dani mikɛ amɛ ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Root crops should be stored off the ground in a cool, dark, dry, and well-ventilated area; direct light causes them to sprout and turn green, while moisture leads to quick rotting.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ tsei shishifãi ato shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, duŋ, egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. La ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baaha efite oya.

english: Can I keep reusing tubers from my last harvest as seeds for the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ bulbs ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba akɛ dumɔwui kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Reusing harvested tubers as seeds over many seasons causes disease to build up in the plant stock, leading to smaller yields over time, so it is best to buy fresh certified seeds periodically.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ tsu nii ekoŋŋ akɛ dumɔwui yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ, ebaaha helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli be kɛ bei amli.

english: How can I know if market women and buyers will buy a new crop variety before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji jara nɔ yei kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baahe tsei srɔtoi heei dani madu amɛ?

english: Before planting a new crop variety, visit local markets to ask buyers if consumers like its taste, color, and cooking style, as people are often slow to purchase crop varieties they do not recognize.
ga: Dani obaadu ŋmɔshi nibii heei Yaa maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ ni obi mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛji amɛsumɔɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ, ehiɛ su, kɛ bɔ ni ahoɔ nii ahaa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, gbɔmɛi sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛheɔ tsei srɔtoi ni amɛyoooo lɛ.

english: Why do some uncommon crop varieties sell for higher prices in the market than regular ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahenɔi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ No hewɔ lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ jara nɔ fe tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ daa lɛ?

english: Uncommon crop varieties often sell for higher prices because supply is low, or because they have special qualities like sweeter taste, unique color, or longer shelf life that premium buyers prefer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ tsei srɔtoi ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ nɔ ni baa shi lɛ hewɔ. aloo akɛni eyɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi, tamɔ su ni yɔɔ srɔto ni ŋɔɔ fe tsutsu lɛ loo shihilɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ biɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my potato plants produce many big leaves but only tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-potato tso lɛ woɔ baai wuji babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii pɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive leaf growth usually happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which makes the plant spend all its energy growing leaves on top instead of developing tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni daa fe nine lɛ baa kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni eeefee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do crops brought from another region sometimes perform poorly when I plant them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei ni akɛjɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ aba lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops adapt to specific weather, rainfall, and soil conditions; seeds brought from different climates may get stressed by local heat or soil types, resulting in poor growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi anɔ. Dumɔwui ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi amli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ loo shikpɔŋ henɔ lɛ haoɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni ehiii

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition forces the plants to stretch upward to reach the sun, leaving them weak and without enough energy to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi koni eshɛ hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do extension officers always advise me to plant plantains alongside my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa be fɛɛ be akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and soil moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. The plant is moving its remaining nitrogen from older leaves up to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Tsei miitsi nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. High temperatures make it hard for the flower to pollinate itself, so the plant sheds the flower to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa ewaa ahaa fɔfɔi lɛ akɛ amɛbaafee pollination. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns natural nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and erect tall wooden stakes for my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni matswa tsei ni kwɔlɔ kɛha mi sweet potato tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce the food required to swell their underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and protecting them from shade.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ baai helai anaa ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he.

english: Why do my seeds wither and die even when I sow them immediately after the first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: The very first rainfall of the season is often followed by a hot dry spell before the main rains fully establish. Planting too early means tender seeds germinate into hot, drying soil without enough continuous moisture to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi kwraa. Dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ bɛ mli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off naturally, and the soil right around the main stem starts to swell and crack open from the growing tubers below.
ga: Cassava tsei tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni efoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli.

english: What is causing caterpillars to eat the soft leaves right inside the funnel of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ funnel lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. The adult moth lays eggs on the plant, and the hatched caterpillars crawl deep into the moist, sheltered central funnel where they feed on young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ tsei anɔ. ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ mli. ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii

english: Why did my pepper plants burn and turn brown after I put dry fertilizer right against their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ewo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Placing dry fertilizer directly against a crop stem without mixing it into wet soil draws moisture straight out of the plant's roots and stem, causing chemical burns.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni okɛfutuuu shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ tsofa shãa baa

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the dirt so the hot sun does not dry out the roots quickly.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak plants that produce small or empty corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa onáa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Yam plants need their leaves spread out high in the sunshine to produce food. Lifting the vines off the ground helps the leaves get maximum sunlight, which makes the yam tubers under the ground grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ wuji.

english: Why are there small ragged holes and caterpillar droppings inside the leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii afɔfɔi?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. These pests hide inside the growing center of the plant during the day and eat the leaves, which can destroy the crop if not treated early.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why is it bad if I plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot allows soil diseases and pests that love tomatoes to build up in the ground over time, making your plants weaker with every new planting.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sumɔɔ tomato lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ be fɛɛ be ni abaadu lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient it needs from the soil or fertilizer to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot breathe when they sit in soaked, waterlogged soil for too long. Excessive water suffocates the roots, causing fungal rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or lack of pollination from insects.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ amɛmli lɛ hao tsei lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even after I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong root systems that steal the water and fertilizer from the soil before your main crops have a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ náa hegbɛ ni ekɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Can flowers actually be grown as a main farm crop in Ghana just like maize or cassava?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu fɔfɔii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri yɛ Ghana tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Yes, flowers like roses and lilies can be farmed commercially in Ghana just like food crops. Ghana's warm climate and sunshine make it suitable for growing high-value flowers year-round, provided they receive proper water, shade, and nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, fɔfɔi tamɔ roses kɛ lili. Abaanyɛ adu kɛha jarayeli yɛ Ghana akɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii. Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fɔfɔi ni jara wa waa lɛ akwɛmɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ, kɛji akɛ amɛná nu, hulutsoo kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni sa.

english: What makes non-traditional export crops like flowers yield more income than standard local food crops?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee kusum nifeemɔi ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ, tamɔ fɔfɔii lɛ, náa sɛɛnamɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ niyenii ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Export crops sell in international markets where consumers pay higher prices for premium quality. Because flowers are high-demand luxury goods sold in international markets, they can generate much higher revenue per acre than basic local staples.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔii ji nibii ni jara wa waa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei. No hewɔ lɛ fɔfɔii baanyɛ aha shika babaoo aba yɛ acre kome mli fe maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni akɛyeɔ nii.

english: Why do some farmers grow crops under plastic shade structures instead of out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ plastic tsɔnei ashishi moŋ fe ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Covering delicate crops with plastic structures or shade nets protects them from heavy rains, burning heat, and insects. It creates a mild environment inside so crops grow faster, develop better blooms or fruits, and remain healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plastic loo shade netting ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ la ni tsoɔ kɛ kooloi amli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni esaaa baa mli koni tsei lɛ adara oya. Fɔfɔi loo aduawai fɔ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Can crops that originally come from cold European countries really grow well in warm Ghanaian soil?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni shishijee lɛ amɛjɛ Europa maji ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, many foreign crop varieties can thrive in Ghana if they are given proper shade, controlled watering, or planted in suitable microclimates. Using shade nets and greenhouse covers helps lower the temperature so these crops feel comfortable.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ Ghana kɛji akɛ aha amɛ hulutsoo ni sa. kudɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ loo adu yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo yɔɔ ni sa Kɛ akɛ shade netting kɛ greenhouse covers tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi koni tsei nɛɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do flower crops require so much more daily attention and work compared to grain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi tsei biɔ daa gbi kwɛmɔ kɛ nitsumɔ babaoo fe ŋmãa tsei lɛ?

english: Delicate crops like flowers lose their market value if their stems or petals get damaged. They need constant care, daily watering, precise feeding, and insect checks so every single harvest meets strict quality standards.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baaje jara nɔ kɛji akɛ amɛshishifãi loo amɛyibii lɛ fite. Amɛbiɔ ni akwɛ amɛ daa, aha amɛ nu daa gbi, aha amɛ niyenii ni ja. kɛ kooloi amli kwɛmɔ Bɔni afee ni ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashɛ shishitoo mlai ni mli wa ni kɔɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ he.

english: How does plant food or fertilizer change the way flowers open and grow on the field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsake bɔ ni fɔfɔii lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe amɛhaa ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourage plants to produce strong buds and bright, uniform blooms. Proper nutrients ensure stems grow straight and sturdy enough to hold heavy flowers.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni phosphorus kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi daa. Niyenii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi ni tsii lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to prune or cut back plant stems after flowers finish blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ loo afolɔ tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Pruning removes old and dying parts so the plant does not waste energy trying to feed them. Cutting back old growth encourages the plant to direct its energy into pushing out fresh, healthy new stems and flowers.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ nibii ni egbɔ kɛ nibii ni miigboi lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ akafite hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha amɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ dalɛ momo lɛ mli lɛ, ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ atsu nii koni ekɛjie tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ fɔfɔi heei, ni yɔɔ ehee, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some delicate crops need to be harvested early in the morning before the sun gets strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he waaa lɛ leebi maŋkpa, dani hulu la lɛ ashɛ waa lɛ?

english: In the early morning, plants are fully filled with water from the night. Harvesting before the heat of the sun prevents the crops from losing moisture quickly and wilting before they can be processed.
ga: Kɛ́ je tsɛre lɛ, nu yiɔ tsei lɛ amli obɔ kɛjɛɔ gbɛkɛ mli kɛyaa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nii dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni amɛkagboɔ dani anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii.

english: How do farmers keep cut flowers fresh for days so they can be shipped long distances overseas?
ga: Okwaafoi lɛ baaha fɔfɔi ni afo lɛ ahi shi gbii babaoo. Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akɛya maŋsɛɛ yɛ gbɛ kakadaŋŋ nɔ?

english: Cut flowers are placed in cold storage rooms right after harvest to slow down their natural aging process. Keeping them in nutrient water inside chilled containers keeps them fresh until they reach distant buyers.
ga: Akɛ fɔfɔi ni afo lɛ woɔ he ko ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛha adebɔɔ mli dalɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo nu ni haa mɔ hewalɛ mli yɛ friji mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ mɔ ko ni heɔ nii yɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Why does using clean drip water help crops perform better than relying only on rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni hoɔ ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe nugbɔ pɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drip irrigation delivers clean water directly to the plant roots without wetting the leaves. This reduces leaf diseases caused by wet foliage and ensures the plants receive steady moisture even during dry spells.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni mli tse baa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛ baai lɛ efɔɔɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe helai ni baa ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tsei lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ po.

english: Why do some of my corn plants grow tall with big ears while others right next to them stay short and produce almost nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi kɛlɛ ni amɛtoii lɛ dara yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ yɛ kukuji ni eshwɛ fioo ni amɛwooo nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Corn plants compete heavily for soil nutrients, light, and water. If seeds are planted too close together or if fertilizer is spread unevenly, the stronger plants take most of the nourishment, leaving neighboring stalks stunted and weak.
ga: Abɛi tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, la, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli waa. Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo aja ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, Bɔ ni tso lɛ he wa ha lɛ, nakai ebaaná niyenii kpakpai babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: What causes the soft hairs on my corn cobs to turn brown, and does that mean it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa yitsɔi feɔ blɛoo? Yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: The soft hairs, called silks, turn brown and dry up after they have successfully collected pollen to form kernels. Dry brown silks mean pollination is complete and kernels are filling out, signaling that harvest is only a few weeks away depending on whether you want fresh or dry corn.
ga: Yitsɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ni atsɛɔ lɛ siliki lɛ, feɔ blɔfo ni egbiɔ beni abua pollen naa yɛ omanyeyeli mli ni etsɔ dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ. Kpoji ni egbi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ pollination lɛ egbe naa ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nikpamɔ lɛ baahe otsii fioo pɛ. Edamɔ kɛji oosumɔ ŋmãa hee loo ŋmãa ni egbi nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize stalks turning yellow from the tips downward in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛba shi yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: This yellowing is a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the corn plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the younger growing leaves at the top, indicating that your farm needs compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen lɛ faaa Abɛi tsei lɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ koni amɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy green leaves, but produce small and woody tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ yi mi nyafii ko nɛ ngɛ tso ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing foliage above ground instead of tubers below. Cassava needs balanced soil with adequate potassium to encourage energy storage in the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ ni ja ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia cassava koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open, fully cleared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse kwraa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural leaf canopy that protects young trees from drying out during their early years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli baai ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Why does planting beans or cowpeas alongside my maize help the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ewaa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil and provides nearby maize plants with essential nutrients.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a heatwave or dry spell before the main rainy season settles in. Seeds sown too early will sprout with the first moisture, but then wither and die when the water disappears shortly after.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be loo nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Shi ebaagbi ni ebaagbo kɛ́ nu lɛ laaje yɛ be fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: Why do my mature corn cobs start rotting on the stalk before I can harvest them during rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmeii momo lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani akpaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rot occurs when rainwater enters inside the husk surrounding the cob, creating a damp shelter for fungus to thrive. Choosing corn varieties with tight husk covers helps keep rain out and protects the drying kernels.
ga: Rot baa kɛji nugbɔ nu bote tso lɛ yibii ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ feɔ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni ekwɛ̃. Abele henɔi ni ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ ni ahalaa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ he, ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest perform poorly when I plant them the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed from two distinct parent plants to give maximum strength in the first generation. Seeds harvested from those plants lose that special genetic combination, resulting in uneven growth and much lower yields in the next crop.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔlɔi tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo aha yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔmɔ nii krɛdɛɛ ni akɛfutuɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi kwraa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: What causes the central funnel of my young maize plants to look chewed with dark powdery dirt left inside?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn plants lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ miiho ni muji ni tamɔ powder ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ miiho?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the tender whorl of young corn plants. Treating the crop early prevents the pest from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the exact same spot immediately after harvesting my last batch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ beni akpa naagbee fã lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soil needs time to rest and recover its nutrients, and pests left behind in the soil need time to die off. Giving the land a break or rotating crops prevents diseases and keeps the soil healthy for the next planting cycle.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ená niyenii mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ashiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ heɔ be dani amɛgboiɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mligbalamɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai anaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants slow down and take a break from fruiting after giving a heavy harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ekpaa yibiiwoo yɛ ŋmaa babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plants exhaust their nutrient reserves after producing a big yield. Giving them a short recovery period with proper watering and fertilizer allows them to regain strength to flower and fruit heavily again.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ beni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo sɛɛ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ be kuku ni amɛkɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ha amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How long does it usually take from planting maize seeds to harvesting the mature corn?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ ŋmãa ni eda lɛ kpamɔ nɔ?

english: Most common maize varieties in Ghana take about 3 to 4 months (90 to 120 days) to fully mature and be ready for harvest, depending on rainfall and soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi henɔ ni afɔɔ naa waa yɛ Ghana lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) dani edaa kwraa ni efeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ. Edamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my fresh crop of cowpea take about three months before I can harvest the pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea hee lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ dani abaanyɛ akpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally follow a fixed growth cycle that requires about 60 to 90 days to move from germination, through flowering, to seed pod development.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli, ni amɛdaraa be fɛɛ be. Eheɔ aaafee gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 dani eshiɔ shweremɔ. kɛtsɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ nɔ kɛyashi dumɔwui akutsei lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ

english: How many months after planting cassava can I expect to start harvesting the roots?
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ, nyɔji enyiɛ mli abaanyɛ akpa shishifãi lɛ?

english: Cassava generally takes between 9 to 12 months to reach full maturity, although some early-maturing varieties can be harvested starting around 6 to 8 months.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani eshɛɔ ŋmei he. Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ akpa ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ yɛ aaafee nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 mli moŋ.

english: Why does the very first crop harvested on newly cleared land yield better than the second crop planted right after?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ ni adu yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ?

english: New land has accumulated rich organic nutrients over time. The first crop feeds heavily on this natural fertility, so subsequent crops need added compost or fertilizer to match that initial yield.
ga: Shikpɔŋkukui heei ebua niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo naa yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Klɛŋklɛŋ tsei lɛ ye nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo nɛɛ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, tso henɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛ shishijee yibiiwoo lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Why do I need to keep my cocoa seedlings under shade in a nursery for several months before moving them to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ toɔ hulutsoo be mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji babaoo dani mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by hot sun and heavy rain. Keeping them in a shaded nursery gives them time to build strong root systems before facing harsh outdoor conditions.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Amɛkwɛmɔ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha amɛná be ni amɛkɛto shishifãi ni mli wa amɛma shi dani amɛyashɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How long should my tomato seedlings stay in the seedbed before I transplant them into my main field?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ awo miŋmɔ titri lɛ mli?

english: Tomato seedlings usually need about 3 to 4 weeks in the seedbed until they grow 4 to 5 strong leaves and sturdy stems ready to survive transplanting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe hiaa ni tomato dumɔwui lɛ ahi otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛbaaná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 4 kɛyashi 5 kɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni esa akɛ adu amɛ.

english: Why do plantain suckers produce fruit faster than a completely new plant grown from scratch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui woɔ yibii oya fe tsei heei ni adu kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers receive continuous energy and stored nutrients from the parent plant's root system, allowing them to mature and bear fruit much faster than a fresh planting.
ga: Plantain sucker lɛ naa hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ kɛ niyenii ni ebua naa kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya kwraa fe nibii ni adu ehee lɛ.

english: How often can I harvest leafy vegetables like spinach or kontomire without killing the plant?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa aduawai ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ spinach loo contomurs ni migbeee tso lɛ?

english: You can harvest leaves every 1 to 2 weeks, provided you leave enough leaves for the plant to make food and give it enough water and nutrients to grow new leaves between harvests.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa baai lɛ daa otsi 1 kɛyashi 2, ni oshi baai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni tso lɛ kɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha baai heei akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ ateŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. When soil lacks nitrogen or heavy rains wash it away, applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color and energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oná su kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out very thin and small when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibioo kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain small when planted too close to each other or in hard, compacted soil. Giving each plant enough distance allows the underground roots space to gather soil nutrients, store food, and swell into thick tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ buaa niyenii mli hewalɛ naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ekɛ niyenii toɔ, ni efuɔ ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I put my chemical fertilizer directly touching the stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo tsei ashishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem causes severe chemical burns to the plant's skin and shallow roots. Fertilizer should always be applied in a ring a few inches away from the stem where the outer roots can absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ekɛ tsofa shãa hewolo lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ waa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ mli. ni kponɔgbɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains next to them provides living shade and keeps the air humid until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ ni akwɛɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara ni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out and crack just two days after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi ni egbɛ eshwa gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water very fast when exposed to direct sun and hot winds. Covering the earth around your crops with dry leaves or straw—a method called mulching—traps soil moisture and keeps the ground cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Mulching ni okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwieɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe - gbɛ ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - haa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out and catch maximum sunlight to make food. If leaves lie on the wet ground, they rot easily and cannot generate enough energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ baai lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ Egboɔ oya ni enyɛŋ ejie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I see ragged holes and dark droppings inside the middle leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-abɛi bibi lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside young corn leaf funnels are caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. This pest hides inside the growing tip during the day and feeds on soft leaves, requiring early monitoring and safe pest treatments to control.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei bibii lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ teeɔ ehe yɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii. Esa akɛ akwɛ enɛ nɔ mra. ni akudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling tightly into cups and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or by viruses spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents them from damaging young leaves and stunting plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite baai bibii ni amɛkaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants suffer from extreme heat or irregular watering. Severe heat stress prevents pollination, causing the plant to shed its blossoms to preserve its water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsiɔ pollination naa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal soil nutrients and water away from the main plantain tree. Removing all but one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tsobii loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Ajieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and dry up after I spray weedkiller near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weedkillers contain strong chemicals that can drift through the air or drift in the soil to non-target plants, burning their leaves and stopping them from making food.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya tsei ni jeee nɔ ni akɛtaoɔ lɛ anɔ. Obaanyɛ oshã baai lɛ ni okpa nihoomɔ.

english: If I use too many strong chemicals on my farm to kill insects quickly, will it spoil my soil for future seasons?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni mli wa babaoo tsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛgbe kooloi bibii lɛ oya hu? Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ baafite yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Overusing harsh chemicals destroys the good organisms like earthworms and helpful microbes in the soil, which eventually leaves the land tired, infertile, and hard to farm for generations to come.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ nibii kpakpai tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ, ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ewaa akɛ abaatsu nii yɛ yinɔi ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Are there natural ways to protect my maize from pests without using expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, planting companion crops like cowpeas or spraying natural solutions like neem leaf extract can keep pests away while keeping your soil and crop safe and healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, nanemɛi tsei adumɔ tamɔ cowpea loo adebɔɔ mli tsabaai tamɔ neem baa mli nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ etsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha oshikpɔŋ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even though I plant the exact same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, causing the land to lose its strength over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What happens to my farm soil if I burn all the cleared bush and weeds before planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishã tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ fɛɛ dani midu?

english: Burning destroys the living topsoil, kills good organic nutrients, and dries out the land, making you start all over again to rebuild healthy soil.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Efiteɔ niyenii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojeɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shishi ekoŋŋ koni otswa shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do cover crops help protect my land so my children can also farm on it in the future?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ koni mibii lɛ anyɛ atsu he nii wɔsɛɛ?

english: Cover crops carpet the ground to prevent heavy rain from washing away good topsoil, while adding natural nutrients that keep the land fertile for long-term use.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kpakpa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii koni akɛtsu nii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ fataa he.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and stop growing when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense to protect itself from losing water during extreme heat, but persistent hot weather without shade or water will stunt its growth.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ he. Shi kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yaa nɔ ni hulutsoo loo nu bɛ mli lɛ baatsi dalɛ naa.

english: Why is my yam crop rotting under the ground before I even harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Underground rotting usually occurs when excess water gets trapped in poorly drained soil, creating conditions where bacteria and fungi can spoil the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ baa kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bote shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni bacteria kɛ fungi baanyɛ aha tuber rot aba lɛ baa.

english: How does planting groundnuts together with my maize help both crops grow better?
ga: Te ŋmei ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that nourishes neighboring plants like maize.
ga: Peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress such as sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or a lack of nutrients, shedding flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle harsh direct sunlight because their young leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside them provides living shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the young trees grow.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ akɛni amɛ baai bibii lɛ shãa oya lɛ hewɔ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. Enɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs fertilizer before I plant my maize this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu ŋmãa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: If your previous crop grew slowly, had pale yellow leaves instead of deep green, or produced small cobs, your soil is low on nutrients like nitrogen. Testing the soil or applying well-rotted manure and recommended fertilizer before planting restores these essential plant foods.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. loo eyɛ ŋmei bibioo ko Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooka okwɛ loo ni okɛ ŋmei ni egbo kɛ ŋmei ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ awo mli dani adu lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Curling and yellowing leaves on cassava are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings helps prevent this disease from reducing your harvest.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava ŋmɔshi nibii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hela nɛɛ naa koni ekaha okpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: What causes small holes in my cabbage leaves, and how can I stop pests from eating them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ cabbage baai anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by hungry caterpillars like the diamondback moth larvae. Inspecting the undersides of leaves early and applying biological controls or safe insecticidal sprays early in the morning prevents pest damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ daimondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akafite nii.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell before steady rains begin. Planting too quickly causes seeds to germinate and then wither in dry soil; waiting for consistent rain ensures young roots get enough moisture to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ yaa nɔ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce very small fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots fight for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing pepper plants properly gives each plant enough light and food to produce larger, healthier peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Pepper tsei ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee pepper ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida fiofio eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your main crop. Clearing weeds during the first three to six weeks after planting gives your crops the best chance to grow strong without stress.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii titrii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdara waa ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant suffers from irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the base of the plant during hot weather helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Tso lɛ shishi yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yams rot easily if they get bruised during harvesting or are stored in hot, dark rooms without air movement. Storing uninjured tubers off the ground in a raised, cool, and well-ventilated traditional yam barn stops rot from spreading.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni mli ewo duŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Akpaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni pilaaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ kusum mli sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni akpa fitemɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why is clearing my farmland without burning the bushes better for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛ brɔshi shãaa lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Burning land destroys organic matter, useful earthworms, and soil moisture that crops need to thrive. Clearing without fire leaves organic mulch on top of the soil, which decays into natural plant food and protects the soil from drying out.
ga: Hei ni ashã lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara La ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Why should I plant plantains on the same piece of land where I am planting my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct heat. Fast-growing plantains provide crucial shade and moisture during the first year, acting as living umbrellas until the cocoa plants are strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni dɔlɛ fiteɔ oya. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hɔnɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Will leaving existing large trees on my farm help or hurt my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani tsei ni edara momo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛbaashi lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye mi-kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ awui?

english: Leaving selected large shade trees helps your cocoa. Cocoa trees naturally thrive in partial shade, which reduces water loss, keeps the soil cool, and protects young seedlings from scorching heat.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua okoo lɛ. Cocoa tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he

english: How long should I keep plantains growing alongside my cocoa trees?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ?

english: Plantains should remain as shade cover for the first 2 to 3 years. Once the cocoa trees grow taller and create their own canopy, you can gradually reduce the plantains so they do not compete with the cocoa for light and nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ aha plantains lɛ ahi hulutsoo be mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli, beni kookoo tso lɛ daa ni ekɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshishitoo lɛ maa shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ plantains lɛ aba shi fiofio bɔni afee ni okɛ cocoa lɛ akatswa akaŋ yɛ la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he.

english: What is the most important thing I need to do to keep my cocoa seedlings alive in their first year?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafee koni mi-kooko dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: The most important focus in the first year is shade management and weed control. Protecting seedlings from harsh sunlight and keeping weeds from choking their roots ensures high survival rates.
ga: Nibii ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli ji shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he kɛ jwɛi ni atsĩɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anaa lɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi babaoo.

english: Is it safe to cut down big shade trees during the first year after planting cocoa?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaafolɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli beni adu kookoo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, you should avoid felling large trees directly over young cocoa plants in the first year. Falling heavy branches or trunks can crush fragile seedlings and suddenly expose them to full sunlight, causing severe stress.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okpa tsei wuji ni ooofo yɛ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ lɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Tso nine loo etso ni egbee shi baanyɛ akumɔ dumɔwui ni waaa ni eshi amɛ trukaa yɛ hulu la mli. ni kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa

english: How can I protect my new cocoa plants when the hot, dry season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cacao tsei heei lɛ ahe kɛji hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ je shishi pɛ?
