english: You can protect young cocoa by keeping plantain shade overhead, placing dry palm leaves or straw around the base of the plants as mulch to retain soil moisture, and clearing dry weeds around the farm perimeter to prevent bushfires.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni oooha amɛ yɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmei baai ni egbi loo jwɛi abɔle tso lɛ shishi akɛ mulch koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. ni ajie jwɛi ni egbi ni yɔɔ Fam husu lɛ he lɛ koni koo mli la akatswa

english: When is the best time of year to put my new cocoa plants into the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei heei yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: The best time to plant cocoa is at the beginning of the major rainy season. This gives young roots plenty of time to establish in wet soil before dry weather arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo ji nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shishijee. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ náa be babaoo ni amɛkɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ baa.

english: Should I clear all the natural bush off my land before planting cocoa and plantains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie adebɔɔ mli tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu kookoo kɛ plantains?

english: You should clear weeds and underbrush, but do not clear every single tree. Selective clearing allows you to keep good shade trees that will protect your cocoa for years to come.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii. Shi kaajie tso fɛɛ tso kɛjɛ ohe. Kɛ́ ohala he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná hulutsoo jogbaŋŋ, ni no baabu o-cocoa lɛ he afii babaoo.

english: Can I harvest and sell plantains while waiting for my cocoa trees to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa plantains ni mahɔ̃ɔ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, plantains start producing fruit within 10 to 12 months. This gives you food and early cash income while your cocoa trees take several years to reach full production.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains baabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ nyɔji 10 kɛyashi 12 mli. Enɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika mra. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, o-cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛshɛɔ yibiiwoo he jogbaŋŋ.

english: How close together should I plant plantain suckers and cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu dumɔwui kɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ he tɛŋŋ?

english: Plantains are typically planted about 3 meters apart, with cocoa seedlings planted in between them. This spacing ensures every cocoa plant receives proper shade without being choked by the plantain roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3, ni aduɔ cocoa dumɔwui yɛ amɛteŋ. Nɛkɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa kookoo tso fɛɛ tso naa hulutsoo ni sa ni plantain shishifãi tsiii enaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die during the intense dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow root systems and tender leaves that cannot handle direct sunlight and severe heat. Providing temporary shade with food crops like plantains and placing mulch around the base retains soil moisture and keeps the young roots cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaa bibii ni nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa. Niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains ni akɛhaa amɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ Cones lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa branches fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-kookoo niji babaoo miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but many drop off due to lack of pollination by tiny insects, water stress, or lack of nutrients. Feeding the tree proper nutrients and keeping the soil moist helps more flowers turn into full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo eba shi yɛ kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ ahewɔ. nu mli haomɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ.

english: How does black pod disease spread so fast across my cocoa farm during the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni black pod hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp conditions. Raindrops splash water from infected pods or soil onto healthy pods, carrying the fungal spores with them and spreading the rot quickly across the farm.
ga: Fuŋ ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ kɛ pods diji baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii loo shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Amɛhiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ. ni ekɛ rot hela gbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your cocoa tree is starving of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or is being attacked by sap-sucking pests like mirids (capsids). Fertilizer and pest control restore the tree's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, loo kooloi ni yeɔ nu, tamɔ mirids (capsids) miitutua amɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso mli kɛ nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does rice grow so much better in flooded areas than on dry, high land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ fe hei ni egbi ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants are uniquely adapted to survive in water-logged soils where other crops would suffocate. Standing water keeps the roots constantly hydrated and naturally smothers most competing land weeds.
ga: Afee ŋmãa tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei krokomɛi nyɛŋ amu Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ anáa nu ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do birds attack my rice field so much more than my maize or cassava crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ fe mi ŋmãa loo mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice grains grow out in the open on exposed stalks and are small, soft, and easy for birds to swallow. Maize is protected by a thick husk and cassava grows underground, making rice an easy primary target for bird flocks.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ tsei ni miiba lɛ anɔ. Ni eyɛ bibioo, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni okpoi miɔ lɛ oya. Akɛ ŋmei ni mli tse buɔ ŋmei he ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa ŋmãa feɔ nɔ titri ni okpoi taoɔ.

english: Why does my rice produce empty grain heads even though the stems grew very tall and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice lɛ dumɔwui bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ? Trunk lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Tall green stems mean the plant had enough nitrogen to grow leaves, but empty grains mean it lacked water or key nutrients like potassium at the exact moment the flowers were forming into grains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni kɛlɛ ni ji eŋɔli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ potassium, yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ miifee dumɔwui.

english: Should I buy imported high-yield seeds or just plant seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ loo madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Imported certified seeds are specially bred in laboratories to produce bigger yields and resist diseases. Saved seeds lose their strength and yield potential over time, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛba maŋsɛɛ ni awo he odase lɛ ewo laboratori ko mli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops when I open up a new farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ migbele ŋmɔ hee ko naa lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are hardier than cultivated crops and immediately jump to capture open sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. You must clear weeds early so they do not steal food from your young crops.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. ni efoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni emɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ehe miihia ni ojie jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to feed my crop different types of fertilizer at different times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi aha mitsei lɛ? Yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli?

english: Crops need different food at different growth stages. Nitrogen is needed early on to build strong green leaves and shoots, while phosphorus and potassium are needed later to develop strong roots, flowers, and heavy fruits or grains.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii srɔtoi yɛ amɛdalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium he miihia yɛ sɛɛ mli koni ekɛfee shishifãi, fɔfɔi, kɛ aduawai loo dumɔwui ni mli wa.

english: Why do some weed sprays kill the weeds with wide leaves on my farm but leave the grassy ones growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ekomɛi gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ha jwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Weeds belong to different families. Broadleaf weeds have wide leaves, while grass-type weeds have narrow leaves. Different weed medicines are specifically made to target one type without affecting the other.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ jɛ wekui srɔtoi amli. Jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ yɛ baai babaoo. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi jwɛi lɛ yɛ baai bibii. Afee tsofai srɔtoi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛtutua jwɛi henɔ kome ni enaaa ekroko nɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell the difference between broadleaf weeds and grass weeds on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: If you look closely at the plant, broadleaf weeds usually have wider leaves with net-like veins and branching stems. Grass-type weeds have long, thin leaves with straight veins running from top to bottom.
ga: Kɛ okwɛ tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Broadleaf jwɛi lɛ fɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ. Eyɛ baai fãji ni tamɔ ŋshɔŋlooi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ niji. Jwɛi jwɛi lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni linei ni ja jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa shishi.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow and stay small when weeds grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ bibii kɛ́ jwɛi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds act like extra mouths to feed on your farm. They steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your maize needs, leaving your crops starved and weak.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ naabui krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa o-ŋmãa lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii ni oduɔ nii lɛ, ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ.

english: Will leaving weeds on my farm during the first few weeks lower my final harvest yield?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ baaha mi naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, young crops need all the water and plant food they can get to build strong roots. If weeds compete with them early on, the crops will never reach their full size, resulting in a smaller harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei bibii lɛ he miihia nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo akaŋshii mli mra lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛɛɛ elɛɛmɔ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: When is the right time for me to spray or clear weeds from my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ loo mafo jwɛi?

english: It is best to remove weeds early when they are still very young and small. Waiting until they grow tall makes them harder to kill and allows them to damage your crops early on.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie jwɛi lɛ mra. Beni amɛji gbekɛbii bibii waa ni amɛji bibii lɛ Mɛɛ ni amɛbaafee mɛi ni dara lɛ baaha amɛgbemɔ afee nɔ ni wa. Ni ha amɛfite onibii mra.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after I cut them down with a hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ ŋmei shwieɔ amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Hoeing cuts off the top of the plant, but many weeds have deep roots or seeds hidden in the soil. Once it rains, these roots sprout again and hidden seeds rise to the top to grow.
ga: Kɛtsɔ spade nɔ lɛ, ofo tso lɛ yiteŋ. Shi jwɛi babaoo yɛ shishifãi loo dumɔwui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shishifãi nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Can I use the same weed spray on my cassava field that I use on my corn field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ tamɔ bɔ ni mifeɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: No, different crops handle weed medicines differently. A spray meant to clear weeds in corn might burn or kill cassava plants, so you must select the right spray for each crop.
ga: Dabi, esoro bɔ ni tso fɛɛ tso tsuɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe nii eha. Spray ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo egbe ŋmãa tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ohala tsofa ni sa kɛha tso fɛɛ tso.

english: Why did the weed medicine I sprayed on my farm fail to work after it rained?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain can wash the weed medicine off the leaves before the weed has time to drink it in. You need clear, dry weather for the medicine to settle and take action.
ga: Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ baai lɛ anɔ dani jwɛi lɛ aná be ni amɛnu. Shihilɛi ni mli tse ni mli egbi he miihia bo koni tsofa lɛ mli awa ni etsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops curling up after I sprayed weed medicine nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If weed spray drifts onto your crop leaves or if you use too much, the crop absorbs the medicine as if it were a weed, causing leaf burning or damage.
ga: Kɛji tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ otso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ loo okɛtsu nii babaoo lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ tsofa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eji jwɛi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa loo efiteɔ.

english: How do I know if a weed spray is safe to use around my specific crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ hi akɛ akɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ?

english: Safe weed sprays are made to attack specific weed types like grass or broadleaf plants while leaving certain crop types unharmed. You must match the spray to both the weed type and the crop you are growing.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ koni ekɛtutua jwɛi henɔi komɛi, tamɔ jwɛi loo tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo. Kɛtsɔ tsei komɛi ni ashiɔ ni amɛyeee awui lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ato jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees fail to grow well in rocky or gravelly soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ tɛ loo ŋmei shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, soft, and nutrient-rich soil so their long taproots can grow deep to find water and food. Gravelly or rocky soil blocks root growth and cannot hold onto water or fertilizer, causing the trees to dry out and die.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia kokoo tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, taproot kakadaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ada kɛya shɔŋŋ koni ena nu kɛ niyenii. Shikpɔŋ, ŋmei, loo tɛi tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa. ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ato Ehaa tso lɛ gĩɔ ni egboɔ.

english: How do I know if my land has the right conditions to support growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shihilɛ ni sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cocoa needs deep, dark soil that drains water well, along with regular rainfall and shade from taller trees. If your land is mostly sand, rock, or stays flooded for weeks, cocoa trees will struggle and fail to produce healthy pods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli edɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia Cocoa. Kɛfata nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ tsei kakadaji amli lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo ji ŋã, tɛi, loo nu ewo nɔ otsii babaoo Cacao tso lɛ baaná amanehulu ni enyɛŋ ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa aba.

english: Is it safe for me to mix crop chemicals with dirty water taken from a nearby stream?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baafutu nu ni mli ewo muji ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli?

english: No, dirty or muddy water contains soil particles and minerals that bind to the chemical and weaken it. This makes the chemical less effective against pests and can sometimes form clumps that damage your crops.
ga: Dabi, nu ni mli ewo muji loo ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli sũ kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni kpɛtɛɔ tsofai ahe ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ lɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tsofai lɛ akatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ agbemɔ mli. Ni bei komɛi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ afite onibii lɛ aba.

english: What happens to my crops if I apply fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Crops cannot absorb dry fertilizer directly through their roots. Without water to dissolve the fertilizer, the strong mineral salts sit against the roots and can actually burn them, damaging the plant.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ atsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji nu bɛ ni akɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ Mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ. ni kɛ fitemɔ baa tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Can spraying my crops with more chemical than the recommended amount kill them?
ga: Ani tsofai ni fa fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe amɛ?

english: Yes, using too much chemical or making the mixture too strong will burn the leaf tissues, stunt the plant's growth, or kill the crop entirely because the plant cannot process high doses of toxic substances.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ ni afee ni mli wa tsɔ lɛ baashã baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ. etsĩɔ tso lɛ dalɛ naa loo ehaa tso lɛ gboɔ kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ atsu nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei babaoo ahe nii.

english: Why do my crop roots rot when water stands on my field for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu ta miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to breathe, just like humans need air. When water covers the field for too long, it pushes out all the oxygen, suffocating the roots and causing fungal decay.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ nu ha ŋmɔji anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Water dissolves nutrients in the soil so roots can drink them up, allowing leaves to make food efficiently through sunlight. In dry weather, plants slow down their growth to conserve energy and avoid dying.
ga: Nu shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni eha shishifãi lɛ anu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ. yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ Tsei haa amɛdalɛ baa shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why do my crop leaves stay yellow even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the roots are damaged by disease or excess water and cannot absorb nutrients, or that the crop is suffering from a pest attack rather than a lack of plant food.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ hela loo nu ni fa fe nine efite shishifãi lɛ. ni enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko miipiŋ tso lɛ moŋ fe tso niyenii ni bɛ.

english: Why do my plants drop their flowers before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plants drop flowers when they experience sudden stress, such as severe drought, extreme heat, heavy insect attack, or a lack of specific nutrients needed to form strong fruits.
ga: Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛkɛ trukaa nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kooloi tutuamɔ ni naa wa kpe. aloo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa koni afee aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni bɛ.

english: How do shade trees help young crops survive during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Shade trees block scorching sunlight, lowering the ground temperature and keeping moisture in the air and soil so young crops do not lose water faster than their small roots can drink it.
ga: Tsei tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ akafite nu oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Amɛ nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni anuɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an important plant food, or the ground is soaked with too much water. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green color so they can make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji tsei niyenii ni he hiaa Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛ nu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my crop yield get smaller every year if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize draws specific nutrients out of the ground each season. Planting it repeatedly on the same plot wears out the soil, so switching to crops like cowpeas or groundnuts for a season puts good nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be, ni kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii kpakpai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to grow full, healthy cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baaha tsei fɛɛ aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make energy for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch maximum light, which helps build larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha tso lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni la babaoo aba. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots while carrying heavy bunches at the top. Soft, wet soil combined with strong wind causes the roots to pull out of the ground unless you support the main stems with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ fɔfɔi ni tsii yɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fata he lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ajie amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ja okɛ tso nibii fiɔ tsɔne wulu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when there is continuous heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive. Too much rainfall fills all the small air spaces in the ground with water, preventing the roots from breathing and causing them to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground, known as mulching, shields the soil from the harsh sun, traps moisture so the ground stays wet longer, and stops unwanted weeds from popping up.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛtsi jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni amɛkaje kpo.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack nutrients, or are attacked by small insects like mirids. Planting shade trees and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers stay on the tree and form pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen tutua amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa ni aduɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning yellow during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling happens when tomato plants suffer from heat stress and lack of water, or when tiny insects like whiteflies spread plant viruses. Regular watering and partial shade keep the plants cool and healthy.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hewɔ. Aloo beni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be fioo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to dry soil. They wake up fast and absorb the early rainwater and soil nutrients much quicker than crop seeds, which need time to germinate.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Amɛteɔ shi mra ni amɛheɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii oya fe dumɔwui, ni heɔ be dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off during dry weather, and will the crop die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ni ani ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baagbo?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells to save water and protect themselves. The crop is not dead; the roots underground stay healthy and will shoot out fresh green leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Nibii ni adu lɛ gboko lolo. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ baawa ni amɛbaakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How should I push my cassava stick cuttings into the soil so they grow properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ bɔni afee ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: You should plant cassava cuttings at a slanting angle with the small buds pointing upward toward the sky, burying at least half of the stick in loose soil so strong roots can form easily.
ga: Esa akɛ odu o-cassava niji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛtsɔ kɛ hoo lɛ, tso lɛ nine lɛ fã ni ekɛaafu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni shishifãi ni wa amamɔ afee mlɛo

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top. When the soil gets soaked and weak from rain, wind easily pushes them over, which is why supporting the stem with a strong wooden prop is helpful.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Enɛ hewɔ ni tso ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ.

english: How can I tell the difference between a banana plant and a plantain plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ banana tsei kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Banana stems often have reddish or purplish shades and produce sweeter fruit eaten raw when ripe, while plantain stems are usually greener and produce firmer, starchier fruits that are meant to be cooked before eating.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, banana tsei lɛ yɛ tsuru loo purple. ni aduawai lɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ aye lɛ ŋmɔŋ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, banana tsei lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ starch ni esa akɛ ahoo dani aye.

english: Yellow leaves on young corn usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen food or that too much water is sitting in the soil, preventing the plant roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant too many corn seeds together in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo fee ekome yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds in one spot forces the young corn plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny, weak corn ears.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing all over my garden egg leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmeii ahe baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Tiny holes on garden egg leaves mean small insects like flea beetles are feeding on the plant. Spraying the leaves with organic neem water or recommended pest treatment will protect them.
ga: Bu bibii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ahe baai amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni ji flea beetles lɛ miiye tso lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem nu loo tsofai krokomɛi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe.

english: Garden egg flowers drop off when the soil is too dry, when the weather gets extremely hot, or when there are no beneficial insects around to help move pollen between the flowers.
ga: Eggplants ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ fɔfɔi ahe ni baaye abua ni ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ.

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand. High soil mounds give the tubers room to grow long and thick while protecting the roots from getting soaked and rotting in trapped rainwater.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato koni egbɛ eshwa. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfite yɛ nugbɔ nu ni emɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes so their leaves can spread out in full sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves make food, which flows down to build bigger tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la lɛ fɛɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ yitso agbo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up and look limp during hot, dry afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ shwane ni edɔ ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during dry spells to protect themselves from losing water through evaporation, which helps the plant survive until it receives rain or water.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ amɛnaa nugbɔ loo nu.

english: How does clearing weeds and breaking hard soil help my cassava grow bigger roots?
ga: Te jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mligbalamɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cassava lɛ ni eshishifãi wuji lɛ aba tɛŋŋ?

english: Loosening the soil allows the cassava roots to expand easily underground, while removing weeds ensures that the crop gets all the nutrients and moisture without competition.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in very dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds require moisture to soften their outer shell and activate the biological process inside that starts growth; without water, the seed stays asleep or dries out and dies.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu koni amɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo ni ekanya amɛmli wala yibii ni jeɔ dalɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baawɔ loo amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing very tall and thin instead of producing thick stems and fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ aduawai lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough direct sunlight, they spend all their energy stretching upwards toward the light instead of growing strong stems and developing fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa, nɛ e woɔ yiblii.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same farm patch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in that ground over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor pollination, as the plant tries to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni ehiii Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller cobs and fruits when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ aduawai kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight with each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leaving none of the plants with enough energy to grow fully.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eda kɛmɔ shi.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts under the ground are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are mature when the leaves start turning yellow and dropping, and when you open a few sample pods, the inner skin of the shell has dark markings.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ogbele sample pods fioo komɛi lɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mligbɛ lɛ jieɔ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ kpo.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and bent instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep, stone-free soil to expand downward easily; hard or compacted soil blocks their path, forcing them to twist and remain small.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni tɛi bɛ nɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsiɔ gbɛ lɛ naa. Anyɛɔ enɔ koni etsɔ ehe ni ehi shi bibioo

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow when there is too much standing water on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water drowns plant roots by cutting off air in the soil, preventing the roots from absorbing nutrients properly, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemical pest treatment on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Spraying early in the morning or late in the evening is best because the hot afternoon sun causes chemicals to evaporate too quickly and can burn the plant leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ ni eshãa tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up and droop during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl during the hottest part of the day as a natural mechanism to reduce water loss, and they will usually bounce back once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: What will happen to my maize if I apply more fertilizer than the recommended amount to make it grow faster?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya?

english: Applying too much fertilizer creates chemical burns on the plant roots and leaves, which damages or kills the crop rather than making it grow faster.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsofai ni shãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ shãa. Enɛ fiteɔ loo efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow after heavy, continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Excess water fills all air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots so they cannot take up nutrients properly, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade trees planted above them when I clear a new plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ nɔ kɛji mijie saatso hee lɛ nɔ pɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight, so shade trees act as a protective cover while keeping the soil moist until the cocoa bushes mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin without producing big ears when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛbɛ toi wuji kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize is planted too close, plants compete for limited sunlight and nutrients, spending all their energy growing upward instead of building thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo lɛ he akaŋ. Ekɛ nakai hewalɛ ni fa lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ ni ekɛfeɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds from my maize field while the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni tsei lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal key nutrients and water from the soil when your young maize plants need those resources most to establish strong stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii titrii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni o-abele tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa nakai nibii lɛ fe fɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant undergoes stress, which is usually caused by sudden heat, dry soil, or a lack of moisture during flowering.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ dɔlɛ trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why does planting cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year lead to smaller tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Cassava continuously pulls specific nutrients from the soil, so growing it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those nutrients unless the soil is rested or replenished.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ baaho aya. ja ashɛre shikpɔŋ lɛ he loo awo mli ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a long time to start growing after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ dalɛ shishi beni mikɛ amɛ ewo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers direct their early energy into rebuilding root systems below the ground before you will notice new leafy growth above the surface.
ga: Plantain suckers kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ shishijee koni amɛkɛtswa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ekoŋŋ. Dani obaana baa hee ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my mangoes look clean on the outside, but when I cut them open they are rotten and full of tiny worms inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mangoi lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ? Shi beni ogbala mli lɛ, egbo ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli?

english: Fruit flies pierce the skin of young mangoes while they are still growing on the tree to lay eggs inside. As the fruit ripens and turns sweet, the eggs hatch into tiny worms that eat the soft flesh from the inside out.
ga: Yibii amli ŋmeii shwieɔ mango ŋmeii amli beni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo koni amɛkɛ amɛwui lɛ awo mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ ekwɛ ni ehi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. ni yeɔ loo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ

english: How do worms get deep inside my fruit if I cannot see any big holes on the outer skin?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii boteɔ mi yibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ? Ni kɛji akɛ minaaa bu agbo ko yɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ hu?

english: Female fruit flies use a tiny, needle-like tip to sting the young fruit and deposit eggs under the skin. The tiny sting hole heals quickly on the outside, hiding the eggs that are safely growing within.
ga: Fruit ŋmeii yei kɛ tip bibioo ko tsuɔ nii. Tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai bibii ni akɛ ŋmeii woɔ hewolo lɛ shishi ŋmeii bu bibioo Ebaatsa oya kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ. Ekɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ emli lɛ teeɔ.

english: Why do my young green mangoes fall off the tree before they get a chance to grow big and ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-mango bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛshwere lɛ?

english: When insects like fruit flies lay eggs inside developing green fruits, the hatching maggots feed on the core and weaken the fruit, causing the tree to naturally drop the damaged fruit early.
ga: Beni kooloi bibii tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ aduawai eŋɔli ni miida lɛ mli. Kplukai ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ shishigbɛ ni amɛhaa aduawai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai ni efite lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi mra.

english: How can I check if a young green mango hanging on my tree already has insect eggs inside?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji akɛ mango bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni fĩ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ kooloi awui yɛ mli?

english: Look closely for tiny dark specks or clear sap leaking from small pinprick punctures on the skin of the green fruit, which show where an insect stung it to lay eggs.
ga: Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ona ŋmeii diji bibii. Aloo mliki ni mli tse ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei bibioo ko mli. yɛ aduawai eŋɔlii ahewolo nɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ he ni kooloo lɛ ŋmɔɔ amɛ koni ekɛ amɛwui lɛ awo.

english: When is the right time to start protecting my fruit trees from insects like fruit flies?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi mi aduawai tsei lɛ ahebuu kɛjɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ahe?

english: Protection must start early when the fruits are young and small. Once fruit flies lay their eggs inside the green fruit, chemical sprays cannot reach the worms hidden deep within the flesh.
ga: Esa akɛ aje hela lɛ naatsii shishi mra. Beni aduawai lɛ ji gbekɛbii lolo ni amɛji bibii Beni aduawai amli ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii yɛ aduawai eŋɔli mli Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ loo lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Can I protect my mango fruits from pests without spraying chemical pesticides directly on the fruit?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabu mi-mango lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwieee aduawai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, you can hang protein bait traps in your orchard to catch adult flies before they lay eggs, or cover individual young fruits with paper bags to block insects from touching them.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ protein bait traps awo otso yibii abɔɔ lɛ mli koni omɔ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ dani amɛwo ŋmeii. Aloo okɛ woji aha aduawai bibii lɛ ahe koni kooloi akata amɛhe.

english: Why do insects attack my fruits more heavily during the warm and rainy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi aduawai lɛ waa yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Warm weather and high moisture make fruit fly eggs hatch much faster, while abundant fruit growth provides endless food for insect populations to multiply rapidly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa aduawai amli ŋmeii afɔ̃ɔ oya kwraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, aduawai babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni bɛ naagbee haa kooloi akuu lɛ koni amɛfɔ oya.

english: Why do crop buyers and exporters reject my whole basket of mangoes if only a few fruits show signs of worms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ mɛi ni kɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ kpooɔ mi-mango tsɛnsi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji akɛ aduawai fioo komɛi pɛ jieɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he okadi kpo lɛ?

english: Exporters fear that healthy-looking fruits might contain hidden eggs or young worms. If even one infested fruit reaches a foreign country, whole shipments can be seized or destroyed to prevent spreading the pest.
ga: Mɛi ni kɛ nibii majeɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ sheɔ gbeyei akɛ ekolɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo ŋmeii bibii yɛ aduawai ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Kɛji aduawai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ shɛ maŋsɛɛ Ebaanyɛ emɔ loo efite aduawai fɛɛ ni akɛyaa lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa.

english: What should I do with damaged fruits that drop to the ground under my trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee aduawai ni efite ni egbee tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Collect and destroy fallen fruits immediately by burying them deep in the soil or sealing them in clear plastic bags under the hot sun. Leaving them on the ground allows worms to crawl into the soil, turn into adult flies, and attack your next harvest.
ga: Buamɔ aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ anaa ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛtsɔ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni ooofu loo plastic kotoku ni mli tse ni oookɛwo mli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. tsɔ ŋmei onukpa ni otutua oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do fruit processors care about fruit flies if they are just going to peel and process the mangoes anyway?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni feɔ aduawai lɛ yɔɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ahe miishɛɛ lɛ? Be ni amɛbaatsa nɔ amɛfolɔ mango lɛ he ni amɛtsu he nii kɛkɛ?

english: Fruit fly maggots ruin the taste and color of the fruit flesh and introduce rot-causing bacteria, which spoils products like dried fruit or juice, making them unsafe for market.
ga: Fruit fly maggots lɛ fiteɔ aduawai amli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ amɛhe su ni amɛfeɔ helai ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ. Enɛ haa nibii tamɔ aduawai ni egbi loo aduawai amli nu fiteɔ. ni haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha jarayeli

english: Why does my maize turn yellow and stop growing after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much rain washes essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them, and waterlogged soil prevents roots from breathing. Adding fertilizer or manure after heavy rains helps feed the plants again.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my crop yield get smaller every year when I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the soil every season. If you do not give the soil a break, add compost, or rotate with crops like groundnuts that feed the soil, the ground gets tired and cannot feed new plants properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji osumɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ atsake. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua tsei heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves and produce fewer pods during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed leaves during dry weather to conserve water and survive heat. Planting shade trees like plantains or forest trees keeps the soil cool and moist so the cocoa trees can stay healthy year-round.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Koni kookoo tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when weather gets too hot or when they do not get enough water consistently. Mulching the soil with dried leaves keeps root temperatures steady and traps water.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aya hiɛ ni nu lɛ ahi mli.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cassava and maize on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize grows quickly and gives you a harvest in a few months, while cassava grows slowly, withstands dry weather, and can stay safely in the ground until you are ready to harvest or sell it later in the year.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Be mli ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa loo ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for light, water, and soil food. This makes the stalks grow thin and weak, resulting in very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa baa loo ŋmeii ko kwraa bɛ mli.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my young maize leaves so fast during the minor rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms fiteɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm weather helps armyworm moths lay hundreds of eggs that hatch quickly into hungry caterpillars. Checking under young leaves early in the morning allows you to spot and treat them before they spread across the field.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ, ni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai bibii lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, obaana amɛ ni otsa amɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small even when the weather is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ afee bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ hi moŋ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crop's roots. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life ensures all nutrients go straight into your yield.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of just planting grains saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makwɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to resist common diseases, survive dry spells, and produce bigger harvests. Saved grains lose their strength over generations and often produce lower yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot or get eaten by insects while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ egbo loo kooloi bibii eye lɛ beni mikɛtoɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rots if it is stored before being fully dried, and insects enter through tiny gaps in ordinary bags. Drying grain completely in the sun and storing it in airtight bags protects your harvest from moisture and pests.
ga: Abɛi baagbo kɛji akɛ akɛto dani egbi kwraa. Ni kooloi bibii baanyɛ abote hei bibii ni yɔɔ daa kotokui amli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ogbi oŋmaa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color so the plants can produce bigger corn ears.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji bɔni afee ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da.

english: Why is it bad to plant my tomatoes in the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu tomato yɛ he kome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases that target that crop to build up. Swapping tomato spots with crops like beans rests the soil and breaks the disease cycle.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake tomato he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe ni ebaakpa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Cassava plants drop leaves when water is scarce to prevent moisture from evaporating into the air. The plant goes quiet above ground while keeping its roots alive under the soil until the rains return.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ. Tsei lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ shi yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa amɛshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce flowers that just drop off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni edaaa ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience stress, such as intense heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save its energy for survival until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni esaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni yaa nɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ mli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up in the middle of hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas fold their leaves inward during the hottest part of the day to shield themselves from direct sunlight and reduce the amount of water lost through their leaves.
ga: Cowpeas shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa nu ni tsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa shi

english: How do I determine the right distance to leave between my crops when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, soil water, and nutrients without fighting its neighbors. It also leaves space for air to blow between crops, which keeps fungal diseases away.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rainfall and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not anchor deeply into the earth. When heavy fruit bunches grow at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs sturdy wooden props for support.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akuu ko ni tsii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii fe ŋwɛi ni ehe baahia ni akɛ tsei ni wa atsu nii koni ekɛfi esɛɛ.

english: Why must I clear weeds away from my crops when the crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have weak roots and easily lose the fight for survival if weeds grow nearby. Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil food from your crop, while also harboring harmful insects.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ wala he ta lɛ nɔ kunim oya kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ. Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eji he ko hu ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting while still attached to the tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ekpɛtɛ nitsumɔhe nine lɛ he lolo?

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet, overly shaded farms. Pruning tree branches to let in sunlight and fresh air stops the damp conditions the fungus needs to spread.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ kookoo diji baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Tsei ni afoɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kpaa.

english: What causes the tubers on my yam plants to grow small and covered in strange bumps?
ga: Mɛni miiha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ afee bibii ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ehà amɛhe?

english: Bumps and poor growth on yam tubers are usually caused by microscopic worms in the soil called nematodes. They attack the roots, preventing the yam from absorbing nutrients smoothly from the earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii kɛ dalɛ ni ehiii ni baa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛtutuaa shishifãi lɛ koni sweet potato lɛ akaŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their soft leaves burn and dry out easily. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them creates a protective canopy that keeps the soil moist and shields the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Shade tsei tamɔ dumɔwui loo shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, overly damp conditions. Pruning excess canopy branches to let in sunlight and airflow, along with removing affected pods early, stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ. Afoɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Agbɛnɛ hu, jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Is it better to burn the weeds on my land or clear them with a cutlass before planting cassava?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mikɛ ŋmei baatsu nii dani mikɛ ŋmei adu?

english: Clearing without burning is much better for your soil. Burning destroys beneficial soil organisms and nutrients, whereas clearing with a cutlass leaves organic mulch that rots into the ground, fertilizing the soil and keeping it moist.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni oootsi ni shãaa lɛ hi kwraa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii. yɛ be mli ni akɛ ŋmei tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, eshiɔ sũ ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is lacking nutrients before I plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa dani madu ŋmãa?

english: If your previous crop leaves turned yellow or the plants stayed short and thin despite getting enough rain, your soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen. Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost before planting restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo tso lɛ tee nɔ efee kuku ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each stalk grows strong and produces full, healthy cobs of corn.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko daa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are worms eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a common pest that attacks the growing heart of maize plants. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or wood ash into the leaf whorls can protect the young crops.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ atsui. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tso mli sũ ni akɛwoɔ baai amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe.

english: When is the best time for me to plant cassava in Ghana to get large roots?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ Ghana koni maná shishifãi wuji?

english: Planting cassava at the start of the main rainy season gives the cuttings enough moisture to establish deep root systems before dry spells come, allowing the plants to swell into big tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ yitso agbo.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to feed the tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground toward the sun, preventing leaf fungal diseases and boosting tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa ni ehaa yitso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant sap and transmitting viruses. Spraying plants early with neem water or insecticidal soap helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ashwie tsei anɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without forming any fruits during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: High temperatures and irregular watering cause heat stress, making tomato plants drop flowers to conserve energy. Mulching the soil around the base and watering consistently early in the morning helps the plants retain flowers and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Ha tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni awo lɛ nu daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants full of holes and looking like they were eaten overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni etamɔ nɔ ni aye amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. The caterpillars hide inside the plant's central leaves during the heat of the day and come out at night to eat, requiring early morning or late evening pest control before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli. ni amɛje kpo amɛbaye nii gbɛkɛ Esa akɛ atsu tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits turning dark and rotten at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni egbo yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom end rot, which usually happens when the soil moisture fluctuates or the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake loo tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi enaa.

english: Which way am I supposed to stick my cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji oodu lɛ, te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems should always be planted with the buds or nodes pointing upward towards the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to grow properly, leading to weak plants and very small tuber yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei be fɛɛ be ni amɛshishifãi loo amɛshishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaawa akɛ oookwɛ tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Look for 'sword suckers,' which have a wide bulbous base and narrow, spear-shaped leaves. These grow faster, form stronger roots, and produce bigger fruit bunches compared to suckers that already have wide, broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ ni tamɔ bulbous kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ lance. Nibii nɛɛ daa oya. Bɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni owo aduawai akui wuji kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ momo lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and the stems break easily during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ fãa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: This is often caused by plantain stem borers or parasitic worms attacking the root system underground. Cleaning your suckers thoroughly before planting and keeping the base free of rotting weed piles helps protect the root system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain stem borers loo ŋmeii ni tutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ otsumɔ oshishifãi lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ dani odu ni oha jwɛi ni fiteɔ ni abua naa lɛ akafee shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I place my fertilizer right against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is strong and concentrated; placing it directly against the stem will burn the soft stem tissues and roots. It is best to apply it in a circle or short strip a few inches away from the stem where the outer roots can reach it safely.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli ni ebɔleɔ he. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ afee blɛoo ni ebaashã shishifãi lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛwo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ loo yɛ kukuji amli. Inchi fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. ni kponɔgbɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same bed where we planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ he ni wɔdu ŋmei yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the dirt. Rotating them with maize naturally restores the soil's fertility without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmã tsu nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why do I need to clear shade trees and put long sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ni mikɛ tsei niji kakadaji atsu nii kɛha sweet potato wain tsei ni mikɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose maximum leaf area to direct sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground where air can circulate, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to make enough energy to grow large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ aba tsei lɛ ahe. Staking jieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can drink before the heat sets in. Afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate quickly in the sun and can cause hot water droplets to scorch sensitive leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi koni tsei lɛ aná nu dani latsaa lɛ aba. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ mli babaoo atsɔ oya yɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Ni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli nui lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the ground when I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain after a long dry spell often warms the soil without providing lasting ground moisture. If a dry period follows immediately, seeds absorb heat and moisture, sprout prematurely, and then die in the hot, drying ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I just leave animal manure sitting on top of my land after spreading it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni migbɛ eshwã lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving manure exposed on top of the soil allows the hot sun to dry out its good nutrients and heavy rain to wash them away. Mixing it into the ground and covering it with dirt traps the nutrients so your crop roots can actually feed on them.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ashã niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Egbi ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ amɛ kɛyaa. Kɛ́ okɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okɛwo mli lɛ, ebaamɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ koni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye amɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Is it helpful to mix organic manure into sandy soil before planting my vegetables?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafutu shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli dani adu aduawai?

english: Yes, mixing manure into sandy soil helps hold water and plant food near the roots, keeping the soil moist longer so your crops do not dry out quickly in hot weather.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu kɛ tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩii oya tamɔ bɔ ni eji yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I gradually mix dry leaves and sand into heavy dirt on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ lɛ blɛoo? Okɛ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋã afutu mli koni efee shikpɔŋ ni tsii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Mixing loose sand and organic matter into hard, heavy soil opens up tiny spaces so air and water can reach plant roots easily, helping the roots grow strong instead of getting choked.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã ni mli tse kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli futu shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tsii mli lɛ, egbeleɔ hei bibii anaa. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe mlɛo. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa moŋ fe ni amɛaatsi amɛhe.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cover chemical fertilizer with soil after putting it down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aha sũ he beni wɔkɛwo mli lɛ?

english: Covering fertilizer with a layer of soil protects it from sunlight that causes nutrients to evaporate into the air, and stops heavy rain from washing your expensive fertilizer off the farm.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ ko ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ he. ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it better to feed my crops fertilizer little by little instead of giving it all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli fiofio moŋ fe nɔ ni aaawo fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Giving all your fertilizer at once can burn plant roots and waste nutrients that the young crop cannot use yet. Applying small amounts over time feeds the plant gradually as it grows bigger.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wo mli shikome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni efite niyenii ni tso bibioo lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛtsu nii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ fioo ko tsu nii yɛ be mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ niyenii fiofio be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: What is the correct way to apply fertilizer to my maize crop so it doesn't get wasted?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli koni ekafite?

english: Dig a small hole a few inches away from the plant, place a small measure of fertilizer inside, mix it slightly with the soil, and cover it up so the roots can reach it safely.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu bibioo ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo afata he. Okɛ sũ fioo afutu mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ha nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: How long does buried manure or plant waste take to break down and feed my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei ni afu loo tsei amli jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii?

english: Organic matter breaks down slowly over several weeks or months as tiny living organisms in the soil turn it into plant food, giving your crops a steady supply of nutrients over a long period.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ fiofio. yɛ otsii loo nyɔji komɛi amli akɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii Enɛ haa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni yaa nɔ daa, ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why are my crops taking a long time to show results after I put compost in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani etsɔɔ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Unlike chemical fertilizers that give a fast boost, compost breaks down slowly in the soil little by little, building long-term soil health and feeding crops continuously over their entire life.
ga: Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi oya lɛ he. Kompost lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio, fiofio, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛshihilɛ be fɛɛ mli

english: Why must I wait a few weeks after mixing fresh poultry manure into my soil before planting seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni mikɛ kooloi ashishifã hee efutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Fresh poultry manure is very strong and produces high heat as it starts breaking down, which can kill young seeds; waiting allows it to rot safely into the soil first.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa waa ni ekɛ dɔlɛ babaoo baa beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfiteɔ lɛ. ni baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui bibii Mɛmɔ baaha egbo shweshweeshwe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How does covering buried crop food with dirt help my plants stay strong during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ haa mitsei lɛ anáa hewalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: A top layer of soil acts like a blanket that keeps moisture locked around the buried nutrients, preventing the sun from drying out the root zone when rain is scarce.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu, ni emɔɔ nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Niyenii ni afu lɛ Tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha shishifã lɛ he lɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from strong sunlight because direct heat damages their soft leaves. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a canopy that shields the young trees and keeps the soil moist.
