ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ amɛbaai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo buɔ tsei bibii ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small fruits when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to develop strong stems and large yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow starting from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tips of older maize leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK gives the crop the energy it needs to stay green and form healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmãa baai momoi lɛ anaa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni amɛfee toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Excess rain causes waterlogging, which suffocates cassava roots by cutting off air in the soil and encouraging fungal decay. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away safely.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ kɛ nu shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa ŋmei fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Staking lifts yam vines off the ground so leaves can trap more sunlight to build bigger tubers under the soil, while keeping the leaves dry helps prevent fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo ni amɛfee bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ aha baai lɛ agbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baai helai ni ji fungal lɛ anaa.

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids that transmit plant viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and allows the plant to continue flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eya nɔ ewo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do small worms bore holes inside my cowpea pods before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ bu yɛ tsina ŋmeii amli dani amɛkpaa lɛ?

english: Pod borers lay eggs on the flowers and young pods, and the hatched caterpillars eat into the seeds inside. Spraying appropriate insecticides at the flower bud stage prevents these pests from laying eggs.
ga: Pod borers woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ pod bibii anɔ amɛwui. Ni ŋmeii ni baa lɛ baaye dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkawo amɛwui.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily during light winds when they bear fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa beni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantains can easily fall over if root pests like nematodes or banana weevils damage their root systems, destroying the anchors that hold the heavy plant firmly in the soil.
ga: Plantains baanyɛ agbee shi oya kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii fite amɛshishifãi lɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋshɔkei ni ŋmɛɔ tsei ni tsii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni eeefite lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off due to extreme heat or severe dry spells, which prevents pollination. Regular watering during hot weather helps the flowers stay healthy and develop into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ hewɔ. ni tsiɔ pollination naa Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are my rice heads producing empty grains with no seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice bulbs lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty grains in rice, often called chaff, happen when fields run dry during the flowering stage or when sucking bugs damage the young, soft seeds before they fully form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ omɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ akɛ omɔ ŋmeii. Ebaa kɛji ŋmɔji lɛ mli egbi yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ kpata dumɔwui bibii ni edako lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: This happens when the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. To survive and feed its growing upper leaves and corn ears, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves, causing them to turn yellow and die.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni ehi shi ni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋwɛi baai kɛ ŋmãa toi ni miida lɛ. Tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves look scorched and brown when I remove all the shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees to filter the heat, intense sun breaks down the chlorophyll in the leaves and dries them out, causing leaf burn.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be ko bɛ ni baatsi dɔlɛ naa lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haa klorofil ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baa shãa

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upward and shrinking during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves up to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which helps them save water and prevent drying out during the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before any pods can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they feel stressed by dry weather, intense heat, or poor nutrients. Dropping flowers allows the tree to conserve water and energy so the main trunk and roots stay alive.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni esaaa amɛye lɛ hao amɛ. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛbuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their small young peppers right after they form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ pepper bibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛfee lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed young fruit when soil moisture changes too drastically—such as going suddenly from very dry soil to heavy rain—or when temperatures become uncomfortably high.
ga: Pepper tsei woɔ yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ tsakemɔi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ, tamɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛyaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nɔ. aloo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa ni ehaaa mɔ he ajɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cowpea crops attract so many insects as soon as they start opening their flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ gbalaa kooloi babaoo kɛji efɔ fɔfɔi pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and bright petals as part of their natural reproductive process, which naturally attracts sap-sucking insects looking for food.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ nu kɛ fɔfɔi ni kpɛɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ fã. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni nuɔ nu ni taoɔ niyenii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when the rain becomes heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave the soil waterlogged, oxygen is blocked, causing root cells to suffocate and rot underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abaatsi oxygen lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green sprouts in my barn before I sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ bɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up from dormancy after a few months in storage. Warm temperatures signal to the yam that it is time to shoot new growth for the next planting cycle.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ sɛɛ. He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛha ŋmeii adumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when their fruit bunches become large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ eyibii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the top-heavy weight easily pulls the shallow root system out of the soil during wind or heavy rain.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ Muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli.

english: Why are some of my maize plants staying very short while neighboring plants in the same line grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi be kukuoo nɛkɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni tamɔ nakai ni yɔɔ line kome mli lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Stunted maize is often caused by underground root stress, such as parasitic weeds like Striga attaching to the roots, localized soil compaction, or uneven nutrients in that spot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni haoɔ, tamɔ jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ Striga ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ dwarf corn baa. shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo niyenii ni ejaaa yɛ nakai be lɛ mli

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make food and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the nutrients they need to turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha niyenii feemɔ kɛ shweremɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, known as mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun so moisture stays in the ground longer. It also stops weeds from growing easily and breaks down into natural plant food over time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛkumɔ amɛfee adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars suddenly destroying the inner leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miifite mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds heavily on corn foliage. Inspecting your farm early and spraying safe biological treatments or recommended pest controls while the worms are small prevents major crop damage.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai babaoo. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋaa ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ darako lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii waa.

english: Why are my tomato plants drooping and dying even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: This wilting is often caused by small diseases in the soil that block the plant's stem channels, preventing water from reaching the leaves. Planting non-vegetable crops like maize in that field next season helps clean the soil of these plant diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela bibioo ko kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ baa. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Nibii ni jeee aduawai, tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ajie tsei ahelai nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting groundnuts in the same farm as maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei?

english: Groundnut plants have a natural ability to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Nearby maize plants feed on this extra natural fertilizer, allowing both crops to grow better together without competing for nutrients.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ekome kɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as intense heat without shade, lack of soil moisture, or damage from tiny pests like mirids. Maintaining shade trees and protecting the flowers from bugs ensures pods develop successfully.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo ni bɛ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ fɛ̃i fiteɔ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni abuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ omanye.

english: Why should I trim off extra young shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Excess shoots, called suckers, steal water and soil nutrients away from the main mother plantain tree. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers allows the main tree to concentrate its energy on producing a large, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Tsobii krokomɛi, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama plantains akui wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water collects around them for too long in heavy soils, choking the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain away safely so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Yam vines need to stretch their leaves out into direct sunlight to make food for the tubers underneath. Staking keeps the leaves high above the ground where they catch maximum sunlight and stay free from ground diseases, producing bigger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he koni ekɛha bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ he ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ amɛhe. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni da fe tsutsu lɛ

english: The first rain often warms up dry soil without soaking deep enough into the ground. If dry weather follows for a few days, seeds that sprouted will dry out and die; waiting until rain falls consistently ensures seeds get enough moisture to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni eboteee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ tee nɔ gbii fioo krokomɛi lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ amɛmɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: How do I know if the seeds I bought are good quality and will actually grow well on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Good seeds are firm, heavy, and clean without small holes or cracks. You can test them by putting a handful in a bowl of water—seeds that sink are healthy and ready to grow, while floating seeds are usually damaged and should be thrown away.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ wa, amɛhe wa, amɛhe tse, ni amɛbɛ bu loo ŋmeii bibii. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni okɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni egbo lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hoɔ yɛ nu hiɛ lɛ fiteɔ, ni esa akɛ ashɛrɛ ashwie.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Instead of growing strong and producing big harvests, they stretch upward to reach the light and end up weak.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, e waa nɛ e woɔ yiblii babauu. Mohu ɔ, a kplɛɛ a he konɛ a ya su la a he, nɛ nyagbenyagbe ɔ, a gbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow strong in one part of my farm but stay small and yellow in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi ani eji bibioo lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ fã kroko mli?

english: Soil quality changes across a field because rain washes food out of higher spots or hard dirt prevents roots from spreading. Adding decomposed animal manure or compost to weak areas feeds the soil so all your crops can grow evenly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su tsake yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ. Aloo muji ni wa yɛ ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo hei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii bɔni afee ni onibii fɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting beans or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special plants that pull natural fertilizer from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they feed the soil and help the maize grow bigger without needing as much expensive store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni amɛye amɛbua ŋmãa lɛ ni edara ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni jara wa ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: How can I get my yam and cassava to yield bigger tubers without spending money on chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii awo ŋmeii wuji ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ahe?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—keeps the soil cool and moist. As the leaves rot, they turn into natural food that helps root crops grow much larger.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Beni baai lɛ miifite lɛ Amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Wait until you get two heavy rains that soak the soil deep enough that it stays wet when you push your finger into it. Planting after just a light shower can cause the seeds to sprout and then die if the sun comes back strongly.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni okɛ onine woɔ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ mli wa waa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and curl during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli be mli ni mifeee nakai lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil, so they droop to protect themselves. They usually recover by evening, but watering early in the morning and adding mulch keeps the soil cool.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhe feɔ amɛ shoo beni shɛɔ gbɛkɛ. Shi nu ni oooha lɛ leebi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plant turning yellow and curling up into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow, curled leaves are usually a sign of a plant disease spread by tiny white insects. Removing and burning affected plants early stops the sickness from spreading, and planting disease-resistant cassava stems prevents it next season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra kɛ shãa Ehaa hela gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ni ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize and cowpeas from insects so I can sell them later for a better price?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa kɛ tsina-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe koni sɛɛ mli lɛ mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ?

english: Insects need air and moisture to survive inside stored grain. Dry your grain completely under the sun until it is hard, then store it in airtight storage bags (hermetic bags) which naturally suffocate insects without using chemicals.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia kooloi koni amɛhi shi yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ebaawa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo vacuum kotoku mli. (Vacuum bag) ni baaha kooloi bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii.

english: What can I do on my farm so my harvested tomatoes and vegetables stay fresh long enough to sell at high-value markets?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mi-tomato kɛ aduawai ni mikpa lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jarayeli hei ni jara wa waa lɛ?

english: Harvest your vegetables early in the morning when it is cool, handle them gently so they do not bruise, and keep them under shade immediately. Bruised or sun-baked produce spoils quickly and loses market value.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ o-vegetables lɛ leebi be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso. Okɛ amɛ atsu nii blɛoo koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni okɛ aduawai ato hulutsoo shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ Nibii ni atswa loo hulu eshã lɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛhe ehiaaa yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a living umbrella, protecting the young cocoa leaves from scorching until the trees are strong enough.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tso lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does it take three to five years before my cocoa farm starts bearing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔi afeemɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that must build strong trunk and root systems before it can support flowering and pod production. Once established, however, a well-managed cocoa tree can continue producing yields for decades.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni esa akɛ ená tso kɛ shishifãi ni wa dani ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Shi, kɛ́ adu cacao tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is missing the food my maize needs to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa mi-ŋmãa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: When maize lacks nitrogen, the lower leaves turn light green or yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip. Healthy soil usually looks dark, holds moisture well, and produces dark green, robust plants.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa feɔ duŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa

english: Why do my crops seem to grow better when I leave dead leaves on top of the soil instead of clearing everything clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛ́ mishi baai ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni majie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving organic matter like dead leaves on the ground forms mulch. Mulch traps moisture in the soil, keeps the ground cool, and slowly breaks down into natural nutrients that feed your plants.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Mulch mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa otsei lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize on the same farm plot without one killing the other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni eko egbeee ekroko lɛ?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving plenty of room for the slower-growing cassava to expand its roots afterward.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa haa ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ koni eshishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, weak bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ feɔ bibii ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces crop roots and leaves to fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving plantains enough space allows each plant to grow thick stems and support larger fruit bunches.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akpee. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa tso ni mli tse ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai akui wuji.

english: What is eating small ragged holes into my young maize leaves and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni miiye nakai buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Ragged holes in maize leaves are often caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaf funnels. Inspecting crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts can save the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baa ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni akwɛɔ mli mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ahere baai lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why do my tomato plants turn yellow and wilt even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting in moist soil is often caused by fungal or bacterial diseases in the ground that attack the root roots and block water from traveling up the stem. Rotating crops with maize or cassava helps clean the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni ehaaa nu aya ŋwɛi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry weather as a survival mechanism to conserve water inside its roots. The plant is not dead; once the rains start again, it will sprout new leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ Ebaakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can absorb moisture deeply before the hot afternoon sun causes evaporation, ensuring plant roots get the water they need.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ aba. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ana nu ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rains often mean the soil is waterlogged, which suffocates the roots and stops them from taking up nutrients. Improving water drainage around your farm helps the roots breathe so the leaves can become healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ Oŋmɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ. koni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa ekoŋŋ

english: What is causing small holes in the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: Small ragged holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the central leaves. If left untreated, they destroy the growing point of the plant, preventing normal cob formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Ebaafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Koni akɛtsi cob ni baa lɛ naa

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot withstand direct sunlight. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides temporary shade and holds soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ hewalɛ.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the plant roots can absorb it. Putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn the crop's roots and will waste the nutrient power until rain actually falls.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã ni amɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya hiɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering and balanced fertilizer keep the flowers attached so fruit can develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for planting maize after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait for two or three deep rains before sowing seeds. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry out if a dry period follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ dani odu dumɔwui. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be eho.

english: Why does burning my field to clear weeds make my crop yield worse over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji ni ashãa koni akɛgbe jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ mli woɔ wu yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fire destroys organic matter and beneficial organisms in the topsoil that feed your crops naturally. Over time, burning leaves the soil hard, dry, and dependent on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: La fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbiɔ ni ebiɔ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers growing very thin and small this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin when plants are placed too close together because they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough resources to swell its roots into large tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my harvested maize get eaten by insects so quickly inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ miiye mi ŋmãa lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Insects and mold multiply quickly when maize is stored before it is completely dry. Drying grains thoroughly under the sun until they are hard prevents pests from easily attacking your stored harvest.
ga: Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii babaoo yaa hiɛ oya kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to dani egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ ogbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ebaawa lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkatutua onibii ni okɛto lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts on my land after harvesting a heavy crop like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen food from the soil. Legume crops like groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it back in the soil, restoring fertility for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen nibii babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Legumes, tamɔ ŋmei, jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛ fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Maize pulls specific nutrients out of the soil to grow. If you plant it in the same place every year, it completely empties the soil of those nutrients, causing weak crops and lower harvests over time.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji odu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kwraa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together so I can fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ mikɛ babaoo awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants need space for their roots to spread and leaves to catch light. If planted too close, they fight each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to small, weak crops.
ga: He ko he miihia tsei koni amɛshishifãi lɛ agbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛbai lɛ hu ana la. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a key plant food. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the newer top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil gets too dry. Extreme heat or lack of water stops the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii.

english: Why are black spots appearing on my pepper leaves and causing them to drop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji miije kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛmiiha amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Black spots are usually caused by fungal diseases that spread during wet, humid weather. When water sits on leaves for a long time, fungi grow and damage the leaf.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ helai diji baa. Kɛ nu hi baai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa ni efiteɔ baai lɛ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to reach high to catch maximum sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to make enough food, which results in bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out so fast even after a heavy morning rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa leebi po lɛ?

english: Direct hot sunlight heats bare soil and causes water to evaporate quickly. Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and stronger than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants built to survive harsh soil conditions, so they pull water and food out of the ground much faster than farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni ama koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei.

english: What is making small holes in my young corn leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It feeds on the tender middle parts of the young corn plant and leaves its waste behind, which damages early growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Eyeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni eshiɔ nibii ni fiteɔ nii. ni fiteɔ mra be mli dalɛ

english: How can I tell underground crops like cassava are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and when digging up one sample tuber shows it has grown thick and full of starch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ tso lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni eshwɛ. Ni beni atsa nɔkwɛmɔnɔ kome lɛ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide tall, broad leaves that create crucial shade and protect young cocoa plants during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai kakadaji ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa baa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps bring back their green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting cassava too close makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing leaves enough room underground for the roots to swell into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ shishi koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Planting seeds before steady rains arrive can cause them to sprout and then dry up in hot, dry soil. Waiting for stable rainfall ensures there is enough soil moisture to keep the seedling growing.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the branch, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. You can prevent it by pruning branches to let in sunlight and air, and removing damaged pods early.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni ooofolɔ sɛɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ nɔ. ni ojie pods ni efite lɛ mra.

english: Why do tiny insects make holes in my pepper leaves, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miishi bu yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Insects like beetles and caterpillars chew leaves to feed themselves, which weakens the plant. Spraying safe remedies like neem seed oil extract or recommended agricultural sprays protects the leaves.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ladybugs kɛ caterpillars shwieɔ baai koni amɛna amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo okwaayeli mli tsofa ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from the maize I bought at the market for cooking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ dumɔwui toɔ ni miduɔ koni mikɛtsu nii yɛ minihoomɔ mli lɛ?

english: Maize sold for food is often not treated for planting or may be hybrid grain that produces weak crops in the next generation. Using certified seeds from an accredited dealer guarantees stronger growth and better yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsuuu ŋmãa ni ahɔ̃ɔ akɛ niyenii lɛ he nii kɛhaaa ŋmɔshi nibii loo ebaanyɛ efee dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ ŋmãa ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa shweremɔ ni mli wa kɛ yibii kpakpai baa.

english: Why do weeds hurt my pepper crop so much if I leave them growing in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ awui waa kɛji miha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than pepper plants and steal essential plant food, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes directly into your pepper crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe pepper tsei ni amɛjuɔ tsei niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hia. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni sɛɛnamɔi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa o-pepper tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yam is ready for harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up naturally. This signals that the plant has finished growing above ground and has stored all its energy into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Why should I remove the lowest leaves from my tomato plants as they grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛjɛ tomato tsei lɛ amli be mli ni tomato lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Removing lower leaves prevents rain from splashing soil-borne diseases onto the plant. It also improves airflow around the base, keeping the tomato plant dry and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ lɛ akagbɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ashwã tso lɛ nɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds need to start growing in a nursery before I take them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aje mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani akɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery protects young, delicate sprouts from harsh sunlight, heavy rain, and pests until they build strong roots and stems capable of surviving the rougher conditions of the main farm field.
ga: Nursery lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Kɛyashi amɛbaaná shishifãi kɛ tsei ni mli wa koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji wuji lɛ amli lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my small sprouts are ready to be transferred into nursery bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni dumɔwui bibii miida? Minɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaawo gbekɛbii akwɛmɔ kotoku mli?

english: Your sprouted seeds are ready for nursery bags once they develop their first set of true leaves and a sturdy stem, which usually happens a few days after germination.
ga: Odumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii atoohe lɛ beni amɛjieɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ anɔkwa baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa lɛ kpo lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do some extension officers advise using large plastic nursery bags instead of small ones for seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ plastic kotokui wuji ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe kotokui bibii ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ?

english: Large nursery bags give the young crop's roots plenty of room to grow deep and wide. When roots are trapped in small bags, they wind around each other and struggle to absorb nutrients once planted on the main farm.
ga: Grow bag agbo haa dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa gbɛ babaoo ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛshwereɔ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ ewo kotoku bibioo mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: What kind of soil should I mix to fill my nursery bags for healthy crop growth?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ esa akɛ mikɛfutu kɛha mi-nursery bags lɛ koni tsei lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ?

english: You should use soft topsoil mixed with well-rotted manure or compost. This combination holds moisture well while providing essential nutrients for young roots to grow quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ efutu mli lɛ atsu nii. Nɛkɛ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii nɛɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa koni shishifãi bibii lɛ adara oya.

english: What is an earth auger tool, and how can it help me prepare my farm for planting?
ga: Mɛni ji dɛŋdade ni akɛfoɔ nu? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mi ni masaa miŋmɔ lɛ kɛha dumɔ?

english: An earth auger is a drill-like tool used to quickly dig neat, uniform planting holes in the ground, saving you time and physical labor compared to using a traditional hoe or cutlass.
ga: Dril ji dɛŋdade ko ni tamɔ dril ni akɛfoɔ dumɔ bu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ. Ekɛ be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ baa shi kɛ akɛto blema shɔvel loo dade ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he.

english: How deep and wide should I dig the holes before planting my crop seedlings?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni elɛɛmɔ aha tɛŋŋ dani madu tsei dumɔwui?

english: The hole should be dug slightly wider and deeper than the shape of your seedling's nursery bag so the roots can easily spread into the surrounding loose soil without bending.
ga: Esa akɛ bu lɛ mli alɛɛ fioo ni ekɔ fe bɔ ni dumɔwui kotoku lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. mlɛo ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli

english: When is the best time of day for me to move my seedlings from the nursery to the farm field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛya ŋmɔ mli?

english: It is best to move seedlings early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is mild. Moving them under hot midday sun causes them to lose water quickly and wilt.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. ni ji be ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane teŋ lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha nu baaje amɛmli oya ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ.

english: Do I need to remove the plastic nursery bag before putting the crop seedling into the soil hole?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni majie plastic dumɔwui kotoku lɛ dani mikɛ tso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo sũ bu lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you must carefully remove the plastic bag without breaking the soil ball inside. If left on, the plastic prevents roots from expanding into the farm soil, and the crop will choke and die.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ojie plastic kotoku lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ofiteee muji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Kɛji oshi lɛ Plastic lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli. ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why do my seedlings look droopy and weak immediately after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi ni amɛgbɔjɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock, caused by root disturbance during planting. With regular watering and temporary shade, the plant will stabilize and stand strong again within a few days.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ transplant shock, ni shishifãi ni gbaa mɔ naa yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛji akɛ afɔseɔ nu daa ni ehaa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Tso lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ ni ehe wa ekoŋŋ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: How often should I water my young crop seedlings while they are living in the nursery?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ nu be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water them once or twice daily—early morning and late afternoon—keeping the soil moist like a squeezed sponge, but avoid overwatering so the roots do not rot.
ga: Nu shikome loo shii enyɔ daa gbi. Leebi maŋkpa kɛ shwane mli Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ashɛre Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ he koni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why are my crops not growing well even though I applied the fertilizer I bought from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mihe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Not all fertilizers contain enough nutrients for your crop's needs. Some low-quality fertilizers may look right, but their nutrient levels are too low to give your plants the nourishment required for good yields.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ekomɛi bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiamɔ nii aba mli. Ekolɛ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ sa. Shi niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Does the size of the fertilizer granules matter when I am feeding my crops?
ga: Ani bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara ha lɛ he hiaa beni mikɛ niyenii haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, if the fertilizer granules are larger than they should be, they may not dissolve properly or release nutrients evenly into the soil, leaving your crops without sufficient feeding.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ dara fe bɔ ni esa akɛ amɛfee. Ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ loo ejieee niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, onibii lɛ náaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know if the fertilizer I am buying will actually help my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You should check with an extension officer to confirm the nutrient strength. Some fertilizers contain too many fillers and lack sufficient nutrients, meaning you won't get the desired harvest even after applying them.
ga: Esa akɛ oyabi o-extension official lɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli wa. Fillers babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi amli ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, kɛ́ okɛwo mli po lɛ, onine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo ni otaoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my young plantain suckers?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ mi-plantain tsei bibii lɛ awo mli?

english: You should wait until the plantain plant matures a bit and establishes itself. If you apply fertilizer too early when the plantain is still small, it can cause the plant to grow poorly and fail.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ adara fioo dani amɛma shi. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli mra tsɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ, Ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ eda jogbaŋŋ ni efite.

english: Is it a good idea to put fertilizer in the soil as soon as I plant my young crop?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii pɛ?

english: No, applying fertilizer too early to small, tender plants can damage them. The plant needs to reach the right stage of growth first, otherwise the fertilizer will not give you the desired effect.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli oya tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe amɛ. Ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ ashɛ dalɛ he ni sa lɛ he klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haŋ nɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ aba.

english: What happens if I give fertilizer to my plantain plants before they are mature enough?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mi-plantain tsei lɛ wo mli dani dumɔwui lɛ dara bɔ ni sa?

english: If you feed plantains before they are mature, the plant might grow initially but will eventually fail to produce a healthy crop, wasting your money and labor.
ga: Kɛji oha plantains niyenii dani amɛdara kwraa lɛ, Tso lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ shishijee mli. Shi yɛ naagbee lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa shika kɛ nitsumɔ fiteɔ.

english: How can I make sure I get the maximum benefit from the fertilizer I buy for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ kɛhaa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: To get the best results, you must use fertilizer with adequate nutrients, proper granule size, and apply it only after your crop has matured enough to absorb the nutrients safely.
ga: Bɔni afee ni onine ashɛ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ nɔ lɛ Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa atsu nii. suitable pellet size Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli pɛ kɛji tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why did my plantain plant start growing fast after I fertilized it, but ended up failing to produce good fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ jeɔ shishi edaa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ tsofa wo mli lɛ? Shi yɛ naagbee lɛ, enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Applying fertilizer too early when the plantain is small can cause rapid, weak growth early on, but the plant will fail to yield properly later because it was forced before it was mature.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli mra tsɔ beni plantains lɛ darako lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛdara oya ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ shishijee mli. Shi tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa yɛ sɛɛ mli ejaakɛ anyɛɔ enɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can using the wrong kind of fertilizer cause my plantains to fail completely?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha plantains lɛ akumɔ kwraa?

english: Yes, if the fertilizer lacks sufficient nutrients or has oversized particles, it will not nourish the crop properly, causing the plant to grow weakly and ultimately fail.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli loo eyɛ nibii bibii ni fa tsɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ aha tsei lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why is my plantain crop small and weak even after I added fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ ji bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: If the fertilizer was applied when the plantain was still too small, or if the fertilizer itself did not contain sufficient nutrients, the plant will struggle to grow and will not reach its full potential.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako tsɔ lolo loo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ dalɛ mli ni enyɛŋ eda kɛyashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient responsible for leaf growth and green color. Applying balanced fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa kɛ eŋɔli su. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of lush green leaves but produce very few flowers or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to focus energy on growing leaves rather than producing flowers. Legumes like cowpea make their own nitrogen, so adding high-nitrogen fertilizer prevents proper flowering and pod formation.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ tsina ŋmei feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaatsi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites that spread viral infections to the plant. Controlling these pests early using neem oil spray or approved insecticides stops the damage from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites, ni gbɛɔ helai kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni efite lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my tomatoes develop dark black spots on the bottom of the fruit as they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Black spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when plants don't get enough calcium or face irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent and adding lime helps fix this.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛkɛ nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kpeɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ lime ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines instead of letting them trail on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking raises yam leaves toward sunlight so they can manufacture enough food to grow large underground tubers. Leaves left on damp ground get shaded and pick up fungal diseases easily.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ bɔni afee ni amɛwo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃. Baai ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baaha hulu lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: Too many suckers compete directly with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to small bunches. Keeping only one main stem and one or two replacement suckers ensures large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la mli, ni amɛfeɔ panicles bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso titri kome pɛ kɛ suckers kome loo enyɔ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha plantains lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: Why are the small flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop due to environmental stress such as insufficient shade, lack of soil moisture, or damage from pests like mirids (akate). Maintaining moderate shade trees and controlling pests prevents flower loss.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa hewɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids (akat) lɛ fiteɔ. Shade ni sa ni akɛhaa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ayeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi ni elaajeɔ lɛ tsiɔ naa.

english: What makes my cassava roots rot underground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Waterlogged soil starves cassava roots of air, causing fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely from the root zone.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my rice crop fall over flat in the field right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miigbee shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Rice falls over (lodging) when stems become weak from over-fertilizing with nitrogen or when plants are crowded too closely together. Proper plant spacing and balanced nutrients strengthen the stalks against wind and rain.
ga: Omɔ gbeeɔ shi (ehiɔ shi) kɛji ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔ yɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ hewɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ waa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ he.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot rapidly drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi baajɛ mli oya. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their foliage is tender and their root systems are shallow. They require temporary shade to protect them from heat stress and keep soil moisture stable.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, baai lɛ darako ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Amɛbiɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni amɛtsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi daa.

english: Plantains grow rapidly and produce wide leaves that create living umbrellas. They provide essential shade to shield young cocoa trees from sun damage while keeping the soil cool and moist during the crop's first few years.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of lower leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs significant amounts of nitrogen to develop healthy green leaves and produce heavy, full cobs.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ená baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni ekɛ ŋmãa ni tsii ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the central leaves of my young maize and chew holes in them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli?

english: This leaf damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant funnel. Early detection and targeted treatment prevent these pests from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ gbɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Mra ni ana kɛ tsamɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ Ebaatsi nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is mature enough to harvest without digging up the roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ shishifãi lɛ efooo?

english: Cassava plants show maturity around 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop, and visible cracks begin to form on the soil surface around the stem base.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ daa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why must I erect tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko kɛha mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni makwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to generate energy for growing tubers underground. Staking keeps foliage off the damp ground, which also prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ ahe koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai hu anaa.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It occurs when tomato plants experience irregular watering or low calcium levels in the soil, preventing proper fruit tip development.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ tomato tsei lɛ nu be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without forming any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni ewooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, long periods without water, or over-fertilizing with nitrogen, which causes the plant to grow leaves instead of developing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why does my land yield smaller maize harvests when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients faster than they can naturally recover, while also allowing crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up in the field.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii komɛi oya fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks direct heat from the sun. This stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly and keeps plant roots cooler during dry periods.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shelter, keeps the soil moist, and protects the young trees from heat stress.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa nɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ ko. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain tree, they fight with the parent plant for food and water. Removing extra shoots and leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui babaoo yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ Ekɛ tso nyɛ lɛ baawu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the same spot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nitrogen in the soil and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ekpa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, known as mulching, shields the soil from hot sunlight. It traps moisture so the soil stays wet longer, prevents weed growth, and gradually decomposes into natural plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: What is making ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark waste in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa baa lɛ mli bu ni eshiɔ gunk ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest common in Ghana. The caterpillars hide inside the funnel of the maize leaves, and catching them early with safe, targeted treatments prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli. kɛ amɛmɔmɔ mra kɛ tsofafeemɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ato he gbɛjianɔ Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays pooled around them for too long without draining. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to run off easily, keeping the roots well-aerated and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine bua amɛhe naa. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛyɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollination. Keeping water supply steady and providing light shelter during the hottest days helps flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ falɛ faaa Nu kɛ la ni anáa daa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall with thick green leaves but almost no peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni ekɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse shi pepper ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to put all their energy into leafy growth instead of flowers and fruit. Balancing your soil with phosphorus and potassium encourages the pepper plant to bloom and set fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ he moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ akɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium to shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa pepper tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: It is best to wait until the soil receives two or three steady, heavy rains rather than planting right after the very first rain shower. Planting too early can cause seeds to germinate and then dry out if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ba.

english: If I cut diseased cocoa pods off my tree, can I just leave them on the ground under the tree?
ga: Kɛ mifo kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ, Ani abaanyɛ ashi yɛ tso lɛ shishi?

english: No, leaving cut diseased pods on the ground allows the disease spores to stay alive in the soil and splash back onto healthy pods when it rains. You should gather and bury or burn infected pods away from the farm.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ amli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Esa akɛ obua ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anaa ni ofu loo oshã amɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds growing around my cocoa trees make diseases worse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani mi-cacao lɛ miiha hela lɛ miiwo wu?

english: Weeds trap moisture and block air movement around your trees, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases thrive. Clearing weeds helps the sun dry out the farm and reduces disease spread.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyiɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ naa, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu lɛ gĩɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does crop disease seem to spread faster after I try to cut away infected parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya beni mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mifo hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If your pruning tools are not cleaned after cutting infected parts, or if infected pods are handled roughly, disease spores can spread to healthy trees. Always disinfect your cutlass or pruning tools with soap or alcohol between cuts.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsuuu tsei ahe nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe nii beni afo hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo kɛji akɛ atsuɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Hela mli tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Okɛ samla loo dãa awo okpɔlɔi loo otsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ amli helai yɛ ŋmɔlɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔlɔ teŋ.

english: Can an old, dried-up sick pod from last season still cause disease in my new cocoa crop?
ga: Ani helatsɛmɛi ni egbɔ ni egbi ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aba mi-cacao tsei heei lɛ anɔ lolo?

english: Yes, disease spores can survive for many months inside old, dried-up pods left on the tree or hidden in weeds. Removing all old, dead pods during farm cleaning protects the new crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ahi shi nyɔji babaoo yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi ni ashi yɛ tsei anɔ loo ni akɛtee jwɛi amli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii momoi ni egboi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ ahe.

english: Can I mix my own homemade concoctions to spray on sick cocoa pods to cure them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mishia tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ afutu koni mikɛshwie kookoo ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ koni mikɛtsa amɛ?

english: Using untested chemical or plant mixtures can harm your trees or cause the disease to adapt and become harder to control. It is best to use recommended, tested fungicides and proper sanitation methods.
ga: Tsofai loo tsei amli nibii ni akako amɛ akwɛ lɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye otsei lɛ awui loo eha hela lɛ afee nɔ ni wa waa akɛ oootsake ohe ni oye nɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni ajie yi ni aka amɛ akwɛ kɛ hetsemɔ gbɛi ni sa baatsu nii.

english: How can I tell if a dark spot on my cocoa pod is just a normal bruise or a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ ji ŋmeii ni baa trukaa kɛkɛ loo hela ko?

english: A normal bruise stays small and dries up, while a disease spot like black pod turns dark brown or black, grows larger rapidly, and spreads a white powdery dust in wet weather.
ga: Nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ ji bibii ni egbi. yɛ be mli ni helai ahe hei tamɔ ŋmɔtɔi diji lɛ bafeɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni egbɛɔ sũ ni ji powda yɛŋ lɛ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli

english: Why do leaves on my cocoa tree turn yellow and fall off when the pods are sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hela mɔ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: When pods are heavily infected, the plant undergoes severe stress trying to defend itself and conserve resources, which causes it to drop leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pods lɛ emɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpeɔ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe. ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why do my cocoa pods get sicker during the rainy season than during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela mɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fungal diseases that attack cocoa pods love dampness and high humidity. Rain droplets carry disease spores from pod to pod, making wet seasons the peak time for sickness to spread.
ga: Fungal helai ni tutuaa cocoa ŋmeii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo. Nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ kɛ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli. Enɛ haa nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ feɔ be ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa fe fɛɛ.
