english: If a large cocoa pod gets sick, can I harvest it early to save some of the beans inside?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ kookoo ŋmɔ agbo ko Ani manyɛ makpa mra koni mikɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi ato?

english: If the disease hasn't reached the beans inside yet, you can harvest and salvage healthy beans, but if the infection turns the inside black and slimy, those beans are ruined and must be thrown away.
ga: Kɛji hela lɛ eyashɛko dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe lolo Obaanyɛ okpa ni ohere ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ hela lɛ ha emli lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔtɔ hu? Abaakpata nakai ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ ni esa akɛ ashɛrɛ ashwie.

english: Will planting my cocoa trees further apart help keep them from getting sick?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ lɛ baaye abua kookoo tsei lɛ ni hela akamɔ amɛ?

english: Yes, proper spacing allows sunlight to reach all parts of the trees and lets air flow freely, which dries out excess moisture quickly and stops fungal diseases from spreading easily.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa he fɛɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya, ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil with plastic sheets before planting their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ plastic shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛduɔ tsei lɛ?

english: Plastic sheets, known as plastic mulch, help keep moisture in the ground so you water less often. They also block weeds from growing around your crops and protect the soil from becoming too cold or washed away by rain.
ga: Plastic tsɔji, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ plastic mulch lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni onyɛ okɛ nu awo mli shii abɔ. Ehaa jwɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ hu naa. oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni obu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni fɛ̃i akafee lɛ tsɔ loo nugbɔ akashwie nɔ.

english: Will putting dark plastic on my farm ground overheat and kill my young seedlings?
ga: Ani plastic ni tsuɔ diŋ ni mikɛaawo miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baadɔ tsɔ ni ekolɛ ebaagbe mi dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Dark plastic absorbs a lot of heat from the sun. While soil warmth is good, too much heat can burn tender stems. That is why two-colored plastic sheets, like white on top and black underneath, are used to reflect heat away while still blocking weeds.
ga: Plastic ni tsuɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ dɔlɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ Shi dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine baanyɛ ashã tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. No hewɔ ni plastic woji ni yɔɔ sui enyɔ yɔɔ mli, tamɔ yɛŋ yɛ ŋwɛi kɛ ediŋŋ yɛ shishi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛjie dɔlɛ kpo yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ jwɛi naa lolo.

english: Why would I choose a plastic sheet that is white on the top side and black on the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mihala plastic ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni eyɛŋ ni eyɛ ediŋŋ yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: The white side faces up to reflect sunlight and prevent the soil surface from getting too hot for young plants. The black side faces down to block light from reaching the ground, which stops weeds from growing underneath.
ga: Fã ni yɔɔ futafuta lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi koni ejie hulu la lɛ kpo ni ekɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni edɔ tsɔ kɛha tsei bibii lɛ. Fã diŋ lɛ miikwɛ shi koni kane akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ shishi.

english: Why does soil covered with grass or plastic stay moist much longer than bare soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni jwɛi loo plastic ehà nɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bare soil leaves water fully exposed to the hot sun, causing it to evaporate into the air quickly. Covering the ground creates a shield that traps water in the dirt so your crop roots can drink it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ baaha nu lɛ mli adɔ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Mulching lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ nu naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu nu lɛ.

english: How does strong afternoon sun and high heat affect small crop plants right after planting?
ga: Te hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Young plants have small, delicate roots that cannot pull up water fast enough. Strong heat makes them lose water quickly through their leaves, causing them to wilt, dry out, or stop growing.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni waaa ni nyɛɛɛ agbala nu oya bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa baa lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ, egbiɔ loo ekpaa dalɛ.

english: How can I protect my young vegetable seedlings from getting scorched by the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he?

english: You can provide shade using palm fronds or shade nets overhead, spread dry grass around the base of the plants to keep the soil cool, and water early in the morning before the day gets hot.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei ahe tsei loo hulutsoo ŋshɔŋloo ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ aha hulutsoo. Gbalamɔ jwɛi ni egbi obɔle he. Tso shishitoo koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Kɛ nu leebi dani hulu lɛ adɔ.

english: Why do my young nursery plants droop and look weak after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Moving young plants causes transplant shock because their roots are disturbed and the main field is hotter than the nursery. They need temporary shade and regular watering for a few days until their roots settle.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli woɔ la ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa ni ŋmɔ titri lɛ mli dɔɔ fe ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni afɔ amɛ nu daa gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baa shi.

english: What time of day is best for me to transplant my small crop plants into the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii aya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to transplant late in the afternoon or on a cloudy day. This gives the young plants the cool night hours to recover and settle into the soil before facing the hot sun the next morning.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛwo shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akpee enɔ jetsɛremɔ.

english: Does warm soil help crop roots grow faster or does it hurt them?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛdaraa oya loo efiteɔ amɛ?

english: Gentle soil warmth helps seeds germinate and roots expand faster. However, if the soil gets extremely hot, it bakes the fragile root tips, making it impossible for the plant to take in food and water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ blɛoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya. Shi, kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lɛ, Akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashãa. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii loo nu.

english: How do I know if the heat from the ground is too strong for my newly planted seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ la lɛ mli wa tsɔ kɛha mi dumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ?

english: If the ground heat is too high, you will notice the bottom of the stem turning brown or soft where it touches the soil, leaves curling up, or plants wilting even when the soil has water.
ga: Kɛji la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fa tsɔ Obaana akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo efeɔ blɛoo kɛji ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpe, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, loo tso lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an important food crops need to build strong stems and green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure helps replenish the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil richer for the next crop I plant?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to a plant family called legumes. Their roots work with friendly soil bacteria to pull natural food from the air into the dirt, leaving free nitrogen behind for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata tsei akuu ko ni atsɛɔ amɛ legumes lɛ he. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛya sũ lɛ mli. Eshiɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantains on the same land as my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily dry out and burn in direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa shade and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut wooden sticks to support my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji koni mikɛfi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch direct sunlight, which helps the leaves make food for the tuber below. Keeping the vines off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and catching diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ wein tso lɛ tsi ehe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekafite ni helai akamɔ enɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the dirt whenever there is heavy rain for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the farm without draining away, it suffocates the tubers and causes them to rot, which is why planting on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water run off.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli Yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers during the hot season without growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ ni miduuu pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: When the weather gets extremely hot and dry, pepper plants get stressed and drop their flowers to save water and stay alive. Watering them early in the morning and keeping the root area covered with dry grass mulching helps keep them cool.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ ni amɛbaafɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwie shi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli. Nu fɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi ni okɛ sũ ni egbi aha shishifã lɛ he koni eye ebua ni tso lɛ mli ajɔ.

english: Why do my maize cobs stay small when I plant seeds very close to each other in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots fight over the same water, food, and light. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough space and resources to produce full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bafee ekome lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná nu, niyenii, kɛ la kome. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa he kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even after I buy and apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mihe ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and will quickly steal the fertilizer and water you feed to the soil before your crops can reach it. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: What causes the leaves on my tomato plants to curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is usually caused by a tiny insect called a whitefly that carries a disease from plant to plant. Managing these insects with insect nets or neem oil spray helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni hiɛ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi nɛɛ akwɛmɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but only a few pods end up growing on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow thousands of flowers, but many are dropped if the tree does not have enough water or if there are not enough tiny midges (pollinating insects) around to carry pollen from flower to flower.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛteŋ babaoo baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo kooloi bibii yɛ Kooloi bibii (pollinators) lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ pollen baajɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. As the plant grows, it moves nutrients from older bottom leaves to nourish the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Ejieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and shrivel?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbo?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to high heat, heavy rains, or irregular watering, which prevents proper pollination from taking place.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to grow strong tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread and exposes them to maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Gbalamɔ ni oná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni obaanyɛ.

english: Why should I space my plants out instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mitsei lɛ abɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Giving plants space ensures they do not fight with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients, allowing each crop to grow larger and healthier.
ga: Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkayeɔ amɛhe akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaa ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: Is it good for me to plant maize and cowpea together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize with cowpeas is helpful because cowpeas fix nitrogen into the soil, which feeds the maize and improves overall soil health.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ tsina ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmãa haa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ saa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ náa niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi.

english: Why do young cocoa trees burn and die when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains provides shelter and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ náa he ko ni ehiɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in poorly drained soil, creating a soggy environment where fungal diseases thrive and destroy the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ada ni amɛfite shishifãi lɛ

english: How do I decide which suckers to cut off from my plantain tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ midumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ he?

english: You should leave only one main plant, one medium stem, and one small sucker. Removing the rest stops extra suckers from stealing nutrients needed to form big plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi tso titri kome pɛ. 1 stem ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kɛ 1 ni dalɛ ji bibioo. Kɛ́ ajie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ, no haaa ŋmeii ni fa lɛ aju niyenii ni he hiaa koni afee plantain jwɛi agbo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to local conditions, allowing them to absorb water and fertilizer much faster than domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãa gbee. Enɛ haa amɛheɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe shia tsei.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather as a survival mechanism to conserve water and protect themselves from heat. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and resume normal growth.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaku esɛɛ eba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants curl their leaves upward during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling during hot afternoons is a plant's natural way of reducing water loss through evaporation. If the leaves recover and uncurl in the evening, the plant is managing the heat, but it shows the soil needs watering.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ he wa ni amɛgbala amɛhe gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miikwɛ amɛdɔlɛ lɛ nɔ. Shi etsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni afɔ sũ lɛ nɔ nu.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining consistent soil moisture during flowering helps the blossoms set into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ shi.

english: Planting maize too close forces the stalks to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin plants with small or empty cobs. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to produce full cobs.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi yɛ dumɔwui bibii loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings look weak and droopy right after I move them from the nursery to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings experience transplant shock because their delicate roots get disturbed and struggle to take up water right away. Moving them during cool morning hours or on cloudy days, along with providing shade, helps them recover quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa shoofeemɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbaa amɛnaa ni amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye nu he akaŋ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi amɛ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso loo yɛ gbii ni atatu yɔɔ lɛ anɔ. kɛfata he lɛ, hulutsoo ni akɛaaha amɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe wa oya

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally enriches the soil with food that maize plants need, reducing the amount of chemical fertilizer you need to buy.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni he hiaa o-abele tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my soil become hard like stone after a heavy rain followed by hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like decayed leaves or manure to keep it loose. Adding compost or leaving dead crop leaves on top of the soil helps retain moisture and keeps the ground soft for root growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ loo ŋmeii ni baaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo tso baai ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are holes appearing in my young maize leaves, and will this destroy my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni ani enɛ baafite midumɔ nii lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the fall armyworm feeding on the plant. Damaged leaves cannot catch sunlight efficiently to feed the plant, which slows growth and reduces your total harvest if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni amɛye tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha shweremɔ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my main crops when the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to local soil and can jumpstart their growth with very little water and nutrients. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing water and plant food from your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni ebaanyɛ eje dalɛ shishi kɛ nu fioo kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii fioo pɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize thoroughly under the sun before putting it into sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains moisture that promotes mold growth and attracts insect pests like weevils. Drying grains until they are hard removes excess moisture, keeping them safe from decay and pests during storage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ mli nu ni haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni egbalaa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛhe wa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kɛ kooloi ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their tender leaves burn easily in full direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains keeps the soil moist and protects the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas alongside my maize crop help my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the soil and helps neighbouring crops like maize grow stronger without requiring as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo awo mli tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the tips instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitseiaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the plants turn green and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the plant's sap and spread viruses. Controlling these pests early with neem oil or targeted sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Ni oooye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because water cuts off air to the roots and creates an environment where soil fungi thrive. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. ni ehaa shihilɛ ko ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves or palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Mikɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmei baai baadu miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material (called mulching) blocks weed growth, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, and retains moisture so you do not have to rely as heavily on rain or frequent watering.
ga: Mulching kɛ tso nibii ni egbi Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) baatsi jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ nugbɔ loo nu ni afɔɔ shwiemɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds right when the fruit bunches grow heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛji aduawai akutsei lɛ amli tsii pɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily because underground pests like nematodes weaken their shallow root systems. Supporting the main stem with wooden props and treating the soil around the base prevents the plant from collapsing under the weight of the fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ nematodes lɛ haa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ fi tso lɛ sɛɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi yɛ aduawai lɛ amli tsiimɔ shishi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves into full sunlight to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking keeps leaves off damp soil, reducing fungal diseases and helping the tubers grow much larger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaye ebua bulbs lɛ ni amɛdara babaoo.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the leaves inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the soft growing tip inside the leaf funnel of young maize. Applying recommended control treatments directly into the central leaf funnel early in the morning stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ehaa amɛkpaa nitsumɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, long dry spells without water, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying balanced nutrients helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli loo fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin without producing big ears when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni toi wuji bɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, they compete for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each seed proper spacing allows the roots and leaves to spread out and gather enough food to produce strong stalks and large ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛbua niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni amɛfee tso ni mli wa kɛ toi wuji.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil to catch sunlight and prevents leaf rot diseases, which results in larger yams at harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ ni ebaatsi baai lɛ agbomɔ naa. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ akpa.

english: During Harmattan, the air becomes very hot and dry, causing cocoa trees to lose water faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Dropping leaves is the tree's natural way of saving water so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baadɔ waa ni ebaagbi. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: The small shoots, called suckers, steal water and food away from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the main tree has enough nutrients to grow a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ ji koni tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat damages the delicate pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from being fertilized. When a flower cannot form a seed, the plant sheds the flower to conserve its energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ni etsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawo fɔmɔ nii. Beni fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha wala.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural plant food in the soil. When the roots decay, this extra nitrogen acts as a free fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ miifite Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops so much even when there is plenty of rain for everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nibii awui waa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops, so they quickly suck up the food and fertilizers present in the soil. Even with plenty of water, your crops will starve because the weeds are taking all the nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Kɛ nu babaoo po Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po baaye hɔmɔ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ miiná niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are small ragged holes appearing on the young leaves of my maize, and what causes it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni etse amɛhe lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes inside the center leaf roll of young maize are usually caused by caterpillars called Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the plant during the day and chew through the tender new leaves before they open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni etse ehe yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli lɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature enough to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the base of the stem turns thick and woody. You can also dig up one test root to check if it has grown firm, thick, and starchy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ tso Obaanyɛ otsa kaa shishifã kome hu ni okwɛ kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into fine powdery dust after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ sũ bibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects called maize weevils lay tiny eggs inside dried maize kernels. When the eggs hatch, the young grubs eat the starch inside the grain from the inside out, leaving behind hollow shells and fine dust.
ga: Kooloo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ corn moth lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii. Abɛi mli ŋmeii ni egbi Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Ashiɔ ŋmei ni mli ewo muji kɛ sũ bibii yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight and intense heat. Without enough shade trees or plantains nearby to protect them, heat stress dries out the leaves, causing them to turn yellow, curl, and fall off.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha hebuu lɛ, Heat stress haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛkpokpoɔ, ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why does my maize crop fail to grow big cobs if the rains stop right when the flowers start showing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ ekwɛɛɛ ŋmeii wuji kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ pɛ?

english: Flowering is the most critical stage for maize. If the plant lacks water during flowering, it cannot properly pollinate or transport nutrients to build seeds, which leads to small, underdeveloped, or empty cobs.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination loo amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii aya koni amɛfee dumɔwui jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni edarako loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other for limited soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight from one another. This produces weak plants with tiny yields instead of healthy, high-yielding crops.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ shi ebaawo yibii fioo pɛ. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ woɔ yiblii wawɛɛ nɛ e ngɛ he wami.

english: Why does my plantain produce smaller bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni bɔle tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around a single plantain plant, they compete for the same soil nutrients and water. Pruning away extra suckers leaves maximum nutrition for the main stem to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Dumɔwu kome fa tsɔ. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii babaoo nɔ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why can I leave cassava in the ground for months after it matures, but my harvested maize spoils quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nyɔji babaoo beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miifite oya?

english: Cassava tubers remain alive and fresh while stored underground in the soil, whereas harvested maize grains dry out and are easily attacked by mold, moisture, and storage beetles if not properly dried and stored.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ehee be mli ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli egbi ni ŋmei, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ oya kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtooo.

english: Why do some farmers plant vegetables like pepper or tomato while waiting for long-term crops to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye be kakadaŋŋ lɛ gbɛ lɛ?

english: Short-term vegetables mature in two to three months, providing quick food and regular money to cover household expenses while long-term cash crops like cocoa or oil palm take years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Aduawai ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Eji kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa oya kɛ daa shika kɛha shia shika. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shika ni anáa be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo loo mu tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops grow very bushy green leaves but fail to produce fruits or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii loo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Giving crops too much nitrogen fertilizer forces the plant to focus all its energy on leaf growth instead of making flowers and seeds. Plants need balanced nutrients, including phosphorus and potassium, to set fruit.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ haa amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he nii. Mohu ɔ, a peeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Fosfɔs kɛ potasium fata he koni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This enriches the soil so that the next crop, like maize, grows strong without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo awo mli.

english: Why are small worms suddenly eating the inner leaves of my young maize right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-ŋmei gbekɛ lɛ mli baai lɛ trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hatch rapidly when warm weather combines with early rains. The adult moths lay eggs on young maize, and the hatched caterpillars crawl into the central leaves to feed on tender new growth.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni fɔɔ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ fata he. Moths ni eda lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛye ŋmeii heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ blɛoo.

english: Why do I need to put up wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tsei koni makwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward full sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food, which is then sent down into the ground to build large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ enɛɛmɛi yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops crowd each other and fight for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the maize stalks to grow tall and weak, resulting in smaller leaves and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which means they naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the soil as plant food. Planting them alongside maize helps feed the maize and improves soil health.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ tsei aniyenii. Kɛ́ akwɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ehaa kooloi niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Does the size of the yam seed cut I plant affect how big the harvested yam will be?
ga: Ani bɔ ni sweet potato dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ da ha lɛ baaná bɔ ni sweet potato ni akpaa lɛ da ha lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, larger and healthier yam seeds carry more stored food and energy to feed the young shoot as it emerges. This early nourishment gives the plant a stronger start, usually leading to bigger tubers at harvest time.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, sweet potato dumɔwui ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ toɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo koni ekɛha ŋmeii bibii lɛ niyenii be mli ni amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ. Niyenii ni akɛhaa tso lɛ mra nɛɛ haa tso lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa bulbs wuji baa yɛ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when there are no bigger trees around them to provide shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ ni baaha hulutsoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air cool and preserving soil moisture until the cocoa plants mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yaa nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa.

english: Yellowing of the bottom leaves is usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant pulls nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the crop experiences extreme heat stress, dry spells, or irregular watering. High temperatures prevent proper pollination inside the flower, causing the plant to drop the blossom instead of developing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni baa fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Ehaa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting under the soil during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains water easily. When heavy rains leave water pooled around the roots for days, the soil lacks oxygen, which suffocates the roots and encourages fungal rot to attack the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ he fɛɛ he. shishifãi gbii babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ rot fungi lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua bulb lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my garden crops with dry grass during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts as a protective shield against the sun. It stops heat from drying out the soil, retains water for a longer time, and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu la naa. Ehaa la ni tsoɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: What causes tiny holes and ragged edges in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Kɛ ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: Holes in young corn leaves are commonly caused by armyworms or caterpillars feeding inside the plant funnel. They eat the tender new leaves before they unfold, which weakens the plant if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Weeds have strong, fast-growing roots that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds grow too close, your crops starve because the weeds take most of the available nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa, ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ baaye niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does clearing weeds away from my crops make them grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa amɛfeɔ wuji lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds gives your crops full access to these resources so they grow faster and bigger.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ. Koni tsei lɛ adara oya ni amɛdara

english: Why shouldn't I put dry fertilizer right against the stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fataa he ni bɛŋkɛɔ mi tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong and can burn the stems and roots if placed directly against them. It is best to place fertilizer a short distance away in the soil so the roots can feed safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli wa waa ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei kɛ shishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aye nii shweshweeshwe

english: Cassava plants drop leaves during dry weather to save water and protect themselves from heat. While the top looks dry, the edible roots stay alive and safe underground until the rains return.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi moŋ Shi shishifãi ni ayeɔ lɛ baahi shi ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide natural shade, keeping the soil cool and moist for the young cocoa trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is making holes in my maize leaves and leaving tiny caterpillars inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-abɛi lɛ afee bu ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii bibii? yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center leaves to feed on tender growth. Catching them early and applying recommended pest treatments stops them from destroying the field.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye ŋmeii ni shwereɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra ni akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite jɛmɛ.

english: Curling or wrinkled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from the leaves. Controlling these insects early keeps the foliage flat and healthy so the plant can produce peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Giving tomatoes consistent water helps the flowers turn into healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tomato nɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to build raised soil mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down and need soft, loose earth to expand into big tubers. Mounds loosen the soil for easy growth and allow rainwater to drain so the tubers do not rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛdaa shi shiŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei wuji. Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi koni eha shweremɔ aya hiɛ ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni bulb lɛ akafite.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to come up after I buried them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too deep, they exhaust all their energy trying to push through the soil and die before reaching sunlight. Maize seeds should be planted only two to three fingers deep so they sprout easily.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ hulu la lɛ he. Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli 2-3 inch pɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in full sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.
